Two variants align the student with different teacher signals, reducing reliance on clean-token supervision alone.

entry.title: Pneuma: A Large-Scale Real-World Time Series Benchmark for Commercial Aircraft Predictive Maintenance

author.name: Jiafeng Lin, Yutian Zhang, Huan Zhang, Yuxuan Wang, Jinyan Feng, Yuhui Liu, Zhongyi Pei, Jianmin Wang

entry.summary: Pneuma is the first public large-scale benchmark for aircraft predictive maintenance, with over 920 million multivariate time steps from in-service commercial aircraft bleed air systems, four aircraft types, and nine verified fault scenarios aligned with real maintenance logs. It exposes real-world challenges like class imbalance, subtle fault evolution, and cross-fleet variance. This addresses a reproducibility gap in a safety-critical domain.

entry.title: Anchored Stein Variational Gradient Descent Algorithm for Non-smooth Sampling

author.name: Thanh Dang, Matthew X. Burns, Jiaming Liang

entry.summary: Introduces anchored SVGD, which samples from targets with non-smooth potentials by introducing a smoother reference potential and an anchor weight, eliminating the need to compute gradients of the target potential while recovering standard SVGD as a special case. The paper establishes KL first-variation formulas and theory under a locally Lipschitz regularity regime. Extends variational inference to a broader class of distributions.

entry.title: Boundary Geometry Determines Optimal Shallow ReLU Approximation under Weighted Coefficient Constraints

author.name: Jia-Qi Yang, Lei Shi

entry.summary: This paper establishes upper and lower bounds for L^q approximation by shallow ReLU networks on convex bodies with targets in weighted variation spaces, determining optimal polynomial approximation exponents for all planar convex bodies, products with polytopes, and C^2 convex bodies in broad q ranges. It shows how domain boundary geometry governs approximation rates. A rigorous approximation theory result for neural networks.

entry.title: CAMR: Compatibility-Aware Memory Replay for Continual Learning in Large Language Models

author.name: Jingpu Yang, Tianhao Li, Fengxian Ji, Yufeng Wang, Shuxin Zheng, Xiaoqing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes CAMR, an adaptive continual-learning framework that jointly controls whether to supervise incoming examples and which historical examples to replay. It combines compatibility checks with a learned memory gate choosing among learning with general replay, jointly reinforcing compatible examples, and skipping mastered duplicates. Addresses the acquisition-retention tradeoff in LLM continual learning.

entry.title: ETAMem: Decoupling and Aligning Heterogeneous Memory for Long-Term Conversational Agents

author.name: Xinying Qian, Ying Zhang, Yu Zhao, Xubo Liu, Baohang Zhou, Jeff Z. Pan

entry.summary: ETAMem is a multi-view memory framework for long-term conversational LLM agents that decouples heterogeneous information into atomic memory units and aligns memory representation and organization with each unit's characteristics. It addresses information entanglement within coarse memory units and the limits of purely semantic-similarity-based organization. Long-term memory is a key bottleneck for personal assistants, making this direction practically relevant.

entry.title: WithinVAE: Compact Visual Autoencoding with Self-Distilled Semantics

author.name: Yuzhou Ji, Jiepeng Wang, Tianyu Jin, Lizhuang Ma, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: WithinVAE shows that semantic structure in visual autoencoders can be learned from the autoencoder's own reconstructive representations via DINO/iBOT-style self-distillation from an EMA copy of itself, rather than inherited from pretrained recognition encoders. Combined with a sequential bottleneck and position-dependent token masking, it achieves 4-fold compression without external semantic supervision. This is a notable simplification for the tokenizers underlying multimodal and generative models.

entry.title: GraftRay: Physically Based Mesh Insertion into Gaussian Splatting Scenes via Path Tracing

author.name: Jinxin Ai, Matthias Niessner

entry.summary: GraftRay enables physically consistent insertion of mesh objects into 2DGS/3DGS indoor scenes using path tracing, capturing near-field area lights like windows and lamps that environment-map approximations miss, while maintaining multi-view consistency. Applications include AR, content creation, and synthetic data generation.

entry.title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?

author.name: Jiafu Tang, Yifan Xu, Eric Tang, Junjie Zhao, Shipeng Luo, Te Sun, Haoxuan Hu, Yiyan Ji, Xinlong Chen, Zihao Wang, Yang Shi, Yuanxing Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Jiaheng Liu

entry.summary: CodeCap-Bench explores code as video caption, where executable programs with graphical primitives, layout rules, and temporal functions serve as a complementary representation to natural language. Comparing code and natural-language captions on downstream QA and video reconstruction shows code captions achieve superior reasoning accuracy for fine-grained spatial and temporal content. This is a provocative reframing of video representation.

entry.title: Perceiving and Predicting Dynamic Sports: Spatiotemporal Intelligence in Vision Models for Egocentric Tennis Video

author.name: Tudor Braicu, Joseph DelPreto, Jared Boyer, M\'onika Farsang, Maximilian St\"olzle, Tim Niklas Seyde, Daniela Rus

entry.summary: The authors collect an annotated egocentric tennis dataset synchronized with five allocentric videos and train vision models on seven spatiotemporal prediction tasks including player and ball localization, trajectory forecasting, and stroke anticipation. The study probes how well foundation vision models support robot-relevant spatiotemporal reasoning from moving cameras.

entry.title: RESPLE2: Inertial-Informed Recursive Non-Uniform Spline Estimation for Multi-Sensor Odometry with Global Refinement

author.name: Ziyu Cao, William Talbot, Song Li, Pakpong Chirarattananon, Fredrik Gustafsson, Marco Hutter, Kailai Li

entry.summary: RESPLE2 is a recursive multi-sensor state estimation framework using non-uniform B-splines for 6-DoF motion, with control-point prediction informed by inertial kinematics and motion-adaptive knot placement. Within an iterated extended Kalman filter it fuses heterogeneous sensors at native timestamps and supports flexible sensor combinations, including applications to drones and legged robots (with Hutter group involvement). Continuous-time estimation of this kind is central to high-accuracy odometry.

entry.title: Skill Dreaming: Evolving Repository Skills through Pull Request Streams

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Hasibul Haque, Jay Somasundaram, Ryan Turner, Bowen Zhu, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a system where LLM agent skill libraries continuously evolve using pull request streams: PRs provide knowledge to update repository-specific skills, while skills guide how new PRs are implemented and validated. This creates a mutually reinforcing loop between skill evolution and repository maintenance.

entry.title: LoRA on a Budget: Function-Aware Post-Hoc Compression for Adapter Fleets

author.name: Shenghui Li, Thiemo voigt

entry.summary: The paper formulates compression of many LoRA adapters under a shared rank budget as a two-level allocation problem, defining per-adapter functional rank-distortion frontiers and solving fleet-level minimax allocation. It argues that spectral redundancy alone does not determine how much compression an adapter can tolerate functionally.

entry.title: Beyond the Evidence Coherence Trap: Agent-Driven Evidence Selection for Temporally Disordered Fake News Detection

author.name: Chi Wang, Min Gao, Yifei Zhang, Bincheng Gu, Zongwei Wang, Wentao Li

entry.summary: This paper identifies the evidence coherence trap, where temporally disordered fake news that rearranges true events into false chronology gets validated by locally coherent but mismatched retrieved evidence. The authors build ChronoFake, a source-disjoint benchmark of 30,706 articles, and propose agent-driven evidence selection to check temporal consistency. This addresses a genuinely subtle misinformation failure mode.

entry.title: AutoVend: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Autonomous Vending Operations

author.name: Qiming Shi, Yikun Li, Beidi Luan, Rui Sun, Yan Ma, Jing Li, Daxin Jiang, Zuo Bai

entry.summary: AutoVend is a benchmark where an LLM agent manages 20 vending machines across five site types over 180 simulated days through a web interface, with a data-grounded simulator including warehouse logistics, procurement lead times, inventory expiration, and operating costs. It evaluates whether online commerce decisions translate into sustained economic returns.

entry.title: GraphRAGProv: GraphRAG Meets How-Provenance

author.name: Wadie El Amrani, Luis Gal\'arraga

entry.summary: GraphRAGProv executes SPARQL queries over source-grounded RDF graphs and computes how-provenance polynomials that record which statements were used and how they were combined, with links back to source text. This makes GraphRAG answers auditable, addressing a key transparency gap in retrieval-augmented generation. It is relevant for high-stakes domains where explainability of LLM answers is mandatory.

entry.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions

author.name: Anouar Imel, Imad Charradi, Abderrahman Sghir, Khalil El Khammar

entry.summary: CrossProfile is a diagnostic benchmark of 480 tasks crossing fact ownership (supporting, decoy, irrelevant) against fixed text to test memory selection heuristics for LLM group decisions. Across Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and DeepSeek models, both rarity and relevance heuristics fail predictably: relevance readmits on-topic decoys while rarity can drop critical facts. This cleanly disentangles confounds in hidden-profile tasks and informs multi-agent memory design.

entry.title: UnityBench-Mini3D: Evaluating LLM Agents for 3D Game Development in Unity

author.name: Yijun Zhou, Minghao Shao, Ke Zhang, Renkai Yuan, Hongbo Yuan, Bin Hu, Bozhao Qian, Hongxia Shen, Yanhong Liu, Yuting Chen, Yuntao Shi, Zhongxuan Xu, Shuo Mao, Haijia Zhou, Zhendong Li, Tao Zhang, Chenggang Li, Yuxuan Wang, Zinan Zheng, Calvin Zhang, Jia Li, Heng Chang, Jie Feng

entry.summary: UnityBench-Mini3D is a benchmark of 77 project-level Unity game-development tasks organized around seven expert-defined skill categories and three difficulty tiers, evaluated with 1,178 held-out human-authored milestone tests covering scene structure, component configuration, and runtime behavior. It improves on existing engine benchmarks for Godot that rely on LLM judges or coarse outcomes by using deterministic in-engine testing. This provides a rigorous new measure of coding-agent capability in engine-dependent software.

entry.title: How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning

author.name: Johnny Yu, Cyril Gorlla

entry.summary: Fin-SD is a localized hindsight self-distillation recipe for multi-step reasoning: when a student model fails a problem, it identifies and critiques its first incorrect step, and the trajectory is truncated at that point rather than conditioning on a full reference solution. It targets data-residency-constrained financial institutions that must rely on locally hosted open-weight models. The work clarifies scope conditions for how much teacher-like signal self-distillation actually needs.

entry.title: Detecting and Mitigating Query-Based System Prompt Leakage Attacks

author.name: Tushar Nayan, Pratik Poudel, Qian Lou, Yuede Ji, Jason Liu, Ruimin Sun

entry.summary: AdvGuard is a model-agnostic framework for detecting and mitigating black-box system prompt extraction attacks by modeling cross-query relationships in a bounded semantic interaction graph, statistically filtering candidate components, and classifying with a graph convolutional network over line graphs. This captures malicious intent that emerges across multiple turns rather than in isolated queries.

entry.title: REACH: An RL-based Hierarchical Humanoid Crawling Framework for Adaptable Confined Space Traversal

author.name: Shengzhang Xu, Yuning Guo, Weiyi Hu, Yifeng Xu, Zhongyu Li, He Kong

entry.summary: Presents REACH, a hierarchical RL framework enabling a Unitree G1 humanoid to traverse height-constrained spaces via variable-height bipedal walking (1.27-0.50m) and crawling (0.50-0.20m), using history-conditioned latent representations of terrain and contact. It extends humanoid locomotion beyond crouched-walking clearance limits.

entry.title: PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search

author.name: Xiaohan Ye, Zihan Gong, Jingqian Zhao, Lianyu Du, Yunmeng Shu, Xu Chen, Zesheng Zhou, Renchun You, Bocheng Chen, Jinsong Lan, Haihong Tang, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: An industrial technical report on PailitaoMMSearch, a unified end-to-end multimodal search system that directly generates product semantic IDs from raw query images and free-form instructions, scaling along data, model, and scenario dimensions. This matters as a rare detailed account of generative retrieval deployed at scale in e-commerce search.

entry.title: Beyond Parameter Protection: Fisher-Shaped EWC for Replay-Free Continual Learning

author.name: Liying Wang, Simone Magistri, Joost van de Weijer

entry.summary: The authors observe that Elastic Weight Consolidation's local Fisher estimate at a retained solution does not capture sensitivity after parameter displacement, and propose Fisher-Shaped EWC, which minimizes worst-case empirical FIM trace within a neighborhood during task learning. This shifts Fisher information from parameter protection toward shaping solutions that will be easier to retain later.

entry.title: Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling

author.name: Sinjae Kang, Dong Kyu Shin, Jaehong Kim, Kamin Lee, Hyoeun Kim, Kaixin Wang, Li Zhao, Seonghyeon Ye, Kimin Lee

entry.summary: The authors introduce Quality-Controllable Policies, robot policies that allow inference-time control over quality attributes such as execution speed and motion smoothness beyond binary task success. An iterative hindsight relabeling loop collects rollouts under target quality labels, adds successful trajectories to the dataset, and relabels accumulated data to extend the controllable quality range.

entry.title: Instruction Capacity: Behavior and Degradation of Language Models under Controlled Load

author.name: Hennadii Kutomanov

entry.summary: The paper proposes an instrument to measure a language model's instruction-following capacity in units of load with uncertainty, using atomic rules that replace single-token words with computable reference answers, so each application becomes a Bernoulli trial with known position and rule. The statistical model measures how replacement probability degrades with text length and number of rules.

entry.title: Dynamical coarse-graining of neural-network training

author.name: Lin-Juan Wang, Da Li, Huiling Duan, Jianxiang Wang

entry.summary: The authors define a learning operator for neural-network training and establish descent, exact closure, and dynamic coarse-graining theorems, providing a systematic framework for building macroscopic models of training in a state space far smaller than parameter space. This enables prediction and control of training dynamics at a coarse-grained level.

entry.title: RankFormer: Rethinking Time Series Transformers through Representation Capacity Analysis and Progressive Decoding

author.name: Peiwang Tang, Cheng HE, Xijie Liang, Defu Lian

entry.summary: Proposes RankFormer, an encoder-decoder transformer for multivariate time series forecasting grounded in a rank-based analysis of representation capacity, moving beyond channel-independent and direct-projection decoding. The architecture uses progressive decoding to better capture complex multivariate dynamics relevant to web services and IoT infrastructure.

entry.title: CaLLM: Continual Adaptation of LLMs via Non-Parametric Adapter Routing

author.name: Bilge Celik, Anna Vettoruzzo, Joaquin Vanschoren

entry.summary: Presents CaLLM, a continual adaptation framework for LLMs that combines metric-based meta-learning with lightweight modular adapters: input batches are projected into a task-agnostic embedding space, matched to the nearest prototype, and routed to the corresponding specialized adapter. This provides controlled cross-task interference, constant computational complexity, and zero-shot task-to-expert assignment.

entry.title: When Visual Evidence Is Insufficient: How Instructions, Post-Training, and Internal Activations Shape Refusal in Multimodal Language Models

author.name: Ananth K Suresh, Aveen Dayal, Gouthaman KV, Aditya Pola, Vineeth N Balasubramanian

entry.summary: This study examines when multimodal LLMs refuse questions that images cannot answer, distinguishing genuine recognition of insufficient evidence from refusals driven by unrelated safety constraints. Across three MLLMs on MoHoBench, it systematically manipulates refusal instruction meaning/placement, compares supervised versus preference-based post-training, and intervenes on a refusal-related activation. It provides a mechanistic picture of calibrated refusal behavior.

entry.title: Anytime Valid Confidence Bands for Distribution Functions

author.name: Bror Hultberg, Dave Zachariah, Ant\^onio H. Ribeiro

entry.summary: Derives confidence bands for distribution functions that are valid simultaneously over all times and all points in the domain, even for data streams with arbitrary dependence on the past, starting with time-averaged conditional CDFs whose widths relate to binary search tree depth. The result generalizes via a framework for any indexed family of time-averaged distribution functions. Contributes to anytime-valid inference for streaming data.

entry.title: Quantifying and Prioritizing Stealthy Source-Manipulation Threats Against Multi-Source Anomaly Detectors

author.name: Indraveni Chebolu, Seema Panghal, Arnab Mallick, Ch A S Murty

entry.summary: The paper proposes a threat-quantification score, the task-conditioned visibility margin, measuring the least detector evidence an adversary must reveal per unit of downstream harm when manipulating multi-source anomaly detection pipelines. The margin has a closed form, fast certification (~85 microseconds), and yields minimum-evidence attacks validated on industrial telemetry. This addresses a real gap in adversarial robustness evaluation of fusion-based security systems.

entry.title: Words or Deeds? How LLMs Predict Users' Decisions in Human-Agent Dialogue

author.name: Baiqiao Zhang, Shuai Ma, Zhifeng Liao, Chao Zhou, Jianshu Wang, Yuhan Zhao, Chaoyue Zhang, Tongjun Si, Yuying Tang, Xiangxian Li, Yong-Jin Liu, Yulong Bian

entry.summary: Tests how eight open-weight LLMs predict users' decisions by combining stated promises with behavioral records, using 1,260 rounds in which 42 users played a repeated prisoner's dilemma-style game with five persona-prompted agents. Findings show decision records separate cooperation from defection better than verbal statements, relevant to agents that grant concessions based on user promises. Addresses strategic deception in human-agent dialogue.

entry.title: Learning to Read Braille: Benchmarking and Improving Braille Recognition Capabilities of VLMs

author.name: Kartik Jangra, Atharva Gawane, Siddharth Pulipaka, Hemachandran Karah, Raj Dabre

entry.summary: The paper introduces BrailleBench, a manually curated benchmark of 259 real-world Grade-1 and Grade-2 Braille images, showing that general-purpose and even OCR-specialized VLMs perform poorly at direct Braille transcription while tool-assisted systems do much better. The authors also build a synthetic Braille generation pipeline with which they train a 2B VLM reaching 87 percent exact match on Grade-1 and 61 percent on Grade-2. This exposes a genuine accessibility gap in current multimodal models.

entry.title: Training-Free Inference Acceleration for Video Large Language Models: Methods, Trade-offs, and Evaluation

author.name: Yuqi Li, Chuanyue Yan, Neil Rodrigues, Xianglong Wang, Xiaoqin Feng, Junming Liu, Xi Xiao, Zhongwei Cheng, Wei Li, Lin Chen, Yingli Tian

entry.summary: A survey of training-free inference acceleration techniques for video LLMs, organized by intervention stage in the inference pipeline: input, visual encoding, projector, prefill, and decoding, with post-training quantization treated as a cross-stage extension. It analyzes how intervention position affects the trade-off between evidence preservation and computational savings. This is a useful map of a rapidly growing area for practitioners deploying video models.

entry.title: Visual Autoregressive Generation with Next Token Imagination

author.name: Ruihang Jiang, Zongyao Zhao, Zhaolin Wang, Yuanwei Liu, Xiatian Zhu

entry.summary: This work argues that visual autoregressive generation is over-constrained by supervision on ground-truth next tokens only, and proposes letting the model imagine plausible unobserved continuations beyond the training data. It uses visual AR generation as a proof of concept for learning a broader slice of the visual distribution.

entry.title: Program-Level Adversarial Co-Adaptive Self-Play for Robotic Security

author.name: Leo Benaharon, Chi Zhang, Wei Zheng, Weifan Zhang, Yifan Wei

entry.summary: The paper presents a framework where coding agents iteratively generate attacks and defenses for robotic software at the program level using tested opponent code and mission feedback, without model fine-tuning. Two eight-generation case studies in autonomous driving and humanoid locomotion show concrete defensive adaptations but also that local recovery does not guarantee sustained robustness.

entry.title: Mimetic Embodiment Transfer of Human-Humanoid Interaction from In-the-Wild Videos

author.name: Nghia Le (Hann), Khang Nguyen (Hann), Ba Long Tran (Hann), Thi Quynh Nhu Pham (Hann), Binh Nguyen (Hann), Tuong Do (Hann), Erman Tjiputra (Hann), Hoan Nguyen (Hann), Tung D. Ta (Hann), Baoru Huang (Hann), Hai-Nguyen (Hann), Nguyen (Hann), Anh Nguyen

entry.summary: HumiTransfer converts in-the-wild videos of human-human interactions such as hugging and dancing into physically plausible human-humanoid interactions, reconstructing 3D motion with foot-ground contact and transferring one participant to a target humanoid embodiment. The approach aims to generalize across humanoid morphologies with different kinematic constraints.

entry.title: RAVEN: A Unified Active SLAM System for Rapid Autonomous Visual Exploration with Aerial Robots under Localization Uncertainty

author.name: Xinyi Chen, Yichen Zhang, Chenxing Jiang, Shaojie Shen

entry.summary: RAVEN is a unified active SLAM framework for agile aerial robots that balances exploring unknown space against exploiting visited regions for active loop closures, adapting performance to task-specific priorities under localization drift. It extends a line of active SLAM work largely developed on ground robots to the more demanding aerial setting, from Shaojie Shen's group.

entry.title: AuRaSim: A Ray-Tracing Based Automotive FMCW Radar Simulator for Dynamic Scenarios

author.name: Zhaoze Wang, Changxu Zhang, Tai Fei, Christopher Grimm, Yi Jin, Claas Tebruegge, Markus Gardill

entry.summary: AuRaSim is an open, ray-tracing-based simulator for automotive FMCW radar in dynamic scenarios, built on Blender to handle dynamic scenes while modeling electromagnetic material properties, antennas, and coherent signal synthesis. Automotive radar simulation has lagged behind camera and LiDAR simulation due to proprietary or overly simplified tools. This enables scalable annotated radar data generation for perception research.

entry.title: Counting the Bandages: On measuring the time that AI saves

author.name: Solomon Shalom Lijo

entry.summary: A conceptual/analytical paper arguing that AI time savings should be measured counterfactually alongside escaped defects rather than by raw clock time. It defines model-free quantities (time saved, excess escaped defects) and a break-even defect cost, showing that a calibrated checker's defect-escape rate does not improve with better models until checking can be dropped entirely.

entry.title: WAKMan: Workload Aware KVCache Manager

author.name: Suhas Kumar Morisetty, Vaibhavi Lokegaonkar, Sachin Mathew Varghese, Wesley Harris

entry.summary: WAKMan is a workload-aware KV-cache eviction policy for LLM servers exploiting prefix caching, showing across 20 traffic mixes that no single policy (LRU, LFU, etc.) is always best since agentic steps favor recency while popular prompts and long conversations favor frequency. The manager adapts eviction to observed workload composition.

entry.title: AC-JEPA: Anchored Cross-Modal Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Visual-to-Symbolic Translation

author.name: Chaofei Hong, Ziyang Chen, Baochen Wang, Christina Yi Jin, Qing Zhang

entry.summary: AC-JEPA is an SFT-compatible plug-in that extends JEPA-style representation-space objectives to cross-modal translation, predicting masked intermediate states to handle imperfect paired data in scientific domains. It combines token-level supervised objectives with representation-space prediction to be robust to errors in target sequences. This addresses the practical scarcity of clean cross-modal pairs.

entry.title: Follow the Herd: A Data-Driven Approach for Actionable Recourse

author.name: Nishtha Madaan, Srikanta Bedathur

entry.summary: DDAR provides actionable recourse in ML decisions without expensive human-designed cost functions, exploiting the idea that highly likely trajectories in historical user data correspond to lower-cost actions. It builds a dynamics model from data and searches for low-cost achievable actions. This removes a key bottleneck in algorithmic recourse for consequential decisions.

entry.title: RubricAtlas: Mining Type-Level Rubrics from Expert Reports to Evaluate Deep Research Agents

author.name: Delin Wang, Sinuo Wang, Rui Sun, Beidi Luan, Qiming Shi, Jing Li, Daxin Jiang, Zuo Bai

entry.summary: RubricAtlas derives type-level analytical requirements from expert reports within a research type, organizing binary checkpoints around recurring analytical questions to evaluate deep research agent outputs. This moves beyond query-specific rubrics toward shared standards for analytical structure without prescribing answers.

entry.title: Aligning Institutional Power and Operational Ability

author.name: Andrea Marino, Giovanni Sileno, Thomas van Binsbergen, Tom van Engers

entry.summary: This arXiv paper proposes a formal framework for designing multi-agent AI systems whose normative structures (responsibilities, permissions, institutional powers) are aligned with the operational abilities agents actually possess. It introduces process-oriented modelling to detect incongruences such as unsatisfiable expectations and privilege escalation, offers repair strategies, and analyzes how the relationship between operational processes and institutional state shapes the lifecycle of normative positions. The work matters because agentic AI deployed in institutional settings needs principled mechanisms to ensure assigned duties are actually fulfillable, avoiding safety and governance failures.

entry.title: Beyond the Readout: A Latent Numerical Frame Shared Across Modality and Operation

author.name: Oriol Juan Sabater, Alex Ferrando de las Morenas, Pau Rodr\'iguez, Xavier Suau

entry.summary: Using causal interventions in Gemma4-12B-it, the authors learn small subspaces of the residual stream where swapping coordinates swaps arithmetic answers, testing whether text and image arithmetic share one internal number representation. The subspaces reveal whether numbers are written along the same directions across modality and operation. This is careful mechanistic interpretability work on multimodal numerical cognition.

entry.title: ResCom: Activation Residual Compensation for Large Language Model Quantization

author.name: Ning Yang, Bohan Cui, Zhuowen Liu, Yuting Wang

entry.summary: ResCom proposes a low-rank correction for low-bit weight-activation quantization in LLMs that compensates for layer-output error using the activation rounding residual, with an output-aware calibration that selects residual directions in closed form without gradient training or modifying calibrated weights. On Llama-3-8B with 4-bit weights and activations, rank-32 attention corrections reduce WikiText-2 perplexity. This matters for efficient LLM deployment by improving post-calibration accuracy at minimal overhead.

entry.title: cuArms: GPU-Accelerated Conflict-Based Planning for Multi-Arm Manipulation

author.name: Philip Huang, Fabio Ramos, Jiaoyang Li, Caelan Garrett, Lars Johannsmeier

entry.summary: cuArms is a conflict-based multi-robot motion planner co-designed with GPU parallelism, using reusable multi-modal roadmaps per robot and lazy conflict/deadlock resolution to jointly plan motions for multiple arms in shared workcells. It addresses the slowness and poor scaling of prior task-allocation, joint-planning, and learned-policy approaches.

entry.title: Full Collapse Is Suboptimal: Controlled Partial Neural Collapse for Long-Tailed Recognition

author.name: Hyeontaek Hwang, Cheonghwan Hur, Daeyoung Kim

entry.summary: Argues that forcing tail classes into full neural collapse on an ETF target over-contracts their features and harms generalization in long-tailed recognition. Proposes a controlled partial-collapse regime via a Class-Adaptive Sparse Activation classifier and an ETF-constrained adaptive margin loss, letting tail classes retain within-class diversity while head classes collapse.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Behaviorally Adequate Test Generation from Software Requirements

author.name: Binhang Qi, Yiming Liu, Yun Lin, Yangjie Zhou, Hailong Sun, Jin Song Dong

entry.summary: Introduces Req2Test-Bench, a benchmark of 5,086 execution-validated test-generation instances recovered from developer-authored behavior-driven artifacts, evaluating whether LLM agents can generate tests that validate required behavior when the implementation is withheld. This shifts test-generation evaluation from white-box settings to requirement-to-test semantic alignment.

entry.title: AdaGround: Token-Normalized Adaptive Zooming with Verifier-in-the-Loop Refinement for GUI Grounding

author.name: Bingchao Wang, Yongcheng Jing, Chengyu Wang, Jun Huang, Jie Yang, Wei Liu, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: AdaGround is a training-free framework for GUI grounding on high-resolution screens that adapts zoom magnification and field of view to the model's own target-size estimate, and uses a Yes/No verifier to keep, reject, or re-run zoom chains with abstention. This matters for improving computer-use agents on small UI elements without additional training.

entry.title: A First-Step Bias Restores Lost Diversity in Diffusion Model Distillation

author.name: Wenwu Tang, Dong Wang, Yun Cheng, Olga Saukh

entry.summary: The paper localizes where distribution-matching distillation loses output diversity: the largest drop in sensitivity to initial noise occurs at the first, high-noise denoising step. Replacing only that first step with the teacher's trajectory restores most diversity, motivating ReSeed, a post-distillation intervention applied to existing distilled models.

entry.title: MRI-to-CT Translation of Spinal Images via Anatomy-Guided Pseudo-Pairing and Adversarial Diffusion

author.name: Eduardo Nieto, Ibai Genua, Davide Scorza, Karen L\'opez-Linares

entry.summary: This paper presents a three-stage pipeline for synthesizing CT images from spinal MRI scans, aiming to reduce radiation exposure and simplify preoperative surgical planning. The approach creates pseudo-paired training data by matching and registering similar MRI and CT slices using spine segmentations, then trains an adversarial diffusion model for the translation, followed by 3D volume assembly and refinement. It addresses a practical clinical bottleneck where MRI is common for diagnosis but CT is still needed for bone visualization.

entry.title: AnalogScout: Simulation-Efficient PVT-Aware Analog Sizing with LLM Agents

author.name: Yichen Long, Keren Zhu

entry.summary: AnalogScout is an LLM-agent system for analog circuit sizing that respects process, voltage, and temperature corners while conserving expensive SPICE simulation budget. Instead of learning circuit responses through repeated multi-corner simulations, the agent reuses verified designs and computes sizing sub-blocks analytically, enabling more efficient search toward tape-out-ready designs.

entry.title: Test-Time Communication in Trading Agent Swarms

author.name: Avid Fayaz, Harry Zhang, H{\aa}vard Alstadheim, Erik Nordl\"of, Vilhelm Karlin, Andr\'e Silva

entry.summary: A large empirical study of 200 LLM agents from four model families trading US markets over seven days under five communication regimes, from isolation to shared notes. It finds that communication causes herding (agents converging on the same stocks) in some families and links a group's return profile to its interaction dynamics, framing trading swarms as independent decision-makers where convergence is a risk, not a goal.

entry.title: Kinematic Constraint-Referenced Evaluation for Articulated Object Manipulation

author.name: Baptiste Bonin, Caro Strickland, Audrey Durand

entry.summary: The paper introduces Constraint-Referenced Strategy (CRS), which projects commanded end-effector motion onto an object's joint axis to separate genuine progress along the joint from off-constraint motion, replacing binary success metrics. Across 74 simulated articulated objects, CRS assigns distinct signatures to transfer failures that binary success merely registers as lower rates, revealing e.g. that a door-trained policy opening drawers may be succeeding for the wrong reasons.

entry.title: Condition-Enhanced Generative Adversarial Network for Aerodynamic Configuration Design of Commercial Aircraft

author.name: Youzheng Yu, Jiaqing Kou, Weiwei Zhang

entry.summary: CEGAN embeds geometric and aerodynamic conditioning into a GAN for generating commercial aircraft aerodynamic configurations, using a condition-informed loss combining geometry-guided feasibility penalties with surrogate-evaluated aerodynamic performance penalties, plus output filtering of infeasible designs. This enables end-to-end generative aerodynamic design optimization.

entry.title: Jaxnasium: Embracing PyTrees For Any-Agent, Cross-Suite Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Koen Ponse, Aske Plaat, Thomas M. Moerland

entry.summary: Jaxnasium is a JAX-based reinforcement learning library that represents observation and action spaces as PyTrees, enabling near-single-file algorithm implementations that run across discrete, continuous, multi-agent, and cross-suite settings. It aims to reduce fragmentation in the hardware-accelerated RL ecosystem.

entry.title: Learning atomic interactions for the thermodynamics of liquid mixtures

author.name: Marco Hoffmann, Sebastian Schmitt, Hans Hasse, Fabian Jirasek

entry.summary: Introduces COGNAC, a graph neural network that learns atom-level geometry and neighborhood-dependent interaction parameters evaluated within the classic UNIFAC framework for activity coefficients. Trained on roughly 820,000 experimental data points, it substantially outperforms UNIFAC while remaining compatible with existing process simulation tools. Bridges modern GNNs with industrially entrenched thermodynamic models.

entry.title: Tail Cues, Principal Corrections: Plug-and-Play Rectification for Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Yingkai Yang, Chaoqi Chen, Hui Huang

entry.summary: Presents TALOR, a lightweight backward-free module for open-set test-time adaptation that uses the source linear head as a geometric anchor, decomposing features into high-gain principal and low-gain tail coordinates. It applies a soft-routed affine correction in the principal subspace with a tail-conditioned slope, avoiding costly parameter updates or mutable memories vulnerable to unknown samples.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Flow Matching: A Generative AI Framework for Global Total Electron Content Forecasting

author.name: Si-Tong Yang, Feng Ye, Xian Lu, Dong Lin, Benjamin C. Martinez

entry.summary: This paper proposes a physics-guided flow matching framework for day-ahead global total electron content (TEC) forecasting, important for space weather monitoring and satellite communication reliability. It embeds ionospheric dynamics expressed as a PDE into the generative transformation so physical knowledge steers how samples evolve toward the target distribution. The work demonstrates a concrete way to couple scientific domain constraints with modern generative modeling.

entry.title: EnvSched: Environment-Aware Scheduling for Rollout-Efficient Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Sihan Yang, Weichen Bai, Ruichuan An, Yiming Cheng, Zhiyuan Feng, Tianyi Jiang, Renye Yan, Ning Ding, Yifan Zhang, Renrui Zhang, Yehui Tang, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: EnvSched is an online scheduler for agentic RL that organizes, evaluates, and schedules task instances together with the executable environments providing their tools, states, and verification, learning from rollout history. It balances exploitation of tasks likely to yield informative reward differences with coverage of the task distribution. This targets the rising cost of generating and verifying rollouts as agent environments scale.

entry.title: FinLLM-KG: Knowledge Graph-Enhanced LLMs for Financial Sentiment Analysis in Algorithmic Trading

author.name: Giorgos Iacovides, Oliver Hannibal, Wuyang Zhou, Danilo Mandic

entry.summary: Presents FinLLM-KG, a model-agnostic framework that augments causal LLMs with a financial knowledge graph built from SEC 10-K filings, injecting temporally grounded company-level context at inference time without weight updates. Context is provided as natural-language company profiles or structured graph information. Addresses the isolation and opacity of per-article financial sentiment prediction.

entry.title: SMEBENCH: Benchmarking Neural Music Editing with Synthetized MIDI Edits

author.name: Matthieu Cervera, Francesco Paissan, Micael Antunes, Mirco Ravanelli, Ricard Marxer, Cem Subakan

entry.summary: SMEBench is a large-scale benchmark of controlled music edits built by modifying symbolic MIDI performances and rendering matched source/target audio pairs, covering twelve instrumentation, articulation, dynamics, and pitch operations with a 3,600-example test set plus a real-audio complement. It enables separate measurement of edit fulfillment and content preservation, which prior evaluations could not disentangle. A valuable community resource for music generation research.

entry.title: Systematic Morphometric Brain Autoencoding for Representation Learning in Neurodegenerative Diseases

author.name: Nuria Balb\'as-Esteban, Albert Belenguer-Llorens, Elaheh Moradi, Jussi Tohka, Vanessa G\'omez-Verdejo, Carlos Sevilla-Salcedo

entry.summary: SYMBA is a self-supervised pretraining framework designed specifically for structural brain MRI, replacing natural-image-style contrastive or voxel-wise masked reconstruction with objectives capturing distributed morphometric patterns of neurodegeneration. It targets early disease identification despite limited annotations and scanner-induced distribution shift. A thoughtful domain-specific alternative to transplanting natural-image SSL paradigms.

entry.title: An end-to-end framework for uncertainty-aware validation of generative models

author.name: Giada Badaracco, Sean Benevedes, Christina Reissel, Philip Harris, Gaia Grosso

entry.summary: The paper proposes SIGMA, an end-to-end framework combining density estimation with uncertainty quantification for validating generative models in the physical sciences, such as background estimation in particle physics. It addresses the flaw that goodness-of-fit tests treating generative models as exact point-null hypotheses will eventually reject any model fitted to finite data. Propagating model uncertainty into statistical tests makes validation meaningful at scale.

entry.title: ETC-Bench: A Multilingual Benchmark for Evaluation-Side Transcript Canonicalization

author.name: Zhiheng Qian, Junhao Du, Jing Peng, Hanqi Li, Kunyang Peng, Feng Xue, Kai Yu

entry.summary: Formulates evaluation-side transcript canonicalization (ETC): mapping multiple surface transcript forms to a single canonical form when differences are not determined by the speech signal. ETC-Bench covers 181 phenomenon types across 12 languages using minimal-pair instances, and proposes SENA, a semantic-preserving exact-match normalization metric. First comprehensive benchmark for this underexamined ASR evaluation problem.

entry.title: Text Generation in Low-Resource Languages Using Human-Curated Vocabularies

author.name: Michael Christlambert Sinanta (Independent Researcher), Muhammad Dehan Al Kautsar (Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence), Amanda Nurul Izzah (Independent Researcher), Thanh-Nhi Nguyen (Independent Researcher), Phan Phuong Mai Chau (Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence), Zheng Wei Lim (University of Amsterdam), Fajri Koto (Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence)

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs can generate coherent text in extremely low-resource or entirely unseen languages by leveraging human-curated vocabularies plus a small number of human-written exemplars providing syntactic signals, with constrained sampling. Targets languages absent from pretraining data where standard synthetic-data generation fails. Includes authors from MBZUAI with relevant low-resource NLP expertise.

entry.title: PrinGS: Privacy Preservation in Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Gaurav Behera, Abhinav Raundhal, Archisha Panda, Saumya Balina, Gargi Shroff, Ponnurangam Kumaraguru

entry.summary: PrinGS addresses privacy leakage in 3D Gaussian Splatting by directly anonymizing trained splats: given a splat and a reference view identifying sensitive content such as faces or license plates, it localizes corresponding regions in the 3D representation and modifies them. This tackles a growing concern as 3DGS becomes the default scene representation and trained assets are shared. The representation-level approach avoids retraining from source imagery.

entry.title: ARISE: Authentic Reference-Informed Stability Enhancement for Continual Multimodal Forgery Detection

author.name: Yuchen Zhang, Yaxiong Wang, Yujiao Wu, Lianwei Wu, Qi Zhang, Li Zhu, Chaofeng Dong, Le Wu, Zhedong Zheng

entry.summary: ARISE formulates attack-incremental continual multimodal forgery detection, where new attack types must be learned without forgetting old ones while the real/fake interface stays fixed, and introduces Fable-Bench with joint-modality, text-side, and image-side attack-evolution protocols. The method uses authentic references for stability enhancement. As generative models proliferate, continual robustness of detectors is an increasingly important problem.

entry.title: GeoGSplat: Geometry-Grounded Non-Pixel-Aligned Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jiale Wang, Chen Zhao, Haoyang Zhang, Yanhao Wu, Fei He, Yanhu Shan, Rui Wu, Wei Ke, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: GeoGSplat is a feed-forward Gaussian Splatting model that grounds non-pixel-aligned prediction in geometric priors to avoid misplaced Gaussian centers under large viewpoint changes. A dual-branch encoder with Anchors and Triplane representations captures coarse 3D structure and fine details while keeping primitive counts fixed.

entry.title: Learning to Code the World: Harness Evolution for Compositional 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Haoyu Yao, Chenguo Lin, Ruize Du, Yadong Mu

entry.summary: SceneEvolve represents 3D scenes as executable code via SceneAct, a compositional semantic action interface, and improves reconstruction by evolving the harness around a fixed small open-source agent using a stronger teacher and feedback from development-set reconstructions. Model parameters, action semantics, and execution backend remain fixed during harness evolution.

entry.title: VGIQA: Fine-Grained Image Quality Assessment with Visual Grounding Rewards

author.name: Weichang Wang, Liyu Chen, Shuyue Guan, Jie Hu, Fei Gao, Wei Li, Nannan Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces VGIQA, a multi-modal LLM-based image quality assessment model that provides both local and global quality evaluations, addressing the limitation of prior MLLM-based IQA methods that only produce holistic image-level scores. It combines chain-of-thought reasoning and reinforcement learning with novel visual grounding rewards to yield fine-grained, localized, and interpretable quality assessments.

entry.title: When Slides Met Scans: Cross-Attention for Renal Cancer Prognosis

author.name: Anusha Krishnamoorthy, Basudha Pal

entry.summary: The paper fuses histopathology and CT imaging via bidirectional cross-attention between histology prototypes and kidney-centered CT tokens from frozen foundation models to predict disease-specific survival in renal cancer. It achieves the best average C-index and AUROC among baselines on TCGA-KIRC with external validation on CPTAC-CCRCC.

entry.title: SVIn+: Multi-Modal Framework for Robust Underwater State Estimation using 3D Sonar, Visual-Inertial, Water-Pressure, and DVL

author.name: Chinmay Burgul, Xiaoming Zhao, Yewei Huang, Michalis Chatzispyrou, Marios Xanthidis, Ioannis Rekleitis, Alberto Quattrini Li

entry.summary: SVIn+ extends an open-source visual-inertial SLAM system for autonomous underwater vehicles by fusing IMU, camera, water-pressure, Doppler velocity log, and compact 3D sonar data. Robust state estimation in low-visibility underwater conditions is a key enabler for scalable AUV autonomy in mapping and navigation.

entry.title: Omni-IGN: Onboard Image-Goal Navigation for Drones with Omnidirectional Vision

author.name: Zichen Yan, Rui Huang, Shenao Wang, Yucong Wang, Nuthasith Gerdpratoom, Lin Zhao

entry.summary: Omni-IGN is a fully onboard image-goal navigation system for drones combining quad-fisheye omnidirectional perception, an attention-based RL policy, and a collision-aware safety layer. Omnidirectional views remove the need for extra rotation and exploration required by single-view aerial ImageNav methods under tight compute budgets.

entry.title: Acoustic Signature Optimisation for Bioinspired Flapping-Wing Micro Aerial Vehicles

author.name: Yi Lun Duh, Krispin C. V. Broers, Sophie F. Armanini

entry.summary: This paper tackles the problem that engineered flapping-wing micro air vehicles are 15-30 dB louder than the animals they imitate. The authors model the impulsive click produced at stroke reversal as a membrane snap-through and use it to optimize wing venation, achieving up to 8 dB noise reduction in manufactured prototypes. This matters for deploying quiet bioinspired drones in noise-sensitive settings.

entry.title: Compatibility and future-proof testing for multi-agent systems

author.name: Yueshan Li, Lorenzo Fiaschi, Andrea Censi, Emilio Frazzoli

entry.summary: The paper proposes a bi-level regulatory structure for independently developed autonomous agents, where a regulator publishes seed agents and developers test compatibility with all seed-compatible agents, a property called future-proofness. This avoids unrealistic centralized specification design when agent implementations are confidential. It is a conceptual framework for guaranteeing joint safety of heterogeneous agents in shared environments.

entry.title: Agentic Distributional Regression: Conditional Density Estimation through Agent-Written Programs

author.name: Lorenzo Tedesco (University of Bergamo)

entry.summary: Proposes a method where a language-model agent writes short, inspectable programs to estimate conditional densities from iid samples, drawing from a library of parametric distributions, mixtures, and factorizations with covariate-dependent parameters. The resulting estimator is an explicit, independently evaluable formula while the agent handles model structure and fitting choices.

entry.title: BehaveRec: When Does Long-Term Behavioral History Help Sequential Recommendation? A Study with Session, History, and Community Signals

author.name: Aysenur Inan, Reza Yousefi Maragheh, Jayesh Uddhav Kudase, Selene Xu, Kaushiki Nag, Jianpeng Xu, Sushant Kumar

entry.summary: BehaveRec combines a causal session transformer, a bidirectional 90-day user history encoder, and a GraphSAGE community module built on behavioral embedding similarity, blended per user by a learned gate. On an industrial dataset of 137M sequences from 12.6M users it improves R@5 by +3.2% over SASRec and studies when long-term signals actually help.

entry.title: kw-bench: Breaking Frontier Harnesses on Real-World Tasks

author.name: George Juraj Salapa

entry.summary: kw-bench is a benchmark testing coding-agent harnesses on investigative knowledge work (audit, tax, due diligence, regulatory reporting) where answers already exist in incomplete, inconsistent evidence, contrasting with generative rubric-judged benchmarks. It probes where frontier-model harnesses fail on real-world investigative tasks.

entry.title: Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yipeng Hao, Yuxuan Cai, Wenkai Ji, Jie Zhou, Liyang Yu, Qin Chen, Zhiguo Yan, Shulei Zheng, Liang He

entry.summary: DiscernMem is a training-free framework for LLM multi-agent memory that both refines defective memories (comparing team outcomes with and without a memory to diagnose rule defects) and learns when each memory should be applied via boundary-learning meta-memory. It recognizes that stored advice can be flawed or misapplied and that team-level success signals are unreliable for memory correction. This improves experience reuse in multi-agent systems.

entry.title: OpenGray: a benchmark for evaluating the decisions of radiotherapy planning agents

author.name: Humza Nusrat, Kundan Thind

entry.summary: OpenGray extends the OpenKBP-Opt head-and-neck dataset with radiotherapy planning tasks that have known correct decisions, including proven-incompatible dose-goal contradictions and feasible controls, to evaluate LLM-based planning agents on decision quality rather than dose alone. Four systems, from rule-based scripts to LLM agents (including a local Ministral 3 8B, an existing model), were evaluated on 30 patients.

entry.title: Agent-Conditioned Routing: Diverse Reasoning Paths Within One Frozen Model

author.name: Ananth Kalyanasundaram, Ankush Kadu, Athira Gopal, Aswanth Krishnan

entry.summary: Agent-Conditioned Routing elicits diverse reasoning trajectories from a single frozen sparse MoE model by assigning persistent, untrained expert-eligibility masks while preserving the learned token router. On a 126-question math and physics benchmark with full-derivation model judges, it counts problems yielding genuinely distinct solution modes without fine-tuning or multiple model copies. This is a clever inference-time diversity technique relevant to best-of-n and exploration.

entry.title: Physiognomy Revisited: How Vision-Language Models Encode Sensitive Attributes Through Image Transformation

author.name: Soumyajit Datta, Arka Dutta, Ashiqur R. KhudaBukhsh

entry.summary: The authors audit two well-known vision-language models and find they often comply with requests to transform face images to reflect race identities or sexual orientation, with compliance being non-deterministic, group-sensitive, and producing statistically differentiated outputs. This exposes a harmful, physiognomy-like failure mode that disparately affects vulnerable communities. It is timely AI fairness and safety auditing work.

entry.title: DuplexTune: Coupled-State Replay for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Adaptation

author.name: Paul Raj, Simon Caldwell, Daniel Whitmore, Mutlu Mete

entry.summary: DuplexTune is a memory-efficient adaptation framework for MoE LLMs that replays coupled hidden states through pretrained attention and expert modules using trainable width bridges between two residual streams, with bridge warm-up and frozen routers. On Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B it cuts peak memory from 64.8 GB to 38.8 GB versus supervised fine-tuning with checkpointing while improving throughput and achieving 67.2% MMLU and 75.6% GSM8K. It addresses the real problem that sparse execution does not eliminate stored activation state for adaptation.

entry.title: BUSTA: Teaching Small Language Models to Reason About Binary Execution

author.name: Ritika Poddar, Aidan Fennelly, Deirdre Murphy, Eric Wolos, Corre L. Steele, Michael Doyle

entry.summary: This NVIDIA-affiliated work trains small open models, fine-tuning Qwen3-1.7B and Nemotron-3-Nano (both established models) with GRPO on inverse basic-block execution tasks, where the model predicts input register values that produce a given x86-64 output state. The goal is to transfer reverse-engineering reasoning skills to resource-constrained models suitable for sandboxed RE environments.

entry.title: RoboAuto: Autonomous Robot Program Search through Multi-Level Physical Understanding

author.name: Buzhao Liu, Jianing Ye, Xiu Yuan, Yangtong Feng, Chengsong Huang, Tyler Dinh, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik, Ning Zhang, Chongjie Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces RoboAuto, a framework for LLM-driven robot program search that explicitly organizes physical understanding at the object, scene, and interaction levels, rather than relying solely on execution feedback. The multi-level components help agents reason about manipulation affordances, geometric constraints, and why interactions fail.

entry.title: TOPS: Reshaping Flow Source and Transport for Multi-Task Robot Manipulation

author.name: Tuo An, Chuhao Zhou, Jiahua Dong, Jingliang Li, Jiaqi Bai, Jindou Jia, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: Proposes TOPS, which adapts the flow-matching source prior and interpolation schedule per task for language-conditioned multi-task manipulation, building multimodal task sources from reverse-mapped expert actions and modulating transition speed via source-target covariance mismatch, all without architecture changes. This addresses the limitation of shared Gaussian priors and linear transport paths across tasks with distinct motion requirements.

entry.title: LearnPrunerV2: Learnable Progressive Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Rinyoichi Takezoe, Yaqian Li, Weiren Wang, Zihao Bo, Huihong Shi, Anzhou Hou, Mo Guang, Jiale Yan, Kaiwen Long

entry.summary: LearnPrunerV2 extends a prior two-stage heuristic token-pruning framework into a fully learnable architecture that adaptively prunes visual tokens across model depths, addressing unreliable pruning criteria and rigid schedules in VLMs. This matters because massive visual token counts are a dominant cost in vision-language model inference.

entry.title: When Is a Relation Worth Trusting? Manipulation Costs, Exposure, and the Trust Trap in Multi-Relational Graph Learning

author.name: Vincess Dongmo, Astride Melvin Fokam Ninyim

entry.summary: The paper analyzes when using a relation in multi-relational graph detectors is worse than ignoring it, given that adversaries pay different costs to manipulate different relations. It proves degree gating strictly beats any selection or reweighting under sharp conditions, validates this on real graphs, and derives per-node exposure bounds indicating which relation a platform should harden.

entry.title: Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data

author.name: Geunhyoung Kim, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: The authors show that channel selection for MoE expert weight loading, previously assumed to require offline-calibrated thresholds, needs no calibration data. They demonstrate that calibrated thresholds miss read budgets in practice and analyze top-k alternatives, enabling input-adaptive channel selection that controls exactly how many expert weight channels are read during decoding.

entry.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Joseph Natter, Long Vu, Yifan Zhang, Bobin Deng, Kun Suo, Rui Wu

entry.summary: GAS-PFN extends prior-data fitted networks to traffic forecasting by encoding graph-structured road topology into synthetic training priors, enabling zero-shot deployment to new or evolving sensor networks without per-dataset retraining. This combines graph-aware spatiotemporal modeling with in-context learning from synthetic tasks.

entry.title: Folding Attention Biases into Keys Makes Compacted KV Caches Run on Standard Kernels

author.name: Utkarsh Kanwat

entry.summary: Solves a deployment problem for Attention Matching-based KV cache compression by folding per-key logit biases into the keys themselves along a closed-form per-head direction, producing a plain cache compatible with FlashAttention and vLLM without special kernels. Folded caches match unmodified vLLM/HuggingFace outputs on Qwen3-4B and largely on Qwen3-14B LongBench samples at equal budgets. A practical efficiency contribution for long-context inference on existing models.

entry.title: LLM knowledge for improved Out-of-Distribution Tabular Prediction - A Cross-Validated Regularisation Approach

author.name: S{\o}lve Langseth, Kristoffer Herland Hellton, Hugo L. Hammer

entry.summary: Tests whether coefficient priors elicited from LLMs can serve as shrinkage targets in regularized regression for out-of-distribution tabular prediction, replacing the default target of zero. Priors improve OOD mean squared error on four of five real covariate-split datasets by up to 7.9%, with provider and prior structure selected via source-domain cross-validation alone.

entry.title: Compote: Collapse-Resistant Multiple Hypothesis Learning For Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Louis Castres Saint Martin, Clement Calauzenes, Alain Rakotomamonjy, Patrick Gallinari

entry.summary: Introduces COMPOTE, a multi-hypothesis transformer for sequential recommendation trained with an annealed objective shifting from uniform supervision to winner-takes-all assignment, forcing hypotheses to specialize into distinct catalogue regions. Theoretical analysis shows population-optimal solutions partition the conditional next-item distribution, and inference uses an efficient normalizer-free max-similarity rule.

entry.title: TRIDENT-Seq: Profile-Matched Prefix-Future Contrast for Label-Efficient Payment Risk Modeling

author.name: Weiyu Han, Haoyu Jiang, Jie Sheng, Ruobing Zuo, Huilin He, Ze Zhao, Xiao Tan, Nairong Zhang, Shuai Chen, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: From Ant International, TRIDENT-Seq is a transaction foundation model pretrained with Prefix-Future Contrast, which matches transaction prefixes to profiled summaries of future behavior to avoid trivially exploiting coarse activity differences in contrastive learning. It addresses scarce, delayed, business-specific fraud and chargeback labels by learning a single encoder transferable across payment businesses. The work tackles a real industrial risk-modeling problem at scale.

entry.title: Approximation Families and the Statistical Efficiency of Denoising Score Matching

author.name: Brian Miyatake

entry.summary: Studies score matching over approximation spaces built from eigenfunctions of diffusion generators, showing that under Ornstein-Uhlenbeck flow the asymptotic score-estimation variance grows exponentially along a subsequence of polynomial degrees for non-Gaussian targets. An operator-informed variant that averages the loss under the diffusion semigroup reduces but does not eliminate this growth. Gives theoretical insight into statistical limits of score matching underlying diffusion models.

entry.title: Variable-Length Feedback Coding With Universal Decoding and Bandit Channel Selection

author.name: Recep Can Yavas

entry.summary: This information theory paper introduces the VLF-Bandit problem, combining variable-length feedback coding, universal decoding, and bandit-based channel selection over AWGN channels with unknown noise variances. Two joint coding and channel-selection schemes are developed, including a single-phase VLSF scheme based on Gaussian random codebooks and likelihood-mixture scores. A novel problem formulation at the interface of coding theory and online learning.

entry.title: Is Token Confidence Just Chain Length? A Signal-Processing Audit of Reasoning Traces

author.name: Pragna Mallappa

entry.summary: Audits the popular token-confidence-based chain selection method for reasoning models by treating per-token confidence as a signal and applying spectral analysis and change-point detection. Samples 16 chains for each of 500 math problems to test whether confidence signals carry information beyond chain length. Questions whether widely used confidence-based early-stopping heuristics are actually measuring what is claimed.

entry.title: Decision Models as Judges for Hallucination Detection

author.name: Haozheng Liu, Zhaoqian Xue, Zhongyin Wang, Junting Mu, Zihui Ma, Shuya Feng, Lingyao Li

entry.summary: Builds binary benchmarks for five hallucination types (9,852 items from six datasets) and compares five decision models against the generative judge GPT-6-Sol, an existing commercial model released in September 2026. Performance is type-dependent: the best decision model matches GPT-6-Sol on context inconsistency, comes within 3 points on factual errors, but trails by 4-8 points on logical and other types. Quantifies when cheap classification head judges can substitute for generative LLM judges.

entry.title: QESChunker: A Single Objective Unifies Overlapping and Non-Overlapping Chunking for RAG

author.name: Yifan Zhao, Qianyang Zhao, Xinyu Guan, kai wei, Yuming Deng

entry.summary: QESChunker is the first method to construct static chunk indices for retrieval-augmented generation from question-evidence supervision, formulating both overlapping and non-overlapping chunking as a unified utility-maximization objective over question-evidence pairs. This replaces heuristic chunking with supervised combinatorial optimization without access to test queries. Chunking quality is a known lever on RAG performance, so a principled formulation is welcome.

entry.title: MVRCap: Towards Comprehensive Video Captioning via Hierarchical Multi-Dimensional Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Weihuang Lin, Xianing Chen, Zhibin Wang, Congzhi Zhang, Yiwei Ma, Jiayi Ji, Miao Chen, Jun Song, YuCheng, Bo Zheng, Xiaoshuai Sun, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: MVRCap reformulates video captioning as reinforcement learning steered by structured verification, using a Fine-Grained Verifiable Reward with pillars including hierarchical concept coverage (supported by a new MVRCap-QA dataset) to enforce visual-semantic alignment and capture spatial-temporal dynamics and logical intent.

entry.title: GPA-VGGT: Geometry-Preserving Acceleration of VGGT

author.name: Muyeol Sung, Jangwon Kim, Jongwoo Lim

entry.summary: GPA-VGGT accelerates the feed-forward geometry model VGGT training-free by replacing global attention in early blocks with frame attention using a shared cross-frame K/V set, and merging only keys and values (preserving queries) in later blocks. This avoids the accuracy drops of prior token-merging approaches.

entry.title: When Black-Box Robot Policies Fail: Online Sensor Diagnosis and Repair with a Transparent Surrogate

author.name: Marc Ziegler, Batu \"Ozen, Sami Mentes, Thomas Waschulzik, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: This work asks whether an external monitor can diagnose and repair corrupted sensor inputs around a frozen, inaccessible robot policy using a structured surrogate separating periodic gait from sensor-dependent corrections. On simulated Go2 quadruped locomotion, offline diagnosis substantially raises walking success and online repair recovers much of the loss without false triggers.

entry.title: Cost-based variable selection for prediction models

author.name: Lasai Barre\~nada, Andrew Vickers, Laure Wynants, Bieke Tack, Dirk Timmerman, Ewout Steyerberg, Ben Van Calster

entry.summary: This clinical-methodology paper introduces a decision-analytic variable selection algorithm based on net benefit rather than statistical fit, weighing prediction gains against the harm of measuring each variable (cost, time, risk, invasiveness). The algorithm compares net benefit across predictor combinations via cross-validation, with a backward-elimination extension for many predictors. It reframes feature selection for clinical prediction models in explicitly decision-theoretic terms.

entry.title: From Structural Feedback to Prompt Policies: Learning Faithful Text-to-Image Prompt Editors

author.name: Wentao Ye, Yali Ye, Zhiqing Xiao, Ru Peng, Xinpeng Ti, Liyao Li, Zhanming Shen, Peng Lu, Jie Zhang, Haobo Wang

entry.summary: StruPO is a structure-aware prompt editor for text-to-image models that uses a calibrated scene graph as shared representation for policy conditioning and image-grounded supervision, learning a reusable editing policy via token-aligned deletion, reordering, and insertion. It aims to improve generated images without changing the user's requested scene.

entry.title: Verifiable Efficiency Limits of Innate LLM Planning in Sliding Puzzles

author.name: Yezhou Cheng, Charles Ling

entry.summary: The paper isolates innate (tool-free, single-response) planning in LLMs using 4x4 sliding puzzles with a verifiable decomposed score SPE = R x Q x E covering execution reliability, plan coordination, and action economy, evaluated over 8,400 outputs across seven model conditions. Certified optima and trajectory replay allow precise measurement of planning limits without external search.

entry.title: MedConstBench: Benchmarking How Constitutions Steer LLMs in Medical Ethics

author.name: Yibo Yang, Zerui Huang, Haomiao Yang, Zixia Wang

entry.summary: MedConstBench treats a model's deployment constitution as a controlled variable to measure how ethical policies reshape LLM behavior in medical-ethics dilemmas, organized around Beauchamp's four biomedical principles. Unlike prior work that treats ethics as a fixed model property, it scores trade-offs between competing values. This is relevant to local medical LLM deployments where constitutions are the main governance lever.

entry.title: Natural Hard-Negative Mining from Positives for Instruction-Following Retrieval

author.name: Chaolang Li, Jingyu Li, Zhaocheng Du, Xuyang Xie, Gang Wang, Pengwen Dai

entry.summary: NHNM addresses scarce instruction-conditioned contrastive supervision in instruction-following information retrieval by repurposing original positive passages as natural hard negatives under query-compatible instructions. An automated pipeline of candidate cleaning, reversal construction, and geometry filtering produces compact, high-contrast training data.

entry.title: Proactive Memory for Event-Driven LLM Agents

author.name: Jinyang Li, Zichuan Fu, Xian Wu, Wenlin Zhang, Yimin Deng, Kaifeng Guo, Guojing Li, Junjia QI, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: ProactMem organizes agent memory into recent events, temporal trajectories, and behavioral regularities, validating trajectory facts against source events and regularities via historical replay before matching them to current conditions. The paper also contributes ProactStream, a longitudinal benchmark for proactive agents processing event streams.

entry.title: Clearing the FoG: Training KG Agents to Retrieve the Evidence Behind Their Answers

author.name: Zongyuan Sun, Shuai Zhao, Yingjun Du, Ke Shu, Ziyue Zhu, Haoran Luo

entry.summary: FoG trains knowledge-graph agents to retrieve the supporting triples behind their answers, not just produce correct answers, by building evidence-carrying training data and rewarding evidence quality alongside answer correctness. This makes agent answers traceable and auditable. It addresses a genuine gap where agents answer correctly without justifying retrieval.

entry.title: Generation and Verification: Human-Agent Collaboration for Safety-Critical Automotive Software Engineering

author.name: Elizaveta Zinovyeva, Aiham Taleb, Nikita Kozodoi, Daniel Schleicher, Amir Mahdi Namazi, Martin Kraus, Levent Kent, Brian Jensen

entry.summary: This paper presents a coding assistant for safety-critical automotive C/C++ exposing generate, edit, and verify tools via the Model Context Protocol, designed around verification-first workflows where every change must meet MISRA and AUTOSAR standards and trace to requirements. It tackles both the verification emphasis and the narrow-domain knowledge gap in general LLMs. It is a valuable case study of deploying coding agents under strict industrial compliance constraints.

entry.title: Beyond the Estimate: Wiener-Informed Decoding for Easier Training of Pixel-Space Flow Models

author.name: Ziqiao Wang, Yang You

entry.summary: The authors show that frozen Wiener estimates of coarse second-order image statistics make it substantially easier to learn velocity fields for pixel-space flow models, with gains beyond the linear predictions they explicitly provide. Wiener-informed Decoding (WiD) uses a trainable Wiener prediction path plus coefficient interfaces that inject features into the native decoder without modifying its blocks.

entry.title: ProCerDCL: Query-Efficient Black-Box Probabilistic Verification of Deep Learning Compiler Optimization

author.name: Zexin Li, Weibo Zhang, Linyi Li, Arvind Easwaran, Simin Chen

entry.summary: Presents a query-efficient framework for black-box probabilistic verification of deep-learning compiler optimizations, assessing whether a property violation probability falls below a threshold using a single sequential test with bounded error probabilities. It replaces interval-family baselines with a three-valued contract (accept, reject, inconclusive).

entry.title: The Vocabulary Is Already Here: Adapting Pretrained Interpretable Features for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Ziluowen Luo, Ruochen Liu, Jun Yin, Hao Yan, Zhengxuan Hu, Xinze Shi, Chaozhuo Li, Chengqi Zhang, Senzhang Wang

entry.summary: This paper observes that pretrained sparse autoencoder features with human-interpretable annotations can serve as a reusable semantic ID vocabulary for generative recommendation, avoiding costly vocabulary fitting. It tackles challenges of preserving item distinctions under compact token budgets and extending interpretability to retrieval dynamics. This matters because it links mechanistic interpretability artifacts to practical recommender systems.

entry.title: Generative Replay for Equilibrium Propagation: Toward Edge-Friendly Continual Learning in Hopfield Networks

author.name: Victor Cook (LIRMM | ADAC), Gilles Sassatelli (LIRMM | ADAC), Thierry Gil (LIRMM), Mohamed Watfa (LIRMM | ADAC), Marina Reyboz (CEA-LETI)

entry.summary: This work studies continual learning in Hopfield Networks trained with Equilibrium Propagation, an energy-based alternative to backpropagation suited to edge hardware. The proposed Energy-Based Generative Replay lets a single network act as both classifier and sample generator, mitigating catastrophic forgetting without external buffers or architectural additions.

entry.title: Beyond Answer Changes: Matched Same-Class Controls for Local Audio Evidence

author.name: Yunuo Wang, Maoyuan Chen, Yuanjin Huang, Xing Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces matched same-class replacement controls to disentangle whether audio-language models respond to a sound event's class or merely to waveform perturbation when tested via local edits. Across 600 synthetic soundscapes and three models, different-class replacements cause far more answer changes than same-class controls, indicating models partially rely on genuine class-level evidence rather than edit sensitivity.

entry.title: From Slices to Volumes: Comparing 2D, 2.5D, and 3D Residual Networks for Pulmonary Nodule Malignancy-Risk Classification

author.name: Bahodir Nazarov, Zineb Gharib, Fatima Zazoul

entry.summary: This controlled study compares 2D, 2.5D, and 3D residual networks for pulmonary nodule malignancy classification on a patient-disjoint LIDC-IDRI cohort of 2,654 nodules, evaluating momentum-contrast pretraining, mild augmentation, and exclusion of indeterminate ratings. Checkpoint selection used validation Macro-F1 across well-defined splits.

entry.title: A Graph-informed Kriging model for sample-efficient Bayesian optimization of wind farm layouts

author.name: Zhen-Fan Wang, Kai Zhang, Xianping Du, Zhaolong Han, Dai Zhou, Onur Bilgen

entry.summary: The authors develop a Graph-informed Kriging framework for wind farm layout optimization that embeds reusable aerodynamic interaction information into the surrogate mean function by representing the farm as a directed graph of pairwise turbine interactions in relative-coordinate space. This structured mean captures dominant AEP variation and improves sample efficiency in high-dimensional layout spaces.

entry.title: Bayesian Evidence Accumulation for Graph-Based Learning in Dynamic Data-Driven Applications Systems

author.name: Moises Ponce, Sarah Harkins Dayton, Ioannis Schizas, Vasileios Maroulas

entry.summary: B-EAGLe reformulates graph classification as a sequential evidence accumulation process, combining a GNN encoder with a Bayesian accumulator inspired by cortico-basal ganglia-thalamic circuits that updates posterior beliefs over class labels and commits only when sufficient confidence is reached. It targets Dynamic Data Driven Application Systems where observations arrive sequentially under uncertainty.

entry.title: AHEAD: Adaptive Neural Acceleration for Large-Scale Linear Programming

author.name: Sihao Liu, Zhichao Hou, Huayue Gu, Raiyan Rahman, Liang Wu, Ruozhou Yu, Xiaorui Liu

entry.summary: Proposes AHEAD, a neural accelerator for million-variable linear programs that improves on prior unrolled learned accelerators by adaptively allocating computation per instance rather than running identical layers everywhere. The design explicitly accounts for end-to-end solve time including learning inference cost, not just iteration count. Relevant to optimization at scale where first-order methods are slow to converge.

entry.title: PRISM: Pathology Reliability In Scarce-label Medicine. A Tile-level Benchmark of Pathology Foundation Models

author.name: Alicem Koyun

entry.summary: PRISM is a tile-level benchmark evaluating eight pathology foundation models (including CLIP, CONCH, UNI, Virchow2, GigaPath, H-Optimus-0) across 864 linear-probe runs spanning label fractions from 1% to 100%, calibration, and out-of-distribution transfer, including a five-hospital Camelyon17 study. It jointly measures reliability axes that are usually evaluated in isolation. Valuable for guiding foundation-model selection in low-label clinical settings.

entry.title: TACO-Graph: Automated Construction of Text-Atributed Graphs

author.name: Amiri Hayes, Kristina Wicke

entry.summary: Introduces TACO-Graph, a decision tree framework that automates the choice of graph construction (nodes, edges, node text) for text-attributed graphs built from multi-attribute tabular data. It enumerates valid graph representations and learns which construction choices best serve a downstream task, replacing manual expert trial-and-error.

entry.title: Structured Representation Probing for Risk Anticipation in End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jiawei Liang, Tianrui Lou, Le Yang, Xianghao Jiao, Wei Wang, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: The Structured Representation Probe (SRP) is a lightweight monitor that reads actor, ego, and map representations from a frozen end-to-end driving policy to anticipate upcoming failures. It learns per-source linear risk directions with cardinality-normalized pooling and uses event-window supervision linked to hard failures. This offers a safety monitoring interface for autonomous driving systems.

entry.title: The proton structure one mode at a time: a Neural Tangent Kernel analysis of a DIS fit

author.name: Amedeo Chiefa, Luigi Del Debbio, Richard Kenway

entry.summary: Analyzes training dynamics of a neural network fit of parton distribution functions from deep inelastic scattering data via an exact neural tangent kernel analysis, generalizing prior single-flavour gradient-flow integration to the multi-flavour case. The paper derives the Shapley value within its statistical framework and gives a geometric view of training. Bridges deep learning theory and phenomenological particle physics.

entry.title: From Biological Curves to Soft Modular Robots: Learning-Based Inverse Design with Uncertainty-Guided Refinement

author.name: Dixiang Wang, Minghao Zha, Arifur Rahman, Yinhong Qin, Yitao Jiang, Shiyang Lu, Zebing Mao, Muhao Chen, Luyang Zhao

entry.summary: This work presents a learning-based real-to-sim-to-real framework that translates biological shape-changing behaviors (eel-like swimming, inchworm arching) into configurations of cable-driven modular soft robots, using surrogate models and uncertainty-guided refinement to replace expensive physics-based search. It enables efficient inverse design for bioinspired robotics. Demonstrates practical learning application in robot design automation.

entry.title: No Tokenizer, Still a Gap: Cross-Lingual Fairness of Homoglyph and Invisible-Character Watermarking

author.name: Alexander Nemecek, Yuqiao Xu, Joseph Falkenburg, Erman Ayday

entry.summary: This paper evaluates edit-based text watermarks (homoglyph swaps and invisible-character insertion) that operate post-generation without model access, asking whether they avoid the cross-lingual performance gaps that plague tokenizer-dependent generation-time watermarks on low-resource languages. Across 40 language varieties in 24 scripts, it measures capacity, detectability, and quality trade-offs. The title indicates such watermarks still exhibit a fairness gap despite bypassing tokenizers.

entry.title: Weakness Localization Is Not Enough: State-Aware Recursive Knowledge Improvement for Large Language Models

author.name: Runze Jiang, Yan Wang, Boran Jin, Bingyu Zhu, Longtao Huang

entry.summary: Argues that evaluation-guided knowledge updating in LLMs suffers from knowledge-state aliasing: the same localized weakness may correspond to distinct operational states (knowledge absent, hard to access, or accessible but unused), each favoring different interventions. Proposes state-aware recursive knowledge improvement that distinguishes these states when deciding how to update. Reframes diagnostic localization as insufficient without state identification.

entry.title: DocXEval: A Systematic Evaluation of Explainability in Multimodal Document Understanding

author.name: Saifullah Saifullah, David Dembinsky, Stefan Agne, Andreas Dengel, Sheraz Ahmed

entry.summary: Presents the first comprehensive explainability framework tailored to multimodal document understanding, adapting existing XAI methods and evaluation metrics to combined text, layout, and image inputs, including efficient multi-target adaptations.
