Addresses the gap between strong document-AI performance and the black-box nature that blocks deployment in high-stakes sectors. Both a framework and benchmark-style contribution.

entry.title: Same Verdict, Different Readers: Personalizing Fact-Checking Explanations from Relative Preferences

author.name: Haokun Wen, Xuemeng Song, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: The paper formulates Faithful Personalized Fact-Checking Explanation Rewriting, which adapts fact-check explanations to individual readers while preserving factual fidelity, learning from preferences of LLM-simulated readers instead of reference explanations. The proposed PER framework tackles persona-specific preference separation and generalization beyond predefined explanation styles. This matters for making misinformation interventions more effective across diverse audiences.

entry.title: LingGS: Decoupling Feed-Forward Geometry Prediction from Camera Tracking for High-Fidelity Gaussian SLAM

author.name: Da Li, Yihan Zang, Ivan Viola, Zeyu Wang, Dominik Engel

entry.summary: LingGS is an online monocular RGB Gaussian Splatting SLAM system that uses a frozen streaming 3D foundation model as a virtual RGB-D sensor and an explicit geometric solver for camera tracking via feature reprojection, outperforming learned camera prediction. A streaming Gaussian mapper integrates observations into a dense scene representation.

entry.title: RePAIR: Inverting Backdoor Attacks in Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Arnold Brosch, Kira Maag

entry.summary: RePAIR is a post-hoc, label-free, attack-unaware defense against backdoor attacks in semantic segmentation, exploiting the observation that backdoor-induced shifts are stronger in the classifier head than internal representations, leaving recoverable victim-class semantics. It infers victim-target relations without retraining or model modification.

entry.title: ASPEN: Adaptive Semantic Reasoning via Command Persistence Prediction for Efficient Navigation VLAs

author.name: Vieri N. Akustia, Bin Hu

entry.summary: ASPEN is an event-triggered scheduler for navigation VLA policies that predicts whether a frozen base policy would reissue its previous command, reusing commands when persistence is likely and triggering costly semantic reasoning otherwise. A lightweight multimodal predictor combines observations, instructions, execution history, and cached VLA confidence.

entry.title: A Trainable CPG Framework for Quadruped Locomotion

author.name: Xiyan Liu, Yide Liu, Guoyong Mao, Shaoxing Qu

entry.summary: CPG-ENN combines a symmetry-based eight-neuron central pattern generator with a shared learned execution network to produce joint references for quadruped locomotion, modulated by a single feedback policy over interpretable trajectory variables. It handles walk, trot, pace, bound, and pronk gaits with smooth transitions without gait-specific controllers, reporting 99.39% transition success in simulation.

entry.title: Predict the Swing, Match the Speed: Robotic Pipe Stabbing With Learned Stereo Vision and Residual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mohamed Ashraf Mostafa, Taher El-Fakharany, Samir Khaled

entry.summary: StabBot is a robotic system for oilfield pipe stabbing that tracks swinging pipe joints with a pendulum Kalman filter over stereo images, uses a ResNet-18 keypoint network for 3D localization, and refines capture with a residual RL policy matched to the pipe's velocity. Evaluated on 200 paired random jobs across nine pipe sizes, it demonstrates full automation of a hazardous manual task. This is a strong example of applied perception-plus-RL in heavy industry.

entry.title: PDE-Based Bounds on Optimal Exponents in Active Simple Hypothesis Testing

author.name: Sushant Vijayan, Himadri Mandal

entry.summary: The paper derives general upper and lower bounds on the optimal error exponent for Active Simple Hypothesis Testing, combining a recent PDE characterization of the exponent with comparison principles for viscosity solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi PDEs. The bounds are parametrized by convex functions, sets, and lower Hamiltonian relaxations, generalizing many known results. This advances the theoretical understanding of a long-studied problem spanning bandits and information theory.

entry.title: OA-RAG: Ontology-based Agentic RAG for Faithful LLM Reasoning

author.name: Hui Yang, Jiaoyan Chen, Yongsheng Gao

entry.summary: OA-RAG integrates formal reasoning over domain ontologies with LLM reasoning in a retrieval-augmented agent, reporting ontology observations as evidence plus a model-assessed grounding level for each answer. It targets hallucination reduction in knowledge-intensive domains like biomedicine.

entry.title: CIVER: Causal Intervention Verification for Reliable Code Review

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Hasibul Haque, Jay Somasundaram, Ryan Turner, Bowen Zhu, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: CIVER tackles false positives in LLM-based code review agents by using causal intervention verification to distinguish actionable findings from unsupported claims, motivated by the flood of agent-generated contributions needing reliable review. It targets evidence quality in reviews rather than just generation quality. This addresses a timely reliability problem as agentic software development scales.

entry.title: Dense Representation Learning and Differentiable Shape Modeling for Spine Landmark Detection

author.name: Augustin Daridon, Sofiane Sifaoui, Ayman Assi, Mohamad Karam, Wafa Skalli, Elsa Angelini, Loic Le Folgoc

entry.summary: This paper reframes anatomical landmark detection on spinal X-rays as pixel-level contrastive representation learning matched against landmark prototypes, plus learnable shape priors over global spinal configuration to resolve ambiguities. The approach yields more discriminative heatmaps than standard heatmap regression even with a generic U-Net backbone. This matters for clinical spine deformation assessment and pre-operative planning.

entry.title: Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?

author.name: Sichun Luo, Yi Huang, Mukai Li, Haochen Luo, Guanzhi Deng, Haibo Wang, Jian Xu, Zefa Hu, Junlan Feng, Qi Liu

entry.summary: This work studies how to split evaluation budgets in LLM-driven agent scaffold evolution between guiding iterative search and selecting the final scaffold. Experiments show sparse feedback can sustain productive evolution while targeted evaluation improves final selection, and the authors propose an allocation framework leveraging shared informative items and a common scoring reference.

entry.title: Efficient Quantization Training with Stochastic Rounding via Structured Subspace Randomness

author.name: Zeyu Wang, Yiheng Duan, Tao Chen, Donghyun Koo, Sihan Liu, Wenbo Zhang, Chuan He, Liang Liu

entry.summary: Identifies that per-element random thresholds for stochastic rounding saturate accelerator vector units, making low-precision INT8 training with SR slower than BF16 training. The paper shows that shared-threshold schemes degrade training through a common rounding offset mainly via the activation gradient, and proposes structured subspace randomness to remove the cost while preserving unbiasedness. Directly relevant to efficient low-precision training infrastructure.

entry.title: CRISP: Co-designing Pruning and Scheduling for Efficient MoE Inference on Edge Servers

author.name: Congwei Zhang, Youming Tao, Yifei Zou, Yu Yang, Ruirui Zhang, Xiaoyu Zhang, Falko Dressler, Xiuzhen Cheng, Dongxiao Yu

entry.summary: CRISP co-designs expert pruning and runtime scheduling for Mixture-of-Experts inference on memory-constrained edge platforms, where input-dependent routing forces all expert weights to remain accessible. It exploits the skew in expert combination frequencies and asymmetric expert contributions within combinations, reordering neurons so one stored expert can serve partial roles. This targets a growing deployment constraint as MoE models proliferate.

entry.title: Geometric priors for single-patch neural Calabi--Yau metrics on the quintic: a conservative fixed-$\psi$ Ablation study

author.name: D Yang Eng

entry.summary: Compares four neural ansatze (SIREN potential, Cholesky metric, algebraic section, and hybrid) for approximating the complex Monge-Ampere equation on the quintic Calabi-Yau threefold, using a 96-run ablation with multi-seed controls. Section-based models achieve validation sigma around 4% versus roughly 30-44% for baselines. Provides careful evidence that geometric priors dominate naive parameterizations in this setting.

entry.title: Do We Need an LLM to Know Why Sources Conflict? Decision Models for Knowledge-Conflict Typing in RAG

author.name: Parv Khatri, Harshul Jain, Mehak Kapoor, Tanya Sah

entry.summary: Studies whether small typed decision models, which output label probabilities in a single forward pass, can classify why retrieved RAG sources conflict (multiple valid answers, contested topic, stale information, false source), a task where prior work showed typing improves generation by about 24 points but frontier LLMs struggle. Evaluates 11 decision models from 7 providers on the CONFLICTS benchmark using the original prompt. Probes cost-effective alternatives to generative classification.

entry.title: Hierarchical Low-Rank Reparameterization for Parameter-Efficient

author.name: Rong Huang, Yi Xiong, Yuan-Yuan Cheng, Xiao-Ming Fu

entry.summary: Observes that trainable parameters introduced by PEFT methods still contain redundancy and proposes hierarchical low-rank reparameterization: reorganizing PEFT trainable parameters into an approximately square matrix, decomposing it low-rank, and applying this recursively level by level. Combined with LoRA, DoRA, MoSA, and RaSA, it drastically reduces trainable parameter counts while maintaining task performance.

entry.title: CohortFlow: A Steerable Clinical Cohort Curation Agent with Localized Semantic Correction

author.name: Neil Chen, Adrian Serapio, Hanxue Gu, Evan Lee, Kang Wang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: CohortFlow is a clinical cohort curation agent that applies natural-language corrections as localized updates to a structured cohort specification, using a persistent execution graph to selectively invalidate affected computations. On 100 trial-eligibility scenarios it slightly outperforms full regeneration with the same 8B model.

entry.title: Spiking Neural Networks Are Harder to Steal: A Benchmark Study of Model Stealing Attacks

author.name: Ayana Moshruba, Maryam Parsa

entry.summary: This benchmark study examines model stealing attacks against spiking neural networks (SNNs), whose sparse, temporally dynamic spike-based outputs differ fundamentally from ANN mappings. The results suggest SNNs are substantially more resistant to black-box model extraction than conventional ANNs.

entry.title: ATEMPO: Amortized Transfer Entropy Model Per-lag Over-Time

author.name: Emma Andrews, Konstantinos Kontras, Keane Ong, Maarten De Vos, Gianmarco Mengaldo

entry.summary: ATEMPO is a diffusion-based estimator of transfer entropy amortized across lags and time, recovering the specific delays at which one time series informs another without separate fits per source and conditioning depth. This improves on existing transfer entropy methods whose fixed input windows bundle informative and irrelevant history. Applications span scientific time-series analysis where lag structure matters.

entry.title: Conservative Policy Iteration For Zero-Sum POSGs

author.name: Erwan C. Escudie, Matthia Sabatelli, Jilles Steeve Dibangoye

entry.summary: This paper introduces an approximate policy-iteration algorithm for finite-horizon zero-sum partially observable stochastic games, maintaining one policy per player updated jointly along occupancy trajectories. It avoids approximating a full central value function by using supporting hyperplanes induced by the current joint policy.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Discovery of CNOT Decompositions for Quantum Permutations on Constrained Topologies

author.name: Daniele Lizzio Bosco, Jacopo Cossio, Simone Faro, Francesco Pio Marino, Gabriele Messina, Carla Piazza, Giuseppe Serra

entry.summary: Using an AI-assisted synthesis tool called AlphaCNOT, the authors discover a recurring decomposition for remote transpositions on constrained qubit topologies that improves on adjacent-SWAP routing, and extract principles to guide new deterministic compilation algorithms. The work demonstrates AI as an exploratory tool for discovering compiler constructions.

entry.title: Grounding LLM Agents in Business Processes: Process-Aware Knowledge Graphs for Reliable Multi-Step Service Invocation

author.name: Saiful Khan, Afrah Farea

entry.summary: The authors build typed property graphs combining OData metadata and BPMN reference processes so LLM agents can select enterprise API endpoints that respect process order and schema constraints. A hybrid dense-and-graph retriever evaluated on 42 enterprise services improves multi-step service invocation, especially for low lexical overlap queries. This targets a real enterprise reliability problem for tool-using agents.

entry.title: What Improves During Pretraining? Tracking Knowledge Acquisition with Point-in-Time Models

author.name: Chang Su, Bin Wu, Emine Yilmaz, Yao Lu

entry.summary: Using point-in-time models trained on web snapshots from different years, the authors propose a temporal variability score based on the coefficient of variation of an item's negative log-likelihood across models, to track how knowledge is acquired during pretraining. Analyzing six benchmarks and six open-source model families, they characterize how low- and high-variability knowledge differs. This offers a novel longitudinal lens on pretraining dynamics.

entry.title: A Hyper-Logical View on Multi-Agent Path Planning

author.name: Hadar Frenkel, Dor Atzmon

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that many variants of multi-agent path planning can be modeled in HyperLTL and its omega-regular extension HyperQPTL, offering a unified specification-centered view instead of per-variant algorithms. The authors are explicit that hyperproperty model checkers do not replace specialized MAPP solvers but provide a common formal foundation. It matters as a conceptual unification for a field fragmented across many algorithmic special cases.

entry.title: Pricing Cross-Bank Context in Federated Anti-Money Laundering

author.name: Lidia Losavio, Dario Fenoglio, Martin Gjoreski, Marc Langheinrich

entry.summary: The paper examines federated graph learning for anti-money-laundering detection across banks, using transactions recorded by both endpoint banks to locally approximate remote account states for multi-layer GNN computation without extra account-specific exchange. It then quantifies whether additional context is worth sharing via a disclosure ladder of increasing information exposure. This is a thoughtful privacy-utility tradeoff analysis in a high-stakes financial application.

entry.title: count-catcher: Lean Theorems from Model Counting Certificates

author.name: Johannes K. Fichte, Stefan Szeider

entry.summary: count-catcher converts CPOG certificates produced by the exact model counter d4 into formally verified Lean theorems stating that a CNF formula has exactly N models, enabling counting results about combinatorial objects to be checked in a proof assistant. The tool verifies both forward and reverse implications between the formula and the certificate circuit using Lean-checked computations and an LRAT refutation checker.

entry.title: FIDES-Live: Evaluating Behavioral Concordance in Sequential Trading Agents

author.name: Arther Tian, Alex Ding, Simon Wu, Aaron Chan

entry.summary: FIDES-Live extends the FIDES protocol to audit sequential trading agents, checking whether decisions, orders, execution receipts, ledger states, and reports remain mutually consistent over time. It audits ten inference routes over 7,299 cryptocurrency account-rounds plus an equity pilot with real market data and local paper execution, separating decision validity, commitment adherence, and reconciliation.

entry.title: Dream-COP: Guiding Algorithm Discovery for Combinatorial Optimization Problems in an Experience World

author.name: Kuan Xu, Jianming Wang, Ni Zhang, Yaoxin Wu, Yong Wang, Zhiguang Cao

entry.summary: Introduces Dream-COP, where a policy agent learns from replaying past search trajectories in an experience world to guide a discovery agent that generates and refines COP-solving programs with LLMs. Dreaming over recorded outcomes provides feedback on program quality and search efficiency within a limited budget.

entry.title: Making Self-Driving Laboratories Auditable:A Unified Framework for Hybrid Actions,Measurements, and Safe Execution

author.name: Zihan Zhang, Zeyu Wu, Xin Zhang, Mingyu Luo, Haohui Que, Tong Zhu

entry.summary: The paper presents a traceable framework for self-driving laboratories combining a Lab Action Model (LAM) that extends vision-language-action paradigms to emit both robot trajectories and typed instrument API calls, an OpenSDL execution substrate, Safe-SDL for safe execution, and the L3-Bench benchmark. This matters because autonomous labs need unified, auditable interfaces between flexible robot control and instrument APIs.

entry.title: Beyond QASecClaw: Agent Scaling, Verifier Feedback, and Evidence Reliability in Software Assurance

author.name: S M Abdulla Al Mamun, Akif Islam, Mohd. Ruhul Ameen

entry.summary: This empirical study runs five experiments on LLM-based software assurance using Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct across 13,638 model requests, finding that scaling specialist contexts from 1 to 50 increases token use 49-fold without improving unsafe clearance, and that model configurations trade clearance against unresolved outcomes even with deterministic tool evidence. This matters as a caution against naive agent-context scaling in security workflows.

entry.title: CoS-VQ: Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization for Large Language Models

author.name: Zukang Xu, Zhixiong Zhao, Xing Hu, Zhe Jiang, Xin Si, Dawei Yang

entry.summary: CoS-VQ is a vector quantization method for low-bit LLM weight compression that preserves low-dimensional codewords while jointly optimizing hard indices and their shared scale across positions. It tackles scale-induced coupling, where the optimal scale depends on the whole codeword combination and shifts candidate rankings, by collecting candidates across positions before updates.

entry.title: Which Hand Was Late? Diagnosis for Robot Failure Recovery in Bimanual Tool Use

author.name: Baptiste Bonin, Caro Strickland, Audrey Durand

entry.summary: The paper studies failure diagnosis for bimanual robot manipulation, where VLM-based diagnosers trained on single-arm perturbation failures encounter new failure types such as tool slip while held and mistimed gestures. Using a simulated bimanual tool-use task with ground-truth failure causes, it characterizes which sensing channels permit distinguishing which failure causes.

entry.title: REGER: Modeling inter-item Relations with Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Yuxi Huang, Silin Zhou, Chenhao Wang, Zihan Li, Gangming Guo, Pei Ke, Shen Gao, Shuo Shang

entry.summary: REGER explicitly injects inter-item semantic and collaborative relations into generative recommendation, which otherwise learns them only implicitly through random semantic-ID token embeddings and next-token supervision. It incorporates relations into semantic pretraining, history encoding, and SID generation stages, creating a unified framework.

entry.title: Exponential Wake-Up Overshoot in Explicit Gaussian Point-Process Filters

author.name: Hanwu Qin, Dianhai Wang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how explicit Gaussian point-process filters exponentially amplify the first state update after a long silence, deriving the exact distribution of this update, a computable overshoot index, and second-order silence expansions of the state variance for explicit and implicit filters. It separates the bin-width regimes where amplification occurs versus where the true rate is overshot.

entry.title: When Can a Learned Design Surrogate Be Trusted in a Self-Driving Microfluidics Laboratory? An Offline Closed-Loop Framework Built and Tested on Six Public Tables

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhang

entry.summary: Formalizes when learned design surrogates in self-driving laboratories can be trusted, defining measurable quantities such as a competence ratio, measurement budget, time-to-target, and priced decisions. It instantiates the framework offline on six public droplet-microfluidic and liposome datasets with 107 leave-one-group evaluations and a pre-registered protocol. Notable for its rigor: sealed negative validations and pre-registration are rare in ML-for-science.

entry.title: Underdamped Anchored Langevin Dynamics

author.name: Qi Feng, Hoang M. Nguyen, Lingjiong Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes underdamped anchored Langevin dynamics and a corresponding Monte Carlo algorithm, extending anchored sampling from the overdamped to the underdamped (momentum-based) setting. This enables sampling from non-differentiable and heavy-tailed target distributions with the efficiency benefits of underdamped dynamics. A rigorous sampling-theory contribution with potential uses in ML sampling and Bayesian inference.

entry.title: Algorithmic Monoculture in Machine Learning-based Site-Specific Fertilizer Recommendation

author.name: Abdelghani Belgaid

entry.summary: Studies systemic risk from correlated ML recommendation errors across farms in fertilizer prescription, linking expected social loss to model adoption shares and using the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index to characterize concentration effects. It derives a two-model threshold for when privately optimal monoculture is socially dominated and proposes a convex portfolio rule limiting private regret.

entry.title: Bayesian Inference of Expensive Simulators: Survey and Comparison of Design Choices

author.name: \v{S}imon Sold\'at, V\'aclav \v{S}m\'idl

entry.summary: This survey unifies Bayesian optimization-based methods for Bayesian inference with prohibitively expensive simulators into a general framework, then systematically compares key design choices empirically in terms of simulation budget. A key finding is that inference efficiency is often dominated by the surrogate-model response variable choice. It brings coherence to a fragmented literature.

entry.title: Interpretable Meta-Policies for Neural Decision Making

author.name: Raban Emunds, Jannis Bl\"uml, Quentin Delfosse, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: NEXUS is a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework combining neural skills with symbolic meta-policies, shifting transparent reasoning to the high level to reduce symbolic complexity while preserving performance. Object-centric observations enable high-level reasoning and LLM-assisted design of reward functions and meta-policies. It addresses the interpretability-alignment tension in deep RL.

entry.title: Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control via Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Emmanuel S. Ameh, Samuel E. Otto

entry.summary: Introduces BASOC, a model-reduction framework that identifies state-space directions along which the value function is most sensitive and along which optimal trajectories exhibit maximum variance, leveraging trajectory optimization and the Pontryagin maximum principle to combat the curse of dimensionality in Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations. Targets real-time optimal feedback control for high-dimensional nonlinear systems such as stall recovery and flow relaminarization. Combines balanced truncation ideas with active subspaces for control.

entry.title: ORBITAL: Optimization of Robust Brain--Computer Inference Through Architecture-Aware Low-Precision Compression

author.name: Saim Rehman, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: Presents ORBITAL, a robustness-constrained compression framework for EEG decoders in embedded brain-computer interfaces, combining structured compression, recovery-aware operating-point selection, multi-attack evaluation, and native edge validation. On BCI Competition IV-2a across nine subjects, a TRADES-based compressed EEGNet variant achieves higher robustness than the uncompressed model with about 26% fewer parameters and 25% fewer MACs. Shows compression and adversarial robustness can be jointly optimized on edge devices.

entry.title: Neuronal Identity as an Organizational Basis for Analyzing Neural Population Dynamics

author.name: Seungjae Han, Joshua Yedam You, Soi Kim, Minho Eom, Jinho Park, Seunghee Park, Byeongwook Lee, Young-Gyu Yoon

entry.summary: This neuroscience-ML paper proposes using shared biological profiles of individual neurons (molecular, morphological, electrophysiological) as a common reference for routing neurons into latent groups and analyzing population dynamics at group level across subjects and sessions. This anchoring in cross-subject-consistent biology enables better comparability of neural recordings. An interesting intersection of representation learning and systems neuroscience.

entry.title: Evaluating AlphaEarth Embeddings for Crop Classification: Separability, Temporal Dynamics, and Cross-Regional Transferability

author.name: Priyanka Goyal, Maitreyee Sar, Adway Mitra, Manjira Sinha

entry.summary: The study benchmarks 64-dimensional AlphaEarth geospatial foundation model embeddings against Sentinel-2 reflectance and NDVI-derived baselines for crop classification across geometric separability, temporal dynamics, spatial robustness, and cross-regional generalization. It provides a representation-agnostic evaluation framework for geospatial embeddings in agriculture. Useful empirical guidance on when foundation model embeddings beat spectral features.

entry.title: Online gas classification at the edge

author.name: Ton Juny Pina, Hugh Greatorex, Elisabetta Chicca

entry.summary: Inspired by the insect olfactory system, this paper presents a lightweight neural network that classifies raw gas-sensor-array readings online using sparse high-dimensional binary representations, handling dynamic sample streams of single gases and binary mixtures with few-thousand-neuron, sub-milliwatt-scale efficiency targets. It addresses recalibration from limited labels for portable and robotic sensing. A compelling neuromorphic application for edge AI.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Co-Adaptive Hip Exoskeleton Control (MARL-Exo) for Metabolic Energy Reduction

author.name: Yifei Yuan, Jakob Wolf, Ghaith Androwis, Xianlian Zhou

entry.summary: MARL-Exo trains a bilateral hip-exoskeleton control policy concurrently with a full-body musculoskeletal human model (304 muscle actuators) using multi-agent RL and a metabolic-energy reward, with domain randomization over anatomy, gait, and speed. The goal is to reduce walking metabolic cost in new users without per-user tuning. This sim-to-real co-adaptation approach could make exoskeleton assistance practical at scale.

entry.title: 3, 7, 14, 17, 42: Instruction Tuning Installs and Sharpens Number-Choice Heuristics in Language Models

author.name: Samar Ansari

entry.summary: This paper measures, without sampling error, the exact probability a language model assigns to each integer 1 through N when asked for a random number, evaluating 18 open-weight model lines across 29 decoding configurations and 15 matched base/instruction-tuned checkpoint pairs. It finds instruction tuning makes number-choice distributions less uniform, installing round-number avoidance and sharpening endpoint avoidance heuristics. The exact-enumeration methodology is a methodological advance over prior sampling-based studies of LLM biases.

entry.title: Personality Latents: Conditioning Frozen Language Models on Individuals from Their Own Writing

author.name: Gunhee Cho, Yun-Gyung Cheong

entry.summary: Proposes Personality Latents, which learn a per-person latent vector from the person's own writing without personality labels or authored profiles, injected into a frozen LLM as a soft prefix. Uses generative latent optimization for training persons and an encoder that predicts latents for new people in a single forward pass with optional test-time refinement. Enables style/personality control from writing samples alone.

entry.title: Multi-Label Agreement: A Flexible Framework for Inter-Annotator Reliability

author.name: Tim Menzner, Jochen L. Leidner

entry.summary: This paper introduces Multi-Label Agreement (MLA), a framework for measuring inter-annotator reliability in multi-label annotation tasks where classic metrics like Cohen's kappa and Krippendorff's alpha do not directly apply. MLA preserves full binary label vectors and uses average pairwise Hamming agreement, capturing both joint selections and joint omissions. It addresses a real methodological gap as multi-label annotation becomes standard for LLM training data.

entry.title: UT-HMR: Uncertainty-Guided Temporal Modeling for Robust 3D Human Mesh Recovery

author.name: Zhibo Wang, Sirisha Rambhatla, Yuhao Chen, Maria Koshkina, David Clausi

entry.summary: This paper introduces UT-HMR, described as the first one-stage 3D human mesh recovery framework that models correlated pose uncertainty across joints using Gaussian distributions over SMPL pose parameters with a low-rank-plus-diagonal covariance. It targets ambiguity from occlusion, distance, and motion blur in settings like sports, without requiring person crops or external 2D cues. The approach could make monocular HMR more reliable in real-world, weakly observed scenarios.

entry.title: 4D Reconstruction with Events & RGB

author.name: Dulanga Weerakoon, Darshana Rathnayake, Van Minh Do, Hemanth Sabbella, Kaichen Zhou, Fangneng Zhan, Alok Prakash, Sanjay E. Sarma, Archan Misra, Paul Pu Liang

entry.summary: This preliminary study investigates whether event cameras, which capture per-pixel brightness changes at microsecond resolution, can be integrated into existing feed-forward RGB-based 4D reconstruction pipelines via a minimal extension, without full architectural redesign. Event signals are largely immune to motion blur and temporal aliasing that plague RGB under fast motion, making the combination attractive for robotics and AR/VR. Self-labeled preliminary work with a strong multimodal sensing team including Paul Liang.

entry.title: Forget the Data, Keep the Capability: Switchable Unlearning for Retrieval

author.name: Jingong Chen, Kyle Gao, Guangyuan Li, Chulwoo Pack, Sijia Liu, Kwanghee Won

entry.summary: MoME is a switchable machine unlearning framework for re-identification models, splitting a backbone into core parameters that preserve general retrieval and zero-initialized parasitic parameters carrying full-data knowledge, trained under gradient isolation. Disabling the branch satisfies data-deletion requests while enabling it restores standard inference.

entry.title: SplatScout: Query-Driven Part-Level Referring Segmentation in Gaussian Scenes

author.name: Yihan Zang, Da Li, Shinkyu Park, Ivan Viola, Dominik Engel

entry.summary: SplatScout is a closed-loop, query-driven approach to part-level referring segmentation in Gaussian scenes where a VLM actively selects views, directs segmentation, and inspects rendered 3D results, replacing fixed segmenter candidate pools. It also contributes PartRef-ScanNet++, a benchmark with 261 manually verified queries across 12 ScanNet++ scenes.

entry.title: 3D-SceneQ: Empowering 3D LLM With Query-Guided Adaptive Pruning and Multi-Modal Feature Enhancement

author.name: Yongqi Shan, Lu Zhang, Jiazuo Yu, Yunzhi Zhuge, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: This paper presents 3D-SceneQ, a 3D LLM for scene understanding that tackles two common limitations: noise from task-irrelevant 3D object tokens and reliance on point clouds alone, which lack rich 2D semantics. It unifies query-guided adaptive token pruning with multi-modal semantic enrichment from complementary 2D signals such as color, texture, and context.

entry.title: CTBakeGS: training-free baking of photorealistic CT volume renderings into 3D Gaussian splats

author.name: Haruki Fukuda, Constantin Lux, Wolf Schweitzer, Tadashi Hosoya, Lars Ebert

entry.summary: CTBakeGS converts CT volume renderings directly into 3D Gaussian splat models without per-scene training, placing splats on an adaptive octree and computing color and opacity analytically from the renderer, enabling real-time photorealistic viewing on low-power devices. Existing medical 3DGS approaches require minutes to hours of training per scene. This makes photorealistic medical visualization broadly accessible.

entry.title: Characterizing Privacy Leakage in Spiking Neural Networks: A Systematic Analysis of Temporal Dynamics, Stochasticity, Neuronal Dynamics and Learning Mechanisms

author.name: Ayana Moshruba, Maryam Parsa

entry.summary: This study systematically analyzes membership inference leakage in spiking neural networks, isolating the roles of temporal representation, stochasticity, intrinsic neuron dynamics, and learning mechanisms. It finds biologically inspired firing patterns can reduce membership leakage without architectural changes, positioning temporal dynamics as a privacy design variable.

entry.title: SG^2SLAM: Spatial Geometry-Informed 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Monocular Outdoor Navigation

author.name: Ziang Guo, Didar Seyidov, Yixiao Zhou, Xuefeng Zhang, Ali Alridha Abdulkarim, Chen Min, Zufeng Zhang, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: SG^2SLAM couples streaming spatial geometry with a ray-conditioned 3D Gaussian Splatting kernel for monocular outdoor SLAM, replacing per-frame 2D-3D correspondence with chunk-level metric priors. This prevents tracking error from cascading into the map, providing robust camera motion estimation and a dense navigable map.

entry.title: A fully articulated humanoid dexterous hand with human-level joint structure enabled by linkage-based actuation

author.name: Jihao Li, Jianguo Wang, Haotian Guo, Yanzhe Wang, Guodong Lu, Huixu Dong

entry.summary: Torch-Hand is a 21-DOF humanoid dexterous hand replicating human joint structure and motion hierarchy, including a five-DOF multi-axis thumb, using linkage-based actuation to balance anthropomorphic complexity with robustness and load capacity. Such hardware addresses persistent trade-offs limiting dexterous manipulation in unstructured environments.

entry.title: State estimation for a hybrid rigid-continuum space manipulator system

author.name: Lorenzo Ticozzi, Patricio A. Vela, Panagiotis Tsiotras

entry.summary: This work formulates state estimation for a space manipulator whose distal link is a tendon-driven continuum robot as MAP inference over the hybrid configuration, conditioned on discrete noisy measurements. Combining soft mechanisms with space manipulators promises reduced stowage volume and improved safety for on-orbit servicing.

entry.title: Understanding Human-Robot Collaboration through Joint Action

author.name: Chengwen Zhang, Jianyang Wang, Chang Liu, Yukun Wang, Yuan Xu, Zhoutong Ye, Jie Cai, Chun Yu, Yuanchun Shi

entry.summary: This systematic review (PRISMA 2020) analyzes 83 empirical human-robot collaboration papers from 2021-2026 through the lens of Joint Action theory, organizing findings into nine constructs across Representation, Prediction, and Integration capacities. It maps where empirical evidence concentrates and where gaps exist. The review offers a shared conceptual vocabulary for HRC research.

entry.title: The sleep framework: A new way for LLMs to retain knowledge in continual learning

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google Research blog post describing a sleep framework inspired by biological memory consolidation as a way for LLMs to retain knowledge during continual learning, allowing new information to be integrated without catastrophic forgetting. The available content is minimal, but the topic addresses a core open problem in deployed language models.

entry.title: From Interaction to Capability: Task Advancement as State and Supervision for GUI Agents

author.name: Ziyang Chen, Qian Li, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: Task Advancement Memory (TAM) defines task advancement as verified progress, maintaining a Task Advancement State during execution and applying post-task supervision to abstract reusable operations from successful interactions. This helps GUI agents build on earlier achievements across applications in long-horizon workflows. It targets the well-known memory and skill-reuse problem for computer-use agents.

entry.title: MedJev: Evaluating Zero-Shot System-One Decision Making in Medicine

author.name: Simon A. Lee, Jiahang Sha, Moonseong Jeong, Yunbei Pan, Jeffrey N. Chiang

entry.summary: MedJev evaluates an open, laptop-local System One model that answers structured medical questions in a single forward pass without generating text, across ten benchmarks including MedQA, USMLE-style questions, and patient-level prediction with MIMIC IV. It approaches published GPT-4 performance (72.5% MedQA, 75.4% USMLE, 80.1% NEJM) with well-calibrated confidence (ECE 0.028-0.063). This suggests efficient single-pass architectures could enable accessible clinical decision support.

entry.title: HIDRA: Hierarchical Dual-Routing Attention for Replay-Free Lifelong Imitation Learning

author.name: Fanqi Yu, Matteo Tiezzi, Cigdem Beyan, Tommaso Apicella, Vittorio Murino

entry.summary: HIDRA is a structured routing framework for replay-free, single-pass lifelong imitation learning that decouples instruction-level expert retrieval from context-dependent refinement via hierarchical dual attention. A key-lengthening mechanism stabilizes expert routing under the representation drift that afflicts expert-based approaches in sequential updates.

entry.title: FrameForge: Harnessing Priors of Video Foundation Models for Unified Image Generation

author.name: Yijing Lin, Zhendong Mao, Mengqi Huang, Yuxin Wang, Yongdong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes FrameForge, which repurposes pretrained video foundation models for unified conditional image generation by modeling input-adaptive virtual temporal relations between condition and target, instead of assigning them fixed temporal positions. It uses a mixture-of-temporal mechanism capturing complementary relation types.

entry.title: Self-Keyed In-Parameter Memorization for External Memory-Free Dialogue Recall in Frozen Language Models

author.name: XinYu Piao, Myunghoon Ryu, Joongheon Kim, Jong-Kook Kim

entry.summary: SKIM explores whether dialogue content can be stored directly in a frozen language model's parameters without external memory: the model generates self-questions per dialogue turn and writes them into parameters as retrieval keys for later answering. This matters for privacy-preserving, storage-free conversational memory, though catastrophic forgetting and capacity limits are inherent risks.

entry.title: GCSR-OCC: Geometry Calibration and Semantic Routing for Open-Vocabulary Occupancy Prediction

author.name: Bohua Wang, Congyang Zhao, Tianxiong Lv, Chenxu Zhao, He Zheng, Hangqi Fan, Leigang Luo, Zhihao Liao, Yihong Guo, Yang Cai

entry.summary: GCSR-OCC targets open-vocabulary 3D occupancy prediction from a single RGB indoor image, fixing failure modes of Gaussian-based scene reconstruction such as scale inflation, Gaussian overlap, and semantic mixing. It introduces an Evidence-Conserving Gaussian-to-Occupancy operator with kernel mass normalization and multi-mode query-conditioned semantic routing.

entry.title: Persistence, Exposure, and Credit Routing in Linear Temporal Predictive Coding

author.name: Akira Tanase, Julian Gould, Jeffrey Seely

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical analysis of linear Temporal Predictive Coding, an alternative to backpropagation, using cellular sheaf theory to show that temporal credit assignment involves a tradeoff between spatial displacement and temporal errors governed by persistence and exposure operators. It identifies a persistence-error tradeoff where modes preserving long-range influence fail to expose it as temporal error, and shows recurrence can route around this via inter-mode credit. A mathematically deep contribution to the biologically plausible learning literature.

entry.title: The Batch Size Can Be One: Test-Time Adaptation from Classifier Geometry

author.name: Jaeho Hwang, Yujin Oh, Juhyeon Shin, Juhye Lee, Sungroh Yoon, Uiwon Hwang

entry.summary: Proposes OriTTA, a test-time adaptation method for single-sample streams that exploits the fact that corruptions shift features while leaving the frozen classifier's decision regions unchanged, constructing fixed geometric targets from the source model and adapting selected features toward them. This avoids the pitfalls of confidence-based sample selection with batch-size-one inputs. Addresses a practical deployment constraint often idealized away in TTA research.

entry.title: GNN-Guided Network Reduction for Centralized Urban Traffic Routing

author.name: Nikolai Antonov, Luk\'a\v{s} Chrpa, Andrii Nyporko, Jan H\r{u}la

entry.summary: Proposes a learning-based urban network reduction method for centralized traffic routing, where a GNN scores road segments for each origin-destination flow to build reduced networks that make MILP optimization tractable within operational time budgets. Unlike prior reduced-network heuristics, the approach accounts for vehicle information within each OD flow.

entry.title: GTFormer: A Syntax-Free Graph Network Alternative to Transformers for 8192$\times$ Length Extrapolation in Linear Time

author.name: Elisabeth Fink

entry.summary: GTFormer replaces flat self-attention with a syntax-free hierarchical GNN combining a balanced binary reduction tree and bounded-degree structure, targeting linear-time long-context sequence modeling. It claims 8192x length extrapolation beyond the training horizon, addressing the quadratic compute and attention dilution limits of Transformers. Built on ideas from algebraic graph learning (WPNet).

entry.title: Reconstructing the Human Development Index at the Individual Level from Survey Microdata: Development and Validation of a Methodology

author.name: Tcharlies Bachmann Schmitz (PX Center, Brazil), Natalia Veronez da Cunha (Universidade do Planalto Catarinense, UNIPLAC), Isabelle Ferreira (Universidade do Planalto Catarinense, UNIPLAC)

entry.summary: Develops and validates a methodology for reconstructing the Human Development Index from individual-level survey microdata across 21 countries and roughly 40,000 respondents, enabling disaggregated estimates for demographic subpopulations while staying consistent with official HDI. Health, income, and education dimensions are estimated via calibrated adjustments to national indicators. Useful for inequality-aware development measurement.

entry.title: RAG-CSI: Global Local Retrieval via Joint State and Dynamics Matching for CSI Prediction

author.name: Xinyue Jiang, Tong Li, Shiceng Zhang, Ke Chen, Zhu Xiao

entry.summary: RAG-CSI is a retrieval-enhanced Transformer for wireless channel state information prediction that augments model prediction with relevant historical channel knowledge drawn from a global-local knowledge store spanning scenes, using joint state-dynamics matching for retrieval. This moves CSI prediction beyond knowledge locked in model parameters. An early application of retrieval-augmented generation ideas to communications.

entry.title: QD-PINN:A Physics-Informed Neural Network Approach to Bayesian Quickest Detection in High-Dimensional Diffusions

author.name: Hang Ye, Yi Liu, Haipeng Xing

entry.summary: QD-PINN applies physics-informed neural networks to Bayesian quickest detection problems, estimating optimal stopping boundaries for high-dimensional diffusions with spatial dependence where traditional variational-inequality solvers struggle. The authors prove an equivalence between the free-boundary PDE and an infinite-dimensional stochastic optimization problem, justifying finite-dimensional neural approximation and mitigating the curse of dimensionality. This extends deep learning to an important class of sequential detection problems.

entry.title: Detect Before You Disambiguate: Perturbation-Based Input Ambiguity Detection in LLMs

author.name: Tiejin Chen, Xiaoou Liu, Michael Clifford, Ahmadreza Moradipari, Yitao Chen, Kyungtae Han, Nejib Ammar, Hua Wei

entry.summary: The paper proposes a label-preserving perturbation framework for detecting ambiguous inputs to LLMs before answering, arguing that prior methods that generate clarifications already disambiguate the input before measuring ambiguity. It instantiates two detectors, a black-box rule-based perturbation library and a learned variant, addressing input ambiguity as an upstream source of uncertainty. This improves when models should ask for clarification rather than answer directly.

entry.title: Agentic Data Sampling Framework for Multilingual ASR via Linguistic-Aware Error-Driven Optimization

author.name: Zhiheng Qian, Junhao Du, Jing Peng, Hanqi Li, Kunyang Peng, Feng Xue, Lu Chen, Shuai Wang, Kai Yu

entry.summary: Proposes inserting an LLM agent into the multilingual ASR training loop to decide data sampling, driven by a linguistically grounded rubric analyzing errors from phonological, morphological, and syntactic perspectives. The agent uses error feedback, training statistics, and budget constraints to replace manual, heuristic sampling strategies. Aims to automate a previously hand-tuned component of multilingual speech model training.

entry.title: TrawMem: Reframing Agent Memory as Task-Oriented Role-Adaptive Workspaces

author.name: Mingyu Zhang, Zixu Li, Zhiheng Fu, Zhiwei Chen, Jinhe Bi, Yupeng Hu

entry.summary: Reframes LLM agent memory systems as task-oriented, role-adaptive workspaces in which memories are selected and organized by the roles they play in task solving rather than purely by query relevance. TrawMem organizes interaction histories so the same memory can directly support an answer or link complementary memories with weaker semantic relevance but necessary information. A conceptual plus systems contribution to agent memory architecture.

entry.title: Decoupling Consistency and Conflict across MLLM Layers for Fake News Detection

author.name: Kai Qian, Dongjie Xu, Weijie Shi, Jiaqi Wang, Haolun Ma, Jia Zhu, Jiajie Xu

entry.summary: MLCCD detects multimodal fake news by capturing image-text conflicts at different semantic levels from different layers of multimodal large language models, treating consistency and conflict dynamically rather than statically. It exploits the observation that different MLLM layers encode distinct levels of knowledge to detect mismatches in objects, scenes, events, and claims. This improves sensitivity to sparse, varied-level conflicts typical of fake news.

entry.title: Ground-to-Satellite Knowledge Distillation for Crop Classification under Temporal and Geographic Shift

author.name: Miro Miranda, Rocco Sedona, Valerio Marsocci, Gabriele Cavallaro, Claudia Paris

entry.summary: The paper uses ground-level field photographs as privileged supervision via a frozen photo-teacher distilling into satellite-embedding-based crop classifiers, addressing limited reference data and robustness under temporal and geographic shift. This enables scalable crop type mapping without requiring ground photos at inference.

entry.title: MvT: Event-based Multi-view Projection for Multiple Object Tracking

author.name: Muxi Zha, Banglei Guan, Minzu Liang, Zibin Liu, Yang Shang, Qifeng Yu, Laurent Kneip

entry.summary: MvT is a multi-view pipeline for event-camera multiple object tracking that keeps the 2D pseudo-frame format so image-based techniques apply directly, while adding spatio-temporal views to resolve ambiguities from overlapping trajectories. It addresses a core failure of prevailing pseudo-frame methods for event-based MOT. The work is from a credible event-vision group.

entry.title: Leveraging Distributed Sensing and Hyperdimensional Computing for Non-Line-of-Sight Passive Object Sensing

author.name: Placido Mursia, Marco Rossanese, Francesco Devoti, Adrian Lendinez Ibanez, Lanfranco Zanzi, Xi Li, Xavier Costa-Perez

entry.summary: The authors propose a framework using integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with distributed wireless devices and hyperdimensional computing to passively detect humans and obstacles outside a robot's line of sight in smart factories. This addresses safety risks that LiDAR, radar, or cameras cannot cover due to occlusions. It couples communication infrastructure with lightweight, energy-efficient inference.

entry.title: Ontology-guided multi-agent reasoning for explainable differential diagnosis

author.name: Roxana Ramona Szomiu, George Ursu, Adrian Groza

entry.summary: The paper proposes an ontology-guided multi-agent approach to LLM-based differential diagnosis that structures patient case descriptions and grounds reasoning in structured clinical knowledge, exposing evidence and rationale for each recommendation. It targets the problem that LLMs often produce plausible but unsupported diagnostic conclusions.

entry.title: PsyJev: Psychological Analysis via System-1 Judgment

author.name: Fangyuan Liu, Sirui Zhao, Xiaohao Wang, Guo Cheng, Peng Zhang, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: PsyJev is a System-1 model that directly produces answer distributions for question-conditioned psychological content analysis, trained jointly on PsyJudgeBench (13 datasets, 82 questions across six psychological areas) with a judgment-anchored RLCD stage adapting logit-space reward optimization to heterogeneous criteria. It unifies diverse web self-disclosure analysis tasks under one decision interface. Useful for scalable psychological content analysis.

entry.title: SpectRAG: Weighted Chunk Graphs for Token-Budgeted Context Selection in Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Zafer Sahinoglu, Abdulazeez Mohammed, Buse Yaren Kazangirler, Cahit Berkay Kazangirler

entry.summary: SpectRAG combines hybrid candidate seeding, weighted chunk graph construction, spectral relevance propagation, and token-budgeted context selection to improve multi-hop RAG, addressing redundancy and incomplete evidence from independent dense retrieval. Chunks are represented via dense embeddings plus graph-spectral coordinates.

entry.title: Split Federated Unlearning

author.name: Jia Chen, Yecheng Lv, Xinrong Hu, Mingdi Huang, Jun Bai

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic formulation of unlearning in split federated learning, where removing a client's or class's contributions is complicated by cross-partition model coupling and dual-side aggregation. The paper theoretically characterizes historical influence propagation and mode-dependent feasibility of unlearning, and proposes an initial solution. Relevant to privacy and data-deletion compliance in distributed edge learning.

entry.title: IOSage: Detecting HPC I/O Bottleneck Patterns to Guide LLM Recommendations

author.name: Mahdi Banisharif, Tabassum Mahmud, Ahmad Tarraf, Suren Byna, Ali Jannesari

entry.summary: Presents IOSage, a system where a classifier trained on labeled Darshan logs, rather than the LLM itself, decides which HPC I/O bottleneck patterns a log contains, with the LLM then writing recommendations given the detected patterns, job configuration, and benchmark-derived evidence cards. This corrects a flaw in prior LLM-based tools like ION and IOAgent where a single log gives the LLM no baseline for abnormality. Improves expert-level I/O tuning accessibility for HPC applications.

entry.title: Sample-and-Score: Surrogate-Guided Coordinated Spatial Reuse in IEEE 802.11 Networks

author.name: Maksymilian Wojnar

entry.summary: The paper proposes a sample-and-score method for coordinated spatial reuse configuration in IEEE 802.11bn networks: random configurations are drawn and scored by an offline-trained surrogate without online exploration, recovering 52-77% of perfect-surrogate throughput on unseen topologies and approaching bandit/heuristic baselines. A perfect scorer reaches 95% of the upper bound. Practical wireless networking optimization with an efficient deployable recipe.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Multimodal Event Spotting in Soccer Broadcasts

author.name: Sadia Kamal, Mahmudul Hasan, Tony Braskich

entry.summary: This paper presents a zero-shot framework for detecting, classifying, and temporally localizing events in full-length soccer broadcasts without task-specific training, representing each match as compact visual storyboards aligned with commentary transcripts processed by a general-purpose multimodal model. On three annotated matches with 130 events, it achieves 72.0% F1@5s and outperforms SoccerNet-trained CALF and NetVLAD++ in cross-dataset settings. It demonstrates that general multimodal models can replace domain-specific training pipelines for video understanding.

entry.title: ObjectTwin: Measuring the Asset Correspondence Gap for Capture-Anchored Digital Twins

author.name: Zhenghe Guo

entry.summary: ObjectTwin introduces a scan-grounded measurement protocol for evaluating generated meshes inserted into captured scenes as editable object proxies, freezing the instance, cameras, and depth while swapping only the object representation. The resulting asset correspondence gap quantifies lost observation agreement against scan-derived visible geometry without treating the scan as complete ground truth. This fills a real evaluation gap for capture-anchored digital twin workflows.

entry.title: CRLoMTL: Conflict-Resolution through Low-rank matrices for Multi-Task Learning

author.name: Ahmed Agiza, Tasneem Shaffee, Rahil Badkul, Sherief Reda

entry.summary: CRLoMTL mitigates negative transfer in multi-task vision learning by operating in low-rank parameter-update space instead of manipulating gradients. Each task learns its own LoRA updates via task-specific passes, which are then fused in a shared subspace. This offers a parameter-efficient alternative to gradient-conflict methods, relevant to adapter-based training broadly.

entry.title: Taming Noise Initialization for Zero-shot Video Restoration with Image Diffusion Priors

author.name: Chong Wang, Zixuan Fu, Hao Cheng, Siyuan Yang, Alex C. Kot, Bihan Wen

entry.summary: This paper improves zero-shot video restoration with pre-trained image diffusion models by replacing frame-wise independent or identical noise initialization with a scheme that captures temporal correlations among degraded frames. This avoids costly video diffusion pre-training while restoring temporal consistency. It addresses a key limitation of the popular reuse-image-priors approach.

entry.title: Segmentation Confidence for Arbitrary CNNs

author.name: Baris Oguz, Xing Yao, Claudia Tawil, Alison Pouch, Brett Byram, Gabriel Arenas, Nadav Schwartz, Ipek Oguz

entry.summary: This paper presents voxel-based uncertainty estimation methods that can be added to existing medical image segmentation CNNs without retraining or custom architectures, plus a novel method to collapse uncertainty maps into a single confidence score. Evaluations across different regions of interest and modalities support the confidence estimate quality. Usable confidence scores matter for clinical deployment safety.

entry.title: Every route counts, but some count more: a max-plus view of the C. elegans brain

author.name: Emma Reyner-Fuentes, Sebastian Rudolph, Carmen Pel\'aez-Moreno, Francisco J. Valverde-Albacete

entry.summary: The authors model neural signaling as routing rather than diffusion using max-plus algebra, where the strongest path dominates, and analyze the C. elegans connectome as a time-varying combination of electrical, synaptic, monoaminergic, neuropeptidergic, and hormonal layers. Each analyzed network collapses onto a small set of dominant feedback circuits.

entry.title: Learning Side-by-Side Navigation for Personal Mobility Vehicles from Human Drivers

author.name: Luis Yoichi Morales, Florent Ferreri

entry.summary: Two personal mobility vehicles plan cooperatively to maintain a side-by-side social formation enabling conversation, using distributed sampling-based MPC planners that exchange only observed odometry and resolve joint decisions via utility matrices. Behavioral parameters are learned by inverse reinforcement learning from 409 minutes of human-driven PMV pairs.

entry.title: MARQ: A Modular, LLM-Agnostic Requirement Quality Assessor Infused with Systems Engineering Knowledge

author.name: Jannatul Shefa, Alejandro Salado, Paul Wach, Taylan G. Topcu

entry.summary: MARQ is a modular, LLM-agnostic prototype that improves LLM-based assessment of engineering requirements by injecting expert-derived knowledge operationalizing INCOSE requirement quality criteria. It addresses the finding that off-the-shelf LLMs miss many expert-identified requirement defects.

entry.title: Plenty of Room in the Middle: Revealing Opportunities on a GPU Cluster via Fine-Grained Monitoring

author.name: Andrew Sheinberg, Samyak Gupta, Kai Li

entry.summary: The paper deploys a lightweight DCGM-based monitoring tool capturing 100 ms GPU utilization metrics across an 89-node, 319-GPU university cluster, revealing underutilization invisible to coarser-grained monitoring. The fine-grained data exposes optimization opportunities beyond job-level scheduling.

entry.title: Learning to Formalize: Bridging Open-Ended Workloads and Fast Decision Models

author.name: Chengxuan Pei, Ziyao Wang, Teng Mei, Zhe Li

entry.summary: This paper trains a small candidate formalizer that converts open-ended task contexts into explicit, validated alternative lists, which a frozen fast decision model then selects from, bridging generative and decision-model interfaces. A motivating comparison on CALVIN-D reports 11% success with generic motions versus 46.5% with a formalized pipeline using DeepSeek V4 Flash. The approach trades LLM generation cost for fast decision-time selection.

entry.title: Noise Steering: Exploiting Wake Steering and Acoustic Directivity for Noise-Constrained Wind Farm Control via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mart\'in de Frutos, Baptiste Corban, Claire Bizon Monroc, Ana Bu\v{s}i\'c, Donatien Dubuc, Jiamin Zhud, Esteban Ferrer

entry.summary: The paper proposes Noise Steering, a model-free RL strategy that jointly controls turbine yaw angles and power setpoints to maximize wind farm power subject to local noise constraints, exploiting both wake interactions and acoustic directivity. A low-fidelity acoustic model enables training at reduced computational cost.

entry.title: Do bots feel bad? Assessing empirical evidence for functional valence in LLMs

author.name: Iwan Williams

entry.summary: This philosophical analysis critically assesses recent empirical claims that LLMs possess functional valenced states such as functional pleasure, pain, or welfare. The author argues that key aspects of valence, as understood in philosophy and cognitive science, remain untested in LLMs and that existing paradigms have limitations.

entry.title: RPSD: Retrieval-Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation with Optimal Transport

author.name: Dongyue Li, Zebang Cheng, Zhongyi Deng, Hongboxu, Yi Bin, Fei Ma

entry.summary: RPSD targets LLM-based sequential recommendation post-training with GRPO, identifying credit-blind optimization and collaborative-blind supervision as key flaws. It proposes on-policy self-distillation where a privileged teacher guides a student, using optimal transport for token-level credit and retrieval to share behavioral patterns across similar users. It addresses known weaknesses of applying RLHF-style methods to generative recommendation.

entry.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry

author.name: Wenqing Peng, Michael Boy, Zhi-Song Liu

entry.summary: KPPax is a preprocessor that converts atmospheric chemistry mechanisms written in the KPP language into differentiable, JIT-compiled, vectorizable JAX code, using sparse log-space rate evaluation and diffrax stiff solvers with exact adjoints. This connects decades of atmospheric chemistry infrastructure to modern machine learning workflows. It enables sensitivity analysis and ML integration for climate and air-quality modeling.

entry.title: ReCoPII: A Relation-Grounded Framework for Building Contextual PII Masking Datasets

author.name: Taehwan Lee

entry.summary: This paper proposes ReCoPII, a framework for constructing contextual PII masking datasets that derives MASK/KEEP labels from planned entity relations rather than the single-data-subject assumption used in author-based augmentation like SPY. It uses ontology-constrained relation planning, LLM-generated insertion sentences, code-based annotation reconstruction, and separate LLM verification, evaluated on Korean documents across six domains. It matters because privacy restrictions make real contextual PII data scarce, and better synthetic datasets directly improve practical privacy tools.

entry.title: Dirichlet Process Mixtures within Semiparametric Bayesian Networks: A Novel Conditional Density Estimation Approach

author.name: Victor Alejandre, Pedro Larra\~naga, Concha Bielza

entry.summary: The paper defines a new conditional-probability-distribution model for semiparametric Bayesian networks using Bayesian nonparametric Dirichlet Process Mixtures instead of kernel density estimators, yielding data-adaptive clustering and a more compact representation while retaining flexibility. This reduces inference costs and density-estimation errors inherent to KDE's one-component-per-observation mixtures. It is a solid statistical-machine-learning contribution for probabilistic graphical models.

entry.title: Can AI Guide Testing Without Generating Tests? A Comparative Study of AI-Assisted Unit Testing

author.name: Zihan Fang, Ron Asoulin-Handelman, Helen Wu, Yu Huang, Gina R. Bai

entry.summary: TestCompass is a generative AI tutor that gives students targeted feedback on weaknesses in their unit test suites without writing tests for them, aiming to preserve skill development that fully automated test generation may erode. A classroom study compares this guidance-only approach against AI-assisted test generation.

entry.title: Concorde: Geometry-Aware Link Prediction via Decoupled Energy Minimization

author.name: Ege Demirci, Ambuj Singh

entry.summary: Concorde is an energy-based link prediction framework for sparse graphs that decomposes link likelihood into three decoupled branches: a parameter-free spectral anchor, a mixed-curvature residual on a learnable hyperbolic-spherical product manifold regularized by an Ollivier-Ricci curvature proxy, and a continuous vector field for non-local structural alignment. This addresses spectral instability when coupling learned representations with diffusion operators.

entry.title: LociArt: A Unified Paradigm for Free-Style Local Video Stylization

author.name: Yuxuan Chen, Feng Xie, Jiagao Hu, Fuhao Li, Zepeng Wang, Fei Wang, Daiguo Zhou

entry.summary: Presents LociArt, a framework for local video stylization that lets users specify which regions to stylize and with what style while preserving the rest of the content, with an emphasis on spatial control and temporal consistency. Its GRNStyle module uses a polar style-aware mask and representation-geometry conditioning, with a data pipeline providing paired supervision.

entry.title: A Quantitative Approach to Asch Conformity in Frontier Large Language Models

author.name: Senthil Rajasekaran, Stylianos Loukas Vasileiou

entry.summary: Adds a quantitative layer to Asch conformity experiments with LLMs by repeatedly sampling a single question to obtain answer distributions before and after manufactured consensus, enabling distribution-to-distribution comparison. It confirms frontier LLMs conform to social pressure and quantifies the effect beyond prior binary demonstrations.

entry.title: Generative Refinement Learning for Temporal Interpolation in Scientific Machine Learning

author.name: Pu Ren, Michael W. Mahoney, N. Benjamin Erichson

entry.summary: The authors propose iFLEX, a model that learns to correct a simple weighted-average interpolation for reconstructing intermediate scientific fields between low-resolution observations. Training signals are derived by subtracting the naive estimate from observed intermediate fields. This matters for scientific ML applications where expensive simulations produce temporally sparse data.

entry.title: Hardware-Matched Spiking Neural Networks for Real-Time Purkinje Cell Spike Classification

author.name: Arooba Farhan, Afsah Syed, Muhammad Fahd Ibrahim Bhatti, Muhammad Areeb Khalid Kidwai, Muhammad Ahsan Salar Khan, Vincenzo Romano, Muhammad Ali Siddiqi

entry.summary: The authors design two compact spiking neural networks for classifying Purkinje cell simple versus complex spikes directly on untethered headstage hardware, where power budgets prevent streaming raw recordings. One SNN maps to a microcontroller matrix-vector processor and the other to a streaming architecture, enabling accurate real-time on-device classification for freely behaving animals.

entry.title: JEPA-Inspired Latent Field Prediction for Sparse-Pilot MIMO-OFDM Channel Reconstruction

author.name: Yuzhi Yang, Brahim Mefgouda, Hang Zou, Lina Bariah, Anis Bara, Yuhuan Lu, Hao Zhang, Merouane Debbah

entry.summary: The paper applies a joint-embedding predictive architecture to MIMO-OFDM channel state information reconstruction from sparse pilots, predicting in a latent propagation-field domain rather than directly on phase-sensitive raw CSI coefficients. This exploits spatial, temporal, and frequency correlations of wireless channels to reduce pilot overhead robustly.

entry.title: MoI-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generation and Editing on Mobile Devices

author.name: Kailai Feng, Haoxiang Rao, Yuxiang Wei, Bo Chen, Junsong Li, Yang Pan, Chengkun Cai, Jagmohan Chauhan

entry.summary: MoI-Bench is a benchmark grounded in real mobile user needs for on-device image generation and editing, with 64 subtasks and 1150 samples organized along 16 operations and 8 visual target categories. It also proposes MoI-Eval with task-specific criteria to quantify capability gaps between on-device and server-side image models.

entry.title: KORA: Deterministic-First Execution Control for AI Workloads

author.name: Albert Heekwan Kim

entry.summary: KORA proposes a pre-inference control layer that routes structured, deterministic, or verifiable workloads through deterministic paths first, escalating to model inference only when needed, with validation and telemetry along the way. The paper reports bounded evidence from reproducible benchmark workloads.

entry.title: Knowledge distillation across teacher architectures for compact diabetic retinopathy grading

author.name: Mossa Manisa, Habiba Jahan Priya, A. K. M. Fakhrul Hossain

entry.summary: The authors conduct a controlled study of offline response-based knowledge distillation for five-class diabetic retinopathy grading on APTOS 2019, distilling ResNet-50, MobileNetV3, and Swin-T teachers into a MobileNetV3-Small student across a grid of temperature and hard-label weight settings. The best configuration achieved a quadratic weighted kappa around 0.91, though multi-seed results showed variance.

entry.title: Confidence Is Not a Promise: A Reference Audit of Typed Decision Models

author.name: Pedro Carvalho Brom

entry.summary: Examines how probability outputs from typed decision models are treated as guarantees by software, and measures what a probability actually licenses statistically. Across 190 evaluations, point-estimate-chosen thresholds break accuracy promises in most cases, while conformal-style Learn then Test and a proposed Beta lower-bound rule maintain guarantees, with the Beta rule deciding more items on average. Single-author work with a rigorous statistical auditing perspective relevant to trustworthy deployed ML.

entry.title: Normalized Cuts and Data Clustering via Matrix Fractional Programming

author.name: Yannan Chen, Beichen Huang, Licheng Zhao, Chris Ding, Kaiming Shen

entry.summary: Recasts the normalized cut clustering problem using a novel multidimensional quadratic transform in fractional programming, handling the multi-ratio case that classical Dinkelbach transforms cannot, and reduces NCut to a bipartite matching problem solvable by linear search. Includes a recognizable author (Kaiming Shen) with a strong optimization background. A clean theoretical contribution to a classic clustering problem.

entry.title: Gaussian Process Bandits for Constraint Black Box Lever Optimization

author.name: Bram van den Akker, Hidde Fokkema, Anastasiia Kornilova

entry.summary: Proposes a segmentation-agnostic GP-UCB approach for optimizing discrete allocation weights across budget segments in sequential decision-making with delayed, noisy, aggregate feedback and adjustment constraints. By placing a Gaussian Process prior over the reward function, the method handles the combinatorial action space and sparsity that defeat independent-arm bandit algorithms.

entry.title: Euclidean Crowding-Driven Adaptive Euclidean-Hyperbolic Graph Learning

author.name: Hao Chen, Jian Sun, Chuan Shi, Hongying Zhang

entry.summary: This paper provides a geometric quantification of Euclidean crowding and a generalization-theoretic explanation for why hyperbolic embeddings excel on hierarchical graph data. It then develops an adaptive Euclidean-hyperbolic fusion framework that decides when to use each geometry. The work connects empirical hyperbolic graph learning success to theory.

entry.title: Learning on-the-fly quasi-stationarity diagnostics from low-dimensional surrogates

author.name: No\'e Blassel

entry.summary: Proposes an alternative to MCMC-based decorrelation diagnostics in accelerated molecular dynamics by coarse-graining non-linear conditioned probability flows and using simulation-based inference, with non-asymptotic uniform-in-time error estimates for killed Markov jump processes. This improves estimates of when metastable processes reach quasi-stationary distributions. Relevant to efficient rare-event simulation.

entry.title: Evaluating Federated Vision-Language and Vision-Only Models for Privacy-Aware Breast Cancer Imaging

author.name: Malithi Mithsara Wanniarachchi Kankanamge, Ning Yang, Sree Bash Debnath, Md Zobaer Islam, Abdur R. Shahid

entry.summary: Evaluates a privacy-aware federated learning framework combining pretrained vision-language models (CLIP, BiomedCLIP) and a ViT baseline with client-level differential privacy on two public breast imaging datasets, including text-pathway ablations and patient-level ROC-AUC with bootstrap confidence intervals. Provides practical guidance on accuracy-privacy tradeoffs for federated medical imaging. Relevant to training on fragmented, sensitive clinical data.

entry.title: HorizON: A Multi-Horizon Deep Operator Network for Property Prediction of Organic Battery Stacks

author.name: Subhash V. S. Ganti, Lukas Woelfel, Arla Diengdoh, Tzvetan Mihaylov, Thomas Nevolianis, Jan Meyer, Christopher Kuenneth

entry.summary: HorizON extends a prior data-fusion multi-task framework to predict multiple coupled battery-stack metrics (voltage, capacity, retention, energy density) for organic electrode materials across discharge horizons using a deep operator network. It targets the sustainability-driven shift away from lithium/cobalt/nickel chemistries. A specialized scientific ML application with practical materials-design relevance.

entry.title: Low-degree polynomials lower bounds for clustering in small dimension

author.name: Alexandra Carpentier (MISTEA), Nicolas Verzelen (MISTEA)

entry.summary: This theoretical work establishes computational lower bounds for clustering mixtures of K isotropic distributions in low dimension d, in the regime where K is much larger than d. Using a construction based on dual BCH codes producing indistinguishable moment tensors, the authors strengthen existing low-degree lower bounds from n greater than dK-squared. This advances understanding of when tensor-based clustering procedures are computationally hard to beat.

entry.title: Graph Representation Learning via Adaptive Expectile Aggregation

author.name: Tianyi Zhu, Wei Lan

entry.summary: ExpectileGCN replaces standard mean neighborhood aggregation in GNNs with a learnable expectile level that interpolates between minimum- and maximum-type aggregation, targeting heterophilic graphs where means lose class-relevant distributional information. The expectile operator is made differentiable via sigmoid smoothing and fixed-point iterations, with stability and transductive generalization guarantees. This is a clean generalization of a core GNN primitive.

entry.title: Lipi-Ghor: A Large-Scale, Diarized, Multi-Domain Bengali Speech Corpus and a Scalable Pipeline for Building It

author.name: Sanjid Hasan, A H M Fuad, Risalat Labib, Bayazid Hasan Simon

entry.summary: Lipi-Ghor is an 885-hour weakly-supervised Bengali speech corpus built from 998 YouTube videos across 596 channels and 17 domains, annotated in an SSTT format combining automated diarization with caption tracks. It is the first Bengali corpus pairing long-form audio with diarization at scale, addressing severe under-resourcing of a language spoken by over 230 million people. The accompanying scalable pipeline enables replication for other low-resource languages.

entry.title: semanticfa: An R Package for Response-Free Semantic Factor Analysis of Psychometric Scales

author.name: Devon Yanitski, Chris Westbury

entry.summary: semanticfa is an R package that performs factor analysis of psychometric scales using language-model embeddings of scale items instead of human response data, including factor interpretation, redundancy flagging, and short-form construction. A worked example on the IPIP Big-Five markers embedded with Qwen3-Embedding-8B recovers factor structures consistent with an analysis of over 874,000 human respondents. It demonstrates that embeddings can proxy large-scale human judgments in instrument development.

entry.title: ConformalMOS: Uncertainty-Aware MOS Prediction with Conformal Intervals and Ordinal Modeling

author.name: Kehinde Elelu, Joshua E. Siegel, Mohammadali Saffary, Tashfain Ahmed, Simeon Babatunde, Ebuka Okpala

entry.summary: ConformalMOS augments mean opinion score prediction for synthetic speech with conformal prediction intervals that carry statistical coverage guarantees, while modeling MOS labels in an ordinal-aware manner using Gaussian-smoothed distributions. This addresses the unreliability of point-estimate-only predictors in TTS and voice conversion evaluation. Uncertainty calibration matters for trustworthy automated speech quality assessment.

entry.title: SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation

author.name: Truman Hickok

entry.summary: SO-101 Bench is a simulated benchmark for language-conditioned spatial manipulation built on an Isaac Lab digital twin of a low-cost SO-101 robot arm, featuring four tasks in five scoring families, 138 objects across seen/unseen splits, 916 evaluation episodes, and 3,629 demonstrations. It fills a gap by enabling standardized policy evaluation for the most common entry-level robot learning platform. This improves accessibility and reproducibility in robot learning research.

entry.title: Multi-task Disentangling Fusion Mamba-CNN for MODIS Spectral-Temporal Unmixing with Endmember Variability Modeling

author.name: Motasem Alkayid, Yimin Zhu, Naser El-Sheimy, Lincoln Linlin Xu

entry.summary: MDF-Mamba pairs per-channel convolutional spectral experts with a bidirectional Mamba temporal branch to disentangle coupled spectral-temporal information in MODIS time series unmixing, while explicitly modeling endmember variability. The multi-task design targets abundance mapping and spectral library construction.

entry.title: OmniGlimpse: Asymmetric Identity Memory for Online Multi-View Tracking

author.name: Rangya Zhang, Jiaping Xiao, Yujing Shang, Yuhang Zhang, Mingsheng Li, Mir Feroskhan

entry.summary: OmniGlimpse addresses online multi-view identity maintenance, where targets are initialized once per view with no further labels, without offline scene-specific training or camera calibration. It proposes an asymmetric propose-verify framework to match observations across views while avoiding error amplification from online adaptation.

entry.title: TriDifNet: A Unified Three-Task Diffusion Network for End-to-End RGB-T Perception

author.name: Qianchao He, Jing Liu, Yunhao Li, Xiaoqing Tian

entry.summary: TriDifNet is claimed to be the first diffusion-based network jointly optimizing registration, fusion, and detection for misaligned infrared-visible pedestrian perception, with three diffusion modules (RegDM, FusDM, and a detection module) preventing registration errors from propagating downstream.

entry.title: MCP-Net: Real-Time Coronary Perception Network and Topological Analysis for Robotic Guidewire Navigation

author.name: Sahar Nasirihaghighi, Tianyuan Wang, Kenan Niu, Stefano Stramigioli

entry.summary: MCP-Net is a multi-task perception network for robotic coronary guidewire navigation that jointly performs vessel segmentation, vascular topology extraction, and roadmap generation from X-ray fluoroscopy, trained on simulated data derived from 3D CT angiography. It integrates perception tasks that are usually handled separately, providing structured scene understanding for downstream robotic control. This matters for advancing autonomy in percutaneous coronary interventions.

entry.title: INTR++: INterpretable TRansformer with better Accuracy, Interpretability, and Adaptability

author.name: Dipanjyoti Paul, Arpita Chowdhury, Maneet Chatterjee, Daichi Kitaguchi, Tanya Berger-Wolf, Tetsuya Sakurai, Wei-Lun Chao

entry.summary: INTR++ extends Prompt-CAM for interpretable vision transformers by adding a lightweight Prompt Adapter Module that makes prompts adaptive to domains with substantial variation in input image characteristics. The goal is to achieve ViT-like broad applicability while retaining concept-based interpretability across domains. This tackles the known tension between interpretability and generalization.

entry.title: Hierarchical Sparse Graph for Multi-dimensional Assignment in Event-based Tracking

author.name: Muxi Zha, Yang Shang, Wenlong Zhang, Qifeng Yu, Banglei Guan

entry.summary: This paper reformulates event-based tracking as multi-dimensional assignment across multiple batches simultaneously, using a hierarchical sparse graph to handle the fact that event detectors can produce multiple valid, spatially distinct tracklets per object per batch. This violates the one-to-one assumption of classic data association and enables handling long-term occlusions and missed detections. It advances global rather than purely online association for event data.

entry.title: GNBG-C: A Unified and Configurable Benchmark Generator for Constrained Continuous Optimization

author.name: Ali Ghasemzadeh, Erfan Babakhani, Armin Khosravi, Pariya Ghasemzadeh, Yong-Hong Kuo, Seyedali Mirjalili, Amir H. Gandomi

entry.summary: GNBG-C is a configurable benchmark generator for constrained continuous optimization that treats constraint properties as adjustable parameters, enabling targeted study of constraint-induced difficulty.
