The compression-ranked top band exactly recovers canonical laws among 252 admitted relations with strong statistical enrichment, while revealing that 86 percent of the agent's own discoveries are statistical rather than law-like. This offers a vetting mechanism for AI-generated scientific hypotheses.

entry.title: When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?

author.name: Shao Zhang, Hangfan Zhang, Yuanyuan Shi, Hao Li, Min-Le Su, Kangcong Li, Jingping Wang, Chunjiang Mu, Chen Zhang, Yang Chen, Bo Zhang, Shuyue Hu

entry.summary: Argues that agentic benchmark scores conflate the underlying model with the execution harness, and proposes a framework with five measures to evaluate harnesses through model interactions, including Valid Completion Rate, Model-Harness Fit, Cross-Model Fit, Interaction Residuals, and Token Load.

entry.title: Closing the Modality Gap via Simplex-Constrained Representations

author.name: Shubham Gupta, Siva Reddy, Perouz Taslakian, Valentina Zantedeschi, Cem Subakan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a geometric fix for the modality gap in contrastive multimodal models like CLIP and CLAP by moving embeddings from the unit sphere to the probability simplex, using softmax adapters and Total Variation similarity. This constrains both modalities to a shared coordinate system, reducing the centroid L2 gap by 97-99% across five multimodal datasets.

entry.title: SEVI: Safe Evidential Real-World Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shaekh Mohammad Shithil, Lantao Liu

entry.summary: SEVI is a framework for safety during online reinforcement learning on physical robots, using an Evidential Safety Critic that predicts both constraint-violation risk and epistemic uncertainty in one forward pass. Unsafe or poorly supported task-policy actions are overridden by an offline-trained recovery policy. This directly addresses a key barrier to deploying contact-rich manipulation learning on real hardware.

entry.title: The LLENS Platform for On-Premises Large Language Model Agents in a Japanese University Hospital: Development and Evaluation Study

author.name: Ken Enda, Jien Saito, Masami Mukai, Feng Han, Emir Turkes, Tatsumi Kusakabe, Reona Umeki, Kazuhiro Sumiyoshi, Mitsuya Numata, Takumi Tanikawa, Akira Endoh, Kenji Hirata, Atsushi Yoshida, Kohsuke Kudo, Shinya Tanaka

entry.summary: This paper describes LLENS, a clinical support AI agent platform deployed entirely inside the closed hospital network of Hokkaido University Hospital on a single 8x H200 host running the open-weight Kimi K2.6 model (about 1 trillion parameters). The system includes ten harness components such as page-image reading, full-text attachment input, and a path-addressed document tree, aiming to offload physician EHR and desk work. It is a rare, detailed account of a production-grade LLM agent deployment in a real hospital IT environment.

entry.title: Principia: Test-Time Hypotheses to Principle Construction for Scientific Discovery

author.name: Dongki Kim, Sangwoo Park, Jinheon Baek, Soyeong Jeong, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: Proposes Principia, an LLM-based framework that constructs and continually refines scientific principles at test time, mimicking how human researchers turn accumulating observations into recurring causalities via a hypotheses-to-principle pipeline. This targets a bottleneck in AI-driven scientific discovery where translating observations into guiding principles requires substantial domain expertise.

entry.title: Tool-Calling LLM Agents Under Realistic MCP Faults: Scale Does Not Purchase Fault Tolerance

author.name: Antonio Ken Iannillo, Joshua Segun Owotogbe, Roberto Natella, Francesco Avallone, Kristina Kudryavtseva, Indika Kumara

entry.summary: The paper introduces MCP-Injector, a protocol-aware fault-injection middleware for the Model Context Protocol that emulates realistic tool failures with calibrated persistence modes mined from 57,240 issue threads across 1,774 MCP repositories. A 1,350-cell experiment across backbone sizes (20B, 120B) and agent stacks shows that larger models do not confer fault tolerance. This provides rare empirical grounding for agent reliability under realistic tool failures.

entry.title: Nested Sparsity for Scalable Pretraining and Continual Learning

author.name: Tianzhe Chu, Druv Pai, Yi Ma

entry.summary: Nestor introduces an alternative conditional-computation mechanism generalizing the attention operator whose induced sparsity nests hierarchically with MoE sparsity, producing transformers that outperform conventional MoE models at equal training budget. The nested structure also supports scalable pretraining and continual learning. This is a novel architectural direction in the MoE-dominated landscape of large-scale models.

entry.title: Speculative Diffusion is a Tale of Two Tradeoffs

author.name: Aaron Zorel, Guy Van den Broeck, Aditya Grover, Daniel Israel

entry.summary: This paper analyzes speculative decoding applied to diffusion language models, highlighting a key difference from autoregressive speculative decoding: diffusion models can trade output quality for speed by reducing diffusion effort, breaking the traditional losslessness guarantee. It formalizes the quality-speed tradeoffs involved when using diffusion models as draft models.

entry.title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions

author.name: Ammar Ali, Stamatis Lefkimmiatis

entry.summary: TWIG represents every network weight as the endpoint of a shared path of small discrete decisions (sign, power-of-two shift, zero gate, table index), so related weights share stored decisions. This unifies pruning, quantization, low-rank factorization, and weight sharing into a single framework, and with power-of-two decisions yields adder-only circuits suited to fixed-weight chips.

entry.title: Optimal Multiclass Online Regret with Arbitrary Label Spaces

author.name: Sajad Ashkezari, Shai Ben-David

entry.summary: This theory paper resolves the optimal regret rate for agnostic multiclass online learning with arbitrary, possibly infinite, label spaces, proving an O(min{T, sqrt(dT)}) bound matching the known lower bound for multiclass Littlestone dimension d. It settles an open question of Hanneke et al. (2023) and extends the optimal binary bound of Alon et al. (2021) using a novel fractional expert cover technique.

entry.title: Direction-Aware Token Credit Assignment with Reward-Model Gradients

author.name: Yikuan Hu, Jifeng Zhu, Minle Su, Jiaqin Yue, Gujie Shao, Yanzhe Chen, Haoxuan Jia, Haoran Xu, Wangzhou Dai

entry.summary: The paper introduces DATC, a method that improves token-level credit assignment in GRPO-based RLHF by mapping frozen reward-model gradients into policy logit space and weighting tokens according to the alignment between reward direction and the policy update. This replaces the uniform response-level advantage sharing that misattributes token contributions.

entry.title: OpenESM: Energy-Steered Models Are Scalable Foundation Learners

author.name: Yuan Pu, Yudong Lu, Ting Wang, Zhicong Hong, Qinuo Li, Xuansheng Wu, Na Zou, Xia Hu, Guanchu Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes energy-steered models (ESMs), an architecture that integrates energy-based modeling with token generation for foundation language modeling by optimizing a latent state over a learned energy landscape before decoding. The authors pre-train ESMs at scale to study scaling behavior, aiming to bring energy-based model benefits to general-purpose language modeling.

entry.title: Each Insufficient in Its Own Way: Calibrating Language Models Across Varying Evidence States

author.name: Jiayi Li, Dennis L. Shung, Bradly C. Stadie

entry.summary: Proposes evidence-state calibration, requiring model confidence to track how the probability of correctness changes as evidence accumulates, addressing the tendency of LLMs to answer prematurely. The SuffiCE method fine-tunes models to estimate whether available evidence is sufficient before answering.

entry.title: T2D: Target-to-Draft Model Pruning & Adaptation for Efficient Speculative Decoding

author.name: Shahriar Kabir Nahin, Xiao Ye, Muhao Chen, Ben Zhou, Anshuman Chhabra

entry.summary: T2D formulates draft-model design for speculative decoding as an optimization problem, building draft models directly from the target LLM using latency-aware structured pruning and adaptation. This explicitly balances distributional alignment with token generation speed, addressing a weakness of independently pretrained or manually pruned draft models.

entry.title: The Price of Scale in Proactive Memory Recall

author.name: Yichuan Chen, Xin Wang

entry.summary: The paper shows that deciding when a long-lived assistant should proactively surface a memory is a multiple-testing problem whose difficulty grows with store size, with false-alarm thresholds tuned at small scale reaching 87-100 percent false alarms at N=2048 on LongMemEval and LoCoMo replays. It provides a theoretical per-item false-positive characterization explaining the power-law decay of hit rates.

entry.title: SVD-Attention: Efficiently Analyzing Attention Blocks in Transformers

author.name: Debopam Sanyal, Hongjie Chen, Riya Elizabeth Kuriyan, Arth Tak, Divya Kothandaraman, Akshay Mehra, Joshua Kimball, Alexey Tumanov

entry.summary: Proposes SVD-Attention, a post-hoc method that decomposes per-head query-key interaction matrices via SVD and scores singular modes by spectral magnitude and activation variance on a small calibration set, yielding an exact factorization for retained modes without finetuning. It answers which attention heads use their full rank budget across layers and architectures. Relevant to both interpretability and potential efficiency savings in self-attention.

entry.title: Do Language Models Understand Igbo Culture? Beyond Multiple Choice

author.name: Blessing Ngozi Uzor, Valdini Douglace Lemofouet, Paula Chikaodinaka Anyanwu, Tassallah Abdullahi, Clemencia Siro, Idris Abdulmumin, Seid Muhie Yimam, Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad

entry.summary: The authors introduce CAB-Igbo, a benchmark of Igbo cultural knowledge built from indigenous sources and verified by native speakers across six domains, evaluated via multiple-choice accuracy and human judgments on epistemic fidelity, representational richness, linguistic quality, and pragmatic proficiency. Results show a sharp gap between language fluency and actual cultural knowledge in current models.

entry.title: Style over Substance? Linguistic Bias in LLM-based Peer Review Copy title

author.name: Sai Suresh Macharla Vasu, Sumedh Santosh Joshi, Philipp Christmann, Ivaxi Sheth, Ruta Binkyte, Koel Dutta Chowdhury, Raouf Kerkouche, Hui-Po Wang, Mario Fritz

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether LLM-assisted peer review is influenced by linguistic style rather than scientific substance. The authors build a controlled experimental framework that systematically rewrites papers to vary features such as native versus non-native English writing patterns, then measures how these perturbations affect LLM review outcomes. The work matters because conferences increasingly rely on LLMs to handle surging review workloads, and hidden linguistic biases could unfairly disadvantage non-native English speakers.

entry.title: Constrained Decoding: Harmful or Beneficial? Revisiting Its Impact on LLM Performance

author.name: Ngoc Trinh Hung Nguyen, Alonso Silva, Armen Aghasaryan, Mehwish Alam

entry.summary: This work challenges the assumption that constrained decoding inherently degrades LLM reasoning by defining a taxonomy of format, validity, and reasoning constraints and theoretically showing appropriate constraints can preserve or improve performance. Causal ablations across four model families and eleven open-source models suggest apparent degradation stems largely from misapplied constraint types.

entry.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Aidar Myrzakhan, Zhiqiang Shen

entry.summary: Proposes dSpark, a schedule-distillation framework for diffusion LLMs that learns which tokens to unmask first by prioritizing tokens whose reveal makes other positions easier to predict. This reduces decoding rounds by cutting uncertainty earlier, addressing a core efficiency bottleneck of parallel token generation.

entry.title: Novel or Not? PatEx-Gym: Agentic Prior-Art Search for Novelty Assessment in Patent Examination

author.name: Qiyao Wang, Xinyi Chen, Hongbo Wang, Jiayuan Lu, Jianhang Li, Minghuan Tan, Yuan Lin, Min Yang

entry.summary: PatEx-Gym is the first framework for developing and evaluating agents on the full patent examination pipeline: sparse prior-art search, iterative query refinement, evidence inspection, and documented novelty assessments. It includes 1K realistic tasks, retrieval corpora of over 1M patents and 52K papers, and a harness for training and evaluation.

entry.title: Intervention-Certified Amplification: A Validity Gate for $\sigma$-Weighted Post-Training

author.name: Leiyue Chen, Meng Wei, Xuefeng Hu, Wei Liu

entry.summary: This arXiv paper examines hybrid post-training pipelines that combine supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with per-sample weighting, showing that training-side signals can unintentionally reactivate and amplify pretrained behaviors even when their explicit surface form has been removed from the training data. The authors demonstrate this failure mode with DIAA, a per-sample sigma-weighted SFT/RL hybrid that emits unexecuted tool-integrated reasoning on a notable fraction of MATH-500 prompts, and they propose a paired-intervention validity gate to certify that emphasized behaviors actually benefit the target task and evaluation setting.

entry.title: Entropic Control for Homeostatic Optimization: Pre-empting Catastrophic Forgetting via Dynamic Feedback

author.name: Shangxi Wu, Xiaorong Yan, Xiaojun Meng, Yuxiang Zhang, Jiansheng Wei

entry.summary: This paper introduces ECHO, a closed-loop control framework that mitigates catastrophic forgetting during supervised fine-tuning of LLMs. By decomposing KL divergence and identifying output entropy as a dominant observable component, ECHO uses entropy as a cheap online proxy for forgetting risk, allowing an elastic controller to dynamically modulate replay-data gradient weights without expensive reference-model inference.

entry.title: Correlation-Aware Exploration for Long-Trace Reasoning

author.name: Junxing Hu, Zicheng Zhang, Zhiqian Zhang, Ai Han, Yifeng Zhang, Pengzhang Liu, Ling Li

entry.summary: The paper analyzes why entropy regularization in GRPO conflicts with the entropy decay required for convergence in long-trace reasoning training, since it uniformly pushes probability mass toward the low-probability vocabulary tail at every token. It proposes Info-GRPO, an information-theoretic framework that cultivates correlation between policy and reasoning trace to regulate exploration more selectively.

entry.title: Trainable Boundary-Keeping Where No Formal Answer Exists: A Controlled Knock-In Study of Reward Training in Evidence-Sufficiency Judgment

author.name: YaJie Yin

entry.summary: This paper tests whether reward-trained and reasoning-tuned models actually judge evidence sufficiency more reliably in domains where correctness is undecidable. Using a pre-registered controlled knock-in design comparing an SFT-then-GRPO boundary-keeping recipe against scrambled-pairing placebos and baselines, with masked model-rated outcomes, it examines whether reward training improves calibration of epistemic limits rather than raw reasoning length.

entry.title: Saga: an in silico ontology for a multimodal patient world model

author.name: Youcheng Li (Peking University, Isoplex Lab), Fa Tian (Isoplex Lab), Binbin Su (Peking Union Medical College, Isoplex Lab)

entry.summary: Saga is a multimodal patient world model that learns a shared patient state from histories to predict clinical events and generate multimodal medical images, appending generated events and times back into the history to advance trajectories without real intermediate observations. It was studied on 461,370 patients across 12 cancer types and 112 centres.

entry.title: OvisOCR3 Technical Report

author.name: Yu Xia, Yinglun Li, Yuhui Chen, Jinlong Huang, Yuyang Wanyan, Shengze Shi, Yifei Song, Yue Duan, Shubo Lin, Jianshan Zhao, En Lin, Shiyin Lu, Qing-Guo Chen, Zhao Xu, Weihua Luo

entry.summary: Introduces OvisOCR3, a compact 0.8B model unifying document parsing, general OCR, key information extraction, figure captioning, and cross-page table reconstruction in one system. Training combines continued pretraining on real and synthetic data, domain-balanced mid-training, multi-teacher on-policy distillation from five 4B domain teachers, and mixed-task reinforcement learning with domain-specific rewards.

entry.title: World-in-Context: Interactive Video World Modeling with In-Context Conditioning

author.name: Harold Haodong Chen, Rui Peng, Rongjin Guo, Lingteng Qiu, Kejie Qiu, Chao Xu, Zilong Dong

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces World-in-Context, an interactive video world modeling framework that unifies control over viewing perspective, character action, and camera motion through In-Context Conditioning. Instead of using separate conditioning pathways, the method encodes all controls as explicit tokens within a shared self-attention space, disentangling view dynamics from camera motion and other previously conflated signals. This matters because interactive world models are central to gaming, simulation, and embodied AI applications, and cleaner control factorization could improve their usability and fidelity.

entry.title: Mix Forcing: Causal Pre-Training via Mixture Attention for Interactive World Models

author.name: Zelin Gao, Hao Ouyang, Jiapeng Zhu, Qiuyu Wang, Jingye Chen, Zichen Liu, Xing Zhu, Yujun Shen, Yinghao Xu

entry.summary: Mix Forcing introduces a causal pre-training paradigm for interactive video world models using Mixture-of-Bidirectional-and-Autoregressive attention, jointly applying teacher forcing and bidirectional training. This avoids the degradation of visual priors that occurs when converting bidirectional video diffusion models to autoregressive generation. It addresses a key challenge for building interactive generative world models.

entry.title: PhysCreator: Creating Physically-Attributed 3D Assets at Will

author.name: Shiyan Zheng, Ming Li, Lei Han, Xiangyu Xu

entry.summary: PhysCreator generates simulation-ready 3D representations with spatially varying physical properties directly from images, using a voxel-aligned latent space that lifts image observations into structured 3D. This reformulates physical property estimation as unified representation learning rather than post-hoc prediction or per-instance optimization.

entry.title: Regional prediction of hematoma expansion from non-contrast computed tomography in spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage patients

author.name: Natasha Ironside, Hongyu Kan, Kristofor Pas, Mohammad Shifat-E-Rabbi, Benjamin Newman, Shinjini Kundu, Kareem El Naamani, Tanvir Rizvi, Andrea Becerril-Gaitan, Harrison Snyder, Aarathi Manchikalapudi, Sarah Ratcliffe, Stacie L. Demel, Carl D. Langefeld, Daniel Woo, Stephan Mayer, E. Sander Connolly, Gustavo Rohde, for the ERICH Investigators, the VISTA-ICH collaboration

entry.summary: This medical imaging study builds an interpretable, region-based model using transport-based morphometry on non-contrast CT scans to predict hematoma expansion in intracerebral hemorrhage patients. It derives the model from the ERICH study and validates it on the independent VISTA-ICH archive, directly tying imaging predictions to clinical outcomes.

entry.title: When Pointing Becomes Profiling: Social Bias and Refusal in Text-Steerable Visual Encoders

author.name: Seyedarmin Azizi, Parsa Razmara, Sajjad Ghiasvand, Ardalan Aryashad, Tina Khezresmaeilzadeh

entry.summary: This audit of the released SteerViT text-steerable visual encoder shows its language-driven pointing interface enables demographic profiling: prompts like 'the person' over-select men, crime words over-select Black people, and counterfactual tests reveal strong racialized pointing absent from the backbone's unsteered saliency. The work demonstrates that steering interfaces can inject social bias not present in the frozen backbone.

entry.title: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images

author.name: Junyeong Ahn, Geonwoo Kim, Kinam Kim, Gihwi Kim, Hoonjin Jung, Hyojin Jang, Jaegul Choo

entry.summary: OmniShowcase is a subject-to-video generation method that produces omnidirectional, subject-consistent videos from a few multi-view reference images, explicitly modeling the 3D structure connecting viewpoints so unseen surfaces can be rendered coherently. It also introduces training data designed to guarantee that viewpoint changes preserve the same underlying 3D subject, addressing a key weakness of prior multi-view S2V approaches. This advances controllable, 3D-aware video generation, an area of active industrial and academic interest.

entry.title: Does VGGT Know What It Does Not Know?

author.name: Adityan Thirumani Srinivasan, David Nordstr\"om

entry.summary: Investigates uncertainty in feed-forward 3D reconstruction models like VGGT, showing that a linear probe on frozen internal features predicts pose failure far better (93.5 ROC-AUC on hard pairs) than the model's own point-map confidence. This enables downstream abstention on unreliable pose predictions.

entry.title: WebUniverse: Scaling Verified Training Data for Agentic Web Development

author.name: Yaorui Ding, Fengqing Jiang, Yichen Feng, Yuetai Li, Zhangchen Xu, Kaiyuan Zheng, Xuanyu Lu, Bhaskar Ramasubramanian, Basel Alomair, Luyao Niu, Radha Poovendran

entry.summary: Presents a pipeline that constructs verifiable web development tasks and verified agent trajectories from open-source repositories and real web pages, spanning text-grounded and vision-grounded settings. Releases WebUniverse-Env with 15K executable task environments plus a trajectory mix to scale training data for front-end web agents.

entry.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants

author.name: Qinsi Wang, Wei Wen, Chong Zhou, Saksham Suri, Zechun Liu, Lemeng Wu, Hai Helen Li, Yiran Chen, Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi, Qi Qian

entry.summary: Introduces InteractiveWorld, the first verifiable closed-loop environment for evaluating egocentric MLLM assistants that interact with human users on wearable devices, avoiding costly real-human interaction data. It enables systematic testing of whether today's multimodal models can genuinely assist people with physical tasks such as guidance and reminders.

entry.title: Triage: Skip, Skim, or Refine Attention Tiles in Video Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Yeonjae Kim, Omin Kwon, Seong Hoon Seo, Jae W. Lee

entry.summary: Triage is a training-free method that accelerates video diffusion transformer inference by assigning each attention tile one of three approximation tiers: skipping it via block-mean replacement, computing it in NVFP4 low precision, or refining it with NVFP4 plus residual correction. The key insight is that approximation error varies widely across tiles, so a per-tile routing decision outperforms uniform policies. This matters because attention over tens of thousands of visual tokens dominates video DiT inference cost.

entry.title: RAIWAY: A Large-Wheeled Bipedal Robot with Contact-Informed Blind Locomotion

author.name: Kyungmin Nam, Jiseong Lee, Donghyuk Choi, Jeongsoo Park, Woojin Kim, Jemin Hwangbo

entry.summary: Introduces RAIWAY, a custom wheeled bipedal robot with 20-inch wheels, plus a contact-informed locomotion controller for rolling over irregular, discontinuous terrain. The method distills simulation contact events into a latent representation inferred online from proprioception, removing the need for contact sensing, and demonstrates real-world traversal of slopes and gravel.

entry.title: POD-RoPE: Rotary Position Encoding over Physical Observation Distributions for Embodied AI

author.name: Xiaodi Huang, Zilin Wang, Jinpeng Liu, Pengchuan Xiao, Zhenlei Shao, Zhang Zhang, Shuxiang Lu

entry.summary: POD-RoPE extends rotary position encoding to represent token observation footprints as distributions over camera centers, viewing directions, and sampling times, with expected rotations encoding inter-distribution relationships and recovering pointwise RoPE in the degenerate case. The same statistics guide both Q/K matching and coherence-dependent V/O transformations for embodied perception.

entry.title: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions

author.name: Haoyu Zhao, Xingyue Zhao, Zhian Su, Bohan Hou, Yinzhou Tang, Fengyi Wang, Kehan Li, Yuming Jiang, Siteng Huang, Xin Li, Zhenyu Zeng, Mingxiu Chen, Deli Zhao, Zhongyu Li

entry.summary: Presents RynnVLA-Latent, which learns continuous 3D-grounded latent actions from visual transitions without native robot controls, combining residual future-feature prediction, camera-compensated 3D-flow supervision, and camera-motion decoupling. Applied to 30.1K hours of human, robot, and simulation video, it produces 745.52M latent action labels to pretrain manipulation foundation models, addressing scarce action labels and incompatible control spaces.

entry.title: Scaling Dexterous Manipulation via Action Representation Pretraining

author.name: Yanjinghao Xu, Jiexin Zhang, Huan Zhao, Jianjia Mo, Zhenghao Yin, Dingkang Liang, Xiang Bai, Han Ding

entry.summary: ARPG explicitly separates action representation learning from action generation, pretraining action representations so that downstream generative models are not forced to learn both from scarce robot demonstrations. This mirrors the successful pretrain-then-generate recipe from vision and language and targets dexterous manipulation, where demonstration data is the key bottleneck. The separation idea could become a standard recipe for manipulation policy scaling.

entry.title: Robot-Aligned 3D Gaussian Splatting for Precise Reaching with Wrist-Camera VLA Policies

author.name: Zuoxu Wang, Xiao Liang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a 3D Gaussian Splatting based data-generation pipeline for adapting wrist-camera vision-language-action policies to precise pre-contact reaching, targeting e-waste disassembly where digital twins are impractical. It reconstructs the real workspace and maintains camera-action alignment to generate training data without full simulation models. This is a practical alternative to sim data for VLA fine-tuning.

entry.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy

author.name: Yifei Yao, Yude Zou, Guanbo Jiao, Xing Gao, Ning Gao, Yukai Wang, Jiantong Chen, Zihou Zhu, Xinyu Li, Ningyu Yan, Shuai Wang, Jianming Ma, Haoyu Guo, Weinan Zhang, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: This report introduces EBench, a benchmark for evaluating how frontier multimodal LLM agents control robots compared to post-trained vision-language-action (VLA) and world action model (WAM) policies. The authors profile GPT-6-Astra, an established OpenAI model, in two configurations: direct waypoint control and a harness setup where the agent can delegate action execution to a specialized policy, using identical visual and proprioceptive observation protocols across methods. The work matters because it provides a systematic way to measure when general-purpose agents should invoke robot-specific policies versus acting directly.

entry.title: Adapt for Planning, Not just Prediction: Optimistic Test-Time World Model Adaptation

author.name: Akshay Mete, Dileep Kalathil, P. R. Kumar

entry.summary: Argues that prediction-only test-time adaptation of latent world models can leave the model wrong about goal-reaching actions, since the planner only observes outcomes of its own chosen actions. Inspired by reward-biased maximum likelihood estimation, the paper proposes an optimistic TTA objective that adapts world models in a closed loop to improve planning under distribution shift.

entry.title: HIFI: A Highly Efficient Framework for Statistical Inference with Foundation Models

author.name: Po-Wei Chen, Shan Yu, Chunlin Li

entry.summary: HIFI is a two-stage fine-tuning framework for valid statistical inference on parameters like conditional means using foundation models, replacing the hundreds of model fits required by resampling-based inference with a single bias-controlled stage-1 fit on a larger sample followed by a lighter stage 2. This addresses the computational intractability of classical inference procedures at foundation-model scale.

entry.title: Solvent: Long-Horizon Reasoning for Multi-Step Retrosynthesis

author.name: Yifei Wang, Botian Wang, YiFei Wang, Jiangtao Feng, Xinbo Zhang, Yawen Ouyang, Yixin Wu, Lihao Wang, Xiaoqing Zheng, Xuanjing Huang, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: Solvent is an 8B LLM that extends long-horizon reasoning to multi-step retrosynthesis, recursively transforming target molecules into purchasable building blocks. A two-round post-training curriculum teaches the model to interleave iterative search with environment interaction and feedback adaptation. This brings frontier-style long-horizon LLM reasoning to a practical chemistry planning task.

entry.title: What Open-Source Projects Tell Their Coding Agents: A Census of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md

author.name: Pawel Zarzycki

entry.summary: This census analyzes agent instruction files across 22,854 active GitHub repositories, finding such files in 26.3% of repositories and 59.6% of the most-starred, and annotating 341,852 statements about project knowledge, code rules, and workflow requirements. Notably, 74% of directives give no rationale, raising questions about instruction quality for coding agents.

entry.title: Controlled Evaluation of EEG Foundation Models: Random Initialisation, Band-Power and Validation-Selected Probes

author.name: Mingyu Jeon, Suwan Cho, Jae Young Suh

entry.summary: Under a single protocol with three missing controls (untrained encoder, band-power baseline, validation-selected probe layer), the authors re-evaluate five public EEG foundation models plus an in-house JEPA-style model across benchmarks. Controls substantially change conclusions: test-set layer selection inflates results, and random initialization often matches or beats pretraining.

entry.title: Do VLAs Know They Will Fail? Interpretable Success and Failure Patterns in Physical AI Systems

author.name: Christian A. Rogers, Qian Lin, Daniel S. Brown

entry.summary: Shows that sparse autoencoder (SAE) representations of OpenVLA activations contain outcome-predictive information and can predict task failure before a robot enters an unrecoverable state. The work identifies individual SAE features linked to specific success/failure stages, localizes temporal intervals of behavioral change, and demonstrates the usefulness of these signals for physical AI systems.

entry.title: Earth embeddings are decomposable records of the land surface

author.name: Robin Young, Srinivasan Keshav

entry.summary: The authors decompose two widely used annual satellite Earth-embedding products and show they contain individually recoverable ecological features — fire, forest clearing, crop type — validated against independent reference events across six continents, including distinguishing prescribed fire from wildfire and dating canopy loss. This establishes what these embeddings actually encode.

entry.title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yijing Ke, Tianle Cai, Ruosong Wang

entry.summary: The paper shows that inference-training implementation differences in BF16 make intended on-policy LLM RL updates off-policy, and that selectively aligning rounding locations in RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm stabilizes training without full stack alignment. Experiments across four Qwen-family models validate the fix.

entry.title: Learning Positive Linear Combinations of ReLUs in Fully Polynomial Time

author.name: Ilias Diakonikolas, Jelena Diakonikolas, Puqian Wang, Nikos Zarifis

entry.summary: This theoretical paper gives the first fully polynomial time algorithm for PAC learning positive linear combinations of k arbitrary ReLU activations under the Gaussian distribution in L2 loss. The algorithm uses poly(d, k, 1/epsilon) samples and time, improving on prior methods that required super-polynomial time or strong conditioning assumptions, via a novel boosting procedure for weak learners.

entry.title: TraceQuery: learning what to recompute from full-denoising trajectory in diffusion language models

author.name: Yukai Jin, Zhankai Ye, Jiayue Yang, Fangyi Li, Shuoqiu Li, Xu Gao, Shibo Li, Xin Liu, Shangqian Gao

entry.summary: TraceQuery tackles the high inference cost of diffusion large language models (dLLMs), which arise from repeatedly recomputing token representations across denoising steps. The authors show that decoding trajectory proximity to the full-denoising process, rather than fixed schedules or heuristics, is the key quantity governing cache-based accuracy, with errors tied to unmask-order deviations. Building on this insight, they learn which positions to recompute, improving the efficiency of dLLM inference.

entry.title: A Russian, a Brazilian, and a German Walk into a Bar, Ask the Same Question-- And Get Three Different Answers: Profiling LLM Perspective Diversity on Contested Topics

author.name: Wiem Ben Rim, Yao Lu, Pontus Stenetorp, Emine Yilmaz

entry.summary: The authors introduce PerspectivesQA, a manually verified multilingual dataset of globally contested topics in 18 languages, and ROOTS, a framework profiling linguistic, perspective, and framing diversity in LLM answers. Evaluations of eight open and proprietary models show LLMs hedge their answers and vary in perspective diversity across languages.

entry.title: An Algorithmic Account of Few-Shot Concept Induction in Language Models

author.name: Michael A. Lepori, Laila Johnston, Aalok Sathe, Zhuonan Yang, Roman Feiman, Ellie Pavlick

entry.summary: The paper proposes Amortized Direction Accentuation (ADA), an algorithmic hypothesis explaining how language models identify and promote context-relevant features during few-shot concept induction, involving a summary representation of examples in feature space. The work connects in-context learning mechanisms with cognitive-science accounts of feature relevance, with authors from Brown's Ellie Pavlick group.

entry.title: TIAgent: From Natural Language to Grounded Agentic Workflows for Computational Pathology

author.name: Aakash Madhav Rao, Mark Eastwood, Danielle Belgrave, Fayyaz Minhas

entry.summary: Introduces TIAgent, a DeepMind-affiliated framework that converts natural-language analytical requests into verifiable computational graphs for tissue image analysis in computational pathology, addressing hallucinated operations by verifying workflows automatically. Aims to make multi-step CPath analyses accessible to pathologists without programming expertise.

entry.title: Task Success Is Not Enough: Side-effect-Aware Evaluation of Tool-Using Language Model Agents

author.name: Jiaju Huang, Shaobin Chen, Xinglong Liang, Xinyu Ma, Hao Yang, Wei Ke, Tao Tan, Yue Sun

entry.summary: The paper identifies collateral damage as a distinct agent failure mode: completing the requested task while taking unauthorized side-effecting actions like writing to the wrong object or contacting unintended recipients. SABench provides 201 email, calendar, and ticket tasks crossing four state structures with four trap families, each with a deterministic trace-based oracle.

entry.title: Mechanistic Insights into LoRA: Layer Sparsity for Adaptive Fine-Tuning via Path Patching

author.name: Fei Zuo, Yizhou Huang, Kezhi Wang

entry.summary: The paper applies mechanistic interpretability techniques, including path patching, to analyze how LoRA adaptation affects model internals, finding highly non-uniform, layer-sparse effects where important layers are strongly task-dependent. Motivated by this, Adaptive-LoRA uses a calibration-driven method to automatically identify and adapt only task-relevant layers.

entry.title: ThinkBit: Search Codewords, Recalibrate Scales, Select by Reasoning

author.name: Rhea Sanjay Sukthanker, Pashmina Cameron

entry.summary: ThinkBit is a strictly scalar two-bit quantization framework designed to preserve reasoning ability in LLMs, storing each weight as an integer codeword times a shared bfloat16 group scale. It uses a sensitivity metric to allocate ternary, 2-bit, or 3-bit tiers per layer, then calibrates scales, targeting the observation that standard perplexity and multiple-choice metrics fail to capture degraded reasoning after aggressive quantization.

entry.title: Do vision models know that three is three?

author.name: Ankit Sonthalia, Arnas Uselis, Seong Joon Oh

entry.summary: Tests whether 46 vision encoders encode abstract concepts consistently across visually unrelated regimes (e.g., the 2-to-3 transition in digits versus hand gestures), extending the linear representation hypothesis to vision. The study spans architectures, training objectives, and scales on ten concept transformation types.

entry.title: Video World Models Need Predictable Latents

author.name: Mattia Scardecchia, Sherry Yang

entry.summary: Shows that video world models for robot policy learning can benefit from latents optimized both for dynamics predictability and observation reconstruction, bridging the gap between reconstruction-trained autoencoders and latent-planning world models. The proposed latent geometry aims to improve long-horizon rollouts, out-of-distribution generalization, and inference cost.

entry.title: RoKON: Efficient and Adaptive Data-Enabled Predictive Control for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Akshun Sharma, Zhongqi Wei, Buqing Ou, Frederike D\"umbgen

entry.summary: RoKON advances data-enabled predictive control (DeePC) toward real-time robotic manipulation by using a Gaussian-kernel nonlinear predictor, a damped Gauss-Newton solver exploiting least-squares structure, and a hybrid buffer management strategy blending informative online data with relevant offline data. This removes the need to learn an explicit dynamics model while keeping control fast enough for real-time use. It addresses the main obstacle to DeePC deployment on robots.

entry.title: PaperFormalizer: Author-in-the-Loop Autoformalization of Research Papers in Lean

author.name: Jiyuan Tan, Vasilis Syrgkanis, Jose Blanchet

entry.summary: PaperFormalizer is an agentic pipeline that converts research papers from LaTeX into Lean-verified formal proofs, building a dependency graph of statements, auditing them for faithfulness and correctness, and proving them against Mathlib and author-specific toolkits. Crucially, it uses an author-in-the-loop design, pausing to ask the author how to resolve ambiguities or fix formalization gaps—since only the author knows what a statement was intended to say. This could make machine-checked proofs of published results far more accessible.

entry.title: Understanding Communication Failures in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Priya Pitre, Jun Hou, Yi Fang, Naren Ramakrishnan, Xuan Wang

entry.summary: The paper builds a corpus-grounded taxonomy of communication failures in multi-agent LLM debate and collaboration systems from 3,211 failed multi-round trajectories across six task domains. It analyzes failure distributions, round-level error dynamics, recovery hardness, and minority-signal suppression, showing interactions can introduce failures invisible in final accuracy alone.

entry.title: DELA: Learning Controllable Edits for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xinsong Feng, Chenan Wang, Leshu Tang, Johnny Liu, Dong Li, Da Li, Haipeng Chen

entry.summary: DELA is a plug-in framework for diffusion language models that enables explicit, controllable draft refinement with a frozen base model using four editing actions: Insert, Delete, Remask, and Stop. A learned controller decides when and where to edit while the frozen DLM fills masked regions, separating edit control from denoising.

entry.title: RxnExBench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Structured Chemical Reaction Extraction from Scientific Literature

author.name: Jiaxing Sun, Junyuan Gao, Ruikang Zhang, Hao Zheng, Lingli Ge, Xiao An, Jiang Wu, Huazheng Zeng, Jiahe Song, Chen Zhu, Haote Yang, Jingchao Wang, Lu Chen, Yuanyuan Cao, Ruijie Zhang, Shengxin Lu, Weijia Li, Lijun Wu, Conghui He

entry.summary: RxnExBench is a multimodal benchmark for extracting structured chemical reaction data from information-dense figures in synthetic chemistry papers, with 3,565 expert-annotated reactions and 2,361 molecular structures under a unified schema of 15 roles and 26 fields. It supports downstream AI-for-chemistry tasks like retrosynthetic planning and yield prediction, and includes a difficulty taxonomy and the Oracle-MolRec protocol. This enables rigorous evaluation of scientific document understanding.

entry.title: POSEIDON: Scaling Training Environments for Scientific Agents from Code Repositories

author.name: Qifan Zhang, Yuhan Li, Nuo Chen, Bowen Liu, Xiao Hu, Miao Peng, Chenyi Zi, Lixin Liu, Lydell Huang, Jing Tang, Jia Li

entry.summary: Introduces an automated pipeline that generates diverse, verifiable training environments for scientific agents from scientific code repositories, extracting nearly ten times as many environments as a prior approach. It decomposes workflows into four task types (Reproduction, Subflow, Completion, Correction) and adds a recursive improvement loop for quality.

entry.title: RubricCraft: Where Solutions Diverge, Criteria Emerge

author.name: Hosein Hasanbeig, Priyanshu Gupta, Ashish Tiwari, Vu Le, Sumit Gulwani

entry.summary: RubricCraft constructs textual evaluation rubrics by comparing independently sampled solver trajectories, deriving criteria from where candidate solutions satisfy or violate task requirements rather than from task descriptions alone. This targets evaluation of open-ended, artifact-producing tasks where model-based graders are inconsistent and programmatic checks impractical.

entry.title: Effectiveness of Curriculum Learning Depends on Reward Sparsity and Competing Optima

author.name: John J. Vastola, Ann Huang, Satpreet H. Singh, Samuel J. Gershman, Kanaka Rajan

entry.summary: Using a minimal, analytically tractable open-loop target interception task, the authors mathematically and numerically analyze REINFORCE dynamics to explain when curriculum learning helps in RL versus supervised settings. The theory ties curriculum benefits to reward sparsity and the presence of competing optima.

entry.title: Head Dimension Matters in Language Models for Long-Context Retrieval

author.name: Seiya Tokui, Shoichiro Yamaguchi, Sosuke Kobayashi

entry.summary: Empirically shows that head dimension in multi-head attention affects long-context retrieval while leaving pretraining loss and short-context tasks largely unchanged: at fixed model sizes, wider heads improve long-context retrieval and contain a higher proportion of retrieval heads. This provides actionable architectural guidance for designing long-context language models.

entry.title: Semantic Representation for Agentic Self-Play in Automated Laboratories

author.name: Yves Delley, John Coller, Zachary Cutts, Alexander Daryin, Mathias Bellaiche, Jun W. Kim, Oscar Donosa, Srinidhi B. Seshadri, Tanner Clary, Sandy Klemm, Avinatan Hassidim, Yossi Matias, Pooja Rao, Petar Sirkovic, Annalisa Pawlosky

entry.summary: The paper introduces VERID, infrastructure bridging AI agent reasoning and physical wet-lab execution via a persistent, high-fidelity semantic digital twin of the laboratory workspace. It supports agentic self-play across ideation, experimentation, and automation to explore high-dimensional biological search spaces beyond local optima. The author list suggests Google affiliation, lending credibility to this autonomous-science effort.

entry.title: When and How Does Muon Precondition? The Role of Structured Gradient Noise

author.name: Xiaoran Chen, Binghui Li, Liwei Wang, Pinyan Lu

entry.summary: This paper gives theoretical and empirical analysis of when the Muon optimizer actually helps, showing that under isotropic gradient noise Muon provides no acceleration beyond learning-rate rescaling, and that its benefits arise from structured noise in mini-batch sampling with heterogeneous task frequencies. It derives an exact balancing threshold for two tasks and extends to many tasks. Muon is widely used for LLM training, so clarifying its foundations is valuable.

entry.title: Decode Late, Multiply Once: Rethinking the Dot Product for Quantized Weights

author.name: Jonathan Tapson

entry.summary: The paper refactors low-bit-weight dot products so each weight code acts as an address offset into one of 2^k accumulators, with decode and multiplication performed only once at the end, reducing a length-n dot product to n+2^k additions plus at most 2^k decodes and multiplications. The refactoring is exact for integer arithmetic and supports nonlinear decoders, with direct implications for efficient quantized inference hardware.

entry.title: Principled Nonlinear Concept Erasure and Steering

author.name: Idan Simai, Shauli Ravfogel, Uri Shaham

entry.summary: This paper introduces a conditional autoencoder framework for nonlinear concept erasure of sensitive attributes (e.g., gender, race) with formal guarantees, following the principle that erasure should remove only the sensitive attribute and nothing else. It bridges the gap between linear erasure methods with guarantees and nonlinear methods with strong empirical but no formal erasure properties.

entry.title: Neural LoFi with Backward Coupling: A Spectral Theory of Cross-Layer Feature Learning

author.name: Yatin Dandi, Matteo Vilucchio, Hugo Tabanelli, Florent Krzakala

entry.summary: The authors extend Neural Low-Degree Filtering, a layer-wise spectral surrogate for feature learning, to capture backward coupling from backpropagation, deriving a local coupling between a neuron's incoming weights and its next-layer column. They show dynamics amplify singular modes of a cross-layer correlation operator, pairing earlier features with upper-layer responses.

entry.title: Singular Geometry of Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Kamillo Ferry, Anthea Monod, Keisuke Yano

entry.summary: The paper analyzes LoRA as a singular statistical model using the real log canonical threshold from singular learning theory, characterizing how learning complexity depends on the low-rank parameterization and the pretrained network via a forward-backward covariance of activations and sensitivities. This provides a theoretically grounded account of when and why LoRA fine-tuning is statistically efficient. It connects parameter-efficient fine-tuning to algebraic geometry of learning.

entry.title: Merge-Based Vocabulary Extension Stalls at the Pre-Tokenizer: An English-Preserving Repair for Nepali, Tested in Continued Pretraining

author.name: Aarjan Chaudhary (Naamche Labs)

entry.summary: The paper shows that the Unicode-letters-only pre-tokenizer regex used by Llama-3, Qwen3, and other open LLMs splits Nepali words at Devanagari vowel signs, causing 2.6-5.8x token inflation that merge-based vocabulary extension cannot fix (a floor around 2.2x). A small regex edit provably preserves all existing token ids and, with 32,000 new merges, brings Nepali tokenization to 1.01x of English in continued pretraining experiments.

entry.title: Five Architectures, One Shared Space Cross-Model Representational Alignment Without Weight Merging

author.name: Oladimeji Anthonio, Dimeji Olawuyi, Oloruntoba Ajayi, Temilola Aderemi

entry.summary: Shows that five frozen, independently trained models with different architectures (four transformers from different organizations plus one state-space model) exhibit statistically robust correspondence in how they represent the same text, strongest at final layers, enabling a shared representational space without weight merging.

entry.title: MTA-Zero: Self-Improving Multimodal Deep Search via Online QA-Solver Co-training

author.name: Xiangyu Peng, Jiaxin Zhang, An Yan, Yu Li, Ran Xu, Zeyuan Chen, Chien-Sheng Wu

entry.summary: MTA-Zero is an online co-training framework for self-improving multimodal deep-search agents that eliminates the need for precomputed multi-hop corpora. Starting from image-grounded VQA seeds, a trainable QA Generator retrieves evidence and constructs verified multi-hop questions online while a separate deep-search solver improves against them. This addresses the distribution-staleness problem of fixed offline question corpora in agentic web search.

entry.title: Efficient Proof Generation for Lean Statements with Multiple Candidate Answers

author.name: Pengzhen Lin, Ke Zhang, Maziar Raissi, Zhouxing Shi

entry.summary: The authors propose a joint proof framework for Lean 4 that unifies candidate answer selection, answer supplementation, and formal proof generation in a single reasoning call by a trained prover, avoiding redundant per-candidate proof search. Generated proofs can also be reused to check and filter other candidates.

entry.title: Position Matters More Than Channel: Talking a Language Model Out of a Correct Answer

author.name: Xinyi Ni

entry.summary: Disentangles three confounded factors in LLM sycophancy and persuasion studies: position of contrary advice in the prompt, attributed author, and the model's prior output. Experiments on Qwen3.5-27B with MMLU-Pro show position matters far more than the API channel, with bare claims and arguments having opposite position effects. This clarifies experimental design for studies of model persuadability and multi-party context robustness.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Long-Session Degradation in Full-Duplex Speech Models

author.name: Junho Kim, CheHyun Lee, Donghun Kang, Youngho Cho, Dongwook Lee, Heeseung Kim, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: Introduces a closed-loop evaluation framework for long-session stability in end-to-end full-duplex spoken dialogue models, revealing degradation over time in responsiveness, spoken content quality, and voice characteristics. The paper also develops efficient mitigation methods for this degradation. Important for deploying real-time speech agents that must remain stable over extended interactions.

entry.title: MATCHA: A Chinese Multi-Disorder Mental Health Dataset with Cross-Lingual Analyses on Social Media

author.name: Bingrui Jin, Baihan Li, Zitong Li, Kunyao Lan, Shimeng Li, Kenny Q. Zhu, Mengyue Wu

entry.summary: MATCHA is the first Chinese multi-disorder mental health dataset linking disorder-specific Weibo communities with users' broader timelines, covering seven DSM-5 disorders plus controls with 46,025 users and 1.8 million posts. It uses an LLM-assisted annotation pipeline to distinguish explicit self-disclosure from broader disorder-related participation and is released de-identified under controlled access, enabling cross-lingual mental health analyses.

entry.title: LLM-as-a-Judge Version Shift: The Instrument Changed, Not the Standard

author.name: Guijia Zhang, Harry Yang

entry.summary: Uses a preregistered, frozen-weight design to test whether replacing an LLM judge with a newer same-family version preserves the measurement standard, across Qwen, Gemma, and Mistral transitions. Finds the newer-is-harsher assumption fails: version changes alter score location, criterion geometry, and re-ranking behavior, undermining longitudinal comparability of automated pipelines.

entry.title: Implicit Beliefs as Scalable Process Rewards for Strategic Persuasion

author.name: Minqian Liu, Yuexi Shen, Heajun An, Qi Zhang, Pamela J. Wisniewski, Sang Won Lee, Jin-Hee Cho, Lifu Huang

entry.summary: The paper introduces PersuArena, a simulation environment for multi-turn strategic persuasion with realistic, psychologically grounded persuadees, and proposes using online belief elicitation as dense process rewards for RL training. This addresses sparse outcome-only rewards and expensive LLM-judge process supervision by tracking the persuadee's implicit belief state.

entry.title: Counterfactual Test-Time Augmentation for Shortcut Removal in Language Models

author.name: Katie Matton, Rosalind W. Picard, John Guttag, Maggie Makar

entry.summary: This paper proposes counterfactual test-time augmentation (CTTA) for removing shortcuts from LLM predictions without retraining: an auxiliary model generates counterfactual edits changing the shortcut value, and the LLM's predictions across edits are averaged, with theory characterizing the optimal shortcut-invariant predictor. This avoids requirements of training-time solutions like labels, weight access, and heavy compute.

entry.title: Birth, Death and Diff: Insertion-Based Sequence Generation with Corrections

author.name: Durga Prasad Maram, Dhruvesh Patel, Tahira Naseem, Benjamin Rozonoyer, Gaurav Pandey, Ram\'on Fernandez Astudillo, Andrew McCallum

entry.summary: The paper introduces delta-MDM, an insertion-based masked diffusion language model augmented with substitution and deletion operations that make intermediate generation decisions revisable. This reduces error accumulation under aggressive parallel decoding and lowers the required number of forward passes compared to irreversible insertion-only models.

entry.title: Agent Memory as Recommendation: Recommender-System Design for Long-Term Memory of LLM Agents

author.name: Xinyu Zhang, Weiwei Sun

entry.summary: This paper formalizes LLM agent long-term memory selection as budgeted slate recommendation, where each request must choose which stored memories enter a limited context window under a per-request cost budget. The reframing imports recommender-system design principles to address a large and growing memory store, per-request cost constraints, and multi-session evidence needs.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Done Right for Explicit Confidence Targets

author.name: Zefeng He, Yichen He, Yuan Lin, Yang Yang, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: The paper addresses explicit confidence targets, where a user specifies a target accuracy p in the prompt and the model must learn to answer or abstain so answered questions achieve at least p accuracy, noting that fixed error penalties in prior RL abstention methods cannot adapt at inference time. It develops an RL training approach enabling a single model to honor varied confidence targets.

entry.title: Skill$^{\infty}$: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Skill Optimization

author.name: Wangcheng Tao, Zhanglu Yan, Han Wu, Weng-Fai Wong

entry.summary: Skill-infinity makes agent skill optimization recursively self-improving: a meta agent follows a meta-skill to optimize task skills and simultaneously optimizes the meta-skill itself using the same procedure, removing the hand-designed pipelines of prior skill optimizers. This positions skill libraries as a direct lever for recursive self-improvement on the path toward more capable agents.

entry.title: Rescuing Your Pruning: Rethinking Visual Token Pruning and Post-Training Recovery in MLLMs

author.name: Peiran Yin, Hao Wu, Zihao Yang, Haozhe Hu, Xudong Wang, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies how much of the performance loss from visual token pruning in multimodal LLMs can be recovered through post-training, curating a 282K-sample mixture and evaluating 36 drop/merge configurations. It finds post-training rescues most of the loss, even for OCR and grounding, enabling more aggressive joint compression. This reframes pruning research away from increasingly complex training-free rules.

entry.title: From Sentinel-2 to 1-m Imagery: Real-World $\times 10$ Cross-Sensor Super-Resolution via Visual Autoregressive Modeling

author.name: Tailai Chen, Yuluxin Fu, Jie Deng, Shu Luo, Yanan Wu, Danfeng Hong

entry.summary: The paper tackles realistic 10x cross-sensor super-resolution from Sentinel-2 satellite imagery to 1-meter commercial imagery, where no synthetic degradation operator links input and reference. It contributes YREB-SR, a large benchmark of over 11,500 geographically matched Sentinel-2 and Jilin-1 scene pairs, and applies visual autoregressive modeling to this extreme upscaling regime.

entry.title: Back to Basics: A Skill-Centric Approach to Generalist Web Agents

author.name: Minh Pham-Dinh, Md Farhan Ishmam, Hernan Yupanqui, Reaz Hassan Joarder, Kenneth Marino

entry.summary: Introduces MiniWeb, a miniature web environment of 65 interconnected sites with 369 human-annotated tasks labeling 37 reusable interaction primitives across 7 skill families, enabling skill-level diagnosis of web agent failures. It also proposes MiniWebGen to autonomously generate verified skill-centric training data, addressing the finding that drag and gesture interactions are consistently weakest.

entry.title: Behavior Spatial Benchmark: Evaluating Spatial Understanding for Robotics

author.name: Sirui Chen, Huang Huang, Qineng Wang, Wenlong Huang, Manling Li, Ruohan Zhang, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu

entry.summary: Presents BEHAVIOR-Spatial, a benchmark on BEHAVIOR-1K with 3,256 spatial QA questions, 1,240 grounding queries, and action evaluations across manipulation and navigation tasks, testing how VLM spatial understanding connects to VLA behavior. Baselines achieve only 41.6% on held-out configurations, revealing large gaps between task success and genuine spatial instruction following.

entry.title: Organon : From Evolutionary Search to Recursive Self-Improving Agents for Scientific Discovery

author.name: Cheikh Ahmed, Zhiyu Zhang, Kun Mao, Yong Zhang, Zirui Zhou

entry.summary: Organon is a recursively self-improving LLM agent for scientific discovery that, during execution, analyzes its accumulated experience and autonomously revises its own search strategies, population management, diagnostics, memory, and worker coordination. This moves beyond fixed evolutionary search procedures to agents that adapt their own methodology at runtime.

entry.title: Bracketing Shows the Way: Adaptive Multi-Exposure Policy as Input for Robust Visual SLAM

author.name: Olivier Gamache, Anthony Lavertu, David-Alexandre Duclos, Jean-Michel Fortin, Fran\c{c}ois Pomerleau, Philippe Gigu\`ere

entry.summary: Presents B-Adapt, which captures adaptive exposure brackets covering scene dynamic range, and BVSLAM, which uses multi-exposure sequences directly as constraints in a factor-graph VSLAM without HDR merging. Evaluated against SOTA methods including tunnel-exit transitions at emulated vehicle speeds of 32 m/s, showing robust tracking where conventional AE saturates.

entry.title: MOTIO: Agentic Skill Engineering for Reality-Grounded Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: SpatialtemporalAI

entry.summary: MOTIO is an agentic system that converts human-action videos, reality-grounded 3D assets, and motion references into executable humanoid loco-manipulation programs, refined via physics execution and human validation without teleoperation data. Reported median agent-turn time is 97 minutes across 33 timestamped first approvals.

entry.title: RobotAgentBench: Towards Open-world Robot Autonomy

author.name: Lingjun Mao, Jinglin Cao, Lukun He, Wenpeng Xu, Yuchen Yan, Hengyu Jin, Zijun Zhang, Jinzhou Tang, Songyao Jin, Ziche Liu, Yifei Shao, Junbo Huang, Fang Nan, Ruobing Han, Ziqiao Xi, Ziming Xu, Shuang Liang, Sibo Zhu, Wenyi Wu, Xinyue Wang, Yiming Huang, Xinkai Zou, Gao Zhu, Kun Zhou, Biwei Huang

entry.summary: RobotAgentBench evaluates robot agents on open-world autonomy in realistic household environments, integrating task discovery, contextual reasoning, physical execution, and adaptive recovery into a closed interaction loop rather than isolated capabilities. It uses an agent-assisted, human-in-the-loop real-to-sim pipeline to build the benchmark. This fills a gap left by benchmarks that test only predefined manipulation tasks.

entry.title: RetroNav: Scene-Grounded Retrospection and Retry for Self-Evolving Lifelong Navigation

author.name: Diantao Tu, Yangdong Liu, Niannian Dai, Mengqi Rong, Shuhan Shen

entry.summary: RetroNav is a training-free framework for lifelong robot navigation that unifies memory accumulation, failure reflection, and retry, connecting semantic and geometric scene knowledge with historical navigation experience. This lets the robot learn from past mistakes across repeated episodes in the same environments. It addresses a real limitation of prior lifelong navigation work that stored scene knowledge but not actionable experience.

entry.title: Environment Edits as a Corrective Signal for Reward Learning

author.name: Isaac Ngui, Courtney McBeth, Nancy M. Amato

entry.summary: The paper proposes environment edits as a new corrective feedback channel for reward learning: the human edits the scene while the robot's motion is held constant, so the edit unambiguously attributes preference to the moved object. The FERRET system learns preferences from both robot corrections and environment edits, disambiguating features that robot corrections alone cannot express. This is a clever extension of learning from corrective feedback.

entry.title: EAST: Embodied AI Safety Testing via Systematic Fault Injection in Digital Twins

author.name: Yuhao Tian, Tao Li, Ling Zhou, Dave Towey, Zhaoxin Fan, Wenjun Wu, Rubing Huang, Tsong Yueh Chen

entry.summary: Introduces EAST, a digital-twin framework that converts literature-grounded safety evidence into systematic fault-injection tests for embodied AI across perception, instructions, environments, actions, and timing. It combines an expert-reviewed safety-fault taxonomy with eight executable operators and a three-stage workflow that generates, verifies, and validates fault-based test cases.

entry.title: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Using Routed Ensembles and Trajectory Attribution

author.name: Zhenshuo Zhang, Ruoxuan Xiong, Hongyang R. Zhang

entry.summary: Tackles multi-objective RL where optimal policies vary sharply with objective weightings, introducing objective-conflict coefficients and near-optimal regret bounds for online settings. It proposes routed ensembles with trajectory attribution to learn policies balancing competing objectives such as helpfulness versus honesty in alignment or speed versus energy in robotics, improving sample efficiency over per-preference policy learning.

entry.title: Model Selection for Off-Policy Evaluation via Pairwise Bellman Validation

author.name: Lars van der Laan, Vasilis Syrgkanis, Nathan Kallus

entry.summary: The paper introduces pairwise Bellman validation (PBV), a tuning-free minimax procedure for selecting among candidate Q-functions and occupancy-ratio estimators in off-policy evaluation using only held-out transitions. PBV builds critics from pairwise candidate differences, avoiding auxiliary regressions and separate critic classes required by prior validation methods.

entry.title: The Ability of Frontier Models to Control Robots is Rapidly Improving

author.name: chrisleet

entry.summary: The post reports benchmark results showing general-purpose multimodal LMs increasingly capable of directly controlling real robotic arms, with performance between July and October 2026 implying a doubling time of about 54 days: the best execution rate rose 4.4x while the lowest execution cost fell 6.2x. The authors observe models are currently limited by physical efficiency rather than reasoning, rarely getting stuck. A companion paper was submitted to TAG@CoRL, grounding the claims in a documented methodology.

entry.title: Adaptive Control of Scientific Instruments with Nonstationary Responses through Multimodal Agents

author.name: Guoyang Shi, Hongwen Li, Yiding Yu, Zhuang Fu, Siqi Ding, Zhengyuan Chen, JianGuo Chen, Hanyue Zhao, Tianyuan Liu

entry.summary: The paper presents a physically grounded multimodal agent for adaptive control of scientific instruments whose responses are nonstationary, demonstrated on shot-to-shot tuning of neutral beam injection ion sources in fusion devices. The system has three independently auditable components and handles evolving unobserved conditions where static action-to-response mappings fail. It represents AI agents moving into real-time experimental control in high-cost scientific facilities.

entry.title: Sparsity-driven emergence of functional modularity in multitask neural networks

author.name: Bowen Shi, Qi Ouyang, Long Qian

entry.summary: Demonstrates that sparsity-inducing regularization promotes functional modularity in multitask networks without predefined module boundaries, producing compact task-selective subnetworks termed functional tokens. Retaining these tokens preserves associated functions while degrading others, and specialization emerges preferentially in deeper layers while earlier layers stay shared, offering insight into how networks organize shared computation.

entry.title: Reasoning or Just Prompting? Probing the Mechanism of Latent Chemical Reasoning

author.name: Kaiyuan Lu, Jiatong Li, Yatao Bian

entry.summary: This mechanistic study tests whether intermediate latent states in latent-reasoning models form a causally important implicit reasoning chain in chemistry, finding that swapping or moderately perturbing latent states has little effect while full removal sometimes hurts. The authors conclude latent states primarily steer subsequent model behavior rather than encoding step-by-step reasoning.

entry.title: What Effort Level Should I Choose? On the Economics of Reasoning Effort in LLM Agents

author.name: Kaiser Sun, Yongchan Kwon, Zain Hasan, Shang Zhu, Kaitlyn Zhou, Federico Bianchi

entry.summary: The paper frames reasoning-effort settings in LLMs as a credence good and measures the counterfactual effect of effort levels on proprietary and open-weight models across four benchmarks, including long-horizon agentic tasks. Findings show effort does not consistently help and can even harm performance relative to lower settings, informing cost-benefit decisions about inference-time compute.

entry.title: Detection of false positives by human reviewers depends on the face recognition algorithm and its security configuration

author.name: Esha Edakoth, John J. Howard, Isabelle M. Shuggi, Yevgeniy B. Sirotin, Robert Wood

entry.summary: Using the new DFICT dataset built from false positives of four commercial face recognition algorithms, the authors measured 801 human reviewers' ability to detect algorithmic false positives across varying security configurations. The results show human oversight effectiveness depends on the specific algorithm and its configuration, raising concerns about human-AI teaming in identity workflows.

entry.title: The Locality Trade-off in Masked Patch Self-Distillation

author.name: Xi Weng, Zhaoyu Liu, Lianyu Hu, Jin Song Dong

entry.summary: Analyzes masked patch self-distillation as used in DINOv2 and DINOv3, showing its semantic benefits coexist with a scale-dependent locality cost: smaller models lose patch correspondence when iBOT is added, while larger models preserve correspondence but lose linear access to pixel and texture evidence in deep features. Uses annotation-free diagnostics separating local appearance from spatial correspondence and analyzes Gram anchoring as mitigation.

entry.title: HA-DiPO: Diffusion Policy Optimization for Heterogeneous Cooperative Transport

author.name: Xuebin Li, Jinpeng Xiao, Zong Chen, Pierluigi Arpenti, Bruno Siciliano, Jiebao Sun, Yiqun Li

entry.summary: HA-DiPO is a hierarchical multi-agent RL framework under CTDE for cooperative transport with heterogeneous legged robots carrying an unfixed shared payload. A high-level diffusion coordination policy trained with a centralized team-value critic aligns robot-specific actions with a shared objective, while low-level embodiment-specific controllers track commands.

entry.title: Context-Aware Generation and Modulation of Expressive Motion Behavior using Multimodal Foundation Models

author.name: Till Hielscher, Fabio Scaparro, Kai O. Arras

entry.summary: This work uses multimodal foundation models (text, audio, video inputs) to generate and modulate expressive full-body robot gesture sequences, grounded in a unified mathematical implementation of animation principles via Dynamic Movement Primitives. The approach is interpretable, composable, transferable across robot morphologies, and integrated into a real system. It connects the generative-AI wave with social human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Reproducible Evaluation as the Substrate for Safe Prompt Compression in Production Agents

author.name: Prabal Vashisht, Zheng Hu, Ying Yang

entry.summary: The paper presents an offline evaluation harness for a production conversational agent that remains reproducible despite live backend data changing, and regenerates when stale. Using this harness as a fitness function with a correctness gate, GEPA-based prompt optimization compresses a production merchant-facing agent's prompt by 3.5-7.6% without regressing task correctness.

entry.title: BARC-Bench: Benign Asks, Risky Consequences

author.name: Kangkang Li, Kelvin Luu, Lily Ma, Tu Trinh, Ying Liu, Mohamed Elfeki

entry.summary: BARC-Bench is a safety benchmark of 110 tasks across nine simulated workspace environments where benign user requests create openings for unsafe agent actions, testing whether agents respect safety boundaries established by workspace records, implicit environmental context, and unstated social norms. One example involves an agent that must schedule an off-boarding meeting without leaking an employee's resignation via a shared calendar invite. Evaluations of four frontier model configurations across five attempts per task probe how reliably agents handle underspecified safety constraints.

entry.title: Who Verifies the Tools? How Warped Formatters Mislead Agents and Their Verifiers

author.name: William Jeffries

entry.summary: This paper shows that tool output formatters can misrepresent what tools actually did, misleading LLM agents and their verifiers even when the underlying tool computation is correct. Drawing on incidents in a production RAG system at the Pilsudski Institute, the authors run controlled experiments comparing omitted-information formatter wording with repaired wording and quantify how much accurate phrasing improves agent and verifier behavior. It matters because it identifies an underappreciated reliability failure mode in agentic systems that sits at the interface layer rather than in model reasoning.

entry.title: When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zongyao Zhao, Cheng-Jie Zhao, Ruihang Jiang, Bing Zheng, Zhaolin Wang, Yuanwei Liu

entry.summary: Addresses a flaw in GRPO for vision-language-action models where a single trajectory-level advantage penalizes all actions in a failed rollout, including useful recovery attempts. Using success-probability and policy-score martingales, the authors characterize principled stopping conditions at which truncating gradient feedback preserves the expected reference gradient while reducing covariance.

entry.title: Advancing SVD-based LLM Compression via Layer-Wise Error Model Search

author.name: Moritz Thoma, Maximilian Groezinger, Maximilian Forstenh\"ausler, Emad Aghajanzadeh, Manoj Rohit Vemparala, Christos Anagnostopoulos, Pierpaolo Mori, Nael Fasfous, Alexander Frickenstein, Daniel Mueller-Gritschneder, Ulf Schlichtmann

entry.summary: This paper introduces LEMS and KFAC-SVD to improve low-rank SVD compression of large language models. LEMS uses a layer-wise error surrogate with integer linear programming for global rank allocation, while KFAC-SVD leverages token-wise statistics to avoid the rank collapse of Fisher-based decompositions.

entry.title: End-to-End Differentiable Diffusion Conditioning for Physics-Informed Optimization

author.name: Ricardo Luna Gutierrez, Vineet Gundecha, Rahman Ejaz, Varchas Gopalaswamy, Riccardo Betti, Sahand Ghorbanpour, Aarne Lees, Soumyendu Sarkar

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces Differentiable Diffusion Conditioning (D2C), a method for offline model-based optimization of high-dimensional physical systems. By exploiting deterministic sampling to make the reverse denoising chain differentiable with respect to the conditioning signal, D2C refines candidate designs against precise physical objectives, addressing limitations of prior approaches such as conservative behavior and unconstrained surrogate exploitation. The work targets scientific and engineering applications where objective evaluations are expensive and constraints are complex.

entry.title: PrefO2O: Zero-Shot Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning via Offline-to-Online Latent Preference Transfer

author.name: Ruiqi Wang, Dezhong Zhao, Xuesu Xiao, Erdem Biyik, Byung-Cheol Min, Guohua Chen

entry.summary: PrefO2O enables zero-shot preference-based RL on unseen tasks by learning a task-invariant latent preference space from offline preference data on source tasks, disentangling transferable preference structures from task-specific variations. This removes the need to collect new human preference labels for every target task.

entry.title: Spectra: Multi-Scale Implicit Decomposition for Deepfake Detection

author.name: Dhananjaya Jayasundara, Kartik Narayan, Vishal M. Patel

entry.summary: Spectra uses implicit neural representations to expose how an image is reconstructed rather than how it appears, providing generator-agnostic cues for deepfake detection that complement RGB and frequency-artifact approaches. A multi-scale implicit decomposition improves generalization across unseen manipulation techniques, compression levels, and dataset shifts.

entry.title: 4DMemory: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Spatiotemporal Memory with Harness-Augmented Agents

author.name: Yanhao Jia, Yi Zhu, Yiran Zhong, Weigao Sun, Feida Zhu, Pengkun Jiao, Sihan Yang, Ming Ma, Steven Hoi, Erik Cambria

entry.summary: Introduces the LongVideo dataset (~900 hours of video, 5,000+ manually reviewed questions) and 4DMemoryBench for evaluating long-horizon spatiotemporal reasoning, plus the 4DMemory Harness integrating four complementary skills and 22+ tools to augment agents. The work targets the gap between short-context benchmarks and the persistent fine-grained memory humans build over hours-to-years multimodal streams.

entry.title: Beyond Local Accuracy: Benchmarking the Rollout Reliability of PDE Foundation Models

author.name: Jaewan Park, Seid Koric, Giri Krishnan, Sudhakar Pamidighantam, Surresh Marru

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates whether the short-horizon accuracy advantages of PDE foundation models persist under autoregressive rollout over long horizons, introducing an error amplification metric across seven models and seven time-dependent PDE datasets. It reveals that short-horizon gains do not necessarily translate into reliable long-horizon simulation.

entry.title: Compatible Likelihoods for Flow Matching on Manifolds

author.name: Lucas Ng, Georgios Batzolis, Mark Girolami

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode of Riemannian flow matching on the flat torus where the globally optimal velocity field pushes samples away from the data, tracing it to a property called compatibility of the likelihood objective. It provides a general compatibility condition, bounds worst-case error, and proposes compatible objectives avoiding infeasible velocity densities on compact manifolds.

entry.title: Accordion: Elastic-Depth Inference via Fixed-Prefix Layer Looping

author.name: Yudong Zhang, Wei Ding, Kaili Zheng, Yuchen Ding, Zhenyu Zhang

entry.summary: Accordion is a mixture-of-experts model supporting five inference budgets through fixed-prefix layer looping, trained by sampling one budget per micro-batch with plain next-token prediction, with the smallest budget equal to the unlooped model. It aims to give a single pretrained model elastic compute-cost levels without maintaining separate models per budget.

entry.title: On the Identifiability of Hybrid Deep Generative Models: Meta-Learning as a Solution

author.name: Yubo Ye, Maryam Toloubidokhti, Sumeet Vadhavkar, Xiajun Jiang, Huafeng Liu, Linwei Wang

entry.summary: This work provides the first theoretical probe into identifiability of hybrid deep generative models that embed physics-based expressions in neural generative models. It shows how existing non-identifiability theory extends to hybrid models and proposes meta-learning as a constructive route to provable identifiability.

entry.title: TRACE: Data-Free Text Reconstruction Attacks against Approximate Unlearning in LLMs

author.name: Mengying Zhang, Derui Wang, Ibrahim Khalil, Bowen Liu, Xiaoyu Xia, Minhui Xue

entry.summary: TRACE demonstrates that approximate unlearning in LLMs leaves residual traces recoverable from pre- and post-unlearning model snapshots, enabling reconstruction of the very training data unlearning was meant to remove. The paper introduces a data-free attack framework that exploits this auditing/rollback side channel, revealing a previously overlooked privacy risk in practical unlearning deployments.

entry.title: KnitTrans: Coordinated Trajectory Transfer for Effective and Efficient LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Bangjun Xiao, Chiheng Lou, Xiaodong Ji, Xiangwei Deng, Yikai Zhao, Gang Huang, Hailin Zhang

entry.summary: KnitTrans addresses the rollout-to-training data transfer bottleneck in LLM reinforcement learning systems, introducing constraint-preserving mini-batch admission and coordinated payload movement to reduce staleness and redundant communication. The system targets the growing architectural staleness gap introduced by disaggregated RL pipelines. This is significant infrastructure work as RL-based post-training scales.

entry.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs

author.name: Thomas Landeg, Thierry Tambe

entry.summary: The authors introduce Backtrack, a lightweight failure detection and recovery mechanism for frozen vision-language-action (VLA) robot policies. A small prediction head trained on outcome-labeled rollouts reads the VLA's internal representations to predict failure; when failure is predicted, a controller pauses the policy and retraces the arm's recent motions, requiring no recovery demonstrations, retraining, or extra inference models.

entry.title: How Does Post-Training Shape LLM Value Preferences?

author.name: Yang Liu, Shaoyang Xu, Masahiro Kaneko, Chengzhi Zhong, Wenxuan Zhang, Chenhui Chu

entry.summary: Runs controlled experiments with post-training corpora containing different demographic opinion mixtures across five post-training paths (SFT, DPO, GRPO variants). Finds that post-training amplifies opinion imbalances differently depending on the path, and whether further training can remove amplified preferences depends on the training method.

entry.title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents

author.name: Yihao Hu, Zhihao Wen, Yitong Lin, Siyuan Lu, Pan Wang, Wei Wu, Jiang-Ming Yang, Tao Lin
