entry.summary: Argues that successful tool-use trajectories can be poor supervision due to missing compositional coverage and ungrounded actions, and introduces Trajectory2Gym to synthesize executable interactions targeting under-supported compositional structures with supervision derived only from decision-grounded actions.

entry.title: When Personas Become Harmful: Guiding LLMs with Global Citizenship Values Alignment

author.name: Siqi Shen, Lajanugen Logeswaran, Moontae Lee, Honglak Lee, Rada Mihalcea

entry.summary: The authors build an 11k-example dataset of controversial topics paired with value-based personas mapped to Schwartz Value Survey dimensions and use an agentic refinement pipeline to surface harms emerging from persona-conditioned requests. Unlike adversarial safety benchmarks, these harms are not overtly malicious, so standard alignment methods miss them, causing models to either refuse legitimate value expression or comply with unsafe personas. The work proposes values-based guidance as a middle path.

entry.title: Higher Reasoning Effort Improves Reference Verifiability and Changes Reasoning Summaries in GPT-5.5

author.name: Melika Mobini, Andres Algaba, Vincent Ginis

entry.summary: This empirical study analyzes GPT-5.5 (an existing OpenAI model) generating scholarly references for 1,000 papers under paired low- and high-reasoning-effort settings, matching outputs to external bibliographic records and scoring reasoning summaries. It finds higher reasoning effort improves reference verifiability and measurably changes reasoning-summary behavior.

entry.title: LADDER: Diagnosing Domain-Level Self-Assessment Under Noisy Feedback

author.name: Zhenshuai Yin, Jianshu Liang, Xuyue Xiong, Yongxin Guo, Mingda Zhang, Zhongze Luo, Haoyue Liu, Lianmin Zhang, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: LADDER studies how language models form domain-level self-assessments under unreliable interaction feedback, finding that models can accurately report supplied performance information yet fail to build trustworthy self-assessments from experience, with apparently accurate assessments obscuring capability differences. It argues self-assessment should be validated against observed task performance and predictive value.

entry.title: DynEdit: Dynamic Entropy-Guided Sequential Editing for Large Language Models

author.name: Jinhu Fu, Yan Bai, Yihang Lou, Li Sun, Jiahong Wu, Xiangxiang Chu, Sen Su

entry.summary: Presents DynEdit, a knowledge editing framework for long-sequence targets in LLMs that uses token entropy to identify hard-to-edit, information-dense regions and dynamically allocates editing effort there. It improves on single-point editors with limited coverage and fixed chunk-based editors that distribute effort uniformly. This is a practical efficiency and accuracy improvement for updating model knowledge without retraining.

entry.title: Ask Before You Answer: A Question-Driven Evidence Reasoning Architecture (QERA) for In-Context Learning

author.name: Jinhu Qi, Minda Hu, Wentao Zhang, Zixing Song, Irwin King

entry.summary: Proposes QERA, an architecture for in-context learning over real-life user traces that first converts a request into a requirement checklist of implicit rubrics before retrieving and reasoning over evidence, motivated by findings that frontier LLMs solve fewer than one in five CL-bench Life tasks and that over 80% of rubrics share under 60% content words with the request. Direct-answering LLMs pass only 67% of implicit rubrics versus 81% of explicit ones. Addresses the gap between what users ask and what they actually want.

entry.title: High Scores, Hidden Failures: Evaluating Codebook-Based LLM Content Analysis

author.name: Elena Senger, Yuri Campbell, Rob van der Goot, Barbara Plank

entry.summary: This large-scale empirical study examines LLM-based codebook annotation pipelines used in computational social science across four datasets and five models, systematically testing stability, robustness, and conceptual validity under perturbations and domain shifts. It reveals multiple failure modes invisible to standard aggregate metrics, showing high scores can coexist with unreliable annotations.

entry.title: From Self-Confidence to Statistical Accuracy: Scaling Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation with Direct and LLM-Assisted Auditing

author.name: Harine Choi (Texas A&M Transportation Institute, Texas A&M University System), Chenchen Kuai (Zachry Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Texas A&M University), Zihao Li (Department of Civil, Construction and Environmental Engineering, Marquette University), Jiwan Jiang (Zachry Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Texas A&M University), Yunlong Zhang (Zachry Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Texas A&M University), Zhiwen Fan (Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Texas A&M University), Zhengzhong Tu (Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Texas A&M University), Yang Zhou (Zachry Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Texas A&M University)

entry.summary: Develops a unified statistical framework for auditing LLM and MLLM outputs, combining confidence-stratified sampling for direct human audit with LLM-as-a-judge assisted auditing. Provides finite-sample uncertainty guarantees and shows miscalibrated self-confidence can still enable efficient accuracy estimation.

entry.title: Of Chains and Gains: What Reinforcement Learning changes on Reasoning-based Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Yixuan Li, Yuxuan Jiang, Hanwei Zhu, Hancheng Zhu, Fan Zhang, Shiqi Wang, David Bull

entry.summary: This paper rigorously tests whether reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) genuinely improves reasoning in vision-language models for image quality assessment, or whether gains are mostly sampling effects. Through sampling-aware evaluation, controlled reasoning interventions, and shortcut experiments, it finds RL-trained models mainly win under large-budget max_g@k evaluation and that improvements beyond averaging concentrate in-distribution.

entry.title: AndroidFlux: Evaluating and Reward Modeling Failure Recovery Capabilities in Mobile Use Multimodal Agents

author.name: Gyubeum Lim, Yemo Koo, Ghunwoo Jang, Zsolt Kira

entry.summary: AndroidFlux is a failure-recovery benchmark built on AndroidWorld that restores recorded trajectories to controlled checkpoints before, at, and after the first recoverable error, letting different agents resume from identical device states. It isolates the previously unmeasured ability of mobile multimodal agents to detect and recover from intermediate failures.

entry.title: Improving Reasoning with Rollout Agreement for Group-Based Policy Optimization

author.name: Sohyun Son, Yerim Hong, Jaeyun Park, Mujeen Sung

entry.summary: Through blind paired analysis of a GRPO-trained model, the authors find that low-agreement correct-answer traces contain more spurious reasoning than high-agreement traces (35 percent versus 22 percent), including internal inconsistencies and misuse of problem conditions. Based on this, they propose using rollout agreement to improve group-based policy optimization in RLVR.

entry.title: Integrate the Reward, Don't Sample It: Window Likelihood for Interruptions and Backchannels in Full-Duplex Speech Models

author.name: Guoqiang Hu, Lichao Zhang, Yizhou Peng, Yuhao Luo, Haifeng Hu, Sallen Sun, Will Yang, Eng Siong Chng

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses two failure modes of sequence-level GRPO with binary timing rewards in full-duplex speech dialogue models: a zero-gradient trap on exactly the windows needing learning, and credit leakage from spreading one rollout score over unaddressed listening decisions. It proposes window likelihood, which integrates over binary control decisions in closed form instead of sampling a known reward function.

entry.title: Oddin: Latent Visual Reasoning in Unified Multimodal Models via Self-Distillation from Image Generation

author.name: Jaeyong Ko, Hankyeol Kim, Pilsung Kang

entry.summary: Proposes Oddin, a framework for latent visual reasoning in unified large multimodal models that replaces intermediate generated images with compact latent tokens handled by the understanding branch, reserving image generation for the final output. Trained via offline self-distillation with generation, text-distillation, and cross-entropy objectives. This reduces the heavy computational cost of interleaved text-image chain-of-thought while keeping unified generation ability.

entry.title: TrackTok: Object-Centric Video Tokenization with Semantically Persistent Tokens

author.name: Nhi Pham, Christopher Wewer, Bernt Schiele, Jonas Fischer, Jan Eric Lenssen

entry.summary: TrackTok is a video tokenization framework producing object-centric tokens that consistently encode the same semantic objects across time despite movement, deformation, and occlusion. This yields more compact latent video representations for downstream generative flow models while preserving semantic structure. Relevant to efficient video generation and world modeling.

entry.title: Semantic Concept Steering Breaks the Explanation Drift Loop in Continual Learning

author.name: Yehonatan Elisha, Oren Barkan, Noam Koenigstein

entry.summary: This paper identifies a structural flaw in explanation-aware continual learning: pixel-level saliency regularization supervises from the model's own frozen saliency maps, creating a self-referential drift loop that reinforces spurious attention across tasks. The proposed C3L method anchors regularization to class-consistent semantic concepts, breaking the loop and reducing explanation drift while maintaining accuracy.

entry.title: Birth-Death Structural Learning for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Quan Tran Hong, Long Nguyen-Chi, Binh T. Nguyen

entry.summary: Replaces heuristic cloning, splitting, and pruning rules in 3D Gaussian Splatting with first-variation birth-death control, a principled variational criterion for deciding where new Gaussians should be allocated and which can be pruned. This directly targets the multi-view reconstruction loss rather than proxy signals like gradients or opacity.

entry.title: GUIFlow: Temporal Redundancy-Aware Incremental Inference for GUI Agents

author.name: Ye Li, Haoran Ding, Huanan Liu, Yuan Meng, Yutian Shen, Yuansong Wang, Kangye Ji, Hanyun Cui, Hongbo Duan, Chen Tang, Jiawei Li, Shu-Tao Xia, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: GUIFlow addresses the high cost of multi-step GUI agent inference by avoiding recomputation of overlapping visual representations across interaction steps. It introduces full-pipeline incremental inference that selectively updates computational states across trajectories instead of rebuilding them, adapting to evolving context and interface changes.

entry.title: Joint Latent Reasoning and Observation for Agentic Video Understanding

author.name: Junzhang Liu, Hao Yuan, Qi Zhang, Yiming Wu, Long Chen, Zhecan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces LARVA, a framework that distills multi-round video agent behavior into smaller models by replacing textual captions with compact continuous latent representations passed between an observer and a reasoner. The reasoner jointly selects where to acquire further visual evidence and when to answer. This addresses the problem that text descriptions omit cues needed to guide subsequent observation.

entry.title: Printed and Scanned: Exposing the Fragility of Single-Image Morphing Attack Detectors under Print-Scan Degradation

author.name: Diogo J. Paulo, Hugo Proen\c{c}a, Jo\~ao C. Neves

entry.summary: This paper examines how print-scan degradation, a real-world step in some passport issuance pipelines where applicant photos are printed and re-scanned, undermines single-image morphing attack detection (S-MAD) systems. The authors show that benchmarks like SYN-MAD22, which operate purely in the digital domain, overstate detector robustness, since halftoning and scanning artifacts alter the statistics that detectors rely on. The work highlights a significant gap between lab evaluation and operational border-control conditions, with implications for biometric security in identity document issuance.

entry.title: From Speech Tokens to Stolen Voices: Attacker-Chosen-Text Speaker Impersonation via Representation Inversion

author.name: Ye Lu, Shen Wang, Runze Liu, Zhitao Ou, Haonan Huang, Yihan Yan, Fanghui Sun, Zhaoyang Zhang

entry.summary: Demonstrates a Speech Token Inversion Attack showing that speech representations transmitted from on-device frontends to remote servers leak speaker identity, enabling an attacker to generate speech in a victim's voice with attacker-chosen text from a single short sample. This exposes a previously underappreciated privacy risk in end-to-end speech language model architectures.

entry.title: CounterFlow: Target-Conditioned Flow Matching for Visual Counterfactuals

author.name: Paul Sevellec, Elisa Fromont, Romaric Gaudel, Laurence Roze, Paul Viallard, Laetitia Houeix

entry.summary: CounterFlow uses conditional flow matching with target-conditioned vector fields to generate visual counterfactual explanations, steering a source image toward a user-specified target class. It achieves state-of-the-art realism and target-class switching on standard benchmarks with substantially lower computational cost than GAN- or diffusion-based approaches.

entry.title: MedVTok: A General-Purpose Medical Visual Tokenizer

author.name: Chenglong Ma, Yuanfeng Ji, Junzhi Ning, Jiyao Liu, Yujie Wei, Shaohao Rui, Chaoyang Zhang, Wenjie Li, Wenhao Tang, Cheng Tang, Wei Li, Shujian Gao, Yujie Zhang, Ying Chen, Zilong Li, Zongyuan Ge, Diping Song, Jin Ye, Ming Hu, Junjun He, Hongming Shan

entry.summary: MedVTok is a general-purpose visual tokenizer that maps 2D images and 3D volumes from diverse medical imaging modalities into a unified token space, providing a common visual interface for multimodal medical AI. It tackles two challenges—preserving anatomical structure across dimensions and capturing clinical semantics across modalities—using techniques such as slice differential regularization to model inter-slice anatomical relationships. This could reduce fragmented, modality-specific representations in medical foundation models.

entry.title: A Dynamic Decomposition Strategy for the MOEA/D With Proven Performance Guarantees

author.name: Benjamin Doerr, Martin S. Krejca, No\'e Weeks

entry.summary: This paper proposes the first dynamically adjusted decomposition scheme for the MOEA/D multi-objective evolutionary algorithm in discrete bi-objective optimization, backed by a rigorous runtime guarantee. The authors state this is the first proven runtime analysis of a dynamic multi-objective evolutionary algorithm, demonstrating advantages on distorted LOTZ benchmarks where static decompositions fail.

entry.title: Interpretable Collision Avoidance and Feasibility Guarantees through an Uncertainty Aware Pipeline

author.name: Doris Xu, Jin Hyun Park, Guadalupe Alvarado Fernandez, Adhyan Prasad, Mark Campbell

entry.summary: Proposes a modular perception-prediction-planning pipeline for autonomous vehicles that propagates uncertainty as interpretable structured quantities, providing simultaneous collision-avoidance guarantees and real-time feasibility in dynamic scenes like intersections and roundabouts. It addresses the gap between chance-constrained planners that become infeasible and deterministic planners that ignore uncertainty.

entry.title: Tiny Recursive Policy: Recursive Latent Refinement for Visuomotor Control

author.name: Hakan Aktas, Cengiz Oztireli

entry.summary: TRP is a parameter-efficient behavior-cloning policy for manipulation that maintains persistent temporal latent state and recursively refines high- and low-level latents with a shared computation module before decoding action sequences. It performs competitively on LIBERO-100, MetaWorld ML45, and LIBERO-Mem benchmarks.

entry.title: VLA-HWBench: Where the Time Goes When VLA Models Run on Edge Hardware

author.name: Borui Xu, Hongshi Tan, Wenqi Jiang, Bingsheng He, Ming Wu, Jason Zeng, Michael Heinrich

entry.summary: VLA-HWBench benchmarks 18 open VLA models across NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor and AMD Ryzen AI Max+ hardware with a seven-stage inference breakdown, quantifying how latency constrains closed-loop robot control on edge devices. It identifies action-generation strategy as the dominant factor and compares inference optimizations on the same models, addressing a gap since most VLA work reports only task success. This is the kind of systems grounding VLA deployment has lacked.

entry.title: How Tuning, Reference Preview, Actuator Modeling, and Fallback Policies Change Quadrotor Controller Comparisons: A Reproducible Simulation Study

author.name: Xuan-Quy Dao, Le-Minh Nguyen, Ngoc-Bich Le

entry.summary: A large-scale reproducible simulation study (over 2000 episodes across primary and confirmation studies) quantifying how tuning effort, reference preview, actuator modeling, and optimizer fallback change the ranking of standard quadrotor controllers such as PID, LQR, sliding-mode, MPC, and geometric SO(3). It shows that single tracking-error comparisons are misleading without controlling for these factors. This is valuable for benchmarking hygiene in aerial robotics.

entry.title: Contract-Based Agentic Systems Engineering: Delegation as Quotient for Assured System Design

author.name: Sai Sandeep Damera, Ryan Matheu, John S. Baras

entry.summary: Proposes an assume/guarantee contract framework for agentic systems, showing that a component generated from a prompt can satisfy the prompt yet violate system-level assumptions of its neighbors. It formalizes delegation as a quotient over SysML v2 requirements and shows Signal Temporal Logic is closed under the quotient, enabling assured decomposition of system requirements into agent component contracts.

entry.title: Prior-Data Fitted Networks for In-Context Off-Policy Evaluation

author.name: Shuguang Yu, Ting Li, Fan Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes InCOPE, a prior-data fitted network pretrained on synthetic OPE tasks over MDPs and behavior-target policy pairs, which then performs in-context off-policy evaluation on new tabular decision problems. This amortizes OPE across tasks, addressing the difficulty of evaluating policies when behavior data are limited and the target policy visits rarely observed states.

entry.title: The Noise-Transmission Burden of Diffusion Network: Why Image Prediction Can Outperform Noise Prediction

author.name: Gyeonghun Kang, Pengxi Liu, Bingshuo Qian, Xiang Cheng

entry.summary: The paper explains theoretically why x-prediction can outperform epsilon-prediction in finite diffusion networks despite population-level equivalence: noise prediction must preserve input information to cancel corruption, and a rank-r input bottleneck imposes a sigma-squared times (d-r) error floor. It connects this to design choices like EDM attention.

entry.title: Ambiguous Fits: The Rashomon Effect and Challenges in Scaling Law Estimation

author.name: Bruno Mlodozeniec, Spencer Frei

entry.summary: The paper examines the often-overlooked fitting stage of neural scaling law estimation, showing that standard heuristic non-convex optimization can fail to find near-optimal fits and can obscure the Rashomon effect where fundamentally different parameterizations fit the data comparably well. This has direct implications for how much trust to place in extrapolated scaling predictions used for frontier model planning. It argues for more careful, uncertainty-aware fitting methodology.

entry.title: DMAIC-Bench: From Self-Reflection to Self-Restraint for Agents in Multi-Stage Analytical Tasks

author.name: Shan Peng, Shuaiqi Cheng, Miao Peng, Chenyi Zi, Jia Li

entry.summary: DMAIC-Bench measures self-restraint, the ability of LLM agents to let evidence change their next action (continue, redirect, or stop), which self-reflection benchmarks do not test. It uses 97 seeded tasks across 15 industrial cases in four sectors with counterfactual variants requiring opposite actions at the same workflow point, distinguishing warranted restraint from indiscriminate stopping. This targets a subtle and consequential agent capability grounded in Lean Six Sigma practice.

entry.title: From Target Selection to Condition Reuse: Auditing Residual Interventions in Tool-Use Models

author.name: Tianda Sun, Dimitar Kazakov

entry.summary: Studying activation interventions in Qwen3.5-27B on tool-use tasks, the paper shows that residual-writing interventions dramatically improve target-selection accuracy but fail to generalize when familiar facts are recombined or probed via independent eligibility judgments. The work suggests interventions can steer outputs without instilling the intended internal condition use.

entry.title: Trajectory Matching: Discrete Flow Matching with Structured Actions

author.name: Niklas Kemper, Marten Lienen, David L\"udke, Stephan G\"unnemann

entry.summary: The paper proposes trajectory matching, a discrete flow matching variant that conditions the flow on full action sequences connecting endpoints (e.g., attaching molecular fragments or inserting graph nodes with edges) rather than independent component-wise edits, enabling generation in natural structured units. This resolves tractability issues with endpoint conditioning for non-factorizable actions.

entry.title: Early learning in large residual networks

author.name: Vladimir Narovlansky, Boris Hanin

entry.summary: The authors analyze early training dynamics of nonlinear residual networks in a refined limit where width, depth, dataset size, and input dimension diverge sequentially, going beyond standard mean-field analysis. Their main result is a diagrammatic computation of network outputs and hidden representations after a few gradient steps in terms of input inner-product statistics.

entry.title: Schema-Free Text-to-SQL: Learning Enterprise Database Structure from Query Logs

author.name: \"Omer Faruk Akg\"ul, Nikhil Kapahi, Prajit Reddy Muppidi

entry.summary: This paper presents the first text-to-SQL framework that operates without schema documentation, learning database structure by parsing historical query logs into a knowledge graph of table co-usage, joins, and column-to-concept mappings, with entity-driven GraphRAG retrieval. It targets the well-known gap between academic text-to-SQL benchmark performance and enterprise reality where documentation is missing and naming is cryptic. This addresses a genuine deployment pain point.

entry.title: Heard Enough to Act: Early Tool Calling in Spoken Dialogue Systems

author.name: Yizhou Peng, Chen Chen, Donghang Wu, Hexin Liu, Eng Siong Chng

entry.summary: The authors define the earliest-actionable-point problem for latency-sensitive spoken agents, deciding when heard speech already grounds a tool call, and build a synthetic pipeline producing 26,694 dialogues (786 hours) across 48 domains with gated annotations and disjoint train/test argument values. This enables training and evaluating agents that act before a turn completes.

entry.title: AskGLP1: A Knowledge Graph LLM Agent for Exploring GLP-1 Experience from Online Patient Narratives

author.name: Zhaoqian Xue, Anay Somani, Siddhartha Singh, Junting Mu, Zhongyin Wang, Haozheng Liu, Ayesha Khatun, Yeaeun Kwon, Renkai Ma, Siyuan Ma, Zhe He, Danxia Yu, Lingyao Li

entry.summary: Presents AskGLP1, a system that uses an LLM-assisted pipeline grounded in MedDRA to screen roughly 8.5 million Reddit posts and 2,506 WebMD reviews into a knowledge graph of 385,790 drug-side-effect and drug-purpose relations for GLP-1 medications. It enables question answering over patient experiences, revealing source- and drug-specific patterns relevant to pharmacovigilance. A strong demonstration of large-scale patient narrative mining.

entry.title: EXCISE: Locating and Excising Distracting Sentences in Medical Question Answering

author.name: Yerim Hong, Sohyun Son, Heeseung Chung, Mujeen Sung

entry.summary: The paper shows that attention blocking to a known distractor sentence restores correct answers in medical QA, that hidden states mark the distractor as the least-fitting sentence even when the model follows it, and proposes EXCISE, an inference-time method to remove distractor effects without knowing which sentence is distracting. This improves robustness of models intended for clinical decision support.

entry.title: LLMs Can Tackle High Energy Theoretical Physics, yet Gaps Remain: Part I, Quantum Field Theory

author.name: Tong Liu, Bohan Li, Gongrui Cheng, Zixiong Yu, Yulan He, Volker Tresp

entry.summary: Introduces QFT-Bench, 75 graduate- to research-level quantum field theory problems with closed-form answers, evaluated via symbolic verification plus LLM judging across 39 proprietary and open-source models. Finds frontier models show substantial capability on nontrivial derivations but with identifiable gaps.

entry.title: Knowing When the Evidence Is Enough: Requirement-Directed Search with Horn-Closure Certificates

author.name: Xinyu Zhang, Weiwei Sun

entry.summary: The Certify system makes evidence-sufficiency decisions structural for search-augmented models: it decomposes a query into a requirement hypergraph of jointly necessary facts, searches per requirement with entity-verified passage links, and computes a Horn-closure certificate identifying minimal sufficient passages or an abstention. This replaces holistic model judgment about when to stop searching.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Evidence Misgrounding in Multimodal Knowledge Editing

author.name: Zhiwu Wang, Yichen Wu, Jinqian Yang, Yizhou Yang, Renzhen Wang, Qian Zhao, Deyu Meng

entry.summary: Identifies evidence misgrounding in multimodal knowledge editing, where an edit yields the target answer yet relies on incidental context rather than the intended visual evidence, which answer-level metrics miss. The paper introduces WaterBird-Edit, a controlled diagnostic set decoupling labels from background, and VICE, a retrieval-based visual in-context editing framework that mitigates the problem.

entry.title: What Remains OOD? OODConceptBench for Open-World Concept Recognition in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhiran Luo, Zhiyong Yang, Zitai Wang, Sicong Li, Qianqian Xu, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: OODConceptBench is a hierarchical benchmark for open-world concept recognition containing 30,752 images (with a harder 14,285-image L2 subset) spanning 560 concept phrases across seven open-world categories, used to evaluate 37 vision-language models. Findings show recognition degrades on the harder subset and characterize what remains genuinely out-of-distribution as zero-shot generalization blurs known-unknown boundaries. It clarifies the actual open-world capabilities of modern VLMs.

entry.title: MedAdaptAgent: An Automatic Harness for Adapting Medical Imaging Models to New Sites

author.name: Hanxue Gu, Zhonghao Liu, Xingrui Gu, Kang Wang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: MedAdaptAgent is an LLM-driven harness that converts a pretrained medical imaging model, target site data, and a free-text request into an automated new-site adaptation workflow. An Adaptation Planner uses model-site evidence to select compatible experiments and iteratively revise adjustments, requiring demonstrated improvement over the pretrained baseline.

entry.title: VibeVideoBench:Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation

author.name: Muxi Diao, Wenbin Xu, Lele Yang, Xuyang Ma, Yuzhe Chen, Jiankang Chen, Kaiyu Jiang, Changyi Liu, Haoyu Zhang, Hongyi Fu, Jianxiong Wang, Tianke Zhang, Haonan Fan, Yingxin Li, Bingyi Li, Xu Wang, Xuanyu Zheng, Bin Wen, Tingting Gao, Han Li, Wentao Zhang, Weiran Xu, Kongming Liang, Zhanyu Ma

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 239 bilingual tasks evaluating multimodal agents on code-driven video generation, where agents must write code to render frames and synthesize sound, delivering a finished MP4 in a sandboxed harness. Evaluation is hierarchical and evidence-based, covering data stories, lessons, and explainers.

entry.title: Model-Aware Generation of Safety-Critical Scenes for Robust End-to-End Driving via Distilled Planner Surrogates

author.name: Khaled M. Seyam (University of Stuttgart, Germany), Julian Wiederer (Mercedes-Benz AG, Germany), Samar Fathalah (University of Stuttgart, Germany), Markus Braun (Mercedes-Benz AG, Germany), Bin Yang (University of Stuttgart, Germany)

entry.summary: Analyzes NeuroNCAP failures and finds 95.9% of DiffusionDrive collisions are planning rather than perception failures, attributed to the rarity of safety-critical interactions in real driving logs. The paper proposes a model-aware framework that generates safety-critical training scenes by attacking a specific planner at the BEV level through a differentiable surrogate distilled from its planning head.

entry.title: MOON: Learning When to Forget and How to Move On in Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Jingmeng Zhou, Seson Sun, Binyao Xu, Lingming Zhang, Hanshi Wang, Fudong Ge, Weiming Hu, Jin Gao, Zhipeng Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies behavioral inertia in VLN policies, where retained visual history prevents turning when a turn is needed after a route deviation. MOON adds two lightweight modules (<1% parameters) to a frozen VLN policy: a deviation judge that decides when to clear history and a mechanism to move on, substantially improving recovery from deviations.

entry.title: RoboJev: An Open Vision-Language Judge for Robot Success Detection

author.name: Josef Liyanjun Chen

entry.summary: RoboJev-27B is an open-weight VLM that judges manipulation success from task instructions and 10 frames of an attempt (plus optional auxiliary-camera frames), fine-tuned with a rank-32 LoRA on 52,598 episodes and a source-specific KL penalty. It uses a calibrated two-token readout for single-pass success/failure probabilities.

entry.title: DEX-PHD: A Dexterous Portable Handheld Device for Multimodal Data Collection

author.name: Jooyoung Hong, Noboru Myers, Obin Kwon, Yixian Yang, Joohyung Kim

entry.summary: DEX-PHD is a portable, untethered handheld device for collecting dexterous manipulation data that combines kinematic-chain accuracy with vision-based portability: it integrates a dexterous robot hand, continuous per-finger joint-level control, and multimodal logging of proprioception, fingertip contact, and wrist camera video. This enables data collection across diverse environments for contact-rich tasks. Data collection hardware of this kind is a key enabler for dexterous policy learning.

entry.title: Intrinsic Gradient Barriers in Pushforward Deep Generative Models

author.name: Edric Tam, Qingyang Liu, Barbara Engelhardt, Ray Bai

entry.summary: Shows that difficulties of deep generative models with heavy tails and well-separated modes reflect intrinsic properties of the transport problem rather than architecture or training choices. The paper establishes quantitative lower bounds on gradients and Jacobians of pushforward mappings from log-concave sources, with gradient magnitude growing with tail weight of the target.

entry.title: When is early stopping beneficial under label noise? A phase diagram for kernel gradient flow

author.name: Fabrizio Boncoraglio, Lenka Zdeborov\'a

entry.summary: Motivated by CIFAR10 experiments showing that early stopping becomes unnecessary in large deep networks even under fully random labels, the paper derives a phase diagram for kernel gradient flow determining when late-time test-error deterioration under label noise disappears. This connects memorization of noise to benign overfitting phenomena in overparameterized models.

entry.title: RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training

author.name: Binghang Lu, Yige Sun, Guang Lin

entry.summary: RSI-Opt is a plug-and-play system of LLM agents that monitor neural-network training dynamics and adjust optimizer settings, evolving their own policy artifacts (prompt, playbook, code library, decision cadence) across runs via a meta-agent. Across five generations on three tasks, the meta-agents develop reusable procedures and improve training outcomes.

entry.title: Watermarking Diffusion Language Models with Learned Foresight and Balanced Bands

author.name: Hyojun Kim, Hyeseon An, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: The paper addresses watermarking for diffusion language models, where tokens can be generated before their predecessors, breaking standard green-list watermark assumptions. The authors learn vocabulary bands and a foresight predictor that estimates how each candidate token shifts neighbors' green lists, improving detection fidelity while keeping the null distribution exact. This extends AI-generated text attribution to an emerging non-autoregressive model class.

entry.title: Beyond Gain: Measuring Skill Internalization for Agent Skill Retirement

author.name: Yanze Wang, Pengfei Yao, Tianyi Sun, Hongda Chen, Yunyun Han, Jun Sun, Chuanrui Hu, Yafeng Deng

entry.summary: The paper tackles skill-hub curation for LLM agents, noting that gain-based retirement rules cannot distinguish internalized skills from the uncovered case where neither model nor skill provides the capability. The authors propose withholding the skill and scoring the model on a task synthesized from it, validating high unaided scores only when another model gains from the skill, since nearly half of high scores come from tasks no model can solve. This enables reliable measurement of skill internalization at hub scale.

entry.title: Async-RBench: Benchmarking Asynchronous Task Execution in LLM Agents

author.name: Detao Zeng, Guilin Ou, Nuo Chen, Yunhao Feng, Hongliang Wang, Qinli Yang, Junming Shao, Zhong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Async-RBench, a benchmark of 200 executable tasks across eight scenarios for evaluating LLM agents on asynchronous execution, where subagent results arrive while the main agent continues working and state may have changed. A scenario controller governs result delivery and an Event Response Contract defines correct handling, going beyond final-task-success metrics.

entry.title: Concept Acupuncturist: An Efficient and Precise Concept Erasure Method for Diffusion Models via Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Yiran Xiahou, Siliang Qin, Kai Chen, Shengzhi Zhang, Renyang Liu

entry.summary: ConceptACP is a machine-unlearning framework for diffusion models that uses SAE-based interpretability to locate sparse, precise concept-related components, enabling inference-free fine-tuning for targeted concept removal while preserving general capabilities. It avoids costly full-trajectory fine-tuning and imprecise large-scale edits.

entry.title: ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation

author.name: Shuo Han, Zhilin Wang, Peng Ling, Wenjia Gong, Yang Liu, Guanjun Jiang, Yukun Cao, Xike Xie

entry.summary: Proposes ImageRSI, a framework for agentic image generation that keeps the generator frozen and combines within-task verification and repair, a cross-task experience library gated by paired A/B validation, and offline judge updates using SFT and GRPO. Also releases ImageReq-Bench, 961 hard real-world text-to-image requests. The approach aims to make repair improvements transfer across tasks rather than fixing single outputs.

entry.title: "Not" is Not Lost in Translation: A Causal Analysis of Negation Representations in Multilingual LLMs

author.name: Giang Son Nguyen, Wray Buntine, Dung D. Le, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: Uses causal interventions on synthetic contrastive data and a FLORES-200-derived negation translation dataset across six open models and four languages to show that negation representations are causally controllable and largely shared across languages: a contrastive activation direction from one language can induce or remove negation in others. This provides mechanistic evidence for language-agnostic semantic representations of negation in multilingual LLMs.

entry.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection

author.name: Amber Xie, Jiawei Fu, Xiaofeng Guo, Carmelo Sferrazza, Guanya Shi, Haozhi Qi

entry.summary: DexPort is a portable handheld interface for collecting demonstrations for high-DoF dexterous robot hands, using the same hand hardware for collection and deployment to eliminate the embodiment gap while recording both commanded joint targets and measured states. It leverages a small set of skills to reduce operator burden compared with teleoperation or retargeted human motion capture. It addresses a key data bottleneck for manipulation learning.

entry.title: GS-MoE: Training-Free MoE Compression via Groupwise Subspace Sharing and Pruning

author.name: Carson Cary, Yukai Jin, Yihao Huang, Zhankai Ye, Fangyi Li, Ting Hua, Xin Liu, Shangqian Gao

entry.summary: GS-MoE compresses Mixture-of-Experts models without retraining by sharing low-rank subspaces across expert groups and applying Nystrom-based neuron compression within each expert, addressing both cross-expert and within-expert redundancy. Reconstruction-error analysis guides expert grouping and hierarchical budget allocation under a global compression target.

entry.title: Detection and Validation of Hidden Subgroup Disparities in Clinical AI

author.name: Alceu Bissoto, Trung-Dung Hoang, Tim Fl\"uhmann, Nina Weng, Susu Sun, Christian F. Baumgartner, Lisa M. Koch

entry.summary: This work evaluates algorithmic subgroup discovery methods for detecting hidden performance disparities in clinical ML models when demographic metadata is unavailable, addressing the previously unsolved problem of validating discovered subgroups against unknown true stratifications. It aims to make subgroup-based fairness monitoring practical in clinical workflows.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Step Transition Predictions: A Bellman Theory

author.name: Chenbei Lu, Zaiwei Chen, Tongxin Li, Chenye Wu, Adam Wierman

entry.summary: This paper develops a Bellman-equation theory for discounted MDPs where the decision maker receives K-step probabilistic transition predictions under a block-feedback protocol, avoiding exponential state-space growth. It shows predictive information creates value by recursively reshaping local dynamics and quantifies when multi-step predictions help.

entry.title: Linear-Time Context Compression with State-Space Encoding

author.name: Marc Serra Ortega, Andrey Barsky, Carlos Boned Riera, Tom\'as Ockier, Dimosthenis Karatzas

entry.summary: The Boa Compressor is a plug-and-play online context compressor built on a Mamba state-space model that encodes arbitrary-length context in a single linear-time pass, unlike existing soft-prompt compression methods that reuse the Transformer backbone and incur high latency. This enables online compression for LLM inference rather than only offline reuse of compressed contexts.

entry.title: Mine or Yours? Mind-Bridged Language Models Take Each Other's Memories as Their Own

author.name: Yunlong Xu

entry.summary: Using two copies of one language model where a receiver attends to a partner model's internal memory, the paper shows the receiver claims the partner's private rule as its own in 97% of answers when the partner's memory is doubly weighted, and misattributes the partner's code word in open reports. Ownership misattribution does not track the receiver's ability to identify what the partner was assigned, suggesting memory bridge access does not preserve self-other boundaries.

entry.title: Towards a Learnable Retriever for Textual Graph Question Answering

author.name: Kaifeng Jin, Yuchen Yan, Zhichen Zeng, Xiao Lin, Lihui Liu, Yinglong Xia, Hanghang Tong

entry.summary: Identifies architectural and retrieval-supervision gaps in GraphQA/GraphRAG and proposes making the retriever itself a learnable LLM for evidence selection within an end-to-end retrieve-then-generate pipeline, supervising evidence selection with gold answer signals.

entry.title: EdgeDeID: A 0.6B Clinical De-identifier Trained Without Real Patient Data

author.name: Sina Daneshgar, Raya Namazi, Amirali Khosravi, Pouria Rouzrokh, Bardia Khosravi

entry.summary: EdgeDeID is a 0.6B-parameter local clinical de-identification model trained entirely on synthetic notes written by LLM teachers and re-annotated to a single convention. It achieves 0.994 micro-F1 with no missed identifiers in 99% of notes on a verified synthetic benchmark, versus 0.857 and 12% for the best of eight off-the-shelf systems, and runs quantized on CPU in 615 MB. This sidesteps the privacy paradox of using hosted LLMs for de-identification.

entry.title: STEP: Soft Trajectory Estimation of Prediction Correctness via Per-Step Probability Scoring

author.name: Chenyang Yu, Zifan Zeng, Qunli Zhang, Feng Liu

entry.summary: STEP is a training-free framework for estimating LLM prediction correctness without ground truth, scoring each reasoning step via lightweight forward passes to build soft trajectory features capturing per-step confidence and its progression. It outperforms output-only baselines like entropy and perplexity across varied tasks.

entry.title: Text Is the Bottleneck: A Small-Scale Replication of LLM Game Playing in Riichi Mahjong

author.name: Mingge Xu

entry.summary: Replicates a prior LLM mahjong study under a drastically smaller budget, showing that tiny non-LLM models (a 2.6M-parameter convolutional encoder and a 4.9M-parameter Transformer) match or beat text-prompt LLMs up to 0.8B parameters on decision agreement and table placement. The finding that text is the bottleneck for game playing via language interfaces challenges assumptions about LLM superiority in structured decision tasks. Good example of rigorous, budget-conscious replication science.

entry.title: SimPOTrans: Self-Adaptation for Offline-to-Simultaneous Speech Translation via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haotian Tan, Hiroki Ouchi, Sakriani Sakti

entry.summary: Introduces SimPOTrans, an RL framework that self-adapts offline speech translation models into simultaneous speech translation without synthesized read/write trajectories or joint quality-latency optimization, avoiding instability of prior dialogue-style SimulST training. It formulates simultaneous translation as multi-turn dialogue with LLMs and reaches state-of-the-art performance. Relevant to low-latency translation of streaming speech.

entry.title: MechAlign: Evaluating Semantic Alignment at the Project Level in Mathematical Formalization

author.name: Hao Shen, Ruichen Qiu, Lihong Zhi, Xiao-Shan Gao

entry.summary: MechAlign is a framework for checking whether a Lean formalization faithfully expresses the mathematical claim of a manuscript, going beyond proof verification by reviewing statement-level semantic alignment across project dependencies. Its LeanTrace tool builds statement dependency graphs from elaborated declarations, and an LLM-based reviewer assesses correspondence.

entry.title: Hierarchical Skill Evolution for Coding Agent

author.name: Jun Gao, Yun Peng, Changhai Zhou, Yuhan Zhu, Xiangyu Zeng, Shiyang Zhang Yuhua Zhou, Luozheng Qin, Qian Qiao, Xiaoteng Ma, Baian Chen Weiyi Shang, Zhen Ming Jack Jiang, Lizhi Liao, Xiaoxue Ren

entry.summary: HSE progressively distills reusable procedural skills from coding-agent trajectories through hierarchical evidence aggregation: extracting task-level evidence, consolidating repository-specific skill candidates, and merging cross-repository patterns into transferable skills. This lets coding agents accumulate experience without modifying the underlying model.

entry.title: Evolving to Match Capabilities: Improving Harness Self-Evolution via Skill Adaptation

author.name: Zhihao Yang, Haojin Wang, Juncheng Wu, Kuan Zhang, Yukun Chen, Run Luo, Yaojie Lu, Yuyin Zhou, Lu Wang, Xianpei Han

entry.summary: Finds that harness-level skill guidance benefits strong models but can degrade weaker ones (103 task-skill pairs where GPT-5.6-luna gains 31.1 points while Gemma-4-E4B loses 8.8), with most weak-model failures violating requirements already stated in the skill. Proposes skill adaptation: reformulating existing skills to match a model's capabilities without parameter updates.

entry.title: EnvLunch: The Environment as a Free Lunch for Learning to Interact

author.name: Wei Liu, Min Gao, Yali Du, Yulan He

entry.summary: EnvLunch is a warm-up stage that converts executable environments (e.g., databases) themselves into verifiable training tasks for LLM agents without human annotation, by sampling valid action trajectories and executing them. This cheap supervision precedes downstream agentic reinforcement learning and reduces dependence on annotated tasks.

entry.title: Can LLMs Trust Appropriately? Evaluating Calibrated Reliance on Imperfect Partners

author.name: Mengdi Chu, Jintao Huang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a 324-scenario benchmark across 23 collaboration categories evaluating whether LLMs form appropriately calibrated trust in imperfect human and AI partners, with each scenario involving three sequential decisions with explicit transition dynamics, feedback, and cost schedules permitting exact analytical evaluation. Seven models are evaluated against expected-consequence baselines.

entry.title: Automated, auditable dating of the Babylonian Astronomical Diaries with language models and astronomical tools

author.name: Lucas Carrit Delgado Pinheiro, Yuan-Sen Ting, Jon Clindaniel, Lu Li, Yingbin Liang, Ness Shroff

entry.summary: This work builds a system that automatically dates broken Babylonian Astronomical Diary tablets using language models combined with astronomical verification tools. A rule-based parser extracts observation clauses from the text, an LM audits and augments them, and astronomical computations rank all candidate years from 626 BCE to AD 75, producing auditable datings at scale.

entry.title: Natural Jammers: When Non-Robust Features Become Antagonistic

author.name: Jiaming Zhang, Fuyao Zhang, Pengjun Xie, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: This computer-vision paper shows that non-robust features can actively mislead standard models on clean, unmodified images rather than merely serving as shortcuts, identifying a Jammed Set where robust models outperform standard models. Through disagreement analysis and causal interventions, it demonstrates Spectral-spatial Locking: jamming requires precise alignment of high-frequency components with specific spatial structures.

entry.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Shuo Shen, Guangran Cheng, Chengqi Lyu, Xiangsen Wang, Yanan Sun, Wenwei Zhang

entry.summary: S3AC introduces a practical critic-training recipe for long chain-of-thought RL with verifiable rewards, addressing coverage gaps over diverse trajectory lengths and early gradient domination by a newly initialized value head. The trained critic provides token-specific advantages and prompt-specific baselines that critic-free methods lack.

entry.title: DuoPIC: Uncertainty-Aware Voxel-Level Digital Twins of Cerebral Perfusion with Transport PDEs in Acute Stroke

author.name: Anh Duong Tran, Quang-Anh N. D., Toan Sy Pham, Trang H. Hoang, Minh N. Do, Duy Ton Mai, Huan X. Nguyen

entry.summary: Introduces DuoPIC, a digital twin of cerebral perfusion combining a Windkessel flow model with a tracer-transport PDE and a population-level neural closure that conserves tracer mass and mean transit time by construction, with tempered posteriors quantifying uncertainty. Achieves state-of-the-art lesion detection on ISLES'17 MR (AUC 0.745) and ISLES'24 CT (0.743) without reference maps.

entry.title: Gaussian Episodic Memory for Long-Term Spatiotemporal Reasoning

author.name: Ling-Chia Chen, Abdelrhman Werby, Kaan Aytekin, Kai O. Arras

entry.summary: Presents GEMS, combining a persistent spatio-temporal 3D Gaussian Splatting map with an agentic reasoning pipeline for robot long-term memory. The 3DGS map is updated only in regions where the scene changes, storing modifications while preserving visual detail over time, bridging the gap between structured representations limited to captured entities and viewpoint-constrained image memories.

entry.title: GeoLift: Grounding Video Spatial Reasoning in Explicit 3D Maps

author.name: Xinglin Li, TingTing Long, Jingzhi Zhou, Jiajing Chen, Jian Yang, Jin Xie

entry.summary: GeoLift addresses weaknesses in multimodal LLM video spatial reasoning, showing that existing models degrade to near-random accuracy on route-planning tasks requiring three or more turns, and grounds reasoning in explicit 3D maps so models can connect observations across viewpoints into a shared spatial structure. The diagnostic finding itself is a valuable contribution to understanding MLLM limits. It points toward 3D-grounded architectures for embodied and navigation tasks.

entry.title: TopX: Text-to-Motion for Unseen Skeletons from the Skeleton File Alone

author.name: Tengjiao Sun, Pengcheng Fang, Xiaoyu Zhan, Dongjie Fu, Xiaohao Cai, Hansung Kim

entry.summary: TopX is a 73M-parameter flow-matching transformer that generates joint rotations and root trajectories for arbitrary kinematic trees using only the skeleton file, with no clips, retargeting, or fine-tuning. It normalizes motion by rest pose and skeleton size with randomized rest conventions, using factorized attention over joints and frames.

entry.title: Interpretable Brain Age Prediction Using White Matter Fiber Orientation Distributions with Rotation-Equivariant Deep Learning

author.name: Chenyang Fan, Robert D. Sanders, Elie Matar, Yixuan Yuan, Xiang Li, Sharon L. Naismith, Fernando Calamante, Jinglei Lv

entry.summary: The paper presents an interpretable brain age prediction framework combining white matter fiber orientation distributions from diffusion MRI with an SE(3)-equivariant CNN operating directly on spherical harmonic coefficients. This preserves geometric transformation properties of orientation-dependent features that conventional CNNs and DTI scalar metrics ignore.

entry.title: Generative Structure from Motion with Native 3D Diffusion

author.name: Haobin Duan, Binbin Huang, Mochu Xiang, Yiqun Zhao, Zibo Zhao, Yi Ma, Shenghua Gao

entry.summary: Proposes GenSfM, which integrates image-based 3D reconstruction with a native 3D diffusion model to jointly recover object structure and camera motion from a few uncalibrated views. A multi-modal diffusion transformer jointly denoises geometry and images, avoiding error cascades from simply concatenating reconstruction and generation stages and producing 3D objects faithful to both the input images and the learned distribution.

entry.title: FL4N: Feed-forward Latent Model for 4D Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Eunbeen Hong, Hyeonseo Yu, Honggyu An, Jooho Son, Hyunah Ko, Soowon Son, Chaehyun Kim, Jahyeok Koo, Jisoo Kim, Junhwa Hur, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: Introduces the first feed-forward latent 4D novel view synthesis model, encoding scenes in a unified spatiotemporal latent representation rather than explicit 4D Gaussians. It learns temporal dynamics as residuals over a pretrained static latent prior, enabling effective 4D modeling with limited dynamic training data.

entry.title: RoboReason: Boosting Robotics-Relevant VLM Reasoning Through Scalable Data Generation

author.name: Sagnik Anupam, Utkarsh Lal, Aneesh Edara, Botong Zhang, Yao Tang, Jiatao Gu, Dinesh Jayaraman, Osbert Bastani

entry.summary: Proposes robotics-relevant benchmarks for VLM visual reasoning based on spatial and temporal ordering tasks using stereo and wrist camera images from real robots, covering frame ordering, depth ordering, and left-to-right object ordering. It also generates scalable training data to improve VLM reasoning for manipulation pipelines.

entry.title: SceneAgent: An Agentic Pipeline from 3D and 4D Captures to Simulation Environments

author.name: Luke Hollis, Tianxing Fan, Heng Yang

entry.summary: Presents SceneAgent, an agentic pipeline that converts diverse captures (3D Gaussian Splatting, photogrammetry, LiDAR, AI-generated scenes, 4D video) into interactive simulation environments using simulator-based visual inspection and repair, covering segmentation, physical parameter estimation, articulation, and deformable simulation. It also generates object variants and scripted demonstrations to support policy learning.

entry.title: Improving Signals, Declining Encoder: A Known-Answer Test of Label-Free Monitoring in Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Nilotpal Kakati

entry.summary: Using synthetic images with known generating factors, the authors construct a known-answer test for label-free SSL monitoring: LeJEPA encoders demonstrably lose readability of specific factors, yet the training loss keeps falling and most of eleven monitored label-free signals rate declining runs as better. The result shows standard unsupervised monitoring signals can be blind to real capability regressions.

entry.title: Open-World Law-to-Action: Vision-Language Priors and Touch for Parts with Hidden Physics

author.name: Mohamed A. Mabrok

entry.summary: Presents L2A, where a VLM proposes motions, law-of-motion terms, and locking hypotheses for unseen movable parts (doors, drawers, lids, taps), each treated as a prior with a floor that touch can always overturn. The robot identifies each part's law online via Bayesian linear regression with closed-form evidence and provides proofs that touch alone suffices for certain identifications.

entry.title: Dream to Assist: Intent-Conditioned World Models for Shared Vehicle Control

author.name: Jonathan DeCastro, Thomas Balch, Emily Sumner, Deepak Gopinath, Laporsha Dees, Patricio Reyes Gomez, Elliot Weiss, Megan Applegate-Kenton, Todd Rowell, John Leonard, Avinash Balachandran, Guy Rosman

entry.summary: Dream2Assist extends a recurrent state-space world model with intent inference and trains an assistive policy via fictitious co-play to anticipate human objectives in shared vehicle control without overriding human agency. It also describes a full deployment pipeline translating the world-model policy into a safe, human-centered system. The dual focus on proactivity and legibility addresses a real tension in shared autonomy.

entry.title: Resilient Decentralized Radar-LiDAR-Inertial Odometry in Challenging Subterranean Environments

author.name: Moumita Mukherjee, Avijit Banerjee, Anton Koval, George Nikolakopoulos

entry.summary: The paper introduces a decentralized odometry framework fusing LiDAR, FMCW radar, and inertial sensing for robust pose estimation in GPS-denied subterranean environments degraded by smoke, dust, or fog. An Adaptive Residual Thresholding mechanism handles radar sparsity and outliers while exploiting LiDAR resolution when available. This targets a genuine pain point for autonomous operations in degraded conditions.

entry.title: High-resolution tactile observation makes hidden racket-control mechanisms learnable

author.name: Haoyang Tian, Zhengwei Li, Houcheng Li, Xu Yang, Peigeng Gu, Xinyue Wang, Tairan Zhu, Shuo Jiang, Long Cheng

entry.summary: Uses an 864-node tactile-inertial glove at 100 Hz to record over 14,000 badminton strokes from more than 70 participants across skill levels, then applies a mechanics-grounded two-layer framework to infer object-driving and grip-stabilizing control from tactile history. It reveals that higher proficiency correlates with selective reliance on rapid tactile feedback, uncovering control mechanisms experts cannot consciously articulate.

entry.title: Provably Efficient Q-learning for Robust Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuchen Jiao, Gen Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes an asynchronous Q-learning algorithm for distributionally robust RL over robust MDPs with Markovian data, filling a gap since prior efficient model-free robust RL methods were lacking. It provides sample-efficiency guarantees for infinite-horizon discounted settings.

entry.title: The Information Geometry of Representation Formation

author.name: Sanjukta Krishnagopal

entry.summary: This work studies how neural representations form during training rather than only analyzing trained endpoints, using Bures geometry to track movement through representation space and quantum Fisher information to measure sensitivity to input factors. The findings show learning concentrates sensitivity on task-relevant factors and that changing the prediction target reorganizes this geometry. It offers a principled geometric lens on training dynamics relevant to interpretability.

entry.title: Minimax Regret for Sobolev Kernel-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haichen Hu, David Simchi-Levi

entry.summary: The paper establishes minimax regret rates for episodic kernel-based RL with rewards and transition densities in Sobolev RKHSs over continuous state and action spaces, proving a rate that separates the difficulty of action selection from learning across states. The authors propose Sobolev Optimal Value Iteration (SOVI), which attains the rate, and match it with lower bounds. This provides sharp theoretical grounding for nonparametric RL.

entry.title: Permission to Retry: A Study of Authorization and Recovery in AI Agent Workflows

author.name: Deekshith Marla, Kushagra Bhatnagar

entry.summary: This paper studies execution-time reliability of tool-using agents, separating recovery decisions from language-model behavior. It defines distinct obligations around checkpoints, dispatch permission, external-effect evidence, and reconciliation, and validates them through a finite conformance study of 336 histories on LangGraph and Temporal hosts.

entry.title: MedCaseAgent: From Multimodal Clinical Evidence to Rare Disease Case Reports

author.name: Hongkang Chu, Yifan Shen, Tianjiao Yu, Zhuoqing Zhong, Jianguo Cao, Meihuan Huang, Xu Cao

entry.summary: MedCaseAgent is an end-to-end agentic system that generates publication-quality rare disease case reports from unstructured clinical notes, combining patient-level data mining with iterative tool-integrated reasoning that queries medical literature and knowledge bases. Its hierarchical, modular design supports multiple backbone LLMs and assesses case novelty. It targets the difficult problem of rigorous evidence-based clinical documentation for atypical cases.

entry.title: MBABench-2.0: Evaluating AI Agents on Constructing Financial Spreadsheets Beyond Simple Verifiability

author.name: Julian Poeltl, Thomson Yen, Patrick Shea, Shubham Anil Varma, Dhruv Rastogi, Zihao Chen, Mengshi Zhang, Hongseok Namkoong

entry.summary: MBABench-2.0 introduces 101 original spreadsheet construction tasks requiring modeling decisions, format design, and layout choices from scratch, moving beyond fill-in-the-blank spreadsheet benchmarks. It tests LLM agents on the full workbook-building workflow characteristic of finance knowledge work.

entry.title: AgentTrace: Execution-Level Fingerprinting of Black-Box LLM Agents

author.name: Gejian Zhao, Hanzhou Wu, Xinpeng Zhang

entry.summary: AgentTrace identifies the foundation model behind a black-box LLM agent by injecting structurally ambiguous probes that trigger tokenization-sensitive serialization failures at tool interfaces, then fingerprinting model-specific multi-step repair behaviors with lightweight sequence models. It sidesteps obfuscated system prompts and schema-constrained tool generation that defeat semantic attribution and watermarking.

entry.title: MS-TTRL: Breaking the Frequency Conflict in Multiple-Solution Test-Time Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhixia Zhang, Binqian Xu, Huaiyang Wang, Yikun Ban, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: The paper identifies the Frequency Conflict in test-time RL on multi-solution reasoning tasks: generation frequency must serve both correctness estimation and outcome diversity preservation. MS-TTRL resolves this via Outcome-Level Self-Verification producing frequency-independent correctness estimates while preserving group-level diversity for label-free RL on unlabeled test instances.

entry.title: PathJev: Decision-Native Vision-Language Modelling for Histopathology

author.name: Cristian Tommasino, Antonio M. Rinaldi

entry.summary: PathJev-P builds a decision-native histopathology model on MedGemma-1.5-4B with LoRA adapters and a decision head that returns calibrated distributions over run-time candidate sets, trained on 40,000 patch states from three public collections. The design uses typed questions with organ-specific candidates and a none-of-these option, evaluated under a pre-registered analysis plan. It offers a principled alternative to free-form VLM outputs for clinical decisions.

entry.title: SEDATE: Do Large Language Models Share an Aggression Circuit Across Languages?

author.name: Sagnik Basu, Sayan Das, Somnath Banerjee, Animesh Mukherjee

entry.summary: Proposes SEDATE, a training-free detect-edit-verify approach that locates neurons responsible for aggressive outputs, edits them, and verifies responses, evaluated across 7 languages and 4 model families. Investigates whether aggression is mediated by a shared circuit across languages.

entry.title: Beyond the Opening: Tracing the First Token's Persistent Influence on Reasoning Length

author.name: Ruochen Liu, Hao Yan, Ziluowen Luo, Senzhang Wang, Sihong Xie

entry.summary: This mechanistic study traces how the first reasoning token persistently changes reasoning length in LLMs, showing that swapping only the first token of a reasoning prefix and resuming generation substantially alters remaining length even with all other prefix tokens fixed. It compares next-token distributions to locate how this influence propagates.

entry.title: Rethinking Evaluation for Principled Generalization Using a Kripkean Challenge to Meaning as Use

author.name: Niyar R Barman, Omar Naim, Nicholas Asher

entry.summary: Argues via Kripke's Wittgensteinian rule-following paradox that finite histories of use cannot determine a unique rule for future extension, challenging meaning-as-use assumptions underlying LLM evaluation and OOD generalization debates. The authors propose testing abstraction and recursion as capacities central to preserving rules under principled domain extension, and offer an experimental paradigm. A theoretically grounded contribution to evaluation philosophy in NLP.

entry.title: ImgMT: Wikipedia-based Dataset For Evaluating Text-in-Image Translation

author.name: \v{S}\'arka Uramov\'a, Petar Kirilov Petrov, Josef Jon, Ond\v{r}ej Bojar, Michal Nov\'ak

entry.summary: ImgMT is a massively multilingual benchmark mined from localized SVG illustrations on Wikimedia Commons, with 35,612 aligned image pairs spanning 129 languages and 4,886 language pairs for text-in-image translation. It proposes a multi-level evaluation protocol covering text-region detection, OCR, and translation quality, and benchmarks multimodal models on this underexplored task.

entry.title: UMAS: System-Level Uncertainty Quantification for Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Hanwen Li, Jinhao Duan, Xiaoshuang Shi, Yue Zhang, Tianlong Chen, Kaidi Xu, Chenxi Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes UMAS, a parameter-free, cost-neutral framework for system-level uncertainty quantification in multi-agent LLM systems, estimating credibility of inter-agent influence from intrinsic confidence and aggregating node-level uncertainty across the system graph. Addresses the gap where UQ methods target single agents only.

entry.title: SkillShift-Bench: Benchmarking Skill Learning under Environment Evolution for Web Agents

author.name: Bo-Yu Chen, Zhi Zhou, Yu-Feng Li

entry.summary: SkillShift-Bench is the first benchmark evaluating web-agent skill learning under controlled open-environment shifts, simulating contextual, perceptual, and execution shifts across three self-hosted web systems. Experiments reveal systematic robustness degradations in learned skills as environments evolve.

entry.title: Improving VLMs on Scientific Chart Analysis via Autonomous Evolution

author.name: Abhinav Sudhakar Dubey, Vidushi Goel, Kiran Rana, Shikhar Mathur, Vaggos Chatziafratis

entry.summary: The authors improve open vision-language models on scientific chart QA without modifying model weights, by applying autonomous evolution (in the spirit of AlphaEvolve) to search over inference programs and surrounding code for a frozen model. Starting from a baseline inference program, iterative evolution recovers substantial accuracy from errors rooted in inexact answering.

entry.title: The Voice on the Line

author.name: Husein Zolkepli

entry.summary: This work trains causal voice isolators (masking transformers of 140M-374M parameters, 20 ms latency) that enroll a caller from the call itself for real-time telephony. It identifies failure modes hidden by short evaluation windows, such as forgetting the caller during long solo speech from another voice, and shows that making WavLM-Large weights causal and training them reduces error from 11.44% to 10.55% with a distilled student improving further.

entry.title: WorldCast: World-Consistent Character Video Generation with Large-Angle Camera Control

author.name: Lei Cao, Yu Liu, Wenhua Liao, Peng Zhang, Fei Wang, Hao Zhang, Jiajun Le, Daiguo Zhou, Jian Luan, Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: Proposes WorldCast, a framework for world-consistent character video generation under large-angle camera trajectories combining rotation, translation, and radius variation, addressing geometric distortion and identity drift when viewpoint changes reveal unseen character regions. Also releases CLACT, a large-scale character-centric dataset and benchmark with accurate camera geometry and multi-view observations.

entry.title: Distilling Dense Trajectory Teachers For Large-Motion Video World Models

author.name: Shuofeng Sun, Linqing Zhao, Haibin Yan

entry.summary: The paper proposes Dense Trajectory Teacher Distillation (DTTD), a post-training framework that transfers a video world model's generation capability from dense, small-motion trajectories to sparse, large-step camera trajectories, addressing frozen frames, inaccurate camera motion, and geometric drift at inference. The diagnosis of train-inference trajectory mismatch is crisp and relevant to world models for embodied agents. It targets a key failure mode of camera-controllable video generation.

entry.title: ProMo3D: Probing Motion Cues in Frozen 3D Foundation Models

author.name: Xiaoang Zhang, Mert Kiray, Yordanka Velikova, Manoj Biswanath, Benjamin Busam

entry.summary: This paper probes whether frozen 3D foundation model tokens already encode motion-relevant information, finding that static-dynamic separation is decodable from frozen representations and concentrated in a low-dimensional subspace via rank and spectral analysis. It builds lightweight readout functions (ProMo3D) for dynamic 4D understanding rather than training high-capacity motion decoders. Informative about what 3D foundation representations contain.

entry.title: FlockWorld: Toward Population-Scale Multi-Agent Video World Models through Artificial Life Simulation

author.name: Meryem Koksal, Yunzhe Wang, Volkan Ustun

entry.summary: FlockWorld is an artificial-life environment based on the Boids algorithm for training population-scale multi-agent video world models, with synchronized egocentric crops and configurable camera-agent counts. FlockDiT, an action-conditioned latent diffusion transformer trained with flow matching, jointly generates synchronized multi-agent video.

entry.title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation

author.name: Guowen Zhang, Liyi Chen, Xu Hu, Pengfei Wang, Jingfan Chen, Chenhang He, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes OSWAM, a world action model for autonomous driving and embodied control that achieves one-step action generation instead of tens of denoising steps, enabling real-time inference while preserving action quality that naive step reduction would destroy.

entry.title: RoboDuo: Attempt, Check and Atomic Recovery through Code for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jie Wang, Bo Zhang, Renzhi Lu, Jianyu Chen

entry.summary: Proposes RoboDuo, a closed-loop dual-system framework where a coding agent writes a program coordinating two VLAs: a full-task VLA attempts the task, completion is checked, and failures are recovered by composing reusable atomic skills. This targets the problem that open-loop VLA models cannot detect or recover from a single failed step in long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Omni-InteractScope: Benchmarking Proactive and Agentic Interaction in Continuous Omnimodal Streams

author.name: Yinsong Yan, Ling Wang, Yuxuan Wang, Yifan Yang, Ruiyang Xu, Junming Lin, Qi Chen, Meng Gao, Minghao Han, Yunfei Chu, Qize Yang, Xize Cheng, Jin Xu, Jibin Wu

entry.summary: Introduces Omni-InteractScope, a benchmark of 1,479 human-annotated interactions with 1,790 temporal targets across eight task groups, evaluating how Omni-LLMs handle proactive, query-free assistance and event-timed tool invocation in continuous audiovisual streams. Results reveal critical limitations in how reliably current models connect stream evidence to timely, sustained interventions.

entry.title: A Differentiable Chassis Safety Layer for Intelligent Vehicle Motion Control

author.name: Lu Xiong, Xuge Hu, Yufei Song, Weidong Liu, Chen Tang

entry.summary: Proposes a differentiable safety layer integrating task-oriented vehicle control with explicit chassis constraints (actuator limits, tire forces, handling envelopes) via sequential quadratic programs. Implicit differentiation enables temporal gradient coupling through projected commands, so safety filtering co-adapts with policy learning in a two-stage scheme.

entry.title: Behavioural Quality Is Not Learning Utility: Objective Mismatch in Human Behaviour Models for Robot Learning

author.name: Haoyang Jiang, Dana Kulic, Michael Burke, Pamela Carreno-Medrano

entry.summary: This paper identifies an objective mismatch in using human behavior models as RL training partners: models that best resemble real human data may not provide useful training experiences for downstream robot policy learning. Across highway driving and object handover domains, it evaluates behavior models with generative metrics versus their utility as training partners. The finding challenges standard evaluation practice in HRI and RL-from-simulation.

entry.title: Distributed Predictive Flocking for a Swarm of Miniature Vibration-Driven Robots in a Confined Arena

author.name: Prajol Shrestha, Siddhant Mohapatra, Filip Novkoski, Julian Oelhaf, Nicolas Vandewalle, Ana-Sun\v{c}ana Smith, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: The paper presents a distributed predictive flocking controller where each miniature robot solves its own NMPC problem, exchanging only predicted trajectories with neighbors while optimizing cohesion, alignment, safety, and task objectives in a confined arena. It systematically compares six barrier and control-barrier-function safety constraint formulations as density increases. This quantifies how constraint choice limits how many robots can safely coexist.

entry.title: Replicate What Varies: Resource Sharing for Domain-Randomized Embodied Simulation

author.name: Zixu Hao, Weijun Wang, Xiangyu Li, Liang Mi, Hao Wu, Yunxin Liu, Ting Cao

entry.summary: Presents Patchwork, a resource-sharing system for domain-randomized embodied simulation that represents environments as a shared template plus patches of mutations (E = T + Delta). By separating randomization sampling from replay and reusing templates, it reduces the substantial CPU and GPU memory costs of running many concurrent diverse simulation instances.

entry.title: Depth Improves Training-Time Scaling for Difficult Tasks in Deep Linear Networks

author.name: Taishi Watanabe, Ryo Karakida, Jun-nosuke Teramae

entry.summary: Through refined analysis of deep linear networks, the paper shows that the task spectrum determines when depth improves training-time scaling: for spectrally difficult tasks depth improves the asymptotic scaling exponent, while for easy tasks the exponent is depth-independent. This helps settle whether depth can improve training-time scaling laws.

entry.title: Recertifying decisions via e-closure: uniform improvements of conformal risk control and randomized e-BH

author.name: Tian Bai, Aaditya Ramdas

entry.summary: Building on e-value representations of risk-controlled decisions and the e-closure principle for multiple testing, the paper formulates recertification: a general paradigm for improving conservative statistical procedures by exploiting computable slack in their validity certificates. The authors show uniform improvements over conformal risk control and randomized e-BH while preserving risk guarantees. This is a notable unifying contribution to e-value-based inference.

entry.title: Import AI 478: Math for alignment; ProgramBench; and Mirendil shows what RSI means

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: Jack Clark's newsletter covers Resolution's (formerly Sequent) autoformalization of the resolution of singularities in mathematics using orchestrated AI agents, framing it as groundwork for connecting loss-landscape geometry to generalization and as a case study in AI-driven research workflows. The issue also previews ProgramBench and commentary on what recursive self-improvement looks like in practice.

entry.title: PEAR: Adaptive Advantage Reshaping for Perception and Exploration in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Junxin Wang, Yingfeng Luo, Xiangchen Song, Weiqiao Shan, Runsong Zhao, Xinyu Liu, Shunjie Xing, Yifu Huo, Dingyang Lin, Qiuyu Gu, Yongyu Mu, Chenglong Wang, Changliang Li, Jingbo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: PEAR is an adaptive advantage reshaping method for multimodal RL that fixes underweighting of high-entropy, low-visual-dependency tokens important for exploration. It retains visual dependency as the base signal and adds an entropy-based exploration gain selectively at high-entropy positions with conditions on visual dependence. The work improves the balance between reliable visual perception and diverse reasoning in vision-language model training.

entry.title: ALLMTS: Automated LLM-based Medical Triage System

author.name: Micha{\l} Remigiusz Janiszewski, Artur Stopa, {\L}ukasz Lenkiewicz, Wojciech Achtelik, Bartosz Gonczarek

entry.summary: Presents an LLM-based medical triage system for telephone intake that grounds every disposition in the same commercial telehealth guidelines nurses use, having the LLM execute the guideline rather than triage directly. The disposition follows deterministically from the guideline evaluation, improving auditability and reducing over-escalation of routine cases.

entry.title: ReMedI: Inference-Time Refinement and Self-Distillation for Controllable Molecular Optimization

author.name: Jia Yi Zhang, Shivanshu Shekhar, Allison McLevige, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: ReMedI uses a Metropolis-Hastings search at inference time to exploit useful molecular edits already present in a pre-trained molecular language model, avoiding expensive RL post-training like C-MORAL and its task-specific datasets. It targets multi-objective lead optimization (e.g., permeability up, toxicity down) with limited scaffold changes, using self-distillation to internalize search gains.

entry.title: Rethinking LoRA Initialization for Robust Asymmetric Learning Rates

author.name: Disen Liao, Yaoliang Yu

entry.summary: Studies why LoRA+ style asymmetric learning rates (larger LR for the up-projection B than down-projection A) can cause unstable training and ratio-dependent performance collapse under standard initialization. The paper identifies the initialization as the culprit and proposes initialization changes that make training robust to large LR ratios, reducing hyperparameter brittleness in parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

entry.title: Beyond Pattern Matching in 3D MLLMs: Part-Level Functional Reasoning for Generalizable Recognition

author.name: Weihong Li, Hao Jiang, Yaohua Zha, Tao Dai, Shu-Tao Xia

entry.summary: Shows that 3D multimodal LLMs recognize objects via pattern matching that fails on geometrically similar objects requiring functional reasoning, exposing a 33.7% versus 84.0% accuracy gap between ambiguous and unambiguous samples via a per-sample Geometric Confusion Score. Proposes PFIR, built on PartNeXt with a 507K QA-pair pipeline, that reverses a function-as-annotation pattern so functional language supports inference rather than decorating known identities.

entry.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms

author.name: Xi Chen, Fengqi Hu, Zeyu Shen, Jiaying Xu, Shangding Gu, Pan Xu, Anqi Liu, Laixi Shi

entry.summary: RobustRLlib is a library and benchmark integrating 17 representative robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified interface, paired with an enhanced evaluation platform covering real-world distribution shifts and humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. It aims to improve algorithm reusability and clarify the empirical capability boundaries of robust RL. Systematic evaluation across this breadth is a useful community resource.

entry.title: DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making

author.name: Changxu Ni, Yiyang Ni, Jun Li, Feiran You, Hongyang Du, Haitao Zhao, Shi Jin

entry.summary: DT-JEPA replaces the Decision Transformer's reliance on expected future returns with JEPA-style latent prediction of future representations, addressing the incompleteness of return conditioning and its dependence on task-specific rewards. This enables offline RL policy learning that transfers better to tasks with similar but unseen rewards and requires no reward labels.

entry.title: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators

author.name: Aaditya Prasad, Steven W. Flavell, Brian DePasquale

entry.summary: ZENO is a neural operator trained against the Zakai equation, the SPDE governing unnormalized filtering distributions, enabling state inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters that are analytically and numerically intractable. It leverages operator learning and physics-informed advances with applications across engineering and neuroscience.

entry.title: Let's Do Turbulence Right: In Space and Time!

author.name: Maximilian Plattner, Fabian Paischer, Johannes Brandstetter

entry.summary: Using massive time-resolved direct numerical simulations exceeding 28 TB per run, the authors assess how numerical choices affect the resolved (3+1)-dimensional physics of 3D Navier-Stokes turbulence, then study how neural networks represent turbulent motion. The key finding is that spatial and temporal evaluations of learned emitters can diverge, arguing for rigorous space-time assessment. This is an important methodological caution for neural emulators of turbulent flows.

entry.title: The Social World Model Evaluation Gap

author.name: Denglin Jiang (New York University), Annie Wang (New York University)

entry.summary: This audit of 113 works from 1999 to 2026 finds that evaluations of social world models rarely test whether systems can predict a real person's response to an action: only 9 primary evaluations measure this, and only 2 compare an explicit response forecast against the actual response under randomized intervention. A full-text check of 25 language-model works finds no experiment meeting these conditions.
