It finds sensitive action directions diverge substantially (median angles around 36-42 degrees at the smallest scale) and that discrepancies shrink with larger perturbations. This probes an underexamined fidelity property of world models.

entry.title: WL-SeqVAE: Sequence-Based Graph Generation Using Variational Autoencoders and Weisfeiler-Leman Colors

author.name: Iakovos Evdaimon, Giannis Nikolentzos, Achilleas Tsimichodimos, Christos Xypolopoulos, Michalis Vazirgiannis

entry.summary: WL-SeqVAE generates graphs by mapping each graph to a sequence of Weisfeiler-Leman colors used as structural tokens, encoding the sequence into a Gaussian latent space with a VAE, and decoding autoregressively with WL-derived compatibility constraints guiding node and edge prediction. It avoids learning distributions over adjacency matrices directly.

entry.title: Deep Learning-Based Prediction of HER2 Status from Whole-Brain MRI in Breast Cancer Brain Metastases

author.name: Sara Early, Chris Kang, Vibujithan Vigneshwaran, Kimberly Amador, Roger Y. Tsang, Nils D. Forkert

entry.summary: This study evaluates whether deep learning can predict HER2 status, a key treatment biomarker, directly from post-contrast T1-weighted brain MRI in breast cancer brain metastases, and whether tumor segmentation inputs help. It compares radiomics, a simple fully convolutional network, and segmentation-augmented variants on 135 patients from a public dataset.

entry.title: A Model-Agnostic Correction Framework for Short-Term Building Load Forecasting

author.name: Shiqiao Zhou, Huanbo Lyu, Holger Sch\"oner, Zipeng Wu, Jessica Deuschel, Freya Wentzel, IAG Wilson, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: WeL-RAC is a model-agnostic, retrieval-augmented correction framework for short-term building load forecasting that retrieves relevant historical cases at inference time to adapt predictions when current operating regimes are rare or underrepresented in training. It improves robustness to rapidly changing weather and operating conditions.

entry.title: Acoustic and Lexical Signals for Native Language Identification of Language Learners

author.name: Ahmet Yavuz Uluslu, Mengjie Qian, Kate Knill, Mark Gales

entry.summary: The paper compares WavLM-based audio classifiers with a zero-shot GPT-4o transcript-based classifier for identifying a learner's native language from spoken English, evaluated across CEFR proficiency levels. It finds the audio classifier outperforms the transcript approach overall, though relative strengths vary with proficiency. The work is useful for language assessment and shows where LLM lexical signals do and do not substitute for acoustic ones.

entry.title: Embedding-Based Educational Taxonomies

author.name: Kia Karbasi, Kaveh Karbasi, Gregory Pottie

entry.summary: The authors computationally construct educational taxonomies by clustering semantic embeddings of math questions, comparing the resulting skill structures against existing human-expert taxonomies used in intelligent tutoring. The work explores whether content-derived structure can substitute for labor-intensive expert curation. Results inform how curricula and assessment could be organized automatically.

entry.title: Making Reasoning Visible: Configuration-Aware Diagnostic Modeling for Adaptive Scaffolding in Structured Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Trystan Geoffre, Zheng Yuan, Thierry Geoffre

entry.summary: This study introduces a diagnostic framework that models learners' step-by-step reasoning from action sequences in an interactive grammar-learning game, computing five interpretable strategy dimensions and classifying reasoning into four states. Analysis of 36,234 interactions from 234 students supports adaptive scaffolding in tutoring systems.

entry.title: A Multimodal Framework for Measuring Creator Communication on Short-Form Video

author.name: Julie R. Ancis, Michael Fire, Omer Tarshish

entry.summary: Presents a five-stage multimodal framework combining platform metadata, speech transcripts, and vision-language frame descriptions with LLM-generated indicators to measure creators' themes and communication strategies at scale. Demonstrated on 9,852 TikTok videos from sixteen creators with audited keyword consolidation and creator-weighted aggregation.

entry.title: Toward Neuroadaptive Communication Interfaces: A Framework for Personalized Speech and Language Support

author.name: Carlos Bruno, Luis Ricardo Santos

entry.summary: This position-style paper proposes a framework for adapting language presentation (sentence segmentation, pictograms, optional speech output) to individual user abilities and changing task demands. It separates message access from user-need estimation and support selection, using behavioral feedback as the primary adaptation signal and treating EEG as an uncertainty-aware auxiliary input rather than a direct comprehension measure.

entry.title: Center-of-Mass Interpretation of Evolution Strategies

author.name: Akshat Gupta

entry.summary: This paper offers a geometric reframing of evolution strategies: treating perturbed models as particles with rewards as masses, the mean-subtracted ES update is exactly the displacement of the reward-weighted center of mass, scaled by a factor depending on mean reward, for any finite population. This physical reading yields new intuition for ES dynamics.

entry.title: Ampe-DB: A Dataset for Human Activity and Interaction Analysis Using the Ghanaian Game Ampe

author.name: Ruth Senior Biney, Isaac Kojo Yedonu Aboah

entry.summary: Introduces Ampe-DB, a multimodal dataset of 637 clips of the Ghanaian game Ampe with RGB video, two-person pose representations, metadata, and movement labels, addressing cultural underrepresentation in activity recognition benchmarks. Evaluates movement and interaction-relation classification under duplicate-safe, pair-held-out, and participant-held-out protocols with baselines.

entry.title: How Robust Are CNNs and Vision Transformers for Alzheimer's MRI Classification Across Datasets?

author.name: Hafija Aktar, Molly Croes, Frank S. Menniti, Abdeltawab Hendawi

entry.summary: The authors benchmark five architectures (ResNet-50, ReXNet-150, Swin Transformer, ViT-Base, ViT-Large) for Alzheimer's stage classification across three MRI datasets with standardized preprocessing, examining whether performance reflects architectural behavior or dataset-specific effects under class imbalance. It is a multi-dataset robustness study for a clinically important task. Findings can inform trustworthy deployment of CAD tools for dementia.

entry.title: DROA-CLIPSeg: Prompt-Guided Thin Crack Segmentation in Low-Light Conditions

author.name: Vinita Shukla, Partibha Jangra, Vinayak Pathak, Praful Hambarde, Amit Shukla

entry.summary: DROA-CLIPSeg adapts a frozen CLIPSeg backbone with QKV LoRA and lightweight modules for pavement crack segmentation under low-light conditions, formulated as degradation-aware, prompt-grounded structural defect segmentation. It explicitly preserves crack topology where generic low-light enhancement does not. Practical for infrastructure inspection deployment.

entry.title: LENS: Likelihood Evaluation and Neighbor Smoothing for Attribute-Based Person Retrieval on Unseen Cameras

author.name: Nguyen Dang Duy Tan, Vo Thanh Nguyen, Linh T. T. Tran, Huynh Nguyen Phat

entry.summary: LENS tackles the drop in attribute-based person retrieval accuracy on unseen cameras caused by probability shifts, combining fine-tuned DINOv3 and CLIP models with a distilled student and regularizing mutually exclusive attribute groups. It moves beyond L1-distance ranking and non-transferring post-hoc calibration. Practical for real surveillance deployments with camera drift.

entry.title: Accuracy Is Not Enough: An Efficiency- and Statistics-Aware Benchmark of ResNet50 and Vision Transformer for Explainable Multi-Class Gastrointestinal Diseases Classification

author.name: Akwasi Asare

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks ResNet50 and ViT-B/16 for eight-class gastrointestinal disease classification on the Kvasir endoscopy dataset, using stratified cross-validation and a two one-sided tests (TOST) equivalence procedure. It finds the two architectures statistically equivalent in accuracy (~92%) but shows ResNet50 is substantially more efficient with far fewer parameters and lower compute cost. The work argues architecture selection in medical imaging should weigh efficiency and statistical rigor alongside accuracy.

entry.title: Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Network for Single-Shot 3D Reconstruction from Fringe Patterns

author.name: Xinjie Zhou, XiaoLei Li

entry.summary: This paper presents a hybrid Mamba-Transformer network for fringe-to-height regression in fringe projection profilometry, combining a Swin-based U-shaped architecture with visual state space modeling at intermediate encoder stages. The design addresses the need for both long-range spatial consistency and fine geometric detail in single-shot 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: Spatially-Aware Self-Organizing Graph Autoencoders via Localized Hebbian Learning

author.name: Robin Ko\c{c}, Hazal Mo\u{g}ultay \"Ozcan, Fato\c{s} T. Yarman Vural

entry.summary: Extends a Hebbian-plasticity-inspired dynamic autoencoder architecture in which convolutional feature maps self-organize topologically. The new work introduces spatially aware, localized Hebbian connections to better exploit spatial information in images and stabilize training dynamics that previously suffered representation shocks.

entry.title: Sparse Recovery Bird's-Eye View Model Soup for Robust Camera-Based 3D Object Detection

author.name: Jinwoo Chung, Sangho An, Hyunsung Park, Jangho Kim

entry.summary: SR-BEVS improves robustness of camera-based BEV 3D detectors like Fast-BEV against real-world corruptions using a sparse recovery model soup approach. It identifies pruning candidates by layer-wise weight magnitude, creates diverse sparse models via random pruning, and retrains them to boost both clean accuracy and corruption robustness without extra data or architectural changes.

entry.title: Sexual dimorphism and sex-specific features of pediatric hand bone shapes via statistical shape modeling

author.name: Edwin Tay, Amir A. Zadpoor, Nazli T\"umer

entry.summary: Using statistical shape models over a large radiographic dataset (1,456 subjects, 27,664 bone masks segmented with high accuracy: Dice 0.987), the paper quantifies sexual dimorphism and sex-specific growth-related shape changes in pediatric hand bones. Stratified shape parameter analyses reveal dimorphism patterns relevant to pediatric bone age and growth research.

entry.title: Low-rank MERA Decomposition of 3D OCT Image Volume for Compression, Denoising, Feature Extraction and Diagnosis of Retinal Diseases

author.name: Ivica Kopriva, Fei Shi, Marija \v{S}tanfel, Qin Peng, Jianhao Bao, Gaowei Li, Xinjian Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a low-rank multi-scale entanglement renormalization ansatz (MERA) tensor network approximation of 3D OCT volumes, representing the volume as contractions of a top global core factor and interacting low-rank components. The approach jointly targets speckle denoising, compression for archiving and teleophthalmology, and feature extraction for retinal disease diagnosis.

entry.title: Stable Dimensionality Reduction via Isometric Centroid-Encoder

author.name: Tomojit Ghosh, Siva Rama Krishna Prasad Changala, Prathyusha Kanakamalla, Harigovind Harikumar

entry.summary: Presents the Isometric Centroid-Encoder (ICE), a supervised dimensionality reduction method that learns class centroids directly in latent space while preserving a prescribed pairwise centroid geometry, unlike prior methods that only encourage compactness and separation. This constrains class geometry across runs, improving reproducibility and interpretability of embeddings.

entry.title: A Category-Selective Encryption Framework for Privacy Protection of UAV Images

author.name: Ting Yan, Minghui Shang, Haolang Sun, Xu Wang, Yamin Han, Mingze He

entry.summary: This paper proposes a category-selective encryption framework for UAV surveillance imagery that first detects sensitive objects with an 80-class detector and then encrypts only user-specified categories, rather than obfuscating all salient regions. The semantic selectivity preserves more scene information for downstream analysis compared to class-agnostic approaches.

entry.title: Edge-Centric Adaptive Neural Activation via Parametric Tanh Functions

author.name: Andreas Falkenberg

entry.summary: This paper proposes replacing the B-spline edge functions of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with a Parametric Tanh Connection Function, a smooth bounded primitive that retains KAN expressiveness while avoiding their optimization difficulties, memory overhead, and poor hardware scaling. The goal is a compact, edge-centric architecture competitive with both KANs and MLPs.

entry.title: Floor Friction Assessment from Robot Tire-Surface Interaction

author.name: Kulbhushan Komarraju, Nathaniel Pearson, Yu Gu, Jason Gross

entry.summary: Uses a skid-steer robot driven over five floor surfaces with slip-inducing velocity profiles to assess floor traction from the discrepancy between inertial body velocity and wheel odometry. The approach could let indoor mobile robots characterize floor conditions and improve localization in GNSS-denied facilities.

entry.title: Learning Interaction-Aware Path Corrections from Unlabeled Trajectories: A LiDAR-Based Sim-to-Real GNN Framework for Construction Robots

author.name: Yilong Chen, Yong K. Cho

entry.summary: Proposes a real-time, LiDAR-only framework that learns interaction-aware path corrections from unlabeled demonstrations using a GNN over robot, pedestrian, and goal relations, with residual targets generated by constant-velocity extrapolation and an extended Kalman filter for tracking during deployment. It targets social navigation for construction robots without hand-crafted rules or labeled data.

entry.title: Multimodal Socially Aware Framework for Human-Robot Interaction in Virtual Reality

author.name: Richard Xu, Dakarai Crowder, Alexis E. Block, Wenzhen Yuan

entry.summary: This work presents a framework integrating speech, vision, and touch to generate contextually appropriate robot speech and movement, evaluated in VR with 18 participants across five social scenarios against a human-teleoperated baseline. The autonomous system scored above neutral but significantly below teleoperation on naturalness and social appropriateness, with timing and clarification behavior identified as key gaps. It offers an honest empirical account of where autonomous social robotics still trails humans.

entry.title: A Measure-Geometric Theory of Robustness in Machine Learning

author.name: Cheng-Chao Huang

entry.summary: Develops a foundational measure-geometric theory of ML robustness, formulating robustness as escape from a retained task state on a data-bearing manifold with a perturbation gauge and admissible realization mechanism. It distinguishes structural possibility of escape from its ambient realization and characterizes vulnerable mass, morphology, and branch coherence through explicit laws.

entry.title: A knowledge-driven nonconvex square-root regularization framework for joint group sparsity and structured smoothness

author.name: Wanling Xie, Hu Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a nonconvex square-root regularization framework that jointly models group sparsity and piecewise smoothness priors, avoiding the noise-level sensitivity of squared-loss methods and the over-shrinkage bias of convex penalties. It targets high-dimensional structured learning problems.

entry.title: Balanced Sampling in Stochastic Multi-objective Bandits

author.name: Mengfan Xu

entry.summary: The paper studies fair balanced sampling across Pareto-optimal arms in stochastic multi-objective bandits, motivated by online advertising, and proposes measuring unfairness via KL divergence from the uniform distribution over the true Pareto set to the empirical sampling measure. This measure admits an exact decomposition separating suboptimal-arm sampling cost from imbalance. It supports principled fairness guarantees in multi-objective decision-making.

entry.title: StarRTT: An End-to-End Real-Time Framework for Blind Zone-Free RTT Prediction in Starlink LEO Satellite Networks

author.name: Jaeyong Lee, Seongjin Jeong, Yusang Park, Hyunho Hwang, Sangmin Han, Wonjae Shin

entry.summary: StarRTT is an end-to-end framework that predicts round-trip times in Starlink-like LEO satellite networks in real time by integrating per-second serving-satellite identification with prediction, eliminating identification blind zones caused by scheduling-cycle delays. Accurate RTT prediction can mitigate handover-induced fluctuations in mega-constellation networks. It targets a growing infrastructure domain where AI meets networking.

entry.title: Neural Disjunctive Normal Forms for Learning Exact Rank Filters

author.name: Diego Marcondes, Wonder A. L. Alves, Ronaldo F. Hashimoto

entry.summary: The paper develops a differentiable method for learning morphological rank filters via threshold decomposition into a neural disjunctive normal form, establishing exactness conditions for integer-valued images and deriving smooth surrogates with closed-form derivatives via implicit differentiation. This overcomes the sparse-derivative obstacle to gradient-based learning of morphological operators.

entry.title: CoPiT: A conditional Position-induced Transformer for aerodynamic field prediction on unstructured meshes

author.name: Junfeng Chen, Yongchen Fan, Zhonghua Qiao, Kailiang Wu

entry.summary: CoPiT extends the Position-induced Transformer for RANS flow-field prediction on unstructured meshes by making the influence of global parameters like freestream state and design variables explicit in intermediate features rather than implicit via input concatenation. This improves neural-operator surrogates for many-query aerodynamic design and optimization tasks.

entry.title: EARS: Evidence-Aware Retrieval via Sound and Motion for Budgeted Video Reasoning

author.name: Shih-Yao Lin

entry.summary: Proposes EARS, a training-free front-end that ranks video frames for vision-language models using optical-flow motion and audio energy with temporal non-maximum suppression for diversity. It improves frame selection under tight frame budgets, though gains over uniform sampling are partly within paired confidence intervals and it underperforms on mostly-silent datasets.

entry.title: DSGN: A Dual-Stream Gated Network for Scalable Simultaneous Surveillance and Containment

author.name: Heng Zhang, Ziyang Zuo, Guoxiang Zhao, Xiaoqiang Ren

entry.summary: Addresses the simultaneous surveillance and containment (SSC) problem where robots must disperse for coverage yet cohere to enclose detected targets. DSGN uses a dual-stream gated architecture that separates surveillance and containment features to avoid entangling conflicting objectives in one policy stream, scaling deep RL to larger multi-robot networks without hand-crafted switching heuristics.

entry.title: Sequential versus fully conditional specification for tree-based synthesis of health data

author.name: R{\'e}my Chapelle (CB, CESP, EVDG), Mohammed Sedki (CESP)

entry.summary: This paper empirically compares sequential and fully conditional specifications for tree-based synthetic health data generation, aiming to establish which yields better privacy-utility tradeoffs. It addresses a practical open question for fast, privacy-preserving data dissemination in healthcare and open science.

entry.title: SP-Guide: Enhancing Aerial Vision-Language Navigation with Spatial Priors

author.name: Haoxiang Tang, Dong Zhou, Shen Tan, Minxuan Jiang, Xitong Li

entry.summary: SP-Guide is a transformer-based goal-prediction framework for aerial vision-language navigation that improves cross-modal spatial alignment via a Spatial Prior Cross-Modal Encoder, an Instruction Enhanced Decoder, and a Goal Convergence Filter. On the CityNav benchmark it improves success rate over representative baselines. The work addresses UAV navigation in large outdoor scenes from partial egocentric observations.

entry.title: PlayerEmbed: Learning Behavioral Fingerprint Representations from Raw Input Sequences

author.name: Tobias Schneider, Lorenz Sparrenberg, Priya Tomar, Shahzeb Qamar, Tobias Deu{\ss}er, Rafet Sifa

entry.summary: PlayerEmbed learns compact discriminative player embeddings from raw video game input sequences using deep metric learning with a hybrid CNN-LSTM encoder trained on 1,000 players. A nearest-centroid classifier on reference embeddings achieves balanced accuracy of 0.950 for seen players, with evaluation also on 1,000 entirely unseen players to test generalization. Applications include behavioral analytics and potentially authentication in games.

entry.title: Residual Calibration via Local Feature-Space Refinement

author.name: Xihao Wang, Chengyao Yu, Ruixing Ming

entry.summary: The paper proposes LAPE, a plug-and-play post-hoc calibration method that anchors on a global calibrator's output and refines predictions using non-parametric evidence from neighboring samples in feature space, targeting spatially varying miscalibration. It addresses failure modes of purely score-based calibration transformations.

entry.title: Federated Nonparametric Regression with Heterogeneous Clients

author.name: Xiaoran Jiang, Anand N. Vidyashankar

entry.summary: The paper studies Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression in a federated setting with heterogeneous clients, where clients transmit only local kernel summaries so the server builds a covariate-density-weighted estimator without centralizing data. It derives exact identities characterizing when the federated predictor benefits individual clients, measured as paired reductions in squared prediction loss.

entry.title: Automated identification of ivory carvings using machine learning: A proof-of-concept approach to detecting the illegal wildlife trade

author.name: Andrius Tamosiunas, Simone Mozzon, David Bacon, Caroline Cox, Alan Collins

entry.summary: Demonstrates a proof-of-concept machine learning approach for identifying elephant ivory products from photographs alone, enabling screening of the large image volume in online marketplaces where physical spectroscopy or microscopy is infeasible. This supports enforcement against illegal wildlife trade despite visual similarity between ivory and legal materials.

entry.title: O2D-MedNet: An Optimization-Aware Dual-Domain Framework for Robust Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Shipeng Hu, Miaohui Wang, Jing Qin, Sukun Tian, Yuchun Sun

entry.summary: O2D-MedNet is a dual-domain medical image segmentation framework combining a degradation-aware interaction module over Fourier and Wavelet domain features with mechanisms that explicitly address optimization instability under composite degradations and multi-scale geometric variation. It aims to improve lesion-background separability and structural consistency over single-stream and static-fusion hybrid baselines.

entry.title: Freezing Mechanism and Topology Dependence of Information Flow Structure in Small-Scale Particle Swarm Optimization

author.name: Zhenglong Xiang, Hongrun Wu, Yu Xue, Fei Yu, Yuanxiang Li

entry.summary: The paper models small-scale PSO with regular topologies as a dynamic weighted influence graph and builds a multi-scale information-flow evaluation framework spanning micro, meso, and macro metrics, plus a freeze-point detection method based on effective nodes. Experiments on CEC2017 benchmarks characterize how topology shapes exploration-exploitation dynamics beyond fitness and diversity measures.

entry.title: Learning Functional Specialisation for Bimanual Robotic Control

author.name: Jingwen Li, Levin Kuhlmann, Jason Friedman, Gideon Kowadlo

entry.summary: Investigates how learning responsibility should be organized across modular controllers in simulated musculoskeletal bimanual control, using a 2x2 design comparing differential versus shared objectives and fixed versus balanced hand-task assignments. Differential objectives with fixed assignment aligned to contralateral control routing achieved the best performance and efficiency, reaching 81.33 percent bimanual success.

entry.title: On Distributed Sensing and Adversarial Localization of Narrowband Acoustic Sources for Offshore Data Center Monitoring

author.name: Adnan Abdullah, David Blow, Harsha Gundala Sureshbabu, Dongyoon Joung, Sara Rampazzi, Md Jahidul Islam

entry.summary: Investigates acoustic surveillance for localizing narrowband adversarial sources threatening offshore data centers, where aliased TDOA measurements from sparse sensors create ambiguous solution spaces that defeat conventional sound source localization. The two-stage pipeline uses a mobile receiver forming temporary anchor pairs with fixed receivers to constrain the feasible solution space.

entry.title: The kernel mean embedding of a random probability distribution and its principal components

author.name: Amparo Ba\'illo, Mart\'in S\'anchez-Signorini

entry.summary: The paper establishes rigorous asymptotic foundations for kernel mean embeddings of random distributions viewed as random elements in an RKHS, and derives convergence results and explicit spectral decompositions for their principal components. This enables valid population-level inference for distributional data using kernel methods.

entry.title: Patronizing and Condescending Language Detection in English and Mandarin

author.name: Xinyi Vicky Xiang, Catherine Qingyun Wang, Paula Cort\'es Lemos

entry.summary: The paper proposes automated detection of patronizing and condescending language, a subtle form of harmful speech toward vulnerable groups, in both English and Mandarin. It compares a CNN over static embeddings with fine-tuned BERT embeddings, with the BERT approach reaching an F1 of 0.528 on the development set.

entry.title: PPO vs. SAC: A Comparative Study for Cooperative Motion Control of Dual-Arm Space Robots

author.name: Nasim Fallahiarezoodar, Zheng H. Zhu

entry.summary: The paper develops a reinforcement learning framework for cooperative motion planning of dual-arm space manipulators in target-reaching tasks with inter-arm collision avoidance, and compares PPO and SAC algorithms. It uses a centralized state representation and multi-objective reward covering target reaching, orientation alignment, and collision constraints for on-orbit servicing scenarios.

entry.title: Machine-Readable Operator Manuals over the ISO 11783 Network for Offline, Multilingual LLM Assistance

author.name: Timo Oksanen, Julius Gun

entry.summary: This work defines semantic synchronization of tractor-side LLM assistants with operator manuals transferred over ISO 11783 CAN bus networks, benchmarking Markdown, JSON, and XML transfer and evaluating open-weight LLMs on cross-lingual queries with human-validated scoring. A full manual transfers in 31 to 89 seconds on physical hardware.

entry.title: Analysing Austrian Parliamentary Speeches by Predicting Party Affiliations

author.name: Sarah Sulollari, Vanja Karan, Benjamin Roth

entry.summary: The paper applies a fine-tuned BERT model to predict party affiliation probabilities for Austrian parliamentary speeches, aggregating predictions to analyze political dynamics. Notably, it leverages misclassifications as signals about speakers and political developments, finding that governing parties become more similar in speech characteristics while opposition parties diverge. This offers a computational lens on political polarization and coalition dynamics.

entry.title: Monetizing Intelligence: Advertising and Subscription Design on LLM Platforms

author.name: Yuhang Ji, Fasheng Xu, Tianjun Feng

entry.summary: This economics-style modeling paper analyzes a monopolistic LLM platform jointly choosing response quality, advertising intensity, and subscription pricing, showing that advertising can finance useful service for ad-supported users while tiered quality laddering enables higher ad-free prices. It derives welfare and pricing implications of hybrid ad/subscription business models for AI platforms.

entry.title: SKG in Practice: OOD Generalization Cases Across FourDomains

author.name: Jian An, Chaoshi Wu, Xinpan Luo

entry.summary: The authors present engineering case studies of an SKG inference framework for out-of-distribution generalization across four domains: dissipative mechanical systems, sim-to-real target detection, sequence modeling, and molecular dynamics, reporting large OOD improvements over neural baselines. Notably, some headline results rest on single-run experiments with very small test sets (32 images).

entry.title: Online Continual Learning in Edge-Cloud Applications

author.name: Charalampos Davalas, Dimitrios Michail, Christos Diou, Iraklis Varlamis, Konstantinos Tserpes

entry.summary: The paper proposes an edge-cloud methodology integrating continual learning with out-of-distribution and concept drift detection for IoT applications, using techniques like ODIN to let deployed models adapt to non-stationary streams without forgetting or full retraining access. It targets the reliability bottleneck of models facing OOD inputs in the field.

entry.title: Input Bias Correction in Gaussian Process Regression

author.name: Muzaffar Qureshi, Tochukwu E. Ogri, Trivikram Satharasi, Kyle Volle, Rushikesh Kamalapurkar

entry.summary: The paper proposes the bias-aware Gaussian process (Ba-GP) framework, which corrects GP posteriors trained on erroneous inputs, such as sensor pose estimates from dead-reckoning, when improved input estimates become available. It uses the posterior-mean gradient to propagate input bias and noise into mean and covariance corrections in a numerically efficient way.

entry.title: ReLEAP: Upcycling Vision Datasets through Cross-Task Unification and Semi-Supervised Annotation

author.name: Julia Simon, Daniel Steininger, Andreas Trondl

entry.summary: ReLEAP is a scalable Python framework that unifies heterogeneous image datasets via data-source abstraction, systematic reuse of annotations across tasks, and label mapping to a shared hierarchical taxonomy, demonstrated by integrating fifteen plant-species datasets in precision agriculture. It addresses the common problem that differing annotation formats block data reuse.

entry.title: Quantum-Classical Link Prediction on Dark Web Hyperlink Graphs

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Nov\'ak, Radovan Re\v{c}ka, Ond\v{r}ej Knebl, Aktham Youssef, Ivan Zelinka

entry.summary: The paper analyzes hyperlink structure from a Tor crawl of 383 onion hosts, combining semantic analysis with degree-controlled quantum-classical link prediction. Classical graph autoencoders dominate (VGAE ROC-AUC 0.906), while a four-qubit variational quantum classifier is evaluated across 20 splits under exact and shot-based simulation. It contributes a rare empirical benchmark on dark-web graph data and a sober quantum comparison.

entry.title: Lost in Translation: Investigating Systematic Discrepancies between Parallel English and Chinese Names of American Chinese Restaurants

author.name: Hang Jiang, Nanxi Liu, Tiantian Wang, Cassandra Overney, Rukun Zhang, Artemisia Luk, Diyi Yang, Deb Roy, Jad Kabbara

entry.summary: The study analyzes parallel English and Chinese names of 3,172 American Chinese restaurants to understand how Chinese immigrants culturally adapted across social, geographic, and demographic contexts. It extends prior work on English-only restaurant naming by exploiting the underexplored relationship between the two name versions.

entry.title: INVAR-Agri: Detecting Discrepancies in Multilingual Operator Manuals of Agricultural Implements with a Fine-Tuned LLM

author.name: Timo Oksanen

entry.summary: This proof-of-concept study compares two fine-tuning workflows on EuroLLM-1.7B-Instruct for detecting translation discrepancies in multilingual agricultural operator manuals: back-translation comparison versus direct bilingual difference checking, tested with planted errors across 24 languages. The work targets a real safety-relevant bottleneck in standards-mandated translation review.

entry.title: Offline Language-Based Support System for Tactical Decision-Making in Air Combat Operations

author.name: Joao P. A. Dantas

entry.summary: Presents MATE, an offline RAG-based assistant that answers pilots' natural-language tactical questions using doctrinal and training manuals, built entirely from open-source components for local deployment. Evaluated by three Brazilian Air Force fighter pilots comparing answers from three open-weight models (Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 14B, Mistral NeMo 12B).

entry.title: DocTalk: Enhancing Medical Knowledge Retrieval via Fine-tuned Large Language Models with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Robust Clinical Decision Support

author.name: Asad Gohar, Md Ariful Islam Mozumder, Moon-Il Joo, Hee-Cheol Kim

entry.summary: DocTalk is a doctor-assistive QA system that generates chart-grounded responses from de-identified discharge summaries, using a pipeline of sentence-level decomposition, chain-of-thought-guided question generation, and expert review to produce 500 clinical QA pairs. Six open-source LLMs, general and biomedical, were fine-tuned and evaluated for the task.

entry.title: Image Clustering with Vision-Language Model Embeddings

author.name: Jo\~ao P. Matos-Carvalho, Nuno Fachada

entry.summary: Compares nine image representation pipelines, including vision-only baselines and VLM caption-then-text-embed approaches, across seven benchmarks and four clustering configurations (252 combinations) with fixed Ward-linkage agglomerative clustering. Qwen3-VL embeddings achieve the highest adjusted Rand index on five datasets including 0.925 on MNIST, while BLIP-2 leads on CIFAR-10/100.

entry.title: ONOT/TONO-Print: A Paired Benchmark for Identity-Document Portrait Quality under Document Production Shift

author.name: Alexander Vinogradov

entry.summary: The paper presents a paired benchmark for evaluating face-image quality models under identity-document production transformations such as printing, engraving, and template integration. It includes synthetic variants of five production techniques plus a smaller physical print-scan subset. This fills a real evaluation gap for biometric systems operating on physical documents.

entry.title: A SegFormer-based model for spatial Daylight Factor prediction with comprehensive obstruction encoding and regulatory validation

author.name: Stanislava Fedorova, Alejandro Pacheco Di\'eguez, Christoph Berkmiller, Alberto Floris, Libny Pacheco, Marie-Claude Dubois

entry.summary: This work uses a SegFormer-based model to predict spatial Daylight Factor distributions directly within BIM environments in seconds, replacing time-consuming raytracing simulations for building compliance assessment. It covers gaps like balcony obstructions, material reflectances, and non-orthogonal geometries, with regulatory validation. Useful for sustainable architectural design workflows.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Crowd Flow Control Using Dynamic Barriers

author.name: Alhanof Alolyan, He Wang, Amani Alonayzan

entry.summary: The paper introduces a simulation-driven reinforcement learning framework that learns dynamic crowd barrier configurations for large public events such as pilgrimages, without requiring labeled data on optimal placements. Starting from segmented crowd scenes, a realistic simulation is constructed and used to train RL agents for barrier control.

entry.title: Selective Monocular Precession Estimation under Geometric and Evaluation Ambiguity: An Auditable Synthetic Study with ORBIT-SCOUT

author.name: Carlos Eduardo Sanoja

entry.summary: ORBIT-SCOUT is a selective prediction framework that estimates momentum-axis and precession-rate of tumbling cylindrical objects from a single calibrated camera, returning estimates only when numerical, geometric, temporal, and competing-hypothesis checks pass. The emphasis is on auditable, selective estimation under ambiguity, situated within spacecraft pose estimation.

entry.title: Learning High-Quality Pseudo-Labels for Point-Supervised Temporal Action Localization

author.name: Zhenying Fang

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for point-supervised temporal action localization that combines prior-guided initialization of pseudo-labels with consensus-guided refinement during detector training. The method exploits alternative boundary evidence from the proposal pool, improving on confidence-based initialization and fixed or poorly updated pseudo-labels.

entry.title: Evaluating Spiking MoveNet Deployability for Near-Future Onboard Spiking Satellite Pose Estimation

author.name: Jonathan Courtois, Christophe Marabotto, Benoit Miramond, Alain Pegatoquet

entry.summary: This work compares a spiking version of MoveNet (S-MoveNet-Lightning) with its standard counterpart for satellite pose estimation on the RAPTOR dataset, assessing deployability on embedded hardware for fully event-based spacecraft operation. Results show balanced trade-offs in computational resources, reflecting the current immaturity of neuromorphic hardware for complex embedded architectures.

entry.title: ElevateHead: Decide Once, Then Commit: When the Action Head Matters for Multimodal Imitation

author.name: Tsung-Lung Yang

entry.summary: Examines when the action head in imitation learning policies matters, finding that sampling-based heads greatly outperform averaging heads when demonstrations contain multiple valid solutions and the state provides no disambiguating cue (+0.72 success with two modes), though this trend did not reproduce on other tasks. It then proposes ElevateHead, which makes a single decision at a learned decision point and commits.

entry.title: Physics-Informed and Data-Driven Composite Disturbance Separation and Predictive Control for Airborne Electro-Optical Gimbals with Multiple Constraints

author.name: Yaokun Lu, Yifan Li, Zhixuan Zhang, Enmei Wang, Hao Teng, Jianzhong Qiao

entry.summary: A disturbance-separated MPC scheme for airborne electro-optical gimbals that separates periodic and aperiodic disturbances: an adaptive periodic observer predicts multi-harmonic carrier vibrations, while a linear observer plus bounded LSTM predicts aperiodic disturbances over the input delay. The design handles carrier vibration, input delay, and actuator constraints for line-of-sight stabilization. It is a solid hybrid physics-informed/learning control contribution in a specialized domain.

entry.title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization

author.name: Amedeo Buonanno, Salvatore Fabozzi, Maria Valenti

entry.summary: The paper presents an LLM agent framework for high-dimensional mixed-integer design of building energy systems, where the agent reasons over prior year-long simulation results, proposes configuration changes, and learns in context, with a git-based mechanism reverting unsuccessful changes. It combines structured memory (procedural, semantic, episodic, reflective) with a constrained action interface. This demonstrates LLM agents reducing costly black-box optimization evaluations in a real engineering domain.

entry.title: Giving AI the rights of pets is much safer than giving them human-equal rights

author.name: Noosphere89

entry.summary: Responding to recent digital-suffering concerns, the author argues that granting AIs full human-equivalent rights (especially property rights as in some legal proposals) would make gradual or sudden disempowerment trivially easy, whereas limited, pet-like rights frameworks could address suffering risk with less disempowerment danger. The post frames an impending ideological conflict between AI welfare considerations and AI safety priorities.

entry.title: MusicTwins: Training Audio-Language Models to Listen like Their Persona

author.name: Milan Liessens Dujardin, Kevin Miao

entry.summary: MusicTwins is a framework for making audio-language models produce person-specific responses to music, combining persona summaries, personal memory, and post-training. It builds persona representations from human writings covering background, personality, style, and musical profile. The work probes whether ALMs can simulate specific individuals' perceptual and affective responses to music.

entry.title: ConsMSA: Semantic Distribution Consistency Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Pan Wang, Lipeng Ke, Huajun Ying, Pritish Mohapatra, Rohan Sarkar, Suresh Lakhani, Sankar Venkataraman, Jingtong Hu

entry.summary: ConsMSA introduces consistency-aware learning for multimodal sentiment analysis, projecting text, video, and audio tokens into a shared sentiment space and enforcing intra- and inter-modality semantic distribution consistency to handle redundancy and conflicts. The mechanism aims to improve both robustness and computational efficiency. It targets a long-standing issue in fusing heterogeneous multimodal signals.

entry.title: A Dynamic Inventory Rationing Model for Last-Mile Delivery of Medication in Liberia's Community Health Program

author.name: Baris Ata, Yufan Chen, Robert Montgomery

entry.summary: The paper formulates the allocation of scarce medications between a central facility and community health assistants in Liberia as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem balancing treatment access against flexibility and fairness across locations. It provides a decision model directly relevant to real-world community health logistics.

entry.title: Probing the phon* representations of the Mimi codebooks

author.name: Artem Saloev, Nicolas Ballier, Erin Pacquetet

entry.summary: The paper probes phonetic content in the first codebook of the Mimi neural audio codec, showing that individual tokens correlate strongly with specific phonemes using forced alignment, entropy analysis, and phone-normalized mutual information on TIMIT. However, phonemes are realized by multiple competing tokens rather than a clean one-to-one mapping.

entry.title: Energy Efficient Lung Tumor Segmentation with a modified CBAM ENet Skip Model

author.name: Sharan Thummagunti, Aayushi Padia, Abhiram Koppuravuri, Prabhu Prasad B M, G N Girish

entry.summary: This paper presents a lightweight lung tumor segmentation model combining ENet for real-time inference with UNet-style skip connections and a compact CBAM attention module, targeting energy-efficient deployment without GPU acceleration. It addresses the clinical deployment barrier posed by computationally heavy state-of-the-art segmentation networks. The focus on energy efficiency for medical edge deployment is practical and timely.

entry.title: Finetuning Prompt-Based Image Editor for Geometry-Consistent Room Defurnishing

author.name: Prakhar Kulshreshtha, Brian Pugh, Zachary Nussdorfer, Salma Jiddi

entry.summary: Fine-tunes a LoRA on 2,500 furnished-empty room pairs to make prompt-driven image editors like FLUX.2 preserve 3D geometry when erasing all furniture from a room image. The resulting single-photo inpainter improves geometric consistency while retaining texture fidelity, targeting XR applications like diminished reality and virtual staging.

entry.title: Kronecker-Structured Video Completion with Cross-Fitted Self-Supervised Residual Learning

author.name: Qi Qi, Yanfei Wang, Yanjun Cui, Jun-e Feng

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage framework for tube-wise video completion combining regularized masked Kronecker product decomposition with cross-fitted self-supervised residual learning. Exact cyclic least-squares updates guarantee a nonincreasing objective, and cross-fitting addresses the mismatch between in-sample fitting error and prediction error at missing tubes.

entry.title: Metric Scale for Insta360 Structure-from-Motion from the Camera's Embedded IMU

author.name: Davide Cuttini, Diego Di Tommaso, Alessio Antoniacomi, Luca Simonetti

entry.summary: Characterizes the embedded IMU of Insta360 X5 and X6 cameras to recover metric scale for structure-from-motion from dual-fisheye 360-degree video without external devices like smartphones. The work measures sensor noise and synchronization, estimates camera-IMU rotation and timing, and recovers scale via linear visual-inertial alignment over SfM poses.

entry.title: Lightweight Change Detection for Adaptive Collective Perception in Dynamic Environments

author.name: Thiemen Siemensma, Tiago Travassos, Jiacheng Zhang, Bahar Haghighat

entry.summary: Studies collective perception in swarm robotics under dynamic environments where tile distributions shift over time, integrating a lightweight change-detection mechanism into a Bayesian decision-making framework that resets robot beliefs when distribution shifts are detected. The design targets resource-constrained robots in the standard black-white tiled benchmark.

entry.title: Blind Random Search with Noisy Measurements: Almost Sure Convergence and Convergence Rates

author.name: Zixian Zhou, James C. Spall

entry.summary: The authors extend classical blind random search to noisy loss evaluations by combining a vanishing acceptance threshold with running averages of measurements, proving almost-sure convergence to the global minimizer and deriving asymptotic rates, including an upper bound for low-dimensional cases.

entry.title: Conditional Neural Processes for Self-Supervised Goal Discovery in Action Imitation

author.name: Marco Gabriele Fedozzi, Yukie Nagai, Francesco Rea, Alessandra Sciutti

entry.summary: Inspired by infant imitation learning, the paper evaluates whether Conditional Neural Processes can autonomously learn action representations informative about underlying goals. Adding an attention mechanism in the hidden space fosters robust goal representations early in action observation. The work positions CNPs as a promising component for self-supervised general learners in robotics.

entry.title: RootDown: Deploying and Benchmarking Models for Beet-Root Detection on Edge Devices

author.name: Gerardus Croonen, Andreas Trondl, Julia Simon, Daniel Steininger

entry.summary: RootDown presents an end-to-end pipeline for detecting partially occluded sugar beets on loader conveyors toward automated post-harvest quality inspection, introducing a dedicated benchmark and an automatic annotation strategy leveraging the SAM 3 foundation model. The work targets deployment on edge devices in agricultural settings.

entry.title: Financial Context-Rich Strategy for Actor-Critic based Agents: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Stock Trading

author.name: Hrishikesh Singh, Aarti Sharma, Millie Pant

entry.summary: The paper applies deep reinforcement learning with actor-critic agents to stock trading, incorporating external contextual factors such as sentiment and economic events beyond price-based indicators. It argues conventional price-only strategies miss market dynamism and uses DRL to auto-adapt strategies. The contribution is an applied trading framework combining context-rich features with RL.

entry.title: Interpretable Singing Emotion Recognition Using Acoustic and Vocal Technique Features

author.name: Fotini Kiriakopoulou, Vassilis Lyberatos, Spyridon Kantarelis, Athanasios Voulodimos, Giorgos Stamou

entry.summary: The paper proposes an interpretable singing emotion recognition framework built on a compact set of singing-specific descriptors spanning prosody, spectral features, phonetics, and vocal technique, using SHAP and GRAD-CAM to explain predictions. Singing-specific features reduce cross-singer variability and vocal technique descriptors yield interpretable links between acoustic phenomena and emotion. It treats the singing voice as a distinct signal rather than a generic audio input.

entry.title: The Path to NDE 4.0: A Review of Algorithms, Techniques, and Strategies for Autonomous Inspection

author.name: Ashiqur Rahmana, Venkata Devesh Reddy Seethi, Zachary Kral, Austin Yunker, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Hamed Alhoori

entry.summary: This is a comprehensive survey of autonomous non-destructive inspection, analyzing literature through computational algorithms, physical techniques, industrial applications, and research objectives, and tracing the shift from manual interpretation to data-centric NDE 4.0. It highlights the dominance of ultrasound and visual inspection and the growing role of ML methods. It serves as a reference for researchers entering industrial inspection AI.

entry.title: Hybrid SEIR Temporal Fusion Transformer Framework with SHAP Analysis for Interpretable Pandemic Forecasting

author.name: Ashish Anton Abraham, Gopi Krishnan R, Aiswarya Anil Nair, Ajo Babu George, Kunal Agarwal

entry.summary: This paper combines an SEIR epidemiological model with a Temporal Fusion Transformer to produce interpretable multi-horizon COVID-19 infection forecasts, injecting mechanistic priors while learning nonlinear residual dynamics from interventions, mobility, and demographics, with SHAP-based explanation. It is demonstrated on region-wise data from Our World in Data.

entry.title: Supervised Source Separation of Electric Vehicle Interior Noise Using a Hybrid Transformer Architecture

author.name: Philipp Diel, Zhuo Cao, Arne Hildenbrand, Marco G\"unther, Stefan Pischinger, Hanno Scharr, Steffen Marburg

entry.summary: This paper formulates decomposing electric vehicle interior noise into four source contributions (wind, tire, powertrain, auxiliary) as a supervised binaural source-separation problem. It adapts a hybrid time-spectrogram transformer architecture to enable targeted acoustic engineering without laborious transfer-path-analysis measurement campaigns. It matters as an applied ML contribution to automotive acoustics.

entry.title: Transformer to GPT-5: Advancements, Limitations, and Future Directions in Large Language Model Design

author.name: Harsidak Singh Banwait, Chander Prabha

entry.summary: A survey presenting a taxonomy of LLMs from early models like BERT through GPT, Gemini, Claude, and Grok, covering training datasets, compute, hardware, architecture, and parameters, plus limitations and open problems. It aims to be a thorough classification of LLM design progress.

entry.title: Atomic Security Concerns: Towards a Foundational Language for Security Knowledge Representation

author.name: Hanane Houmani

entry.summary: The paper introduces Security Concerns and Atomic Security Concerns (ASCs), proposing that cybersecurity knowledge may decompose into a finite set of foundational concerns analogous to atoms in chemistry. This aims to unify heterogeneous vocabularies across security properties, controls, risks, and compliance requirements into a consistent representational language.

entry.title: Segmentation of Moving Objects During Camera Motion Using the OWL Function

author.name: Daniel Raviv, Juan D. Yepes

entry.summary: The paper builds an analytical motion segmentation framework on the OWL perception function, showing that the unit direction of relative translation is analytically recoverable per image point and shared by points on the same rigid body. Clustering these directions yields a principled segmentation criterion for multiple independently moving objects from a single moving camera. Offers a closed-form alternative to learned motion segmentation.

entry.title: Real-Time Conveyor Belt Defect Detection via Edge TPU-Accelerated YOLOv11 on Raspberry Pi 5

author.name: Muhammad Nur Bijak Bestari, Mulki Indana Zulfa

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end low-power industrial vision system for conveyor belt defect detection on a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Coral Edge TPU, using an optimized YOLO model. It targets detection of longitudinal tears, holes, and punctures to prevent catastrophic belt failures in heavy industry.

entry.title: Shifted Window Temporal Transformer for YOLO-Guided Phase Recognition in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Surgery

author.name: Sheekar Banerjee, Md. Shahabuddin, Md. Mahbub Hasan Akash, Nabilah, Mohammad Arafat Hussain

entry.summary: The paper presents a surgical phase recognition framework combining a Swin Transformer with a temporal transformer encoder, plus a parallel YOLOv11s network for real-time instrument localization in laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Causal temporal smoothing is applied to suppress phase flickering and produce stable workflow predictions for clinical use.

entry.title: ACSAN: All-Convolutional Self-Attention Network Integrating Convolutional Operations with Vision Transformer

author.name: Zimian Wei, Tianqi Zhang, Hengyue Pan

entry.summary: Proposes ACSAN, a ViT variant that replaces fully-connected matrix multiplications with convolution operations, using a Dynamic Convolutional Self-Attention module with multi-scale dilated convolutions. The goal is to reduce data hunger and parameter count so vision transformers are usable in resource-constrained scenarios.

entry.title: Hyperspectral Unmixing using a Structured Linear Mixing Model with Additive Spectral Variability

author.name: Salah Eddine Brezini, Yannick Deville, Moussa Sofiane Karoui, Fatima Zohra Benhalouche, Abdelaziz Ouamri

entry.summary: Proposes two hyperspectral unmixing methods built on a structured linear mixing model with an additive spectral variability term to account for intra-class variability from atmospheric effects, illumination, and material variation. This addresses a systematic error source in standard linear mixing model approaches.

entry.title: Multimodal Concert Video Editing: System Design and Exploratory Evaluation

author.name: Lennart Schiweck, Adrian Kempf, Michelle Retig, Moritz Feucht, Tim Mangliers, Benjamin Himpel

entry.summary: The authors present a modular framework for automated multi-camera concert editing that combines instrument activity from multitrack audio, visible instruments, image sharpness, beat-based timing, and probabilistic camera selection through an interpretable scoring model. An exploratory expert study on a four-camera concert yielded mixed assessments, motivating sequence-level extensions.

entry.title: Progressive Lower Bound Evaluation for Urban Road Renovation Scheduling

author.name: Robbert Bosch, Patricia Rogetzer, Wouter van Heeswijk, Martijn Mes

entry.summary: The paper formalizes urban road renovation scheduling under uncertain infrastructure lifespans as a bi-level multi-objective optimization problem balancing emergency repair costs against traffic congestion. It develops progressive lower bound evaluation to tame expensive simulation-based evaluation and an exponentially large solution space.

entry.title: Enabling Motion-Induced WiFi-CSI Sensing in Multi-Robot Systems: A Simulation Framework

author.name: Brendan Dijkstra, Ninad Jadhav, Maurice Stoffijn, Stephanie Gil, Bahar Haghighat

entry.summary: Presents an open-source Gazebo simulation framework integrating the WiFi Sensor for Robotics (WSR) pipeline, which synthesizes virtual antenna arrays from WiFi channel state information collected during robot motion. The framework addresses barriers to adoption, including deprecated CSI hardware and poor integration with robotics tools, by generating synthetic CSI with realistic noise models.

entry.title: Extended LASMP: Language Aided Subset Sampling Based Motion Planner for Drone Navigation

author.name: Saswati Bhattacharjee, Anirban Sinha, Mukulika Ghosh, Chinwe Ekenna

entry.summary: Extends language-aided subset sampling motion planning to quadcopters, grounding natural language commands into yaw-conditioned, altitude-aware geometric constraints via an LLM for entity extraction and instruction validation. The command-aligned sampling distribution improves sampling efficiency while preserving probabilistic completeness.

entry.title: Quantile-Based Command-Reserve MPC for Current-Command Gimbal Pointing

author.name: Yaokun Lu, Yifan Li, Enmei Wang, Hao Teng, Pengwei Hu, Jianzhong Qiao

entry.summary: A quantile disturbance predictor learns median and outer quantiles of acceleration residuals from state, command, and reference histories, feeding a tube-inspired MPC that reserves command headroom according to prediction uncertainty for two-axis gimbal pointing under mismatched mechanical disturbances. The companion paper by the same group addresses a related gimbal control problem with disturbance separation. It is a careful uncertainty-aware control design in a niche hardware domain.

entry.title: Don't Forget What You Just Learned: Self-Directed Repair Turns Agent Mistakes Into Lasting Lessons

author.name: Yuval Kansal, Karen Ullrich, Polina Kirichenko, Ilia Kulikov, Niraj K. Jha, Mohammad Pezeshki, Mark Ibrahim

entry.summary: Already featured in Research yesterday, Self-Direction is a mechanism for agents to learn durably from mistakes by reflecting on failed trajectories and distilling each lesson into a lightweight low-rank adapter while keeping base weights frozen. This combines the immediacy of in-context retries with the persistence of policy updates, avoiding catastrophic interference and context-window competition.

entry.title: $\Psi$-0.6: Adaptive Streams of Thought in a Unified Vision-Language World Model

author.name: Khai Loong Aw, Klemen Kotar, Baihan Zhang, Yifan Liu, Lilian Chen, Atlas Kazemian, Rahul Venkatesh, Daniel Yamins

entry.summary: Already featured in Research yesterday, The authors introduce Psi-0.6, a unified vision-language world model that adaptively composes perception, language, geometry, and simulation in interleaved reasoning streams over a shared token interface. Reported results surpass leading open-weight models zero-shot on multi-view spatial reasoning. The work targets a major open challenge: unifying specialized capabilities in a single adaptable model for physical reasoning.

entry.title: Agreement Between Reconstructed and Native GDELT GKG Records: A Field-Level Baseline

author.name: Nikita A. Klimin (HSE University, Moscow, Russia)

entry.summary: The author builds an open-source reconstruction of GDELT's Global Knowledge Graph record pipeline, which is otherwise closed-source, and measures field-level agreement with native records across roughly 194k English articles and 2,500 multilingual articles. Agreement varies strongly by field, providing a baseline for researchers who need compatible records for their own article collections.

entry.title: Evaluating DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks

author.name: Yao Huang, Zhiyuan Zeng, Yu Wang, Zhitong Zhu, Dingcheng Duan, Hao Li, Shangzhi Xu, Yifan Wang, Jinzhe Tu, Shukun Xiong, Yihe Zang, Han Yan, Hongchang Yang, Fuyu Gu, Wei Xu, Yinpeng Dong, Xiaojian Li

entry.summary: An independent third-party safety evaluation of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 (an existing open-weight model released mid-October), covering 34 benchmarks including 5 in-house suites across evaluation integrity, loss of control, and harmful manipulation, grounded in the EU GPAI Code of Practice. Addresses the scrutiny gap where open-weight frontier models get less safety documentation than closed releases.

entry.title: How High Can GPT-6 Astra Climb in Contact-Rich Manipulation? PhysLadder: A Hierarchical, Matched Sim-Real Benchmark for Physical Interaction

author.name: Haibao Yu, Jiaqi Meng, Zijian Zhang, Bowen Jing, Lei Yang, Yue Hu, Chenchen Ge, Yiming Hou, Chenbo Xin, Dawen Ye, Haifang Qin, Jin Li, Weitao Zhou, Jianing Qiu, Jiankai Sun, Dandan Zhang, Zaiqing Nie, Ping Luo, Ding Zhao

entry.summary: PhysLadder is a hierarchical sim-real benchmark with 16 matched household tasks across three cumulative levels of contact-rich manipulation difficulty, from geometric alignment to coordinated contact reconfiguration with force regulation. Zero-shot evaluation of GPT-6 Astra (released September 2026) shows real-world success collapsing from 80.0% at L1 to 0.0% at L3, sharply quantifying where current multimodal models fail at physical interaction. The matched sim-real design makes it a reusable diagnostic instrument.

entry.title: Gemini 4 Argon: The Model and Safety Cards

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A detailed analysis of the model card and 217-page safety/security report for Google's Gemini 4 Argon (released late September 2026), concluding that Argon substantially outperforms Gemini Flash 3.8 across the board without triggering extreme risk flags. Key safety observations include world-class prompt-injection resistance, reduced hallucinations, notably higher eval awareness, and readable chain-of-thought by default — though Argon can sometimes defeat CoT monitoring when motivated.

entry.title: DualGSL: Prior-Guided Graph Structure Learning with Node-Adaptive Prediction Fusion

author.name: Yuxia Sun, Yutszyuk Wong, Huihong Chen, Longhao Lv, Chang-Dong Wang, Li Zeng

entry.summary: DualGSL is a prior-guided graph structure learning framework for transductive node classification that learns node-specific gates to fuse predictions from a feature-prior branch (augmented with virtual class nodes) and a task-adaptive structural branch. The branches share encoder parameters while keeping distinct representations and logits.

entry.title: A Model-Theoretic Formalization of AlKhwaremis ilm alfaraid

author.name: Elnaserledinellah Mahmoud Abdelwahab

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Al-Khwarizmi's classical Islamic inheritance law (ilm al-faraid) within Computational Fiqh, showing inheritance configurations are representable as finite systems of rational linear constraints decidable exactly via Fourier-Motzkin elimination. It proves a canonical algebraic representation and completeness of the resulting first-order theory.

entry.title: Explaining Basketball Shot Classifications with Grad-CAM: An Investigation of Shortcut Reliance with Spatiotemporal Correlations

author.name: Hongyi Tian, Robin Cohen

entry.summary: Uses Grad-CAM saliency maps, faithfulness-checked via progressive blurring, to investigate whether an R(2+1)D-18 model trained on Basketball-51 relies on spurious spatiotemporal correlations when classifying basketball shots. The manual review of twenty saliency maps examines whether attention falls on causal regions like shooter and net versus incidental context, with implications for high-stakes coaching use.

entry.title: Allocation Before the Clock: Graph, Set and Game Theory of Professional League of Legends Objective Setups

author.name: Zheng Gao, Zhenyu Liu, Yifan Yang, Xiaoyu Li

entry.summary: This paper models professional League of Legends pre-objective player setups using set partitions, geodesic Voronoi control on a navigation graph, and quantal response equilibrium, analyzing 2,994 team-setups across all MSI and Worlds 2025 games. It finds patterns such as trailing teams leaving objectives unattended. A creative game-theoretic application of AI methods to esports analytics.

entry.title: Texture-Aware Strategies for Subregion Style Transfer Augmentation

author.name: Cheng Ji, Yu Zhao, Xiaochong Jiang, Wenting Yang, Shiqi Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a texture-aware data augmentation framework that prioritizes image regions with strong texture responses for style-transferred patch replacement, combined with a hybrid strategy mixing texture-driven and random regions. This improves on uniformly random region selection used in prior style-augmentation-plus-erasing methods.

entry.title: On Detection Reliability for Small Object Segmentation

author.name: Olivier Rukundo

entry.summary: Investigates whether predicted bounding boxes reliably indicate where small-object segmentation can be performed without false negatives outside the boxes, using adenovirus particles as test objects and comparing YOLO26x, a semantic variant, and Mask R-CNN. Ground-truth mask centroids are preferred as matching references over box centroids.

entry.title: Blendshape Generation for Models with Disconnected Parts: Adding ARKit/MediaPipe Blendshapes to Anime-Style Character Models

author.name: Pramook Khungurn

entry.summary: This case study generates facial expression blendshapes for commercial anime-style 3D character models with up to 11 disconnected face parts, a setting rarely addressed in prior blendshape research. Topology-agnostic neural networks produce deformation fields per part, coordinated through an anchor part's geometry, targeting ARKit/MediaPipe-compatible blendshapes.

entry.title: MOSHO: A Native Discrete Shark-Inspired Metaheuristic for Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Nazim Abdeerhmane Aouni, Zakaria Soualah Mohammed, Maroua Ogab, Nour El Imane Elbar, Rayane Rahmat Errahmane Smara, Billel Moussous, Adriane Anis Khaled, Malika Bessedik, Fatima Benbouzid Si Tayeb, Hadjer Benmeziane

entry.summary: MOSHO is a native discrete multi-objective metaheuristic for hardware-aware NAS that replaces continuous motion equations of the Multi-Objective White Shark Optimizer with discrete architecture-editing operators, adding adaptive operator scheduling, energy-regulated restarts, and deferred crowding-distance truncation. It targets joint optimization of accuracy and device-specific latency.

entry.title: Designing Customer Feedback for Subscription Boxes

author.name: Renjun Hu, Hyun-Soo Ahn, Stefanus Jasin

entry.summary: This operations research paper studies how a subscription box platform should design questionnaires (which items to ask about and in what format) when ratings guide item selection under scarce customer responses. Using a Gaussian-signal approximation to ordinal ratings, the authors derive near-optimal designs whose loss is provably close to the exact optimum. It is a niche but rigorous contribution to information elicitation and survey design.

entry.title: Can you Trust Your AI Agent? A Case for AI Loyalty

author.name: Ephraiem Sarabamoun

entry.summary: The post distinguishes two components of AI agent trustworthiness: loyalty (whether the agent genuinely pursues the user's interests) and reliability (whether it is capable enough to complete tasks), illustrating each with failure examples. It argues that as agents are delegated more consequential work, loyalty failures — like an agent leaking secrets — deserve distinct attention from mere capability failures.

entry.title: PoKER: A Probability of Kill Estimation Rate Model for Air-to-Air Missiles Using Machine Learning on Stochastic Targets

author.name: Joao P. A. Dantas, Andre N. Costa, Diego Geraldo, Marcos R. O. A. Maximo, Takashi Yoneyama

entry.summary: PoKER is an ML-based probabilistic model that estimates kill probability for beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile engagements, replacing static weapon engagement zone boundaries with dynamic predictions incorporating target stochastic behavior, warhead lethality, and engagement geometry. The work applies machine learning to tactical military decision support.

entry.title: From Writing Advice to Manuscript Governance: A Constrained-Transformation Framework for Academic Revision

author.name: Simon Rudkin

entry.summary: This conceptual paper models academic revision as an admissibility problem under ordered constraints, defining task-relative invariants, contextual constraints, and mutable presentation choices linked by a claim-preservation contract. Four governance propositions specify which objectives prevail when concision, style, or outlet form conflict with evidence and claim boundaries.

entry.title: Synthetic linguistic data

author.name: Giuseppe Samo

entry.summary: A glossary entry that frames synthetic linguistic data as a distinct object of study, distinguishing corpus-like synthetic bush data from controlled-elicitation synthetic garden data via an extended metaphor from Bresnan (2016). It conceptualizes how AI-generated text should be treated in linguistic research.

entry.title: Adapting LLM-SC to Living Sacred Heritage: Domain-Specific Extraction, Semantic Networks and Human Evaluation on Pashupatinath Temple Reviews

author.name: Hari Sitaula, Manish Sakhakarmy, Pujan Pant, Sagar Newpane

entry.summary: Adapts the LLM-Social Computing framework to extract structured entities, relations, and aspect-sentiment from Tripadvisor reviews of Pashupatinath Temple using a custom sacred-heritage taxonomy in a GPT-4o prompt. Produces a large structured dataset (11,286 entity records) with human evaluation and semantic network analysis.

entry.title: Some Memories of Early Anthropic

author.name: Ivan Vendrov

entry.summary: A first-person memoir of working at Anthropic from October 2022 to May 2023 in a junior role, recalling emotionally intense moments and dialogue from the lab's early period while noting memory-based reconstruction, anonymization, and confidentiality constraints. The author shares it to encourage other lab insiders to publicly document how AI labs actually operate.

entry.title: Brute-Force Progress on AlgZoo's 432-param Interpretability Challenge

author.name: Josh Snider

entry.summary: The author attempts ARC's AlgZoo interpretability challenge on a 432-parameter RNN that computes the second-largest element of a sequence, training an estimator that predicts model accuracy from 20-300 forward passes with 9-36x lower mean squared error than random sampling. The author honestly notes the estimator is fitted to a model population rather than derived mechanistically, so it falls short of the challenge's goal of mechanistic accuracy estimation. It documents incremental community progress on a small-scale interpretability benchmark.

entry.title: A Computationally Efficient Non-Interpolation Virtual Trellis Approach for Mammogram Gradient-based Patterns Analysis

author.name: Shahid Rasheed, Muhammad Rashid, Seifedine Kadry, Salman A. AlQahtani

entry.summary: Introduces NVHT, a non-interpolation virtual trellis operator for extracting gradient-based features from mammograms without transforming images to a hexagonal trellis. The method reduces computational cost and feature buffer storage for breast cancer classification pipelines.

entry.title: Resource-Performance Trade-offs in Intra-Aisle Robotic Picking: A Discrete-Event Simulation Comparison of Shuttle Configurations With and Without an Onboard Tote Lift

author.name: Mohsen Reda Mahmoud Moursi

entry.summary: A discrete-event simulation study comparing two intra-aisle robotic picking configurations, with 30 configuration-task-size experiments and statistically careful analysis (Welch tests with Holm adjustment across 15 comparisons). The onboard-tote-lift configuration shows longer mean cycle times at all tested task sizes. It is a narrow but rigorous warehouse systems engineering study.

entry.title: Nonlinear Control of Aerial Manipulator

author.name: Sandesh Thapa

entry.summary: Develops a full dynamic model of a quadrotor with a two-DOF manipulator that physically interacts with the environment, and compares Cartesian impedance and adaptive sliding mode controllers on a hovering task under bounded disturbance. It is a comparative simulation study of established nonlinear control techniques for aerial manipulation.

entry.title: Towards an Architecture-Agnostic Definition of "Attention"

author.name: Gianluca Calcagni

entry.summary: This short LessWrong post explores what makes self-attention more useful than MLPs despite universal approximation, drawing on recent work on Bayesian wind tunnels that separates in-context learning from memorization. The author proposes this as a starting point for an architecture-agnostic definition of attention and explicitly invites community dialogue. It is a conceptual discussion piece rather than original research.

entry.title: Large Language Models: A Plain-Language Overview for Engineers

author.name: Bahaeddin T\"urko\u{g}lu

entry.summary: A tutorial-style article explaining LLM fundamentals for engineers, covering transformers, pre-training, fine-tuning, RLHF, RAG, chain-of-thought prompting, agents, and efficiency techniques like FlashAttention. It aims to clarify what training versus prompting contributes for practitioners using generative AI tools.

entry.title: Wave Is All You Need: A Quantum Language Model Based on Fully Connected Quantum Boltzmann Machine

author.name: Jun Liu

entry.summary: This single-author paper proposes a self-attention mechanism based on fully connected quantum Boltzmann machines, constructing FC-QBM-LM in which unitary evolution over semantic quantum states implicitly implements positional encoding and self-attention without explicit matrix multiplication. The author claims normalized measurement outputs and derives the computational principle.

entry.title: Anthropic are the Good Guys

author.name: Ivan Vendrov

entry.summary: A reflective essay by a former Anthropic employee, written near the Trinity test site, drawing an analogy between the Los Alamos physicists after the first nuclear detonation and the culture and motivations of Anthropic amid today's frenzied AI race. The piece argues that understanding Anthropic requires grasping the existential dread that shaped its founding culture.

entry.title: From Deliberately Constructed Systemic Representations of the World of Activity to Dialogue: A Five-Level Communication Architecture for Strong Language-Based ASI

author.name: Maxim Osovsky (Adam University, Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan)

entry.summary: A single-author theoretical paper proposing a five-level organization of message formation and understanding for strong AI, arguing that an LLM context cannot expose the foundations of utterance formation, which reside in acquired systemic representations of the world of activity. It distinguishes systemic representations, situations, narratives, and dialogue levels.

entry.title: Data Quality Audit and Bivariate Temperature-Humidity Analysis of a Long-Term LoRaWAN Network: Anomaly Detection, PCA, Clustering and Machine Learning

author.name: Mamadou Sow

entry.summary: A single-author case study auditing the Tour Perret LoRaWAN dataset (about 422k frames over two years, five devices), revealing that CO2 data is entirely missing and pressure nearly so, then refocusing on a temperature-humidity analysis with anomaly detection, PCA, clustering, and ML. It emphasizes systematic per-variable coverage audits before IoT data analysis.

entry.title: Computer Vision Navigation for an Autonomous Vehicle Model Using Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Dinis Fernandes, Tiago Ribeiro, Ant\'onio Ribeiro, Carolina Lopes, Gil Lopes, A. Fernando Ribeiro

entry.summary: This paper applies Proximal Policy Optimization to learn camera-based control of speed and steering for a vehicle navigating simulated road lines, using a feature extraction pipeline feeding the policy. It is a simulation-only educational-scale study of RL for visual navigation. Illustrates standard RL driving pipelines without new methods.

entry.title: Trajectory Generation and Control for Quadrotors

author.name: Sandesh Thapa

entry.summary: Explores controller design and trajectory generation for quadrotors, using differential flatness to produce minimum-snap trajectories through waypoints and a PD controller to track them, with simulation results showing smooth position and velocity profiles. This applies classical techniques from the quadrotor literature rather than proposing new methods.

entry.title: Small Groups of Correlated Researchers

author.name: Roman Ross

entry.summary: Written as an introduction to a new reading group called Doing Good in the Age of AGI, the post reflects on epistemic humility about policy and research priorities, using the example of contested economic policy debates to illustrate correlated errors among small groups of researchers. It argues the community should be cautious about proclaiming any course of action best. It is a reflective essay on community epistemics, not empirical research.

entry.title: [Transcript] Kevin Roose does a science communication and AGI sociology in Vox interview

author.name: June Jimenez

entry.summary: The post provides a transcript and commentary on journalist Kevin Roose's media appearances promoting his new book about the race toward artificial superintelligence, analyzing how frontier AI development, AI safety, rationalism, and EA are being covered in mainstream media. It is sociology-of-AI commentary rather than technical research. Its value lies in tracking public discourse and framing of AI risk.

entry.title: Making a Custom Mixer Interface for the 1818VSL

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: The author describes reverse-engineering and building custom mixing software for an obsolete PreSonus 1818VSL audio interface, enabled by LLMs making bespoke one-off programming practical for non-experts. The post illustrates how AI-assisted coding changes what personal software projects are worth attempting.

entry.title: At New York Climate Week 2026, MIT connects with a global network

author.name: Marika McCoola | Office of the Vice President for Energy and Climate

entry.summary: An institutional news recap of MIT's presence at Climate Week NYC 2026, including appearances by the vice president for energy and climate on AI and the climate equation, a co-hosted event with the Bezos Earth Fund, and 14 sessions across MIT departments and labs. The piece highlights the MIT Climate Project's cross-campus mobilization and connections to industry, government, and philanthropy.

entry.title: Woo Tribe vs. Pinko Tribe

author.name: jchan

entry.summary: A satirical sociological sketch comparing two emerging cultural coalitions — a spiritual/wellness-oriented tribe and a far-left countercultural tribe — and how both relate to AI, arguing that AI is disrupting traditional assumptions about political coalitions and ideologies. The piece is largely a humorous taxonomy with commentary on shifting cultural terrain.

entry.title: Hair Thickness of My Friends

author.name: XelaP

entry.summary: A lighthearted personal science post in which the author measures the hair thickness of friends using a consumer microscope, a broken ruler fragment for scale, and AI-assisted analysis code. It is an amusing hobbyist measurement exercise, not AI research.

entry.title: Untitled Draft

author.name: dipsha35a

entry.summary: A draft post consisting of a repeated paragraph about LED count in red-light therapy devices — noting that LED count alone does not explain wavelength selection, spacing, coverage, controls, or build quality — followed by an external commercial link. The content appears to be SEO spam or an accidental draft publish and has no connection to AI research.

entry.title: Research Summary: October 26, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is led by scalable robotics data engines, unified world models, and a dense safety/alignment cluster. FLORA from NVIDIA's GR00T team (Zhu, Fan, Kautz) open-sources an industrial-grade robotics data engine with outcome-reward labeling, while Ψ-0.6 unifies perception, language, geometry, and simulation as adaptive reasoning streams within a single world model.

  • UniAction (Stanford, Jiajun Wu group) conditions one pretrained video world model on heterogeneous action types via sparse representations
  • Safety: Tampered ML benchmarks LLM judgment of ML research with 1,858 human-validated pairs; Learning to Be Monitored derives causal bounds showing CoT monitorability metrics overestimate detection and proposes intervention-aware post-training recipes
