It matters as a real-world case study in taming LLM score inflation and variance in high-stakes auditing contexts.

entry.title: ActionRAG: Evidence-Refining Graph Diffusion for Long-Term Memory in LLM Agents

author.name: Navyansh Mahla, Sashank Vandrangi

entry.summary: ActionRAG is a graph-based long-term memory architecture for LLM agents that couples cautious indexing (tiered entity resolution to avoid fragmenting or merging entities) with query-time graph retroevaluation that revises initial similarity scores using surrounding graph evidence. Dual-channel entity and triple retrieval aims to recover precise, mutually consistent evidence from interaction histories. It targets relational questions that flat semantic retrieval handles poorly.

entry.title: MBABench-2.0: Evaluating AI Agents on Constructing Financial Spreadsheets Beyond Simple Verifiability

author.name: Julian Poeltl, Thomson Yen, Patrick Shea, Shubham Anil Varma, Dhruv Rastogi, Zihao Chen, Mengshi Zhang, Hongseok Namkoong

entry.summary: MBABench-2.0 is a benchmark of 101 original spreadsheet construction tasks targeting the full modeling workflow, format design, and layout decisions financial professionals face, rather than fill-in-the-blank edits. This better captures realistic knowledge-work demands on LLM agents. It matters for assessing whether agents can perform genuine financial analysis work from scratch.

entry.title: Rethinking Representation Geometry in Supervised Contrastive Learning under Long-Tailed Data

author.name: Joonhyeok Jeong, Jy-yong Sohn, Kibok Lee

entry.summary: The authors develop a theoretical framework showing that supervised contrastive objectives under long-tailed distributions fail to form the predicted regular simplex geometry at optimum because solutions remain dependent on per-class sample counts. Motivated by this diagnosis, they introduce structural balancing that provably achieves the desired geometry and improves downstream performance.

entry.title: Rethinking LoRA Initialization for Robust Asymmetric Learning Rates

author.name: Disen Liao, Yaoliang Yu

entry.summary: This work studies why LoRA+ style asymmetric learning rates, which use a larger rate for the up-projection matrix B, can cause unstable training and ratio-dependent performance collapse under the standard LoRA initialization. The authors identify the initialization as the culprit and propose revised initializations that make asymmetric learning rates robust. This matters because it reduces hyperparameter brittleness in one of the most widely used parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods.

entry.title: InferSlice: A Reference Architecture for SLO-driven LLM Inference over a Telco Wide-Area Network

author.name: Juan Parra-Ullauri, Anthony Chiu, Hari Madhukumar, Zhaozhou Wu, Anderson Bravalheri, Alex Healing, Andy Corston-Petrie, Dimitra Simeonidou, Nektaria Efthymiou

entry.summary: Presents a reference architecture for SLO-driven LLM inference across geographically distributed telco infrastructure, integrating network slicing, GPU partitioning, elastic serving, and observability to address sovereignty, latency, and locality constraints that centralized cloud serving cannot satisfy. A systems contribution aimed at edge-distributed LLM deployment. Important for operators moving inference to the network edge.

entry.title: Clean-label Poisoning Attack and Defense Game for Federated Learning in Vehicular Networks

author.name: Yalin E. Sagduyu, Tugba Erpek, Nathan Stephenson, Mengran Xue

entry.summary: This paper studies clean-label poisoning attacks against federated learning in vehicular networks, where attackers perturb benign feature vectors toward malicious extremes while keeping labels intact to degrade anomaly detection of Basic Safety Messages. The authors propose a feature-consistency relabeling defense and model the attack-defense interaction as a game to characterize equilibrium strategies. It matters because connected-vehicle safety systems are a realistic and safety-critical FL deployment.

entry.title: PaperScorer: How Predictable Is Paper Acceptance?

author.name: Sachin Konan, Jonathan Liu, Zhuang Liu

entry.summary: PaperScorer is a family of models predicting peer-review accept/reject decisions from extracted paper text or page screenshots, trained on decisions after removing author identity and formatting shortcuts. Vision models are most predictive, achieving 68% accuracy on ICLR papers and 77% on arXiv ML papers, beating text-only and frontier reasoning models. The work quantifies how predictable review outcomes are and probes what signals drive them.

entry.title: Beyond Local Accuracy: Benchmarking the Rollout Reliability of PDE Foundation Models

author.name: Jaewan Park, Seid Koric, Giri Krishnan, Sudhakar Pamidighantam, Surresh Marru

entry.summary: The authors benchmark seven PDE foundation models and baselines on seven time-dependent PDE datasets, defining error amplification as the ratio of full-horizon to short-horizon error to test whether short-horizon advantages persist under autoregressive rollout. They report VRMSE, relative L2, and MAE across scratch-trained, fine-tuned, and frozen in-context settings.

entry.title: From Parameter Rebasin to Functional Transfer Across Heterogeneous Transformers

author.name: Filippo Rinaldi, Aniello Panariello, Giacomo Salici, Simone Magistri, Angelo Porrello, Andrew D. Bagdanov, Simone Calderara

entry.summary: Ariadne is a training-free method that transfers task-specific fine-tuning behavior across heterogeneous Transformers of different depths and widths by characterizing fine-tuning through induced activation changes at matched blocks rather than moving parameter-space task vectors. This avoids shape incompatibility and canonical-coordinate issues.

entry.title: Strongly Adaptive Online Learning with Time-Varying Movement Costs

author.name: Andrew Jacobsen, Emmanuel Esposito, Hao Qiu, Mengxiao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper extends strongly adaptive regret guarantees for online convex optimization to settings where movement (switching) costs vary over time. The authors propose a novel algorithm achieving data-dependent regret bounds on arbitrary sub-intervals, capturing sequential decision-making problems where both the environment and switching costs fluctuate.

entry.title: Real-to-Sim Calibration of Bosch Etching Simulators with Few-Shot XSEM Data and Hybrid Search

author.name: Xinyu Jia, Jainil Shah, Rahul Tripathi, Vijay Gupta, Zhihong Chen

entry.summary: This paper presents a few-shot calibration framework for Bosch-process semiconductor etching simulators, decoupling simulator parameters from direct process variables to infer a recipe-specific parameter vector from sparse XSEM measurements. It enables reliable prediction of etch depth and sidewall angle under held-out process conditions. The work matters for manufacturing because real measurements are costly and sparse, and calibrated simulation can reduce expensive physical experimentation.

entry.title: State Estimation as In-context Tabular Prediction

author.name: Ayushi Jolotia, Parikshit Pareek

entry.summary: This letter reframes power system state estimation as an in-context tabular prediction task, where historical measurement vectors and state estimates form the context for predicting the state from a new measurement. The authors use pretrained tabular foundation models with frozen weights, requiring no power system training data, and demonstrate lower errors than weighted least squares on 14- to 118-bus networks, particularly under low observability and bad data conditions.

entry.title: Probing the limits of forward screening and inverse design of crystal materials

author.name: Zhilong Song, Zijun Pang, Lixue Cheng

entry.summary: The authors match crystals across 55 databases by structure into a self-extending database of 14.6 million crystals and 131.8 million property values, finding only 4.5 percent of crystal-property pairs carry values. They probe the limits of screening- and generation-based materials discovery, providing context for why several announced 'new' generative materials proved to be known phases or close variants.

entry.title: Knowledge Distillation across Item and Code Spaces for Parallel Generative Recommendation

author.name: Yixuan Xu, Hailin Liu, Linxiang Peng, Can Yang

entry.summary: This work proposes two knowledge-distillation objectives that transfer item-level predictive knowledge from sequential recommenders into semantic-ID generative recommenders, bridging the gap between item space (teacher) and code space (student). The goal is to supply distributional information about alternative items beyond hard next-item labels. It targets parallel generative recommendation systems.

entry.title: From Noisy Retrieval to Decision Evidence: Silver Evidence Demonstrations for In-Context Learning

author.name: Masoud Monajatipoor, Fazlolah Mohaghegh, Hamid Reza Hassanzadeh, Akash Uttamrao Bhoite, Robert E. Tillman

entry.summary: The authors propose silver-evidence demonstrations for retrieval-augmented in-context learning: instead of inserting raw retrieved passages into few-shot examples, an LLM generates target-conditioned evidence summaries that are paired with expert labels. This uses existing labels to supervise noise filtering, improving robustness when decision-relevant evidence is buried in long, noisy context.

entry.title: When is more search useful? An Empirical Study of Search Utility in Quality-Aware Decoding for Machine Translation

author.name: Javier Garcia Gilabert, Rico Sennrich, Andr\'e F. T. Martins

entry.summary: This study challenges the uniform candidate-budget assumption in quality-aware decoding for MT, introducing three measures of search utility: total scaling gain, marginal scaling gain, and sampling saturation point. The analysis shows quality gains from additional candidates vary substantially across sentences, enabling adaptive budget allocation for more efficient test-time scaling.

entry.title: KrishokTech: A Bengali Agricultural Advisory System with Explicit Authorization Controls

author.name: Khan Raiyan Ibne Reza, Sanjana Aktar Maria, Shakil Ahmed, Faiyad Hossain, Sumaiya Tabassum Nimi

entry.summary: This paper presents KrishokTech, a Bengali-language agricultural advisory system that places an explicit authorization boundary around LLM generation. It uses rule-based admission checks before retrieval, binds retrieval to a single confirmed crop, and applies a post-generation verifier that removes dosage claims unsupported by external agricultural evidence. The system targets low-resource languages and connectivity-constrained settings, making it a practical example of safety-aware deployment in agriculture.

entry.title: RVG-Bench: A Benchmark for Reasoning-Driven Audio-Visual Temporal Grounding

author.name: Yue Feng, Boshen Xu, Zihao Yue, Xiaokun Liu, Miao Yang, Xin Tao, Pengfei Wan, Qin Jin

entry.summary: Introduces RVG-Bench, a benchmark for reasoning-driven audio-visual temporal grounding where queries require inferring user intent (finding visual evidence, causes of events, or recalled moments) rather than simple descriptive matching. Each query is constructed so the target segment can only be identified through reasoning, with rigorous verification of construction.

entry.title: MDMR-Bench: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Multi-Reference Image Generation

author.name: Bowen Zheng, Jintao Lin, Changheng Yi, Haoran Yang, Binxiao Huang, Chenyang Lei, Rui Liu, Xihui Liu

entry.summary: MDMR-Bench is a multi-dimensional benchmark for image generation conditioned on multiple reference images and text instructions, spanning capability settings such as entity fusion and attribute transfer. Existing benchmarks evaluate too narrowly, so this provides a broader, more diagnostic evaluation suite for an increasingly common generation task.

entry.title: Delay Randomization Widens the Delay Margin of Learned Humanoid Motion Trackers

author.name: Shaoqin Li, Yi Sun

entry.summary: This study quantifies the command-delay sensitivity of learned humanoid motion-tracking policies, finding that with 40 ms constant delay survival drops to about 15 percent with a margin of only 20-30 ms. Randomizing delay between 0 and 50 ms during training raises 40 ms survival to roughly 95 percent and widens the margin to 50-70 ms. Simple, actionable finding for deploying learned humanoid controllers on real hardware.

entry.title: From Freehand Demonstrations to Autonomous Robotic Ultrasound: An Anatomy-Anchored Learning Framework

author.name: Yuan Bi, Fangxu Han, Ye Su, Yiping Zhou, Zhongliang Jiang, Nassir Navab

entry.summary: This paper proposes an anatomy-anchored imitation learning framework for autonomous robotic ultrasound, combining anatomy-guided probe placement from external visual observations with learned ultrasound navigation. The decomposition reflects the anatomically structured nature of expert scanning skills. It moves toward reproducing operator-dependent diagnostic imaging consistently with robots.

entry.title: Natural-Language to Nav2: Operational Policies for Costmap-Based Navigation

author.name: Jiyeong Chae, Hyunkyo Seo, Heonjae Lee, Kyung-Joon Park

entry.summary: This paper presents a natural-language interface for ROS 2 Nav2 robot navigation, using a local LLM to convert operator instructions into JSON policies capturing destinations, spatial constraints, and temporal or event conditions. Deterministic validation checks govern mission acceptance, and costmap adapters inject accepted policies into the navigation stack without altering the planner or controller. Evaluated on 150 real-world scenarios, the approach lets warehouse operators encode temporary access rules and route preferences that raw sensor data cannot convey.

entry.title: Reproducible Evaluation as the Substrate for Safe Prompt Compression in Production Agents

author.name: Prabal Vashisht, Zheng Hu, Ying Yang

entry.summary: The authors present an offline evaluation harness for a production conversational agent that stays reproducible despite changing backend data, with on-demand regeneration when it goes stale. They use it as the fitness function for GEPA-based prompt optimization under a correctness gate that guards against reward hacking, compressing a production merchant-facing agent's prompt by 3.5-7.6% without regressing held-out correctness.

entry.title: Lifelong Context Adaptation through Bidirectional Memory-Skill Learning

author.name: Tianyi Xu, Huazheng Wang

entry.summary: MemCryst is a framework for lifelong LLM agents that jointly learns memory and skills with a frozen language model: recurring episodes in memory support skill creation and revision, while skill-guided interactions feed back into future learning. This bidirectional design addresses the tension between expanding experience and bounded context windows.

entry.title: LGMT: A Tool for Testing the Logical Reasoning Reliability of LLMs

author.name: Zenghui Zhou, Xiaoke Fang, Zheng Zheng

entry.summary: LGMT is an open-source tool that detects LLM reasoning inconsistencies using metamorphic relations grounded in first-order logic: it generates logically equivalent restatements of a source case and checks whether entailment predictions agree, requiring no ground-truth labels. It ships 20 built-in relations and targets LLMs used as reasoning components in software systems. It addresses a reliability gap static benchmarks miss.

entry.title: Astro2Method: Benchmarking LLMs on Machine Learning Method Selection in Astronomy

author.name: Xingzhong Fan, Hangfeng He, Fatemeh Nargesian

entry.summary: Astro2Method is a benchmark of 500 expert-reviewed questions on ML method selection for astronomy, drawn from 346 recent papers with Easy and Hard splits. Five LLMs score 87.5-92.5 percent on Easy questions but only 58.9-64.5 percent on Hard ones, and RAG or agent scaffolding adds little. This reveals a real gap in scientific method-selection reasoning relevant to AI for science.

entry.title: Spectra: Multi-Scale Implicit Decomposition for Deepfake Detection

author.name: Dhananjaya Jayasundara, Kartik Narayan, Vishal M. Patel

entry.summary: Spectra argues that deepfake detectors should analyze how an image is reconstructed, not just how it appears, by fitting implicit neural representations to images and examining internal activations across scales to expose generator-agnostic reconstruction dynamics. This aims to improve generalization across unseen manipulation techniques, compression, and dataset shifts.

entry.title: ReMedI: Inference-Time Refinement and Self-Distillation for Controllable Molecular Optimization

author.name: Jia Yi Zhang, Shivanshu Shekhar, Allison McLevige, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: ReMedI argues that pretrained molecular language models already contain useful edits that zero-shot generation cannot efficiently reach, and uses a Metropolis-Hastings search with inference-time refinement and self-distillation for multi-objective lead optimization. It reduces reliance on expensive task-specific datasets required by RL-based post-training like C-MORAL.

entry.title: Representation Learning via Composite Subspace Flow Matching

author.name: Jos\'e Afonso, M\'ario Figueiredo

entry.summary: Composite subspace flow matching (CSFM) proposes a new self-supervised representation learning paradigm that bridges joint-embedding and generative approaches: instead of isotropic noise corruption, it formulates representation learning as variance-minimizing inversion of a deterministic degradation curriculum across spectral, color, and illumination subspaces. The aim is to preserve spatial detail while isolating semantics from raw images. This targets a long-standing trade-off in self-supervised learning.

entry.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning

author.name: Yuhan Liu, Lianhui Qin, Shenji Wan

entry.summary: SceneBloom is an agentic framework for generating simulation-ready indoor environments that combines diffusion-based visual layout sampling within functional zones with contract-guided 3D compilation for geometric fitting and pose correction. Across five room types it produces realistic, diverse layouts suitable for training generalizable embodied agents. It addresses the shortage of varied, physically valid training environments for embodied AI.

entry.title: Sharp Bounds on the Winner's Bias under Independent and Nonnegatively Correlated Noise

author.name: Ivan Viakhirev, Kirill Borodin, Grach Mkrtchian

entry.summary: The paper sharply characterizes the winner's bias—the overstatement from reporting the best of M noisy scores—for two intermediate noise regimes: independent non-identical noise and pairwise nonnegative correlation, resolving a special case of an open question about expected range. It provides matching finite constructions and derives a corollary bounding cross-validation estimator bias.

entry.title: A curated multi-endpoint drug-protein bioactivity dataset with construct-aware protein targets

author.name: Lina Abou-Abbas, Nour Mhanna, Hasan Bazzi, Sleiman El Hajj, Abdulkader Helwan, Rabah Omrani, Khadidja Henni

entry.summary: Curate-DTI is a large curated drug-protein bioactivity dataset derived from a 2026 BindingDB export, distinguishing protein constructs by experimental sequence rather than UniProt accession alone, and processing IC50, Ki, Kd, and EC50 endpoints independently. It contains nearly 3 million measurements across ~2.3 million endpoint-specific interactions.

entry.title: Autoregressive Physics-Informed Neural Operator Surrogates and Joint 4-D Seismic-Production Bayesian History Matching

author.name: Clement Etienam, David Blom, Hari Pattathil, Tsubasa Onishi, Harpreet Sethi, Lalson Vincent, Suraj Pawar, Kishan Ramesh Kumar, Pandu Devarakota, Faruk O. Alpak

entry.summary: The work presents a surrogate-accelerated Bayesian history-matching framework for subsurface flow, replacing the forward map with an autoregressive Fourier neural operator trained in closed loop with black-oil residual physics penalties. It assimilates production data and 4-D seismic via adaptive regularized ensemble Kalman inversion on a realistic 100k-cell synthetic model.

entry.title: A Model-Agnostic Correction Framework for Short-Term Building Load Forecasting

author.name: Shiqiao Zhou, Huanbo Lyu, Holger Sch\"oner, Zipeng Wu, Jessica Deuschel, Freya Wentzel, IAG Wilson, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: WeL-RAC is a model-agnostic, retrieval-augmented correction framework for short-term building load forecasting that retrieves relevant historical cases at inference time to adapt predictions under changing weather and operating conditions. It targets reliability failures when current regimes are rare or underrepresented in training data. This matters for energy management where accurate forecasts under distribution shift directly affect operational decisions.

entry.title: A Broader Look into MLLM's Retrieval Heads

author.name: Jia Wang, Yuqing Li, Jiangnan Li, Zheng Lin, Mo Yu

entry.summary: The study investigates whether retrieval heads, sparse attention heads transferring context information to outputs, extend to newly added modalities by constructing paired audio-visual inputs where the same evidence is spoken or shown on screen. It finds retrieval-head sparsity persists across modalities and explores how the mechanism can be exploited to improve model performance on long multimodal inputs.

entry.title: Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond

author.name: Zheng Jiang, Yiming Chen, Houde Qian, Ling Li, Chaoyang Li, Lifeng Sun

entry.summary: Frontier-OPD is an on-policy distillation framework for multi-turn agents that identifies a student's learning frontier: decision situations that remain challenging but permit useful autonomous continuation after brief teacher guidance. It organizes experience into a shared-state trajectory graph and uses trajectory-balanced aggregation of teacher-student disagreement to select intervention candidates while preserving histories for replay.

entry.title: AudioLift: Audio-Driven Single Image to Full-Head Gaussian Avatar via Multi-view Video Generation

author.name: Zhuoyuan Jiang, Weijie Lyu, Xiaoyuan Wang, Tiancheng Shen, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: AudioLift is a two-stage framework for generating audio-driven 3D talking avatars from a single portrait, using generated multi-view videos as an intermediate representation instead of parametric face models like 3MM or FLAME. It combines synchronized multi-view video generation with inconsistency-robust Gaussian reconstruction to recover coherent full-head geometry, capturing extreme expressions and accessories that parametric models struggle with. This removes the need for per-instance optimization.

entry.title: Interpreting Physics in Video Encoders using Multi-Object Interaction Videos

author.name: Ayushi Mehrotra, Sai Vidyaranya Nuthalapati

entry.summary: This probing study examines whether frozen self-supervised video encoders (V-JEPA2 and VideoMAE) represent relational physics quantities such as momentum transfer, restitution, and friction in two-body interactions, which prior interpretability work on single-object quantities has not covered. Findings are mixed: both encoders reliably separate elastic from inelastic collisions, but V-JEPA2's predictor is less consistent in other respects. The work is relevant to whether video encoders can serve as world models for physical AI.

entry.title: AlphaAnything: Extending Pretrained RGB Generators to RGBA

author.name: Qijie Wang, Zhixin Xu, Zhe Li, Haowei Zhu, Honghao Qiao, Bo Peng, Dawei Li, Bin Wang

entry.summary: Presents AlphaAnything, a lightweight LoRA-based framework that extends pretrained RGB generators to RGBA generation directly in their original latent space, attaching an alpha branch to the frozen RGB VAE decoder. Unidirectional RGB-to-alpha feature sharing guarantees RGB decoding remains identical to the pretrained decoder for any fixed latent, avoiding RGBA reconstruction pretraining.

entry.title: STROKE: Simple Sparse Structural Occlusions for Black-Box Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Ankit Gupta, Akshat Pandya, Paul Lin, Christoph Adami, Emily Dolson

entry.summary: Presents STROKE, a query-efficient score-based black-box adversarial attack built from simple oriented rectangular occlusions optimized via a greedy add-and-refine procedure. It achieves high attack success with very few queries at small perturbation areas while substantially reducing wall-clock attack time compared to existing patch attacks.

entry.title: VisFlow: Interpretable Flow Matching for Visibility Reconstruction, Characterization, and Recognition

author.name: Rahul Moorthy, Volkan Isler

entry.summary: Addresses the challenge of learning representations for geometric objects combining continuous shape with discrete combinatorial structure, using polygons and visibility graphs as the canonical case. VisFlow applies flow matching to reconstruct visibility graphs, characterizing and recognizing them despite the fact that tiny geometric perturbations cause discrete jumps that break smoothness assumptions.

entry.title: RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training

author.name: Binghang Lu, Yige Sun, Guang Lin

entry.summary: RSI-Opt is a plug-and-play system in which LLM meta-agents monitor neural-network training dynamics and evolve the knowledge guiding optimizer settings, including a prompt, playbook of procedures, library of tested optimizer code, and decision cadence, using evidence from earlier runs. Across five generations on three training tasks the meta-agents develop reusable procedures and conduct their own self-improvement.

entry.title: PEAR: Adaptive Advantage Reshaping for Perception and Exploration in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Junxin Wang, Yingfeng Luo, Xiangchen Song, Weiqiao Shan, Runsong Zhao, Xinyu Liu, Shunjie Xing, Yifu Huo, Dingyang Lin, Qiuyu Gu, Yongyu Mu, Chenglong Wang, Changliang Li, Jingbo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: PEAR is an adaptive advantage reshaping method for multimodal RL that retains visual dependency as a base signal and adds an entropy-based exploration gain only at high-entropy positions, especially those with lower visual dependency. This corrects an underweighting of high-entropy, low-visual-dependency tokens that matter for exploratory reasoning.

entry.title: WiMoT: Replay-Free Continual Wi-Fi Sensing via Moment Transport

author.name: Chunchun Yang, Yang Cao, Zhitang Chen

entry.summary: WiMoT enables continual Wi-Fi sensing without storing raw channel state information, addressing privacy and storage constraints in deployed sensing nodes. It stores per-class feature means and covariances and, when representations change, transports the stored statistics via an affine map on a frozen feature basis so they remain valid without old samples. Supervised contrastive learning plus a closed-form loss preserves class separability across domains.

entry.title: What the Query Remembers: Query Abstraction Governs Lexical and Dense Retrieval of Classical Arabic Poetry

author.name: Omar Farouk Zouak, Selma Mani, Larbi Said Chikh, Raid Abderrezak Ouahioune

entry.summary: Benchmarking nine dense encoders and BM25 on Classical Arabic poetry retrieval, this paper shows which retriever wins depends on how much wording the query retains: BM25 beats all dense models including an 8B state-of-the-art encoder on tip-of-the-tongue queries, but falls to eighth of ten on abstract queries. A single remembered half-verse raises BM25 by 38 recall points. This is a careful, culturally significant retrieval study with broad implications for query-composition effects.

entry.title: Uni-Stream: A Unified Streaming Speech Language Model for Speech Synthesis and Recognition

author.name: Xuan Shi, Chang Zeng, Tiantian Feng, Ye Zhang, Jun Liu, Shih-Heng Wang, Lie Lu, Shrikanth Narayanan

entry.summary: Uni-Stream is a unified streaming speech language model that handles both speech recognition and synthesis in a single compact model by processing interleaved text and speech in a streaming format, achieving performance comparable to task-specific models via two-stage training. The authors also develop a data annotation pipeline for streaming training and plan to release transcriptions with word-level timestamps. It targets real-time human-computer speech interaction.

entry.title: DIGOM: Disentangled Interaction Graphs for Outcome prediction in Multimodal healthcare

author.name: Hakima Laribi, Olivier Lefebvre, Dan Poenaru, Martin Valli\`eres

entry.summary: Introduces a graph-based framework that jointly models three interaction types in multimodal healthcare data: intra-patient cross-modal, cross-patient same-modal, and cross-patient cross-modal relations. DIGOM learns a sparse multiplex graph to improve clinical outcome prediction beyond standard fusion approaches. Conceptually richer than typical unimodal or fusion-only baselines.

entry.title: EditJev: System One Routing for Image Editing Models

author.name: Zhile Guan, Xu Jiang, Yule Duan, Gongbo Zhang, Shuyu Wang, Xiao Chen, Jian Zhang

entry.summary: Studies dynamic routing among instruction-based image editing models, introducing EditJev, a lightweight System One router that predicts sample-level preference scores over candidate editors in a single forward pass. This exploits the fact that different editing models excel on different requests and differ in latency. Contributes to efficient, quality-aware model orchestration for generative editing.

entry.title: AI Alignment for Digital Democracy: Fairer Voters Representation against LLM Biases

author.name: Yi Qi, Srijoni Majumdar, Evangelos Pournaras

entry.summary: This work investigates demographic biases in LLM-emulated electorates for digital democracy, measuring how accurately LLMs reproduce individual votes across three U.S. presidential elections and whether some demographic groups are represented less fairly. The authors test whether alignment techniques can reduce inter-group disparities without sacrificing overall accuracy. It matters as AI-assisted voter representation raises real fairness-of-representation concerns.

entry.title: CuraLoc: Repository-Level Fault Localization via Planned Code Inspection

author.name: Sangeeta Warrier, Anush Sankaran, Ryen White

entry.summary: CuraLoc improves repository-level fault localization by planning code inspection upfront rather than letting the LLM iteratively decide what to inspect, selecting candidate files, representing symbols compactly, and making a single joint planning decision over starting symbols, relationships to inspect, and edit hypotheses before deterministic retrieval. This reduces repeated model calls and token usage. It is relevant to scaling agentic software engineering economically.

entry.title: Aligning Large Language Models with Human Feedback: Mathematical Foundations and Algorithm Design

author.name: Siliang Zeng, Luca Viano, Chenliang Li, Jiaxiang Li, Volkan Cevher, Markus Wulfmeier, Stefano Ermon, Alfredo Garcia, Mingyi Hong

entry.summary: A tutorial-style survey covering the mathematical foundations of LLM alignment, including SFT, RLHF, and DPO, and connecting preference learning to inverse reinforcement learning and discrete choice models. Authored by a strong team including Stefano Ermon and Markus Wulfmeier, it aims to serve as a comprehensive resource for researchers entering the alignment field.

entry.title: Curvature-Aware Clipping: Mitigating Bias in DPSGD via Approximate Second-Order Information

author.name: Xincheng Xu, Thilina Ranbaduge, Thierry Rakotoarivelo, David Smith

entry.summary: CA-DPSGD mitigates the gradient-clipping bias in differentially private training by using approximate second-order curvature information to construct an optimal clipping space, with a rectified curvature estimator and anisotropic noise for privacy. This addresses geometric misalignment that existing clipping approaches leave unresolved.

entry.title: Recommender regret for improving regularised RL estimation with bandits and MCTS

author.name: Danilo Vucetic, Alexandre Larouche, Mohammad Pedramfar, Audrey Durand, Gauthier Gidel

entry.summary: The paper formalizes estimate generation in regularized RL (via bandit sampling, MCTS, or look-ahead) as a recommendation process and introduces regulariser-aware recommender regrets to measure estimate quality rather than just sampling efficiency. It analyzes lower bounds, shows simple algorithms like uniform sampling achieve them, and unifies bandit- and search-based target improvement under a common framework.

entry.title: Neural Disjunctive Normal Forms for Learning Exact Rank Filters

author.name: Diego Marcondes, Wonder A. L. Alves, Ronaldo F. Hashimoto

entry.summary: The paper develops a method for gradient-based learning of morphological rank filters by constructing a neural disjunctive normal form via threshold decomposition, retaining exact operator evaluation while distributing derivatives across the window. A smooth surrogate with closed-form derivatives from implicit differentiation enables straight-through-style training. This addresses the locally sparse derivative problem that has hindered learning of morphological operators.

entry.title: PathJev: Decision-Native Vision-Language Modelling for Histopathology

author.name: Cristian Tommasino, Antonio M. Rinaldi

entry.summary: PathJev-P builds a decision-native histopathology model on MedGemma-1.5-4B with LoRA adapters and a decision head that returns calibrated distributions over run-time candidate sets, trained on 40,000 patch states from three public collections. Evaluation follows a pre-registered analysis plan across seeds on test sets without documented training overlap.

entry.title: Singular Geometry of Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Kamillo Ferry, Anthea Monod, Keisuke Yano

entry.summary: The paper studies LoRA through the lens of singular learning theory, using the real log canonical threshold to characterize learning complexity that parameter dimension alone cannot capture due to the low-rank factorization's non-identifiability. Under a local linearization, a forward-backward covariance built from activations and backpropagated sensitivities determines which directions of the pretrained network are learnable.

entry.title: Measure Before You Train: Typed Decision Models vs. a Classical Baseline vs. a Generative LLM for Routing a Personal Multilingual Inbox

author.name: Federico Lucca

entry.summary: The paper presents Foyer, a self-hosted personal email agent in daily use, and a rigorous measurement protocol featuring stratified sampling, frozen snapshots, thread-grouped splits, pre-registered hypotheses, and human labels. Using 739 real Italian/English emails, it compares nine systems including keyword rules, TF-IDF baselines, typed decision models, and an LLM. The central message is that agent error rates are rarely measured honestly because stored labels come from the system itself.

entry.title: DraMaze: A Multi-Agent Pipeline with Future-Aware Memory for Diverse Microdrama Script Generation

author.name: Siyang He, Qiqi Wang, Fan Liu, Yuncheng Huang, Pengfei Xu, Xi Chen, Ziwei He, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: DraMaze is a multi-agent pipeline for long-form microdrama script generation that explores diverse causal paths via trope memory-guided evolutionary tree search and mutation, and constructs a Backward Narrative Dependency Tree to organize and retrieve historical memories relevant to future plots. It addresses plot convergence and trope reuse observed as LLM generation progresses. The work targets the growing microdrama production market.

entry.title: Disentangling Question, Response, and Verifier Languages in Multilingual P(True) Self-Evaluation

author.name: Jewon Yeom, Jaewon Sok, Seonghyeon Park, Jeongjae Park, Hwiyeong Lee, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: The paper presents a six-language factorial study of multilingual self-evaluation, independently varying the language of the question, the requested response, and the verifier instruction across ten open-weight models (3B-14B). It finds the three languages affect accuracy and discrimination differently, and that matching response language to question or verifier language sharpens discrimination without improving calibration.

entry.title: Residual Expert Routing for Text-Only Domain Adaptation of Factorized Transducer ASR

author.name: Shashi Kumar, Esa\'u Villatoro-Tello, Thibault Ba\~neras-Roux, Sergio Burdisso, Petr Motlicek, Kadri Hacioglu, Andreas Stolcke

entry.summary: The paper proposes conservative residual routing for domain-adapting factorized transducer ASR: the adapted predictor becomes a residual correction to the base, with a 16k-parameter gate deciding per prefix how much to admit. This retains nearly all text-only adaptation gains on held-out domains while preserving source-domain performance, solving a problem that static interpolation weights cannot.

entry.title: SPOOK: Sparse Pixel Optimization for Off-Manifold Knowledge in Vision Encoders

author.name: Ankit Gupta, Akshat Pandya, Christoph Adami, Emily Dolson

entry.summary: SPOOK probes vision encoders far from the natural-image manifold using black-box sparse pixel edits on blank canvases optimized by hill-climbing. On OpenCLIP, optimized canvases achieve strong targeted retrieval of chosen classes, and on DINOv3 they achieve high alignment with class prototypes, revealing that off-manifold inputs can reliably manipulate embedding-based retrieval. This exposes a security-relevant weakness in widely used vision encoders.

entry.title: LOCI: Localized Continuous Control for Multi-Subject Image Editing

author.name: Sai Vidyaranya Nuthalapati, Shlok Kumar Mishra

entry.summary: LOCI enables instruction-following image editors such as Flux.1-Kontext to support explicit spatial localization, continuous per-region edit strength, and independent simultaneous control of multiple subjects, none of which prior methods jointly offer. For example, it can gradually age one person while adding a beard to another at independently chosen strengths. This addresses a real controllability gap in current text-driven image editing.

entry.title: Towards Effective and Transferable Physical Camouflage against Multi-View BEV-based 3D Perception in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Linye Lyu, Jiawei Zhou, Daojing He, Yu Li

entry.summary: Presents BEVCA, an adversarial physical camouflage framework targeting multi-view BEV-based 3D perception in autonomous driving, combining BEV-feature adversarial losses with multi-view neural rendering for transferable attacks across models and tasks. It exposes previously unexplored robustness gaps in BEV perception systems.

entry.title: Fast and Useful: Adapting Distilled Generators for Visual Learning

author.name: Patryk Bartkowiak, Dominik Michels, S\"oren Pirk, Wojciech Pa{\l}ubicki

entry.summary: This paper identifies that classifiers trained on images from distilled fast text-to-image generators underperform those trained on base-model outputs, and adapts released distilled generators by fitting a low-rank update toward an intermediate base-model state before letting the student finish generation. Ablations show why the supervision state matters, and adapted images improve classifier training across three generator families while staying fast.

entry.title: HGWM: Hierarchical Graph-Guided World Model for Zero-Shot Object Navigation via Graph Matching

author.name: I-tak Ieong, Hao Tang

entry.summary: HGWM couples an LLM-generated room-anchor prior with persistent spatial-semantic memory in a hierarchical world model for zero-shot object navigation, using coarse visual-semantic heading scoring and fine symbolic graph matching, with phase-dependent fusion. It reports 62.6 percent SR and 31.5 SPL on HM3D and 46.8 percent SR on MP3D, improving over WMNav. This advances evidence-retaining zero-shot embodied navigation.

entry.title: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control

author.name: Chaoyu Zhang, Guangshen Ma, Mark Draelos

entry.summary: This paper introduces an OCT-guided data-driven framework for closed-loop soft-tissue shape control in medical robotics, learned from user-guided demonstrations. Optical coherence tomography provides high-resolution volumetric perception of tissue deformation, and the work builds 3D representations of observed and desired tissue states to support target-conditioned control at microscales where physics-based models are expensive. The approach aims to enable data-driven tissue manipulation where localized deformation is hard to observe and model.

entry.title: From Visual Affinity to Learning Credit in Multimodal Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuhang Han, Dingning Liu, Yujie Chen, Yaojie Zhang, Jingwei Song, Zequn Yang, Xuanming Shang, Li Ding, Zhijiang Guo, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Outcome-Conditioned Visual Credit (OVC), a plug-in framework for RLVR that separates visual-association measurement from token-level credit assignment, addressing cases where upweighting valid visual observations amplifies negative-advantage updates when later reasoning fails. It adapts to policy-optimization methods with uniform response-level advantages.

entry.title: SemGeo-Gen: Unsupervised Generation of Approximate Cross-Instance Semantic-Geometric Correspondences

author.name: Roy Amoyal, Shira Ifergane, Oren Freifeld

entry.summary: Introduces an unsupervised method that generates approximate semantic-geometric correspondences across 3D object instances from weakly aligned collections, lifting multi-view DINOv2 features to 3D and aligning instances via piecewise-affine registration with semantic pruning. Avoids costly manual correspondence supervision while producing training data diverse enough for modern correspondence models. Useful for 3D understanding without dense labels.

entry.title: Reading Between the Layers: Cross-Modal Alignment and Representational Hierarchy in Vision Transformers

author.name: Sugam Karki, Ra\'ul V\'azquez, Yova Kementchedjhieva

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies how vision transformers inside large vision-language models process rendered text, using cross-modal alignment, probing, and retrieval analyses to map orthographic, grammatical, and semantic organization across layers. It finds strong cross-modal text-to-concept mapping emerges only in the deepest layers, after unimodal recognition has developed, indicating a progression from surface to semantic processing of text.

entry.title: STEP: Surgical Point Tracking from Sparse Endpoints and Pseudo-trajectories

author.name: Bing Fan, Anwesa Choudhuri, Zhongpai Gao, Meng Zheng, Benjamin Planche, Terrence Chen, Heng Fan, Ziyan Wu

entry.summary: STEP is a two-stage framework for surgical point tracking that learns from sparse physical endpoints instead of costly dense trajectory annotations. A frozen offline teacher generates candidate trajectories filtered by temporal reversibility and stereo consistency to supervise a causal student, with physical endpoint and round-trip losses anchoring correspondence. The tracker runs on a single RGB stream with fixed weights and shows strong results on surgical benchmarks.

entry.title: Sounding Surgical Instrument Localisation through Audio-Visual Correspondence

author.name: Dominic Behling, Jonas Hein, Matthias Seibold

entry.summary: Investigates localizing the active surgical instrument from a single microphone and a camera by learning weakly supervised audio-visual correspondence, without position annotations. It adapts co-occurrence-based audio-visual localization to the operating room, exploiting sound as a complement to predominantly visual surgical scene understanding.

entry.title: Behaviour analysis for large language model-driven agents

author.name: Tianqiang Yan, Lizhen Qu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a general framework connecting data-driven behavioral discovery with analysis and experimentation for language agents: behavior categories derived from recorded activity define measurements, relationships are expressed as interpretable hypotheses, and held-out tests plus prompt-steering experiments probe how behaviors relate to outcomes. A study of iterative self-reflection illustrates the framework in action.

entry.title: MedCaseAgent: From Multimodal Clinical Evidence to Rare Disease Case Reports

author.name: Hongkang Chu, Yifan Shen, Tianjiao Yu, Zhuoqing Zhong, Jianguo Cao, Meihuan Huang, Xu Cao

entry.summary: MedCaseAgent is an end-to-end agentic system that generates publication-quality rare disease case reports from unstructured clinical notes, combining patient-level data mining with iterative, tool-integrated reasoning that queries medical literature and knowledge bases. Its modular, pluggable design supports various backbone LLMs and assesses case novelty for clinical fidelity.

entry.title: Adaptive Control of Scientific Instruments with Nonstationary Responses through Multimodal Agents

author.name: Guoyang Shi, Hongwen Li, Yiding Yu, Zhuang Fu, Siqi Ding, Zhengyuan Chen, JianGuo Chen, Hanyue Zhao, Tianyuan Liu

entry.summary: The authors propose a physically grounded multimodal agent with three independently auditable components for controlling scientific instruments whose responses are nonstationary, motivated by shot-to-shot tuning of neutral beam injection ion sources in fusion devices. The system progressively adjusts parameters in response to feedback when static action-response mappings fail.

entry.title: CauProphet: Teaching Agents to Develop Causal Cognition like Humans

author.name: Kaiwen Wu, Chaochao Lu

entry.summary: CauProphet is an LLM agent architecture that builds and refines causal knowledge over time rather than merely retrieving past records. For each task it constructs a Causal Belief combining stored causal knowledge with current evidence, uses it for decisions, and continuously updates both belief and long-term Causal Cognition. It aims to give long-horizon agents human-like causal understanding of their environment.

entry.title: Agentic Hazard Mapper: Emulating Expert Map-Making with AI Agents for Risk Communication

author.name: Sidi Wu, Lifeng Lin, Yizi Chen, Anna Yokokubo, Lorenz Hurni

entry.summary: Agentic Hazard Mapper is a multi-agent system that automates production of hazard maps by emulating professional cartographic workflows and iterative design trade-offs, adapting to different data, locations, and hazards. Informed by a formative study with map experts and validated via user studies with practitioners, generated maps improved spatial understanding and evacuation planning. It democratizes access to cartographic expertise for local governments.

entry.title: Rethinking Structured Generation: Can Graph-Based Reasoning Resolve Ambiguity?

author.name: Ratun Rahman, Atit Pokharel

entry.summary: The paper argues that treating structured generation as a deterministic input-to-single-output mapping is misaligned with natural language, which often admits multiple valid structural interpretations. It reframes structured generation as ambiguity-aware inference over sets of plausible outputs and shows standard training suppresses valid alternatives. This could improve robustness of structured-output systems on underspecified inputs.

entry.title: What Open-Source Projects Tell Their Coding Agents: A Census of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md

author.name: Pawel Zarzycki

entry.summary: This census examines AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md instruction files across popular active GitHub repositories in thirteen languages, using model-assisted annotation with human review. It finds a practical mix of project knowledge and workflow rules, many directives lacking rationale, and inconsistent community norms on AI attribution in commits. It documents an emerging de facto practice for steering coding agents in the wild.

entry.title: MI-MIDI 2: From Observation to Control with Sparse Autoencoders in Text-to-MIDI Generation

author.name: Jakub Po\'cwiardowski, Mateusz Modrzejewski

entry.summary: This work builds an end-to-end protocol for discovering and steering sparse-autoencoder features in text-to-MIDI generators, testing whether SAE feature interpretations actually predict controllability in music models like text2midi and MIDI-LLM. It uses controls including note-density adjustment, matched inactive excerpts, and permutation calibration.

entry.title: SOPO: Socratic Guided Policy Optimization for Span-Level Hallucination Detection

author.name: Jiawei Dong, Zilong Bai, Pengtian zhu, Peng Zhou

entry.summary: SOPO is a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework for span-level hallucination detection that addresses localization ambiguity, reward sparsity on hard examples, and length inflation that challenge standard RLVR. Its key innovation is a Socratic feedback mechanism in which a teacher model guides reasoning trajectories during rollouts. This is relevant to improving the factuality of LLM outputs at a fine-grained level.

entry.title: Decoupling Patient Personas and Clinical Workflows: A Dual-Agent Approach to Realistic Medical Dialogue Generation

author.name: Qiyuan Li, Xiaomei Guo, Chao Gao, Haijiang Liu, Deyu Chen, Caicai Guo, Jinguang Gu

entry.summary: Proposes CoRPS-Dial, a dual-agent framework for synthesizing realistic pre-consultation medical dialogues by pairing a persona-driven patient agent with a workflow-guided doctor agent, plus post-hoc quality control. It addresses privacy and ethical barriers to collecting real medical dialogues at scale. Potentially valuable for training and evaluating healthcare conversational systems.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Help Robotic Engineers? Lessons from Two Focus Days in Industry

author.name: Salim Fares, Steffen Herbold

entry.summary: Reports a case study of AI coding agents used by an SME programming industrial robots in vendor-specific languages with simulation-based visual feedback. The agent did not improve productivity overall except for repetitive code generation, though results improved as engineers learned to use it and as it was domain-adapted. Valuable real-world evidence on the limits of current agents in niche engineering domains.

entry.title: Internal Discrepancy for Contrastive Learning: Generalization Bounds and Downstream Behaviors

author.name: Jialiang Wang, Qing Ma, Xiong Zhou, Gangfeng Hu, Haoliang Li, Xianming Liu

entry.summary: Proposes the internal discrepancy measure, quantifying the gap between mean positive-sample representations and latent cluster centers, and proves a generalization bound for downstream supervised tasks after contrastive learning without extra assumptions. The theory also connects to downstream behavior predictions. A theoretical contribution to understanding contrastive representation learning.

entry.title: Every Edge Needs a Quote: Building a Quote-Grounded Knowledge Graph of Healthcare Software Adoption with Language-Model Agents

author.name: Juan Felipe Duran, Arthur Tobler, Martin Valli\`eres

entry.summary: The paper presents a pipeline of language-model agents that builds a knowledge graph of healthcare software customer and integration relations from the open web, enforcing that every graph edge be supported by a verbatim quote from its cited source. This grounding addresses the correctness problem of agent-extracted claims in a domain where wrong information can mislead hospital purchasing decisions. It demonstrates a practical verification-centric pattern for LLM agent outputs.

entry.title: Topological Equivalence of Spectral and Density Cluster Hierarchies

author.name: Sajjad Hashemian

entry.summary: The paper proves conditions under which a spectral clustering hierarchy built from diffusion distances is topologically equivalent to the density cluster tree derived from superlevel sets, up to monotone rescaling. It further shows a k-NN graph implementation inherits this equivalence, giving a finite-sample bridge between spectral constructions and density-level-set topology.

entry.title: EVOLVE: Uncertainty-Aware Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Prediction with Adaptive Prototype Memories

author.name: Jianxin Jin, Kai Zhao, Shiyan Hu, Yang Shu, Peng Chen, Meng Wang, Zhongwen Rao, Yijie Li, Jing Wang, Bin Yang, Chenjuan Guo

entry.summary: EVOLVE targets unsupervised anomaly prediction in multivariate time series, replacing the standard perturbation paradigm—where shared random perturbations simulate abnormal futures—with variable- and context-dependent evolution learned via adaptive prototype memories. It provides early-warning signals with uncertainty awareness for proactive intervention.

entry.title: When Does Dynamics Randomization Test Context Inference?

author.name: Oleg Smirnov, Sofiane Ennadir, John Pertoft, Bjartur Hjaltason, Sara Karimi

entry.summary: The paper formalizes predictive headroom, the remaining one-step information a context encoder can add in environments with randomized dynamics, and shows such randomization often provides little information for testing explicit context inference in world models. It analyzes discrete and continuous settings to separate query-coverage effects from context-weight effects.

entry.title: Contextual Decision Making: Predictive or Generative

author.name: L. Jeff Hong, Weihuan Huang, Xinyao Li

entry.summary: The paper theoretically compares predict-then-optimize versus generate-then-optimize approaches for contextual decision making, deriving regret bounds showing when smoothness can offset the generative approach's dimensional burden, and identifying optimization tradeoffs within nonnegative-weight PtO methods.

entry.title: Sustainability of TSFM Deployment and Pretraining: From Carbon Footprint Analysis to Mitigation via Pruning

author.name: C\'ecile Luc, Nathana\"el Lemonnier, Ievgen Redko

entry.summary: The paper models cumulative carbon costs of time series foundation models versus periodically retrained supervised models across deployment lifecycles, finding Chronos-2 amortizes pretraining within months for large deployments but classical models remain cheaper for small ones. It also shows pruning a single encoder block via a gradient-free criterion reduces TSFM cost with limited accuracy loss.

entry.title: Input Bias Correction in Gaussian Process Regression

author.name: Muzaffar Qureshi, Tochukwu E. Ogri, Trivikram Satharasi, Kyle Volle, Rushikesh Kamalapurkar

entry.summary: The authors propose a bias-aware Gaussian process (Ba-GP) framework that corrects a recorded GP trained on erroneous inputs, such as pose estimates from dead-reckoning mobile sensors, once better input estimates become available. The method propagates input bias and noise into mean and covariance corrections using posterior-mean gradients in a numerically efficient way. This addresses a practical gap since standard GP regression assumes known inputs.

entry.title: A Dynamic Inventory Rationing Model for Last-Mile Delivery of Medication in Liberia's Community Health Program

author.name: Baris Ata, Yufan Chen, Robert Montgomery

entry.summary: The authors model how a central warehouse in Liberia's community health program should ration scarce medication between a health facility and the Community Health Assistants it supervises, balancing wider treatment access against the flexibility of holding central stock. They formulate the allocation problem as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem that incorporates referral travel costs, untreated-patient risk, and fairness across locations. The work applies operations research and stochastic control to a real-world global health logistics challenge.

entry.title: ReLEAP: Upcycling Vision Datasets through Cross-Task Unification and Semi-Supervised Annotation

author.name: Julia Simon, Daniel Steininger, Andreas Trondl

entry.summary: ReLEAP is a scalable Python framework that unifies heterogeneous image datasets through data-source abstraction, cross-task reuse of annotations, and mapping labels into a shared hierarchical taxonomy. It is demonstrated in precision agriculture by integrating fifteen diverse plant datasets. The work addresses a real bottleneck in vision research: annotation format and label-definition differences prevent dataset reuse.

entry.title: KnitTrans: Coordinated Trajectory Transfer for Effective and Efficient LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Bangjun Xiao, Chiheng Lou, Xiaodong Ji, Xiangwei Deng, Yikai Zhao, Gang Huang, Hailin Zhang

entry.summary: KnitTrans is a systems contribution that coordinates the rollout-to-training path in LLM reinforcement learning, addressing architectural staleness from disaggregated pipelining and redundant data movement of large trajectory payloads. Its three designs include constraint-preserving mini-batch admission, improving both learning quality and system efficiency.

entry.title: Knowledge Graphs Quality Assessment in the Era of LLMs: A Conceptual Framework

author.name: Elwin Huaman

entry.summary: This conceptual paper reviews quality assessment literature spanning data, information, linked data, and knowledge graphs, extending existing frameworks to a catalog of 24 quality dimensions with associated metrics. It addresses when a knowledge graph can be trusted to ground an LLM and how it should be evaluated. The output is a general-purpose, domain-customizable quality assessment framework.

entry.title: Mining Frames: Association Rule Mining as an Unsupervised Framework for News Framing Detection

author.name: Hager Hesham Mustafa (Anmat Computational Analysis Lab)

entry.summary: The paper proposes association rule mining as an unsupervised, annotation-free framework for news framing detection, treating documents as transactions of lexical items and reading high-lift co-occurrence rules as candidate framing signals confirmed by journalist-researchers. Validation focuses on Framing Gaza, 25,512 articles from 16 US, UK, French, and German outlets covering the first year of the Gaza war. It aims to remove dependence on annotated corpora and predefined taxonomies.

entry.title: POS-Signature Demonstration Retrieval for In-Context Dependency Parsing

author.name: Muhammad Azam Afridi, Rajab Ali, Marco Passarotti

entry.summary: The paper studies demonstration selection for in-context Universal Dependencies parsing, proposing a POS-signature policy that represents sentences with weighted part-of-speech statistics to retrieve length-compatible gold-parsed examples. Evaluated without fine-tuning on two open-weight models over the full UD English Web Treebank test set against fixed, semantic, zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and critique-refinement baselines. POS-signature retrieval yields the highest labeled attachment scores.

entry.title: Shorter Is Not Cheaper: A Controlled Comparison of Declarative Animation Specifications and Free-Form Code for LLM-Generated Explanations

author.name: Jiantang Huang

entry.summary: This controlled study tests the common assumption that generating declarative animation specifications is cheaper and more reliable than free-form HTML/JavaScript for LLM-produced interactive explanations. Using a frozen pre-registered analysis plan, a time-indexed declarative format called ExplainSpec, and programmatic observation contracts across 360 jobs on three Claude models, the authors find the expected benefits do not straightforwardly hold.

entry.title: Beyond Final Outcomes: Quantifying Claim-Level Information Dynamics in Multi-Agent LLM Interaction

author.name: Haocheng Jiang, Herun Wan, Yongyuan Peng, Minnan Luo

entry.summary: The authors propose RIVER, a framework that decomposes multi-agent LLM outputs into atomic claims and evaluates convergence, exploration, and retention dimensions of information flow. Applied to five interaction strategies on 40 controlled news-generation cases, it reveals dynamics such as pooled interaction promoting certain convergence and retention patterns that final-outcome metrics miss.

entry.title: CounselPlex: A Stressor-Aware Full-Duplex Counseling Model

author.name: Yeonju Kim, Bella Godiva, Yong Man Ro

entry.summary: CounselPlex is a stressor-aware full-duplex speech model for counseling that combats Stressor Blindness by updating a compact stressor state during seeker silence and injecting it at listening positions, plus RoPE Position Shift Augmentation to improve performance at longer turn depths. LLM-judge evaluations show improved counseling quality and stressor grounding over strong baselines.

entry.title: Communicating with the Entire Population: Machine Translation of Emergency Alerts and Warnings

author.name: Jen Wilson, Vipasha Bansal, William D. Lewis

entry.summary: This work surveys emergency managers nationwide about their workflows and challenges when using commercial machine translation for crisis alerts, then evaluates commercial translation tools against those real operational needs. It offers practical guidance on when automated translation is safe to use in emergencies. The study matters because mistranslated alerts can endanger non-dominant-language speakers during crises.

entry.title: StackGen3D: Stable 3D Block Stack Generation from Multiview Silhouettes

author.name: Xiaopeng Zhang, Luzhe Sun, Yiqing Xu, Matthew R. Walter

entry.summary: StackGen3D generates physically stable 3D block assemblies from a block inventory and three orthographic silhouettes. It uses a physics-informed graph neural network as a fast stability predictor to curate training data, then trains a conditional flow-matching model to capture the multimodal distribution of stable configurations. A lightweight way to couple physical plausibility with generative modeling for structured 3D outputs.

entry.title: Benchmarking Data-Free Continual Model Merging for Whole-Slide Image Survival Analysis

author.name: Vu Minh Tran, Doanh C. Bui, Ma\"i K. Nguyen, Khang Nguyen

entry.summary: Establishes an end-to-end benchmark for data-free continual model merging in whole-slide image survival prediction, covering task-specific fine-tuning, sequential merging, and inference under TASK-IL and CLASS-IL settings. It systematically compares six merging strategies across four TCGA cancer cohorts, filling a gap in understanding how model merging behaves in continual medical analysis.

entry.title: Search-Based Testing of Modality Sensitivity in Vision Language Models

author.name: Oliver Wei{\ss}l, Eduardo Breitembach, Andrea Stocco

entry.summary: Introduces MoST, a black-box testing framework that characterizes VLM modality sensitivity by comparing image-only, text-only, and joint perturbations, using multi-objective search to combine perturbations and tune severity to expose prediction failures. Evaluations across four VLMs on object localization tasks reveal which modality is more susceptible to degradation.

entry.title: Learning Fine-Grained Visual Classification with Text as Privileged Information via Multimodal Distillation

author.name: Aishwarya Venkataramanan, Christian Ickler, Joachim Denzler

entry.summary: FG-LUPI uses textual attribute descriptions as privileged information available only during training for fine-grained visual classification, via a multimodal teacher with gated cross-attention distilled into an image-only student. This sidesteps the deployment limitation that attribute descriptions are rarely available at test time.

entry.title: Consomm\'e: Conditioned Token Merging for Split Inference

author.name: Man Ngo, Jan S. Rellermeyer

entry.summary: This arXiv paper addresses split inference for Vision Transformers, where computation is divided between a resource-constrained edge device and a server, and communication of intermediate tokens is a bottleneck. The proposed method, Consomme, exploits the dual role of the CLS token as both a classification summary and a patch-selection signal: an information bottleneck compresses the CLS token into a compact latent for transmission, which also conditions token merging on the server side. The approach works with a frozen backbone, requiring only a small adapter to be shipped to endpoints, cutting both communication and deployment costs.

entry.title: A Resource-Efficient and Precision-Scalable FPGA Accelerator for Spiking Neural Networks Using Minifloat Arithmetic

author.name: Ali Mehrabi, Philip C. Jose

entry.summary: Presents a precision-scalable FPGA accelerator for spiking neural networks built on parameterized minifloat arithmetic, implementing recurrent LIF and leaky-integrator readout neurons with a configurable unified datapath. The design targets event-driven edge deployment with reduced arithmetic complexity, memory footprint, and power consumption.

entry.title: Incremental-Smoothing-Based ARAIM Protection Levels for Tightly Coupled GNSS/IMU Integration in Urban Canyons

author.name: Jiahao Hu (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University), Xiangru Wang (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University), Weisong Wen (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University), Meng Qian (Southeast University)

entry.summary: This paper formulates ARAIM solution separation and protection-level computation on the posterior of tightly coupled GNSS/IMU factor graph optimization, extending integrity monitoring beyond snapshot GNSS estimation. It shows the fault-excluded covariance and separation follow from the linearized current-state marginal, retaining correlations with velocity, IMU-bias, and clock states. The work targets safety assurance of urban navigation in signal-degraded canyons.

entry.title: HoloBoxing: A Simple Recipe for Humanoid Boxing with 7 Minutes of Single-GPU Training

author.name: Xihan Ma, Bo Zhang, Boxiong Li, Yuhan Bao, Ziyue Liu, Yucheng Wang

entry.summary: HoloBoxing proposes an efficient recipe for humanoid boxing built on a pretrained frozen whole-body controller, separating reusable motor skills from task-level decisions. A compact planner requests future body-point targets via a learned decoder mapping 32-dimensional actions to structured target windows, initialized by measured-state imitation before reinforcement learning. This design reportedly achieves boxing behavior with only about seven minutes of single-GPU task training by avoiding relearning whole-body control.

entry.title: The AI buildout is the largest bet in the history of capitalism.

author.name: Hayekstan

entry.summary: This LessWrong post argues that the scale of AI infrastructure spending over the past four years, with hyperscaler capex around 785-820 billion dollars this year (about 2.4 percent of US GDP) and projected at roughly 1.3 trillion next year, constitutes the largest capital bet in history. The author contends this spending signals that key capital allocators expect very powerful AI within a few years, an underappreciated piece of evidence in AI-impact debates. It aggregates spending comparisons against national budgets to make the scale vivid.

entry.title: Beyond Gain: Measuring Skill Internalization for Agent Skill Retirement

author.name: Yanze Wang, Pengfei Yao, Tianyi Sun, Hongda Chen, Yunyun Han, Jun Sun, Chuanrui Hu, Yafeng Deng

entry.summary: This paper tackles skill retirement in agent skill hubs: gain-based rules cannot distinguish a skill a model has internalized from one where neither model nor skill delivers the capability (uncovered). The proposed method withholds the skill, scores the model on a task synthesized from it, and trusts high unaided scores only when another model benefits from the skill, addressing measurement reliability at hub scale.

entry.title: CASE: Confusion-Aware Skill Evolution for Frozen Multimodal Emotion Models

author.name: Siyu Wu, Zeyu Liang, Linghao Wang, Qiyun Zheng, Yi Yao, Ling Lo, Hongxia Xie

entry.summary: CASE targets systematic confusion between semantically adjacent emotions in multimodal emotion recognition, observing that such errors are localized rather than global. Instead of costly full parameter updates, it maintains a sparse, self-evolving library of reusable pair-specific skills applied to frozen multimodal models. This is presented as the first agent-skill framework for emotion recognition.

entry.title: Distributional Alignment of LLMs and Its Generalization Properties

author.name: Nelson Jo

entry.summary: This work studies how to align LLM output distributions with human reference distributions, e.g., for survey simulation, and how aligned models generalize to unseen samples and unrelated topics. Across two large-scale benchmarks, LLMs achieve distributional alignment and generalize to unseen same-domain questions, with cross-topic generalization depending on topic relationships. This is relevant to using LLMs as human-behavior simulators.

entry.title: ACVA-Bench: Beyond Prompt Following in Abstract Concept Visualization Ability for Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Mengyan Wang, Jiyuan An, Yining Liu, YaoWen Zhang, Liner Yang ang Erhong Yang

entry.summary: ACVA-Bench evaluates whether text-to-image models can autonomously translate abstract concepts lacking fixed visual referents, such as loyalty, into visual representations that are accurate, diverse, and distinguishable from related concepts. The benchmark is category-balanced and grounded in psycholinguistic norms of abstract concepts.

entry.title: Tokamak-SI: Interpreting Tokamak Discharges with Labeled Catalogs

author.name: Nathaniel Chen, Alvin Garcia, Ricardo Shousha, Jalal Butt, Azarakhsh Jalalvand, Egemen Kolemen

entry.summary: Tokamak-SI unifies labels and labeling methods from many prior task-specific studies into a single scalable, time-aligned categorical dataset covering confinement, detachment, Alfvén eigenmodes, edge localized modes, sawtooth, tearing modes, and resistive wall modes in the DIII-D tokamak. Models trained on it match or beat earlier specialized detectors and enable physics-searchable discharge interpretation. It supports fusion science and AI-for-science benchmarking.

entry.title: Efficient Zero-Shot Video Anomaly Detection via Signal-Aware Adaptive Fusion (SAAF)

author.name: Khaled Waleed Dawoud, Muhammad Haris Khan

entry.summary: Introduces a zero-shot video anomaly detection framework built on vision-language models that reduces computational cost via a dual-signal adaptive sampler: a delta signal for sudden events and a drift signal for gradual anomalies, combined with OR-gated adaptive thresholding. Targets the gap between VLM semantic reasoning power and the scale of real-world video streams. Practical for surveillance and streaming applications.

entry.title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations

author.name: Sadra Emami, Benjamin Weigell, Mohammad Reza Mousavi, Gunel Jahangirova, Hugo Araujo, Bernhard Bauer

entry.summary: This empirical study challenges the assumption that LLM-generated performance-optimized code is also energy-efficient, measuring hardware-level energy consumption across 11 open-source models and four decoding configurations on all 1,000 EffiBench problems. It also assesses whether the energy cost of the optimization process itself is offset by execution-time savings. The findings are relevant to sustainable AI-assisted software engineering.

entry.title: DBCM: Dual-Branch Calibration Module for Test-Time Adaptation in Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jaebyeong Jeon, Kunwoo Kang, Sang Yup Lee, Kibok Lee

entry.summary: Observing that forecast residuals in time series often share structure across channels, the authors propose a dual-branch calibration module for test-time adaptation that mixes channel-specific and shared parameterization around frozen forecasters. This reduces the redundancy of purely channel-wise adapters under non-stationary distribution shift.

entry.title: Norm-optimal model order reduction in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces

author.name: Tam\'as D\'ozsa, Andrea Angino, Rolf Krause, Matthias Voigt

entry.summary: The paper generalizes necessary interpolatory conditions for norm-optimal reduced-order models from Hardy-Hilbert spaces to reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, and constructs an IRKA-like algorithm for RKHSs with differentiable kernels. It introduces generalized Malmquist-Takenaka functions enabling orthonormal bases and unitary transformations between separable RKHSs.

entry.title: Let's Do Turbulence Right: In Space and Time!

author.name: Maximilian Plattner, Fabian Paischer, Johannes Brandstetter

entry.summary: Leveraging massive time-resolved direct numerical simulations exceeding 28 TB per run, the authors assess how numerical choices govern the resolved (3+1)-dimensional physics of turbulent Navier-Stokes flows. They then study how neural networks represent the recorded turbulent motion, finding that spatial and temporal assessments can diverge in evaluating learned emulators.

entry.title: Natural Language Autoencoders Identify Without Explaining

author.name: Kristina \v{S}ekrst, Barbara Geld

entry.summary: The paper critiques natural language autoencoders, where internal activations are verbalized as text and then reconstructed, arguing that successful round-trip reconstruction only establishes informational sufficiency for identification, not descriptive faithfulness of the explanation. It connects this to the underdetermination problem in scientific explanation, showing a sentence can identify an activation while wrongly describing what it does.

entry.title: SAGE: A hybrid vision-language and geometry framework for work-zone pathway prediction under temporary traffic control

author.name: Jiaxi Liu, Keshu Wu, Weizhe Tang, Bofeng Cao, Sikai Chen, Xiaopeng Li, Steven T. Parker, Bin Ran

entry.summary: SAGE is a read-decide-execute-check framework for predicting drivable paths through road work zones, using a vision-language model's trajectory preference to select among geometrically constructed candidate paths. A role-decoupled generator builds candidates and rank fusion combines geometric scores with VLM preferences under traffic control compliance checks. It targets a safety-critical gap in automated vehicle navigation through temporary traffic control.

entry.title: Past as State, Present as Attention: Persistent-State Blockwise Flow Matching for Long-Horizon Co-Speech Motion Generation

author.name: Yi Liu, Xiangyue Zhang, Jianfang Li, Jia Ma, Yisheng He, Jianqiang Ren

entry.summary: Proposes a Past-As-State, Present-as-Attention principle for long-horizon co-speech motion generation, compactly summarizing slowly varying style in a persistent state while modeling fast-changing local dynamics with attention in blockwise flow matching. This addresses drift and history-cost limitations of segment-by-segment generation.

entry.title: TIE: Training-free CLIP Embedding Guidance for Compositional Text-to-Image Alignment

author.name: Sujung Hong, Tae Eun Choi, Youngjun Jun, Chanyong Yoon, Seong Jae Hwang

entry.summary: Conducts an embedding-level analysis of concept loss and concept confusion in text-to-image diffusion models and proposes TIE, a training-free method that guides CLIP embeddings to improve compositional alignment on multi-object, multi-attribute prompts. It targets persistent failure modes attributed to the CLIP text encoder's limited fine-grained capacity.

entry.title: CityLift: Compositional 3D Urban Generation from a Single Image

author.name: Haoran Gong, Jie Feng, Chenxu Wang

entry.summary: CityLift generates editable 3D urban scenes from a single image by jointly learning building shape and placement through coupled scene and instance streams, then using generative spatial inheritance to produce detailed textured building meshes with consistent scales and positions. It tackles occlusion and perspective ambiguity in single-view urban reconstruction.

entry.title: OPTARI: An open-source software framework for clinical translation of optoacoustic imaging

author.name: Moritz Schillinger, Maximilian Bader, Adrian Buehler, Felix Wachter, Ferdinand Knieling, Vasilis Ntziachristos, Katharina Breininger

entry.summary: Presents OPTARI, an open-source graphical application for optoacoustic-ultrasound imaging analysis built on napari and PATATO, supporting vendor and HDF5 formats aligned with the IPASC standard. It enables ROI annotation and large-scale clinical studies by users without programming expertise, filling a gap between script-based engineering tools and proprietary vendor software.

entry.title: PAFS: Perturbation-Aware Firing Scaffolds for Robust Event-Based SNNs

author.name: Ning Liu, Jun Sun, Hao Guo, Sen Shen, Xiangfei Yang, Jie Yang, Lan Wu, Shangke Lyu, Thomas Br\"aunl

entry.summary: Introduces PAFS, a labeled post-training calibration method that exploits error-diagnostic structure in late-layer LIF firing trajectories — which final logits lack — to make event-based SNNs robust to event loss, timestamp jitter, and speed variation. It associates standardized firing trajectories with class-probability residuals of an adapter anchor and applies SVD for a compact correction without retraining the backbone.

entry.title: $R^2E:$ A Role-driven Reward Evolutionary Framework for Automated Reward Function Design

author.name: Shouhao Chang, Xuan Liu, Hongye Zhu, Xinning Chen, Shigeng Zhang

entry.summary: R2E structures LLM-based automated reward design through role specialization: an Explorer promotes novelty to expand the reward search space, a Guardian performs conservative refinement, and complementary roles exploit historical feedback. This addresses undifferentiated sampling and optimization instability in prior LLM reward-design methods. It aims to make evolutionary reward search more stable and exploratory.

entry.title: Learning Nonlinear Waveform Fusion Across Scales for Integrated Sensing and Communication

author.name: Jiayu Liu, Kai Wan, Shuo Shao, Giuseppe Caire

entry.summary: The paper proposes learning nonlinear waveform fusion across scales for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), jointly optimizing image transmission and multi-target localization in range and angle. Adaptive temporal feature weighting combines image features with a linearly frequency-modulated reference in a shared waveform, with neural demixing at the user equipment and target estimation at the base station.

entry.title: TGR-EvoDAG: A DAG-based Multi-Agent Code Evolution Framework for Generative Recommendation on Tencent

author.name: Junlin He, Junzhang Zhu, Yudong Li, Yihong Tang, Xuefeng Jiang, Wei Ma, Chengxiang Zhuo, Zang Li

entry.summary: TGR-EvoDAG is a production system from Tencent for LLM-driven automated code evolution in generative recommendation, using a DAG-based multi-agent framework to handle module-cascaded pipelines while addressing cost blindness regarding stage-asymmetric retraining overheads and short-sighted evaluation that discards promising upstream innovations.

entry.title: Rethinking Multi-View Fusion for Urban Representation Learning

author.name: Sean Bin Yang, Zongyi Xu, Jilin Hu, Ying Sun, Kristian Torp, Bin Yang, Torben Bach Pedersen, Christian S. Jensen

entry.summary: This paper identifies two structural flaws in urban region representation learning: modality utility varies across regions so static fusion overemphasizes some signals, and heterogeneous objectives suffer persistent gradient imbalance.
