The authors propose adaptive fusion and optimization corrections for downstream tasks like crime forecasting and demand estimation.

entry.title: Searching with Sparse Histories: Cross-Task Architecture Search from Incomplete Search Logs and Zero-Cost Proxies

author.name: Yuefeng Xu, Jun Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a risk-robust neural architecture search strategy that transfers knowledge across tasks from sparse search logs combined with zero-cost proxies, using champion-based initialization and joint pairwise-ranker pretraining. On TransNAS-Bench-101 it drastically reduces worst-case failures, cutting worst-10% ranks from 290 to 43 in one setting and outperforming a proxy-only ranker on 10 of 13 targets. This matters for making NAS cheaper and more reliable under incomplete prior information.

entry.title: Ontology-Guided Knowledge Graph Construction from Structured Metadata and Climate Science Publications

author.name: Aayush Acharya, Qi Zhang, Eduard Dragut, Longin Jan Latecki

entry.summary: Introduces an agentic, ontology-guided framework for knowledge graph construction from scientific papers, using specialized agents for document understanding, triple extraction with textual evidence, ontology conformance, and entity linking, with multistage verification. Targets the bottleneck of manual curation in climate science literature. Combines LLM agents with schema grounding for trustworthy structured knowledge.

entry.title: Cognitively Constrained Partners for Zero-Shot Coordination in Real-Time Partitioned Control

author.name: Ash Simmons, George De Ath, Richard M. Everson

entry.summary: The paper proposes training human-AI teaming agents against Cognitively Constrained Partners: simulated partners whose diversity comes from procedural constraints grounded in human physiology, such as reaction delays and perceptual limits, rather than reward shaping or historical checkpoints. Preliminary results in a modified Lunar Lander suggest these partners play more like real humans and improve zero-shot coordination. This offers a cheaper alternative to human-feedback training for human-machine teaming.

entry.title: CFBrainAug: Modularity-Induced Counterfactual Brain Network Augmentation for Interpretable fMRI-based Autism Diagnosis

author.name: Yifan Qiao, Sheng Li

entry.summary: CFBrainAug unifies data augmentation and counterfactual explanation for autism diagnosis from resting-state fMRI by learning label-altered brain networks: it retrieves a label-opposite, topologically similar candidate and refines it under a module-number constraint. Training jointly on factual and counterfactual networks mitigates overfitting on small clinical datasets while improving interpretability.

entry.title: Shared Is Not Enough: Predictor Width and Factor Readability Under Masked Latent Prediction

author.name: Nilotpal Kakati

entry.summary: Using a controlled simulator where every generative factor is known, the author shows I-JEPA's narrow predictor retains far less information about factors shared between views than SimCLR, and that widening the predictor to encoder width reverses the ordering. This clarifies which information masked latent prediction methods preserve and implicates predictor capacity as a key determinant.

entry.title: RootDown: Deploying and Benchmarking Models for Beet-Root Detection on Edge Devices

author.name: Gerardus Croonen, Andreas Trondl, Julia Simon, Daniel Steininger

entry.summary: RootDown provides an end-to-end image pipeline for detecting partially occluded sugar beets on loader conveyors as a step toward automated post-harvest quality inspection, introducing a dedicated benchmark and an automatic annotation strategy leveraging the existing SAM 3 foundation model. The work targets edge deployment for a practical agricultural setting. It contributes both a domain benchmark and an annotation-efficiency method.

entry.title: IFC-SSL-Bench: Benchmarking Self-Supervised Learning for Annotation-Efficient Multispectral Imaging Flow Cytometry

author.name: Angelo Jovin Yamachui Sitcheu, Roxana-Teodora Fetescu, Thomas Lautenschlager, Nils Friederich, Linus Schilpp, Stephan Allgeier, Luca Deininger, Daniel H\"ubschmann, Ralf Mikut

entry.summary: IFC-SSL-Bench is a modular benchmark evaluating six self-supervised learning approaches across four backbones on two heterogeneous imaging flow cytometry datasets, measuring downstream classification from 1% to 100% annotation regimes. It finds SSL can match fully supervised baselines while quantifying annotation efficiency for high-dimensional biological imaging. This provides a systematic resource for label-scarce scientific imaging.

entry.title: Sam-Correction: Fully Adaptive Label Noise Reduction for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Takuro Shimaya, Masahiro Saiko

entry.summary: Proposes SAM-Correction, which uses the Segment Anything Model as a foundation-model prior to progressively correct noisy ground-truth masks in medical segmentation without requiring expert-curated clean masks. Prompts for SAM are derived from another source, enabling fully adaptive label denoising.

entry.title: UAV-SwarmAgent: Scalable Multi-UAV Reconnaissance and Task Allocation via Code Generation and Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Oleg Sautenkov, Yasheerah Yaqoot, Muhammad Ahsan Mustafa, Grigorii Kalinin, Chih-Yung Wen, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: UAV SwarmAgent is a hierarchical multi-agent system where an operator states a mission in natural language, a ground-station agent generates code to produce per-UAV routes grounded by a vision-language model, and onboard worker agents verify incidents. In simulation the swarm located incidents in 95.7 percent of 255 missions, with scaling studies from one to five UAVs. It demonstrates LLM-driven autonomy for multi-drone reconnaissance.

entry.title: Is GPT 2XL already clean?

author.name: Jasper Blank

entry.summary: This post reruns OpenAI's 2023 language-model-explains-neuron experiment on GPT-2 XL using Opus 5.5 instead of GPT-4, finding the newer model can identify 3-19 percent of neurons from activations, a large improvement over the roughly 0.3 percent achieved in 2023. The author engages with Goodfire's claim that networks are already clean, defined as being understandable by looking at neurons directly without derived objects. The work was heavily AI-assisted with the author directing Opus 5.5.

entry.title: CEMIR vs. FISER: a comparative study of reasoning-based and enrichment-based approaches to pragmatic intent recognition

author.name: Ziya Hosseynzadeh, Farjad Fallah, Farnoosh Fallah, Soroush Gooran, Mohammad Amanloo, Hossein Sameti

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks two paradigms for pragmatic intent recognition in human-robot interaction: FISER, which uses structured social and embodied reasoning, versus CEMIR, which performs multimodal context enrichment. The diagnostic study clarifies when enrichment helps and when it does not, specifically for ambiguity about unstated human intent rather than missing scene information.

entry.title: Beyond Channel Data: Configuration-Enriched Radio Foundation Models

author.name: Shrihari Vasudevan, H. G. Ranjani, Raaghul Ranganathan, Satwik Sahu, Thirumaran Ekambaram

entry.summary: This paper enriches Radio Foundation Model pre-training with channel configuration information, showing the resulting embeddings act as effective inductive priors for downstream wireless tasks under label scarcity. It evaluates on LoS/NLoS classification, timing advance estimation, and beam selection across three data regimes and in/out-of-distribution configurations. It is a useful step for foundation models in wireless communications.

entry.title: Validating the Comparison, Not Just the Scorer: Why Overall Accuracy Can Mislead in Interactive LLM Evaluation

author.name: Ancil Crayton

entry.summary: This paper shows that validating an automatic scorer with a single overall accuracy or F1 score can hide prompt-specific errors that bias measured differences between prompting conditions in interactive LLM studies. It argues for validating the comparison itself rather than only the scorer, and discusses pitfalls of audits dominated by difficult responses. This is a useful methodological caution for LLM evaluation studies.

entry.title: Reuse, Rewrite, or Reject: Evidence-Constrained Trace Reuse for Repeated Mobile GUI Control

author.name: Bingyu Bai, Cheng Zhang, Erhu Feng

entry.summary: This paper proposes graph-text templates for selective reuse of prior execution traces in mobile GUI agents, validating individual transitions against current task context and interface state rather than rejecting whole procedures. A taxonomy of six variation categories grounds the approach. This reduces redundant LLM inference and execution overhead for repetitive mobile tasks.

entry.title: ENCL: Enabling Efficient Neuromorphic Continual Learning with Local Learning Rule and Sub-Network Freezing Strategy

author.name: Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Shuochen Zhou, Hassan Raza, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: ENCL enables power-efficient neuromorphic continual learning by replacing memory-hungry experience replay and global backpropagation-style surrogate gradients with a lightweight local learning rule plus a sub-network freezing strategy using sparse event-based operations. It targets runtime adaptation of deployed systems under tight energy budgets.

entry.title: Implicit Neural Representations for Variational Problems on Graphons

author.name: Taeyoung Kim, Jineon Baek, Joonkyung Lee, Hongseok Yang

entry.summary: The authors propose a neural framework for solving variational problems over graphons, the symmetric measurable functions that arise as limits of dense graph sequences and are central to extremal graph theory and large deviation theory of random graphs. Graphons are represented by implicit neural networks with a multi-scale sinusoidal residual architecture and optimized via gradient descent. This connects deep learning to deep mathematical questions about graph parameter optimization.

entry.title: Easy-3Dfy: Object-Level Geometric Composition for Single-Image 3D Scene Construction

author.name: Ziang Zhang, Wenyou Yi, Zehan Wang, Jiachen Xu, Xintong Han, Chunchao Guo, Zhou Zhao

entry.summary: Easy-3Dfy is a compositional workflow for single-image 3D scene construction that decouples object generation from scene layout estimation, combining specialized 3D object generators with generalizable 3D foundation models. An RPF-based aligner establishes geometric correspondence between object-local meshes and partial scene pointmaps to recover fine-grained geometry. This addresses quality limitations of end-to-end approaches like SAM-3Dfy.

entry.title: Complementing DINO Features with Image Structure for Part Discovery

author.name: Samyak Rawlekar, Nikhil Chowdary Paleti, Amey Gupta, Narendra Ahuja

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses why DINO-based part discovery produces imprecise boundaries: ViT patches straddling part boundaries yield higher-entropy, lower-confidence features rather than absorbing pixel mixing as invariance training might suggest. The authors complement DINO features with image structure to improve part boundary precision, validated through experiments on over 26K foreground patches. It improves training-free semantic part segmentation.

entry.title: TENET: Time-point Encoding Network for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Dongchan Cho, Juwon Hwang, Keumyeong Kang, Jiho Han, Namsoon Jung

entry.summary: Reframes unsupervised multivariate time series anomaly detection as estimating whether the current point is compatible with the system's latent state. TENET builds a time-point system state from variable-level temporal context in an input window, aiming to avoid unreliable reconstruction-based scoring that local variation can inflate. A solid methodological contribution to a mature subfield.

entry.title: AutoMIL: Automated Multiple Instance Learning for Whole-Slide Image Classification

author.name: Jonas Waibel, Frank Kramer, Dominik M\"uller

entry.summary: Presents AutoMIL, an open-source AutoML framework that automates pipeline construction (preprocessing, training, evaluation) for whole-slide pathology image classification. Benchmarks show strong ROC-AUC on UBC-OCEAN, PCam, and a TCGA-NSCLC subset, comparable to specialized pipelines. Its main contribution is accessibility and reproducibility for computational pathology rather than raw performance.

entry.title: Yalda-Embedding: Open Development of a Competitive Persian Retrieval Model

author.name: Yalda Taheri, Mohammad Hassan Heydari, Armon Rasooli

entry.summary: Yalda Embedding is a 595.8M-parameter Persian retrieval model adapted from Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B using over one million query-document pairs, achieving the best macro-average among 0.6B models on eight Persian FaMTEB tasks and approaching the much larger Qwen3-Embedding-4B. The open development process and ablation study document how language-specific adaptation closes the resource gap for Persian. It advances equitable multilingual retrieval.

entry.title: Not All Retained Clients Are Equal: Client Selection for Federated Unlearning

author.name: Thanh Linh Nguyen, Quoc-Viet Pham

entry.summary: PDF is a path-dependent client-selection framework for federated unlearning that recognizes client influence is path-dependent, tracking contributions during training including critical learning periods to select which retained clients should participate in unlearning. This improves efficiency and effectiveness over treating unlearning as a stateless post-hoc operation. It targets a growing need for machine unlearning under privacy regulations.

entry.title: Cautious Conflict-Free Inverse Gradient Methods

author.name: Damian Hattler, Qiang Liu, Nils Thuerey

entry.summary: The authors identify a vulnerability that arises when the ConFIG gradient-conflict-resolution method for PINN training is combined with adaptive optimizers like Adam, since the conflict-free direction is further processed by the optimizer. They propose a cautious variant that fixes this interaction and improves multi-objective physics-informed training.

entry.title: REDAR: Reinforcement-Driven Adaptive Regularisation for Class Incremental Learning

author.name: Akila Ayanthi, Darshana Priyasad, Tharindu Fernando, Sridha Sridharan, Clinton Fookes, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: REDAR treats regularization-strength selection in class-incremental learning as a sequential decision problem, using a lightweight RL agent that observes performance metrics and incoming data statistics each phase to set distillation coefficients. This replaces the fixed offline-tuned coefficients of standard regularization-based CIL methods.

entry.title: When to Trust Memory: Retrieval-Guided Probabilistic Spatiotemporal Forecasting under Distribution Shift

author.name: Haochen Lv, Jianhao Zhang, Zhichen Lei, Yang Jiang, Xiaowei Mao, Shengnan Guo, Youfang Lin, Huaiyu Wan

entry.summary: REMIND is a retrieval-guided probabilistic framework for spatiotemporal forecasting that explicitly characterizes the degree of distribution shift and adapts prediction strategy accordingly, improving calibration under non-stationarity. It targets real-world decision-making applications where uncertainty estimates matter.

entry.title: Amortized Thompson Sampling and Efficient Information-Directed Sampling for Simulator-Based Design

author.name: Michal Kobiela, Michael U. Gutmann

entry.summary: The paper amortizes Thompson sampling by precomputing approximations of the full Thompson sampling distribution before data collection, enabling efficient sequential decision-making and information-directed sampling for simulator-based experimental design, especially in continuous action spaces.

entry.title: Deep Learning-Based Prediction of HER2 Status from Whole-Brain MRI in Breast Cancer Brain Metastases

author.name: Sara Early, Chris Kang, Vibujithan Vigneshwaran, Kimberly Amador, Roger Y. Tsang, Nils D. Forkert

entry.summary: The study explores whether HER2 receptor status, a key biomarker in metastatic breast cancer, can be predicted directly from post-contrast T1-weighted whole-brain MRI using deep learning. Using 135 patients from a public radiogenomics dataset, it compares a radiomics baseline, a fully convolutional network, and variants augmented with tumor segmentation information.

entry.title: Residual Calibration via Local Feature-Space Refinement

author.name: Xihao Wang, Chengyao Yu, Ruixing Ming

entry.summary: LAPE is a post-hoc calibration framework that treats a global calibrator's output as an anchor and refines predictions using non-parametric local evidence from neighboring samples in feature space, capturing spatially varying miscalibration that score-based transformations miss. It is presented as a plug-and-play module for reliable confidence estimation.

entry.title: PROVE: Probabilistic Visual Grounding via Patch-Level Evidence for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Mayank Nautiyal, Tianru Zhang, Li Ju, Ekta Vats, Prashant Singh

entry.summary: PROVE is a post-hoc evidential adapter that maps frozen CLIP patch features to per-patch Beta distributions, casting visual grounding as per-patch membership with accumulated positive and negative evidence. This yields calibrated uncertainty over localization, allowing a query to match zero, one, or many patches rather than producing a single deterministic relevance map.

entry.title: Sparse Bayesian Neural Networks via Sticky Piecewise Deterministic Markov Processes

author.name: August Arnstad, Geir Olve Storvik, Filippo Pagani, Leiv R{\o}nneberg

entry.summary: The paper shows modern Monte Carlo samplers based on piecewise deterministic Markov processes can asymptotically exactly sample Bayesian neural network posteriors with spike-and-slab priors for pruning, provided numerically constructed rate bounds hold. This offers a principled alternative to train-then-prune for identifying the small subset of weights that matters.

entry.title: Beyond What to Say: Proactive Utterance Timing with Inner Thoughts for Werewolf Agents

author.name: Yoshiki Tanaka, Shuya Uchiyama, Daichi Hamaguchi, Michimasa Inaba

entry.summary: The paper presents a Werewolf-game LLM agent built for the Anytime Utterance Track of the AIWolfDial shared task, extending the Inner Thoughts framework to decide when to speak by generating internal thoughts and evaluating their value. This treats utterance timing, not just content, as a strategic decision in adversarial conversation. It contributes to research on proactive conversational agents.

entry.title: StateBridge: Phase- and Track-Grounded Reasoning for Synthetic-to-Real Traffic Video Captioning and VQA

author.name: Blessing Agyei Kyem, Richard Dzinyela, Joshua Kofi Asamoah, Eugene Denteh, Andrews Danyo, Solomon Owusu-Ansah, Dickson Gyimah Asiedu, Armstrong Aboah

entry.summary: StateBridge is a traffic video-language framework trained on synthetic scenes and evaluated on real traffic, using phase-aware clip construction, pedestrian and vehicle track summaries, and structured prompts to ground models in stable traffic evidence. Fine-tuned public VLMs are combined through fact-locked fusion for captioning and visual question answering. It addresses the synthetic-to-real generalization challenge in traffic safety analysis.

entry.title: Organizing Temporal Evidence in Hyperbolic Space for Video Moment Retrieval

author.name: Mengnan Liu, Sanping Zhou, Kun Xia, Jiaxuan Lin, Gang Hua, Le Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Hyperbolic Temporal Evidence Organization (HTEO), which embeds query-relevant evidence for video moment retrieval in hyperbolic space to jointly capture target regions, boundary transitions, and contextual distractors with distinct temporal structures. It replaces flat Euclidean alignment with a geometry suited to hierarchical relevance organization.

entry.title: VERA-Hand: A Verified Multidimensional Benchmark for 2D Hand Pose Estimation in Third-Person Dynamic Gesture Videos

author.name: Gibran Benitez-Garcia, Hiroki Takahashi

entry.summary: VERA-Hand provides manually verified frame-level 2D annotations for 10,690 hands and evaluates hand pose estimators across detection, localization, identification, and temporal stability, introducing a joint Pose-F1 metric. It exposes failure modes such as missed hands, handedness errors, and temporal instability that PCK/MPJPE metrics overlook.

entry.title: Facultative Swarming: A Capability, Not a Category, for Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Ning Zhou, Edmund R. Hunt

entry.summary: This position/conceptual paper proposes reframing the centralized-versus-decentralized multi-robot dichotomy as facultative swarming: hybrid architectures that operate as centrally planned systems under permissive conditions yet degrade gracefully into decentralized swarming under environmental stress. The authors argue swarming is a dynamic capability rather than a rigid system category. This outlines a design path for collective robots combining optimality and robustness.

entry.title: Bayesian Propensity Score Predictive Inference for Extending Trial Findings to Target Populations

author.name: Jungang Zou, Joseph E. Schwartz, Roderick J. A. Little, Nathalie Moise, Qixuan Chen

entry.summary: The authors develop Bayesian Propensity Score Predictive Inference (PSPI), an interaction-based outcome modeling framework combining Bayesian additive regression trees with cubic splines of the sampling propensity score to extend randomized trial findings to broader target populations. Applied to the CODIACS Vanguard depression-care trial and two All of Us electronic health record cohorts, the method handles treatment-effect heterogeneity when covariate distributions differ between trial and target populations.

entry.title: Autoregressive Multimodal Anomaly Detection with Large Language Models for Microservice Systems

author.name: Yixiang Tang, Fagui Liu, Guoxiang Zhong, Xi Yao, C. L. Philip Chen

entry.summary: LLMMAD is an autoregressive LLM-based approach to multimodal anomaly detection in microservice systems, addressing neglect of modality-specific characteristics and the identity-shortcut problem in feature reconstruction. Reliable anomaly detection matters because failures propagate quickly across cloud services. It targets a real operational reliability problem at scale.

entry.title: TTT in VLA Models: Exploring Training with Human Demonstrations

author.name: Qiangong Zhou, Jiafeng Liang, Yimin Dong, Yang He, Hongxiang Li

entry.summary: The authors integrate Test-Time Training with fast weights into InternVLA-A1 and Pi0.5 to condition robot action generation on human demonstrations, implementing memory transfer and truncated backpropagation across training objectives and gradient coverage settings. At the tested scale, adding TTT and paired-demonstration training did not yield consistent target selection, yielding mostly negative findings.

entry.title: Anti-coherence Regularized Absolute Scaling for Out-of-Distribution Detection

author.name: Donghwan Kim, Youngwoong Jin, Hyunsoo Yoon

entry.summary: The paper fixes an ill-defined case in the SCALE post-hoc OOD detection method, where positive and negative activations cancel in the magnitude ratio, causing failure on backbones like ViT, by computing the ratio over absolute-valued activations. Building on this fix, the authors propose anti-coherence regularization that penalizes the scaling factor to improve OOD detection. This is relevant to AI safety's reliable-deployment goals.

entry.title: MusicTwins: Training Audio-Language Models to Listen like Their Persona

author.name: Milan Liessens Dujardin, Kevin Miao

entry.summary: Introduces MusicTwins, a framework that post-trains audio-language models with persona summaries, personal memory, and musical profiles to generate person-specific responses to music and text stimuli. It explores whether ALMs can simulate an individual's subjective music perception, extending persona simulation beyond text-only LLMs. A distinctive intersection of affective computing, personalization, and human-AI simulation.

entry.title: Does LeWorldModel Preserve Local Action Geometry?

author.name: Vasil Vasilev, Siddharth Nayak

entry.summary: The paper measures whether pretrained LeWorldModel reproduces the effects of small action changes, using Gram matrices to compare action sensitivity between simulator and model across nearly a thousand states in Reacher and OGBench Cube. The most sensitive action directions diverge by median angles of about 36-42 degrees at the smallest perturbation scale, indicating imperfect local action geometry. This provides a diagnostic tool for evaluating world model fidelity.

entry.title: The Standard Deviation in VICReg Buys a Safety Margin

author.name: Hawar Dizayee

entry.summary: This paper experimentally tests VICReg's claim that a variance hinge would fail to prevent collapse, finding that at default weights both hinges perform identically on CIFAR-10 but the standard-deviation hinge's collapse threshold is 35-130x lower because its gradient does not fade as feature variance shrinks. It reframes the variance-vs-standard-deviation choice as a stability safety margin.

entry.title: A Tutorial on Physics Constrained Machine Learning for Hybrid Modeling, Optimization, and Control

author.name: Rahul Golder, Bimol Nath Roy, MM Faruque Hasan

entry.summary: This tutorial presents a modular physics-constrained ML framework, KKT-HardNet, which combines neural network inference with guaranteed satisfaction of algebraic equality and inequality constraints via differential projection. It demonstrates use for hybrid modeling, process simulation, optimization, and model predictive control within a single platform.

entry.title: Operationalising Weaker Faithfulness: Recovery, Ambiguity and Computational Limits

author.name: Cillian Hourican, Rick Quax

entry.summary: The paper investigates how to weaken the faithfulness assumption in causal structure learning via selective protection of adjacency links and explicit retention of alternative directed-graph explanations. Experiments on noisy XOR settings show combining reactivation and protection achieves complete parent-pair recovery where either alone fails, at the cost of additional false edges, and a confirmation study examines computational limits.

entry.title: EMG Tokenization Preserves Movement Information at a Fraction of the Bitrate

author.name: Raul C. S\^impetru, Amin Olamazadeh, Devon Rohlf, Vlad Cnejevici, Alessandro Del Vecchio

entry.summary: The authors show that causal EMG tokenizers - one pretrained to reconstruct EMG spectra and one based on the SPAR spectral-spatial representation - drastically cut wireless transmission payload while preserving information for 3D hand-pose decoding. In 320-channel within-session experiments across nine participants, tokenization changed mean decoding error by roughly 0.01 mm versus continuous features.

entry.title: Standing on Open Shoulders: Regional Fine-Tuning of Open-Weight Camera-Trap Models for UK Wildlife with Modest Data and Compute

author.name: Paul Fergus

entry.summary: A small team fine-tunes the open DeepFaune classifier on 28 UK species with modest data and a single GPU, pairing it with MegaDetector v6 to create DeepFaune-UK, evaluated on 20,212 hand-verified citizen-science images with careful train-test contamination control. It demonstrates that open weights enable meaningful regional contributions to wildlife AI.

entry.title: Universal neural network approximation of symmetric polyconvex energies and envelopes

author.name: Florian Gammer

entry.summary: The paper introduces symmetric polyconvex neural networks (SPCNNs) for small-strain elasticity, showing that weight restrictions on ReLU-based input-convex networks fail to universally approximate lifted representers of symmetric polyconvex functions. SPCNNs achieve universal approximation while preserving the monotonicity needed for weak lower semicontinuity in constitutive modeling.

entry.title: OpenStripe supports open-set identification and spatial stripe profiling in wild Amur tigers

author.name: Yichun Peng, Yansong Li, Jin Hou, Qi Song, Xi Guo, Ning Zhang, Degang Wei, Huang Yang, Yu Guan, Jianping Ge, Lei Bao, Tianming Wang

entry.summary: OpenStripe is a multi-agent framework for open-set individual identification of wild Amur tigers that reconstructs canonical 2D torso patterns and encodes four interpretable local stripe structures, evaluated on 100 camera-trap records of 28 wild tigers. It addresses the hard open-set setting where population size is unknown, important for endangered-species monitoring.

entry.title: Mixed Engression: Distributional Regression for Multivariate Mixed-Type Responses

author.name: Seyong Hwang, Kean Ming Tan, Ji Zhu

entry.summary: The authors propose mixed engression, a distributional regression method for multivariate responses with continuous and binary components that fits a continuous generator via energy losses from bounded discrepancies and thresholds soft binary outputs to produce mixed-response samples. The bounded discrepancies keep the population objective well defined without response-moment assumptions, and the paper identifies and analyzes a subtle failure mode where the full-response energy distance can vanish before thresholding yet stay bounded away from zero afterward.

entry.title: Tradeoff-Aware Territory Design: A Multi-Objective Decision System for Enterprise Customer-to-Seller Allocation

author.name: Nan Wang, Mitchell Turiel

entry.summary: This paper presents a production decision system for B2B go-to-market planning that automates customer-to-seller territory allocation. It combines a multidimensional account-value scoring layer with multi-objective optimization to balance growth, workload balance, seller continuity, and capacity feasibility, replacing a largely manual process.

entry.title: Evidence-Grounded SLM Behavioral Prediction Architecture for Future Assistance Use

author.name: Adeyemi Adeseye, Aisvarya Adeseye, Hannu Tenhunen, Jouni Isoaho

entry.summary: This work proposes using small language models for on-device prediction of whether a user will soon need assistance, based on changes in interaction behavior, motivated by privacy and the computational limits of LLMs in continuous monitoring. It emphasizes evidence-grounded reasoning over low-level sequential interaction events.

entry.title: An Agentic Approach with Evidence-Grounded Verification for Multimodal Emotion Reasoning in Conversation

author.name: Elyas Rashno, Farhana Zulkernine

entry.summary: This paper presents an agentic framework for multimodal emotion recognition in conversation, using modality-specific perception agents that post evidence-cited observations, an integration agent, and traceable error attribution across stages. Built from frozen models, it avoids costly instruction tuning while enabling prompt-space adaptation. It matters as an example of verifiable, debuggable agentic pipelines for affective computing.

entry.title: RobustNCL: Robustifying Neuromorphic Continual Learning under Transient Faults with Lightweight Detect-and-Cure Strategy

author.name: Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Shuochen Zhou, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: RobustNCL is the first framework to study neuromorphic continual learning reliability under hardware transient faults such as particle strikes, adding a lightweight detect-and-cure strategy to protect runtime adaptation. The paper opens fault tolerance as an unexplored dimension of NCL.

entry.title: MG-REPA: Multi-Granularity Representation Alignment for Generative Target Speaker Extraction

author.name: Dohwan Kim, Jung-Woo Choi

entry.summary: MG-REPA extends Representation Alignment (REPA) for generative target speaker extraction by aligning diffusion transformer hidden states with a self-supervised speech model at both frame and utterance levels, since single-granularity alignment leaves either time-varying content or global speaker characteristics implicit. This addresses the slow training convergence of generative TSE models. The work matters for improving efficiency and quality in speech processing.

entry.title: Cycle-of-Thought: Self-Evaluative Iterative Reasoning for Table Visual Question Answering in Document Images

author.name: Somraj Gautam, Gaurav Harit

entry.summary: Presents Self-RefineVQA, a training-free, inference-time self-correction framework for improving VQA over tables in document images, targeting spatial misalignment and logical hallucinations. The approach avoids architectural changes or costly supervised fine-tuning, drawing on iterative human-like revision. A useful efficiency-oriented technique, though framed around existing VLMs.

entry.title: SP-Guide: Enhancing Aerial Vision-Language Navigation with Spatial Priors

author.name: Haoxiang Tang, Dong Zhou, Shen Tan, Minxuan Jiang, Xitong Li

entry.summary: Proposes SP-Guide, a transformer-based framework for aerial vision-language navigation that improves cross-modal spatial alignment via a Spatial Prior Cross-Modal Encoder, an instruction-enhanced decoder, and a goal convergence filter. On the CityNav benchmark it improves success rate over representative baselines. Addresses the underexplored setting of UAV navigation over large outdoor scenes.

entry.title: Monetizing Intelligence: Advertising and Subscription Design on LLM Platforms

author.name: Yuhang Ji, Fasheng Xu, Tianjun Feng

entry.summary: This economic analysis models a monopolistic LLM platform that jointly optimizes response quality, advertising intensity, and subscription prices when ads reduce user value but better service increases ad revenue. It derives results such as ad-supported plans financing useful service for some users while weakening alternatives and enabling higher ad-free prices. The work illuminates the welfare implications of hybrid ad-subscription business models for AI platforms.

entry.title: Towards Trustworthy AI-Enabled Emergency Medical Dispatch: Uncertainty-Aware Ambulance Travel Time Estimation

author.name: Muhammad Adil Abid, Johan Holmgren, Fabian Lorig, Jesper Petersson

entry.summary: This work tackles ambulance travel time estimation for emergency dispatch, arguing that single point predictions are inadequate in safety-critical settings where trips with similar expected times may carry very different uncertainty. The authors develop uncertainty-aware estimation methods that also handle domain shifts in real-world trip logs.

entry.title: Interpreting Supervised Pairwise Graph Representations: Local Evidence, Confounding, and Provable Post-hoc Correction

author.name: Ilya Brekin, Ariela Moldavskaya, Elina Sidorova, Ural Valeev

entry.summary: The paper critically examines supervised pairwise graph representations, showing that their apparent advantage over model confidence in a Transformer error-detection task disappears after controlling for sequence length confounding, and provides provable post-hoc corrections plus analysis of node aggregation as an implicit ensemble.

entry.title: Multi modal perceived conversation success prediction for spontaneous autistic and non-autistic dyadic interactions

author.name: Thanushi Withanage, Desi Jones, Noah Sasson, Elizabeth Redcay, Carol Espy-Wilson

entry.summary: This study predicts participant-perceived conversation success in autistic and non-autistic dyadic interactions from articulatory, facial, acoustic-prosodic, and turn-taking measures across three spontaneous interaction datasets. Unlike prior work focused on diagnostic classification, it targets subjective conversation quality directly.

entry.title: On the Limits of Stochastic Push-Pull over Time-Varying Digraphs

author.name: Feiming Wang, Yutong He, Sulaiman Alghunaim, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: This theory paper constructs a quadratic decentralized problem on period-two networks showing stochastic Push-Pull can fail to achieve linear network-size speedup on time-varying digraphs. It identifies an effective node count governing the leading stochastic term and proves matching convergence upper and lower bounds with Theta(1/sqrt(n_eff T)) dependence.

entry.title: When Human Corrections Travel: Safety in Federated VLA Adaptation

author.name: Vigneshwaran Subbaraju, Obaidullah Zaland, Monowar Bhuyan

entry.summary: This position-style paper examines the intersection of vision-language-action policies adapted from local human interventions with federated learning across robots, arguing that shared corrections can suppress rare safety interventions or behave unsafely on other embodiments. It proposes three requirements: preserving correction context and uncertainty, per-robot assessment of candidate updates, and safety-aware aggregation.

entry.title: Profile-Driven User Simulation via Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Rewards for Task-Oriented Dialogues

author.name: Juan Li, Fangshu Chang, Xinyi Jiang, Ling Huang, Yunzhang Chen

entry.summary: ProfileSim is a reinforcement-learned user simulation framework for task-oriented dialogue in financial marketing outbound calls, jointly modeling user profiles (demographics and Big Five traits) with business process and compliance constraints. It uses hierarchical rewards to capture domain-specific procedures and the spoken, colloquial character of voice interactions where existing general-domain simulators fall short.

entry.title: Real-Time Localisation of Dorsal Anatomical Regions on Dairy Cows in Commercial Rotary Parlours from RGB-D

author.name: Vineet Prasad, Shiron Melvin, Sheikh Azid, Hai Wang

entry.summary: Presents a real-time RGB-D perception system that localizes a target cow, ten bony landmarks, and four named dorsal regions (withers, back, rump, tail-head) in a single forward pass within crowded commercial rotary milking parlours. It uses late-fused color and depth encoders with a shared three-head decoder, enabling automated, region-specific livestock monitoring.

entry.title: Interactive image diagnosis using test-time backpropagation from the auxiliary task

author.name: Takuro Shimaya

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-task gradient assist (MGA) method that lets radiologists give feedback on auxiliary-task predictions and request additional diagnostic suggestions without retraining, using test-time backpropagation from the auxiliary task. It is demonstrated on mammography and CT datasets to make CAD systems more interactive.

entry.title: PCFBench: How Far Can Large Vision-Language Models Go in Physics-aware Photonic Inverse Design?

author.name: Shengchao Chen, Ting Shu, Sufen Ren

entry.summary: PCFBench is the first benchmark evaluating VLMs on photonic crystal fiber inverse design, covering 26 tasks across perception, physics understanding, and decision steps. It probes whether VLMs truly reason about waveguide physics from microscopy images or merely recognize visual patterns.

entry.title: Computational imaging through turbid, bubbly and flowing water near the telescope

author.name: Alexander Ingold, Sabina D. Menon, Aadhi Umamageswaran, Alec Ikei, May H. Hlaing, Syed N. Qadri, Rajesh Menon

entry.summary: Introduces a measured dataset of a telescope imaging displayed targets through a 25 mm water layer under seven combinations of flow, bubbles, and turbidity, quantifying contrast loss and evaluating frame averaging and learned restoration. Findings indicate turbidity mainly removes contrast and learned multi-frame fusion adds little beyond averaging.

entry.title: Covariance-Informed Ensemble Score Filtering: Embedding Localized Covariance Geometry into Score-Based Transport

author.name: Siming Liang, Peter Jan van Leeuwen, Hristo G. Chipilski, Zezhong Zhang, Feng Bao, Guannan Zhang

entry.summary: This work introduces CI-EnSF, a covariance-informed extension of the Ensemble Score Filter for atmospheric data assimilation that embeds localized background-error covariance geometry into score-based distributional transport. The addition provides an intrinsic covariance-mediated pathway for propagating likelihood information from observed to unobserved state components, which standard EnSF formulations lacked. This targets nonlinear data assimilation beyond Gaussian or locally quadratic approximations.

entry.title: Guided Zero-Shot Anomaly Explanation for Anonymized Crowd Video Monitoring: Context, Categorization, and Spatial Localization

author.name: Mulugeta Weldezgina Asres, Lei Jiao, Christian Walter Omlin

entry.summary: XAVAD unifies privacy-preserving video anomaly detection with explainability, combining zero-shot anonymization, anomaly-type categorization, spatial localization, and scene-context description in one framework. It targets trust and transparency for safety and security monitoring deployments.

entry.title: Beyond Heuristics and Commercial Navigation: An AI-Augmented Decision-Support for Ambulance Travel Time Estimation

author.name: Muhammad Adil Abid, Johan Holmgren, Fabian Lorig, Jesper Petersson

entry.summary: Using historical ambulance trips from Sweden's Skåne region, this paper shows that common dispatch heuristics—such as assuming ambulances travel a fixed percentage faster than cars—fail to capture variation by priority, hour, day, and origin-destination. It builds an AI-augmented decision-support approach grounded in real operational data.

entry.title: Score-Preserving Continual Lasso under Task Shift

author.name: Jingyi Guo, Runze Li, Lingzhou Xue

entry.summary: The paper studies continual learning for high-dimensional sparse linear regression, showing that recursively reusing l1-penalized estimators propagates shrinkage bias across tasks. The proposed score-preserving continual Lasso (SP-CL) separates sparse estimation from state transmission and exactly recovers a full-history Lasso minimizer under squared loss.

entry.title: Augmentation Strategy for DINO in Glaucoma Classification

author.name: Ashish Kumar Meena, Chandra Sekhar Seelamantula

entry.summary: The authors show DINO's default augmentation strategy transfers poorly to retinal fundus images and redesign it so cropped views share minimal redundant information while retaining diagnostically relevant signal, improving downstream glaucoma classification. The work highlights that SSL augmentation choices validated on natural images do not reliably transfer to medical domains.

entry.title: FOCUS: A Lightweight Mamba-2 Model for EEG-Based Cognitive Workload Classification

author.name: Ioannis Kyprakis, Stefanos Gkikas, Chariklia Chatzaki, Zongyi Jiang, Randy Gomez, Raul Fernandez Rojas

entry.summary: FOCUS is an extremely compact Mamba-2-based model (0.04M parameters, 0.11 GFLOPs) for binary EEG cognitive workload classification that encodes multi-channel EEG via a fixed FFT decomposition over the five canonical EEG bands instead of learning frequency sensitivity from data. It uses depthwise-separable convolution with a weight-shared encoder-bottleneck Mamba-2 pair.

entry.title: Collaborative In-Context Learning for Indoor Radio Map Estimation

author.name: Yuanzhe Peng, Jie Xu

entry.summary: Poly-Ripple formulates indoor radio map estimation as collaborative in-context learning, where clients use large autoregressive vision models without weight updates, prompting with private demonstrations. This avoids costly labeled data and task-specific training while respecting privacy of building layouts. It is a novel application of ICL to wireless network planning.

entry.title: The Path to NDE 4.0: A Review of Algorithms, Techniques, and Strategies for Autonomous Inspection

author.name: Ashiqur Rahmana, Venkata Devesh Reddy Seethi, Zachary Kral, Austin Yunker, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Hamed Alhoori

entry.summary: This is a comprehensive review of autonomous Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) organized around computational algorithms, physical techniques, industrial applications, and research objectives, tracing the shift from manual analog interpretation to the data-centric NDE 4.0 paradigm. It highlights ultrasound and visual inspection dominance and the trend toward automation. The paper serves as a reference map for ML applied to industrial inspection.

entry.title: DRIVE: Fine-tuning via Data Contribution- and Diversity-aware Weighting with Prior Regularization

author.name: Qing Liu, Xinrui Chen, Yi Du, Ou Wu, Weiyao Zhu

entry.summary: DRIVE is a framework for assigning per-sample weights during single-stage fine-tuning via a unified differentiable objective that arbitrates between knowledge retention (against catastrophic forgetting when source data is inaccessible) and new-task adaptation, incorporating sample diversity and contribution signals.

entry.title: WL-SeqVAE: Sequence-Based Graph Generation Using Variational Autoencoders and Weisfeiler-Leman Colors

author.name: Iakovos Evdaimon, Giannis Nikolentzos, Achilleas Tsimichodimos, Christos Xypolopoulos, Michalis Vazirgiannis

entry.summary: WL-SeqVAE generates graphs by mapping them to sequences of Weisfeiler-Leman colors used as structural tokens, then encoding with a VAE and decoding autoregressively, with WL-derived compatibility constraints guiding node and edge predictions. This offers a compact structural representation for generative graph modeling.

entry.title: Hybrid SEIR Temporal Fusion Transformer Framework with SHAP Analysis for Interpretable Pandemic Forecasting

author.name: Ashish Anton Abraham, Gopi Krishnan R, Aiswarya Anil Nair, Ajo Babu George, Kunal Agarwal

entry.summary: The paper combines an SEIR epidemiological model with a Temporal Fusion Transformer to produce interpretable multi-horizon infection forecasts, using region-wise COVID-19 data enriched with interventions, mobility, and demographic covariates. The SEIR component injects mechanistic priors while the TFT learns nonlinear corrections, with SHAP used for interpretability.

entry.title: Random Jump Forests

author.name: Martin Bladt, Rasmus Frigaard Lemvig

entry.summary: Random jump forests are introduced as a nonparametric tree ensemble for estimating conditional cumulative transition rates and occupation probabilities in multi-state models, using Nelson-Aalen estimators at leaves without requiring the Markov assumption. The authors establish uniform consistency and a functional central limit theorem, enabling pointwise confidence intervals.

entry.title: ARENA: Active Region attENtion Aggregation for interpretable solar flare prediction

author.name: Luis Bauer, Annalena Kofler, Andr\'es Asensio Ramos, Aparna Venkataramanasastry, Valent\'in Mart\'inez Pillet, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf

entry.summary: ARENA predicts solar flares from a variable number of active-region cutouts using multiple-instance learning under weak supervision, requiring only flare/no-flare labels. Its learned attention localizes the active region driving the prediction without explicit origin annotations, aiding interpretability in space-weather forecasting.

entry.title: Hyperparameter-Free Boundary-Interior t-vMF Dice Loss for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Hinako Mitsuoka, Kazuhiro Hotta

entry.summary: Proposes STB-tvMF Dice, a self-tuning extension of the adaptive t-vMF Dice loss that separately adapts the similarity function for boundary and interior regions without hyperparameter tuning. Shape parameters are derived each epoch from the mean prediction-target cosine similarity, maximizing the slope of the similarity function at the observed mean.

entry.title: DeformStruct: Deformable Structure Modeling for Point-Supervised Temporal Action Localization

author.name: Mengnan Liu, Sanping Zhou, Kun Xia, Yonghao Dong, Jie Wang, Gang Hua

entry.summary: Presents DeformStruct, an instance-level deformable structure modeling framework for point-supervised temporal action localization that progressively builds action structure from structural anchors mined at the annotated timestamp. It explicitly models the organization of multiple action-related parts rather than relying solely on classification responses.

entry.title: K-CLUE: A Segmentation-to-Clustering Framework for Ki67 Cell Typing

author.name: Ana Beatriz Vieira, Sara P. Oliveira, Diana Montezuma, Jo\~ao Fraga, Jaime S. Cardoso, Arlindo L. Oliveira

entry.summary: K-CLUE performs annotation-free Ki67 cell typing in breast cancer histology by segmenting nuclei, embedding them with frozen pretrained encoders, and clustering with k-means, avoiding task-specific training. The study systematically examines how encoder choice affects clustering quality across seven encoders.

entry.title: Playing Bias: Epistemic Games for Interpreting Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Amalia Foka

entry.summary: Translates a humanities-informed framework into epistemic games — Interpret, Interrogate, Expose — for building literacy about how text-to-image models encode stereotypes, including a BiasSlot prompting rule where only the bias cue varies. A pilot with undergraduates explores whether such exercises cultivate critical image literacy beyond quantitative bias audits.

entry.title: Structure and Exact Certification of Nonnegative Tensor Decompositions

author.name: Haoming Wang, Ming Yuan

entry.summary: This theory paper studies the structure and exact certification of nonnegative tensor decompositions supplied through rational factor matrices, characterizing failures of minimality and essential uniqueness via irreducible positive exchanges between supplied and competing terms. Using the Lovitz-Petrov splitting theorem and Farkas lemma, the authors reduce certification to semialgebraic systems with fewer than 2R^2 real variables and derive a deterministic algorithm with complexity G(R) times L^(O(R^2)) in input bit length L.

entry.title: Generalization properties of the token perceptron: the role of embedding and vocabulary

author.name: Dario Bocchi, Matteo Negri, Flavio Nicoletti, Francesco D'Amico

entry.summary: The authors introduce the token perceptron, a minimal solvable model where a linear predictor with per-position matrices maps embedded tokens to a d-dimensional output, and compute its generalization error via the replica method. The analysis reveals how embedding geometry and finite vocabulary size shape learning in token-prediction problems relevant to LLMs.

entry.title: SCDM-HTD: Spectral-Wise Conditional Diffusion Model for Hyperspectral Target Detection

author.name: Dunbin Shen, Wenfeng Kong, Jianjun Liu, Xiaorui Ma, Hongyu Wang

entry.summary: SCDM-HTD reformulates hyperspectral target detection as generating a detection map with a spectral-wise conditional diffusion model, using background and target confidence scores as training samples and pixel spectra as conditions to learn background-target distributional discrepancies. This shifts focus from feature comparison to distribution learning.

entry.title: Robust Offset-Free Lane-Keeping Control Framework for Vision-Only Automated Vehicles

author.name: Der-Hau Lee

entry.summary: Develops an offset-free model predictive control framework for vision-based lane keeping during high-speed cornering on large-curvature roads, solved with an interpolation-tube-based constrained iterative LQR. Simulations show it outperforms IPOPT and OSQP solvers with sub-millisecond mean computation time while maintaining vehicle stability.

entry.title: PPO vs. SAC: A Comparative Study for Cooperative Motion Control of Dual-Arm Space Robots

author.name: Nasim Fallahiarezoodar, Zheng H. Zhu

entry.summary: The paper develops a reinforcement learning framework for cooperative motion planning of dual-arm space manipulators in target-reaching tasks under inter-arm collision avoidance, orientation alignment, and sensing uncertainty, motivated by orbital debris removal and on-orbit servicing. It compares PPO and SAC using a centralized state representation and a multi-objective reward function.

entry.title: Correct Answers, Closed Gates: SolveBind for GUI Agents at the Verification Barrier

author.name: Xinhao Song, Haoxuan Peng, Su Su, Hongliang Wu, Sirui Song, Gongshen Liu, Linfeng Zhang, Dongrui Liu

entry.summary: The paper studies protected GUI environments where CAPTCHAs and anti-automation systems judge behavioral signals like trajectories and timing rather than outcomes, so correctly solving a verification task is insufficient for task completion. SolveBind combines hierarchical solving (Perceive, Ground, Solve, Act, Verify) with a runtime supervisor that grounds action commitments in runtime feedback under time constraints.

entry.title: Before the Ticket: Grounding HPC User Support in Documentation and Resolved Tickets with an Agentic LLM Assistant

author.name: Elham J. Barezi, Primus C Kabuo, Niveditha Nerella

entry.summary: This paper describes an on-premises agentic assistant for HPC help desks that combines RAG over live documentation with a QLoRA fine-tuned Llama-3-8B model over 11,244 mined historical tickets, orchestrated via Model Context Protocol tools. Evaluated on 400 held-out tickets from Purdue's system, it shows a practical deployment pattern for privacy-constrained institutional support. It matters as a concrete, privacy-respecting applied LLM system.

entry.title: FSVL: Taxonomic Fast-Slow Vision-to-Language Collaborative Framework for Interpretable Confusable Fish Species Identification and Knowledge Generation in the Middle Yangtze River

author.name: Meng Liang, Fucheng Wang, Lang Zhao, Jun Chen, Ziying Li, Yuxiang Zhao, Haozhuang Chi, Wenkai Fang, Qiong Zhou, Junlin Yang, Jinming Wu

entry.summary: FSVL combines a fast visual classifier with a slow LLM-based retrieval-augmented pathway to identify closely related Yangtze fish species, balancing fine-grained classification accuracy against efficiency and guarding against unsupported biological claims from the LLM. It supports biodiversity monitoring under the Ten-Year Fishing Ban.

entry.title: Dual-Adaptive Z-Score PPO: Dynamic Clipping Using Action Confidence and Normalized Advantage Magnitude

author.name: Taha M. Mahmoud, Naima Kaabouch

entry.summary: This work replaces PPO's fixed clipping threshold with sample-dependent thresholds computed from action confidence and normalized advantage magnitude, forming the Dual-Adaptive Z-Score PPO variant (PPO-DAZ3). The goal is to give more trustworthy policy updates wider trust regions while constraining unreliable ones. It contributes to the ongoing refinement of the most popular on-policy RL algorithm.

entry.title: ChoreoStudio: Planning What, When, and Who in Music-Driven Group Choreography

author.name: Jing Xu, Cunjian Chen, Qiuhong Ke

entry.summary: ChoreoStudio makes group dance generation planning explicit by decomposing music into frame-level rhythmic and segment-level structural features, deciding formations, transition timing, and which dancers execute transitions in alignment with musical structure. This improves formation evolution and inter-dancer interaction over prior methods that generate rhythmically synchronized but limited group motion. It is a creative application at the intersection of music understanding and motion generation.

entry.title: PlayerEmbed: Learning Behavioral Fingerprint Representations from Raw Input Sequences

author.name: Tobias Schneider, Lorenz Sparrenberg, Priya Tomar, Shahzeb Qamar, Tobias Deu{\ss}er, Rafet Sifa

entry.summary: Presents a framework learning compact player embeddings from raw game input sequences using a hybrid CNN-LSTM encoder with deep metric learning, trained on 1,000 players and evaluated on both seen and entirely unseen identities. Nearest-centroid classification over embeddings achieves high balanced accuracy for identification. Useful for game analytics and behavior-based identity modeling.

entry.title: ConsMSA: Semantic Distribution Consistency Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Pan Wang, Lipeng Ke, Huajun Ying, Pritish Mohapatra, Rohan Sarkar, Suresh Lakhani, Sankar Venkataraman, Jingtong Hu

entry.summary: ConsMSA formalizes intra- and inter-modality semantic distribution consistency for multimodal sentiment analysis, projecting token features into a shared sentiment space and computing consistency scores to handle redundancy and conflicts across text, video, and audio. The mechanism improves robustness while reducing computational cost. It is an incremental but coherent advance in multimodal fusion for sentiment.

entry.title: BAARC: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Partial Spectral Measurement to Full Reconstruction for Material Classification

author.name: Adithya Ashok Chalain Valapil, Aishwarya Venkataramanan, Joachim Denzler

entry.summary: BAARC is a Bayesian adaptive acquisition framework for Raman spectroscopy that learns to select small spectral patches sequentially under uncertainty, reconstructing and classifying materials from partial measurements. It reduces required measurement coverage without prior knowledge of distinguishing spectral regions.

entry.title: GeoLEON-CLIP: Graph-Anchored Multimodal Contrastive Learning for Geographic Region Representation

author.name: Radoslaw Malek, Szymon Soltysiak, Aleksandra Kawala-Sterniuk, Piotr Szymanski

entry.summary: GeoLEON-CLIP aligns three views of H3-indexed geographic regions - OpenStreetMap graph embeddings, satellite imagery, and text descriptions - using frozen pretrained encoders with trainable projection heads under a tri-modal contrastive objective. This enriches region representations with structured map context that prior image-text or image-location contrastive methods ignore.

entry.title: The Punjabi Geet Toxicity Dataset (PGT-FG): Fine-Grained Multimodal Annotations for Toxic Content in Punjabi Songs

author.name: Lakhjeet Kaur, Jaspreet Kaur, Komal Rani, Yougal Attri, Ramakant KumarJaydeep Kishore, Pravin Kumar

entry.summary: The paper presents PGT-FG, a segment-level dataset of fine-grained toxicity annotations for Punjabi songs, produced by four native annotators with an overlap subset for agreement analysis, derived from publicly available YouTube music. It provides a much-needed resource for toxicity research in a low-resource language and in multimodal musical content.

entry.title: Synthetic-to-Real Text-Based Person Anomaly Search via Multi-Model Retrieval Fusion and Cross-Encoder Reranking

author.name: Eugene Denteh, Blessing Agyei Kyem, Andrews Danyo, Joshua Kofi Asamoah, Richard Dzinyela, Solomon Owusu-Ansah, Dickson G. Asiedu, Armstrong Aboah

entry.summary: This work tackles text-based person anomaly search where training uses synthetic image-text pairs but evaluation happens on real surveillance images. The framework adapts Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B with bidirectional contrastive learning, explicit negative sampling, false-negative masking, and domain randomization, then fuses multiple retrieval models and applies cross-encoder reranking. It is a competition-style engineering pipeline for a surveillance retrieval task.

entry.title: DS-BiCA-Net: Pair-Preserving Cross-Temporal Modeling for Remote Sensing Change Captioning

author.name: Licheng Zhang, Naveed Akhtar, Siew-Kei Lam

entry.summary: Proposes DS-BiCA-Net for remote sensing image change captioning, which separates intra-image and cross-temporal processing and introduces explicit bidirectional paths for each temporal direction. This disentangled design preserves source-image identity and allows attribution of which modeling component drives performance.

entry.title: Distortion-Aware Spatiotemporal Learning for Real-Time Wide-Angle Video Rectification

author.name: Lang Nie, Yihan Yang, Wenbo Nie, Hongguang Zhu, Yang Wei, Chunyu Lin, Bin Xiao

entry.summary: FastVC performs real-time full-body rectification of wide-angle video via distortion-aware spatiotemporal learning, including a thin-plate spline module with peripheral-dense control points grounded in lens physics. It addresses gaps of prior face-centric, compute-heavy, temporally unstable methods.

entry.title: Are Textual Residuals Truly Complementary? Learning Visual Complements under Semantic Superposition for Visible-Infrared Person Re-Identification

author.name: Xiaoyang Li, Mingming Lu, Wei Zhou, Hao Li, Canhui Zhang

entry.summary: The paper revisits the assumption that textual residuals are visually complementary in text-enhanced visible-infrared person re-identification, showing dense textual differences entangle useful appearance variations with redundancy. It proposes Superposition-Aware Residual Calibration to transform textual differences into selective, visually grounded complements.

entry.title: Monte Carlo-Based Indoor UAV Localization in Dynamic Environments Using Only Four Onboard Range Sensors

author.name: Mohammad Reza Ranjbar Divkoti, A. Pedro Aguiar

entry.summary: The authors propose AF-MCL, an augmented filtered Monte Carlo localization method for indoor 2D UAV positioning using only four single-point range sensors and measured heading. The method rejects inconsistent range measurements against a static map and adaptively injects particles to recover from divergence and kidnapping, with ray-casting cost independent of particle count. Real-world experiments in a small test environment achieve mean position errors of 6.4-7.7 cm while providing an online uncertainty estimate.

entry.title: Mech Interp is a La Croix of Actual Safety Research

author.name: William Klett

entry.summary: The author, a mechanistic interpretability researcher, reports being convinced by Stephen Casper that much mech interp research is interesting but low-utility for actual safety, analogous to replication-crisis-era psychology: novel correlation findings without actionable payoff. The post argues the field should redirect from finding surprising features toward work with direct safety utility. It is a provocative field-level critique from an insider.

entry.title: Spatial Heuristic Strategy based Diffusion Reinforcement Learning for Online 3D Bin Packing

author.name: Tong Li, Qingyang Xu

entry.summary: The authors combine diffusion-based reinforcement learning with spatial heuristic strategies for online 3D bin packing, aiming to fix limited perception of spatial topology and weak layout optimization in prior diffusion RL approaches. The work targets better generalization and adaptability than rule-based heuristics in dynamic packing scenarios.

entry.title: StarRTT: An End-to-End Real-Time Framework for Blind Zone-Free RTT Prediction in Starlink LEO Satellite Networks

author.name: Jaeyong Lee, Seongjin Jeong, Yusang Park, Hyunho Hwang, Sangmin Han, Wonjae Shin

entry.summary: Develops an end-to-end framework combining per-second serving-satellite identification with round-trip-time prediction in Starlink-like LEO satellite networks, eliminating the identification blind zone that limits real-time prediction. Addresses RTT fluctuations caused by frequent handovers in mega-constellations. Relevant to networking and satellite communications rather than core AI research.

entry.title: Conditional Neural Processes for Self-Supervised Goal Discovery in Action Imitation

author.name: Marco Gabriele Fedozzi, Yukie Nagai, Francesco Rea, Alessandra Sciutti

entry.summary: Evaluates whether Conditional Neural Processes can autonomously learn action representations informative of underlying goals, inspired by infant imitation learning. Adding an attention mechanism in the hidden space fosters early-emerging robust goal representations, suggesting promise for self-supervised robotic general learners. A concise robotics/cognitive-AI exploration.

entry.title: Cross-Architectural Feature Fusion for Coronary Artery Stenosis Detection in X-ray Angiography

author.name: Haobo Zhu, Mojtaba Lashgari, Jason Chai, Giovanni Luigi De Maria, Vicente Grau, Abhirup Banerjee

entry.summary: Fusion-YOLOv11-L combines a YOLOv11-L detector with a UNet++ pretrained on the ARCADE vessel segmentation dataset via a channel attention gating module, fusing semantic and vessel-aware structural features for stenosis detection in X-ray angiography. The goal is more reliable localization than detection-only pipelines.

entry.title: Patronizing and Condescending Language Detection in English and Mandarin

author.name: Xinyi Vicky Xiang, Catherine Qingyun Wang, Paula Cort\'es Lemos

entry.summary: The paper builds classifiers for detecting patronizing and condescending language (PCL), a subtle form of harmful speech directed at vulnerable groups, in both English and Mandarin. Comparing CNN-based static embeddings with fine-tuned BERT embeddings, the BERT approach performs better, reaching an F1 of 0.528 on the development set.

entry.title: Generalized green and red concepts for artificial intelligence, big data, and information and communication technologies: Multidimensional framework and countermeasures

author.name: Jinsong Wu, Yixin Xiao, Haowei Bi, Huamin Fang

entry.summary: This position paper proposes generalized green AI and generalized red AI frameworks that extend beyond computational efficiency and carbon emissions to lifecycle trade-offs, service-versus-use impacts, and broader sustainability externalities, grounded in data-center electricity and AI water-demand projections. It aims to give more comprehensive guidance for sustainable AI deployment. It matters as sustainability of AI scaling becomes a first-order concern.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Space Data Centers: A Key Paradigm for Future Non-Terrestrial and In-Orbit Services

author.name: Peng Hu, Mustafa Alhassan, Amjad Iqbal

entry.summary: This position-style paper introduces heterogeneous space-based data centers composed of large and small nodes with differing compute, size, and power budgets to serve ground, aerial, and in-orbit users. It defines use cases, node sizing and placement strategies, and interconnection topologies, analyzing solar power provisioning for dawn-dusk LEO configurations. It sits at the intersection of falling launch costs, AI compute demand, and orbital infrastructure.

entry.title: Analysing Austrian Parliamentary Speeches by Predicting Party Affiliations

author.name: Sarah Sulollari, Vanja Karan, Benjamin Roth

entry.summary: Uses a fine-tuned BERT model to predict party affiliation from Austrian parliamentary speeches and aggregates predictions to analyze political behavior. Notably, it treats mis-assignments as informative signals rather than errors, finding that governing parties converge in speech characteristics while opposition parties diverge. A solid computational social science application of NLP.

entry.title: PoKER: A Probability of Kill Estimation Rate Model for Air-to-Air Missiles Using Machine Learning on Stochastic Targets

author.name: Joao P. A. Dantas, Andre N. Costa, Diego Geraldo, Marcos R. O. A. Maximo, Takashi Yoneyama

entry.summary: PoKER is a machine learning model that predicts probability-of-kill for beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile engagements, replacing static weapon engagement zone models with dynamic estimates that account for stochastic target behavior, miss distances, warhead lethality, and orientations. This provides finer-grained engagement analysis for combat simulation and decision support. It is an applied defense-domain ML contribution.

entry.title: DualGSL: Prior-Guided Graph Structure Learning with Node-Adaptive Prediction Fusion

author.name: Yuxia Sun, Yutszyuk Wong, Huihong Chen, Longhao Lv, Chang-Dong Wang, Li Zeng

entry.summary: DualGSL proposes a graph structure learning framework for transductive node classification that learns node-specific gates to fuse predictions from a feature-prior branch and a task-adaptive learned-structure branch, with virtual class nodes injecting label information. It addresses the fact that the predictive value of priors versus learned relations varies per node.

entry.title: Acoustic and Lexical Signals for Native Language Identification of Language Learners

author.name: Ahmet Yavuz Uluslu, Mengjie Qian, Kate Knill, Mark Gales

entry.summary: The authors compare a WavLM-based audio classifier with a zero-shot GPT-4o transcript-based classifier for identifying a speaker's native language from learner English, evaluated across CEFR proficiency levels. They find the audio approach outperforms transcripts overall, but relative strengths vary with learner proficiency, providing insight into where L1 traces reside.

entry.title: From Promises to Accountability: Comparative AI Modeling and Visualization of Electoral Commitments in Nepali Political Texts

author.name: Prakash Poudyal, Nischal Karki, Amrit Dahal, Rajani Chulyadyo, Sameer Tamrakar, Bal Krishna Bal

entry.summary: This work builds a system for election commitment mining in Nepali political texts, structuring promises from manifestos and campaign materials to enable public accountability tracking. It addresses a real gap in developing South Asian democracies where campaign commitments are rarely archived or systematically analyzed.

entry.title: Polyp-VSSD: A Pre-trained Transformer with Local-Global Joint VSSD Decoding for Polyp Segmentation

author.name: Xiaobo Zhu, Shiwei Wu, Yu An, Yuechen Tao, He Sun, Song Zhang, Zhenyu Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Polyp-VSSD, a polyp segmentation framework combining a pre-trained Transformer backbone with a local-global joint VSSD decoding design that unifies global semantic modeling and fine-grained local reconstruction. It targets improved representation capacity and context integration for colorectal polyp segmentation in endoscopy.

entry.title: HEALPix-Based Implicit Neural Compression of Omnidirectional Images

author.name: Yulong Cheng, Youneng Bao, Junfeng Zhou, Mu Li, Jie Wen

entry.summary: The paper proposes a spherical overfitted implicit-neural-representation codec for omnidirectional images built on HEALPix, an equal-area pixelization that avoids equirectangular distortion and pole oversampling. It targets low-complexity real-time decoding for VR applications.

entry.title: Machine-Readable Operator Manuals over the ISO 11783 Network for Offline, Multilingual LLM Assistance

author.name: Timo Oksanen, Julius Gun

entry.summary: The authors build an offline tractor-side LLM assistant that synchronizes machine-readable operator manuals over ISO 11783 CAN bus networks, benchmarking Markdown, JSON, and XML transfer formats and evaluating open-weight LLMs on cross-lingual queries with human-validated scoring. A full manual transfers in 31 to 89 seconds over physical hardware.

entry.title: Interpretable Singing Emotion Recognition Using Acoustic and Vocal Technique Features

author.name: Fotini Kiriakopoulou, Vassilis Lyberatos, Spyridon Kantarelis, Athanasios Voulodimos, Giorgos Stamou

entry.summary: Proposes an interpretable singing emotion recognition framework built on a compact set of singing-specific descriptors spanning prosody, spectral features, phonetics, and vocal technique, using SHAP and Grad-CAM for explanation. Shows that singing-specific features reduce cross-singer variability and that vocal technique descriptors aid interpretability. A niche but careful interpretable-audio contribution.

entry.title: Exact Global Minimax Risk near Nonidentification

author.name: Kaiyue Yang, Yunan Wu

entry.summary: The paper studies squared-error estimation when a nuisance parameter is unidentified on a submodel but affects a vanishing target, giving sufficient conditions under which the critical-path minimax risk equals the exact asymptotic minimax risk. It characterizes an estimator attaining the leading constant uniformly, with the constant expressed via a bounded-normal decision problem.

entry.title: Cross-Scenario Controller Parameter Transformation from Real-World Driving Data through Flow Matching

author.name: Christian Zink, Maik Pfefferkorn, Eric Lenz, Felix Kallmeyer, Rolf Findeisen

entry.summary: The paper formulates adaptation of Adaptive Cruise Control parameters as a driver-individual scenario-to-scenario transport problem, training a flow-matching generative model to predict target-scenario controller behavior for unseen drivers from limited data. This enables more natural, driver-individual assistance using large-scale real-world driving data.

entry.title: ParaTaxe: a Suite of Tools for Processing and Publishing Multi-parallel Corpora

author.name: Olivier Kraif (LIDILEM), Cyrille Fran\c{c}ois (UNIL), Elnaz Jalilian (LIDILEM), Natacha Rimasson-Fertin (ILCEA4), Pascale Roux (XXI)

entry.summary: ParaTaxe is an open-source suite for processing and publishing multi-parallel corpora, including the AIlign multilingual-embedding-based aligner, a Python conversion and alignment pipeline, and a web interface for managing collections. It responds to the recurring problem that academic parallel corpora become inaccessible due to maintenance and funding gaps.

entry.title: A Regularity Condition Under Which a CPAB Transformation is a Diffeomorphism

author.name: Amit Aflalo, Oren Freifeld

entry.summary: Establishes a mathematical regularity condition under which continuous piecewise-affine based (CPAB) transformations are diffeomorphisms, building on recent work that removed computational bottlenecks for CPAB flows in higher dimensions. The result provides a theoretical guarantee for transformations used in temporal warping and nonrigid spatial deformation.

entry.title: SREdit: Scene Response Guided Appearance Editing for Projection Mapping

author.name: Yuqiao Xia, Yuchen Deng, Ziheng Chang, Bingyao Huang

entry.summary: SREdit combines LLM-based image editors with projection mapping by using measured scene response to guide appearance editing so that projector compensation can physically reproduce the edited result on a real object. This bridges digital editing tools and physical display constraints that standard editors ignore.

entry.title: From Perception to Pixels: Human-Derived Visually Distinct Colors for Improved Dominant Color Extraction

author.name: Uldana Shyndali, Nurdaulet Toleugaliyev, Kuat Zharykbayev, Zarina Abildasheva, Pakizar Shamoi

entry.summary: Builds a Human Color Dictionary from a perceptual experiment with 110 participants judging 120 colors, constructing a co-occurrence matrix and greedily selecting 64 perceptually distinct colors for dominant color extraction. The human-perception-based framework improves on RGB-based quantization for applications like image retrieval and design.

entry.title: Financial Context-Rich Strategy for Actor-Critic based Agents: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Stock Trading

author.name: Hrishikesh Singh, Aarti Sharma, Millie Pant

entry.summary: This paper applies deep reinforcement learning with actor-critic agents to stock trading, incorporating external context such as social sentiment, political instability, and economic shifts beyond price-based indicators. It argues conventional indicator-driven strategies miss market dynamism and proposes context-rich DRL strategies to address this.

entry.title: SKG in Practice: OOD Generalization Cases Across FourDomains

author.name: Jian An, Chaoshi Wu, Xinpan Luo

entry.summary: An engineering-oriented evaluation of the SKG inference framework across four out-of-distribution domains including mechanical systems, sim-to-real object detection, sequence modeling, and molecular dynamics. It reports large OOD gains over neural baselines, though some case results rest on single-run, tiny-sample experiments.

entry.title: Supervised Source Separation of Electric Vehicle Interior Noise Using a Hybrid Transformer Architecture

author.name: Philipp Diel, Zhuo Cao, Arne Hildenbrand, Marco G\"unther, Stefan Pischinger, Hanno Scharr, Steffen Marburg

entry.summary: This paper frames electric vehicle interior noise decomposition into wind, tire, powertrain, and auxiliary-drive contributions as a supervised binaural source-separation problem, adapting a hybrid time-spectrogram transformer. It aims to replace labor-intensive measurement campaigns and expert transfer-path analysis with learned separation for targeted acoustic engineering.

entry.title: The Language of Instruction: Genre and Generative AI

author.name: James E. Dobson

entry.summary: This humanities-oriented article argues that instruction-tuned language models should be understood as instantiating a new genre, termed the instructional-conversational genre, formed from recursive human-model conversations, system prompts, and role-based markup structures. It offers a conceptual framework from literary/rhetorical studies for thinking about how chat models shape discourse. The work is analytic rather than empirical.

entry.title: L0-Norm-Based CycleGAN for Unpaired Brain CT-to-MR Synthesis

author.name: Yunxiao Zhang, Shouqiang Du, Zexian Xu, Chuanlong Xu

entry.summary: This paper replaces the standard L1 cycle-consistency penalty in CycleGAN with a smooth L0-norm approximation for unpaired brain CT-to-MR synthesis, increasing sensitivity to small residuals while suppressing large ones. Medical imaging motivation is that paired CT/MR acquisition is often impractical.

entry.title: Hair Segmentation and Skin Characterization on Macroscopic Dermatological Images for Laser Treatment Parameterization

author.name: Alex Navarro Navarro, Marc Arriaga Hidalgo, Carlos Moreno Rubio, Maxime Talarmain, Noelia Vaquero Gallardo

entry.summary: The paper presents a YOLOv9-based pipeline for hair segmentation and skin characterization on macroscopic dermatological images to support objective parameterization of laser and IPL treatments, replacing subjective manual settings. Unlike prior dermoscopy-focused work, it targets realistic clinical imaging conditions.

entry.title: The effect of limb kinematics on the speed of a legged robot on granular media

author.name: Chen Li, Paul B. Umbanhowar, Haldun Komsuoglu, Daniel I. Goldman

entry.summary: This is a 2013 cross-listed study systematically characterizing how gait parameters and limb kinematics affect the performance of the SandBot legged robot on granular media like sand. It shows high performance occurs only in a narrow region of parameter space and develops predictive models for legged locomotion on yielding terrain, providing hypotheses for biological locomotors. The work predates modern learned locomotion and serves as a foundational empirical reference.

entry.title: Acquisition for Spherical-Linear Bayesian Optimization on the Cube

author.name: Nathan Wycoff

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the computational complexity of globally resolving acquisition subproblems for linear-surrogate Bayesian optimization over the unit cube, where the sphere case admits rapid exact acquisition. It presents both positive and negative complexity results and proposes an alternative to standard multi-start quasi-Newton acquisition optimization.

entry.title: Online Continual Learning in Edge-Cloud Applications

author.name: Charalampos Davalas, Dimitrios Michail, Christos Diou, Iraklis Varlamis, Konstantinos Tserpes

entry.summary: Proposes an edge-cloud methodology integrating continual learning with OOD detection (ODIN) and concept drift detection for IoT systems, so deployed models can adapt to non-stationary streams without catastrophic forgetting or full retraining access. It is an applied systems contribution for edge deployment reliability.

entry.title: Quantum-Classical Link Prediction on Dark Web Hyperlink Graphs

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Nov\'ak, Radovan Re\v{c}ka, Ond\v{r}ej Knebl, Aktham Youssef, Ivan Zelinka
