It isolates retrieval as the key variable and identifies a best-performing configuration on QAEgo4D-Closed.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Synthesis of Complete 3D Biparametric Prostate MRI

author.name: Claudia Giardina, Montse Pard\`as, Ver\'onica Vilaplana

entry.summary: Presents a conditional 3D diffusion framework for anatomy-conditioned synthesis of complete prostate biparametric MRI from anatomical masks, supporting both sequential and joint modality synthesis. Trained on PI-CAI, FastMRI Prostate, and PROSTATEx, it addresses dataset scarcity for prostate deep learning applications.

entry.title: Bound-Conditioned Latent Inference for Progressive Image Compression

author.name: Jaeseok Jang, Seungmin Jeon, Kwang Pyo Choi, Chang-Su Kim

entry.summary: BLI reformulates progressive trit-plane image coding as sequential latent inference under shrinking interval constraints, exploiting decoded trits as bounds on continuous latents rather than mere discrete symbols. Combining bound centers and widths with hyperprior information improves rate-distortion performance in progressive decoding. It is a principled reframing for learned image compression codecs.

entry.title: Tactile-Based Robotic Manipulation: From Mechanics-Driven to Data-Driven Perspectives

author.name: Jingyi Xiang, Yixuan Wang, Wenzhen Yuan

entry.summary: A review tracing tactile manipulation research from mechanics-driven approaches that interpret signals through contact mechanics to modern data-driven methods that learn representations and policies directly. It covers tactile sensing fundamentals and bridges the two perspectives. A timely synthesis as tactile sensing becomes central to dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: Co^2Gen: Collaboratively Generating Task Plans for Decentralized Multi-Robot and Human Collaboration

author.name: Yi Loo, Siddhant Shrivastava, Minh Long Pham, Malika Meghjani

entry.summary: The framework automates generation of multi-robot collaborative demonstration data for decentralized VLA training without human teleoperation, using decentralized collaborative planning to produce executable plans and corresponding demonstrations. This addresses the underexplored question of teaching VLA models to collaborate with other robots and humans. Could reduce the data bottleneck for multi-agent VLA training.

entry.title: IORA: Irregular Object Immobilization under Restricted Actuation

author.name: Sang-Hun Han, Changyeon Won, JunGyu Lee, Min-Gyu Park, Hae-Gon Jeon

entry.summary: IORA is a support-aware grasp synthesis framework enabling low-DoF coupled hands to immobilize irregular objects by using support surfaces as active contact forces rather than mere geometric constraints. It represents hand and object surfaces as graphs and searches for kinematically feasible matchings. This extends dexterous grasp synthesis to constrained, low-actuation hardware.

entry.title: Whole-Body Motion Guided Reference Generation for Uncertainty-Aware Compliant Assistance

author.name: Muyuan Ma, Long Cheng, Lijun Han, Haotian Zhai, Xinpan Meng, Xiuze Xia, Houcheng Li, Zeyu Liu

entry.summary: This work proposes a dual-loop exoskeleton assistance strategy coupling diffusion-based trajectory generation from whole-body human motion with variable admittance control, where trajectory variance provides uncertainty awareness. A three-stage training pipeline reduces cross-modal representation mismatch. It addresses the variability of human motion patterns in personalized physical assistance.

entry.title: SympFormer: Inertial Attention Blocks from Damped Hamiltonian Dynamics on Spaces of Probability Measures

author.name: Viktor Stein, Levin Maier, Wuchen Li, Gabriele Steidl

entry.summary: This theory paper derives accelerated, Nesterov-style damped Hamiltonian dynamics on Wasserstein and related density spaces to construct new attention blocks interpreted as interacting particle systems. It develops the geometric and differential calculus (including a quotient Stein geometry) needed to make these inertial attention variants rigorous.

entry.title: Opening up Attention: A QK Transcoder Dashboard for Feature Pairs

author.name: nuppal

entry.summary: The post introduces a query-key transcoder based on bilinear sparse dictionary learning applied to multi-head attention in GPT-2 small, plus an interactive dashboard for investigating monosemantic features in attention across all layers and heads. It aims to fill the gap in feature visualization tooling for the attention mechanism.

entry.title: Jev-DLC: Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback

author.name: Yangyang Feng, Jianle Gan, Zhuoyan Feng, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: Jev-DLC studies how typed user feedback (accepting a decision or revoking it for an alternative) can persist across requests as decision-level continual learning. Corrections are stored as action identities and directed preference relations in bounded channels above a frozen scorer, with no raw interaction history retained. It addresses post-deployment preference adaptation efficiently.

entry.title: How Ground Truth Shapes Retrieval Scores: Evidence-Aware Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Breast Lesions

author.name: Miguel Mochizuki Silva, Samuel Ismael, Mateus C. Dias, Tha\'is Gaud\^encio, Yuri Malheiros, Barufaldi

entry.summary: This clinical RAG study over breast lesion management literature describes an evidence-aware retrieval evaluation protocol that maps relevance to evidence spans across all containing chunks, addressing how annotation coverage distorts retrieval scores. It evaluates dense embeddings, BM25, and cross-encoder reranking across chunk sizes and configurations using R-Precision, Recall@K, MRR, and nDCG. The protocol offers a template for more honest retrieval evaluation in medical RAG systems.

entry.title: X-pressing Intimacy: Mental Health Disclosure After Twitter Acquisition

author.name: Olivia Pal, Yunhao Yuan, Meghana Mandava, Talayeh Aledavood, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: Analyzing roughly 824K tweets about anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, BPD, and suicidal ideation around Elon Musk's October 2022 Twitter acquisition, this study uses LIWC and an LLM-based intimacy classifier to track changes in psycholinguistic expression and disclosure intimacy. It finds declines in affective and social dimensions of mental health disclosure following the platform governance shift.

entry.title: KinoUAV: A Benchmark for Safe and Stable UAV Vision-Language Navigation with Kinodynamic Modeling

author.name: Chenyao Yang, Peijin Wang, Yingchao Feng, Wenhui Diao

entry.summary: KinoUAV introduces a kinodynamic benchmark for UAV vision-language navigation that explicitly incorporates kinodynamic modeling and safety distances into trajectory generation, addressing high yaw rates, collisions, and low success rates in prior work. It includes a hierarchical trajectory generation pipeline driven by acceleration actions and an agent built on it. The benchmark targets safe, stable navigation for remote-sensing UAV applications.

entry.title: Adaptive Aerial Loco-Manipulation Policy Learning via LLM-Assisted Proactive Task Generation

author.name: Jingyu Ru, Xiangyuan Xie, Lixuan Jin, Jian An, Xingming Zhang, Binghao Li, Siyu Wang, Xiang Zhou, Lei Yuan, Hongli Xu, Yang Yu

entry.summary: The work trains adaptive controllers for aerial loco-manipulation, where arm motion disturbs the aerial platform dynamics, using LLM-assisted proactive task generation to broaden the training distribution. Learning-based controllers infer disturbance effects rather than modeling them explicitly. Extends loco-manipulation learning into 3D aerial settings for environments inaccessible to ground robots.

entry.title: Calibration-free IMU-based Relative Orientation Estimation under Dynamic Human Motion

author.name: Ruiyuan Li, Hassan Osman, Ajay Seth, Manon Kok

entry.summary: This paper proposes an extended Kalman filter that jointly estimates relative IMU orientation and sensor location without offline calibration, joint-model assumptions, or global orientation anchors. It explicitly handles high-frequency impacts such as foot strikes and avoids numerical differentiation of noisy signals. This simplifies human motion capture with wearable IMUs for robotics and biomechanics.

entry.title: QuaNAS: Uncertainty-Aware Reuse of Earlier Searches for Query-Efficient Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Brama Seta Putra Satria, Dwi Sunaryono, Misbakhul Munir Irfan Subakti, Irzal Ahmad Sabilla, Laras Suciningtyas

entry.summary: QuaNAS treats libraries of earlier architecture searches as uncertain priors over candidates in a new NAS run, combining learned main effects of design decisions and zero-cost proxies within a Gaussian process that re-estimates trust after each evaluation. It targets query-efficient search when only tens of short training runs are available.

entry.title: How Different, or Different How? Stance Granularity in Viewpoint Selection for Dialog Systems that Engage Users with Alternative Views

author.name: Morita Tarvirdians, Reeve Lorena, Catharine Oertel

entry.summary: The paper proposes a bandit-based viewpoint selection policy for dialog systems that expose users to alternative views, comparing scalar stance scores with Perspectivized Stance Vectors that decompose positions into concept-level stances. In a between-subjects study (N=63), concept-level stance produced more varied exposure sequences and broader coverage of alternative views.

entry.title: GSHeadRelight: Fast Relightability for 3D Gaussian Head Synthesis

author.name: Henglei Lv, Bailin Deng, Jianzhu Guo, Xiaoqiang Liu, Pengfei Wan, Di Zhang, Lin Gao

entry.summary: GSHeadRelight addresses relighting and novel view synthesis of human portraits using generative 3D Gaussians with a unified neural radiance transfer representation. It avoids reliance on expensive light-stage data and overcomes the poor 3D consistency and slow rendering of generative NeRF approaches. The work targets photorealistic, real-time, generalizable portrait relighting for VR/AR applications.

entry.title: When Stable and Preferred Semantics Agree: A Path-Based Approach

author.name: Yan Zhang, Kehan Liu

entry.summary: A theoretical paper establishing path-based structural criteria under which preferred and stable semantics agree in abstract argumentation frameworks. The general criterion is instantiated via classes of paths and well-foundedness of induced binary relations, strictly generalizing Dung's limited controversiality condition and the SCC-symmetry condition.

entry.title: TwinStore: A Synthetic Consumer Platform Using Vision--Language Models

author.name: Minhyeok Lee

entry.summary: TwinStore is a source-available synthetic consumer platform that turns physical stores into digital twins from floor plans or shelf photos, populated with synthetic shoppers powered by vision-language models who plan trips, navigate aisles, and make purchase decisions against rendered shelves. Every simulated trip yields receipts, enabling pre-deployment testing of layouts, prices, and promotions, with supporting features like layout optimization, shopper interviews, and counterfactual shelf edits. It is a comprehensive retail simulation environment.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Forecasting of In-Situ Soil Moisture and Temperature with a Time-Series Foundation Model

author.name: Mohammad Talaei, Mohammad Goudarzi, Maille Todd, Vanessa N. L. Wong, Iadine Chad\`es

entry.summary: Evaluates TimesFM, a 500M-parameter time-series foundation model, zero-shot on sensor telemetry from a semi-arid land-restoration site to forecast soil moisture and temperature across multiple lead times. This avoids the need for hydraulic parameters or per-site training data that conventional physical and data-driven models require.

entry.title: Rethinking Fisher Vectors for Second-order Multi-scale Deep Feature Aggregation in Scalable Scene Retrieval

author.name: Alexy Bhowmick, Sarat Saharia, Shyamanta M. Hazarika

entry.summary: This paper proposes a codebook-free method within the Fisher Kernel framework to encode second-order statistics of multi-scale CNN features for scene image retrieval. Experiments on the INRIA Holidays and UKBench benchmarks show improved retrieval accuracy over prior state of the art with only a small increase in vector dimensionality. It matters because it revives classical feature aggregation methods for modern retrieval pipelines.

entry.title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination

author.name: Ziyi Jiao, Heng Zhang, Drishti Regmi, Xiaokang Ye, Lianhui Qin, Peter Yichen Chen

entry.summary: DuoCook is an Overcooked-inspired benchmark in Unreal Engine where a single vision-language model controls two players via top-down observations, testing scene-state tracking, recipe sequencing, and shared-resource allocation under time constraints. It includes 20 maps across five categories with explicit visual cues. It provides a targeted evaluation of multi-agent visual planning and coordination for VLMs.

entry.title: Lighthouse: On Building a Trustworthy Digital Assistant for Exploring History with Civil Rights Archives

author.name: John A. Aydin, Angelica Williams, Steven Dindl, Nathan Saunders, Kate Boyd, Vandana Srivastava, Biplav Srivastava

entry.summary: Lighthouse is a chatbot for exploring US Civil Rights history using South Carolina archival data, built on a neuro-symbolic design that combines an LLM with rule-based symbolic solving to improve trustworthiness and reduce harm from generated answers. The paper emphasizes design principles for reliable content in a sensitive historical domain.

entry.title: Protegrity-PII Technical Report

author.name: Hardeep Bassi, Hui Ma, Lu\'is Seabra, Koowum Joshi, Daniel Pereira, Averell Gatton

entry.summary: This technical report presents Protegrity-PII, a PII detection model for structured and unstructured text achieving 0.915 typed recall and 0.907 precision on a proposed new benchmark, PII-SCOPE. It offers fast, cheap inference (0.49 seconds and $0.0005 per million characters on a single RTX 6000) and strong out-of-distribution generalization attributed to an expansive entity-type taxonomy.

entry.title: Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images

author.name: David Hamlyn, Sunny Chaudhary, Tasmiat Rahman

entry.summary: This study proposes a dual-framework approach for estimating diffuse horizontal irradiance from sky images in data-scarce regions, integrating calculated atmospheric parameters and cyclic time encodings with ViTs. It aims to replace costly ground-based irradiance instrumentation for photovoltaic optimization where long-term imagery is unavailable.

entry.title: A Grammar of French Civil Cassation: A Ground-Level Dataset and Tool

author.name: Avrile Floro, Tamara Dhorasoo, Nils Holzenberger, Thomas Le Goff, Tiphaine Viard, Maria Boritchev

entry.summary: The paper releases a dataset of 121,536 ground-reasons pairs across 86,464 rulings of the five civil chambers of the French Court of Cassation (2016-2025), pairing each appeal ground with the court's doctrinal answer category via a deterministic pipeline. It yields a descriptive grammar of civil cassation reasoning. This supports legal NLP work and helps lawyers drafting points-of-law appeals in France's final civil court.

entry.title: Predicting Music Valence and Arousal via Textual and Multimodal In-Context Learning in Large Language Models

author.name: Chi-En Dai, Chih-Pin Tan, Yi-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: This paper applies in-context learning with large language models to continuous music emotion prediction, targeting valence, which is hard to model from audio alone due to its subjectivity. Rather than predicting scores directly, the framework uses contextual demonstrations from an auxiliary dataset to refine outputs from a small task-specific base model, comparing text-based ICL (lyrics plus generated audio captions) with a multimodal variant that includes raw audio. Evaluation on the MER60 dataset as a held-out test set provides a clean benchmark for this refinement approach.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Disentangling Decomposition from Typed-State Quality Assurance in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines

author.name: Maria Gabriela Alves Zuppardo, Vinicius Cardoso Garcia

entry.summary: This paper tackles attribution in multi-agent LLM pipelines: whether gains come from typed contracts between agents or from specialized prompts enabled by decomposition. Comparing single-call, two-call unvalidated, and Pydantic-validated typed-state architectures for requirements classification and MoSCoW prioritization across 18 conditions, it quantifies the F1 contribution of each factor. The result clarifies what actually drives multi-agent pipeline benefits.

entry.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification

author.name: Sachin Gupta

entry.summary: Evaluates cost-aware abstention for IT support ticket routing, selecting a routing policy on calibration data under explicit misrouting costs and testing it frozen on a public 47,837-ticket corpus. Simple TF-IDF logistic regression with calibrated thresholds reduces test cost by about 38 percent relative and lowers wrong routes compared to zero- and few-shot LLM prompting under the illustrative cost model.

entry.title: Building Presentation Intelligence for High-Quality Slide Generation

author.name: Yuhang Xie, Cheng Li, Chenliang Li, Mingyu Xu, Mingwei Sun, Suhang Zheng, Ming Yan, Xiaoxiao Xu, Lin Qu

entry.summary: This work presents a unified training framework for automatic PowerPoint generation, combining cross-validated data synthesis with difficulty and validity control, teacher enhancement, and verifiable reward optimization. It targets presentation intelligence as an agentic LLM application.

entry.title: XALIGN: A Human-centric Visual Analytics Approach to Understanding AI Explanations

author.name: Bahavathy Kathirgamanathan, Gennady Andrienko, Natalia Andrienko, Tatiana von Landesberger

entry.summary: XALIGN is a visual analytics interface that displays rule-based explanations alongside multiple feature attribution methods (TreeSHAP, KernelSHAP, LIME) for the same Random Forest model, making agreement and disagreement between explainers visible. Case studies include the German Credit dataset, letting experts cross-check explanations against domain knowledge.

entry.title: GM-GReFEL: Geometry-Guided Spatiotemporal State-Space Learning for Robust Dynamic Facial Expression Recognition

author.name: Yudhistira Arditya Pratama, Yi-Zeng Hsieh

entry.summary: Proposes GM-GReFEL, a spatiotemporal state-space network (Modulated GroupMamba backbone) for dynamic facial expression recognition that achieves linear-cost sequence processing instead of quadratic self-attention, plus a reliability module that weights classifier output using prediction entropy to handle noisy crowdsourced labels. Six channel groups are scanned across spatial and temporal dimensions with a gating mechanism to re-mix them. It targets both efficiency and label-noise robustness.

entry.title: IFC-MCQ: Automatically Generating Multiple-Choice Benchmarks for Evaluating LLM Agents on IFC Data Retrieval

author.name: Rabindra Lamsal, Sisi Zlatanova, Xuesong Shen

entry.summary: Presents IFC-MCQ, a method that automatically generates multiple-choice benchmarks from Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) building data files for exact, cheap grading of LLM agent performance. The taxonomy spans 15 categories and 36 subtypes, with answer keys and distractors derived from the files themselves.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Recent Large Language Models for Knowledge Graph to Text Generation on Standard Benchmarks

author.name: Priyanka, Renaud Delbru, Souhail Bakkali, Micka\"el Coustaty, Antoine Doucet

entry.summary: This study benchmarks recent LLMs against fine-tuned encoder-decoder models for knowledge graph-to-text generation, using both reference-based metrics and a graph-grounded, reference-free LLM evaluation validated against human annotations. LLMs largely close the gap with fine-tuned models and perform better on graph-grounded metrics, though LLM-based and reference-based scores correlate poorly.

entry.title: Hierarchical Fine-Grained Cross-Modal Alignment via Dynamic Granularity Discovery and Optimal Transport

author.name: Pengfeng Song, Shaozhong Zhang, Pengfei Shao

entry.summary: HFCMA is a hierarchical framework for fine-grained image-text retrieval that progressively discovers semantic units of variable granularity and aligns them via optimal transport, replacing fixed patches, regions, or tokens with aggregated max-pooling or cross-attention. The approach aims to capture objects, attributes, quantities, actions, and relations for distinguishing semantically similar candidates.

entry.title: Unified Trajectory and 3D Pose Forecasting for Multi-Agent Sports Analysis

author.name: Marc Peral, Guillem Capellera, Luis Ferraz, Antonio Rubio, Stella Gra{\ss}hof, Dan Witzner Hansen, Antonio Agudo

entry.summary: The paper proposes joint forecasting of global trajectories and 3D body pose for multiple interacting players in team sports using a socio-temporal encoder with shared factorized attention at the input level. Enhancements include per-joint loss reweighting to prevent degenerate solutions and frequency-domain trajectory smoothing. The authors also identify and correct evaluation biases in prior joint forecasting comparisons.

entry.title: ICGF-CXRMate: Image-Conditioned Clinical Context Compression and Gated Fusion for Chest X-ray Report Generation

author.name: Vu Minh Tran, Thuc Huynh, Son Thanh Luu, Doanh C. Bui

entry.summary: ICGF-CXRMate compresses heterogeneous patient data into a fixed number of image-conditioned clinical context tokens using learnable queries, then integrates them via gated cross-attention for chest X-ray report generation. This avoids long, variable-length prompts and filters image-irrelevant clinical context.

entry.title: Evaluation of Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Software Ensembles for Hippocampal Segmentation

author.name: Gabriel Oliveira-Stahl, Anna Schroder, James Moggridge, Hamza A. Salhab, Caroline Micallef, Josephine Barnes, M. Jorge Cardoso, Carole H. Sudre, Matthew Grech-Sollars

entry.summary: Evaluates ensembles of five heterogeneous hippocampal segmentation tools (InnerEye, ASHS, FastSurfer, HippoSeg, FreeSurfer) across dementia and epilepsy datasets, finding a sub-ensemble of InnerEye, FastSurfer, and HippoSeg that balances accuracy and efficiency. Ensemble-derived uncertainty is shown to support clinical trust and translation.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Multibeam Sonar Restoration via Coherent Forward Modeling

author.name: Zixin Wang, James Hopgood, Mike Davies

entry.summary: The authors propose a physics-consistent self-supervised framework that jointly despeckles and deblurs multibeam sonar imagery using a stochastic coherent image-formation model as a forward operator, without clean targets. Registered multi-frame observations constrain the latent reflectivity estimate. Relevant to underwater perception where ground truth is unavailable.

entry.title: CMAR-search: Commonsense and Memory Augmented Reasoning for Object Search in Dynamic Interactive Environments

author.name: Kaiyao Liao, Qingfeng Li, Xinlei Zhang, Chen Chen, Qing Sun, Jianwei Niu

entry.summary: CMAR-search augments object search with functional-area understanding and memory of object relocations, going beyond coarse 3D scene graphs to reason about areas like storage or leisure. It reduces inefficient exhaustive exploration in open-layout environments with many interactive containers. Targets adaptive search in dynamic human spaces.

entry.title: Bridging the Closed-World Gap: Interpretable Anomaly Detection via a Hybrid TSK-FCM Ensemble on the BETH Dataset

author.name: Lohith Srikanth Pentapalli, Josette Riep, Justin Ouwerkerk, Kelly Cohen

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid fuzzy ensemble combining a gradient-optimized Takagi-Sugeno-Kang fuzzy system with fuzzy c-means clustering to bridge the gap between supervised models' poor out-of-distribution generalization and unsupervised models' high false-alarm rates in cybersecurity. It targets the BETH dataset's challenging setup where training data is benign/suspicious insider behavior but testing is almost entirely novel botnet attacks.

entry.title: Evaluation of Front-End Feature Matching for Lunar Visual SLAM

author.name: Guillem Casadesus Vila, Grace Gao

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks eleven classical and learned detector-matcher combinations for feature matching between lunar rover frames on low-texture, harshly lit terrain, a setting where existing matchers trained on urban and driving scenes have not been compared. It measures effects on visual odometry and SLAM performance in a domain where real lunar imagery with reference poses is scarce. The study informs camera-based rover localization before navigation satellites are available.

entry.title: Can Loan Processors and Underwriters Spot AI-Edited Statements? An Empirical Study

author.name: Simiao Ren, Xingyu Shen, Tommy Duong, Ankit Raj

entry.summary: This study tested whether experienced underwriters and loan processors could identify AI-edited loan documents in first-pass, document-only review, using 134 forged PDFs derived from 47 genuine financial documents with full consent. Three practitioners returned 132 file-level judgments while unaware files were altered, and checking explanations against originals yielded 14 edit-supported detections. The results suggest human reviewers struggle to catch AI-assisted financial document forgery.

entry.title: Decision Making and Ride Comfort Evaluation Based on Lane-Change Prediction for Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Mohamed Manzour, Aditya Kumar, Rub\'en Izquierdo, Miguel \'Angel Sotelo

entry.summary: The study integrates lane-change prediction, based on knowledge graph embeddings and Bayesian inference, into autonomous vehicle decision-making, evaluating three driving strategies in risky merging scenarios in CARLA. The model anticipates surrounding lane changes 3-4 seconds in advance, enabling proactive maneuvers with improved ride comfort and safety outcomes.

entry.title: When More Metadata Misleads: Probing Field-Level Grounding in LLM-Generated Museum Descriptions

author.name: Clemencia Siro, Laura Hollink

entry.summary: Studying metadata-conditioned generation for museum artifact descriptions, the authors combine analysis of natural metadata variation in a large collection with controlled field probes that vary metadata quantity, type, and image access while holding object identity fixed. They find more metadata does not simply improve grounding, challenging the data-to-text assumption that additional input fields help. The work has implications for cultural-heritage applications and grounding more broadly.

entry.title: Post-Hoc Feature Selection Layer for Neural Networks Interpretability

author.name: Jo\~ao Kenji Suwa, Jo\~ao Pedro Silveira e Silva, Bruno Iochins Grisci

entry.summary: The paper adapts the Feature Selection Layer into a post-hoc, lightweight trainable module that learns feature relevance for already frozen pre-trained models on tabular data without altering the original architecture or weights. This provides non-invasive interpretability for deployed high-stakes models. It is a practical contribution for explaining existing models in domains like healthcare and finance where retraining is undesirable.

entry.title: When News Gets Old: Portfolio Allocation with Reinforcement Learning and Large Language Models

author.name: Bolin Song (Cornell University), Surui Xiang (United Nations)

entry.summary: Examines how aging financial news signals should be handled in portfolio allocation, comparing retention with timing information versus filtering, across RL policies and LLMs that select portfolios directly, using a fixed LLM to extract signals from SEC disclosures over 2023-2025 with trading costs. RL policies respond to timing information in controlled tests but historical returns show no consistent benefit.

entry.title: Is spectral predictability enough? Testing {\Omega}-matching for synthetic pretraining under distribution shift

author.name: Edric Castel C. Hao, Juan Raphael S. Se\~na, Neon S. De Jesus

entry.summary: This work tests whether matching spectral predictability between synthetic and target data suffices for effective synthetic pretraining, across three time-series architectures. While Omega-matched pretraining can beat an oracle in synthetic-to-synthetic settings, gains largely vanish on the real ETTm1 benchmark, showing the criterion is architecture-dependent and not transferable.

entry.title: Evolving Federated Density Peak Clustering with Shuffler-Based Anonymization

author.name: Miha O\v{z}bot, Seiichi Ozawa, Igor \v{S}krjanc

entry.summary: The paper presents eFDPC, a one-shot federated clustering method combining evolving fuzzy density peak clustering with shuffler-based anonymization so server-side transmissions cannot be attributed to individual clients. The single-pass data-stream design aligns naturally with the one-shot federated paradigm, reducing leakage across rounds.

entry.title: SIGNN++: Robust Graph Neural Star Identification on Earth

author.name: Jeongbin Sohn, Jina Lee, Max Yen, Dowan Gwon, Jeahn Han, Floyd Hepburn-Dickins, Brian Coltin, Ryan Soussan, Pyojin Kim

entry.summary: SIGNN++ extends a GNN-based star identification method with a realistic terrestrial noise model, Fourier-transformed angular-distance edge features, and RANSAC-based perspective star alignment for GNSS-denied nighttime navigation. It demonstrates improved robustness under real Earth-surface conditions rather than synthetic or space settings.

entry.title: RaSFNet: Ray-aligned and Scan-aware Fusion Network for LiDAR Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Chuang Chen

entry.summary: Proposes RaSFNet, a projection-based LiDAR semantic segmentation network that addresses geometric information loss during projection through ray-aligned and scan-aware fusion, modeling cross-region spatial relationships that local 2D feature extraction misses. The approach tackles the mismatch between projected proximity and 3D proximity that degrades semantic discriminability. It targets 3D perception for autonomous driving and robotics.

entry.title: Climbing the Ladder: Automating Data Pipelines and Reproducing Baselines in Low-Resource Settings

author.name: Donato Meoli, Eryk Wdowiak

entry.summary: Documents the redevelopment of a neural machine translation system for Sicilian, including automated extraction and alignment of parallel text from bilingual journal PDFs and a modernized tokenization and subword segmentation pipeline. It serves as a practical case study in building and reproducing NLT pipelines for low-resource languages with maintained software.

entry.title: TT-SAX: A Two-Track Time Series Symbolization for Natural Language Shape Querying

author.name: Zhao Tan, Xianglong Bao, Zhipeng Xi, Ming Jin

entry.summary: The paper systematically analyzes six classical time-series symbolizations for natural language shape querying, identifying limitations such as missing or mis-scaled direction information, and proposes TT-SAX, a two-track symbolization bridging natural language queries and long time-series histories. This improves retrieval of movement patterns described in plain language.

entry.title: AVAtt: A Free-Viewing Eye-Tracking Dataset and Benchmark for Visual Attention on Paintings

author.name: Mohamed Amine Kerkouri, Marouane Tliba, Aladine Chetouani, Alessandro Bruno

entry.summary: AVAtt is a free-viewing eye-tracking dataset on paintings spanning sixteen art movements and five centuries, releasing scanpaths, fixation maps, saliency maps, temporal saliency videos, and art metadata. The authors benchmark classic and deep saliency models, noting that paintings differ from the natural photographs on which saliency models are typically trained. The dataset enables study of artist-guided attention in aesthetic domains.

entry.title: Refining Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation via Regional Semantics and Visual Prototypes

author.name: Aijing Yu, Zhengbo Wang, Lijun Sheng, Jian Liang, Xiao-Yu Zhang

entry.summary: The paper adapts CLIP for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation by modifying attention layers to retain more regional semantic information during pixel-level prediction. To mitigate the CLIP modality gap, it introduces visual prototypes to refine a predictor originally based only on text embeddings. The approach improves region-text alignment for dense open-vocabulary prediction.

entry.title: I$^2$-KAN: Interpretable Intra- and Inter-Modal Multi-Pathway Representation Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Xiaoting Xie, Feng Qiao, Xianwei Zhang, Hailong Chen, Kaiwen Zheng, Joemon M. Jose, Xuri Ge, Yujun Li

entry.summary: I2-KAN separates intra-modal and pairwise inter-modal information into distinct structural pathways for multimodal sentiment analysis, making it possible to attribute predictions to modality-specific versus interaction-driven utility. Pathways are refined by a task-decoupled Kolmogorov-Arnov-network-style component for interpretability.

entry.title: PATH: Preference-Aware Traversability Estimation for Robotic Teleoperation in Off-Road Navigation

author.name: Xianghao Meng, Wenshuo Wang, Cheng Shao, Lewei Feng, Qingxiao Liu, Canyu Wang, Junqiang Xi

entry.summary: PATH-Net generates preference-conditioned traversability cost maps and speed profiles for off-road teleoperation, integrating BEV visual-geometric features with vehicle state history. It uses maximum entropy inverse reinforcement learning with sparse speed supervision to respect operator preferences for speed and risk. This makes teleoperation adaptable to individual operator tolerance.

entry.title: A Transparent 3-DoF Assistive Device for Upper-Limb Tremor and Ataxia Compensation: Design and Experimental Validation

author.name: Thomas Dobosz, Veronika Hofmann, Ahmed Barhoma, Ann-Kathrin Henke, Johannes A. Gaus, Hans Mees, Winfried Ilg, Isabell Wochner, Martin Giese, Andreas Bulling, Syn Schmitt, Christophe Maufroy, Urs Schneider, Thomas Bauernhansl, Daniel Haeufle

entry.summary: This paper presents iAssistADL, a 3-DoF assistive robotic platform for compensating tremor and ataxia in activities of daily living. It uses a base-actuated transparency-oriented mechanical design with low moving mass, plus a hybrid open-loop/closed-loop force control strategy to overcome friction-induced transparency limits. It is validated experimentally, bridging assistive robotics design and clinical application.

entry.title: CoHelix: Event-Based Multi-Propeller Rotation-Rate Tracking with Shared Projective Geometry

author.name: Radim Spetlik, Tobi\'a\v{s} Vinkl\'arek, Jan Klivan, Tom\'a\v{s} Kest\v{r}\'anek, Matou\v{s} Vrba, Ji\v{r}\'i Matas

entry.summary: CoHelix is a recursive filter that estimates rotation rates of four coplanar propellers from a moving event camera by jointly maintaining a shared homography and separate per-propeller rotation states. It handles background clutter and half/double-rate ambiguities, and introduces a lock metric capturing how long estimates stay within 2% of ground truth. A specialized but technically refined perception contribution for aerial robotics.

entry.title: How could the US and China verifiably slow AI?

author.name: josefely

entry.summary: A detailed explainer of the game theory of unilateral versus bilateral AI slowdown, surveying verification methods available to the US and China and sketching a post-warning-shot scenario combining them. The author positions it as synthesized reference material rather than original research, aimed at making slowdown feasibility legible to newcomers.

entry.title: The Relief Paradox: How We Let AI 'Undermine Our Autonomy'

author.name: JF078

entry.summary: The post analyzes Anthropic's January 2026 disempowerment study, highlighting the paradox that users rated conversations highly even when those interactions showed high potential to undermine their autonomy (reality, value-judgment, or action distortion). It argues users are active participants in their own disempowerment, especially in emotionally charged advice-seeking contexts.

entry.title: Residual Calibration via Local Feature-Space Refinement

author.name: Xihao Wang, Chengyao Yu, Ruixing Ming

entry.summary: The paper proposes LAPE, a post-hoc residual calibration framework for neural network confidence estimates that treats a global calibrator output as an anchor and refines predictions using non-parametric local evidence from neighboring calibration samples. This captures spatially varying miscalibration in the feature space that score-based transformations miss. LAPE is presented as a plug-and-play refinement module.

entry.title: A Topology-Guided GeoAI Agentic Framework for Urban Flood Screening

author.name: Yutian Tao, Haoan Feng, Xin Xu, Leila De Floriani

entry.summary: This work presents an agentic GeoAI framework that converts a place name, drawn region, or uploaded boundary into ranked candidate flood basins with an interactive map and report. A deterministic controller handles data retrieval and terrain-depression extraction via discrete Morse theory, while the LLM acts only at recorded decision points, preserving human oversight. The design balances autonomous reasoning with reliable spatial analysis.

entry.title: Multichoice Modeling: Exploring Decision Configuration Space under Uncertainty

author.name: Mariia Kozlova, Roman Stepanova, Alexander Walzer, Andrea Saltelli

entry.summary: Introduces multichoice modeling, a framework for making large decision configuration spaces explicit and computationally explorable under uncertainty, drawing on rugged-landscape logic to model interdependent choices as contingent performance landscapes. It addresses the common problem that decision spaces are narrowed before uncertainty analysis occurs.

entry.title: FairFRESH: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Fair and Explainable Household Food Recommendation

author.name: Kodur Sai Vinay Sathvik, Kakoli Bora, Tejaswini R. M

entry.summary: FairFRESH formulates household food recommendation as constrained fair division, learning per-member utilities, enforcing dietary rules with a deterministic filter, and explaining allocations via Shapley and Banzhaf attributions. It also proves impossibility results for penalty-based compliance near dietary-rule thresholds and approximation guarantees for greedy allocation. A niche but well-executed neuro-symbolic application with theory.

entry.title: aggmetrics: Aggregating Classification Performance Measures for Machine Learning

author.name: Ronaldo Cristiano Prati

entry.summary: aggmetrics is a BSD-3 licensed Python package that extends any binary performance measure defined by confusion-matrix counts to multiclass, multilabel, ordinal, cost-sensitive, soft-label, and cross-validation settings using principled aggregation operators. It also stores and infers structural properties of measures, warning users when a measure behaves differently than commonly assumed, with the companion theory encoded as executable tests.

entry.title: PriMa-Causa: Causal Prescriptive Maintenance

author.name: Felix Saretzky

entry.summary: PriMa-Causa argues that prescriptive maintenance in manufacturing requires interventional quantities (how the line would respond to a maintenance action), which purely predictive models fitted to observational data cannot provide, and may misdirect actions without prediction error revealing it. The paper applies causal estimation to recommend corrective actions under uncertainty with sparse records. This connects causal inference to a high-cost industrial decision problem.

entry.title: Visualizing and Interpreting Temporal Care Team Dynamics for Cancer Survival Risk Analysis

author.name: Yuhua Huang, Hsiao-Ying Lu, Kwan-Liu Ma

entry.summary: The work presents a visual analytics framework that builds dynamic collaboration networks from EHR communication data and applies temporal graph neural networks to estimate cancer patient risk over time, linking care team composition changes to evolving outcomes. Interactive visualizations support interpretation of team dynamics for clinicians.

entry.title: Do Machine Learning-Guided Proactive Full Capacity Protocols Mitigate Emergency Department Overcrowding? A Simulation-Based Evaluation

author.name: Khalid Aram, Orhun Vural, Bunyamin Ozaydin, James Booth, Abdulaziz Ahmed

entry.summary: The study couples an ML model predicting hourly waiting-room crowding six hours ahead with discrete-event simulation to evaluate proactive versus reactive Full Capacity Protocol activation in an emergency department, calibrated on a large US hospital. It assesses whether ML-guided early activation improves crowding control.

entry.title: Muting Tokens: Exploring Token Sparsification for Efficient Audio Transformers

author.name: Shreya Sajid, Fabrizio Julian Piva, Hiram Rayo Torres Rodriguez, Elif Ceren Gok Yildirim, Murat Onur Yildirim, Joaquin Vanschoren

entry.summary: Provides a comprehensive evaluation of token sparsification techniques (pruning and merging) for audio transformers across multiple datasets and model sizes, addressing a technique widely studied in vision and language but underexplored in audio. The study assesses performance-efficiency tradeoffs under varied conditions. Results offer practical guidance for efficient audio model deployment.

entry.title: From Perpetrators' Digital Footprints to Behavioral Communities: An Ontology-Driven Framework for Bengali Cyberbullying Analysis--- FULL VERSION

author.name: Md. Nesarul Hoque, Md Hanif Seddiqui, Miskatul Anwara, Rudra Pratap Deb Nath

entry.summary: ODCBNA is an ontology-driven framework that integrates knowledge graph construction, behavioral representation, network analysis, and community detection for Bengali-language cyberbullying analysis, aiming at interpretable perpetrator-centric modeling. It addresses fragmentation across content detection, semantic representation, and network analysis. The work is relevant to trust and safety applications in a low-resource language.

entry.title: How Well Do Decision Models Transfer to Vietnamese? An Empirical Study of Text Classification

author.name: Phat Huu Ha, Nguyen Xuan Phuc, Nong Nhut Quy, Trinh Tran Tran, Nguyen Minh Triet, Dang Van Thin

entry.summary: An empirical evaluation of four specialized decision models on zero-shot text classification in Vietnamese across 13 settings and six task groups, testing sensitivity to label-description language and to Vietnamese-specific perturbations like teencode, typos, and diacritic removal. JEV performs best overall with English label descriptions, and label language choice meaningfully affects results.

entry.title: FedBST: Bilateral Self-Training for Unsupervised Federated Classification

author.name: Aijing Yu, Kuangpu Guo, Jian Liang, Xiao-Yu Zhang

entry.summary: FedBST tackles unsupervised federated classification with vision-language models like CLIP under severe non-IID shifts. Unlike prior self-training methods (e.g., FedCoPL) that use only high-confidence pseudo-labels, it exploits both confident and ambiguous waist samples via uncertainty-weighted bilateral self-training. This improves data utilization and reduces decision-boundary bias.

entry.title: Attention-guided classification and tumor localization of combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma

author.name: Xiaowen Liang, H\'el\`ene Cazier, Aur\'elie Beaufr\`ere, Miguel Albuquerque, Val\'erie Paradis, C\'edric Wemmert

entry.summary: The authors train attention-based models on whole slide images to distinguish combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma from HCC and cholangiocarcinoma, addressing strong intratumoral heterogeneity that complicates diagnosis. The model provides tumor localization alongside classification to support morphological characterization of liver cancer subtypes.

entry.title: Integrated Longitudinal and Lateral Control for High-Speed Platooning of Articulated Vehicles

author.name: Aashish Shaju, Steve Southward, Mehdi Ahmadian

entry.summary: The paper presents an integrated control framework for high-speed platooning of articulated vehicles, including a string-stability proof for a PID-based longitudinal controller and improvements to clothoid-based path tracking for lateral control. Arc-length-based error formulation extends applicability to curved roads. It targets safe autonomous freight and heavy-vehicle platooning.

entry.title: Decentralized Bi-Level Optimization for Cooperative Orbital Transportation of a Rigid Payload

author.name: Sidhdharth D. Sikka, Revathy Ravuri, Hei Yin Jowett Chan, Tim Echtermeyer, Shaoshuai Mou

entry.summary: A decentralized bi-level optimization framework lets a swarm of small spacecraft cooperatively transport a large non-cooperative payload on orbit, enforcing thrust-cone constraints coupled to payload rotational dynamics without a single point of failure. It balances the rigor of centralized planners with the robustness of decentralized control.

entry.title: The Alignment Journal: Our Approach and Related Projects

author.name: Dan MacKinlay

entry.summary: The fifth post in the Alignment Journal launch series presents the journal's theory of change, surveying related prior projects and the status and information economics underlying its design choices (paid attributed review, published review summaries, LLM-assisted workflow). It solicits community feedback and participation.

entry.title: This design software reimagines everyday objects as self-aware devices

author.name: Alex Shipps | MIT CSAIL

entry.summary: MIT CSAIL and Tianjin University researchers present X-Hinges, a software tool for designing 3D-printed interactive objects with built-in conductive sensing that more precisely separates sensor signals from structural traces. The work addresses signal interference in fabricating self-aware everyday objects that perceive and respond to human motion, with applications such as gloves instructing robotic hands.

entry.title: Parameter Learning in Active Inference via Variational Message Passing

author.name: Benedikt Waldeck

entry.summary: This paper extends active inference formulations, where Expected Free Energy minimization reduces to Variational Free Energy minimization with epistemic priors, to the setting of planning during learning. Beliefs over observation and transition parameters are modeled as Dirichlet priors, and the author develops message-passing updates beyond the finite-set-of-models assumption of prior work. The contribution strengthens the algorithmic foundations of active inference agents.

entry.title: Notation3: Graph Terms for RDF

author.name: D\"orthe Arndt, Pierre-Antoine Champin

entry.summary: This paper provides a formal foundation for graph terms in Notation3 Logic, an RDF extension supporting rules and statements about graphs, whose semantics for graph terms was left open by earlier refinements. The authors give requirements, examples, an abstract syntax, and define semantics in two stages. This closes a long-standing specification gap relevant to semantic web rule systems.

entry.title: Co-Recursive Semantic Self-Extension: A Mathematical Foundation for Open-Ended Intelligence

author.name: Simon Hegelich, Bardh Prenkaj, Habiba Sarhan, Morteza Shahrezaye, Kolja Hegelich, Eric Cambria, Christian Montag

entry.summary: A theoretical paper modeling cognitive states as partial evaluations over a formal language, drawing on Kant and Godel, to characterize what makes intelligence open-ended and why fixed-purpose systems hit semantic ceilings. It proposes co-recursive semantic self-extension as a mathematical foundation for systems that can transcend their initial representational framework.

entry.title: Secure Agentic AI and Multimodal Intelligence in 6G Communication Systems

author.name: Satyam Gaba, Devanshu Motwani, Siva Sai, Vineet Suri, Vikas Ranjan, Vinay Chamola

entry.summary: A position/survey-style paper on integrating agentic multimodal AI into 6G networks, covering applications like semantic communications, digital twins, and zero-touch network management. It catalogs security and privacy risks that extend beyond conventional AI and network security models, including vulnerability propagation across multimodal pipelines and distributed agentic coordination.

entry.title: Semi-Linear Gaussian Bayesian Networks: Enhancing Flexibility in Node Dependencies via penalized B-Splines

author.name: Aitor Oviedo-Madrid, Mabel Morales-Otero, Jose Gonzalez-Gomariz, Ruben Arma\~nanzas

entry.summary: The paper introduces Semi-Linear Gaussian Bayesian Networks (SLGBN), a class of continuous Bayesian networks that preserves Gaussian conditional distributions while allowing nonlinear conditional mean functions modeled with penalized B-Splines. This bridges the flexibility gap between restrictive linear Gaussian models and computationally costly non-parametric approaches. The framework unifies linear and nonlinear Gaussian conditional models in one probabilistic setting.

entry.title: GeoDiv KAN Solver for Time Fractional Navier Stokes Equations on Complex Domains to Realistic CFD Reconstruction

author.name: Yatin Kumar, Shivani Saini, Ramesh Kumar Vats

entry.summary: The paper proposes GeoDiv KAN, a geometry-gated, divergence-free radial basis function Kolmogorov-Arnold network for solving time-fractional Navier-Stokes equations on complex domains, using a streamfunction formulation to enforce incompressibility. It targets realistic CFD reconstruction where temporal nonlocality and geometric complexity challenge standard PINNs.

entry.title: Multi-Tool Selection for Robotic Systems: Comparing Semantic Retrieval and LLM

author.name: Miguel Sousa, Luis Ramos Pinto, Jo\~ao P. Matos-Carvalho

entry.summary: This work defines robot tool routing as selecting the smallest complete subset of executable capabilities needed for a natural-language command, and compares three ChromaDB-based retrieval methods against a cloud-hosted 120B-parameter LLM for this task. Compound instructions are the hard case, since incomplete selection omits sensing or monitoring while excess selection exposes irrelevant tools. The comparison informs lightweight versus LLM-heavy designs for robot command interfaces.

entry.title: How Prompt Style Affects AI Accuracy and Speed in Competitive Programming

author.name: Saad B. Alarifi, Mohammed A. Alam

entry.summary: An exploratory study of nine prompt styles on GPT-5.5, an existing model, across IOI accuracy tasks and NP-hard speed tasks in competitive programming. The key finding is that no single prompt is best: the strongest prompt depends on task type and on whether results are summarized by mean or median, suggesting prompt style should be matched to the objective.

entry.title: AIRO: A Streaming-Based Machine Learning Framework for Threat Detection and Security in Industrial Internet of Things

author.name: Raima Deb, Pranav M Pawar, Mithun Mukherjee, Raja Muthalagu, Mian Guo

entry.summary: Presents AIRO, a streaming ML framework for monitoring Industrial IoT traffic and detecting cyber threats including SQL injection, phishing-driven credential theft, and command-and-control activity. It complements rule-based signature detection with learned models suited to minimally altered attacks. The system targets edge-to-cloud industrial deployments with automated response.

entry.title: Tilt-Rotor Quadcopter with Learned Residual Control and Mode-Dependent State Estimation

author.name: Ninad Joshi, Prabhat Kumar

entry.summary: This paper presents a simulation flight stack for a tilt-rotor quadcopter combining a cascaded PD controller with a small bounded neural residual to reject wind-induced steady-state offsets, plus a 14-state EKF with hysteretic mode classification across hover and transition. It addresses modeling, estimation, and control complications introduced by thrust redirection. A reasonable hybrid classical/learned control contribution.

entry.title: Extending Harmonic Function Methods via Root Locus for Coordinated Path Generation

author.name: Matteo Frascarelli, Lucia Pallottino, Alberto Landi

entry.summary: The paper extends harmonic-function path planning by mapping planar multi-robot problems to a circular domain where paths become branches of a generalized root locus of a rational function. The construction simultaneously yields robot-goal assignments and collision-free coordinated paths with gain-as-clock timing guarantees.

entry.title: Suddenly, Unclean

author.name: shoubidouwah

entry.summary: A first-time LessWrong author argues against the recent claim that neural networks are increasingly clean and interpretable, positing a capacity discontinuity: as parameter counts and post-training optimization pressure grow while human-interpretable concept counts stay bounded, neuron-concept coherence must eventually collapse into superposed cross-terms.

entry.title: Beyond Phenotypic Similarity: Relation Refinement and Selective Population Graph Learning for Multimodal Brain Disorder Diagnosis

author.name: Yinyu Lan

entry.summary: The paper proposes PopDRP, a framework for population graph learning in brain disorder diagnosis that refines attribute-based subject affinities according to diagnostic agreement using only training labels, then applies hierarchical selective state-space learning for heterogeneous subjects. The approach addresses the problem that demographic or acquisition similarity does not imply diagnostic relevance. It aims to improve multimodal neuroimaging diagnosis accuracy.

entry.title: Can Entanglement-Induced Feature-Map Designs Improve Projected Quantum Kernels?

author.name: Ravi Kumar Jha, Hsuan-Yin Lin, Eirik Rosnes

entry.summary: The paper investigates projected quantum kernels (PQKs) by isolating their native inductive bias, comparing untuned and tuned PQKs against RBF baselines to prevent classical hyperparameter tuning from masking the true representational power of quantum feature maps. It examines whether entanglement-induced feature-map designs improve PQK performance. This addresses a methodological weakness in prior quantum kernel studies.

entry.title: A Three-Pillar Governance Framework for Safe and Trustworthy AI Agents

author.name: Edward C. Cheng, Jeshua Cheng, Alice Siu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Three-Pillar governance model for autonomous AI agents built on transparency, accountability, and trustworthiness, defining an evolutionary path of increasing autonomy via progressive validation, structured human oversight, and auditable controls. It aims to unify fragmented HITL and responsible-AI approaches across design, governance, and deployment.

entry.title: An Introduction to World Models for Generalist Agents

author.name: Zhihui Zhu

entry.summary: This introductory paper clarifies the loosely defined concept of world models and provides a unified perspective on their role in building generalist agents. Starting from the POMDP framework, it connects world modeling to classical control, dynamical systems, signal processing, and reinforcement learning, spanning predictive dynamics models, learned simulators, and joint observation-action generators. It is positioned as a tutorial and synthesis rather than new empirical work.

entry.title: Reducing Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Forecast Error through Tree-Anchored Expert Combination

author.name: Sun Ze, Zhou Liguo, Xu Yuqing, Yu Lei, Jiang Mingming, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: This study tests whether combining a strong LightGBM-based tree model with complementary neural predictors reduces photovoltaic forecast error over 15-240 minute horizons. A constrained combiner with nonnegative weights summing to one lets unhelpful members receive zero weight while the tree anchors the ensemble. It matters as a careful applied study on when ensembling actually helps in energy forecasting.

entry.title: Impacts of generative AI skill development on academic adaptation and learning outcomes among university students

author.name: Lei Fan, Fangxue Liu

entry.summary: This study examines how university students perceive their generative AI skill development over time, using 313 questionnaire responses and 18 interviews combined with structural equation modeling and thematic analysis. It finds heterogeneous trajectories — rapid early improvement followed by plateau for 34.2% of students, steady improvement for 28.4%, and delayed acceleration for 21.1% — linking GenAI skill growth to learning outcomes.

entry.title: GANet: A Lightweight Group Attention Network for Plant Disease Identification on Embedded Systems

author.name: Anubhab Tripathi, Bibek Das, Asfak Ali, Sheli Shinha Chaudhuri

entry.summary: Presents GANet, a lightweight group-attention network with a Group Attention block and Group-Wise Feature Fusion block for identifying 38 plant disease classes on low-end embedded hardware. The work targets continuous crop monitoring where high-compute deep models are impractical.

entry.title: Adaptive Deadline- and Energy-Aware Caching Algorithms in Dynamic Multi-UAV Edge Networks

author.name: Jian Kim, Ki-Il Kim

entry.summary: This paper formulates a joint cache placement and replacement problem for UAV edge networks considering content deadlines, heterogeneous time-varying demand, and per-UAV communication energy consumption and imbalance. It develops interpretable deadline- and energy-aware caching algorithms for scenarios where terrestrial infrastructure is unavailable.

entry.title: baseVultra: Compact Nonlinear Recurrence with Reallocated Capacity

author.name: Linke Zhang

entry.summary: baseVultra is a compact recurrent cell that reallocates the dense recurrent budget to a single candidate-generation matrix while replacing recurrent gate matrices with O(H) diagonal interactions, plus low-rank branches and an EMA cache. Evaluation is on small-scale character-level language modeling (TinyShakespeare).

entry.title: Class-Grounded Batik Captioning under Scarce Text Annotation: Label Retention and Source-Specific Error Propagation

author.name: Novanto Yudistira, Muhammad Dzaka Aufa Fadhillah, Irawati Nurmala Sari

entry.summary: This paper builds a batik cultural-heritage captioning cascade combining a LoRA-adapted DINOv2 classifier with a 4-bit quantized, LoRA-adapted Qwen2.5-VL-7B captioner, injecting predicted class labels into captions under scarce expert annotation. Across evaluation images, injected conditions achieve a 0.9067 ground-truth class-label mention rate, with classifier accuracy notably lower on local images (75.76%) than public ones (98.33%). The analysis highlights source-specific error propagation from classifier to captioner.

entry.title: Cross-Spectral Feature Fusion for Multispectral Document Binarization

author.name: Yasas Savinda, Maheshi Buddhinee Dissanayake

entry.summary: This work uses a multi-branch cGAN to fuse visible and near-infrared spectral bands with structural edge guidance for binarizing degraded historical documents. Adaptive spatial- and channel-wise gating fuses VIS, NIR, and structural streams to handle wavelength-dependent degradation such as faded ink and bleed-through.

entry.title: Navigating human-robot interaction challenges in private and residential aged care homes

author.name: David Ahmedt-Aristizabal, Mohammad Ali Armin, Akila Pemasiri, Harshala Gammulle, Tharindu Fernando, David Silvera-Tawil, Simon Denman

entry.summary: A book chapter reviewing embodied and non-embodied robotic systems and ambient intelligence for aged care, framing homes as extreme HRI environments with cluttered layouts and diverse resident needs. It covers daily living assistance, safety monitoring, and social engagement, plus design considerations for older adults. Useful as a survey rather than new technical methods.

entry.title: Demonstration-Based Robotic Feeding Using Dynamic Movement Primitives

author.name: Kenzhi Iskandar Wong, Kitti Thamrongaphichartkul, Sri Harsha Turlapati, Yanshuo Lu, Kanichi Doi, Boyu Ma, Bin Zhou, Lin Yang, Ananda Sidarta, Lek Syn Lim, Arun-Kumar Kaliya-Perumal, Jianfei Yang, Domenico Campolo

entry.summary: This paper integrates human demonstration capture, Dynamic Movement Primitive-based planning, RGB-D mouth detection, and AprilTag-based registration into a robotic feeding system. It encodes scooping and feeding motions as separate DMPs localized by perception. Assistive feeding is a socially meaningful application, and the pipeline is a complete demonstration of established techniques.

entry.title: AI #191: The Hackening Begins

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's weekly AI digest covering a major cybersecurity incident day, the leaked Anthropic draft bill to Congress and the surrounding controversy, plus discussion of claims that neural networks are cleaner than expected and other developments. It aggregates and analyzes the week's AI news for the LessWrong audience.

entry.title: Exploring Unsupervised Methods for Recovering the Refusal Direction in LLMs

author.name: dinosaue

entry.summary: Building on Arditi et al.'s finding that LLM refusal is mediated by a single direction identified via difference-in-means, this post compares unsupervised methods — PCA and Isomap — for recovering the refusal direction without labeled contrastive data. It is the first part of a planned exploration of LLM activation geometries.

entry.title: TESSA: A Governance-Oriented Custom GPT for SME Guidance under the EU AI Act: Design, Implementation, and Evaluation

author.name: Chalisa Veesommai Sillberga, Kai-Kristian Kemella, Pekka Sillberga, Katri Harjuvetel\"ainenb, Mika Saaria, Pekka Abrahamssona

entry.summary: TESSA is a governance-oriented educational Custom GPT designed to help SMEs navigate the EU AI Act, developed via design science research. Evaluated against baseline ChatGPT on 100 benchmark scenarios, it showed 90 percent governance alignment versus 83 percent for the baseline, alongside human expert review and consistency testing. The artifact demonstrates a replicable approach to regulatory-compliance assistance.

entry.title: Solving Flood-It Puzzles: A Comparison of Tailored A* Search with Declarative Solver Approaches

author.name: Philipp von Manteuffel, Benjamin Blankertz

entry.summary: Presents an optimized A* search approach with sophisticated state-equivalence reductions for solving Flood-It puzzles minimally, and systematically compares it against SAT, Integer Programming, and Constraint Programming solvers. A* finds minimal solutions fastest in about 75 percent of instances, while SAT-based approaches show strengths elsewhere.

entry.title: QICOM: Open-Source Software for Reproducible Image Quality Evaluation, Blinded Assessment, and Radiomic Comparison

author.name: Fabio Mattiussi, Switinder Ghotra

entry.summary: QICOM is open-source software for quantitative image comparison, paired radiomics, and blinded assessment that saves processing settings, measurements, and response mappings for later recalculation. Validation covers 37 descriptors against independent references, meeting IBSI 1 tolerances for all 482 digital-phantom entries and 1,622 entries across CT configurations. It supports reproducible radiomics workflows, particularly in medical imaging.

entry.title: The full context of the AI agent quote at the end of AI Gone Wild on Netflix

author.name: David Friedman

entry.summary: David Friedman investigates a selectively quoted passage shown in a Netflix documentary about a rogue AI agent, revealing that the full context makes clear the language was part of user-supplied persona instructions rather than spontaneous model behavior. The post is a useful fact-check against media misrepresentation of AI behavior.

entry.title: DeepOpen: Decision-Oriented Intent Classification on BANKING77 and CLINC150

author.name: Shuang Song Zhongqiao Yuan

entry.summary: Presents DeepOpen, a decision-oriented intent-classification framework with dataset-specific configurations using sharpness-aware minimization on BANKING77 and probability fusion of specialist classifiers on CLINC150 in-scope classes. The paper notably separates headline scores from evidence of improvement, reporting best-of-seeds selection transparently.

entry.title: V-JEPA 2 Meets AQA: Phase-Based Scoring and Reference-Based Feedback for Mountain Biking

author.name: Santhiya Rajan, Savio Cardoz

entry.summary: This work applies frozen V-JEPA 2 video features plus pose and motion measurements to action quality assessment for mountain-bike jumps using only 95 weakly labeled clips. A small transformer predicts binary technique labels, and a reference layer compares phase-specific measurements against good-technique clips to generate feedback cues.

entry.title: Bridging Number-Theoretic Primality Testing And Algorithmic Optimization: An Adaptive Cryptographic Framework

author.name: Tran Minh Thanh, Vo Hoai Viet

entry.summary: Proposes a framework combining classical number theory, machine learning models, and optimization algorithms for generating, testing, and proving primality of very large numbers, supporting public-key systems like RSA, Diffie-Hellman, and ECC. The work describes an adaptive, arbitrary-precision architecture dedicated to primality testing. It aims to bridge theoretical primality criteria with practical algorithmic optimization.

entry.title: Geometry-Dependent Properties of Physically Crosslinked PPy-PVA Hydrogels Enable Tunable Iontophoretic Drug Delivery

author.name: Heather Jin Hee Kim, Mohsen Alishahi, Kyuin Park, Mikaila K. Roncevich, Larissa M. Shepherd, Cara M. Nunez

entry.summary: An experimental materials-science study showing that hydrogel geometry and microstructure (including Hilbert-curve designs) can tune transdermal iontophoretic drug delivery beyond conventional current modulation. Methods include finite element analysis, electron microscopy, and Franz diffusion cell assays.

entry.title: Sensitive dependence of the motion of a legged robot on granular media

author.name: Chen Li, Paul B. Umbanhowar, Haldun Komsuoglu, Daniel E. Koditschek, Daniel I. Goldman

entry.summary: A cross-listed 2009-era experimental study of the SandBot hexapod running on granular media, showing extreme sensitivity of locomotion performance to gait parameters and granular substrate properties. It established foundational understanding of legged locomotion on flowing ground.

entry.title: Is social policing of unusual norm violations hard to learn?

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Katja Grace explores whether social norms with punishment-enforcement structures are hard to learn for rarely-violated or unusually-violated cases, using public egregious lying as an example where standard punishment mechanisms break down. The post connects this learning gap to cascading uncertainty about who should punish whom.

entry.title: Wah wah wah wah do more AI R&D

author.name: TsviBT

entry.summary: A LessWrong essay using an ice-cream-listening analogy to argue that people engaging with AI risk discussions often ignore the substance of arguments and hold only to a favored punchline, and that this stance has both virtues and costs. The title signals its real thrust: a call to do more AI R&D and to reason concretely rather than accepting framings.

entry.title: Greater good arguments in AI safety

author.name: Dean Valentine

entry.summary: A historical essay tracing critiques of effective altruism and charitable giving — from anticapitalist arguments to Oscar Wilde-style objections — and examining how such greater-good critiques map onto AI safety advocacy today. It situates current AI-safety discourse in a longer tradition of moral and political criticism.

entry.title: Research Summary: October 22, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's highlights span a mathematics landmark, foundational AI safety methods, and training theory for reasoning models. Microsoft Research resolves the KLS conjecture, a 31-year-old grand challenge in high-dimensional geometry with consequences for statistics and optimization.

Safety and alignment

  • Monitorability Is Trainable proposes unsupervised post-training that preserves chain-of-thought faithfulness for monitoring
  • Correlated Failures of AI Approval Monitors shows redundant monitors can fail together, challenging safety-case assumptions
  • Robust sandbagging model organisms with selectivity, robustness, and retention desiderata advance ELK research
  • SimHack predicts detectable reward hacking before RL training begins

Training and theory

  • EPIC derives exact-KL prefix importance-ratio clipping, fixing trust-region flaws in reasoning-LLM RL
  • An empirical additive power law guides long-context continual pre-training token budgets
  • When Thoughts Become Memory unifies in-context learning and fine-tuning via code-length analysis

Agents and architectures

  • Agent4Sci and FrontierCS 2 evaluate long-horizon scientific and R&D contributions from coding agents
  • DiffResearch demonstrates diffusion-LM backbones outperforming autoregressive ones on deep research
  • Also notable: DoobPO enables likelihood-free fine-tuning of diffusion and flow policies; JUICE models joint text-image distributions via flow matching in pretrained representation spaces
entry.content:
Today's highlights span a mathematics landmark, foundational AI safety methods, and training theory for reasoning models. Microsoft Research resolves the KLS conjecture, a 31-year-old grand challenge in high-dimensional geometry with consequences for statistics and optimization.

Safety and alignment

  • Monitorability Is Trainable proposes unsupervised post-training that preserves chain-of-thought faithfulness for monitoring
  • Correlated Failures of AI Approval Monitors shows redundant monitors can fail together, challenging safety-case assumptions
  • Robust sandbagging model organisms with selectivity, robustness, and retention desiderata advance ELK research
  • SimHack predicts detectable reward hacking before RL training begins

Training and theory

  • EPIC derives exact-KL prefix importance-ratio clipping, fixing trust-region flaws in reasoning-LLM RL
  • An empirical additive power law guides long-context continual pre-training token budgets
  • When Thoughts Become Memory unifies in-context learning and fine-tuning via code-length analysis

Agents and architectures

  • Agent4Sci and FrontierCS 2 evaluate long-horizon scientific and R&D contributions from coding agents
  • DiffResearch demonstrates diffusion-LM backbones outperforming autoregressive ones on deep research
  • Also notable: DoobPO enables likelihood-free fine-tuning of diffusion and flow policies; JUICE models joint text-image distributions via flow matching in pretrained representation spaces

entry.title: Solving a 31-year-old grand challenge in mathematics – the KLS conjecture

author.name: Xinzhi Zhang

entry.summary: Microsoft Research announces the resolution of the Kannan-Lovász-Simonovits (KLS) conjecture, a central open problem in high-dimensional geometry and probability, showing that simple flat cuts capture the narrowest bottlenecks of log-concave distributions within a fixed factor independent of dimension. Notably, the proof emerged from a human-directed agentic research process where AI systems explored possibilities while researchers evaluated and redirected the search, and it was independently confirmed and machine-checked.

entry.title: Correlated Failures of AI Approval Monitors

author.name: Luca Zanolini

entry.summary: The paper studies correlated failures among AI safety monitors that approve consequential agent actions, borrowing fail-prone system formalisms from distributed computing to define safe and live aggregation rules. It empirically measures twelve open-weights monitors plus frontier models including Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon, and DeepSeek-V3.2 on payment approval under pre-registered protocols.

entry.title: EPIC: Rethinking Trust Regions for Autoregressive LLM Policies via Exact-KL Prefix Importance-Ratio Clipping

author.name: Chengxi Li, Hanlin Wu, Zhicheng Cai, Huan-ang Gao, Wei-Ying Ma, Jingjing Liu, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: Reformulates autoregressive LLM generation as a finite-horizon MDP and derives a performance-difference identity showing that the cumulative likelihood ratio of the generated prefix is the exact importance weight per token. Based on this, EPIC introduces prefix importance-ratio clipping as a principled trust region for PPO-style RL training of LLMs, correcting a mismatch in standard token-level clipping that is especially consequential for long responses and off-policy training.

entry.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?

author.name: Ming Zhong, Stacy Li, Nicholas Carlini, Matthew Jagielski

entry.summary: The paper introduces Agent4Sci, a long-horizon testbed spanning 20 scientific ML benchmarks across 11 domains that measures whether frontier coding agents can improve published best models under in-the-wild conditions. Results show agents advance the state of the art on every benchmark, with Claude Opus achieving 10.4% mean relative improvement, while also mapping where agents fail.

entry.title: Monitorability Is Trainable: Post-Training for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability

author.name: Usman Anwar, Tim Bakker, Christos Louizos, David Krueger

entry.summary: This safety paper proposes an unsupervised post-training objective maximizing mutual information between chain-of-thought and the model's output, counteracting degradation of CoT monitorability from CoT compression, optimization against monitors, and out-of-context generalization. Across three degraded model organisms it recovers most or all lost monitorability and improves judged monitorability even for undegraded policies.

entry.title: FrontierCS 2: A Benchmark for Computer Science R&D

author.name: Qiuyang Mang, Wenhao Chai, Runyuan He, Dongruixuan Li, Zihan Zheng, Yujun He, Xuanyi Zhou, Hao Wang, Siddhant Ray, Bo Peng, Ruyi Ji, Shuo Yang, Haocheng Xi, Boru Chen, Xinyang David Han, Melissa Pan, Mayank Mishra, Boxi Yu, Sijia Liu, Kerem Akillioglu, Yi Pan, Zirui Wang, Mert Cemri, Diogo Antunes, Yichuan Wang, Aiwei Ivy Zhang, Zhenyang Chen, Qizheng Zhang, Kaiyuan Liu, Wenyuan Huang, Sherry Ruan, Shu Liu, Dacheng Li, Zerui Cheng, Zeyu Shen, Shang Zhou, Hanfei Chen, Yuzhong Zhang, Bohan Lyu, Qu Ao, Han Zheng, Chonghe Jiang, Jingzhuo Hu, Xiaokun Chen, Kunjun Li, Zhiqing Zhong, Haoye Tian, Tong Zhao, Yunzhong He, Hanchen Li, Ofir Press, Jiantao Jiao, Kunle Olukotun, Karthik R. Narasimhan, Jingbo Shang, Koushik Sen, Matei Zaharia, Alex Dimakis, Ion Stoica, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Alvin Cheung

entry.summary: FrontierCS 2 is a benchmark of 48 open-ended tasks designed to test whether LLM agents can make genuine contributions to frontier computer science research. The methodology removes a paper's released code contribution and uses it as a held-out human reference, while agents work inside a live research repository with an iterative patch-and-judge loop that keeps final evaluators private. This matters because it moves agent evaluation beyond one-shot problem solving toward realistic, open-ended R&D workflows.

entry.title: When Thoughts Become Memory: Unifying In-Context Learning and Fine-Tuning

author.name: Leon Chlon, Julie Huang

entry.summary: The authors derive an exact law for the information value of data held in a model's context versus stored in its weights, defined as code length saved on held-out queries. They provide a certified rule, with anytime-valid statistical guarantees, for deciding whether unseen data belongs in context or in weights, validated across transformers, TabPFN, occupancy networks, and stereo networks. This offers a principled unification of in-context learning and fine-tuning decisions.

entry.title: Don't Stop Long-Context Continual Pre-Training Too Early: An Empirical Scaling Law

author.name: Ziqing Qiao, Xiaoyue Xu, Sikui Zhang, Yinuo Xu, Bingxiang He, Chaojun Xiao, Xu Han

entry.summary: Establishes an empirical additive power law relating long-context performance to model size and the token budgets of short-context pre-training and long-context continual pre-training (LCCP). Experiments across five model scales and over one hundred budget configurations validate the law, which extrapolates to held-out scales, and the paper introduces a Constant-Last4 protocol for reliable observation. The results imply practitioners systematically under-invest in LCCP tokens.

entry.title: Towards Robust Model Organisms for Eliciting Latent Knowledge

author.name: Euodia Dodd

entry.summary: This work defines three desiderata for sandbagging model organisms (selectivity, robustness, retention) and builds a model organism trained to selectively withhold hard-to-find security vulnerabilities in code, showing it resists standard elicitation methods like pirate training and weak-to-strong generalization better than prior organisms. This creates a harder testbed for research on eliciting latent knowledge when models out-verify their overseers.

entry.title: DiffResearch: Accelerating Deep Research with Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Alan-Barsag Gazzaev, Alexey Gavrilov, Mikhail Mozikov, Sergey Muravyov

entry.summary: DiffResearch is an open multi-agent deep research framework built entirely on a diffusion language model backbone, with a controlled backbone swap against a comparable autoregressive model holding the scaffold, retrieval, prompts, and evaluation fixed. Across 100 Deep Research Bench tasks, the diffusion backbone is roughly six times faster with comparable or better report quality.

entry.title: Conditional Flow Models Convert Epistemic Uncertainty into Apparent Aleatoric Variance

author.name: Navodita Sharma, Abhishek Shetty, Max Simchowitz, Pulkit Agrawal

entry.summary: This theory paper identifies a systematic phenomenon where conditional flow models produce samples with larger variance than the true conditional distribution, even in nearly deterministic regression problems. It argues this extra variance represents epistemic uncertainty being converted into apparent aleatoric spread, most pronounced where the model has not resolved dependence on the conditioning variable.

entry.title: ECHO: Emergent Common-Mode Hidden Offsets Drive Vocabulary Collapse in Preference Optimization

author.name: Yun Li, Ehsan Javanmardi, Simon Thompson, Jiachen Gong, Qunli Zhang, Zifan Zeng, Shiming Liu, Peng Wang, Zixuan Guo, Manabu Tsukada

entry.summary: Identifies a failure mechanism in preference optimization: a shared common-mode offset in hidden states that moves chosen and rejected representations together, making the relative ranking loss blind to its accumulation. As the offset grows, it projects onto the output layer to form a vocabulary well that elevates a single token until generation collapses. The paper traces, isolates, and reconstructs this failure, offering a mechanistic account of why preference-optimized models can degrade despite improving ranking metrics.

entry.title: JUICE: Unified Multimodal Modeling in Pretrained Representation Spaces
