entry.summary: The paper shows that under Gaussian noise, UCB-style Gaussian process bandit algorithms can achieve near-optimal regret bounds using data thinning, a technique for creating independent datasets from a single dataset. This yields tighter confidence intervals and improves both simple and cumulative regret over classical GP-UCB analyses, unlike prior approaches that required non-adaptive methods.

entry.title: More Memory, Worse Agents: Error Reproduction and Anti-Persistence in LLM Agents

author.name: Ruhan Wang, Kishan Panaganti, Dongruo Zhou

entry.summary: Identifies error reproduction as a feedback mechanism in experience-based LLM agents: errors in stored abstractions propagate through retrieval and reuse, shape execution trajectories, and become the basis for new abstractions that reproduce the original errors. The paper analyzes this counterintuitive dynamic in which more memory can make agents worse, motivating anti-persistence design.

entry.title: Lost in Recovery: Demystifying Recovery Behavior of Computer-Use Agents via Goal-Oriented Action Replay

author.name: Byeonghun Bang, Sangwoo Park, Jinheon Baek, Kangsan Kim, Youngwan Lee, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: ReTrace is a scalable evaluation framework for studying recovery behavior in computer-use agents, where errors accumulate over long horizons and environment resets or full action replay are infeasible. It uses goal-oriented action replay to systematically probe how agents recover from failures with unintended side effects, a largely unexplored capability.

entry.title: Proof-Carrying Contracts: Commitments AI Agents Cannot Break

author.name: Carlo Ciliberto, Alessandro Rudi, Enrico Tassi

entry.summary: PC2 is a framework making agreed constraints enforceable on AI agents: before an operation runs, the agent must supply a machine-checkable proof that the operation preserves the constraints, rather than relying on trust or text policies. This supports a functioning agent economy where parties need not inspect each other's agents.

entry.title: MAS-Guard: Unified Guardrails from Individual Agents to Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Mohammad Kachuee, Phu Mon Htut, Sheng Li, Nikolaos Pappas, Miguel Ballesteros Martinez, Yassine Benajiba, Sujith Ravi, Dan Roth

entry.summary: MAS-Guard is a unified safety framework covering unsafe actions, information leakage, and adversarial manipulation across both single LLM agents and multi-agent systems, where distributed authority and potentially compromised participants complicate enforcement. It aims to close fragmented coverage across local execution, system-level interactions, and enforcement mechanisms. Given the rapid industrial adoption of multi-agent architectures, a unified guardrail framework is timely.

entry.title: Capable Teacher, Myopic Scorer: Reward-Free Teacher Repair for Agentic On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Shu Zhao, Tan Yu

entry.summary: This paper shows that the common compounding-error explanation for failures in agentic on-policy distillation is incomplete: the real problem is teacher next-token scoring myopia, where token-level scores mislead the student even when teacher takeovers from the same states succeed. The authors propose reward-free teacher repair to address this myopia in student training.

entry.title: Certified Sparse Attention via Perturbed Retrieval

author.name: Runguo Li

entry.summary: The paper shows that perturbing attention scores with independent Exp(1) noise turns threshold-based sparse attention retrieval into sampling keys proportionally to their weights, enabling nested samples, Horvitz-Thompson estimates, and simultaneous confidence bounds across a geometric grid of thresholds. Each attention head stops at the first level whose error certificate meets the target epsilon, with per-step failure probability control.

entry.title: Internalizing Chain-of-thought into Looped Transformers

author.name: Kehang Zhou, Pinyan Lu

entry.summary: Constructs constant-bit-size looped transformers that interpolate between explicit chain-of-thought generation and latent recurrent computation, simulating time- and space-bounded Turing machines with context and token budgets reduced by a factor of the loop count. Provides theoretical results on trading generated tokens against recurrence in hidden states.

entry.title: ProteinGeoBench: Frontier Structural-Biology Agents Are Fluent at Lookup but Lost in Geometry

author.name: Matt Turk, Brandon L. Neel, Diana M. Lopez, Zachary D. Smith, Grace N. Johnecheck, James B. Golden

entry.summary: Presents ProteinGeoBench, a 131-task protein-structure benchmark evaluated with over 8,700 rollouts across 30 models, showing frontier agents excel at metadata lookup but struggle with numeric geometric computation. Also studies how much benchmark scores reflect evaluation configuration rather than model capability.

entry.title: FisherEdit: Fisher Information Guided Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models

author.name: Yizhou Yang, Jiahong Fu, Zhiwu Wang, Kailong Fan, Haokun Lin, Yichen Wu, Zhenan Sun, Renzhen Wang, Deyu Meng

entry.summary: Revisits projection-based knowledge editing methods like AlphaEdit and finds their robustness stems mainly from update regularization rather than null-space projection. Based on this insight, FisherEdit replaces coarse activation-space projections with importance-aware regularization grounded in Fisher geometry, penalizing changes to sensitive parameters via an efficient row-wise closed-form solution.

entry.title: Competing Learning in Hybrid Architectures

author.name: Xingyu Shen, Yingfa Chen, Ziqing Qiao, Chaojun Xiao, Xu Han, Zhiyuan Liu

entry.summary: The paper reveals a Competing Learning phenomenon in hybrid language models combining linear recurrence and softmax attention: different mixer types compete to learn the same functions, and when one layer learns a function it suppresses learning signals in other layers. Attribution analysis shows modern recurrence learns retrieval functions faster than softmax attention under typical data distributions, with implications for how hybrid architectures should be trained.

entry.title: Auditing Tool Traces in Agentic LLMs: Source Localization and Counterfactual Dependence Testing

author.name: Junhao Liu, Tianxiao Li, Yongxian Wu, Ziheng Duan, Ren Li, Jing Zhang, Martin Renqiang Min

entry.summary: The paper introduces a two-stage audit for agentic LLMs in scientific prediction: PT2D localizes label-predictive patterns to individual tool results via per-tool TF-IDF decomposition, and token-class redaction counterfactually tests whether the frozen model truly depends on leaked shortcuts like dataset identifiers. Applied to biology tool traces, it exposes hidden label shortcuts that create apparent success without real reasoning. This targets a serious validity threat in agentic evaluation.

entry.title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds

author.name: Jihai Zhang, Runjia Qian, Kaiqin Kong, Biao Jiang, Puyi Wang, Siru Chen, Tianle Li, Guanjie Chen, Junyi Wu, Chubin Chen, Yuanhang Li, Kaichen Huang, Haobo Zhang, Yangguang Li, Wei Yu, Guibin Chen, Yu Cheng, Yahui Zhou

entry.summary: Matrix-Game 4.0 presents an architecture separating game execution from visual generation: a lightweight engine maintains world state and interaction rules, a multimodal coding agent translates player ideas into game code and scene captions, and an autoregressive video model renders low-poly proxies into detailed visuals. This achieves persistent world state, executable rules, and low-latency interaction for playable generated worlds. Part of the growing generative interactive worlds line of work.

entry.title: ACE-Brain-0.6: Scaling Spatial Grounding for Physical Foundation Models

author.name: Yinhe Wang, Tao Tao, Zexin He, Shuang Luo, Wei Mao, Yao Mu, Feng Pan, Hanming Deng, Lewei Lu, Zhi Hou, Xingang Pan, Dahua Lin, Dacheng Tao, Xiaogang Wang

entry.summary: ACE-Brain-0.6 scales visual spatial grounding to strengthen the perceptual foundation of general embodied operation, motivated by an analysis showing that general multimodal models like GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 exhibit strong spatial perception relevant to manipulation. The authors build a unified data pipeline combining robot manipulation recordings with diverse visual data, automatically annotated and converted into verifiable grounding signals. Note these are established models released in September 2026 rather than new launches. The large author team spans major academic groups and industry.

entry.title: Physical Canvas: A Vision Tactile World Model For Robot Policy Evaluation And Learning

author.name: Zebin Xing, Yuhang Zheng, Yupeng Zheng, Yichen Zhang, Zichen Li, Shangqing Zhou, Yujie Zang, Yuchen Liu, Zhongpu Xia, Haoran Li, Qichao Zhang

entry.summary: PhysCanvas is a state-consistent visuo-tactile world model for contact-rich manipulation that unifies multi-view RGB, tactile images, marker displacement, task state, and actions in a shared vision space using a common video VAE and pretrained generative backbone. By making contact dynamics explicit, it provides more reliable feedback than visually plausible but physically misleading predictions for policy evaluation and post-training.

entry.title: Solving the Ho--Nguyen Conjecture for Gaussian Mixtures: Applications to Mixtures of Experts

author.name: Yuyang Zhang, Qihuang Zhang

entry.summary: The authors resolve the Ho-Nguyen conjecture on the exact order of density cancellation in over-fitted Gaussian mixtures, proving the real nonzero-weight system has order 2M for every cluster size M via a sign-change rigidity bound and Gauss-Hermite quadrature construction. This sharpens parameter-learning rates for Gaussian mixtures and applies to mixtures of experts.

entry.title: Navalia: Advancing Cowork Agents through Verifiable Task Synthesis and Long-Horizon Post-Training

author.name: Hengqi Liu, Ziyuan Liu, Yang Qin, Wanting Zhou, Zichuan Wang, Jiachen Liang, Xu Chu, Shaowei Chen, Zhaokai Luo, Mu Chuan

entry.summary: Navalia is a framework that synthesizes verifiable analytical tasks from corporate financial reports by selecting evidence from complete fact sets and constructing executable computation chains, then uses these tasks for long-horizon post-training of cowork agents. It addresses the cost of expert task authoring and the unreliability of direct LLM task synthesis for multistep financial reasoning.

entry.title: Magnolia: A Persistent-Memory Agent Framework for Computational Chemistry

author.name: Tao Jiang, Benjamin Navet, Yousouf Taghzouti, Fabien Gandon, Louis-F\'elix Nothias, \'Elise Dumont

entry.summary: Introduces Magnolia, an LLM-based agent framework with a three-tier persistent memory system that integrates computational chemistry protocols (docking, quantum chemistry), lab notebooks, and chat logs to support chemists in a high-data regime. It matters because it applies agent memory architecture to a concrete scientific domain with growing automation needs.

entry.title: Unsupervised Tool Evolution for Coding Agents in Data-Lake Analytics

author.name: Yuqing Yang, Yurong Liu, Deqing Fu, Manav Garg, Sravan Babu Bodapati, Fatma Ozcan, Alon Y. Halevy, Jiani Zhang

entry.summary: TEAL enables coding agents answering analytical questions over data lakes to build and refine a reusable library of tools and usage skills without ground-truth labels, using an Explorer agent that mines the data lake and a Critic agent that mines worker trajectories for complementary tool-proposal evidence. This eliminates the repeated from-scratch work that current agents discard between questions.

entry.title: Correcting Attribution Patching with a Few Exact Measurements

author.name: Luyang Zhang, Minxing Zheng, Jialu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Guided-AP, a method that uses a small number of exact activation-patching measurements to correct attribution patching's gradient-based error estimates, exploiting structure in the errors: on a single prompt many components share an error sign, and across prompts of one task components are misestimated similarly. This restores accurate causal attribution at a fraction of the full patching cost.

entry.title: MemDev-Bench: Does Memory Help Code Agents?Benchmarking Memory Systems over Real Repository Histories

author.name: Guorui Chen, Tao Liu, Zhenzhen Huang, Yidan Zhang, Liyu Jiang, Shuoyuan Wang, Hanchen Sun, Xu He, Dong Li, Yihan Hu, Jianye Hao, Lei Feng

entry.summary: Introduces MemDev-Bench, which evaluates memory systems for coding agents over real, evolving repository histories with relevance-annotated prior tasks, enabling controlled measurement of whether reusing experience actually helps. It addresses shortcomings of existing benchmarks that lack temporally valid histories or control over prior-task relevance.

entry.title: RITE: Evaluating End-to-End Resilience to Silent Tool Errors in E-Commerce Agentic Systems

author.name: Wenshuo Zhang, Yuquan Lin, Yushi Sun, Yishi Lin, Rui Sheng, Peng He, Han Gao, Wang Jikai, Yifeng Rong

entry.summary: RITE is a benchmark built from human-authored industrial workflows and production logs that tests whether tool-using LLM agents can complete queries after silent tool errors corrupt intermediate states. It formalizes the Silent-error Resilience Task, addressing a realistic failure mode where plausible-but-wrong values propagate without explicit failure signals.

entry.title: Dancing Diffusion: Learning Continuous Programs for Image Generation and Editing

author.name: Cui Enhe, Jinyue Yang, Bojian Yin, Guoqi Li

entry.summary: Dancing Diffusion assigns each span of diffusion timesteps a dedicated continuous condition block, turning conditioning into a latent program compiled from text features and executed by a fixed pretrained generator. This enables trajectory-level editing: a shared prefix is executed once and reused while later operations are rewritten with earlier-fixed content preserved.

entry.title: Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity

author.name: Sahil Joshi, Prithvi Dixit, Aryan Katiyar, Agniva Chowdhury, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Anshumali Shrivastava, Aditya Desai, Kumar Krishna Agrawal

entry.summary: SSA is a unified sparse attention framework combining deterministic retrieval of high-scoring tokens with score-guided sampling to retain residual attention mass, closing the gap to dense attention at aggressive sparsity levels. This targets the KV-cache bottleneck in long-context LLM inference with better coverage than top-k or hybrid uniform sampling.

entry.title: Evolving Semantic Indexes for Generative Retrieval

author.name: Jinming Nian, Jyun-Yu Jiang, Henry Tsai, Yi Fang, Zhirong Liang

entry.summary: This paper introduces an LLM-driven evolutionary program search framework for improving generative retrieval, where search and recommendation are cast as autoregressive generation of discrete semantic identifiers. It uses a locally served open-weight 31B model to mutate executable retrieval components and a small 1M-parameter proxy decoder for fast feedback, avoiding proprietary APIs and costly retraining. The authors claim this is the first application of evolutionary program search to generative retrieval.

entry.title: Exploration via Activation-Space Steering for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Yunan Zeng, Jinhao Jing, Xi Cheng, Yuwang Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Activation-Space Exploration (ASE), an online method that diversifies RLVR training rollouts for LLMs by clustering activation differences between correct and incorrect responses and applying latent steering vectors to push the policy off repeated reasoning paths. This addresses rollout concentration under a fixed sampling budget.

entry.title: Evaluating Context Compaction on the Questions That Come Later

author.name: Junwei Yao, Yongxi Zhou, Zike Yang, Zhijun Wang, Jianan Liu, Yanxian Chen, Wenbo Ye

entry.summary: This evaluation asks whether context compaction methods, which select content for the current question, still serve future questions, comparing methods against random deletion at equal token budgets. Using the existing GPT-6-Luna model via the OpenAI Decisions API, the study finds that current-question selection gives an 11.4-point accuracy gain at 25% of tokens but no detectable benefit over random deletion on later questions. Word-level deletion shows different behavior, pointing to design implications for agent memory systems.

entry.title: Factual Access States in Diffusion Language Models: From Mechanism to Knowledge Editing and Retrieval

author.name: Yuchen Guo, Zhuoyuan Mao, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: This interpretability paper identifies a factual access state in masked diffusion language models, showing that unlike autoregressive models, the fact-lookup representation is assembled in the first attention layer by routing relation wording into the visible entity position. The finding informs knowledge editing and retrieval design for DLMs. As diffusion LMs gain traction, mechanistic comparisons with autoregressive models are timely and scarce.

entry.title: MoDDiT: Simple Token Routing in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Jarek Liesen, Matthew T. Jackson, Benjamin Ellis, Shimon Whiteson, Jakob N. Foerster

entry.summary: MoDDiT is a simple architectural modification to Diffusion Transformers that learns to route tokens independently through MLP and self-attention blocks, enabling dynamic per-token compute allocation that exploits the sparsity of natural images. This targets throughput bottlenecks in real-time video generation, interactive world models, and on-device synthesis.

entry.title: VGL-stGen: Learning a shared multimodal model for lung histology and spatial transcriptomics

author.name: Haenara Shin, Dongjoo Lee, Sungwoo Bae, Kwon Joong Na, Daeseung Lee, Hongyoon Choi

entry.summary: VGL-stGen adapts a pretrained medical vision-language model to jointly model lung histology images and spatial transcriptomics using paired data and single-cell references. A single checkpoint supports thirteen tasks including tissue and cell-type classification, gene prediction, and conditional expression completion. This unification of morphology and spatial gene expression is a meaningful step for computational pathology and precision oncology.

entry.title: Every Model Leaves a Trace: Multi-Resolution LLM Fingerprinting

author.name: Mohammad Reza Modarres, Armin Tourajmehr, Artin Tavasoli, Yadollah Yaghoobzadeh, Mohammad Taher Pilehvar

entry.summary: The paper systematically studies how detectable model-specific fingerprints are in LLM-generated text, introducing the notion of fingerprint resolution across model granularity (families, distilled variants, LoRA adapters) and signal types (behavioral, stylometric, lexical, semantic). Results show fingerprints persist even under paraphrasing, reduced text, cross-language shifts, and in distilled or LoRA-adapted models.

entry.title: UniWALM: Unified World Action Language Model for Embodied Robot Control

author.name: Rahul Sajnani, Diego Romeres, Mingyuan Zhang, Kai Gao, Carl Qi, Baichuan Huang, Srinath Sridhar, Dylan Randle, Lillian J. Ratliff, Jose Barreiros, Manikantan Nambi, Jeroen Vanbaar

entry.summary: UniWALM unifies video, action, and language in a single mixture-of-transformers backbone where each modality serves as both conditioning signal and supervision target, with per-modality diffusion heads co-denoising synchronously. Unlike staged VLM-plus-video-action pipelines, joint generation of language is tested as a way to enrich shared representations and support memory-dependent manipulation behavior.

entry.title: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhen Li, Mingfa Feng, Yiming Zhang, Yang Yu, Changhai Zhou, Pengxiang Li, Dongkuan Wu, Congkai Xie, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: miniTE tackles instability in RL training of LLMs with native 4-bit NVFP4 computation, showing that matching weights and formats across training and sampling engines is insufficient without aligning cross-engine numerical execution. It provides execution diagnostics, numerical alignment, and efficient W4A4 GEMM kernels, improving consistency without changing the RL objective.

entry.title: What Remains Without Test Labels? Re-evaluating a Graph-Level Anomaly Detection Benchmark

author.name: Yujie Lu, Da Yan

entry.summary: This benchmark audit examines whether results on the UB-GOLD graph anomaly detection benchmark, reused across many papers, depend on test labels for model selection despite detectors being trained label-free. Re-running 21 detectors across 14 code bases reveals test-label leakage in checkpoint selection adds an average of 5.12 AUROC points, and that kernel baselines were evaluated against misaligned labels. The paper quantifies how inflated prior reported performance may be.

entry.title: Measuring Empowerment from Offline Data for Intrinsically Motivated Exploration

author.name: Ishir Garg, Vivek Myers, Qiyang Li, Catherine Ji, Benjamin Eysenbach, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: This paper studies how offline prior datasets can guide exploration during online reinforcement learning by measuring empowerment — the number of future states an agent can realize — from offline data alone. It argues states with higher empowerment warrant more exploration and develops methods to estimate this from logged experience, with authorship including Eysenbach and Levine.

entry.title: Tensor Network Datamodels for Training Data Attribution

author.name: Farzaneh Heidari, Md Rifat Arefin, Louis Jaburi, Guillaume Rabusseau

entry.summary: Tensor Network Datamodels (TNDMs) extend linear datamodels for training data attribution using low-rank tensor networks to capture non-additive interactions among training units. The authors prove complementary and redundant training groups can induce high-degree subset functions with compact low-rank representations, and a single fitted TNDM supports attribution queries.

entry.title: Robust Direct Preference Optimization under Preference Label-Flip Attacks

author.name: Chenye Yang, Weiyu Xu, Lifeng Lai

entry.summary: The paper shows DPO is vulnerable to adversarial preference label-flip attacks steering the learner toward an attacker-chosen policy, and proposes Trim-K and Soft-Trim-K Robust-DPO defenses exploiting the fact that flips induce parameter-independent gradient shifts in log-linear DPO. It provides deterministic gradient perturbation bounds uniform over attack sets and presumably empirical validation.

entry.title: Improving the Expressive Power of Hybrid Sequence Models via Multi-Hop Retrieval

author.name: Yam Eitan, Gilad Yehudai, Haggai Maron

entry.summary: This paper theoretically analyzes the expressive power of hybrid language model architectures that combine full-attention layers with efficient sequence layers like sparse attention and recurrence. It investigates whether letting efficient layers access the attention KV cache improves expressiveness, and proposes a multi-hop retrieval mechanism to realize these theoretical benefits. This matters because hybrid architectures are a leading approach to efficient long-context modeling.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Last-Iterate Convergence of SGD in the Smooth Interpolation Regime

author.name: Matan Schliserman, Tomer Koren

entry.summary: This paper proves that the last iterate of SGD with constant stepsize achieves near-optimal expected excess risk on smooth convex objectives in the low-noise/interpolation regime, matching the Omega(1/T) lower bound up to log factors. This improves the previously known O(1/sqrt(T)) rate and holds for any constant stepsize below 2/beta. It matters because it closes a gap in the theoretical understanding of one of the most widely used optimization algorithms.

entry.title: ATEST: Adaptive Resource-Aware Test-Time Scaling for LLM Inference

author.name: Mobina Kashaniyan, Ali Jannesari

entry.summary: This paper introduces ATEST, a resource-aware test-time scaling framework that decides when to stop sampling additional LLM answers based on both the expected value of more samples and live GPU conditions. The authors show that energy cost for the same query can rise over 4-fold under GPU contention, and propose an online mode requiring no offline calibration that monitors answer stability and learns step energy costs on the fly.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs

author.name: Minglei Li, Peng Ye, Haonan He, Jingqi Ye, Qingyu Yang, Tao Chen

entry.summary: This large-scale empirical study establishes design recipes for applying parameter-efficient fine-tuning to mixture-of-experts LLMs, covering which modules to adapt, expert adaptation granularity, PEFT method choice, and load-balancing objectives across three MoE backbones. As MoE architectures become prevalent at scale, such systematic guidance fills a genuine gap. The findings should be directly useful to practitioners adapting large sparse models.

entry.title: Degree Bounds for Separating Polynomial and Neural Invariants for Point Clouds

author.name: Snir Hordan, Harm Derksen, Mircea Petrache, Nadav Dym

entry.summary: The paper establishes the first quadratic lower and upper degree bounds for polynomials that separate point clouds of n points up to rotations and permutations, and derives the first explicit quadratic bounds on the representation order needed for Tensor Field Networks and MACE to be universal. This answers a long-standing expressivity question for equivariant geometric networks. Such theory guides principled architecture choices in molecular and physical modeling.

entry.title: On Data Scaling in Tabular ML: More Data, Better Generalization?

author.name: Ivan Rubachev, Nikita Lazarev, Artem Babenko

entry.summary: This study assembles eight real-world tabular datasets with up to roughly ten million training examples, retaining natural distribution shifts, to systematically examine training-data scaling in tabular ML, an underexplored large-scale regime. GBDTs and MLPs show broadly similar scaling trends benefiting from more data and algorithmic improvements, while tabular foundation models exhibit more varied behavior with recent versions benefiting more consistently from larger contexts. The findings inform debates about whether tabular foundation models or classical methods should dominate large-scale tabular tasks.

entry.title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention

author.name: Anamaria-Roberta Hartl, Levente Z\'olyomi, Michael List, G\"unter Klambauer, Sebastian B\"ock, Sepp Hochreiter

entry.summary: The authors propose KronLSTM, a linear attention architecture extending the xLSTM family with a Kronecker Delta Rule update for associative matrix memories that revises targeted associations along a single matrix direction. This minimally invasive revision reduces interference with stored information, and memory dynamics are analyzable as a Markov chain with uniformly bounded expected memory norms, suited to long-context language modeling.

entry.title: Prefix-Tuning for Arbitrary Output Sequences on Pretrained Transformers

author.name: Peter Cho-Ho Lam, Ziyi Wang, Zirui Zhou

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical analysis of prefix-tuning expressiveness, proving that for any input-output pair where the target output lies in the range of a pretrained autoregressive Transformer, there exists a prefix that induces the model to generate that output. This closes an open question about the theoretical power of parameter-efficient prefix steering and offers a formal foundation for prompt-based control of LLMs.

entry.title: Blackbox Performance Analysis of LLM-based Network Control

author.name: Mahdi Alizadeh, Pooria Namyar, Arvin Ghavidel, Ramesh Govindan

entry.summary: This paper introduces LENS, a black-box auditing tool for LLM-enabled network control systems that extends deep reinforcement learning to search for performance gaps and failure-inducing inputs. The authors show LENS uncovers large gaps in LLM-based traffic engineering and GPU allocation systems, matching white-box analyzers built for hand-crafted heuristics.

entry.title: Over-Defense in Coding Agents Begins at Silent Forks

author.name: Hanjun Luo, Xuecheng Liu, Xiucheng Zhang, Zhuoning Xu, Yingbin Jin, Yankai Chen, Xue Liu, Hanan Salam

entry.summary: This paper identifies defensive over-expenditure in coding agents: unnecessary defensive actions occur at silent forks, turns where every possible next action leads to the same outcome, and frontier models take the disproportionate branch in up to 91 percent of decisive actions under implicit budgets. The authors show trajectory-level reward checkers fail to fix this because 74 percent of GRPO groups have identical rewards, motivating learning signals placed at decision points rather than outcome level.

entry.title: TILDE: Teacher-in-the-Loop Distillation from Embodied Foundation Models

author.name: Yuxiang Lu, Yantong Liu, Jinghua Hou, Xueli Sun, Ruihua Han, Zhe Liu, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: TILDE transfers manipulation capabilities from large pretrained embodied foundation models to smaller policies without action pretraining, combining on-policy distillation at student-induced states with teacher-executed recovery trajectories. Its AutoDAgger pipeline uses a robotic reward model to monitor task progress and trigger teacher intervention, collecting useful recovery data automatically.

entry.title: A Calibrated Instrument for Detecting Disposition Drift in Language Models

author.name: Jerry Kaplan

entry.summary: Jerry Kaplan adapts a calibrated measurement methodology to quantify how safety-relevant traits like deception, power seeking, and sycophancy drift as models are modified by fine-tuning, new data, or inference settings. Applied to several misalignment dimensions in two open-weight models, the instrument establishes measurement precision and enables error-aware interpretation of drift rates beyond single AI-scored summary statistics.

entry.title: Learning to Reason Efficiently with Interventional Step Credit

author.name: Guanda Li, Xuefeng Bai, Yulong Chen, Zhiyong Wang, Kehai Chen, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes interventional step credit (ISC), which estimates the causal contribution of chain-of-thought steps via targeted parameter-level interventions, unlike behavior-based signals such as attention mass or entropy. Builds IGPO, an RL method using ISC for fine-grained advantage rescaling to prune redundant reasoning steps while preserving accuracy.

entry.title: A Pitfall in the Evaluation of Gene Perturbation Models

author.name: George Panagopoulos, Saman Omidi, Tsz Pan Tong, Jun Pang

entry.summary: Shows under a unified protocol across eight methods and six single-gene perturbation datasets that Precision-based rankings on top differentially-expressed genes are highly unstable, with the winning method changing 86.7% of the time as the DE gene count varies. Identifies that repeating a single predicted profile across cell rows, a common practice, inflates evaluation metrics.

entry.title: VeriCUA: Learning Proactive Verification for Reliable GUI Agent Rewards

author.name: Zhizhou Wang, Yaxi Lu, Zhong Zhang, Zikun Hu, Xin Cong, Yankai Lin, Fangming Liu

entry.summary: VeriCUA addresses reliability of proactive reward verification for computer-use agents, where a verifier must decide what to check in a post-execution GUI and when to stop. The authors show prompted judges from 4B-scale to GPT-5.4 plateau at 68-70 percent agreement, because check value depends on environment dynamics learnable only through execution. They train a learned verification policy rather than relying on prompting.

entry.title: FlashMap: Flow Map Speculative Decoding

author.name: Jeff Shen, Zhejian Zhou, Ryan Lee, Jonathan May, Shirley Ho

entry.summary: Introduces FlashMap, a speculative decoding drafter using a continuous flow map language model conditioned on target hidden states to generate whole token blocks in one forward pass while capturing inter-token dependencies. Outperforms a matched DFlash diffusion drafter baseline on Qwen3-8B in speed.

entry.title: Ask Less, Ask Better: Allocating User Attention in Proactive LLM Agents with Interruption Budgets

author.name: Xuanming Zhang, Amir H. Rezaeian, Miguel Ballesteros, Weiyi Sun, Werner Geyer, Lydia B. Chilton, Zhou Yu, Yassine Benajiba, Dan Roth

entry.summary: This paper proposes an evaluation protocol for proactive LLM agents that distinguishes how often agents ask clarifying questions from how well they ask them. It introduces an interruption budget plus a user-attention cost that charges extra for hard-to-read or low-value questions, validated against human annotations with 75% agreement. This matters because question fatigue is a real deployment cost that standard question-count metrics ignore.

entry.title: DeGMatch: Target-Aware Reasoning Data Selection via Deconfounded Gradient Matching

author.name: Changho Lee, Janghoon Han, Rajdeep Mukherjee, Yeda Song, Lening Nick Cui, Xinya Du, Honglak Lee

entry.summary: The paper studies selecting long reasoning trajectories for targeted post-training, finding that existing gradient-matching methods struggle to discriminate target capabilities because dominant population-level gradient structure masks finer signal. DeGMatch constructs a target-relevance-controlled setup that deconfounds gradient matching, enabling more precise data selection for capability specialization.

entry.title: Deep Fusion Memory: A Chunk-Level Parametric Memory for Large Language Models

author.name: Rubin Wei, Siyuan Sun, Hao Sun, Yuliang Liu, Xiang Shi, Jiarui Wang, Junming Zhang, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: DFM is a parametric memory architecture where a causal memory predictor learns to generate memory representations from preceding context, supervised by retrieved chunk embeddings, with memory fused into intermediate hidden states rather than interpolated at output level. This reduces offline search burden for constructing memory-training data and avoids inference-time retrieval overhead.

entry.title: Aligning Cultural Behaviors in Arabic Language Models via Preferences

author.name: Junhong Liang, Daniil Orel, Saeed Almheiri, Bilal Elbouardi, Younes Samih, Abed Alhakim Freihat, Zhuohan Xie, Momina Ahsan, Muhammad Dehan Al Kautsar, Sarfraz Ahmad, Omar El Herraoui, Mohamed Anwar, Preslav Nakov, Fajri Koto

entry.summary: Introduces ArabPref, the first large-scale pan-Arab preference dataset for aligning LLM behavior with country-specific cultural norms, including a preference dataset in English and Modern Standard Arabic plus a multiple-choice benchmark. All test data is validated by native speakers, addressing a gap beyond factual instruction-tuning toward nuanced cultural behavior alignment.

entry.title: AdaExploreBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Proactive Exploration and Test-time Adaptation in Evolving Environments

author.name: Rui Wang, Zishen Lai, Jiayu Liu, Cheng Qian, Jeonghwan Kim, Heng Wang, Xuejun Zhang, Jiateng Liu, Bingxuan Li, Shujin Wu, Qing Zong, Tianshi Zheng, Chunyang Li, Qihan Lin, Chen Li, Dadi Guo, Xiusi Chen, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: AdaExploreBench tests whether LLM agents can proactively discover hidden environmental rules and adapt when those rules drift without announcement. Agents must infer latent dynamics from evidence and detect rule changes from degraded performance, capabilities existing benchmarks largely ignore.

entry.title: VEILED-SH: Vulnerability Expression through Indirect Language Evaluation Dataset (Self-Harm)

author.name: Leanne Tan, Keith Chua, Shaun Khoo, Onno P. Kampman, Lim Ruling Charmaine, Hazirah Hoosainsah, Kellie Yu Hui Sim, Kai He, Kenny Tsu Wei Choo, Roy Ka-Wei Lee

entry.summary: VEILED-SH is a 10,003-prompt benchmark evaluating single-turn AI responses to indirect expressions of suicide, self-harm, and distress across counselor chat, forums, search, and triage contexts, grounded in Singapore-based sources. It includes an expert-validated multi-label taxonomy and six automated evaluator profiles calibrated to practitioners and clinicians, addressing cultural variation and practitioner disagreement.

entry.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Preference Reward Models with Evolving Penalties

author.name: Afonso Baldo, Ant\'onio Farinhas, Marcos Treviso, Ricardo Rei, Nuno M. Guerreiro

entry.summary: The paper presents Dynalize, an online method that mitigates reward hacking in preference-based RL for language models by periodically using an LLM to analyze training rollouts and write penalties for undesirable behaviors the reward model inadvertently rewards. Evaluated on clinical counseling and creative writing, it targets open-ended tasks where verifiable rewards are not available.

entry.title: Axiomatic World Modeling for Physics Reasoning

author.name: Xinye Yang, Zhenyang Liu, Yuxuan Wang, Yuanyuan Lei

entry.summary: The paper identifies modeling drift in LLM physics reasoning, where models silently alter given quantities, fabricate laws, or inject unstated assumptions before reasoning within the corrupted problem. It proposes Reinforcement Learning with Axiomatic feedback (RLAA) to directly supervise world-modeling fidelity rather than only final-answer correctness, complementing RLVR and PRM. This targets a distinct failure mode from knowledge or execution deficits.

entry.title: MemDerive: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Agent Memory over Evolving Data

author.name: Sen Gao, Yongan Li, Han Chen, Bingsheng He, Ming Wu, Jason Zeng, Michael Heinrich, Shixuan Sun

entry.summary: MemDerive is a diagnostic benchmark for agent memory over evolving data where task state is derived from multiple records rather than stored explicitly. It uses Datalog to derive gold answers, records the derivation DAG and supporting events, enabling errors to be traced to missed intermediate states and detecting silently outdated state. This gives memory evaluation far finer-grained diagnostics than final-answer scoring.

entry.title: LoRASpace: A Pool-Wide Shared Substrate for Static and Dynamic Multi-LoRA Composition

author.name: Thamirawaran Sathiyalogeswaran, Navindu De Silva, Chamikara Siriwardane, W. K. Alwis, Jason Mars, Udaya Sampath K. Perera Miriya Thanthrige, Ranga Rodrigo

entry.summary: LoRASpace exploits the observation that stacked low-rank adapters in public LoRA pools span far fewer directions than their summed ranks. Using SVD-derived minimal subspaces, it composes multiple LoRAs in a single forward pass while avoiding the quality loss of naive merging and the linear cost of separate passes.

entry.title: RoboJudge: Multimodal Language Models as Judges for Embodied Video Generation

author.name: Siyuan Ma, Yu Qi, Cheng Ye, Ruotian Peng, Xinyi Xu, Zitiantao Lin, Zedong Cai, Yijian Huang, Weiyang Liu, Siyuan Wang, Yandong Wen

entry.summary: RoboJudge-Bench evaluates multimodal LLMs as judges of embodied video generation quality along Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment, using 800 human-annotated videos from 8 corpora and 10 video generators spanning grippers, human hands, and dexterous hands. Results show uneven alignment between MLLM judges and human judgments. This is important as video world models for robotics increasingly rely on MLLM evaluation.

entry.title: LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors

author.name: Kartik Tandon, Alessio Borgi, Pavel Snopov, In\'es Garc\'ia-Redondo, Davide D'Ascenzo, Sebastiano Cultrera di Montesano, Fabrizio Silvestri, Pietro Li\`o, Francesca Dominici, Randall Balestriero, Claudio Battiloro

entry.summary: LocaLeJEPA extends the LeJEPA self-supervised learning framework, which prevents representation collapse by driving embeddings toward an isotropic Gaussian, to non-Euclidean and domain-specific geometries such as equivariant CNNs and hyperbolic vision transformers. The authors ground the method in a manifold-theoretic reformulation of entropy maximization and introduce LocaLeReg, a locally Euclidean distribution regularizer. This matters because it generalizes a theoretically grounded anti-collapse technique to architectures where global Euclidean assumptions fail.

entry.title: Replan for Error Recovery: Training Embodied VLMs through Verifiable Interaction with Action-Grouped Turn-GSPO

author.name: Zhuoran Wang, Keqing Fan, Yang Li, Jinbo Su, Ke Wang, Sijia Luo, Yuanzheng Tan, Junken Peng, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces ERR-Env, an environment providing verifiable feedback on task progress and execution errors for training embodied VLMs to replan after failures, plus ERR-Bench with held-out tasks spanning nominal, intermediate, and error states. It then proposes Action-Grouped Turn-GSPO, a reinforcement learning variant enabling recovery learning from verified interaction outcomes rather than reference corrections. Error recovery is a recognized weak point of current manipulation policies, making this a timely contribution.

entry.title: HATCH: Hardware-Attested Task Chains for Verifiable Manipulation

author.name: Shiza Charania

entry.summary: HATCH proposes a robot escape room benchmark for manipulation: an openly specified, physically replicable, sensor-scored, and unrehearsable evaluation where chained tasks are unlocked by sensor instrumentation rather than human judgment. Entrants submit attested self-runs with uncut video, sensor logs, and a run-day randomization seed. The design directly targets the gameability and irreproducibility problems of existing closed or simulated robot leaderboards.

entry.title: Embodied Task Agents Can Perform Fine Manipulation through Tactile In-Context Learning

author.name: Yubang Wang, Zezheng Huai, Yifei Zhang, Jinhao Wu, Yitong Chen, Haozhe Zhang, Sixian Li, Jingjing Gong, Zhenyang Lin, Ziyang Chen, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: Tactile-ETA investigates whether embodied task agents can perform fine manipulation without task-specific training by incorporating tactile experience via in-context learning. Expert demonstrations pair robot movements with camera views and bilateral tactile observations, subsampled to salient contact-change moments, and a general-purpose robot model selects actions from these demonstrations plus current vision, touch, and proprioception. The results suggest tactile in-context learning is viable for fine manipulation.

entry.title: FIT-MAC: A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Framework for Robust Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jiatong Li, Jisheng Dang, Qiangqiang Ma, Bimei Wang, Jingwen Zhao, Wenjun Ma, Juncheng Li, Hong Peng, Bin Hu

entry.summary: This paper introduces FIT-MAC, a failure-aware closed-loop multi-agent control framework that wraps vision-language-action (VLA) policies with an inference-time control layer. Planner and recovery agents distinguish failure modes caused by object-position or instruction perturbations and select appropriate recovery strategies. It addresses a real reliability gap in VLA policies that perform well on benchmarks but degrade under nominal-setting deviations.

entry.title: GPT-6-Astra Understands Touch and Outperform Vision--Tactile--Language--Action Models

author.name: Ziyong Wang, Yupei Lin, Runxuan Huang, Liang Lin, Dongyu Zhang, Guangrun Wang

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether general-purpose multimodal models understand the physics of real-world interactions, using contact-rich manipulation and tactile understanding as a testbed. The proposed GPT-as-Tactile-Policy summarizes expert demonstrations into task guidance and uses tactile feedback to correct actions after obstruction, matching or exceeding specialized vision-tactile-language-action models without per-task pretraining.

entry.title: From POMDP Theory to Deep RL with Particle Filters

author.name: Kevin Tan, Ziping Xu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a practical end-to-end model-based RL algorithm for partially observable environments that performs hidden-state filtering via sequential Monte Carlo, updates a latent dynamics model online, and does approximate d-step online planning with value-function bootstrapping. It aims to connect rigorous POMDP theory with modern deep RL practice.

entry.title: Sparse RL Relaxation for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Jiabin Fan, Matthias Lindemann, Zita Marinho, Andr\'e FT Martins, Lili Mou

entry.summary: The paper improves soft chain-of-thought training by treating soft tokens as differentiable intermediate computation steps rather than MDP actions, enabling gradient propagation across soft tokens under an RL relaxation. This captures how one soft-token choice affects subsequent reasoning possibilities, addressing a limitation of prior soft-CoT RL approaches.

entry.title: SAPD: Learning from Agent Experience without Environment Interaction

author.name: Juncheng Diao, Haibin Wang, Wei Shi, Yifan Ding, Qingbin Li, Rongxiang Weng, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: SAPD (Step-Advantage Policy Distillation) enables LLM agents to learn from offline trajectories without revisiting environments, decomposing multi-turn trajectories into relative step advantages to avoid the catastrophic forgetting of SFT and the environment dependence of online RL. This targets the core scaling bottleneck of executable environment construction for agent training.

entry.title: How Intervention History Changes AI Agent Sabotage on Subsequent Tasks

author.name: Daniel Saeedi, Amirali Aghazadeh

entry.summary: This AI-control study examines cross-episode adaptation: whether an agent that learns an earlier sabotage attack was caught changes its evasion behavior on subsequent, different tasks under defer-to-trusted protocols. Using ControlArena's IaC and SHADE-Arena testbeds, it pairs history-conditioned attempts with matched baselines on successor tasks. The work challenges the common evaluation assumption of resetting agent memory between tasks.

entry.title: LiBRA: Logit Fingerprints for Byzantine-Robust Client Selection in Federated Learning

author.name: Saheed A. Tijani, Frank Jiang, Ming Liu

entry.summary: LiBRA replaces parameter-vector comparison in Byzantine-robust federated aggregation with a fingerprint of class-conditional logit responses to optimized pseudo-patterns, enabling client selection that is architecture-agnostic, cheaper than O(n^2 d), and compatible with secure aggregation. It is instantiated as variants of Krum, Multi-Krum, and Bulyan changing only the comparison basis. This resolves a tension between robust aggregation and privacy-preserving aggregation protocols.

entry.title: BCT: Bayes-Consistent Tempering for Flow Language Models

author.name: Daisuke Oba, Hiroki Furuta, Naoaki Okazaki

entry.summary: The authors identify that post-hoc temperature scaling breaks in posterior-induced flow language models because it changes both endpoint and intermediate noisy-state distributions while the denoiser and transport dynamics remain those of the untempered flow. They propose Bayes-Consistent Tempering, which makes temperature explicit in both the distributions and the dynamics. This addresses an underexplored gap as flow-based LMs become a competitive alternative to autoregressive and diffusion models.

entry.title: Recast the Past: Stable Long Video Generation with Full Context Memory

author.name: Yukuo Ma, Cong Liu, Junke Wang, Junqi Liu, Haibin Huang, Zuxuan Wu, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: ReCam tackles long-horizon video generation by compressing historical spatiotemporal blocks into memory tokens projected into a Diffusion Transformer's hidden space, preserving full-history access while cutting token count. A dual-pointer denoising scheme with separate noise schedules mitigates temporal drift during autoregressive rollout.

entry.title: Don't Skip the Baseline: A Controlled Comparison of Dynamic Expert Skipping in MoEs

author.name: Jakob Steimle, Thomas Elsken, Daniel Ehrhardt, Lukas Rinder, Daniel Cremers, Xi Wang

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks four representative dynamic expert-skipping methods for Mixture-of-Experts models against the simple baseline of statically reducing the number of active experts k, using a unified taxonomy and controlled comparison. It addresses the fragmented evaluation practices that have obscured whether added complexity (calibrated scores, similarity metrics, learned allocators) actually helps. Rigorous negative-result-style studies like this improve research hygiene in the efficient-MoE literature.

entry.title: SceneRig: An Agentic System for Simulation-Ready 3D Scene Reconstruction from Single Images

author.name: Rundong Luo, Yunong Liu, Di Cao, Matthew Tancik, Shyamal Buch, Colton Stearns, Wenqi Xian

entry.summary: SceneRig converts a single image into an editable, simulation-ready 3D scene by combining geometric, visual, and physical tools, then having an agent perform edit-and-validate loops inside a physics simulator to ensure scenes behave correctly under manipulation. This addresses a key weakness of post-hoc physics settling approaches that produce visually plausible but physically misaligned scenes.

entry.title: ReTTT: Reflection-Driven Test-Time Training via Experience-Based Parametric Memory

author.name: Kangcong Li, Hangfan Zhang, Shuyue Hu, Shengji Tang, Tao Chen

entry.summary: ReTTT enables LLM agents to self-adapt during multi-turn tasks by reflecting on interaction feedback, maintaining lessons in explicit memory, and performing test-time training that writes those lessons into parametric updates, with continual revision within an episode. This aims to convert per-episode experience into reliable, actionable improvements to subsequent decisions.

entry.title: Representations Have Trajectories: Characterizing Temporal Representation Dynamics in Neural Networks

author.name: Shivaprasad B. Gowda, Sparsh Mittal

entry.summary: A large-scale empirical study tracking representational geometry throughout training, going beyond analyses at convergence. The authors identify three recurring geometric trajectories (persistent high-rank, collapse-and-recovery, persistent low-rank) and a Destructive Rank phase, revealing distinct optimization behaviors across architectures.

entry.title: Auto-MD-bench: Evaluating Autoresearch Agents for Real-World Medical Tasks

author.name: Shenqi Zhou (National University of Singapore, Zhejiang University), Qiran Zou (National University of Singapore), Wenhao Zhao (National University of Singapore), Zhenyu Liao (Amazon), Dianbo Liu (National University of Singapore)

entry.summary: Auto-MD-bench evaluates autonomous ML-development agents on 15 real-world medical tasks, testing whether optimizing simple discrimination metrics like AUROC produces models that are actually usable in clinical practice. It emphasizes calibration and robustness across patient populations as under-tested requirements. The benchmark exposes gaps between leaderboard-style success and real-world medical utility.

entry.title: Rethinking LLM Fine-Tuning via Weight Space Reparameterization: Preserving Safety during Downstream Adaptation

author.name: Min-Seong Kim, Jongbok Won, Jeesup Park, Yonghee Choi, Dong-Jun Han

entry.summary: WSR-Tune is a weight-space reparameterization framework that preserves safety alignment during downstream fine-tuning by constructing a safety-conditioned basis and constraining weight updates in that space, addressing the fact that safety information is distributed across many parameter directions. This tackles the well-documented safety erosion caused by task fine-tuning of aligned LLMs. It is directly relevant to safe customization of deployed models.

entry.title: LLM Evolutionary Search Strategies Should be Compared by Tokens

author.name: Tal Oved, Roi Pony, Oshri Naparstek, Udi Barzelay

entry.summary: This paper shows that evaluating LLM evolutionary search by proposal count hides true compute cost: replaying 600 logged runs reveals proposal costs varying 16k-39k tokens, giving evolution up to 6x the effective budget of independent sampling under equal-proposal comparisons. Matching token budgets and removing scorer exploits largely eliminates the evolutionary advantage, which survives at 5% or less on 12 of 15 task-method pairs.

entry.title: Location, Location, Generation: Where You Ask Matters for Generative Engine Optimization

author.name: Mahe Chen, Nick Koudas

entry.summary: A controlled audit of 31,200 answers showing how user location changes which sources and brands generative search engines like ChatGPT and Gemini cite, with 19 declared and five network locations. The study finds ChatGPT localizes aggressively from declared location down to the city, embedding the place into its own searches. The results have significant implications for generative engine optimization, which is typically monitored from a single location.

entry.title: Write Once, Query Many: Evolving Compact Reusable Memory for Long Videos

author.name: Kerui Chen, Jinglu Wang, Yun Wang, Xinjiang Wang, Yan Lu

entry.summary: Video-EMem proposes an evolvable, reusable memory structure for long-video understanding built on time-anchored text plus sparse images, so a multimodal LLM encodes a video once and answers many queries without repeated processing. A Writer consolidates multiscale observations and a Reader retrieves and organizes evidence, amortizing expensive agentic search. This addresses the context limits of MLLMs on long videos in a practical way.

entry.title: From Seeing to Reporting: A Theory of Reliable Visual Set Generation in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Junzhe Shi, Yuan Gan, Shida Jiang

entry.summary: The paper shows that frontier VLMs can fail at the reporting stage of visual tasks: GPT-6.1 correctly lists all 173 objects in a dense scene yet states counts summing to 188 in the same response. FSR formalizes reporting as a chain from raw responses to constructed sets and answers, yielding exact inference-time procedures for deleting, averaging, and re-reading records that improve frozen VLMs.

entry.title: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages

author.name: Mohsen Fayyaz, Ali Modarressi, Daniel Israel, Lucas Bandarkar, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: Empirically analyzes how diffusion language models adaptively spend forward passes, showing cost per token varies strongly by task and language. Finds that copying or lightly editing input is cheap while open-ended generation is expensive, with input novelty and word rarity explaining much of the variance, illustrated by DiffusionGemma needing over three times as many passes for story writing versus grammar correction.

entry.title: TempoMoE: Identifying and Steering Fast-Slow Thinking Experts for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Xiyue Zhang, Keru Zhou, Ziyi Wang, Bing Hu, Li Wang

entry.summary: Discovers that fast and slow thinking in multimodal MoE reasoning models exhibit distinct expert-routing patterns, with causal evidence that suppressing slow-thinking experts shortens reasoning chains while suppressing fast-thinking experts lengthens them. Uses these findings to steer reasoning depth and reduce overthinking, token cost, and latency without degrading accuracy.

entry.title: ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion Beyond Auxiliary Multi-Token Prediction

author.name: Yuxuan Zhou, Junyuan Shang, Tianyu Wang, Chunrui Zheng, Zichang Liu, Wenbin Chang, Shuohuan Wang, Dianhai Yu

entry.summary: ECHO reformulates multi-token prediction so the backbone's own final layer predicts every future horizon, eliminating the auxiliary modules and extra passes of standard MTP. Dynamic Depth Sampling keeps deeper horizons affordable with depth-decaying training probabilities, integrating future prediction into the autoregressive objective itself. The paper reports that added depth converts directly into downstream accuracy during pretraining.

entry.title: P2N: Reusing Deep Representations for Greater Effective Depth

author.name: Yiqin Hao, Boyi Zeng, Zitong Wang, He Li, Shixiang Song, Feichen Song, Yifan Liu, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: P2N reuses the previous token's already-computed deep hidden state by adding it to the current token's shallow representation, letting later layers build on prior deep computation. This increases effective computational depth for reasoning at negligible decoding overhead, avoiding both extra layers and heavy test-time compute.

entry.title: No Matter Who You Are: Addressivity and Sycophancy in Large Language Models

author.name: Seungjong Sun, Hyunmin Jun, Minsik Yoon, Eungu Lee, Choongwon Kang, Young Seok Woo, Jang Hyun Kim

entry.summary: Hypothesizes that post-training gives model outputs addressivity (utterances directed at an addressee), which creates pressure to align with user preferences and thereby causes sycophancy. Using sparse autoencoders, the authors extract addressivity directions from pre-trained and post-trained models and examine their causal relationship with sycophantic behavior.

entry.title: HarnessRL: Co-Evolving Policies with a Just-in-Time Training Harness for Open-Ended RL

author.name: Xiaoqiang Wang, Ting-En Lin, Yuchuan Wu, Pinyi Zhang, Caixin Kang, Ling Li, Bingxue Qiu, Jieping Ye, Yongbin Li, Bang Liu

entry.summary: HarnessRL targets two failure modes of rubric-based RL for open-ended generation: non-discriminative rewards (scores collapsing uniformly) and spurious rewards (higher scores not meaning better outputs). It introduces a training-time harness that co-evolves with the policy through interfaces for task sampling, rollout guidance, and rubric criteria, keeping task difficulty and evaluation aligned as the policy improves.

entry.title: HybridResearcher: Bridging the Structured-Unstructured Boundary for Deep Research Agents

author.name: Soyoung Yoon, Peiran Xu, Han Wang, Ruofan Wu, Xiaodong Yu, Feng Yan, Mohit Bansal, Debiao Li, Seung-Won Hwang, Yuxiong He, Zhewei Yao

entry.summary: HybridResearcher is a 4B-parameter agent trained to combine evidence across structured databases and unstructured web sources, addressing a gap where frontier agents fail on cross-source analytical questions. It is the first methodology explicitly teaching cross-source reasoning, evaluated against benchmarks like HybridDeepResearch. The small model size makes it notable for efficient deep-research agents.

entry.title: Memory, Know Your PLACE: Governing Lifecycle State and Query-Time Eligibility in Persistent-Memory Agents

author.name: Chen-Fang Hu, Hong-Han Shuai, Woan-Shiuan Chien

entry.summary: PLACE is a governance layer for persistent agent memory that adds write-side state certification and read-side authorization on top of an existing memory backend. A factorial study on Mem0 with small Qwen models shows write governance improves lifecycle state correctness and read governance eliminates causal leakage from ineligible memories. It reframes agent memory reliability as a governance problem rather than purely a capacity or retrieval problem.

entry.title: The Scheduler Is a Hidden Retriever: How Asynchrony Shapes Evidence Acquisition in Search Agents

author.name: Ruiyang Ren, Yuhao Wang, Yinan Zhang, Chunyan Miao

entry.summary: The paper shows that asynchronous delivery timing in parallel search agents redirects evidence-acquisition decisions, with acquisition disagreement up to 24 percentage points above repeat variation despite identical initial evidence, and the effect persists through subsequent searches. It provides an acquisition-regret bound and a matching construction showing that invariance requirements at fixed arrival counts limit evidence use. Asynchrony is thus a hidden confounder in agent behavior and evaluation.

entry.title: From Generic to Dedicated: A Novel Optimizer for Online Continual Learning

author.name: Yongyi Wu, Zheng Wang, Sen Lin

entry.summary: The paper introduces SPIN, a dedicated optimizer for online continual learning that interpolates between Polyak-Ruppert averaging as a plasticity engine and primal averaging as a stability anchor. It explicitly decouples plasticity and stability through optimization dynamics rather than relying on data, architecture, or regularizer changes. This recasts catastrophic forgetting mitigation as an optimizer design problem, a relatively underexplored angle.

entry.title: EmbodyHOI: Embodiment-Aware Generation of Hand-Object Interactions for Humanoid Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Chaitanya Chawla, Kartik Sharma, Ananya Bal, Laszlo A. Jeni, Guanya Shi

entry.summary: EmbodyHOI generates text-conditioned hand-object interaction trajectories constrained to a specific humanoid embodiment by running a differentiable inverse-kinematics solver inside the sampling loop of a frozen foundation motion generator. This addresses the embodiment gap where human-space MANO trajectories fail contact maintenance after post-hoc retargeting and degrade downstream policy learning. The idea of constraining generation by robot reachability at generation time is elegant and directly relevant to humanoid robotics.

entry.title: Bayesian Neural Networks via Dirichlet Process Priors on the Data-Generating Distribution for Randomized Value Functions in Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Sumit Vashishtha

entry.summary: This work introduces a new class of Bayesian neural networks that place Dirichlet Process priors on the data-generating distribution rather than network weights, sidestepping the difficulties of weight-space posterior sampling. Building on this, the authors develop DP-DQN, a deep RL algorithm using randomized value functions for epistemic uncertainty-driven exploration.

entry.title: Privacy Accounting for Empirical Denoisers

author.name: William Cheng, Mijung Park, Dongjun Kim

entry.summary: This paper studies privacy loss incurred during diffusion model sampling, constructing a clipped, training-free empirical denoiser whose per-step sensitivity can be computed explicitly, enabling per-step differential privacy accounting for denoising. It complements DP training by quantifying memorization-driven privacy risk at generation time.

entry.title: A brief(ish) introduction to LM psychology

author.name: Raymond Douglas

entry.summary: A conceptual essay arguing that psychology-style reasoning — treating language models as having analyzable minds with knowable beliefs, goals, and introspective capacities — is a remarkably effective and underappreciated framework for predicting how model behavior generalizes. It surveys core questions of LM psychology, such as whether LMs can introspect and how their internal states should be interpreted.

entry.title: Omni-Woodpecker: Hallucination Correction via Evidence-Prior Rebalancing for Omni LLMs

author.name: Zijian Liu, Chaoyou Fu, Yan Yang, Caifeng Shan, Ran He

entry.summary: Omni-Woodpecker is a training-free framework that mitigates cross-modal hallucinations in omni LLMs by rebalancing representations rather than manipulating outputs. It detects cross-modal conflicts from modality-specific views, uses orthogonal decomposition to separate grounding evidence from learned priors in hidden states, and rebalances them.

entry.title: Unified Sharp Bounds on Probabilities of Causation

author.name: Xin Shu, Ang Li

entry.summary: Proves sharpness of the closed-form bounds for probabilities of causation with multi-valued treatments and outcomes previously left open, and shows PNS, PSub, PRep, and PN are all special cases of a single general formula. This settles the question of sharp bounds for discrete probabilities of causation from experimental and observational data.

entry.title: Recoverability and Verifier Strength: Two Measured Preconditions for Unattended Agent Self-Improvement

author.name: De Wang, Peng Qi

entry.summary: Proposes two measurable quantities gating how much of an agent self-improvement loop can run without humans: verifier strength (agreement between the available verifier and a trusted reference) which limits per-step improvement, and recoverability (cheapness and completeness of undoing a bad change). A platform runs steps unattended only when both are adequate, demonstrated on prompt, tool, and skill changes.

entry.title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE

author.name: Ermo Hua, Xiangyu Hong, Baiting Wu, Che Jiang, Haozheng Hou, Yicheng Gu, Hanjing Wang, Qirui Zeng, Ming Zhang, Ning Ding, Qipeng Guo, Youbang Sun, Biqing Qi, Bowen Zhou

entry.summary: Challenges the per-layer Local Expert design in Mixture-of-Experts models by proposing cross-layer shared Meta Experts, showing via multi-dimensional empirical comparison that sharing reduces parameter redundancy while lowering cross-entropy loss and improving downstream performance. The work suggests a more efficient architectural pattern for sparse model scaling.

entry.title: Toward Agentic AI for the 6G Physical Layer: From Algorithm Discovery to Verified Baseband Silicon

author.name: Eric Mittag, Lukas Brechtel, Maximilian Stark, Hans D. Schotten

entry.summary: This paper presents an agentic workflow where an LLM coding agent implements and optimizes physical-layer algorithms on a commercial 6G baseband SoC, down to agent-written vector assembly, validated on actual silicon. The agent is constrained by an un-editable evaluator suite, a knowledge base of measured platform facts, and per-phase metering.

entry.title: When Do Humans and Machines Truly Complement Each Other? Formal Conditions and Empirical Evidence for Human-AI Synergy

author.name: Andrea Campagner, Federico Cabitza, Vincenzo Crupi

entry.summary: The paper develops a formal framework modeling human-AI interaction via reliance patterns that characterize joint correctness structure, deriving mathematically necessary and sufficient conditions for synergy. It shows synergy depends on Human and Algorithmic Correction — the ability of either party to identify and correct the other's errors — supported by empirical evidence.

entry.title: Claims of emergence in AI should be grounded in information decomposition

author.name: Christoph Riedl, Fernando E. Rosas

entry.summary: The authors argue that informal claims of synergy or emergence in language models, multi-agent systems, and human-AI teams should be operationalized via partial information decomposition, which distinguishes unique, redundant, and synergistic information. This provides a formal framework that makes emergence claims comparable and disputable.

entry.title: Multilingual Brain Decoding Reveals Shared Cortical Semantic Geometry

author.name: Yi Guo, Yong Hu, Michael Kwok-Po Ng, Shuqiang Wang

entry.summary: Using brain recordings from 227 participants across Chinese, English, and French, this study develops a multilingual brain decoding framework and finds consistent cortical semantic geometry across languages and individuals. Cross-language consistency increases from sensorimotor to higher-order association cortex, forming a gradient aligned with principal cortical functional organization. This provides evidence for a shared neural semantic basis across linguistically diverse populations.

entry.title: Robustness of Internal Signals for Hallucination Detection in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Allison Chen, William Yang, Salma Abdel Magid, Jonathan Williams, Olga Russakovsky, Esin Tureci

entry.summary: The paper critically analyzes hallucination-detection methods in VLMs that rely on internal signals, showing that a trivial baseline using a generated word's token position achieves competitive performance and that some detection methods are brittle. This raises concerns about what internal-signal detectors actually measure.

entry.title: Auditing Safety Preference Supervision with Recorded Derivations

author.name: Chenhan Lyu, Amir Rahmani

entry.summary: The paper introduces Symbolic Preference Labeling, where a language model classifies predefined attributes of prompts and responses, explicit rules assign verdicts, and a fixed ranking determines preference labels, producing a recomputable recorded derivation for each label. This makes preference construction inspectable and auditable without rerunning the model. Human annotation on 200 prompts grounds the evaluation.

entry.title: Steering Vision-Language Models for Visual-Contextual Privacy in Location Disclosure

author.name: Wenyue Chen, Yuhan Cheng, Ruixin Yang, Ethan Mendes, Alan Ritter, Jingwei Sun, Hai Li, Yiran Chen

entry.summary: The paper studies visual-contextual privacy in geolocation disclosure, showing that the appropriate granularity of location disclosure is recoverable from pre-generation hidden states along an ordered direction, even when generated responses are misaligned. It proposes an inference-time route-and-steer framework that routes on granularity and steers hidden states to the appropriate disclosure level. This offers a lightweight privacy intervention for VLMs without retraining.

entry.title: Auditing the Product, Not the Recursion: The Evaluation Evidence Behind Recursive Self-Improvement Claims

author.name: Zihan Chen, Di Zhu, Lei Nico Zheng

entry.summary: This study full-text codes 114 studies of recursive self-improvement (RSI), including 90 systems self-described as RSI, to measure how often studies actually report the evidence their product and process claims require. Using independent coding, adjudication, and blind comparison coding, it audits the gap between RSI claims and evaluation rigor. This provides a much-needed metascientific check on a hyped research direction.

entry.title: VLA-Retain: Benchmarking Cross-Dimension Effects of Vision Tuning in VLAs

author.name: Borui Xu, Han Chen, Bingsheng He, Ming Wu, Jason Zeng, Michael Heinrich

entry.summary: This work introduces VLA-Retain, a benchmark measuring how fine-tuning the visual module of vision-language-action models on target-domain data affects robustness beyond the target condition. It carefully separates target gains from off-target regressions, architectural differences, and generic forgetting. The benchmark fills a real gap, since prior robustness evaluations ignore adaptation effects.

entry.title: Causal Discovery for Linear Models with Latent Confounding via Multi-domain Identifiable Representation Learning

author.name: Danru Xu, Aapo Hyv\"arinen, Sara Magliacane

entry.summary: LinADMG learns acyclic directed mixed graphs for linear causal models with latent confounders using identifiable representation learning, leveraging multi-domain data to identify noise variables instead of assuming non-Gaussianity or bow-freeness. The authors show noise identifiability suffices for recovering all direct causal relations.

entry.title: ABACUS: A Benchmark for Image Editing Models to Assess Object Category and Counting Under Scene Conservation

author.name: Aymen Lassoued, Angelique Loesch, Romaric Audigier

entry.summary: ABACUS is a benchmark, evaluation protocol, and scoring metric targeting a blind spot in instruction-based image editing: whether models add, remove, or change the correct number of objects while preserving the scene. It notes that existing benchmarks use holistic metrics or VLM judges that themselves cannot count, so numerical failures have gone unmeasured. This exposes a real and growing weakness as scene complexity and requested counts increase.

entry.title: Rewards for Budget-Aware Multi-Turn Agents That Adapt to Arbitrary Test-Time Constraints

author.name: Tom A. Lamb, Adam Golinski, Eleonora Gualdoni, Sinead Williamson, Michael Kirchhof

entry.summary: The paper studies whether LLM agents can learn to allocate inference budgets (tokens, API calls, environment steps) across multi-turn interactions, adapting eleven reward objectives in a shared training pipeline on AppWorld with 4B and 9B Qwen3.5 models. It adapts length penalties to multi-resource budget constraints and introduces new reward formulations. Budget-aware agents are practically important for cost-controlled deployment.

entry.title: Plausible Future, Wrong Choice: Steering World-Action Models toward Intended Future

author.name: Zhuohao Li, Jiawei He, Yuxuan Yan, Lang Zhou, Yinghao Li, Yanrui Li, Tianyu Zhang, Yi-Yang Song, Xirui Wu andYi-Lin Wei, Fating Hong, Qing Zhang, Zhilin Zhao, Jingdong Wang, Wei-Shi Zheng

entry.summary: This work identifies Stage Confusion in World-Action Models for robot manipulation, where models generate locally plausible but misdirected future rollouts that drift to the wrong task stage in long-horizon tasks. The proposed TaskWAM framework uses closed-loop, stage-aware representations of fine-grained task progress to steer generation toward task-relevant futures.

entry.title: PeekKV: The First Content Token Already Knows Which Heads Matter

author.name: Minyoung Go, Yongjun Park

entry.summary: PeekKV improves KV cache compression by observing that active attention heads shift between prefill and decode stages (breaking offline-profiling and prefill-based selection methods), yet remain stable across content tokens during decode. This allows identifying important heads from the first decode content token, reducing accuracy fluctuation across workloads.

entry.title: On Reparameterizing the Score Function

author.name: Mohammad Hossein Amani, Leonardo Bocchieri, Maxime Peyrard, Cl\'ement Hongler, Robert West

entry.summary: This paper proposes History-Reparameterized (HR) policy gradients for autoregressive sequence models, replacing the frozen conditioning prefix in the score function with a differentiable or relaxed history so gradients can propagate backward through generated trajectories. Because the resulting history-pathwise term is biased, the authors derive OHR, an optimal centered control-variate estimator with closed-form coefficients. This targets the credit-assignment bottleneck of policy gradients under sparse rewards.

entry.title: Morpheus-2.0: Multiscale Probabilistic Forecasting with Dual-Axis Attention

author.name: Aakriti, Manoj Cherukumalli, Prathamesh Patil, Leonidas Tsepenekas, Amit Varshney, Penghang Liu, Elizabeth Fons, Vamsi Potluru

entry.summary: Morpheus-2.0 is a compact encoder-only time-series foundation model that places targets and covariates on a single variable-time grid, with dual-axis attention handling variable and temporal relations jointly in every layer. Unlike prior foundation models, it supports varying horizons, resolutions, and schemas without fixing them before training, enabling a single universal forecaster across tasks.

entry.title: Transformers as Adaptive Kernel Learners across Tasks for In-Context Learning

author.name: Zhaiming Shen, Alexander Cloninger, Rongjie Lai, Wenjing Liao

entry.summary: This theoretical work shows that trained query and key matrices let transformers act as adaptive kernel methods rather than fixed-kernel estimators, providing statistical guarantees for in-context learning across tasks. It extends the attention-as-kernel literature by analyzing the learned, task-adaptive kernel setting with approximation-theoretic tools.

entry.title: T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training

author.name: Dongyang Li, Mingsong Yan, Zheng Zhang, Sui Tang

entry.summary: T-MUON extends the Muon optimizer by grouping structurally related Transformer gradient matrices into third-order tensors and defining the update via t-SVD and the M-transform, proving it is a steepest-descent direction under the star-M spectral norm with convergence guarantees. Experiments span GPT-2-style and LLaMA-style models from 51M parameters upward.

entry.title: CasePlay: Self-Play Reinforcement Learning from Case Reports for Medical Reasoning

author.name: Hao Wang, Zihan Wang, Kai Wu, Jian Yao, Yiwen Ye, Yongcan Luo, Dapeng Wu, Jiale Chen, Haihua Yang

entry.summary: CasePlay converts unlabeled clinical case reports into RL training signals for medical reasoning via document-grounded self-play, identifying and addressing knowledge-point fixation and difficulty-control failures in existing self-play methods. This avoids dependence on expert-labeled questions or costly synthetic data generation.

entry.title: PACT: NVFP4 Data-Flow LoRA Fine-Tuning on Consumer GPUs

author.name: Lei Gao, Hossein Entezari Zarch, Chaoyi Jiang, Murali Annavaram

entry.summary: PACT accelerates LoRA fine-tuning of language models on consumer GPUs by using native NVFP4 GEMMs for frozen projections, storing gate/up activations in NVFP4 for backward passes, and calibrating weights offline with a GPTQ variant adapted to NVFP4. It addresses both memory and compute bottlenecks while limiting quantization error. This broadens access to practical LLM fine-tuning on modest hardware.

entry.title: EG-GRPO: Evidence-Guided Step-level Credit Assignment for Deep Search Agents

author.name: Sijia Luo, Mengjie Gao, Yuxiao He, Mengshu Sun, Cuiping Li, Hong Chen, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes EG-GRPO, which derives step-level reward supervision for LLM search agents from evidence annotations in synthetic deep search data, identifying first supporting citations to guide credit assignment beyond trajectory-level outcome rewards. This addresses a key weakness of RL training for long-horizon search and reasoning. It is relevant to improving agentic retrieval systems trained with GRPO-style methods.

entry.title: Adversarial Post-Training of Foundation Models for High-Frequency Trading

author.name: Alexandre Bismuth, Kang Li, Aramis Marti-Shahandeh, Valentin Mohl, Jakob Foerster, Anisoara Calinescu

entry.summary: The paper introduces a post-training method for limit-order-book foundation models using a WGAN objective, where a critic trained online on rollouts through a non-differentiable matching engine guides evolution-strategies updates over rank-4 LoRA perturbations under a KL trust region, using the memory-efficient EGGROLL variant. This addresses the failure of cross-entropy pretraining to penalize compounding sampling errors in free-running rollouts. The author list includes Jakob Foerster, suggesting strong research credibility.

entry.title: Maestro: Agentic Formal Proof Development by Coordination

author.name: Haoyu Li, Zeren Shui, Yuhao Zhang, Ferhat Erata, Benjamin Mikek, Murali Krishna Ramanathan, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: Maestro is an agentic system for Lean formal proof development that improves on divide-and-conquer provers by coordinating responses to failed lemmas. It distinguishes why a lemma resists proof (insufficient guidance, false statement, or flawed decomposition) and allows revising the plan above the failing node, avoiding endless decomposition along a broken proof strategy. This addresses a structural weakness in current LLM prover pipelines.

entry.title: Logit Averaging During Training Sets a New State of the Art for Non-Invasive Speech BCI

author.name: Miran \"Ozdogan, Gereon Elvers, Michael Bronstein, Oiwi Parker Jones

entry.summary: The paper provides the first systematic comparison of multi-trial aggregation strategies for non-invasive brain-computer interfaces, evaluating six paradigms including attention-based variants across three datasets, four tasks, and two group sizes. Logit averaging during training establishes a new state of the art for non-invasive neural decoding. Treating aggregation as an architectural choice could improve many low-SNR decoding applications.

entry.title: Rethinking weakly supervised localization on chest radiographs: position nulls, protocol dependence, and PACE

author.name: Shixin Qiu
