entry.summary: This critical evaluation shows that weakly supervised localization results on chest radiographs are not comparable across papers due to unstated protocol choices (results regime, extraction threshold, mask-to-box rule), each of which can shift results more than most reported method effects. Against position-null controls, CAM and Grad-CAM beat the null on only a minority of findings, while radiologists clear the null broadly, motivating the PACE evaluation protocol.

entry.title: Encoder-Free Multimodal LLMs Learn Implicit Encoders

author.name: David Harwath, Desh Raj, Xavier Velez, Sandra Arcos-Holzinger, Willie Jeng, Karen Livescu, Leibny Paola Garcia-Perera, Sanjeev Khudanpur

entry.summary: Analyzing two encoder-free multimodal LLMs including Gemma-4 12B, which feed raw audio samples and pixels directly to the Transformer without modality-specific encoders, the authors find that early layers learn to function as implicit encoders with representations largely invariant to cross-modal context. This suggests encoder-free architectures rediscover modality-specific structure internally.

entry.title: Can Agents Keep Secrets They Were Never Told? Benchmarking Latent Privacy Risks Across Sessions with MemJoin

author.name: Qishun Yang, Shu Yang, Difei Xu, Di Wang, Meng Ding

entry.summary: MemJoin is a benchmark of 288 synthetic cases where an agent's combined long-term memory across sessions reveals a sensitive relation that no individual session exposes. Evaluating six memory systems, the paper highlights latent privacy risks that are invisible at memory-write time. It matters for designing memory-augmented agents that respect privacy.

entry.title: The Explainability Illusion: Must ViTs Exhibit Patch-Decoding Interpretability?

author.name: Ronen Schaffer, Hila Manor, Tomer Michaeli

entry.summary: The paper systematically studies whether token-decoding explainability in vision transformers is an inherent architectural property or an artifact of particular training setups, spanning architectures, scales, and objectives with controlled and real-world experiments. The findings caution against assuming patch-decoding yields faithful interpretations across settings.

entry.title: BiDex-100: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Across 100+ Simulation Tasks

author.name: Yong Wang, Kecheng Zheng, Xing Zhu, Chao Xu, Yujun Shen, Shengze Cai

entry.summary: BiDex-100 is a simulation benchmark of 106 bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks spanning five capability axes including generalization, instruction following, long-horizon behavior, and memory, with high-degree-of-freedom hand embodiments. Each task includes an out-of-domain variant with controlled visual perturbations for multi-dimensional evaluation of robotic action models.

entry.title: OrderGPT: Generation Order as a Learnable Modeling Choice

author.name: Chenhe Yang, Yuhuan Lyu, Tianyang Hu

entry.summary: Reframes autoregressive left-to-right generation and masked diffusion as two extremes of a single axis — generation order — and introduces OrderGPT, which learns a task-level generation order without canonical-order supervision by building on Any-Order GPT. Targets structured discrete domains lacking a natural traversal order.

entry.title: WhatIf-Bench: Benchmarking Intervention-Aware Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Arjun Ashok, Mihir Parmar, Palash Goyal, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Chun-Liang Li, Irina Rish, Alexandre Drouin, Jinsung Yoon, Tomas Pfister

entry.summary: WhatIf-Bench measures whether time series foundation models can reliably use in-context covariates for scenario analysis, forecasting target responses to future interventions. It uses semi-synthetic series from mechanistic simulators of data centers, power grids, traffic, and water networks with controlled covariate-target relationships. Tasks require forecasting counterfactual outcomes given covariate interventions, testing causal sensitivity rather than mere correlation.

entry.title: Language Models are Lazy Poets: Creative Mode Collapse at Scale

author.name: Jacob A. Matthews, Sil Hamilton

entry.summary: Conducts the largest survey of LLM mode collapse in creative writing to date, generating over 1.1 million poems across 15 forms, 248 subject tags, and 16 open-weight models. Finds LLM poetic vocabularies and rhyming abilities are substantial but severely underutilized, quantifying self-similarity at million-poem scale.

entry.title: Do Conversational Agents Need Explicit Memory? A Controlled Comparison with Raw-History Retrieval

author.name: Yongjie Zhou, Shuai Wang, Bevan Koopman, Guido Zuccon

entry.summary: This controlled study compares six state-of-the-art explicit memory systems against simple raw-history RAG on LongMemEval-S and BEAM-100K under original and controlled retrieval settings. The finding is that explicit memory systems show only localized gains for specific question types and tight context budgets, with no consistent advantage, and oracle retrieval reveals some systems lose answer-supporting information during memory construction. This is a sobering empirical check on a heavily hyped research direction.

entry.title: When Does Better Acceptance Pay? A Controlled Study of Speculative Decoding

author.name: Yongchao Long, Chunrui Zheng, Yuxuan Zhou, Guangkun Nie, Tian-Chi Ma, Chao Pang, Shuohuan Wang, Yuchen Ding, Xianbin Wen, Dianhai Yu, Junyuan Shang, Yuxi Zhou, Shenda Hong

entry.summary: This controlled study re-evaluates speculative decoding drafters under a shared protocol spanning training, inference, and evaluation across ten benchmarks and two target models. It finds that published acceptance-rate gaps shrink substantially under shared conditions, and analyzes when additional acceptance actually improves end-to-end throughput.

entry.title: Accelerated Drift of Scientific Prose in the LLM Era: Evidence from an Interrupted Time-Series Analysis

author.name: Hanna Hubarava, Benjamin V. Ineichen

entry.summary: Using ChatGPT's November 2022 release as an observational breakpoint, this interrupted time-series analysis examines whether trajectories of scientific abstract writing in vocabulary, punctuation, readability, and syntax changed across arXiv AI, statistics, and quantitative biology. It provides quantitative evidence on how LLM writing tools are reshaping scientific prose norms.

entry.title: Honeyed Words, Hidden Daggers: Benchmarking and Training LLMs to See Through Mock Politeness

author.name: Caixin Kang, Sitong Gong, Tianyu Yan, Kaipeng Zhang, Yoichi Sato, Yifei Huang

entry.summary: ZhenhuanBench is a 1,592-item benchmark built from expert commentary on a Chinese palace drama, testing whether LLMs can detect speaker intent, emotion-language mismatch, and listener reactions behind mock-polite hostile speech. Evaluation of 34 LLMs shows even the top model (GPT-6 Astra, an existing frontier model) reaches only 73.48% overall with a large drop on listener reactions, and the authors show supervised traces plus CPR-GRPO training can improve small models while quantifying saturated and chance-corrected gains.

entry.title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents

author.name: Zhenyu Zhang, Kewei Fu, Yongqi Tong, Chenzhi Zheng, Wei Wu, Jiang-Ming Yang, Jianshe Li

entry.summary: Heartbeat Thinking enables tool-using voice agents to speculate and execute tools while the user is still speaking, using periodic Thinker invocations that read the latest partial transcript and a shared record of completed reasoning. Ongoing invocations and dispatched tools are allowed to finish rather than being truncated on input updates, letting later results resolve missing arguments and pre-compute dependent calls.

entry.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning

author.name: Liana Patel, Rishabh Ranjan, Ion Stoica, Matei Zaharia, Carlos Guestrin

entry.summary: TokenGate is a small drop-in component enabling end-to-end learnable token pruning for long-context prefill, inspired by the intuition that expert readers skim. It introduces token-gated attention, a MoE-like mechanism that re-weights attention logits with token importance scores to overcome the non-differentiable top-K operator, achieving faster and more memory-efficient prefill across diverse tasks.

entry.title: Not Every User Says It All: Training Tool-Using Agents Beyond Ideal Simulated Users

author.name: Han Bao, Zheyuan Zhang, Kaiwen Shi, Yanfang Ye

entry.summary: The authors construct weak simulated users by masking sentences of replies and show that weak users degrade every agent policy on tau2-bench and ToolWOZ, and that training with weak users (via masks, mixtures, or curricula) does not help. They propose StaGPO (State-Grouped Policy Optimization), where the agent writes what it understood of the user state, which improves robustness to underspecified users. This exposes a key gap between idealized evaluation and real user behavior.

entry.title: A failure of Imagination: VLMs fail to use visual representations for text, but self-distillation can help

author.name: Shashwat Singh, He He, Tal Linzen

entry.summary: The paper distinguishes weak multimodality (answering about images) from strong multimodality (text representations becoming vision-aligned enough to help text-only tasks with latent visual structure). Using shape-counting problems with paired text and image specifications, the authors show VL fine-tuning does not transfer to text-only visual reasoning, and demonstrate that self-distillation can partially close the gap. This is a careful conceptual and empirical contribution about what multimodal alignment actually buys.

entry.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?

author.name: Zhaoxi Zhang, Hao Liang, Linxuan Wu, Yiming Wu, Yifu Yuan, Kun Liang, Chenming Tang, Meiyi Qiang, Wentao Zhang, Weikang Li

entry.summary: SpatialScout is a benchmark with 80 indoor scenes and 3,140 objects that tests whether VLM agents can actively explore 3D scenes with a controlled camera and build accurate object-level metric maps in a shared coordinate frame. It targets active spatial intelligence rather than passive spatial QA. This addresses a key open question about whether models can construct spatial representations from autonomous exploration.

entry.title: Convergent Performance, Divergent Mechanisms in LoRA-Adapted Vision Foundation Models for Brain MRI

author.name: Cecilia Diana-Albelda, Fiona Kekwick, Raghav Mehta, Aleksandra Kulbaka, Paul M. Matthews, Jesus Bescos, \'Alvaro Garc\'ia-Mart\'in, Wenjia Bai, Bernhard Kainz

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether vision foundation models with equal downstream performance after LoRA adaptation are truly interchangeable, analyzing four ViT-B/16 backbones (DINOv3, SigLIP2, MerMED-FM, BiomedCLIP) adapted to brain tumor segmentation and Alzheimer's classification. Using attention divergence and weight-change analysis, it shows similar metrics can hide substantially different internal representational shifts.

entry.title: AEON: Unifying Video and 3D World Models

author.name: Weiqi Zhang, Wenyuan Zhang, Yu-Shen Liu, Junsheng Zhou

entry.summary: AEON unifies video-based and 3D-based world models by training a generative model in the text/image-conditioned video latent space that produces renderable 4D Gaussian Splatting primitives as an explicit world representation, combining the appearance realism of video models like Sora with the geometric consistency of 3D generators like Marble.

entry.title: DexGraspFlow: Topology-Aware SE(3) Flow Matching for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasp Generation

author.name: Bin Zhou, Boyu Ma, Xinyu Zhou, Jiahua Dong, Chuhao Zhou, Yizhou Liu, Hao Wan, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: DexGraspFlow is a conditional link-level SE(3) flow-matching framework for generating dexterous grasps across different robot hand embodiments. It uses a dual-stream DiT to model link-link coordination and link-object interaction, with attention biases derived from kinematic-tree distances to encode hand topology explicitly. The cross-embodiment focus addresses a real pain point, since grasp generators trained on one hand usually do not transfer.

entry.title: What Would Removing This Corruption Change? Failure Attribution for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Carson Sobolewski, Anjali Parashar, Fei Chen, Yingke Li, Chuchu Fan

entry.summary: This paper defines failure attribution for VLA models: deciding which of several co-occurring visual corruptions actually caused a failure and how much removing each would help, which detection alone cannot answer and paired rollouts measure only at great cost. The authors introduce a factorized risk model that learns separate representations of corruption contributions to estimate removal benefits without costly paired rollouts. This is a novel and practically useful reliability analysis tool for deployed embodied policies.

entry.title: AWLS: Advantage-Weighted Latent Steering for One-Step Generative Robotic Manipulation Policies

author.name: Jiahong Tang, Jiaju He, Zhiyuan Yang, Ruyang Han, Haiyue Zhu

entry.summary: AWLS is an offline post-training method that improves frozen one-step generative manipulation policies by steering their latent space using offline RL value estimates, avoiding critic-gradient fine-tuning that can amplify critic errors and induce prior drift. Motivated by mixed-quality human demonstrations that standard behavior cloning reproduces indiscriminately, the method biases policies toward higher-value behavioral modes. This offers a training-free-policy pathway to exploit advantage information in diffusion/flow-style robot policies.

entry.title: Frontier LLMs Enter the World of Robotics: A Cross-Model Evaluation on RoboColiseum

author.name: Da Huang, Jichao Wang, Junhui Wu, Tong Ran, Linting Guo, Siying Zhang, Chuang Men, Sukai Wang, Yue Zhou, Maoqing Yao, Mo Wu

entry.summary: This paper conducts a multidimensional comparative evaluation of frontier multimodal LLMs for robot control on RoboColiseum, spanning instruction following, spatial reasoning, general manipulation, and robustness tracks. The Agent2Act harness integrates existing models including GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, and Gemini 4 Argon, all released well before this study, into a shared observation-action-feedback evaluation environment. All four models show a consistent profile: high instruction-following scores with weaker downstream embodied capabilities.

entry.title: Reasoning as a Distribution: Generative Plan Latents for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Matteo Cercola, Katie Z Luo, Milan Ganai, John Alora, Simone Formentin, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: This work introduces Generative Plan Latents (GPL), which represent a VLA model's intermediate reasoning state as a low-dimensional conditional distribution over plans rather than a single committed representation. Without retraining the VLA, plans can be sampled for coverage, selected on request for steering, and reweighted by deployment outcomes. Experiments cover SimplerEnv manipulation with the pi0 policy and reasoning models.

entry.title: AgenticRoboRL: Bringing Coding-Agent Post-Training to Agentic Robotics

author.name: Xinxin Liu, Bingxin Xu, Wenrui Bao, Ming Li, Wentao Bao, Chen Chen, Yuzhang Shang

entry.summary: AgenticRoboRL is a framework for post-training robot planners across different execution harnesses, transferring insights from coding-agent post-training to agentic robotics. Unlike prior work that relies on powerful closed-source planners and improves only harnesses and memory, this approach improves the planners themselves while accommodating both VLA skill invocation and control-code generation.

entry.title: Hilbert-Scale Stability of Posterior Diffusion Priors for Ill-Posed Signal Recovery

author.name: Bahman Moraffah, Raha Moraffah

entry.summary: The paper develops a stability theory for posterior diffusion sampling in linear inverse problems on Hilbert scales, deriving conditions under which a learned score remains informative despite ill-posed forward operators that smooth out unknown signals. An explicit score-amplification condition governs reconstruction stability across regularity scales.

entry.title: Why do fictional jailbreaks work?

author.name: Juan Cruz Mendoza

entry.summary: This post presents a mechanistic interpretability study of why fictional-framing jailbreaks work: the author extracts a narrativity/story direction in two models and shows steering along it can restore or suppress refusal behavior on jailbreaks. The story direction is geometrically and causally distinct from persona, harm, and eval-awareness directions, with a distinct mechanism for restoring refusal.

entry.title: CUA-Recovery: Benchmarking Error Recovery in Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Xu Hu, Haoming Li, Yuxiang Wang, Jinxin Yang, Kangshuo Li, Licheng Wang, Dingyi Kang, Jiayu Song, Tianhao Wang, Zhanhua Hu, Xu Yang, Qiannan Li, Bingzhe Li, Feng Chen

entry.summary: Presents CUA-Recovery, a benchmark for error detection and recovery in computer-use agents during long-horizon multi-application workflows, whose errors are induced by real agent policies rather than manually injected. It targets a key reliability bottleneck, since undetected errors can corrupt persistent state and cascade into downstream failures.

entry.title: TrajEvolve: Trajectory Evolution for Reinforcement Learning with Hindsight Credit Assignment

author.name: Yi Wen, Hao Chen, Wanyu Wang, Maolin Wang, Pengyue Jia, Derong Xu, Huize Tan, Yingyi Zhang, Wenlin Zhang, Weihong Luo, Xiku Du, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: TrajEvolve targets two failures of RL for LLM reasoning on long-horizon tasks: insufficient successful trajectory sampling and indiscriminate sparse-reward credit assignment that encourages redundant steps. It introduces trajectory evolution with hindsight credit assignment, reducing reliance on the base model's ability to stumble into successful rollouts.

entry.title: MLIPS: Multi-Layer Indexer Pool Sharing

author.name: Samkit Jain, Sai Kishan Pampana, Shlok Agarwal

entry.summary: MLIPS is a training-free method for sparse attention that shares a candidate search pool across layers: a producer publishes a top-M pool larger than the attention budget, and subsequent layers select their own top-K from it while retaining their own scoring. Implemented in vLLM for the existing DeepSeek-V4-Flash model, measurements across three sparse-attention model families show broad pools yield substantially higher coverage than final-selection overlap. This reduces repeated full-prefix scanning costs across layers.

entry.title: The Shape of the DPO Hyperparameter Landscape: What to Measure, How It Moves with Scale, and When Not to Transfer It

author.name: Hannan Mahadik, David Salinas, Jacek Golebiowski, Aaron Klein

entry.summary: Through dense hyperparameter grid experiments on DPO across model scales from the same family, this paper maps how optimal learning rate and the reference-policy regularization parameter beta evolve with model size and update steps. It shows intermediate checkpoints provide an inexpensive signal to accelerate hyperparameter optimization, and identifies which hyperparameters transfer across scales and benchmark types. This is directly actionable for post-training practitioners.

entry.title: DISCERN: Identifiable Disease Evidence for Generalizable Medical Multimodal Learning

author.name: Xiaoguang Zhu, Pengyi Jiang, Juncen Guo, Jingyi Wu, Lianlong Sun, Yang Liu

entry.summary: DISCERN models clinical multimodal data with a latent structural causal model in which disease and background factors share generation mechanisms while cohorts differ in selection and measurement, and identifies conditional disease evidence without disease labels or full causal recovery. Conditioning on a minimal selection statistic removes enrollment shortcuts and yields an identifiable reference posterior under a specified shift family.

entry.title: Bombadil: A Foundation Model for Plant Electrophysiology

author.name: James Kirk, Piotr Bednarski, Filip Twardy, Justin Mast, Lee von Kraus

entry.summary: Bombadil is a foundation model for plant electrophysiology, trained to transfer across tasks, species, and environments where prior models were single-task, enabling scalable plant stress monitoring for agriculture, forestry, and horticulture. It opens a new applied foundation-model domain using electrical signals recorded via extracellular electrodes. This extends the foundation-model paradigm to an understudied biological signal modality.

entry.title: Where and Why Search-Augmented LLMs Fail When Reasoning over Rapidly Evolving Knowledge

author.name: Tianyi Hu, Bhavyajeet Singh, Niket Tandon, Akhil Arora

entry.summary: The authors introduce TREK, comprising TREKTRACE for attributing failures to specific retrieval and reasoning stages, and TREKBENCH-WILD, a meta-benchmark of questions requiring reasoning over rapidly evolving knowledge. Their surprising finding is that post-retrieval reasoning, not retrieval itself, is the main bottleneck for search-augmented LLMs.

entry.title: Consistency Training Suppresses Cue Following Without Teaching Cue Selectivity

author.name: Prakhar Gupta, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Zhijing Jin

entry.summary: Training four consistency-training methods on Gemma-2-2B-it and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, the authors show with pre-registered predictions and circuit-level inspection that CT suppresses cue influence broadly rather than selectively. All methods reduce the effect of both incorrect and correct cues by similar amounts, and the trained circuit changes do not reflect the different underlying solutions prior work suggested.

entry.title: Productive State-Space Exploration for Multi-turn RL in LLM Agents

author.name: Mohammed Haroon Dupty, Yong Liang Goh, Song Guo, Wee Sun Lee

entry.summary: Identifies failure modes of LLM agents in multi-turn RL — invalid actions violating environment preconditions and repetitive high-confidence action loops — and argues they stem from a mismatch between the agent's internal state representation and environment dynamics. Proposes productive state-space exploration to steer agents away from unproductive behaviors during long-horizon training.

entry.title: Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kyuyoung Kim, Zilin Xiao, Zhiyuan Wang, Avinash Atreya, Ke Yang, Jinwoo Shin, Kecheng Hao

entry.summary: Retrieval Program Learning lets an RL-trained policy compose search primitives into executable programs with local state and control flow, enabling adaptive multi-step retrieval that decouples retrieval breadth from context consumption. The authors note the resulting flexibility creates a hard exploration problem and address it within their framework. This pushes beyond fixed retrieval pipelines and atomic tool collections toward programmable agentic search.

entry.title: Dual-Slot: From Serial Loops to Parallel Slots in Language Models

author.name: Yiqin Hao, Zitong Wang, Boyi Zeng, He Li, Shixiang Song, Feichen Song, Yifan Liu, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: Dual-Slot reorganizes looped language models by splitting computation into parallel latent and prediction slots: the prediction slot uses the previous token's deep latent state while the latent slot prepares the state for the next step. This removes serial dependencies between loop iterations, replacing two sequential module invocations with one paired invocation and reducing autoregressive latency.

entry.title: When Retrieval Partially Conflicts with Skills: Understanding Procedural Hallucination in Language Models

author.name: Guanqun Jiang, Pengfei Cao, Kang Liu, Jun Zhao

entry.summary: The paper defines procedural hallucination: cases where a model adopts retrieved cues that violate a selected skill and produces a retrieval-supported but skill-invalid answer. It introduces SourceClash, a matched benchmark with 1,271 bundles and 6,355 prompts across ten procedural domains that varies retrieval conflict while holding task, skill, and answer space fixed. This carves out a new, well-controlled failure mode at the skill-retrieval interface.

entry.title: SplatFlux: Feed-Forward 4D Gaussian Reconstruction and Generation from Video Latents

author.name: Runmin Zhang, Binglin Ren, Zhu Yu, Fudong Wang, Jiangke Lin, Yichun Shentu, Si-Yuan Cao, Yi Yuan, Hui-Liang Shen

entry.summary: SplatFlux is a feed-forward framework that decodes pretrained video latents into compact 4D Gaussian representations, unifying video-based 4D reconstruction and conditional 4D generation in one latent space. A static-dynamic decoupled representation predicts per-primitive dynamic probabilities, separating static structure from motion for temporally coherent feed-forward 4D scene construction.

entry.title: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting

author.name: Byungwoo Jeon, Sunghwan Hong, Dohyeon Kim, Jonghoon Lee, Jungwoo Park, Inhee Lee, Doosan Baek, Jinil Kim, Taehyun Lim, Hanbyul Joo, Marc Pollefeys, Saining Xie, Jinwoo Shin

entry.summary: The Video-Point Model (VPM) extends a pretrained world model to condition on multi-view video histories and language instructions, jointly forecasting future videos from arbitrary viewpoints and 3D trajectories of persistent scene points. Supervising point trajectories alongside video generation across all cameras anchors appearance changes in a shared 3D structure.

entry.title: Learning to Be Different: Component Specialization for Compositional Diffusion Policies

author.name: Alec Laprevotte, Haonan Chen, Xiaoshen Han, Yilun Du

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure in compositional diffusion policies with linearly composed scores: current training objectives do not encourage factor specialization, producing near-identical denoiser components whose composition is an uninterpretable average. The authors propose a drop-in score-decorrelation auxiliary loss grounded in projective composition theory that penalizes overlap between component noise predictions with minimal architectural or computational change. This directly repairs the interpretability and modularity premise of compositional policies.

entry.title: On the Accuracy of Approximate Leave-One-Out with Blockwise Nonsmooth Regularization in High-dimensions

author.name: Honghao Lin, Songbin Liu, Arian Maleki, Vahab Mirrokni, Chen Shang, David P. Woodruff, Hanbo Yang, Wenjin Zhang

entry.summary: This paper provides theoretical justification for heuristic approximate leave-one-out (ALO) methods under nonsmooth, blockwise regularizers, extending ALO accuracy theory beyond the smooth losses where Newton-step methods apply. ALO is increasingly important through its connections to machine unlearning and data valuation.

entry.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution

author.name: Nan Jia, Wenxuan Shi, Jingqing Ruan, Zhizhao Zeng, Tianyi Zhai, Zhongda Su, Feng Hong, Zhengyu Chen, Wenhao Yan, Haojin Yang, Siqi Dai, Weipeng Zhang, Ke Zeng, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: DataPraxis is an analytics task synthesis framework that progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, then combines and inherits these workspaces to uncover deeper analytical questions. It builds training tasks whose verification is grounded in accumulated, verified evidence rather than raw data alone.

entry.title: PORA: Learning When More Reasoning Pays Off for LLM Agents

author.name: Bo Yan, Qi Zhang, Zhen Tan, Tianlong Chen, Song Wang

entry.summary: PORA learns when longer reasoning is worth spending from a limited multi-step reasoning budget by comparing outcomes of short and long reasoning from the same interaction state during training. This pairs outcome-guided supervision with budget-aware decisions, estimating downstream value of extended deliberation per action.

entry.title: TxnQA: Benchmarking Analytical Reasoning and Evidence Grounding over Transaction Event Sequences

author.name: Rabimba Karanjai, Yiming Bian, Yun-Shiuan Chuang, Jenna L. Ballard, Zijie Pan, Shivani Shekhar, Yixi Li, Yirou Ge, Avinash Thangali, Richard Williamson, Linsey Pang, Prakhar Mehrotra

entry.summary: Introduces TxnQA, a QA benchmark with 27 task families over synthetic merchant transaction event streams, plus a fraud-risk reasoning suite requiring verdicts and supporting evidence. It decomposes model performance into format-following rate, conditional content accuracy, and end-to-end correctness, and evaluates prompted proprietary models and LoRA-adapted open-weight models.

entry.title: Vulnerability Analysis for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement

author.name: Taozheng Zhu, Shixiong Jiang, Fanxin Kong

entry.summary: Studies inference-time observation attacks against safe multi-agent reinforcement learning, proposing a MinMax Attack framework that jointly selects adversarial actions for compromised agents while modeling the cooperative resistance of benign agents. The paper derives a bound on induced safety cost, providing the first systematic vulnerability characterization for SMARL policies.

entry.title: DuplexLedger: Benchmarking Transactional Memory in Full-Duplex Speech Agents

author.name: Yuxuan Li, Xiangchen Guan, Kunrong Li, Jin Wang, Kaiwen Luo, Yang Xiao, Yufei Guo, Zhisheng Chen, Liang Lin, Kun Wang

entry.summary: Introduces DuplexLedger, a bilingual benchmark of 1,094 persistent sessions with event-level Write/Update/Ignore/Retain supervision for full-duplex speech agents that must update memory while listening and speaking. Evaluations of five models reveal a large interaction-memory gap, with the best final-state fact coverage at only 2.01%, and propose ACT-Mem as a step toward improvement.

entry.title: When Does Experience Memory Help Closed-Loop LLM Driving Agents? A Controlled Evaluation with Resampled Warmup Pools, Token-Matched Fillers, and Audited Baselines

author.name: Yingxin Jia, Xuanyi Li

entry.summary: This paper rigorously evaluates when experience memory actually helps closed-loop LLM driving agents, using a controlled HighwayEnv testbed with resampled warmup pools and token-matched filler controls. It finds that prior published gains were confounded by uncontrolled pool composition and injected prompt tokens, and introduces caution-pricing metrics plus audited baselines to isolate true memory benefits.

entry.title: Slot-JEPA: Object-Structured Prediction Interfaces for Latent World Models

author.name: Peisong Wen, Qianqian Xu, Minye Lei, Siran Dai, Yang Liu, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: This paper proposes Slot-JEPA, which restructures Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture world models around object-centric slot representations rather than dense patch features. The slot-based interface gives downstream predictors reusable object structure and explicit temporal entity correspondence, addressing redundancy and expensive transition modeling in current JEPAs.

entry.title: RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies

author.name: Irene Tenison, Abdulrahman Alabdulkareem, Daniel Karl I. Weidele, Nima Dehmamy, Dan Gutfreund

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces RACE, a method for compressing attention head dimensions in pretrained transformer models to shrink the key-value (KV) cache while also reducing attention computation. Unlike prior head-dimension compression approaches that reconstruct full-dimensional representations during inference, RACE learns a shared projection from joint query and key activations on a calibration set, keeping queries and keys in a common reduced-dimensional space while remaining compatible with RoPE position encodings.

entry.title: Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction: How far should we go?

author.name: Emile Anand, Mohammed Rehan Parwani, Xinyuan Cao

entry.summary: This paper formulates speculation-horizon selection in multi-token prediction as an online control problem, since the optimal draft length varies with context and must be fixed before drafting. It introduces Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction (AMTP), a lightweight controller that uses verification feedback to learn how far drafts can be trusted per context without retraining the target model. This improves the efficiency of speculative decoding.

entry.title: 3D-MoE: Complementarity-Guided Hardware-Software Co-Design for MoE Decode on 3D-Stacked NMP

author.name: Yudong Pan, Lian Liu, Shixin Zhao, Yintao He, Kaiyan Chang, Tianhua Han, Chenyang Ai, Haonan Zhu, Mengdi Wang, Yinhe Han, Ying Wang

entry.summary: This systems paper tackles the memory-bound nature of MoE decoding by co-designing expert-parallel routing with 3D-stacked DRAM near-memory processing. It exploits offsetting expert-load fluctuations across decode steps to resolve the conflict between locality and load balancing in tiled NMP architectures.

entry.title: Target-Aware Curation of Hallucination Stress Tests for Large Language Models

author.name: Jiho Lee, Bingquan Zhang, Lin Ting Liang, Soroush Vosoughi, Weicheng Ma

entry.summary: The authors develop an iterative prompt-editing procedure in which an LLM editor revises source-grounded seed prompts to elicit hallucinations in a specific target model, guided by a judge's category-specific scoring. Experiments across 500 seeds, seven datasets, and ten topics show editing substantially raises judge-rated hallucination severity. This highlights that similar average benchmark scores can hide very different per-model failure modes.

entry.title: Training-Free Continual Learning for Multimodal Forecasting via Prompt Evolution

author.name: Laurent Mombaerts, Jonathan Taws, Jacopo Gargano, Dinesh Gaddam, Kevin George, Srijan Tiwari, Shreyas Rajesh

entry.summary: The authors show that continual adaptation of time series forecasting can be achieved purely through evolving a text guidance block in the prompt of a frozen LLM forecaster, using GEPA-style outcome-driven reflection. With strict contamination control (knowledge cutoff predating all evaluation windows), a 900-word evolved prompt carried by Llama-3.3-70B beats time series foundation models. This suggests prompt evolution as a lightweight alternative to retraining for nonstationary forecasting tasks.

entry.title: CovNav: Conformal Prediction-Guided Adaptive Inference for Object Goal Navigation

author.name: Pengying Wu, Zhejia Wen, Kang Ding, Kangjie Zhou, Chunxuan Jiao, Wei Pan, Xiangli Nie, Chang Liu

entry.summary: CovNav uses conformal prediction to decide when a hybrid reasoning LLM should switch between fast non-thinking and slow thinking modes during object goal navigation, balancing hallucination risk against latency. The framework is training-free and addresses the practical trade-off of deploying LLM commonsense reasoning on robots. This provides a principled adaptive-compute mechanism for embodied agents.

entry.title: Learning Tactile-Aware Hand Representations from Human Hand-Object Interaction Data

author.name: Yeonguk Yu, Jaehong Kim, Byungok Han

entry.summary: HuTact pretrains tactile-aware hand representations from large-scale human hand-object interaction data without requiring real tactile signals, transferring interaction structure from human hand motions to robotic tactile observations. The representations can be adapted with small amounts of unlabeled robot data, improving scalability of tactile learning across hands and sensors.

entry.title: TPO: Tri-level Distributionally Robust Learning for OOD Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Chengtao Jian, Kai Yang

entry.summary: TPO extends Direct Preference Optimization with distributionally robust optimization that explicitly models hierarchical preference-distribution shift at group, prompt, and preference levels. This addresses the unrealistic i.i.d. assumption between training and deployment preferences that matters for safe LLM alignment. The tri-level structure is a more faithful model of how preference data drifts in practice.

entry.title: Brain2Vec: A Self-Supervised 3D Foundation Model for Structural Brain MRI

author.name: Spiros Maggioros, Guray Erus, Gareth Harman, George Aidinis, Alexander Getka, Aristeidis Sotiras, Christos Davatzikos

entry.summary: Brain2Vec is a self-supervised foundation model pretrained on 74,425 T1-weighted brain MRI scans from multiple studies, usable as a fine-tuning backbone or standalone feature extractor. Evaluations cover downstream prediction (brain age), convergence speed, and embedding quality, showing improvements over training from scratch. It contributes a reusable resource for neuroimaging where labels are scarce.

entry.title: BitMTP: When Multi-Token Prediction Meets Low-Bit Large Language Models

author.name: Ning Zhang, Shihao Wang, Jinrui Zhang, Chaodong Xiao, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: BitMTP is an algorithm-system co-design framework that combines ultra-low-bit quantized LLM backbones with multi-token prediction to accelerate decoding. It tackles the incompatibility between masked drafting (which lacks intermediate-token inputs from next-token training) and the extra compute of wider verification and causal KV updates that offsets parallel decoding savings.

entry.title: Factorization-Guided Training and Inference for Diffusion-Drafted Speculative Decoding

author.name: Jiakun Fan, Min Xiao, Qiang Wang, Neiwen Ling, Zhichao Liu, Zhihao Jia, Dimitrios S. Nikolopoulos, Zijun Wei

entry.summary: DScout improves diffusion-based speculative decoding by observing that mean accepted tokens does not directly translate to throughput under prefix-acceptance constraints, and introduces two factorizations guiding drafter training (position-wise loss split into inclusion, weighting, and prediction terms) and inference. It targets actual throughput rather than proxy acceptance metrics.

entry.title: Looped GNNs Beyond Fixed Depth: Graph Size Generalization and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation

author.name: Zhiyang Wang, Zhishang Luo, Yusu Wang

entry.summary: This work studies looped GNNs that apply a single learned local update rule repeatedly beyond training depth, enabling generalization from small to larger graphs whose dependency radius grows with size. The authors categorize six schemes separating depth extension, fine-tuning, and freeze-and-steer adaptation, and establish fixed-depth information limits plus sufficient conditions for size generalization. This provides both theory and parameter-efficient adaptation strategies.

entry.title: The Certification Exponent: Instance-Optimal Sequential Certification of Policy Improvement from History Dependent Logs

author.name: Rui Wang

entry.summary: The paper studies how many logged episodes are needed to certify that a new policy improves on a deployed one when the logging policy is history-dependent. It characterizes an instance-optimal exponent based on KL divergence and proves a matching Kelly-style certifier achieves the log(1/delta)/K-star rate, providing both lower bounds and an attainable algorithm.

entry.title: FlowMaker: From Tasks to Cost-Efficient Generative AI Workflow Deployments

author.name: Dimitrios Liakopoulos, Prasoon Sinha, Neeraja J. Yadwadkar

entry.summary: FlowMaker jointly optimizes workflow structure, LLM model assignments, and deployment configurations for generative AI serving under dynamic workloads, arguing that isolated or early-fixed decisions yield poor cost and goodput. It emphasizes reuse of deployed LLM instances to cut serving costs.

entry.title: Synergy-Aware Residual Flow Matching for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Jingrui Wu, Wangyun Dan

entry.summary: The authors propose predicting only the non-additive residual of combinatorial perturbation responses in single-cell data using flow matching, rather than generating the full expression profile. This decomposition allocates model capacity to the biologically informative synergy signal. It could improve prioritization of therapeutic interventions and understanding of gene regulation.

entry.title: MOSAIC: Multi-Objective Search for Allocating Inference Cache Across LLM Decoder Layers

author.name: Sravanth Kodavanti, Manjunath Arveti

entry.summary: MOSAIC uses multi-objective neural architecture search to learn per-layer KV-cache budgets for token eviction methods like SnapKV, H2O, and AdaKV, replacing uniform layer budgets. A single search maps the budget-score trade-off and transfers across target budgets, beating uniform allocation in 146 of 154 tested settings on Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2. This is a practical memory-efficiency win for long-context LLM inference.

entry.title: Beyond the record: evaluating probabilistic AI weather forecasts deep in the tail

author.name: Bastiaan Van Velthoven, Cas Decancq, Diego G. Miralles, Stijn Luca, Thomas Mortier

entry.summary: The paper evaluates four state-of-the-art AI weather models (ArchesWeatherGen, U-Cast, WeatherNext2, GenCast-mini) against physics-based IFS-ENS on 2022 record-breaking events, using record-threshold weighted CRPS and Brier scores to assess skill deep in the distributional tail. It asks whether AI forecasters trained on historical data generalize beyond their training domain. This is a timely stress test for the rapidly adopted AI weather forecasting paradigm, which Google's WeatherNext line exemplifies.

entry.title: Text Dominance in Paralinguistic Conflict: Tracing Suppression Through Audio LLM Circuits

author.name: Ankur Banerjee, Vishnu Guntakala, Danity Pike, Advay Roongta, Kevin Yang, Ruizhe Li

entry.summary: The paper tests whether audio LLMs actually use acoustic cues (emotion, speaker identity, sarcasm) or simply prioritize the transcript, evaluating six models under conflicting text-audio conditions. It finds a high text-dominance rate of about 0.78, shows the failure is not perceptual since speaker identity remains linearly decodable at the LM input, and traces the suppression mechanism via circuit-level analysis, finding that prior back-patching fixes do not help.

entry.title: Bayesian Model Discovery with Language Models: Closing the Loop between Hypotheses and Experiments

author.name: JooKyung Yuh, Byungmin Park, Eunseo Choi, Jinheon Baek, Junmo Cho, Kyu Hyun Choi, Sung Ju Hwang, Kyong Hwan Jin, Hae Beom Lee

entry.summary: BMD combines LLM-driven hypothesis generation with Bayesian model comparison and experimental design: an LLM proposes model families, a numerical engine fits parameters, weighs them by model evidence, and averages predictions, closing the loop between hypotheses and experiments. This addresses the limitations of pure in-context LLM approaches and of Bayesian methods confined to fixed candidate sets. It is a credible step toward principled AI-assisted scientific discovery.

entry.title: Adaptive Decoding Methods for Token-Efficient Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhaonan Li, Zelei Cheng, Amritansh Mishra, Chia-Hsuan Lee, Mann Patel, Sambit Sahu, Ben Zhou, William M. Campbell

entry.summary: The paper studies how the token support of rollout decoding should evolve during RL with verifiable rewards (RLVR), proposing a schedule that widens from top-K=10 to K=20 to full support as the compute budget grows. In a 4B code-RLVR setting, the adaptive schedule beats matched fixed-K baselines by about 1.8 validation points on average under a fixed 150M-token budget. This directly addresses the practical cost of rollout collection, a dominant expense in RLVR training.

entry.title: Dynamical Batching: How Class-Cycling Training Shapes the Internal Structure of Neural Networks

author.name: Nicol\'as Ratier-Werbin, Samuel Lozano, Miguel Ruiz-Garc\'ia

entry.summary: The authors introduce Dynamical Batching, a sampling protocol that cyclically emphasizes each class in mini-batches without changing loss or optimizer, motivated by nonequilibrium physical systems. On hard problems like a three-arm spiral, capacity-limited networks that plateau under uniform batching can fit the data, with measurable changes to internal representation structure. This offers a simple, optimizer-agnostic lever for training dynamics and could inform curriculum and batching practice more broadly.

entry.title: VaDar: Implicit Goal Conditioning via Value Disaggregation

author.name: Shashwat Saxena, Mehul Goel, Sreyas Venkataraman, Sarvesh Patil, Max Simchowitz

entry.summary: VaDar proposes Value Disaggregation for long-horizon reinforcement learning: a single subgoal-independent policy maximizes a linear combination of per-subgoal critic values, so subgoal information is needed only at training time. This removes costly or cumbersome subgoal selection during deployment. Careful experiments show it is competitive with and often outperforms goal-conditioned baselines, making it a notable alternative to the classic decompose-then-execute paradigm.

entry.title: Same Space or Not: Benchmarking Spatial Intelligence Through Cross-View Contradictions

author.name: Huizi Cao, Guanyu Xu, Zhixuan Liang, Ming Yin, Jiuxiang Gu, Manling Li, Mengdi Wang, Shilong Liu

entry.summary: SSoN is a benchmark of 1,000 cross-view contradiction resolution questions from seven indoor scene sources, where models see three views of an unchanged scene and one of an edited variant and must identify the inconsistent view. This probes whether models maintain coherent scene representations across views, beyond pairwise spatial-relation tests.

entry.title: Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay

author.name: Wen-Zhi Li, Sainyam Galhotra, Claire Cardie

entry.summary: This work studies how RLVR reduces reasoning diversity in LLMs, showing from finite-sample learning dynamics that under-sampled but equally rewarded reasoning modes get progressively suppressed and rarely recover under standard on-policy training. The proposed TAR framework builds a memory bank of diverse base-model solutions and selectively replays them to preserve diverse correct reasoning behaviors.

entry.title: Efficiency Measured in English: Tokeniser Coverage Bounds Small Language Models on Indic Scripts

author.name: Anna Pramod

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that commonly reported memory-efficiency figures for small multilingual language models implicitly assume English and do not transfer to other scripts. Across eleven Indic scripts, TinyLlama's tokenizer produces 22.6 tokens per Kannada word versus 1.34 per English word, with zero percent Odia codepoint coverage and byte-fallback fertility at the theoretical ceiling for five scripts, meaning the model effectively cannot represent these languages efficiently.

entry.title: Compile Once, Run Cheap: Frozen, Portable Skills for Embodied Agents, and What Recursive Self-Improvement Adds

author.name: Jingwen Bai, Guochao Bai, Canbo Zhang, Shuangqi Li, Minchao Hu, Weichun Huang, Shuang Liu

entry.summary: The authors propose a paradigm where a strong general model acts as an offline author that compiles and validates manipulation skills in simulation, which are then frozen as portable code executable without a frontier model at runtime. They formalize a skill-level recursive self-improvement protocol with audit, no-feedback, and tamper-evident controls.

entry.title: Outcome-Anchored Credit Reallocation for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering

author.name: Mingyuan Li, Yucheng Li, Xiaxia Wang, Gong Cheng

entry.summary: The paper targets the coarse credit assignment in outcome-supervised RL for agentic knowledge graph question answering, where outcome-level advantages are assigned uniformly to all tokens despite KG operations having different effects. OACR trains a KG-state outcome model that estimates reward changes between adjacent search states and converts them into per-operation credit.

entry.title: Measurement Validity and Representation Dynamics of Confidence Signals in Large Language Models

author.name: Debojeet Ghosh, Shreyansh Kumar, Ayushman Garg

entry.summary: Pre-registered audit comparing three channels of LLM self-knowledge — verbalized confidence, linear probes on hidden states, and answer-sampling agreement (semantic entropy) — across five Qwen2.5 models on retrieval and reasoning tasks. Finds probes become informative much earlier in layer depth for retrieval (~7%) than reasoning (~28%), challenging the assumption that confidence signals are interchangeable.

entry.title: SPLASH: Contrastive Audit Pressure for Detecting and Localizing Security Hallucinations in Generated Code

author.name: Mirza Masfiqur Rahman, MD Ajwad Akil, Imtiaz Karim, Ashish Kundu, Ramana Kompella, Elisa Bertino

entry.summary: Introduces audit pressure, a contrastive measure comparing teacher-forced log-probabilities of generated code under a security review versus a style review, to detect and localize insecure code that passes functional tests. SPLASH selects secure candidates and pinpoints vulnerable statements with no model training or CWE-specific rules.

entry.title: PhyPro-FM: A Physics and Prompt-Guided Graph Foundation Model for Contingency Analysis

author.name: Xu Yang, Zhanyuan Sheng, Chenhui Lin, Haotian Liu, Qi Wang, Yue Yang, Wenchuan Wu

entry.summary: PhyPro-FM is a physics- and prompt-guided graph foundation model for N-1/N-2 contingency analysis in power grids with high renewable penetration and dynamic topologies. Unlike prior deep learning approaches that treat contingency analysis as pure regression, it integrates grid physics and engineering requirements to achieve generalizable, engineering-viable predictions. This addresses computational scalability of a critical grid-operations task.

entry.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting

author.name: Zehao Wang, Jianpeng Yao, Yuping Wang, Yiping Li, Jiaqi Li, Zhixu Li, Kanghoon Lee, Jinfeng Wang, Cong Liu, Zhaowei Tan, Jinkyoo Park, Jiachen Li

entry.summary: Proposes CoopUQ, a multi-robot social navigation framework combining uncertainty-aware cooperative occupancy forecasting with robust decision-making. It predicts future occupancy grids via cross-robot spatiotemporal fusion to handle occlusions and out-of-distribution scenarios where single-robot RL approaches fail.

entry.title: Toward a Universal Local Speech Feature Extractor Through Distillation

author.name: Jessica Yang, Marcelo Beramendi Caballero, Ju-Chieh Chou, Karen Livescu

entry.summary: The authors distill the computationally heavy CNN front-ends of self-supervised speech models (HuBERT, data2vec, WavLM) into a simple two-layer universal feature extractor. The distilled extractor retains most teacher performance on SUPERB(-SG) tasks, transfers to unseen models like wav2vec 2.0, and uses only about 3% of the original MACs. This suggests the local feature extraction stage of speech models is largely redundant and compressible.

entry.title: A Thousand Faces: A Persuasion Benchmark with Experience-Grounded Persuadees Informed by Psychology and Pragmatics

author.name: Ziqing Zhuang, Dingyi Zhang, Deyu Zhou

entry.summary: ATF-Persu is a persuasion benchmark with 1,000 personas across 200 topics and nine domains, where persuadees' receptiveness is grounded in their experiences via personality/attitude theory and conversational implicature. It argues that benchmarks specifying only beliefs and desires reward arguments that match descriptions but ignore the person's actual reasons, and tests whether models tailor arguments accordingly.

entry.title: From Unverifiable Domain Text to Cross-Lingual RLVR via Code-Switched Task Synthesis

author.name: Cheonbok Park, Jihwan Kim, Shinyoung Joo, Joosung Lee, Hwiyeol Jo, Jeonghoon Kim, Jaegul Choo

entry.summary: Proposes code-switched task synthesis to convert abundant but unverifiable English domain text into automatically verifiable target-language and code-switched RLVR task variants, using fill-in-the-middle multiple-choice QA as the seed format. This addresses the data mismatch blocking RLVR-style reasoning training for non-English specialized domains.

entry.title: Assertion and Belief: Moore's Paradox in Language Models

author.name: Anshun Asher Zheng, Weili Cao, Fangcong Yin, David Beaver, Junyi Jessy Li

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic test of Moore's paradox in LLMs, evaluating 12 models on sentences like 'It is raining, but I don't believe it' that may be true but cannot be sensibly asserted. Models largely recognize the infelicity, and the judgment tracks the speech act rather than memorized form; the authors model this with the Rational Speech Act framework.

entry.title: Speech LLMs That Breathe: Modeling Non-Verbal Vocalizations in Dialogue

author.name: Heyang Liu, Lixin Zhang, Jiayi Huang, Ziyang Cheng, Yuhao Wang, Ronghua Wu, Qunshan Gu, Yanfeng Wang, Yu Wang

entry.summary: This paper addresses the omission of non-verbal vocalizations (NVVs) such as breathing, laughter, and affective sounds from speech interaction models. The authors construct a natural dialogue dataset covering 13 NVV types via an automated synthesis pipeline and use multi-stage fine-tuning plus NVV-aware GRPO to teach speech models to produce contextually appropriate vocal events.

entry.title: Answering While You Type: Optimizing Time-to-Answer with Streaming Generation

author.name: Nikita Dragunov, Matvey Mikhalchuk, Anton Razzhigaev

entry.summary: This paper proposes streaming generation, a decoding regime where the model starts producing a response from an incomplete user request and revises it as the remaining input arrives, so only a small residue remains after submission. This reduces the user-perceived time-to-answer without accelerating decoding itself.

entry.title: AfriGuard: Safety and Robust Refusal For African Languages

author.name: Israel Abebe Azime, Jesujoba O. Alabi, Iffat Maab, Alexander D. Cai, Tadesse Destaw Belay, Atnafu Lambebo Tonja, Jonas Kgomo, Folasade Alabi, Salomey Osei, Saminu Muhammad Aliyu, Nkechinyere Faith Aguobi, Bontu Fufa Balcha, Blessing Sibanda, Davis David, Mouhamadane Mboup, Daud Abolade, Neo Putini, Louis Powell, Kiant'e Brantley, Philipp Slusallek, Dietrich Klakow, Julia Kreutzer

entry.summary: AfriGuard introduces a culturally grounded multilingual dataset for studying harmful intent detection, safety-category understanding, and refusal behavior across 10 African languages plus English. The work highlights that safety risks are expressed and interpreted differently across linguistic and cultural contexts, filling a major gap in LLM safety coverage beyond high-resource languages.

entry.title: KEEP-Bench: Evaluating Evidence Preservation in Context Compression

author.name: Ziqing Man, Di Wu, Jia-Chen Gu, Junyi Zhang, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: KEEP-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark with 4,102 cases that directly measures compression faithfulness in context compression, covering evidence needed for plausible reference resolutions, explicit qualifiers, and minority perspectives. It shows that even the strongest models are unreliable at preserving evidence, with the best option-level accuracy around 50% despite large context windows and short inputs.

entry.title: Neuro-Inspired Inhibitory Message Passing for Accurate and Token-Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Nima H. Siboni, Magdalena Springer, Vahid Rostami

entry.summary: The paper adapts cortical inhibition principles into inhibitory message passing, a training-free communication router for multi-agent systems that cancels redundant evidence at the sentence level while preserving rare decisive signals. This keeps crucial evidence visible as messages accumulate in agent contexts. It improves accuracy and token efficiency in collaborative multi-agent reasoning.

entry.title: CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents

author.name: Zhongwei Xie, Yiming Du, Jiaxin Bai, Baixuan Xu, Chunyang Li, Xiyu Ren, Wei Fan, Tianshi Zheng, Weizhi Du, Jingqiao Yu, Xingsu Li, Zhaowei Wang, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: CoworkEnv is a capability-guided framework for synthesizing executable training environments for AI coworker agents, generating coherent requests, tool interfaces, service records, and grading checks. Teacher executions produce SFT demonstrations while student rollouts supply rewards for reinforcement learning. It addresses a practical bottleneck: the scarcity of consistent, verifiable environments for training long-horizon, tool-using agents.

entry.title: CaMeWM: A Causal Medical World Model for Generative Tumor Evolution and Treatment Planning

author.name: Huanlong Gao, Xuelei He, Fengjun Zhao, Xiaowei He

entry.summary: CaMeWM is a causal world model for predicting post-TACE (transarterial chemoembolization) tumor evolution and supporting treatment planning by modeling interventional disease dynamics rather than reproducing historical treatment allocation. It implements an intervention-to-decision loop that admits queried regimens only for clinically comparable histories, addressing the counterfactual nature of treatment planning where cohorts contain only the regimen actually received.

entry.title: PerQ: Inverse Generative Modeling for Neural Image Compression via Quantization Error Compensation

author.name: Tianhao Peng, Ho Man Kwan, Fan Zhang, Shan Liu, Dave Bull

entry.summary: PerQ reframes perceptual image compression as inverse generative modeling within bounded quantization cells, deriving a transport bound that keeps generative reconstructions close to the codec output. This aims to resolve the classic trade-off between pixel fidelity and perceptual quality in neural codecs without needing separate models per bitrate.

entry.title: GARRET: Generative Feedback for Region Retrieval in Visual Documents

author.name: Weijian Jian, Siyang Chen, Yuguang Yang, Yajun Zhang, Chunyu Xie, Dawei Leng, Yuhui Yin

entry.summary: GARRET trains a region-level retriever for visually rich documents from only (page, question, answer) triplets, avoiding costly region annotations. It uses differentiable generative feedback where an auxiliary vision-language model attends to candidate region crops and aggregates crop-specific information to supervise retrieval. This enables fine-grained multimodal retrieval-augmented generation beyond full-page evidence.

entry.title: PointForward V2: Point-Aligned Interaction for Feedforward Driving Reconstruction

author.name: Xianqi Wang, Cheng Chi, Yuechuan Pu, Hongcheng Luo, Junda Cheng, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Bing Wang, Xin Yang

entry.summary: PointForward V2 extends a state-of-the-art feedforward driving scene reconstruction method by enabling interaction among sparse 3D point queries that were previously processed independently. It mediates query communication efficiently to avoid prohibitive global attention across tens of thousands of queries, improving spatial-temporal information exchange.

entry.title: Latent Bridge: From Video Latents to 3D Geometry via Feature Alignment

author.name: Shuai Zhang, Zhanpeng Ouyang, Zhengqing Chen, Ruohong Mei, Shaoyu Chen, Weiqiang Ren, Hui Sun, Qian Zhang, Wenyu Liu, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: Latent Bridge connects video generative latent spaces (Wan2.1, V-RAE) directly to geometric feature spaces, enabling feed-forward prediction of cameras, depth, and 3D point clouds without decoding to RGB and re-encoding. Bridges are trained via feature distillation on RGB videos with frozen encoders, requiring no ground-truth geometry.

entry.title: On Maximum Clique and Maximum Consensus Formulations in Point Cloud Registration

author.name: Abolfazl Babanazari, Kaveh Fathian

entry.summary: The authors provide a theoretical study of the relationship between maximum clique and maximum consensus formulations used in robust point cloud registration. They prove that a maximum clique can have arbitrarily large alignment error and be arbitrarily larger than the maximum consensus set at any fixed tolerance, while deriving geometric conditions that bound this error. This clarifies when the popular maximum clique surrogate is theoretically safe to substitute for maximum consensus.

entry.title: RoboCasa-Shift: Stage-Aware Robustness Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Policies in Long-Horizon Household Manipulation

author.name: Haocheng Wang, Youquan Liu, Weiyu Guo, Aokai Zhang, Donghang Wu, Hongyu Liu, Sha Zhang, Weidong Yang, Ben Fei

entry.summary: RoboCasa-Shift is a diagnostic robustness benchmark built on RoboCasa365 that combines controlled single-factor distribution shifts, matched clean-perturbed rollout pairs, and simulator-grounded stage-aware diagnostics for long-horizon household manipulation. The authors evaluate GR00T N1.5, an existing VLA policy, on four long-horizon tasks under four perturbation factors and three calibrated severity levels, revealing where failures emerge within executions rather than only aggregate success rates. This addresses a key gap in how VLA robustness is measured.

entry.title: Enumeration-Guided Training of Neural Hamilton-Jacobi Safety Certificates

author.name: Mihaela-Larisa Clement, Tosca Pierro, Ezio Bartocci, Luca Marzari

entry.summary: The paper proposes a verification-guided training framework for neural Hamilton-Jacobi safety certificates that uses probabilistic enumeration of safety constraints to detect forward-invariance violations, producing compact, targeted counterexamples that better capture the failure boundary than standard adversarial attacks. Fine-tuning a pretrained HJ value function with these counterexamples yields larger certified regions. This improves the practical training of neural certificates for formal safety guarantees in control systems.

entry.title: From Predictive Geometry to Action: Learning Complementary Predictive Representations for Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Xiaoxu Xu, Hao Li, Hongtao Zhang, Yili Tang, Jiafei Cao, Junhao Cai, Haoxiang Ma, Weixin Li, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage framework that learns complementary predictive geometric representations from multi-view video, compressing dense features from a frozen 3D foundation model while preserving scene structure and its temporal evolution. These representations are then tied to action supervision for manipulation. It clarifies how predictive geometry should be represented for action generation, going beyond auxiliary-prediction baselines.

entry.title: Planning under Noise with Neural Operators

author.name: Michael Chen, Hong Chul Nam, Xi Deng, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: The paper introduces PUN, a neural operator that learns noise-aware value fields for planning under uncertain control execution across unseen geometries, building on a screened-Poisson formulation of stochastic optimal control. It replaces zero-Dirichlet obstacle boundaries with reflecting Neumann conditions and a goal Dirichlet condition to preserve goal signal along long routes and enable reliable gradient computation.

entry.title: Communication Complexity of Universal Features

author.name: Lunjia Hu, Anish Jayant, Peter Li, Princewill Okoroafor, Abhishek Shetty

entry.summary: This theory paper studies how many bits are needed to encode data so that any task from a given function class can later be evaluated with small error, connecting the ML notion of features to communication complexity. The authors construct a greedy encoder achieving O(d* log(1/eps)) bits, where d* is the dual VC dimension, using joint label patterns of selected functions.

entry.title: Strengthening AI safety evaluation through independent third-party review

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon describes its partnership with AVERI, an independent nonprofit led by Miles Brundage, to conduct third-party review of Amazon's internal AI safety evaluation datasets, examining prompt diversity, difficulty calibration, and whether evaluations adequately stress-test safety boundaries across harmful content, cybersecurity, privacy, and copyright. The post details how the collaboration worked and frames external scrutiny as a quality-assurance principle for frontier model safety.

entry.title: E8-QAT: Efficient 2-Bit Quantization-Aware Training with Implicit Lattice Codebooks

author.name: Xinyu Lei, Hong Huang, Jiebin Zhang, Hongyu Li, Jinlong Song, Decheng Wu, Guanghua Yu, Jianchen Zhu, Sujian Li

entry.summary: Proposes E8-QAT, a 2-bit quantization-aware training framework using the E8 lattice as an implicit eight-dimensional codebook, avoiding the costly search of explicit codebook vector quantization while preserving selected lattice points exactly with under 0.1% index-storage overhead. It matches full-performance baselines on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at 2-bit precision.

entry.title: MMEnterprise-Bench: Evaluating Enterprise Agents over Evolving Multimodal Records

author.name: Seohyun Lee, Jongha Kim, Dohwan Ko, Ji Soo Lee, Seoung Choi, Jayun Ku, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: MMEnterprise-Bench comprises 1,613 questions over evolving multimodal records from simulated collaboration projects, testing evidence reasoning, cross-source and temporal conflict resolution, and recognizing insufficient evidence. It targets a realistic gap in enterprise agent evaluation: workspaces where information is shared, corrected, and versioned over time.

entry.title: FALCA: Falsification-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Deep Search Agents

author.name: Zijun Dou, Kun Luo, Chaofan Li, Shuqi Lu, Zheng Liu

entry.summary: FALCA formulates long-horizon deep search as a propose-falsify process, using a collaborative Searcher-Falsifier architecture in which independent Falsifiers actively seek counterevidence to prevent early errors from compounding. It pairs this with hierarchical credit assignment for reinforcement learning of search agents.

entry.title: Predictive Closure: A Set-Level Characterization of JEPA's Feature Selection

author.name: Mosh Levy, Aly Lidayan, Yoav Goldberg

entry.summary: The paper proposes the predictive closure, a set-level characterization of which features JEPA-style joint-embedding predictive architectures encode, accounting for relationships between features rather than individual predictability alone. This addresses concerns that unpredictable features such as a traffic light would be dropped from representations, since relationships (light color predicting traffic stopping) also affect prediction error. It refines the theoretical understanding of self-supervised predictive architectures.

entry.title: Anytime-Valid Runtime Monitoring of Learned Barrier Certificates

author.name: Zhipeng Cao, Taoran Wu, Weiru Cui, Luke Ong, Bai Xue

entry.summary: The paper proposes an anytime-valid runtime monitor that audits learned barrier certificates for stochastic systems using observed closed-loop trajectories, formulated as an episode-wise sequential hypothesis test with a nonnegative test supermartingale. It detects when statistical support for the deployed barrier condition degrades under dynamics that differ from training. The authors are explicit that detection does not itself guarantee pre-emptive safety.

entry.title: De-Diffusing WAMs: Action-Sufficient Direct Prediction for Robot Control

author.name: Shaoyi Zheng, Zhongtao Jiang, Yue Peng, Wenbo Lu, Shunchi Zhang, Xi Wang, Shengji Wan

entry.summary: The paper analyzes cascade world-action models, finding that resampling video noise has little effect on downstream actions while naive one-step truncation substantially hurts task success. It introduces DirectWAM, which converts pretrained video and action experts into single-step predictors by targeting action-sufficient information, removing costly iterative diffusion inference.

entry.title: The Instruction Tax on Factual Recall: Base Models Can Beat Their Instruction-Tuned Counterparts

author.name: Christophe Khalil, Aya Mourad

entry.summary: In the AKBC LM-KBC 2026 shared task, the authors more than doubled the baseline by showing that a base model prompted via text completion (0.6836) outperforms its instruction-tuned chat counterpart (0.5681) on factual recall, an effect they call the instruction tax attributable to weights rather than prompting. This challenges the default assumption that instruction-tuned models are uniformly better. It has practical implications for model selection in knowledge-intensive applications.

entry.title: Forecasting Patient Trajectories from the Electronic Health Records with Action-Conditioned World Models

author.name: Simon A. Lee, Jiahang Hank Sha, Soomin Chung, Kai Akamatsu, Eran Halperin, Jeffrey N. Chiang

entry.summary: The authors introduce a world model for electronic health records that represents patient histories as action-conditioned latent trajectories, explicitly separating patient states from clinical actions via a state-dependent linearization transition operator. This enables time-resolved prediction, multi-step rollout, and action-conditioned simulation while preserving downstream predictive signal and subgroup-level statistics.

entry.title: UltraData-Code: From Raw Repositories to Algorithmically Dense and Task-Oriented Code Data

author.name: Chengying Tu, Hengyu Zhao, Shuaikang Xue, Zhongming Qu, Jihao Zhou, Xinle Lin, Junshao Guo, Zixuan Fu, Qiang Ma, Jie Zhou, Chaojun Xiao, Hongfei Yan, Yudong Wang, Xu Han, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: UltraData-Code proposes a tiered data-management pipeline for code pretraining data spanning four states: repository archival (L0), standardized natural code (L1), algorithmic selection for density (L2), and task-oriented synthesis (L3), with provenance preserved for reprocessing. It responds to shrinking supplies of high-quality public code by applying increasingly targeted processing to smaller pools.

entry.title: Inside the Loop: A Mechanistic Study of Weight-Tied Transformers on Depth-Bound Algorithmic Tasks

author.name: Magnus Sesodia, Juil Sock, Philip Torr, Christian Schroeder de Witt

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study uses directed permutation traversal tasks with per-hop ground truth to examine what looped (weight-tied) transformers compute at each iteration. The authors find a minimum effective depth is necessary and investigate whether looping genuinely simulates a deeper untied stack. The work is relevant to scaling effective depth without extra parameters or chain-of-thought tokens.

entry.title: Generative Retrieval for Reverse Target Fishing with a Proteome-Scale Benchmark

author.name: Zhichao Deng, Haichuan Tan, Xin Hong, Huaizhi Wang, Tao Huang, Bowen Gao, Yanyan Lan

entry.summary: The paper reformulates reverse target fishing (identifying protein targets for a molecule) as generative retrieval with GenFish, which uses residual vector quantization of protein language model features and autoregressive identifier generation to avoid treating unrecorded pairs as negatives. It also releases ProTargetBench, a proteome-scale benchmark for the task.

entry.title: Latent World Models Should Plan with Distances Along the Latent Manifold

author.name: Zunzhi You, Linwei Tao, Siyu Xu, Yunke Wang, Chang Xu

entry.summary: Studying latent world models, the authors show that Euclidean distance in latent space only reflects goal proximity in a small neighborhood, creating spurious low-cost basins that trap planners, while latents retain physical structure on a curved low-dimensional manifold. They propose measuring terminal cost as geodesic distance along the latent manifold for more reliable planning.

entry.title: Weighted State Souping for Efficient Long-Context Retrieval

author.name: William L. Tong, Aryo Lotfi, Emmanuel Abbe, Josh Susskind, Cengiz Pehlevan, Eran Malach

entry.summary: The paper proposes weighted state souping for state space models: cached state encodings from independent token chunks (documents, tool definitions, memory records) are recombined with learned query-dependent weights to cheaply construct a context for downstream queries. This substantially improves long-context performance of SSMs on crowded contexts over vanilla souping. Author list includes Eran Malach and Emmanuel Abbe, indicating credibility.

entry.title: Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation

author.name: Xuyuan Xiong, Siyu Chen, Zihan Shao, Yue Su, Weiyang Jin, Ping Luo, Zhuoran Yang, Xihui Liu

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies truncated BPTT in looped transformer training via nearly 600 runs varying model size, tokens, and forward/backward loop counts, fitting a unified scaling law with an effective-parameters formulation. Despite truncation's compute savings, the fitted law favors full backpropagation, quantifying when truncation is worthwhile. This gives practical guidance for training parameter-sharing and looped architectures.

entry.title: Copying Under Repetition: From Prefix Matching to Position Hashing

author.name: Anxin Guo, Tianlong Huang, Chenxiao Yang, Zhiyuan Li

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that a two-layer transformer with O(log log N)-bit precision and O(log N / log log N) width can copy any string up to horizon N and terminate correctly even under arbitrary repetition, a setting where frontier LLMs fail. The construction uses RoPE-style rotations of attention values and outputs with small prime periods, so that the Chinese Remainder Theorem jointly distinguishes all required delimiter distances. It illuminates why repetition causes copying failures and how position hashing can resolve them.

entry.title: SPELUNKA: A Framework for Finding Unanticipated Associations in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Cassandra Parent, Isha Agarwal, Kumail Alhamoud, Charikleia Moraitaki, Rafiya Javed, Walter Gerych, Marzyeh Ghassemi

entry.summary: SPELUNKA is an automated inference-time framework for discovering unanticipated distributional biases in VLM retrieval tasks without pre-specified subgroups, human supervision, or fine-tuning. It generates captions for related images, extracts and ranks semantically meaningful associations, and uses frequency-based detection to surface spurious or harmful associations.

entry.title: Bellman Language Models: Solving the Recurring Decisions of LLM Agents

author.name: Adarsh Vatsa, William Eiers

entry.summary: The authors observe that bounded LLM agent workflows repeatedly encounter the same decision states, yet models re-derive each decision from context every turn. Their Discretize, Then Decide approach treats these recurring decisions as an optimization problem solved once from workflow logs and reused thereafter, making agents faster, cheaper, and more reliable.

entry.title: Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention

author.name: Karthik Viswanathan, Plamen Dimitrov, Stefano Rocca, Sarayu Sirikonda

entry.summary: The paper studies the expressivity of one-layer attention-only transformers, defining head complexity of Boolean functions and proving exact normal forms, threshold-degree lower bounds, and matching explicit examples, all formalized and verified with an autoresearch pipeline. For symmetric Boolean functions it characterizes head complexity via Hamming-weight level transitions.

entry.title: DiffuPlan: Editable Planning State for Diffusion Language Model Agents

author.name: Qisheng Zhou, Zhen Xiong, Qiaoyu Tan

entry.summary: DiffuPlan introduces an agent-state paradigm for diffusion language models that exploits their ability to reconstruct earlier text conditioned on surrounding context, maintaining a single editable planning state that is revised in place as new evidence arrives. Instead of appending observations to a growing transcript as autoregressive agents do, only affected planning steps are reconstructed. This is an early exploration of interaction protocols native to dLLM capabilities.

entry.title: SPARC: Spoken Profile Authorship Recognition Corpus

author.name: Efthymios Tsaprazlis, Bowen Yi, Tiantian Feng, Junghwan Kim, David Jurgens, Shrikanth Narayanan

entry.summary: SPARC is a benchmark for speaker and demographic-attribute verification from transcribed speech alone, built from podcast corpora with over 12,500 speakers and 1.5M utterances labeled for sex, age, and accent. Results show LLM adversaries can distinguish same-speaker pairs from text alone, raising privacy concerns for speech anonymization that targets only acoustics.

entry.title: Budgeted Attack Scheduling for LLM Red-Teaming: The Roles of Static Priors, Semantic Guidance, and Online Feedback

author.name: Zhicheng Fang, Han Sun, Jiachen Lei, Xinyi Fang, Zongmin Zhang, Chenxu Fu, Sizhe Fang, Wei Xu

entry.summary: The paper formalizes budgeted attack scheduling: choosing which jailbreak attacks from a large library to attempt under a limited budget, given that effectiveness varies by victim-defense setting. It investigates the value of static priors, semantic guidance, and online feedback for prioritization, reducing the cost of robustness evaluation. This reframes red-teaming as a sequential decision problem.

entry.title: Look Before You Reason: Implicit Visual Thinking for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Zerui Chen, Changrui Chen, Fei Ni, Jiankang Deng

entry.summary: LoRe is an implicit visual thinking framework that lets VLMs perform region inspection within a single-turn interaction instead of the multi-turn zoom/crop/tool-use loops of thinking-with-images approaches, reducing redundant token computation and latency. It targets fine-grained understanding of small or overlooked image regions during reasoning. This addresses the efficiency cost of emerging visual tool-use paradigms.

entry.title: Push-Pull Attentional Anchoring for Diffusion Concept Erasure

author.name: Nattanat Chatthee, Tagon Sompong, Ekapol Chuangsuwanich, Supasorn Suwajanakorn

entry.summary: PPAA is a concept erasure method for diffusion models operating in cross-attention space, displacing target representations while bounding erasure strength via relative cosine-similarity constraints. This avoids the uncontrolled semantic drift caused by heuristic scaling of classifier-free guidance or negative prompts.

entry.title: Edit in Sync: Unified End-to-End Audio-Visual Editing for Human-Centric Videos

author.name: Ziye Yuan, Minghong Cai, Xu He, Ruchang Yao, Xiao Fu, Kaixin Ding, Ming Zhang, Xiangyu Du, Tianpeng Lan, Da Xie, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: AVE is the first unified end-to-end framework for human-centric audio-visual editing, jointly performing reference-guided person swapping, insertion, and deletion across audio and video without masks, ensuring lip-audio synchronization. The authors also build a synthesis pipeline and AVE-Dataset to overcome data scarcity. This eliminates cumulative errors of separate video/audio pipelines.

entry.title: Towards Consistent Geospatial Representations: Aligning One Encoder to Many Foundation Models

author.name: Arthur Ouaknine, David Rolnick

entry.summary: This paper studies whether geospatial foundation model representations are complementary, releasing Pangaea-Latents with frozen embeddings from five GFMs across eleven datasets. It proposes GeoMixture, a multi-representation alignment objective that trains a single ViT encoder to inherit GFM complementarity, tying the best GFM in average rank across nine datasets at the cost of peak per-task performance.

entry.title: OverSeer: Multi-Agent World Models Beyond What Agents See
