entry.summary: SEAM is a zero-audio method for constructing embeddings of unseen tokens in TTS models from known subtokens, using a spectral filter to preserve temporal phonetic order and closed-form ridge regression to align with the pretrained conditioning manifold. Across three languages and two architectures it approaches baseline quality with up to four times less training data. This meaningfully lowers the barrier to extending TTS vocabularies for low-resource and cross-lingual settings.

entry.title: Doubly Robust Learning of Heterogeneous Survival Treatment Effects under Time-Varying Treatments

author.name: Tom\`as Garriga, Munib Mesinovic, Luke De Bretton-Gordon, Gerard Sanz, Axel Brando, Tingting Zhu

entry.summary: This work introduces a doubly robust learner for heterogeneous survival treatment effects when treatments are time-varying, jointly handling sequential adjustment for both treatment decisions and censoring. Existing survival learners handle only baseline treatment assignment while longitudinal effect learners assume uncensored outcomes, a gap this method fills. The problem is central to personalized medicine questions like which treatment sequence maximizes survival probability.

entry.title: Simulation Priors for Rapid Adaptation in Model-Based RL for Autonomous Racing

author.name: Adrian Remonda, Jiajun Xi, Nicklas Hansen, Marcus Greiff, Thomas Lew, John Talbot, John Subosits, Xiaolong Wang

entry.summary: Prior-Informed Adaptation is an offline-to-online model-based RL framework that pretrains a world model on heterogeneous low- and high-fidelity simulation and then adapts it with limited real interaction via uncertainty-regularized planning. Crucially, it treats simulated trajectories as biased priors whose residual mismatch is corrected online, rather than requiring an accurate simulator for transfer. Evaluation in autonomous racing demonstrates the approach for safety-critical physical systems where data collection is costly.

entry.title: Modeling Uncertainty Propagation in 3D Morphable Models

author.name: Megh Shukla, Edo Collins, Prashanth Chandran, Karel Petr\'anek, Sergio Orts-Escolano, Mathieu Salzmann, Alexandre Alahi

entry.summary: CLUE provides a closed-form approximation for mapping parameter-space variance of 3D Morphable Models to per-vertex variance, derived from the law of total variance and replacing expensive sampling or error propagation. The method is modular, fast, and accurate, and the authors integrate it into in-the-wild human mesh recovery training. Reliable per-vertex uncertainty matters for downstream 3D perception safety and filtering.

entry.title: MM-LeJEPA: Correlated Gaussian Regularization for Multimodal Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures

author.name: Haowen Bai, Rui Gong$, Meichen Liu, Ming-Xuan Weng, Bihan Wen, Kim-Hui Yap

entry.summary: This work extends LeJEPA, a self-supervised method using isotropic Gaussian embedding targets, to multimodal settings where tasks read both shared and modality-specific information. MM-LeJEPA models multimodal tasks as strength-weighted combinations of independent and shared components, enabling decoder-free, teacher-free multimodal joint-embedding predictive learning with correlated Gaussian regularization.

entry.title: Means-Ends Analysis Helps LLMs Plan in Continuous-State Domains

author.name: Jiayi Li, Carl Kingsford

entry.summary: The paper argues that existing LLM planning frameworks assume enumerable discrete actions, which breaks in continuous-state domains, and proposes Medaka, a structured prompting framework inspired by Newell and Simon's Means-Ends Analysis that encourages recursive goal decomposition, algebraic derivation, and per-step state tracking. The work also introduces evaluation settings for native LLM planning in continuous domains.

entry.title: Calibration-Free Early Stopping for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning via E-processes

author.name: Dong-Jae Lee, Gyojin Han, Junmo Kim

entry.summary: The paper reframes adaptive early stopping for reasoning LLMs as sequential evidence accumulation, running two e-processes on a shared per-chunk signal to decide when to commit or abstain from further reasoning. This avoids threshold calibration that fails to transfer across models and datasets, offering guarantees robust to test-time horizon shifts.

entry.title: Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners: Adaptive Loop Halting on the Hypersphere

author.name: Arber Zela, Artavazd Maranjyan, Pol Puigdemont, David Berghaus, Valentyn Boreiko, Volkan Cevher

entry.summary: Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners (SFPRM) reformulate damped fixed-point adaptive computation for looped transformers on the unit hypersphere, aligning with normalized transformers (nGPT) so that injection, damping, and halting become geodesic operations. The paper proves fixed-point existence and convergence results and shows empirical gains on Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Hard, and related reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: Polar Switch: Fast Muon Orthogonalization with Polynomial Circuits

author.name: Zhehang Du, Weijie Su

entry.summary: Polar Switch is a new approach to the polynomial gradient orthogonalization used in the Muon optimizer, using polynomial circuits of symmetric matrix products on square buffers to reach high polynomial degree at lower FLOP cost than quintic iterations like Polar Express and Gram Newton-Schulz. This improves the GPU efficiency of a widely adopted LLM training optimizer.

entry.title: Compositional Activation Steering Across Languages and Behaviors with Contextual Gates

author.name: Daniil Gurgurov, Akansh Maurya, Josef van Genabith, Simon Ostermann, Hitomi Yanaka

entry.summary: This work trains contextual gates that adapt the strength of fixed activation-steering directions to the current hidden state, enabling composition of multiple steering directions to control several behaviors simultaneously, including in multilingual settings. The approach outperforms constant-strength steering, prompting, and four baselines across many languages, behaviors, and models while better preserving general knowledge. It turns training-free steering vectors into a composable, state-aware control mechanism.

entry.title: MemBubble: Benchmarking How Agent Memory Shapes LLM Response Diversity

author.name: Jiajun Tan, Fei Sun, Xinyu Ma, Shixuan Zhang, Du Su, Qi Cao, Daiting Shi, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: MemBubble is a benchmark of 1,000 instances built from preferences extracted from real user-assistant conversations, testing whether agent memory narrows response diversity. It measures how memory concentrates response distributions in scenarios distinct from stored preferences, addressing a gap left by synthetic-interaction evaluations.

entry.title: CoMem: Learning to Anticipate Failures from Retrieved Experience

author.name: Yun Shen, Ming Shen, Tianjun Yao

entry.summary: Introduces CoMem (Compounding Memory), which makes retrieved cross-task experience condition the parametric reflective memory rather than being combined additively, allowing agents to anticipate failure modes more effectively. This addresses the limitation that retrieved memory and internalized parametric memory never interact in existing cross-task reflective memory agents.

entry.title: Large-Scale Biomedical RAG: Corpus Scaling, Document Representation, and Efficiency Trade-offs

author.name: Adri\'an S\'anchez-Freire, Gonzalo P\'erez-G\'omez, Aitziber Atutxa, Ander Barrena

entry.summary: A controlled large-scale study of biomedical RAG varying corpus size, document representation (abstract, flat full-text, hierarchical full-text), and reranking, evaluated on five external benchmarks plus a held-out test set with latency and storage costs measured. It provides practical guidance on effectiveness-efficiency trade-offs for biomedical retrieval systems.

entry.title: The Judge Can Debias Itself: Awareness and Self-Debiasing for Reliable LLM-as-a-Judge

author.name: Youbing Yin, Jingyu Wu, Anoop Kumar, Scott Novotney, Daben Liu, Erin Babinsky

entry.summary: The paper shows LLM judges can reduce their own systematic biases without additional training through bias-aware prompting and self-debiasing, where the judge critiques its initial judgment for bias influence. It introduces three new bias benchmarks covering authority, confidence, and formatting bias, evaluating seven bias types across three frontier models. Self-debiasing improves judge reliability while remaining lightweight.

entry.title: SynCalib: Breaking Dataset Shortcuts in LiDAR-Camera Calibration via Extrinsic-Controllable Synthesis

author.name: Huihua Zhu, Shuyang Zhang, Dongqing Chen, Zhuo Yu, Jianhao Jiao, Yilong Zhu, Siyu Teng, Xiaopin Zhong, Zongze Wu

entry.summary: SynCalib identifies a dataset shortcut problem in learned LiDAR-camera calibration: networks overfit fixed nominal extrinsics due to low extrinsic diversity in training data. It proposes a data generation framework with extrinsic-controllable synthesis to train calibration networks that generalize to real deployments.

entry.title: CrossFit-GS: Out-of-Fold Pose Estimation for COLMAP-Free 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Zijian Wu, Jinliang Wang, Mingfeng Jiang, Zidian Lin, Ying Song, Ziqian Lu

entry.summary: CrossFit-GS addresses pose-free 3D Gaussian Splatting by partitioning input sequences into interleaved subsets and maintaining two complementary submaps, so each pose is refined against a frozen submap that never saw the target frame. This out-of-fold scheme mitigates cumulative trajectory drift and error self-reinforcement, with validation safeguards rejecting unreliable updates.

entry.title: Touch-JEPA: Tactile Representation Learning from Hand-Object Video with Limited Tactile Supervision

author.name: Minseong Kweon, Qiao Feng, Yiming Huang, Lingjie Liu

entry.summary: Touch-JEPA learns tactile representations from hand-object video with limited tactile supervision via a self-supervised objective that predicts masked visual features at hand-surface locations, capturing latent contact dynamics. It extends to joint video-tactile representations, reducing dependence on costly tactile measurements for physically intelligent systems.

entry.title: PsycheMME: A Psychology-Informed Benchmark for Social Understanding and Interaction in Videos

author.name: Heran Hu, Yuhang Dong, Zhucun Xue, Kaiwei Chen, Yong Liu, Jiangning Zhang

entry.summary: PsycheMME is a psychology-grounded video benchmark with eight capabilities spanning grounding, states, needs, interaction decisions, memory, and risk, built on Social Information Processing and the Perception-Action Cycle frameworks. It includes 1,000 expert-reviewed questions and a Reasoning-Verified protocol that weights answer credit by rationale support and logical consistency; evaluation of 17 models shows timing-related judgments are weakest.

entry.title: LocoPilot: Single-Operator Bilateral Teleoperation for Loco-Manipulation Policy Learning

author.name: Antonio Langella, Giovanni Minelli, Giovanni B. Dessy, Lorenzo Amatucci, Giulio Turrisi, Victor Barasuol, Claudio Semini

entry.summary: LocoPilot is a single-operator bilateral teleoperation and data-collection framework implemented on a Unitree Go2 quadruped with an AgileX Piper arm, wrist and head cameras, enabling coordinated base-and-arm demonstrations for loco-manipulation policy learning. It bridges the gap between robot-free interfaces, which miss platform-specific signals, and on-robot teleoperation, which previously lacked concurrent whole-system command interfaces. This makes high-quality loco-manipulation demonstration collection substantially more practical.

entry.title: Optimal aggregation in multiclass classification

author.name: Felix Abramovich, Or Davidovitch-Servadio

entry.summary: The paper studies aggregation given a finite dictionary of score functions for multiclass classification, deriving optimal rates for model selection and convex aggregation under 0/1 and multinomial logistic losses. Notably, optimal aggregation rates under 0/1 loss do not depend on the number of classes K, and ERM achieves rate optimality.

entry.title: Pareto-Optimal RTL Code Generation via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models

author.name: Koki Takeshita, Kenji Uebayashi, Hikaru Tomonari, Masaya Tsunokake, Koichiro Yawata, Tatsuya Sasaki, Yusuke Ohtsubo, Kota Dohi, Yasuhiro Sogawa

entry.summary: The paper reframes LLM-based RTL (hardware description) code generation as a multi-objective RL problem, moving away from scalarized PPA rewards toward producing diverse Pareto-optimal circuit designs across power, latency, and area trade-offs. This lets designers pick a preferred trade-off a posteriori rather than committing to one aggregation upfront.

entry.title: Harness Self-Evolution for Long-Horizon Terminal Agents

author.name: Ruhan Wang, Yucheng Shi, Zongxia Li, Junyao Yang, Zhongzhi Li, Yue Yu, Haitao Mi, Dongruo Zhou, Leoweiliang

entry.summary: RiseHarness iteratively improves agent harnesses with model weights frozen, focusing on tasks that flip between success and failure under identical configuration and using successful runs as references for failure analysis. It combines trajectories with internal runtime-monitor traces and a Harness Handbook linking evidence to harness behaviors and source code changes.

entry.title: When LLMs Manipulate: Measuring Behavioral, Social, and Temporal Effects

author.name: Sadia Asif, Israel Antonio Rosales Laguan, Shumaila Asif, Haris Khan, Muneeb Asif, Muhammad Zeeshan Karamat

entry.summary: Proposes a behavioral computing framework quantifying how manipulative LLM outputs affect users, generating controlled manipulative stimuli targeting authority, urgency, and social-proof biases via Manipulation Gradient Descent, then modeling cross-user influence and temporal persistence of behavioral harm. It defines behavioral vulnerability as user susceptibility to manipulative AI responses.

entry.title: COMPASS: Routing via Capability-Oriented Model Profiling with Adaptive Search, Selection, and Tool Use

author.name: Amin Rezaei, Pouya Parsa

entry.summary: COMPASS is an agentic LLM router in which an LLM follows a routing recipe, gathers performance and cost evidence through tools, and optionally inspects candidate answers, requiring no routing-specific training. It improves accuracy and lowers cost versus specialized trained routers on LLMRouterBench and DeepSWE, e.g., 69.85% accuracy at lower spend than the RLCascadeRouter baseline.

entry.title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent

author.name: Rui Gong, Ruoyu Wang, Yalun Dai, Hao Li, Sidi Yang, Qihao Zhao, Hongyu Li, Zeyang Guan, Fangzhou Hong, Zhaoxi Chen, Kim-Hui Yap, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: S-Agent 2.0 equips an off-the-shelf general coding agent with a command-line 3D perception toolkit for spatial reasoning, designing the interface so the VLM can close the evidence loop between raw tool readings and usable conclusions. It targets the observed failure where tools return correct evidence but the model still answers incorrectly.

entry.title: INCARBench: A Benchmark for Scientific Configuration in VASP INCAR by Large Language Models

author.name: Bin Shao, Jixiang Li, Xinyue Zhang, Baishun Yang, Zhiyang Liu, Weichao Wang

entry.summary: INCARBench evaluates LLMs on configuring inputs for the VASP first-principles simulation package via configuration generation and repair tasks, covering 19 model configurations. Results show substantial capability differences, with semantic and policy accuracy often high while task-critical scientific correctness remains much lower. Failure analysis shows parameter-level correctness does not imply scientifically valid configurations.

entry.title: ICLHerd: Herding-Based Data Selection for LLMs with In-Context Learning as a Proxy

author.name: Yuqiao Wen, Lili Mou

entry.summary: ICLHerd improves data selection for LLM training by replacing max-similarity selection (which exhibits mode-seeking bias) with a von Mises-Fisher kernel balancing mode-seeking and mode-averaging, and uses in-context learning as a cheap proxy signal to rank candidate data against a curated development set encoding desired skills.

entry.title: Beyond Scalar Leaderboards: Adaptive Sampling for Pareto Frontier Identification in Multi-Objective LLM Arenas

author.name: Liang Twist Shan, Jiahao Ai, Zhimei Ren

entry.summary: The paper presents VB-EGE, a fixed-confidence adaptive sampling algorithm for identifying models on the Pareto frontier in arena-style LLM evaluation, where each human comparison rates a model pair on a prompt along a chosen performance dimension. It progressively eliminates models once sufficient evidence accumulates, reducing the number of costly comparisons needed. This offers a statistically grounded alternative to scalar leaderboards for multi-objective model assessment.

entry.title: Benefit and Cost of Random-Token Replacement under Repeated Data: A Known-Entropy Decomposition and Evidence from Ten Real Corpora

author.name: Wonsup Shin, Jingu Kim

entry.summary: The paper provides a theoretical decomposition of validation loss into approximation, estimation, and memorization terms to explain why random-token replacement (input corruption augmentation) helps when pretraining data is repeated. It shows replacement shrinks predictions toward the corpus average, implying a bias cost independent of memorization but a benefit requiring memorization. Empirical evidence spans ten real corpora.

entry.title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Injae Kim, Minseok Joo, Jihwan Park, Sehyung Kim, Minseong Bae, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: RLSplat addresses the flaw that existing budget-controllable feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting methods predict a dense Gaussian set before pruning, incurring nearly constant latency and memory regardless of the target budget. It instead makes resource usage linear in the requested number of Gaussians, suiting storage- and latency-constrained deployments. This improves the practicality of single-pass 3D reconstruction on limited hardware.

entry.title: Africa-Papers: A 10-Billion-Token Multi-Domain Academic Corpus for African Foundation Language Models

author.name: Mich-Seth Owusu

entry.summary: Africa-Papers is a 10-billion-token multi-domain academic corpus aimed at correcting the severe underrepresentation of African scientific, medical, legal, and agricultural scholarship in pretraining datasets like The Pile and Dolma, where such content constitutes under 0.5 percent of tokens. The corpus targets improved reasoning on tropical epidemiology, smallholder agriculture, and indigenous linguistic structures.

entry.title: DISTRACT: Degradation-Indexed Study of Textual Reference Across Competing Targets

author.name: Dan Zlotnikov, Ohad Ben-Shahar

entry.summary: DISTRACT is a matched-intervention benchmark that holds video, target, and distractor fixed while crossing four text priors with four image-degradation severities to test whether vision-language trackers actually use textual descriptions. Using behavioral contrasts, layerwise probes, and activation patching across five trackers, it finds that only some models (Molmo2, JointNLT) exhibit directed text use while others respond weakly. This mechanistic-evaluation approach to tracking is unusually rigorous.

entry.title: MindView: Benchmarking Generative Multi-View Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Yanbo Wang, Siqi Luo, Siyu Zhang, Chenming Zhu, Wenzhao Zheng, Qian Yu, Juncheng Yan, Bin Fu, Tai Wang, Yu Qiao, Yihao Liu, Jiwen Lu

entry.summary: MindView is a benchmark for generative multi-view spatial intelligence with 1,500 samples from 513 scenes, spanning seven tasks in two families: geometry-dominant tasks (camera position/orientation changes) and semantics-dominant tasks (inferring viewpoints from object references and spatial relations). Evaluation of eleven image generators reveals substantial room for improvement, with a paired comparison analysis.

entry.title: Compaction-Aware Reinforcement Learning For Ascend Triton Kernel Generation

author.name: Chuansai Zhou, Yanlin Liu, Bingning Huang, Shidi Xi, Chao Huang, Boxing Chen, Mingming Zhu, Guanghuan Fang, Ben Feng, Zongzuo Wang

entry.summary: ATRL is a post-training method for LLM agents generating Ascend Triton GPU kernels, refining GRPO with a compaction-aware, segment-level objective to handle long-horizon context accumulation and sparse terminal rewards. It also constrains context growth during multi-turn interaction with execution environments.

entry.title: Dataset Inference for Data Provenance and Privacy Auditing in Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Dariush Wahdany (CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security), Jesse Cresswell (Layer 6 AI), Naiqing Guan (Layer 6 AI), Atiyeh Ashari Ghomi (Layer 6 AI), Franziska Boenisch (CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security), Adam Dziedzic (CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security)

entry.summary: The authors introduce the first dataset inference method for tabular foundation models, determining whether a suspect dataset was used in black-box pre-training. They systematically analyze candidate black-box signals via input manipulation, finding individual signals weak but showing that combined signals can provide meaningful evidence of training data membership. This addresses a growing provenance and privacy gap as TFMs train on proprietary data.

entry.title: TideKV: Delayed KV Eviction via Layer-Wise Chunked Prefill for Memory-Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Yu Wang, Zhu Wang, Ning Hu, Yifan Guo, Xiu Ma, Bin Guo, Zhiwen Yu

entry.summary: TideKV is an on-GPU cache-construction architecture for long-context LLM inference that performs layer-major delayed KV eviction: all prompt chunks are processed within each transformer layer, full-prompt KV is retained only for the active layer, and eviction occurs at layer end. This preserves global context during cache construction while lowering peak prefill memory.

entry.title: EdgeKernelBench: Unified LLM-Driven Kernel Generation for Edge Backends

author.name: Yuhua Zheng, Xueyi Chen, Xinze Zou, Xin Li, Haoji Hu, Huan Wang

entry.summary: EdgeKernelBench is a benchmark and unified IR framework for evaluating LLM-generated kernels across heterogeneous edge hardware backends. It spans progressively larger program scopes from individual operators to compact model graphs, addressing a gap since prior kernel-generation work targeted only server GPUs.

entry.title: ControlJEPA: Principled Trajectory Regularization via Lyapunov Tube Loss

author.name: Thai-Khanh Nguyen, Nhi Y. Pham, Uyen N. B. Vo, Thieu N. Vo, Cuong Pham, Tan M. Nguyen

entry.summary: ControlJEPA introduces a trajectory regularization framework for sequence models based on a discrete-time Lyapunov contraction condition from input-to-state stability theory, penalizing violations with a scale-invariant Lyapunov Tube Loss that keeps hidden-state trajectories within an explicit tube. The paper derives bounds on transversal energy and variance in both full and partial contraction regimes.

entry.title: HCFM: Helmholtz Component Flow Matching for Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Shyam Sundar Saravanan, Tie Luo, Sanjay Madria

entry.summary: HCFM is an unsupervised time-series anomaly detection framework that decomposes the flow-matching vector field into separate transport, compression, and residual heads, isolating density-changing behavior that is anomaly-sensitive without costly Jacobian trace estimation. This decoupling makes anomaly signals from local expansion and contraction accessible. It offers a scalable generative-modeling approach to a classic problem.

entry.title: NeuroAct: Advancing EEG Analysis and Decoding via Dual-Loop Autonomous Research

author.name: Wei Xiong, Jiangtong Li, Han Zhao, Linxiao Yang, Jie Li, Changjun Jiang

entry.summary: NeuroAct is an autonomous research agent framework for EEG analysis that runs dual loops of hypothesis-driven experimentation across EEG foundation models, task predictors, and model combinations. Inner-loop roles (research, development, review) use evidence about signal structure, representations, and training dynamics to select interventions, rather than relying on fixed pipelines or pure reward search. It exemplifies AI-driven scientific automation in a specialized domain.

entry.title: BatchParScale: Sparse Batch-Mixing for Sequence Models

author.name: Hans Peter Lyngs{\o}e Raaschou-jensen (University of Copenhagen), M. Onurcan Kaya (Technical University of Denmark), Desmond Elliott (University of Copenhagen)

entry.summary: The paper extends parallel test-time scaling by allowing multiple reasoning streams to exchange information during inference, addressing the limitation that prior methods like ParScale keep streams independent. The proposed sparse batch-mixing lets discoveries in one rollout influence others. This is relevant to improving inference-time compute efficiency for reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Distributionally-Robust Policy Learning with Observational Data

author.name: Debmalya Mandal

entry.summary: The paper studies policy learning from observational data that maximizes worst-case policy value over f-divergence balls around the data-generating distribution, using cross-fitted doubly-robust scores for conditional treatment effects paired with a DRO solver supporting KL, chi-squared, and CVaR ambiguity sets. Convergence guarantees are established for the resulting estimator. Applications include personalized medicine and welfare targeting.

entry.title: Is it RL or Data? A Controlled Comparison of GRPO and Rejection-Sampling Fine-Tuning

author.name: Lakshya Chaudhry

entry.summary: This controlled study re-examines a 2026 finding that mixed-difficulty prompts give GRPO up to 5x sample efficiency, testing whether the benefit is specific to GRPO or obtainable by rejection-sampling fine-tuning (RFT) given the same prompts, verifier, and token cap on Qwen3-4B-Base with LoRA. Six experimental arms cross the two methods with three prompt sets, using pre-registered hypotheses and falsifiers with multiple seeds. It asks whether reported RL gains reflect the algorithm or merely the data.

entry.title: Asynchronous On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Xidong Wu, Qi Qi, Yuqiong Ji, Shangqian Gao

entry.summary: The paper introduces AsyncOPSD, a framework where a single LLM acts as both student and teacher in on-policy self-distillation, with rollout generation decoupled from learner updates to remove the synchronous generation bottleneck. Because teacher and student share parameters, the approach avoids the multi-model coordination overhead that complicates asynchronous conventional on-policy distillation. This improves training throughput for LLM post-training.

entry.title: Toward Online Robust Zero-Sum Markov Games with Function Approximation

author.name: Chenhao Zhou, Jiyu Wei

entry.summary: The authors develop an optimistic dual robust Bellman framework for online robust zero-sum Markov games with function approximation, combining dual robust Bellman fitting, optimistic minimax planning, backward-validated confidence sets, and exploiter-mix data collection. The analysis via robust Bellman residuals yields regret reductions over existing robust RL theory. This advances multi-agent robust reinforcement learning theory in the challenging function-approximation regime.

entry.title: Strength Controls Change How Interventions Compare Across Sparse Autoencoder Codes

author.name: Jinchen Zhang, Zheyuan Liu, Yihan Zhu, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: The paper studies how strength-control choices (norm matching versus output KL calibration) affect comparisons of interventions on sparse autoencoder codes in Gemma and Llama models, finding that conclusions about intervention effects can reverse depending on the control used. This is a methodological caution for the interpretability community, where SAE-based causal interventions are widely used. Rigorous intervention methodology matters for drawing valid mechanistic claims.

entry.title: PACT: Plan-Augmented Coordination via Trace-Graphs for Dynamic Multi-Agent Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Xiao Zhou, Alex Schutz, Victor-Alexandru Darvariu, Nick Hawes

entry.summary: PACT addresses multi-agent neural combinatorial optimization under dynamics, where problem information is revealed progressively as agents act, a setting existing methods that assume full upfront knowledge fail to handle. It augments the environment graph with auxiliary nodes representing plans and traces to coordinate exploration and exploitation of newly revealed information. This extends neural combinatorial optimization toward more realistic dynamic routing and logistics scenarios.

entry.title: Language-Forcing: Advancing Humanoid Loco-Manipulation via Semantic Alignment of Whole-Body World Action Models

author.name: Yanjun Li, Jiarui Ye, Weiyu Guo, Zixiao He, Kangjie Ye, Dihan Wang, Yishuo Cheng, Zishang Xiang, Mingju Gao, Hao Tang

entry.summary: LANGUAGE-FORCING is a training strategy for whole-body World Action Models that uses a frozen VLM to assess task progress and generate descriptions of plausible future state changes, aligning future visual representations with language to emphasize task-relevant transitions over incidental scene changes. This improves the distinction between progress-bearing and irrelevant visual dynamics for humanoid policies.

entry.title: Recording-Aware Evaluation of Multimodal OT Intrusion Detection

author.name: Mustafa Umut Ozbek, Khalil El-Khatib, Li Yang

entry.summary: Introduces a recording-aware evaluation procedure for ML-based intrusion detection in operational technology, comparing attack windows against background from the same recording and testing temporal alignment against randomized event schedules. On the ProvICS multimodal dataset, cyber modalities distinguish benign and attack recordings before the first labeled attack, suggesting benchmark results may reflect recording artifacts rather than attack detection. This exposes a serious confound in common IDS evaluation.

entry.title: Training with Ciphers to Enhance In-Context Terminology Learning For Translation from Rare Languages

author.name: Deevyanshu Malu, Deeptanshu Malu, Sunita Sarawagi

entry.summary: The paper formalizes in-context term learning (ICTL) for machine translation, showing that standard fine-tuning with in-context examples only weakly teaches models to use context terms for rare-language translation. The proposed RareCipherFT anneals training data where rare terms are replaced by character-shuffled ciphers, forcing the model to copy terms from context, improving ICTL without lexical resources. This targets low-resource language translation, an impactful application area.

entry.title: Is User Calibration Still Necessary for Continuous Myoelectric Control? A Closed-Loop Comparison of Calibration-Free Controllers

author.name: Amir Reza Hariri, Kevin B. Englehart, Erik Scheme

entry.summary: This study compares six calibration-free myoelectric controllers trained on 306 users against three calibrated controllers in a closed-loop Fitts' law target-acquisition task with sixteen human participants. Despite calibrated controllers achieving higher offline accuracy (90.6 percent versus 73.1 percent), the closed-loop results inform whether expensive per-user calibration remains necessary for real-world prosthetic and rehabilitation control.

entry.title: Reliability-Preserving Compression for Deployable Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Sagar Kumar, Shailja Sharma, Tirthajit Baruah, Punit Rathore

entry.summary: This work shows that post-training compression (quantization, pruning, distillation) of medical MRI/CT segmentation models can keep Dice scores stable while degrading uncertainty signals crucial for safety-critical deployment. It proposes SGAV-MP, a mixed-precision compression framework that selects layer precisions under explicit reliability constraints.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Controllers for Fusion Scenario Development

author.name: Evgeny Adishchev, Maxim Nurgaliev, Dmitry Sorokin, Alexander Granovsky, Maksim Stokolesov, Igor Prokofyev, Eduard Khairutdinov, Georgy Subbotin

entry.summary: Replaces iterative manual tuning of tokamak discharge controllers with a single goal-conditioned RL controller trained once against a free-boundary equilibrium and transport simulator, so new scenarios are specified only by target waveforms of physical quantities. Aims to streamline scenario development from breakdown to flat-top in fusion experiments.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Policy and Reward for Code Generation: A Mechanistic Study of Single-Adapter Drift

author.name: Amarsaikhan Batjargal, Noriko Tomuro

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether the SPARK framework, which co-evolves a policy and a reward model by recycling execution-verified rollouts, transfers from reasoning tasks to code generation. It includes a mechanistic study of single-adapter drift when policy and reward are trained jointly. The work clarifies whether execution-grounded reflection provides genuine self-improvement signal.

entry.title: Which Long Documents Matter? A Controlled Study of Data Selection for Context Extension

author.name: Junlong Jia, Jiang Zhou, Xing Wu, Chaochen Gao Tinghao Yu, Feng Zhang, Lilin Wang

entry.summary: A controlled study of data selection for long-context extension training on Qwen2.5-3B at 128K under matched 6B-token budgets. The surprising finding is that random sampling of natural long documents beats repacking, and selecting documents by LongPPL key-token density yields further gains where generic-quality and LLM-judge selectors fail. The proposed truncLongPPL scores only a truncated prefix, achieving near full-span performance at a measured speedup (about 2.28x).

entry.title: A Measurement Perspective on Benchmarking LLM-Generated Text Detectors using Item Response Theory

author.name: Yanbin Zhao, Zhipeng Chen, Guangsheng Bao, Guandong Zhang, Yan Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes treating AI-text-detector benchmarks through multidimensional item response theory, modeling benchmark texts as measurement items and detectors as respondents. This yields text-level discrimination and difficulty parameters, revealing how benchmark composition shapes detector comparisons in ways aggregate metrics like F1 or AUC cannot.

entry.title: Truncated Reasoning Under a Budget: Evaluating System-1 Models as Decision-makers

author.name: Zhongyin Wang, Zhaoqian Xue, Junting Mu, Haozheng Liu, Ye Yuan, Haolun Wu, Lingyao Li

entry.summary: Evaluates using a System-1 decision model (Jev) to read truncated reasoning traces instead of forcing the reasoner to answer from incomplete chains of thought. Across seven reasoners and five benchmarks, Jev yields higher accuracy at tested budgets (500-16,000 tokens), improving accuracy by 4.1 points overall and 8.6 points on truncated questions at a 1,500-token budget with statistically significant gains.

entry.title: Rethinking BPE: Merge Selection as Model Selection

author.name: Vijini Liyanage, Fran\c{c}ois Yvon

entry.summary: This paper reframes the choice of BPE merge budget as a statistical model selection problem and derives information-theoretic criteria for computing optimal merge sets directly from corpus statistics. It also augments BPE training corpora with synthetic texts to improve merge selection in low-data conditions.

entry.title: Joint, Decoupled, or Agent: When Each Multimodal Alignment Paradigm Wins

author.name: Yi Fang, Gaurav Srivastava, Sirui Ding, Xuan Wang

entry.summary: This work compares three multimodal alignment paradigms, joint pretrained encoders, independently pretrained encoders with a fusion head, and an LLM agent with unimodal readouts, across 16 paired datasets in five domains and multiple label budgets. No paradigm dominates the 144 dataset-budget combinations, with wins split roughly evenly among the three. The result offers practical guidance on when each multimodal design choice pays off.

entry.title: Medical Fine-Tuning Reshapes, Not Reduces, Patient-Facing AI Risk: A Rubric-Based, LLM-Judge Evaluation Framework

author.name: Savan Doshi

entry.summary: The paper introduces a risk-sensitive evaluation framework for patient-facing medical LLM responses, scoring six categories of risk-bearing language (treatment directives, contraindications, dosage, urgency-triage cues, high-alert medications, overconfident assertions) with a three-judge LLM ensemble. It finds medical fine-tuning reshapes rather than reduces patient-facing risk. This argues that factuality-only evaluation is insufficient for clinical deployment.

entry.title: GLOBE: Geometry-Led Online Behavioral Early Exit via Unit-Sphere Trajectories

author.name: Xinyue Peng, Zhenlin Liang, Meng Cai, Hua Wang

entry.summary: GLOBE is a training-free online method for early termination of chain-of-thought reasoning: it embeds completed reasoning segments on a unit sphere and analyzes the semantic trajectory shape, combining a trial-answer phase with confidence thresholds and trajectory-phase checks. This avoids wasted generation after the correct answer is already reachable, cutting cost and sometimes preventing correct intermediates from degrading. No training or model modification is required.

entry.title: VitronEdit: Universal Visual Editing across Images, Videos, and 3D Scenes

author.name: Jing Wang, Yanlin Li, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu, Shengqiong Wu, Hao Fei

entry.summary: VitronEdit is a unified framework for instruction-based visual editing spanning images, videos, and 3D scenes, using a shared sequence representation and progressive multimodal training to transfer editing knowledge from data-rich 2D modalities to data-scarce 3D editing. It adds geometry-aware post-training leveraging a pretrained geometry reconstruction model. This extends unified editing beyond the image-video pair to 3D.

entry.title: Causal Spatiotemporal State Evolution for Monocular 4D Reconstruction

author.name: Qiaowei Miao, Yijing Guo, Lipei Zhang, Qifeng Cheng, Yuru Xiao, Ziqian Ni, Sheng Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a feed-forward framework for monocular 4D reconstruction that models visual geometry as a causally evolving state using a Causal Spatiotemporal Mamba, with joint supervision coupling geometry and motion rather than treating them as disjoint objectives.

entry.title: Differentiable Task-Driven Coded Aperture Camera Design with 3D Gaussian Scene Representations

author.name: Chengyang Yan, Donald G. Dansereau

entry.summary: The paper presents a fully differentiable framework for jointly designing coded-aperture camera optics and downstream depth-from-defocus perception tasks, using 3D Gaussian scene representations rather than pre-captured 2D images or non-differentiable simulators. It demonstrates monocular and stereo coded-aperture depth camera designs. This bridges hardware optics design and perception optimization end to end.

entry.title: OV-Foam: How 3D Representations Shape Semantic Feature Lifting

author.name: Yousef Rajeh (King Abdullah University of Science and Technology), Alejandra Esparza Pelcastre (Universidad Panamericana), Ivan Viola (King Abdullah University of Science and Technology), Dominik Engel (King Abdullah University of Science and Technology)

entry.summary: OV-Foam examines how the choice of 3D representation affects open-vocabulary semantic feature lifting, observing that backprojection becomes a well-conditioned least-squares problem only when primitives do not share rays. It uses a power-diagram-based representation with zero primitive overlap, yielding closer-to-optimal feature lifting for 3D Gaussian splatting-style scenes.

entry.title: Predictive Latents for Autoregressive Language Models: Possibility, Gauge, and Obstruction

author.name: Yuzhou Hong

entry.summary: This theoretical note formalizes latent iterative computation in language models (continuous thoughts, pause steps, recurrent depth) by separating token risk, teacher-forced latent risk, and open-loop risk on a single latent process. It characterizes when a width-k latent with a linear transition and refit unembedding can match the Bayes next-token predictor, and identifies identifiability conditions and obstructions.

entry.title: PLaCA: Learning Patch-Level Future Latent Change for Action Generation

author.name: Zhan Yi, Yuchen Wang, Chao Li, Lei Hong, Boyuan Yang

entry.summary: PLaCA is a world-to-action framework for vision-language-action models that predicts spatially structured patch-level future latent change rather than full future images or heavily compressed latents. This preserves local information about expected environmental changes while avoiding the computational cost of complete future image generation. It is a sensible efficiency-oriented contribution to the growing world-models-for-manipulation literature.

entry.title: RadGeoLoc: Radar Geolocalization via Particle Filtering

author.name: Shaunak Kolhe, Peng Jiang, Kasi Viswanath, Srikanth Saripalli

entry.summary: RadGeoLoc localizes a spinning radar against overhead satellite RGB imagery using a particle filter with a learned observation model, leveraging a radar representation pretrained by masked reconstruction and radar odometry for pose propagation. Evaluated across 31 routes on 8 urban and offroad datasets with only a coarse local prior, it targets GNSS-denied field autonomy. Radar-to-satellite geolocalization is a valuable capability for GPS-denied environments and the evaluation scale is convincing.

entry.title: Knowing When to Stop Thinking: A Dissection of Expected Free Energy as a Test-Time Compute Controller for Latent World-Model Planning

author.name: Tong Zhang, Zhiyuan Shi, Yun Peng, Tao Xie

entry.summary: This paper dissects when expected free energy (EFE) can serve as a test-time compute controller for planners using learned latent world models, separately testing candidate scoring, stopping, and online predictor update components. Stopping when elite cost stalls reduces wasted refinement on plateauing tasks with success close to fixed-depth references, while rewarding model disagreement can lower success with a frozen model and online updates fail when training data omit regions needed to reach the goal. The analysis offers a candid, fine-grained view of EFE's actual utility in planning.

entry.title: Predicting silent failures of learned inference under restricted access: what measurement physics and prior information explain

author.name: Mario Gianni

entry.summary: This paper studies the blind set: cases where learned priors used for reconstruction under restricted measurement access produce intervals that exclude the truth while all ground-truth-free diagnostics appear normal. The authors derive an exact risk factorization for linear-Gaussian models, approximate it by linearizing a VAE prior, and validate prospectively on real X-ray CT data.

entry.title: MoSAIK: Motion Search with Artificial Intelligence in K-space

author.name: Oscar Dabrowski, Abijith Jagannath, Fr\'ed\'eric Grouiller, S\'ebastien Courvoisier

entry.summary: MoSAIK retrospectively estimates in-plane rigid-body motion directly from multi-coil T2-weighted turbo spin-echo brain MRI k-space data, using k-space self-consistency violations without navigators or reference scans, and feeds predicted motion parameters into model-based motion-aware reconstruction. It targets motion artefacts that reduce diagnostic confidence and force repeated scans.

entry.title: When Does an Added Planning Capability Create Operational Value? An Observable Evidence Standard

author.name: Yihua Xu, Yan Lyu, Jize Li, Jiani He, You Lin, Yidan Hu, Rubing Qiang

entry.summary: Proposes an observable evidence standard for attributing operational value to individual components of industrial AI planning systems, separating opportunity to act, executed-plan change, operational consequence, equivalence, uncertainty, and operating scope. Applied via forecast-to-plan replay on Favorita, M5, and Walmart datasets, it exposes limits of single-indicator evaluation such as composite policies concealing negligible component contributions.

entry.title: Runtime Control for AI Agents: Closing the Evaluation--Execution Gap in Operational Workflows

author.name: Jayesh Bhadane, Ramachandra Yerramsetti, Rajesh Gupta, Sumit Kumar

entry.summary: Defines the evaluation-execution gap: approvals valid at issuance may no longer authorize execution after relevant facts, policy, or authority change, in agent workflows involving commitments like payments. The paper specifies a state-bound runtime assurance layer that binds execution allowances to decision-relevant bases, invalidates them on logged changes, and rechecks admissibility at dispatch, with eight enumerated failure modes.

entry.title: Beyond Experience: Knowledge-Guided Evolution for NPU Kernel Generation

author.name: Xi Chen, Ming Shen, Haotian Yan, Ruoyu Sun, Tianjun Yao

entry.summary: Presents ASCENDEVOLVE, an LLM-agent system for generating kernels on Ascend NPUs that grounds evolution in external hardware knowledge rather than only self-accumulated experience, arguing memory of past trials cannot supply unknown mechanisms. The approach targets the gap where emerging accelerator programming models are barely represented in pretraining data.

entry.title: Privacy-preserving inference on hosted models: a learned input-embedding transform for frozen Qwen3.8-27B

author.name: Mahendra Roopa, Srikanth Roopa

entry.summary: The authors keep prompts on the client by locally converting text to embedding vectors and passing them through a small 55.6M-parameter trained transform before sending to a host running frozen Qwen3.8-27B, so the host never receives text or token ids. The transform combines a forward-KL utility term with an auxiliary repulsion term, evaluated on held-out MMLU questions against the frozen model as a fixed judge.

entry.title: Staged Continual Adaptation of Multimodal Foundation Models for Japanese Financial Documents

author.name: Genshin Kakimoto, Atsushi Yanagisawa

entry.summary: Tracking an 8.4B multimodal model through three post-training phases on Japanese financial documents, the study finds phases interact non-additively: math-only distillation overwrites earlier financial knowledge while domain tuning repairs more than it installs. A skip-phase ablation is best for domain knowledge but forfeits numerical-reasoning gains, showing per-phase contributions are not decomposable.

entry.title: IECG: Weakly-Supervised Interpretability-Enhancing Foundation Model for Electrocardiogram

author.name: Huynh Dang Nguyen, Trong-Thang Pham, Anh-Thuan Do, Phuong-Nhi Dinh, Brijesh Patel, Ngan Le, Van Nguyen

entry.summary: IECG is a weakly-supervised ECG foundation model that jointly performs diagnostic classification and abnormality localization without manual region annotations. It derives heatmap pseudo-labels from clinical ECG knowledge and uses KL-divergence loss to align CLS-token attention with diagnostically relevant regions.

entry.title: OptScientist: Automated Discovery of Optimization Laws

author.name: Ma ZhenYao, Yue Liang, Jian-Qiao Zhu

entry.summary: OptScientist is an automated discovery framework that infers compact symbolic optimization laws from data, based on a model that represents data as optimization problems and extracts their symbolic form. It embeds this in an LLM agentic system that integrates literature priors, proposes candidate laws, abstracts mechanisms, and suggests new experiments.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Small Language Models for Reliable VASP INCAR Generation

author.name: Xinyue Zhang, Jixiang Li, Bin Shao, Baishun Yang, Zhiyang Liu, Weichao Wang

entry.summary: This companion work shows a small language model fine-tuned on reference VASP calculations, combined with a deterministic post-processor called VASPGuard, can reliably generate INCAR files from natural-language requests. The resulting INCAR-SLM built on Qwen3-4B outperforms every general-purpose LLM evaluated on INCARBench while supporting local, offline, privacy-preserving deployment. This addresses cost and privacy limitations of relying on proprietary cloud models in high-throughput materials workflows.

entry.title: Expert-Guided Rubrics as Dense Reward Signals for Reinforcement Learning in Non-Verifiable Domains

author.name: Ashish Bansal, Hossam Amer, Keerat Kaur Guliani, Parinita Edke, Lesley Matheson, Leizer Teran

entry.summary: The paper proposes using expert-guided rubrics as dense reward signals for RL with GRPO in non-verifiable domains such as financial-services agent tasks, where binary verifiable rewards are unavailable and sparse rewards give no learning signal. It addresses query rewriting and retrieval under domain-specific constraints requiring graded subject-matter-expert judgment. This extends RLHF-style training beyond verifiable tasks.

entry.title: Dynamic Dual-Feedback Conformal Inference for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Songlin Du, Ling Luo, Uwe Aickelin

entry.summary: The paper extends online conformal inference for time series by adding a second feedback signal: instead of relying only on miscoverage indicators, it also uses empirical prediction thresholds derived from an oracle conformal method to adaptively adjust prediction sets under distributional change. This improves uncertainty quantification for sequential forecasting.

entry.title: ValiAssist: Scaling LLM-generated Programming Feedback Validation by Demonstration

author.name: Xiaohang Tang, Rehema Abulikemu, Peng Gao, Yan Chen

entry.summary: ValiAssist is a validation-by-demonstration system that infers reusable validation logic from how instructors revise AI-generated programming feedback, letting instructors inspect and refine that logic across student submissions. A study with 16 instructors shows it produces feedback better aligned with pedagogical goals. It addresses the practical gap between scalable LLM feedback generation and instructor quality control.

entry.title: Beyond the Prompt: Recovering Hidden Concepts in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Zhengfeng Zheng, Minghong Fang

entry.summary: EmbGA is an embedding-space genetic algorithm that recovers concepts present in a set of generated images but absent from the prompt, enabling audits of implanted hidden associations in text-to-image models. It avoids limitations of gradient-based, evolutionary, and LM-guided search approaches. This provides a practical auditing tool for a genuine safety concern in generative models.

entry.title: ABench: Adversarily Benchmarking Large Language Models across Taxonomized Values

author.name: Liping Yang, Yongqi Leng, Jingting Zheng, Yuqi Ren, Shaolin Zhu, Deyi Xiong

entry.summary: ABench is a handcrafted Chinese-language alignment benchmark with a hierarchical taxonomy of 158 value subcategories and 2,895 open-ended questions using role-playing and logical traps to probe robustness against adversarial value induction. It addresses the English-centric and discriminative-task bias of existing alignment benchmarks. This supports safer deployment of LLMs in Chinese cultural contexts.

entry.title: A Head Camera Is (Almost) All You Need: An Electronics-Free UMI Glove Labelled and Observed by One Moving Camera

author.name: Yosub Shin, Yuan Liu, Igor Molybog

entry.summary: This paper shows that a single $122 egocentric head camera paired with a $22 electronics-free glove with printed fiducials can replace the wrist camera, pose tracker, and multiple synchronized data streams in handheld robot demonstration collection. The same camera frames used for pose extraction are the ones a policy will see at deployment, simplifying calibration. This matters because cheaper, simpler demonstration collection could lower the barrier to large-scale robot imitation learning.

entry.title: Hallucinations of Large Language Models in Cross-Language Code Translation: Phenomena and Mitigation

author.name: Yali Du, Yunji Zhang, Ming Li

entry.summary: This paper systematically characterizes hallucinations specific to cross-language code translation by LLMs: outputs conflicting with the source program, violating target-language facts, or introducing inconsistent dependencies. Such failures are especially dangerous because small semantic deviations can silently change program behavior. The study covers taxonomy, distribution, and mitigation strategies for this underexplored failure mode.

entry.title: APRIL: Ambiguity-Aware Expert Routing for Respiratory Sound Domain-Incremental Learning

author.name: Xinhong Li, Weiping Tu

entry.summary: APRIL is an exemplar-free domain-incremental learning framework for respiratory sound classification that uses a frozen BEATs backbone with sequentially inherited, isolated domain experts. It introduces ambiguity-aware routing to select the correct expert at inference when domain labels are absent and acoustic distributions overlap, addressing catastrophic forgetting under privacy constraints in clinical deployment.

entry.title: Reframing Object-Centric Reinforcement Learning: From Absolute to Relative Representations

author.name: Cedric Derstroff, Jannis Bl\"uml, Janosch Moos, Michael Girstl, Zihan Ye, Debora Clever, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: The paper proposes ORCA, describing objects in anchor-relative frames rather than fixed global coordinates, and ORBiT, a transformer architecture with object-relative inductive biases for object-centric RL. This removes the need for agents to relearn behaviors at every absolute location and prevents performance collapse under scene shifts.

entry.title: Local Inference of LLMs on Long Contexts: A Data Systems Perspective

author.name: Mattias D\"urrmeier, Alberto Lerner

entry.summary: The authors study why serving long-context LLMs on a single local GPU is difficult, framing inference bottlenecks from a data-systems perspective rather than defaulting to quantization. By identifying memory and data-management limitations that prevent local long-context serving, the work points toward cheaper, private, rate-limit-free inference. It is relevant to democratizing long-context LLM use outside multi-GPU datacenters.

entry.title: CountVideoBench: A Benchmark to Evaluate Prediction Biases on the Object Counting task by Video-Language Models

author.name: Marc Chapus, Carlos Crispim-Junior, V\'eronique Eglin, Atilla Baskurt

entry.summary: The paper surveys nine VideoQA benchmarks and shows their ground-truth count distributions are heavily skewed toward small values (median at most five), masking counting failures of video-language models at rare cardinalities. CountVideoBench provides 2,600 synthetic videos spanning 26 cardinalities from 5 to 50 to expose value-dependent prediction biases. It complements ABACUS in revealing that numerical competence of multimodal models is systematically mismeasured.

entry.title: Spatially Informed and Direction Sensitive Representation Learning for Spatial Transcriptomics

author.name: Azim Dehghani Amirabad, Ali Khodabandeh Yalabadi, Artem Moskalev, Yun-Ching Chen, Mehdi Pirooznia, Scott Oloff, Rui Liao

entry.summary: This work presents a representation learning method for spatial transcriptomics that captures both spatially informative gene signals and intercellular organization, addressing limitations of prior approaches that reduce the microenvironment to proximity alone or rely on arbitrary absolute coordinates. The method encodes direction-sensitive cell-cell relationships to distinguish cells with similar neighbor distances but distinct spatial organization.

entry.title: Beyond Prediction: A Component-Level Study of Concept Recovery in In-Context Learning

author.name: Xufeng Liu, Fang Wan, Yi Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces a component-level evaluation framework for in-context learning that decomposes concepts into defining parts and applies controlled structural interventions to determine which components models actually recover from demonstrations. Testing four instruction-tuned LLMs, it separates model limitations from demonstration ambiguity.

entry.title: Visual Causal-chain Bookmarking: Retrieval-Weighted Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning from Delayed Reward

author.name: Prathap Selvakumar

entry.summary: This paper introduces Visual Causal-chain Bookmarking (VCBM), a method that concentrates credit on the decision points causally responsible for an episode's return in delayed-reward RL settings. It is evaluated in two regimes, including a low-dimensional MDP with ground-truth comparisons against the RUDDER baseline, converging to about 95% correct decisions. The work addresses the fundamental credit-assignment bottleneck when rewards arrive many steps after the causal action.

entry.title: Muon Operates Beyond the Edge of Stability

author.name: Niko Covic, Baraq Lipshitz, Alexander Padula, Stefan Visnjic

entry.summary: This empirical study shows the Flat Minima Hypothesis applies to the Muon optimizer, with sharpness correlating with generalization gap (r = 0.45-0.69 on CIFAR-10). Notably, Muon operates above the sharpness-based Adaptive Edge of Stability threshold that bounds diagonally-preconditioned optimizers like Adam, yet remains stable, suggesting a fundamentally different optimization regime. The authors also derive Muon's implicit preconditioner.

entry.title: Latent State Utilization in Probabilistic Circuits

author.name: Zilei Shao, Anji Liu

entry.summary: This paper uses mutual information to study why adding latent states to probabilistic circuits yields diminishing likelihood gains. Experiments with Hidden Chow-Liu Trees on ImageNet32 show that learned dependence grows slowly and stays well below both the latent-state upper bound and estimated dependence in the data, and the authors track how strongly samples favor particular latent states during training.

entry.title: A Multi-Step Inertial ADMM Algorithm for Federated Learning

author.name: Hao Li, Qingsong Wang, Xihong Yan, Chengcheng Yan, Deren Han

entry.summary: This paper introduces MiFedADMM, a multi-step inertial variant of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) for federated learning. It uses multiple historical iterates on the server to build a higher-order extrapolation after each aggregation, accelerating convergence while addressing communication overhead and system heterogeneity, with convergence guarantees under mild assumptions.

entry.title: LLM-Based Evaluation Planning for Heterogeneous Optimization

author.name: Nian Ran, Sebastian Brulin, Markus Olhofer, Mauricio A. \'Alvarez, Richard Allmendinger

entry.summary: REP-HO replaces hand-designed heuristic selection rules in heterogeneous optimization with an LLM reasoning-based planner that receives surrogate predictions, uncertainties, costs, and budget information. The work demonstrates that LLMs can act as decision-makers inside engineering optimization loops rather than just as text generators.

entry.title: UpLoop: Upcycling Large Language Models with Gated Loop

author.name: Tieyuan Chen, Huabin Liu, Yingtao Zhang, Shijie Li, Tengyu Pan, Weiyao Lin, Jianguo Li

entry.summary: UpLoop converts pretrained non-looped LLMs into looped models via layer-wise recurrence with hidden-wise gates on attention and MLP residual branches, preserving the pretrained depth hierarchy while making additional loop iterations act as progressive refinements. This offers a cheap post-training upcycling alternative to expensive from-scratch looped pretraining.

entry.title: Decentralized Online Exp-Concave Optimization

author.name: Hao Qiu, Mengxiao Zhang, Yuanyu Wan

entry.summary: This paper resolves an open problem in decentralized online convex optimization by showing that logarithmic regret is achievable for exp-concave losses. The authors propose Decentralized Online Newton Step (D-ONS), which combines blocking and accelerated gossip techniques with the Online Newton Step algorithm, achieving a regret bound scaling with the network spectral gap and polylogarithmically in the time horizon.

entry.title: LLM Agents as Suppliers of Physical System Models: Calibration and Acceptance in Modelica

author.name: J\"org Frochte, Herbert Schmidt

entry.summary: This paper tests LLM coding agents acting as suppliers that build Modelica simulation models of physical systems from client specifications, including a real switching magnet. It proposes accepting models by membership in the set of admissible models rather than matching a single reference, and adds physical invariant checks that catch, for example, an energy-creating model that otherwise reaches the noise floor. This matters because it reframes acceptance testing for AI-generated engineering artifacts.

entry.title: Trackable Skill Library Lifecycle Management for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xi Zhu, Yuanlin Duan, Changyi Yang, Kai Mei, Riyang Bao, Shichao Zhu, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: TrackRL addresses skill lifecycle management in skill-augmented agentic RL, tracking whether individual skills become redundant, remain valuable scaffolding, or turn harmful as the policy evolves. It tackles attribution problems like free-riding among co-retrieved skills and missing counterfactual evidence to enable reliable library management. This improves long-horizon agent training efficiency.

entry.title: Learning When to Abort in Transformer Planning: A Mechanistic Study

author.name: Shi Feng, Qimin Zhong, Siwei Wang, Yifei Shen, Shang-Hua Teng, Hao Liao, Wei Chen

entry.summary: The paper studies whether transformers can recognize their own planning errors, abstracting planning as graph path-finding and training models to emit an abort token upon invalid transitions. It constructs a transformer with width O(|V|) that provably detects all invalid transitions and provides a mechanistic analysis. This contributes to understanding error recognition as a component of planning capability in transformers.

entry.title: Enhanced Masked Diffusion Unlearning

author.name: Tomer Garber, Tom Tirer

entry.summary: The paper improves machine unlearning for masked diffusion language models (MDLMs), building on the first public MDU method by identifying and fixing two of its limitations via anchor-based divergence minimization refinements. As MDLMs move toward deployment, effective unlearning of sensitive or copyrighted content is essential. This extends an important safety capability to an emerging model class.

entry.title: FTFM: Factorized Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Josif Grabocka

entry.summary: FTFM is a tabular foundation model architecture that preserves cell-level representations while factorizing computation through one contextual latent per row and one per column, so cells interact via row and column latents rather than direct attention. This resolves a trade-off between expensive cell-level attention and lossy row-embedding collapse in prior tabular foundation models. If it delivers competitive accuracy at reduced cost, it advances in-context learning for tabular data.

entry.title: Progress-Guided Preference Generation for Aligning Generative Control Policies

author.name: Tung M. Luu, Tri Ton, Duc M. Nguyen, Xuan Thanh Nguyen, Nguyen Gia Binh, Quang Tan Nguyen, Vu Duong, Daniel Sonntag, Duy M. H. Nguyen, Vien Anh Ngo, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: PGPG is an unsupervised preference alignment framework for generative control policies that removes the need for human annotation by deriving pseudo-preference labels from autonomously collected rollouts, using ordered coverage alignment against a small expert demonstration set to measure sequential progress. This enables preference-based fine-tuning of imitation-learned policies at scale. It addresses a key bottleneck: scarcity of expert data and cost of human labeling.

entry.title: The KV-Surgeon: Compensation-Aware Offline KV-Cache Compaction

author.name: Moritz Wagner, Christophe Roux, Max Zimmer, Sebastian Pokutta

entry.summary: KV-Surgeon addresses offline KV-cache compaction by accounting for nonlinear coupling among deletion decisions, which prior per-entry scoring ignores because softmax renormalization links all attention weights. Using calibration data, it derives a tractable quadratic surrogate with closed-form expressions that captures interaction effects between retained and deleted entries. This improves the quality of compacted caches for repeatedly queried fixed contexts.

entry.title: Learning from a Bandit Learner

author.name: Michela Petriconi, Nicolas Menet, Claire Vernade

entry.summary: This inverse-bandit theory paper infers a demonstrator's subjective beliefs about suboptimality gaps rather than true reward parameters, considering no-regret randomized demonstrators like Thompson sampling. It characterizes algorithm families admitting per-step inversion of arm-selection distributions, and identifies an inherent stability-coverage trade-off where inversion becomes ill-conditioned as the demonstrator concentrates on one arm. This has implications for imitation learning and preference elicitation from adaptive agents.

entry.title: Nash-MOPD: Optimizing Task Trade-offs in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Siyuan Gan, Bo Yang, Linjian Meng, Boyan Wang, Xiaolong Qi, Jing Huo, Yang Gao

entry.summary: This paper proposes Nash-MOPD, an adaptive domain allocation scheme for multi-teacher on-policy distillation that formulates budget sharing among domain-expert teachers as a game-theoretic trade-off problem. It addresses the weakness of prior heuristics like fixed ratios and reverse-KL-based allocation that under-train slower-improving domains. The work matters because distilling multiple specialist teachers into one student is a growing post-training strategy for building generalist models.

entry.title: ITU-DESC: a missingness-aware machine-learning dementia risk score in the UK Biobank cohort

author.name: Abdullah Kavakl{\i}, Faik Boray Tek

entry.summary: ITU-DESC is an explainable machine-learning dementia risk score combining broad feature selection across roughly 8,000 candidate features with explicit control of informative missingness, evaluated on about 500,000 UK Biobank participants over a median 16.6-year follow-up. It uses unconditional random hot-deck imputation to withhold missingness patterns and stabilized BorutaSHAP feature selection across seeds. This is a well-powered clinical risk-prediction contribution.

entry.title: Global Time-Aware Conditioning (GTC): A Mechanism for Time-Aware Pediatric Sleep Representation Learning

author.name: Saurav Raj Pandey, Harlin Lee

entry.summary: Introduces Global Time-Aware Conditioning, a mechanism that conditions self-supervised sleep representations on where each input window falls within the full night of sleep, complementing local positional encodings. Evaluated across three SSL frameworks, five clinical tasks, and two independent pediatric cohorts with severe class imbalance, GTC generally improves F1 and AUPRC. This matters because explicit session-level temporal awareness is often missing in sleep representation learning despite clinically meaningful physiology changes overnight.

entry.title: Trajectory Replay: Continuous-Time Mixture Transport for Lifelong Generative Models

author.name: Alessandro Palma, Charles Jones, Tristan Cinquin, Fabian J. Theis, Frederik Wenkel

entry.summary: Trajectory replay improves generative replay for lifelong learning with continuous-time generative models by bypassing full sample generation. Instead of simulating trajectories (which accumulates discretization error and degrades replayed distributions), it trains an updated velocity field to match both a frozen historical velocity along its trajectories and the incoming task's velocity field, weighted by a stability-plasticity coefficient. This addresses a core bottleneck in continual learning for diffusion-style generative models.

entry.title: Next Best Action: Causal Constrained Offline RL for Business Action Targeting

author.name: Surya Ramachandiran, Yiming Li, Juan Mancilla-Caceres, Tao Ye, Jun Liu

entry.summary: This paper formulates Next Best Action selection in business contexts (discounts, promotions, lifecycle interventions) as a Constrained Markov Decision Process, integrating off-policy causal correction of customer dynamics directly into the LP formulation. The approach maximizes long-term economic value while enforcing operational guardrails, and the LP structure yields shadow prices interpretable as constraint values.

entry.title: FrameScout: Scouting Query-Relevant Frames for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Haonan Hu, Shuhao Chen, Weisen Jiang, Lizhao Gao, James Kwok, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: FrameScout improves keyframe selection for long-video VideoLLMs with a streaming selector that uses a sliding-window KV cache and successor aggregation for temporally contextualized frame scoring, plus ranking objectives that are easier to optimize than prior chunk-isolated approaches. This addresses token budget limits when videos span tens of minutes to hours.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Discovery of Motion Styles for Compositional Robot Control

author.name: Heedo Woo, Antonio Marino, Eduardo Sebasti\'an, Amanda Prorok

entry.summary: CODES is a framework for compositional robot control that discovers a repertoire of motion styles from diverse demonstration recordings using motion retargeting, weakly supervised consensus encoding, and density-based clustering, without a prescribed style taxonomy. It then composes a selected style with independent task commands, balancing potentially competing objectives when a robot has more degrees of freedom than the task requires. This enables style-preserving task execution from unlabeled data.

entry.title: When Does Evidence-Graph Structure Predict Answer Correctness? Label-Free Abstention for Structured Retrieval

author.name: Anjan Goswami

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free abstention signal for retrieval systems based on the weighted cut between selected and unselected evidence in an evidence graph, requiring no correctness labels or trained confidence model. On MemoryAgentBench FactConsolidation multi-hop queries it improves area under the precision-coverage curve from 0.736 to 0.785 over the best score baseline. The work addresses the practical gap between a high retrieval score and actual answer trustworthiness.

entry.title: Training-Free Prompt Selection for Efficient Reinforcement Learning With Partial Rollouts

author.name: Lei Jiang, Honghui Bao, Yue Zhou, Zhengyao Gu, Langzhou He, Natalie Parde

entry.summary: LIFT is a training-free data selection method for RL with verifiable rewards that estimates prompt value using hidden states from partial reasoning rollouts, addressing the problem that 26-32% of full greedy rollouts fail to terminate within budget. By relying only on partial rollouts, it reduces computational cost of prompt selection while still identifying informative training examples.

entry.title: Learning from the Right Regions: Class-Conditioned Explanation Guidance for Medical Imaging

author.name: Zubair Faruqui, Rahul Dubey

entry.summary: This work proposes a class-conditioned explanation-guided learning framework for multi-label medical imaging that builds separate Grad-CAM explanations per positive class and penalizes evidence outside annotated regions. It is evaluated across 14 abnormalities using EfficientNet and ViT backbones. This addresses shortcut learning in safety-critical clinical models.

entry.title: Rethinking EEG Spatial Super-Resolution as Dynamic State Decomposition and Filtering

author.name: Hongjun Liu, Leyu Zhou, Chang Ge, Shitong Duan, Chao Yao

entry.summary: This paper reframes EEG spatial super-resolution, reconstructing high-density neural signals from sparse electrodes, as a sequential state filtering problem. The proposed Dynamic State Filtering (DSF) method explicitly separates predictable state evolution from newly emerging changes in the signal, rather than relying on a single temporal reconstruction pathway. This could improve brain-computer interfaces and clinical neuromonitoring where electrode density is limited.

entry.title: Spherical Physics-informed Neural Operator with Multi-scale Coupling for Meteorological Downscaling

author.name: Yiqiang Ye, Yichi Wang, Haodi Zhang, Jiawei Wen, Jiahui Jiang, Zhaoyu Zhong, Jiangjian Yu, Chunxia Xiao

entry.summary: This paper introduces a Spherical Physics-informed Neural Operator for meteorological downscaling that uses Spherical Laplacian Decomposition to split atmospheric fields into hierarchical frequency components with exact point-wise correspondence across scales. It also adds a localized spherical integral operator for evaluation at arbitrary locations, addressing geometric distortion and multi-scale coupling issues in neural-operator weather models.

entry.title: Query-Dependent Reading for Quantized Inner-Product Estimation: A Minimax Separation

author.name: Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Siddharth Bhandari, Shiva Prasad Kasiviswanathan

entry.summary: This theory paper studies quantized inner-product estimation in a bit-probe model where an encoder stores w bits before seeing a query and a reader probes at most r of them. The authors prove that query-independent readers gain nothing from extra storage, establishing a minimax separation between query-dependent and query-independent reading at fixed positive rates, with implications for vector search and retrieval under storage budgets.

entry.title: Estimating Causal Bounds from Observational Data With Neural Generative Models

author.name: Max Zhu, Srivathsan Amruth, Sina Akbari, Qingyuan Zhao

entry.summary: The authors introduce a framework for estimating partial identification bounds on causal effects from discrete observational data using neural generative models plus a new extrapolation procedure. Across benchmark problems with known exact bounds, their approach yields tighter and more accurate bounds than existing general neural methods.

entry.title: Fair Regression under Approximate Demographic Parity

author.name: Weiwei Wang, Xianyang Zhang, Raymond K. W. Wong

entry.summary: Proposes a tunable notion of approximate demographic parity for regression by bounding pairwise Wasserstein distances between group-specific prediction distributions, rather than requiring exact equality. The authors derive transport-form predictors, show convexity conditions via a quantile reformulation, and connect prediction and constrained transport problems through a shared infimum.

entry.title: ForagerSim: Evaluating Embodied Map-Based Reasoning in Large-Scale Dynamic Worlds

author.name: Tom\'a\v{s} Musil, Martin Kot\'ik, Michal Vavre\v{c}ka, Karla \v{S}t\v{e}p\'anov\'a, Sebastian Scherer, Martin Saska

entry.summary: ForagerSim is an interdisciplinary simulation platform for studying embodied agents that build and use cognitive maps in large-scale dynamic environments, inspired by animal spatial reasoning. It fills a gap in embodied AI benchmarks, few of which require genuine map-based reasoning over unmodeled dynamics. The platform enables studying learned map-like representations beyond metric spaces.

entry.title: Gradient descent reaches arbitrary accuracy in a fixed number of large steps on multiclass logistic regression

author.name: Andreea-Alexandra Musat, Nicolas Boumal

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that gradient descent with a sufficiently large step size achieves epsilon optimality gap on multiclass logistic regression in a number of iterations independent of epsilon, depending only on dataset properties such as size and margin. The proof connects large-step rescaled GD to the perceptron algorithm in the separable case. One additional data quantity is shown necessary for choosing the step size in dimension at least three.

entry.title: Discuss More, Comment Less: Boosting Automated Research via Multi-Perspective Collaborative Review

author.name: Junkai Zhou, Jiajia Wu, Zhaoyi Zhang, Shiting Guan, Chuanguang Yang

entry.summary: Proposes RoundtableReview, a multi-agent framework modeling peer review as structured deliberation with eight semantic slots and six simulated academic and industry reviewers. Aims to improve automated review quality control for AI-generated research papers.

entry.title: Pronouncing Hard Words: Phoneme Adaptation of a Pretrained Conversational Text to Speech Model

author.name: Yashish M. Siriwardena, Dinesh K. Gnanasekaran, Tanmay Laud, Shinji Watanabe, Subhabrata Mukherjee, Shanil Puri

entry.summary: This paper addresses the problem of getting conversational TTS models to correctly pronounce rare but critical words like drug names, which are too infrequent and fast-growing to be learned during training. The authors retrofit explicit phoneme controllability onto a pretrained conversational TTS model by extending its vocabulary with ARPAbet phonemes, applying continued phoneme-augmented supervised fine-tuning, and adding a training-free inference mechanism, all without costly pre- or mid-training. This matters for voice agent pipelines (ASR to LLM to TTS), where mispronouncing trust-critical entities like medications can undermine reliability and user safety.

entry.title: Ask, Don't Guess: Targeted Clarification for Speech Recognition Errors

author.name: Sankalp Parashar, Preethi Jyothi, Sunita Sarawagi

entry.summary: PARDON is a framework for online error localization in streaming ASR that identifies spans likely to benefit from asking the speaker to repeat under better acoustic conditions. It uses clean audio to estimate counterfactual recognizer output, aligning noisy and clean decodes with a pair-HMM to produce soft supervision for a counterfactual gain scorer. This enables a recourse mechanism rather than silent errors in far-field conversational speech recognition.

entry.title: MapSteal: Map-based Autonomous Knowledge Stealing Attack Against Large Language Models

author.name: Zhengao Li, Chuxu Zhang, Yushun Dong

entry.summary: Proposes MapSteal, a student-independent framework for structured recursive knowledge acquisition from black-box LLMs, expanding acquisition targets from initial roots via teacher-proposed directions with question realization, admission, and deduplication constraints under a fixed QA budget. It frames autonomous knowledge extraction as both a distillation tool and a security concern.

entry.title: Reading Time Modeling with Pixel-Based Language Models

author.name: Junlin Li, Sara Alhajeri, Tatsuki Kuribayashi

entry.summary: The paper integrates tokenization-free pixel-based language models into computational psycholinguistics, using them to estimate next-word predictability for human reading-time modeling while incorporating orthographic visual features. This removes tokenization bias that plagues surprisal estimates from token-based models.

entry.title: Self-Consistency of Entity Sets and Citations in a Deep Research System under Repeated Prompting

author.name: Lauri Pyk\"al\"a, Kimmo K. Kaski

entry.summary: This study measures the self-consistency of a commercial deep research agent across ten identical runs of an open-ended cybersecurity prompt, representing reports by named-entity sets and retrieved citations.
