This avoids prescribing a temporal basis or fixed query grid, relaxing constraints in prior distillation parameterizations. The goal is accurate few-step generation from dense local supervision.

entry.title: Real In, Real Out: What If We Only Use Real Data for Scene Text Editing?

author.name: Xingsong Ye, Yongkun Du, Jiaxin Zhang, Chong Sun, Zhineng Chen

entry.summary: This work challenges the reliance on synthetic paired data in scene text editing by constructing self-paired supervision from real images via controlled disruptions such as cropping, shuffling, and masking. The result avoids artifacts and hallucinations common to synthetic-pipeline training.

entry.title: HistoLoop: Iterative Contextual Inference with a Looped Transformer for Histology-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction

author.name: Ziang Liu, Jie Liu, Shuai Li, Yigui Feng, Qinglin Wang

entry.summary: HistoLoop formulates spatial gene expression prediction from H&E histology images as iterative contextual inference using a looped transformer with memory-mediated spot-state updates. At each refinement step it aggregates spot states into multi-resolution context tokens and retrieves spot-specific information via cross-attention.

entry.title: SenseAlign: Understanding Vision and Touch through Language at Test Time

author.name: Chuyang Ye, Qinting Jiang, Jingyan Jiang

entry.summary: SenseAlign is a test-time adaptation method for tactile-visual-language models that detects which modality is reliable under distribution shift (lighting changes, contact quality, sensor hardware) by comparing accumulated observations against text embeddings of candidate classes. It refines features during deployment without requiring labeled data.

entry.title: KoalaGS: Complexity-Aware Continuous Level of Detail for Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Radu Beche, Raoul de Charette

entry.summary: KoalaGS introduces continuous level-of-detail control for 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes, using an image-complexity prior computed before optimization to predict where reconstruction error concentrates and to bias Gaussian allocation during training. This lets one primitive set remain effective under shrinking render budgets, with the study showing oversallocation in simple regions hurts low-budget rendering.

entry.title: Real-Time Disturbance-Aware Koopman Model Predictive Control for Quadrotors in Spatially Varying Winds

author.name: Stella Kombo, Masih Haseli, Alejandro A. Stefan-Zavala, Peter I. Renn, Morteza Gharib, Joel W. Burdick

entry.summary: The DA-KCF framework preserves an offline-identified nominal Koopman model for quadrotor MPC while a lightweight residual ensemble learns only a low-dimensional disturbance correction online from causal state-command-state transitions, enabling flight in spatially varying winds. The disturbance-aware model is embedded in MPC with corrections evaluated along the prediction horizon. This is a well-structured combination of Koopman operator theory, learning, and MPC for a practical aerial robotics problem.

entry.title: How I discovered an Exoplanet & the science apocalypse

author.name: jonathanbreitg

entry.summary: The author describes using agentic LLM tooling, primarily Claude Opus 5.5, to identify exoplanet candidates in TESS survey data, walking through the technical process. The second half reflects on the implications of increasingly capable agentic systems for the near future of scientific practice and the structure of scientific institutions.

entry.title: Teaching AI Agent to Play Poker Strategically Through Preference Optimization

author.name: Phurinat Polasa, Thanapon Thanadunpremdet, Phatthanasak Kraiduang, Saksorn Ruangtanusak

entry.summary: The authors propose SPOKE, a strategic preference optimization method with teacher-relative value penalties, policy anchoring, risk constraints, and structured rationale supervision, to train a compact 4B-parameter poker agent under hidden information. They compare it against SFT, DPO, GRPO, and GSPO baselines across exact-game and six-player settings.

entry.title: Measuring Consensus in AI Agent Networks

author.name: Jin Gao

entry.summary: The paper presents an evaluation framework treating consensus formation in connected AI agent networks as the evolution of publicly stated positions toward a shared region, using accumulated communication history as context. It tracks position trajectories, group dispersion, and information content of messages, validated through case studies on staffing decisions with distributed and duplicate facts. Results from 1,872 runs associate specific communication patterns with consensus outcomes.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Reusability of LLM Pipelines: Financial Extraction, Multilingual Reasoning, and Semantic Screening

author.name: Joong Ho (Joshua), Choi, Sherine George, Jiayang Zhao, Jayesh Rathi, Ashwin Kandath, Ananya Sane, Vishvak Srinivasan

entry.summary: An empirical study testing whether LLM pipelines validated in English can be reused across languages, evaluating accuracy, reasoning-effort transfer, and behavioral stability across cheque extraction, multilingual QA (Mintaka, nine languages), and a FinanceBench pilot over SEC 10-K filings in four languages. It finds accuracy reusability is bounded in key ways.

entry.title: AnomalyJev: Towards Evaluating Image Anomaly Explanations via Claim-Level Verification

author.name: Qizhou Wang, Jiawen Zhu, Guansong Pang, Christopher Leckie

entry.summary: AnomalyJev evaluates textual anomaly explanations from multimodal LLMs by extracting verifiable claims and checking them against ground-truth annotations, avoiding costly LLM-judge token generation. This grounds explanation evaluation in available truth rather than subjective rubrics. It improves scalability and reliability of evaluating explainable anomaly detection.

entry.title: Learning Inter-Graph Interactions Between Heterogeneous Substructures of Chemical Systems

author.name: Gyoung S. Na

entry.summary: The paper proposes a data descriptor and graph neural network for modeling interactions between heterogeneous substructures, specifically organic and inorganic components within complex chemical systems such as hybrid solar cell materials. Prior graph methods assumed homogeneous graph-level interactions. This extends graph representation learning to practically important mixed organic-inorganic materials.

entry.title: Radar-Based 3D Human Pose Estimation via Motion-Aware Pose Initialization and Observation-Guided Refinement

author.name: Woo-Jin Jung, Chan-Bin Lim, Seung-Hyun Kong

entry.summary: I2R-Pose is a two-stage framework for privacy-preserving 3D human pose estimation from millimeter-wave radar, combining motion-aware pose initialization with observation-guided refinement to handle insufficient or overlapping body-part reflections. It targets smart-home monitoring where lighting robustness and non-image capture matter. The refinement stage addresses a known core limitation of radar-based perception.

entry.title: Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment for LLM Reasoning over Temporal Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Jiapu Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes co-aligning retrieval and parameter adaptation for LLM reasoning over temporal knowledge graphs, addressing retrieval methods that ignore temporal validity and event order and PEFT methods with fixed, input-agnostic low-rank updates. The approach seeks temporally coherent evidence and time-aware parameter updates to improve temporal reasoning.

entry.title: Gated Prototype Transfer for Zero-Support Medical Vision Language Model

author.name: Sumaiya Fazal, Rizwan Qureshi, Laleh Behjat, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou

entry.summary: GProtoT is a training-free module that transfers visual residual information from supported classes to missing (zero-support) classes in medical vision-language few-shot adaptation, combining VLM similarity with ontology-based clinical distance and a validation-free evidence gate to limit unsupported extrapolation. Evaluated in paired one-shot trials on MESSIDOR, it improves on purely textual prototypes for low-prevalence classes. This targets a realistic clinical constraint where rare classes lack labeled examples.

entry.title: Web Agent Agentic Reinforcement Learning Decision Model Under Multi-Cost and Failure Risk

author.name: Qianli Ma, Limengxi Yue, Shuyang Xu, Yanpei Shi, Hongrui Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a constrained agentic RL model for web agents that unifies page accesses, search requests, and API calls into a long-term decision framework with multidimensional costs, jointly optimizing success rate with budget constraints and tail-risk control. It addresses unrealistic behaviors like high success with high cost or conservative failure under risk.

entry.title: Hidden Trajectories Don't Lie: Correcting Corruption Drift for Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Amirhossein Sabour, Amir Khasahmadi, Mengliu Zhao

entry.summary: Drift-TTA adapts pretrained models at test time by exploiting hidden trajectories, the ordered sequence of intermediate representations across network layers, which are shown to become more separable between clean and corrupted inputs as severity increases. Zero-initialized low-rank adapters on a frozen backbone are trained to align corrupted trajectories with cleaner ones, in source-dependent and source-free variants. It offers a new signal for test-time adaptation beyond output logits.

entry.title: Contrastive Adversarial Training for Robust Graph Neural Networks under Label Poisoning

author.name: Manshika Charvi Bissessur, Melis Ilayda Bal, Michael Muehlebach

entry.summary: CoLAT is a contrastive adversarial training framework defending GNN node classification against label poisoning, where a few corrupted training labels propagate errors via message passing. Its structure-aware detection model uses contrastive label-flipping to distinguish adversarial poisoning from naturally hard examples, unlike prior defenses built for label noise.

entry.title: Label-Space Mismatch Distorts Cross-Cohort Evaluation in Breast Cancer Molecular Subtyping

author.name: Suxing Liu, Byungwon Min, Zhijian Zheng, Jiahao Wang

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates that cross-cohort evaluation of breast cancer subtype classifiers is distorted when annotation standards differ (METABRIC six-class versus PAM50 five-class), showing that label-space restriction alone accounts for the dominant accuracy correction on TCGA-BRCA and GSE21653. It disentangles evaluation-rule effects from genuine calibration gains such as EM prior correction.

entry.title: FHKAN: Fractional Hermite Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Data-Driven and Physics-Informed Learning

author.name: Arsha Farnoush, Amirhossein Sadr, Aida Pakniyat, Dara Rahmati, Saeid Gorgin, Kourosh Parand

entry.summary: FHKAN equips Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with a trainable fractional-order generalized Hermite basis that is orthonormal on the entire real line, removing the need for saturating squashing of pre-activations required by bounded-interval Chebyshev bases. The paper derives closed-form derivatives supporting data-driven and physics-informed learning. It advances the KAN architecture family with better spectral foundations.

entry.title: DROD: Dual-Ratio Ordered Dropout for Federated Continual Learning on Heterogeneous Devices

author.name: Berk Sezer, \"Ozg\"ur Soysal

entry.summary: DROD extends FjORD's Ordered Dropout with two independent reduction axes (shortcut ratio and branch ratio) to extract sub-models, targeting the underexplored intersection of capacity-heterogeneous federated learning and continual learning on drifting data streams. Trained from scratch on Split-CIFAR-100 with ResNet-18 fleets, it achieves the highest mean accuracy on a shared parameter/FLOP budget ladder among compared strategies. It addresses a practical deployment gap.

entry.title: Paloma: Phase-Conditioned Residual Modulation for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jingru Fei, Wei Fan, Kun Yi, Qi Zhang, Zhendong Niu

entry.summary: Paloma shows that residuals remaining after removing periodic components from time series exhibit structured, phase-dependent deviations rather than being unstructured noise, supported by empirical and theoretical analysis. It proposes a phase-conditioned residual modulation module inspired by classical signal processing. This offers a simple, general improvement for periodic time series forecasting models.

entry.title: FracTS: Hierarchical and Autoregressive Time Series Generation

author.name: Jiayu Li, Umair Afzal, Zilong Zhao, Milad Abdollahzadeh, Uzair Javaid, Biplab Sikdar

entry.summary: FracTS adapts fractal generative modeling from images to multivariate time series via a hierarchical, coarse-to-fine autoregressive model that captures global trajectory structure at coarse scales and local dynamics at fine scales. It targets known weaknesses of flat autoregressive generators: low diversity, error accumulation, and poor long-range modeling. Relevant to privacy-preserving data sharing and augmentation.

entry.title: How Much Does One Wrong Answer Cost? Error Propagation in Constraint Pruning with Noisy LLM Oracles

author.name: Zhengtao Gui (University of California, Irvine), Weining Shen (University of California, Irvine)

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how errors from noisy LLM oracles propagate through constraint pruning systems, such as entity resolution and LLM-based ranking, where one accepted wrong answer corrupts every question it implies. It derives first-order risk results showing, for example, that implication-rule pruning in random order adds no first-order risk. The work provides a principled risk framework for judging pruning under oracle errors.

entry.title: A Simple and General Approach to top-$k$ Selection

author.name: Motti Goldberger, Nils Rudi

entry.summary: The paper studies Bayesian top-k identification under a fixed adaptive sampling budget, proposing a batch allocation rule that minimizes a surrogate objective derived from an upper bound on expected opportunity cost. The method is general across arbitrary k, batch sampling, and many sampling distributions, with theoretical and empirical support. This connects to best-arm identification and adaptive experimentation.

entry.title: Learning to Refer: Inference-Time Collaboration in Decentralized Federated Learning

author.name: Yuheng Ma, Chendi Wang, Qiong Zhang

entry.summary: The paper formulates inference-time collaboration in decentralized federated learning as budgeted local expert referral: a query moves only between neighboring clients, and only visited clients contribute to the prediction, exploiting complementary client expertise without global coordination. EdgeDRM learns a density-based routing potential per client, using potential differences between neighbors to select successive referrals. This is a novel angle on federated systems, improving predictions at inference time rather than through model averaging.

entry.title: Censored Flow Matching for Synthetic Time-to-Event Generation

author.name: Jianbin Tan, Xingran Chen, Kevin He, Zhenke Wu, Bhramar Mukherjee, Anru R. Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes censored flow matching (CFM), a flow-based generative method for synthesizing time-to-event data that handles censoring without survival likelihoods, exploiting monotonicity of differential flows via pullback sampling in an alternating procedure. This enables flexible generation and density learning for survival data that standard generative models struggle with.

entry.title: Prototype-Guided Optimization of Quantum Data Embeddings with Linear Cost

author.name: Seokhoon Jeong, Daniel K. Park

entry.summary: The paper proposes a prototype-guided framework for data-adaptive quantum embeddings that replaces O(B^2) pairwise fidelity evaluations with an O(B) objective based on class-prototype separation and compactness, with a measurable lower certificate for class distinguishability. This removes a key computational bottleneck in quantum machine learning embedding optimization.

entry.title: Knowledge Manifold Optimization for Scientific Discovery

author.name: Shigeru Obayashi, Yoshiaki Kawagoe, Kazuhiko Komatsu, Tomonaga Okabe

entry.summary: KMO treats scientific discovery as multiobjective search over a continuous literature-derived knowledge space, evaluating candidates via boundary strength, white-space novelty, semantic-gradient magnitude, and evidential support to identify Pareto-optimal Supported Knowledge Gaps. It aims to point researchers to where new, supportable knowledge may emerge as literature grows.

entry.title: GLOSS-MT: Controllable Low-Resource Machine Translation with an Editable Dictionary

author.name: Mich-Seth Owusu, Stephen E. Moore, Akwasi Asare, Lawrence Adu Gyamfi, Paul Azunre, Joel Budu, Jonathan Asiamah

entry.summary: GLOSS-MT enables terminology control in machine translation for low-resource languages by looking up source noun phrases in an offline English-Twi dictionary, replacing them in place with Twi translations, and fine-tuning once on these mixed inputs. Applied to NLLB-200 at three scales, OPUS-MT, and TranslateGemma 4B, every fine-tuned model beats its pretrained baseline on a document-level English-to-Asante Twi benchmark. The approach reduces the costly fine-tuning cycle typically needed for terminology adaptation.

entry.title: DiaLong: Benchmarking Reminiscence in Long-Context Dialogues

author.name: Owen Bianchi, Samer Aslan, Ryunosuke Saito

entry.summary: Presents DiaLong, a benchmark of 100 human-created, LLM-augmented long-context dialogues with a fact-recall task where models classify 40 candidate facts about a conversation as true or false. It standardizes quantitative evaluation of how LLMs retain and retrieve long-range dialogue information.

entry.title: Hierarchical Token Merging with Recursive Autoencoders for Unsupervised Grammar Induction

author.name: Murat Guney Kemal, Robert Lieck

entry.summary: The paper introduces a hierarchical token-merging autoencoder that recursively combines tokens to test whether meaningful hierarchical structure, evaluated via unsupervised grammar induction, can emerge from compression alone. This connects representation learning and structured linguistics without explicit structural supervision.

entry.title: Rate as a Feature, Not a Nuisance: Curriculum FiLM Training for Event-Based Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Kavyansh Tyagi, Andreas Ziegler

entry.summary: This paper argues that event-camera data rate, typically normalized away or treated as a nuisance, is informative signal. The authors show rate normalization costs about 6 percentage points of accuracy on N-Caltech101 and propose curriculum FiLM conditioning so graph neural networks exploit variable event rate instead of being invariant to it. This reframes a standard preprocessing choice in event-based vision.

entry.title: Provisioning Robust and Efficient LiDAR Perception for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Tingxu Han, Zijie Shen, An Guo, Lyuke Wang, Chunrong Fang, Zhenyu Chen, Wei Song

entry.summary: This work formulates LiDAR perception provisioning as jointly satisfying robustness to point-cloud corruption and constraints on latency and GPU memory. It trains candidate detectors on corruption samples mimicking extreme weather and selects configurations meeting both robustness and resource budgets.

entry.title: From Proper Scoring Rules and Edge Biases to Mumford-Shah Models: Robust Unsupervised Hyperspectral Image Segmentation

author.name: Fabian Conrad, Benjamin Berkels

entry.summary: This theoretical work derives an unsupervised hyperspectral segmentation framework from strictly proper scoring rules and parametric probability families, connecting them to the piecewise-constant Mumford-Shah functional. The feature-agnostic method targets spectral variability, mixed pixels, and band correlation without labeled data. An elegant theory-driven contribution.

entry.title: Unified RAW Image Exposure Correction and Restoration via Linear Illumination and Frequency-Adaptive Enhancement

author.name: Yingkai Zhang, Yunhao Zou, Ying Fu

entry.summary: This paper proposes RIECR, a unified framework in the RAW domain that jointly corrects exposure and restores degradations for both under- and over-exposed images. It decomposes the problem following the RAW imaging model into linear illumination correction and residual degradation restoration with frequency-adaptive enhancement, unifying previously separate single-degradation methods.

entry.title: Neural Implicit Energy Optimization for LiDAR Mapping

author.name: Hrishikesh Viswanath, Md Ashiqur Rahman, Chi Lin, Damon Conover, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: The authors formulate large-scale LiDAR mapping as optimization of classical surface energy functionals over the parameter space of neural implicit SDF representations, regularizing the field through the curvature (shape operator) of its level set to suppress jitter and artifacts from sparse, noisy inputs. This bridges classical geometric processing and neural implicit mapping.

entry.title: Active Pilot Sampling for Multi-fidelity Estimation in Stochastic Optimization

author.name: Thomas E. Coons, Aniket Jivani, Xun Huan

entry.summary: The paper develops active pilot-sampling strategies for multi-fidelity estimators like approximate control variates within iterative stochastic optimization, exploiting the smooth variation of model-output covariances across optimization iterations. This addresses the cost of estimating unknown control-variate weights and sample allocations in high-fidelity simulation-based optimization.

entry.title: Tsinghua started an AI-safety residency

author.name: Andrew Gritsaev

entry.summary: Announcement of the Beijing AI Safety Residency at a Tsinghua-affiliated hub, co-directed by Soren Mindermann and Professor Xu Wei with Andrew Yao as Chief Scientist, offering self-directed three-month residencies for technical AI safety researchers with funding and support. Applications for the Spring 2027 cohort close November 6, 2026.

entry.title: Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing

author.name: Lei Ren, Haiteng Wang, Shixiang Li, Jing Zhang, Yuqing Wang, Jingwei Guo, Yunfei Zhu, Yuanjun Laili, Yang Tang, Lihui Wang

entry.summary: A survey-style overview of LLM-driven industrial agents for smart manufacturing, presenting five key challenges, a unified taxonomy of application scenarios and capability levels, a four-layer system architecture, and its core modules. It maps how agents can move beyond predefined workflows toward autonomous planning in constrained industrial environments.

entry.title: EDMA: Entropy-Driven Multimodal Answering

author.name: Emanuele Mezzi, Gertjan Burghouts, Fabio Massacci, Mengyuan Zhang

entry.summary: EDMA formalizes multimodal question answering as iterative entropy reduction, using logical entropy to quantify how much each modality contributes to distinguishing correct answers from distractors. This improves process traceability and final performance in multimodal QA with heterogeneous data sources.

entry.title: RaspAssistant as an Agentic Framework for Automating Adsorption Simulation Research in Porous Materials

author.name: Marko Petkovi\'c, Susanne Gooijer, Jos\'e Manuel Vicent-Luna, Vlado Menkovski, Sof\'ia Calero

entry.summary: Tests RaspAssistant, a hierarchical multi-agent framework that automates porous-material adsorption simulation workflows from force-field preparation through validation and separation analysis. Across twelve workflow-reproduction runs and a force-field extraction benchmark, the system achieves consistently high rubric scores, demonstrating end-to-end scientific workflow automation.

entry.title: Temporal Evidence Allocation For Longitudinal Clinical Retrieval: A Position And Technical Report

author.name: Soumya Ranjan Sahoo, Divya Bharti, Sanand Sasidharan

entry.summary: Argues that longitudinal clinical retrieval should be framed as allocating a limited evidence budget across time rather than pure similarity ranking, since repeated restatements of diagnoses crowd out one-off pivotal events like recurrences or therapy changes. The position paper decomposes the task into temporal evidence allocation, candidate reconstruction, and clinical validation.

entry.title: Physical Operating-Condition-Guided Vision-Language Matching for Cavitation Diagnosis in Industrial Pipeline Systems

author.name: Yu Sha, Junqi Tao, Deyu Wang, Horst Stoecker, Domagoj Vnucec, Andreas Widlf, Kai Zhou

entry.summary: POC-VLM incorporates sample-specific operating variables into candidate cavitation text descriptions for industrial pipeline diagnosis, dynamically aligning physical semantics with acoustic time-frequency responses via global-local vision-language matching. This addresses the problem that identical acoustic patterns can reflect different cavitation states depending on operating conditions.

entry.title: Exploring Temporal Context-Aware Physical Grounding in Latent World Models

author.name: Yilei Man, Yang Chen, Jingcai Guo

entry.summary: The paper proposes G-JEPA, which adds shared causal temporal modeling to physical grounding in JEPA-based world models and couples the learned model with prior-guided action planning instead of generic sampling distributions. It addresses explicit temporal context aggregation and more effective action planning in latent space.

entry.title: Semantic Observability for Autonomous Systems Diagnostics

author.name: Jitendra Solanki, Anand Todkar, Ziran Min

entry.summary: The paper introduces Semantic Observability, a multi-agent framework that unifies heterogeneous microservice log streams into a dynamic property graph database modeling infrastructure topology, software dependencies, and event sequences. It aims to help SREs isolate root causes during cascading failures by bridging the semantic gap across monitoring tools. The system replaces manual keyword filtering with graph-based semantic queries.

entry.title: CoASFL: Coupled Consistency Optimization for Asynchronous Split Federated Learning

author.name: Junhao Cheng, Yunming Liao, Hongli Xu, Yang Xu, Zuan Xie

entry.summary: CoASFL addresses two coupled sources of inconsistency in asynchronous split federated learning — across clients and between clients and server — using a dynamic activation merging mechanism and consistency-aware model aggregation. The goal is to prevent biased representations and client drift on resource-constrained edge devices.

entry.title: CARLAR Influence: A Structured Hallucination Risk in Multimodal Cheque Extraction and an Exploratory Compressed-Image Countermeasure

author.name: Joong Ho (Joshua), Choi, Aditya Paul, Nidhi Singh

entry.summary: The paper documents CARLAR influence, a structured hallucination where multimodal LLMs return the same amount in both courtesy and legal amount fields of cheques despite differing annotations, evaluating GPT-4.1 and Claude 4.5 Sonnet across 243 cheques and ten prompting conditions, with a compressed-image countermeasure achieving 73.7% reduction under courtesy redaction.

entry.title: Theorem prover Arend

author.name: Fedor Part, Valery Isaev, Sergey Sinchuk

entry.summary: An exposition of the Arend theorem prover from JetBrains Research, a language based on a homotopy type theory variant with cubical syntax closer to Martin-Lof Type Theory while retaining useful computational properties. The paper details its class and record system with subsumptive subtyping and partial implementations, designed to support formalization of constructive and univalent mathematics. It serves as a reference for a mature but less widely known proof assistant.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Personalized Federated Learning (PPP-FL) for Medical Imaging

author.name: Md Morshedul Islam, Hossain Shahriar, Alfredo Cuzzocrea

entry.summary: This work studies privacy attacks and defenses in federated learning for medical imaging, proposing a DCGAN-based model inversion attack adapted to FL systems and a corresponding personalized defense framework. It matters because existing attack/defense literature is centralized, and FL architecture introduces distinct vulnerabilities for sensitive medical data.

entry.title: WORTH Benchmark: Evidence Discovery under Not-Fully-Cooperative Information -- A Two-Episode Pilot

author.name: Bo Zou, Chao Xu

entry.summary: WORTH evaluates whether models can autonomously discover evidence: reading professionally written mystery narratives without clue annotations, selecting key clue sentences, identifying participants, and explaining reasoning, while narrative structure actively delays truth revelation. The pilot covers two episodes and seven models. It probes an underexamined reasoning skill combining evidence selection and judgment under non-cooperative information presentation.

entry.title: Corpus Quality Improves, Retrieval Utility Does Not: An Ablation of Preprocessing and Refinement in a Speech-to-QA Pipeline

author.name: Wonsup Shin, Jingu Kim

entry.summary: This ablation study examines whether preprocessing and refinement stages that improve the perceived quality of an LLM-generated QA corpus from Korean conference speech actually help downstream retrieval. While four LLM judges and six human experts consistently rank the fully refined corpus highest, the quality gains do not carry over to retrieval utility. The finding challenges a common assumption in corpus construction pipelines.

entry.title: Slots Are Not Speakers: Training-Free Speaker Linking for Frozen Streaming Diarizers

author.name: Aditya Srinivas Menon, Kumarmanas Nethil, Kavya Manohar

entry.summary: The paper presents a causal, training-free post-processing linker that lets frozen streaming diarizers like Streaming Sortformer track more speakers than their fixed output slots, by splitting slot activity at speaker changes, embedding segments with an off-the-shelf speaker encoder, and matching against a bank of seen speakers. Because it only relabels, detection error rates are unchanged.

entry.title: Adaptive Pullback: Reweighting Supervision at Penalty Jumps in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Guangyu Liu, Siyuan Gan, Shilong Zhou, Linjian Meng, Boyan Wang, Jing Huo

entry.summary: The paper identifies penalty jumps in on-policy distillation, abrupt sustained increases in student-teacher log-ratio penalties accompanied by decreasing teacher confidence, a pattern it terms penalty-confidence tension. It proposes adaptively reweighting supervision at these jumps to improve distillation dynamics.

entry.title: Region-Guided Food-Package Evidence Extraction and Abstention-Aware Draft R3337 Screening with Selective VLM Review

author.name: Mayimunah Nagayi, Alice Scaria Khan, Tamryn Frank, Rina Swart, Clement Nyirenda

entry.summary: This paper presents a workflow for screening South African food-package photographs against draft R3337 nutrition warning criteria. A three-class detector localizes nutrition panels, ingredient lists, and product-identity regions, then OCR and deterministic rules assess compliance, with the system abstaining via Review or Insufficient-evidence outcomes when data is incomplete, and selectively escalating to a VLM. It matters because it demonstrates deployment-oriented AI in a public-health regulatory context with an explicit abstention design.

entry.title: When Do LLMs Help with Feature Selection? A Systematic Empirical Study

author.name: Fateme Memar, Dongjie Wang, Arvin Agah

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates whether LLMs improve tabular feature selection, comparing five classical baselines against frozen Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.3-70B selectors and GRPO-adapted Qwen2.5-7B models across an 18-dataset framework. Results characterize when semantic feature names and summary statistics help relative to established statistical methods, measured by ROC-AUC and R-squared.

entry.title: Fast Construction of Inner Sphere Trees Using Machine Learning

author.name: Jianneng Huang, Wenjia Rao

entry.summary: ML-IST reformulates inner sphere tree construction for collision detection as single-shot set prediction: a network predicts inscribed sphere candidates from voxel geometry, refined via differentiable coverage feedback and geometric projection. This parallelizes what was previously a sequential, greedy construction, benefiting physics simulation, VR, and robotics.

entry.title: Dynamical Kernel Attention: Estimating the Present from a Record of the Past

author.name: Peter Racioppo

entry.summary: DKA derives attention weights from robust estimation of a latent state evolving under stochastic dynamics, so evidence from past tokens decays according to the dynamics rather than a heuristic recency bias; it can abstain when evidence is weak and guarantees bounded error when old tokens are discarded, at the same computational cost as standard attention.

entry.title: Client-Aware Security Adaptive Early Exit Vision Transformers for Heterogeneous Federated Learning

author.name: Sahar Refaei Ghalibafan, Samira Nazari, Christian Herglotz, Maksim Jenihhin, Mahdi Taheri

entry.summary: The authors propose client-specific early-exit thresholds for Vision Transformers in federated learning, replacing a single global acceptance threshold with per-client bases derived from label entropy and confidence, adjusted per-input via predictive entropy and class margins. The security-aware routing achieves 88.7% CIFAR-10 accuracy with 32% depth savings and 73.7% ImageNet-1K top-1 with 30% savings. This tackles compute heterogeneity across federated clients.

entry.title: Inducing Fourier Geometry: A Smoothness Prior Imposes Approximate Translation Equivariance in Multimodal Stellar Embeddings

author.name: Ilay Kamai, Alex M. Bronstein, Hagai B. Perets

entry.summary: The authors show that a graph-Laplacian smoothness prior over a known physical parameter space induces Fourier-like geometry in learned embeddings, since the continuum limit selects Laplacian eigenfunctions. Applied to multimodal stellar representations from six astronomical surveys, the prior produces Toeplitz Gram structure and sinusoidal modes along stellar parameters. This demonstrates that approximate symmetries can be induced rather than assumed.

entry.title: Transport What Shares the Conduction Pathway: Normal-Anchored SPD Geometric Transport for Source-Free Patient Adaptation of Holter and Patch ECG

author.name: JinKook Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes Normal-Anchored Geometric Transport (NAGT), a source-free adaptation method for ECG beat classifiers that estimates a closed-form SPD congruence map from label-free normal-beat anchors, adapting only shared-pathway prototypes while keeping ventricular and fusion prototypes fixed. It addresses the extreme class imbalance of real Holter recordings, where label-free prefixes are nearly all normal beats.

entry.title: DeliMF: Gated Cross-Attention Fusion of Structured Time Series and Clinical Text for Early Intensive Care Delirium Prediction

author.name: Yibo Yang, Zerui Huang, Haomiao Yang, Zixia Wang

entry.summary: DeliMF is a multimodal framework predicting ICU delirium within the first day of admission by fusing structured EHR time series with free-text clinical notes and radiology reports via gated cross-attention. Early identification of delirium risk gives clinicians a window to intervene for a condition linked to longer stays and higher mortality.

entry.title: Pair-Aware Optimization: Coordinating Exploration and Refinement for Jailbreaking LLM Agents

author.name: Juanyang Xu, Zheng Wang, Xingyu Zhao, Siddartha Khastgir, Andi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper systematically compares four optimization strategies for jailbreaking LLM agents (pure ZO, pure FO, ZO->FO, FO->ZO) and develops a ZO-FO framework that explores adversarial prefixes with zeroth-order optimization and refines suffixes with first-order methods. Pair-aware optimization retains candidate pairs to coordinate the two processes.

entry.title: An Impossibility Result for ETF Target Geometry, and an Equinorm Remedy for Imbalanced Analytic Continual Learning

author.name: Berk Sezer

entry.summary: This paper analyzes whether combining analytic continual learning (exact ridge-regression classifier updates on frozen features) with progressively expanding simplex ETF target geometries yields improvements, proving the fusion collapses to standard one-hot ACIL because simplex ETFs are not nested across class counts. It proposes an equinorm alternative to handle imbalanced class settings in exemplar-free continual learning.

entry.title: Self-organizing reinforcement learning: a swarm approaches the explore-exploit optimum

author.name: Galen J. Wilkerson

entry.summary: This single-author paper shows that a minimal foraging swarm with no learner and no reward signal approaches the ideal-free/Nash allocation of a multi-agent resource-sharing game, using Levy-flight exploration, threshold-cascade recruitment, and crowding-based dispersal. The swarm attains the shape of the explore-exploit optimum though not the exact equilibrium, remaining measurably exploitable. It offers a mechanism-free perspective on the core RL trade-off.

entry.title: World Models, Trees and Foundation Models for Retail Forecasting: Evidence from Four Public Data Sets

author.name: Karthik Iyer, Madan Dabbeeru

entry.summary: This paper compares forecasting models at different grains of the retail hierarchy (item-store, item-chain, category, financial plan) across four public datasets including M5, using rolling origins, paired tests, and model confidence sets. It evaluates a world-model approach against tree ensembles and foundation models, with one dataset held out of all development. The grain-dependent conclusions offer practical guidance for retail forecasting model selection.

entry.title: Emergent Sparsity: How Many Effective Variables Survive Coarse-Graining in AlphaEarth Embeddings?

author.name: Johannes Hirn

entry.summary: This study analyzes AlphaEarth's 64-component land-pixel embeddings, asking how many effective nonlinear variables are needed at different reconstruction tolerances and spatial scales, using beta-VAE scans to estimate effective dimension. It frames effective dimension as a two-control surface over tolerance and spatial scale. The work matters for geospatial ML and for understanding when coarse-grained representations suffice for scientific tasks.

entry.title: Dynamics-Aligned Representation Learning under Induced Partial Observability

author.name: SM Mazharul Islam, Manfred Huber

entry.summary: The paper proposes a stochastic gating mechanism for model-based RL that induces controlled partial observability during training by masking raw observations with a Beta-Bernoulli random field, reducing over-reliance on reconstruction objectives. This aims to produce latent dynamics models with better long-horizon prediction quality rather than representations biased toward visual fidelity. It targets sample-efficient continuous control from high-dimensional observations.

entry.title: Evidence Sufficiency and Model Comparisons in MexRegQA: An Item-Level Audit of Mexican-Spanish Regulatory QA

author.name: Fred Hu (Huawei Technologies de M\'exico, Mexico), Yeqi Wang (Huawei Technologies de M\'exico, Mexico), Xing Zhou (Northeastern University, USA)

entry.summary: This audit of Mexican-Spanish financial-regulatory QA shows that retrieval coverage does not guarantee evidence sufficiency: 35 of 135 covered items lacked load-bearing facts, and removing evidence-defective items flips the significance status of 14 of 55 model comparisons. Zero-evidence accuracy ranges widely across eleven prompt-matched models, and evidence removal under abstention-permitting prompts cuts accuracy by 63-81 points. It is a valuable methodological caution for RAG evaluation and low-resource language benchmarks.

entry.title: Cognitively Decoupled Meta-Induction for Out-of-Distribution Generalization

author.name: Yuqian Wang, Yuanzheng Wang, Chaojun Xiao, Ke Xu, Bingxiang He, Jinghan Tan, Zijun Chen, Lu Chen, Yi-Xin Huo, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: CoDI improves out-of-distribution generalization in in-context learning by inducing task-level inductive representations (rules) rather than relying on neighbor-based matching between queries and demonstrations. It combines a cognitive-decoupling framework for query-blind rule induction with dual-loop meta-inductive learning across diverse tasks. The goal is rule-based reasoning that transfers across task families where ICL matching fails.

entry.title: Graph-to-Table Interfaces Control Relational Generalisation

author.name: Alessandro Cagiano, Lorenzo Molfetta, Gianluca Moro, Matteo Zignani, Pasquale Minervini

entry.summary: This work decomposes graph-to-table systems into encoder, context constructor, and tabular decoder, then runs matched comparisons varying one component at a time across CLUTRR, GraphLog worlds, and knowledge graphs with logistic regression, CatBoost, and TabPFN-3. The key finding is that conclusions about one component can reverse when others change; for instance, absolute positional encodings fit short-path settings well yet generalize worse than relational alternatives. The paper shows component evaluations are not independent in relational learning pipelines.

entry.title: Variance-Aware Non-Stationary Bandits:All-Budget Regret Bounds and Adaptation Costs

author.name: Xiaojin Zhang

entry.summary: The paper refines the variance-variation trade-off in non-stationary multi-armed bandits, giving minimax dynamic regret bounds for every admissible pair of variance budget Q and variation budget B, within a logarithmic factor. It also characterizes the deterministic boundary Q=0 without logarithms and analyzes how monitoring costs depend on supplied variance and variation budgets. This provides a unified, nearly complete regret characterization for this setting.

entry.title: OceanTensorCube and ST-MMT: A Multimodal Data and Transformer System for Seven-Day Forecasting of Pyropia Bleaching

author.name: Gwangjin Kim, Cheolyoung Jang, Yosep Jo

entry.summary: This system paper presents OceanTensorCube, which aligns 32 public marine, meteorological, and satellite channels on a 30 m grid, and ST-MMT, a 9.2M-parameter spatiotemporal transformer forecasting Pyropia (laver) bleaching seven days ahead for Korean seaweed farms. The ensemble detects all reported positive events with at most 3.5% false-alarm rate on validation data. It demonstrates practical AI impact in aquaculture with a well-engineered multimodal pipeline.

entry.title: Learning SOCP Solver Dynamics with Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Adam Ghalem, Lou Sala\"un, Davide Rinaldi, Fragkiskos D. Malliaros

entry.summary: The paper explores GNN-based solvers for second-order cone programs that learn the iterative solver dynamics rather than predicting optimizers in a single forward pass, aiming to combine classical interior-point accuracy with real-time efficiency. This targets repeated-solve settings in engineering where classical methods are too slow. It contributes to the growing intersection of machine learning and convex optimization.

entry.title: Nested Shared-Operator Recursion on ARC-AGI-1: An Empirical Study of HRM, TRM and URM

author.name: Sara Neri, Eugenio Gaeta, Andrea Ceschini, Andrea Facchinetti, Giuseppe Fico

entry.summary: This empirical study tests whether adding a persistent intermediate state that integrates repeated updates through a shared learned operator improves recursive reasoning models. Implemented within three small recursive architectures (HRM, TRM, URM) and compared at matched parameter counts on ARC-AGI-1 using official codebases. The abstract indicates the experimental results are mixed or limited, which is valuable evidence for the fast-moving recursive-reasoning-models subfield.

entry.title: CAVA: Complementary-Label-Aware Data Valuation

author.name: Tan-Ha Mai, Hsuan-Tien Lin, Vu Nguyen

entry.summary: CAVA extends optimal-transport-based data valuation to complementary-label learning, where labels name a class an instance does not belong to. Direct application of OT valuation creates a semantic mismatch because a complementary label means not-class-c in training but class-c in validation, which the paper identifies and resolves. This is useful since complementary labels are cheap to collect from crowdworkers or VLMs but error-prone, and such errors are especially harmful because models are explicitly trained to suppress the true class.

entry.title: Composable Parametric Demographic Injection for Values Survey Simulation

author.name: Xinyuan Cao, Qingyi Pan, Bangde Du, Yujia Zhou, Hexi Wang, Weihang Su, Yiqun Liu, Yueyue Wu, Min Zhang, Qingyao Ai

entry.summary: PARADE represents demographic attribute values as reusable, composable LoRA modules for LLM-based survey simulation, separating task-common survey capability from demographic-specific value shifts. This improves generalization to unseen demographic combinations and reduces the prompt-sensitivity and inference overhead of demographic prompting.

entry.title: Vocabulary-Incomplete Unsupervised Vision-Language Model Adaptation

author.name: Si Qin, Jiawei Tang, Yaxin Hou, Yan Chen, Yutong Xie, Chen Li, Yuheng Jia

entry.summary: VI-UVA relaxes the assumption of prior unsupervised VLM adaptation methods that the adaptation vocabulary contains all class names, addressing the realistic case where unlabeled data contains overlooked or out-of-scope classes. The method adapts VLMs using pseudo-labels when only a subset of class names is available.

entry.title: Spatio-Temporal Detection of Photovoltaic Systems on Industrial Building Rooftops Using Satellite Imagery and Machine Learning

author.name: Frederick Bruch, Christian Knoth, Florian Detsch, Edzer Pebesma, Hanna Meyer

entry.summary: The study develops a machine learning framework for detecting industrial rooftop photovoltaic installations using open-access Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery combined with OpenStreetMap building geometries, addressing gaps in administrative registries. This enables scalable, low-cost monitoring for grid operators, developers, and policymakers.

entry.title: The Weight of Teamwork: Does Communication Structure Help LLM Scientists Search for Scientific Laws?

author.name: Jianing Shi, Zaibin Zhang, Shijun Lei, Zhenfei Yin

entry.summary: Using symbolic regression as a testbed for scientific discovery, this study disentangles candidate generation from selection in LLM teams and compares communication structures such as Ring, Star, and Independent policies under fixed budgets. The largest gain comes from distributing the budget across more independent trajectories, while the Ring policy actually reduced mean held-out fitting score relative to independent runs.

entry.title: BanglaShield: A Script-Robust Safety Classifier and Benchmark for Bangla Native, Romanized, and Code-Mixed Prompts

author.name: Mohsinul Kabir, Md. Tariquzzaman, Mohammad Rashidujjaman Rifat, Tharindu Ranasinghe, Nishat Raihan

entry.summary: BanglaShield is a resource and model for graded prompt-safety classification across Bangla in native script, romanized Latin script, and code-mixed forms, consolidating 10,245 prompts from six sources under a four-level taxonomy with aligned renderings enabling paired comparisons. Benchmarking of six contemporary LLMs across tens of thousands of queries reveals gaps in safety coverage for script-variant and code-mixed text.

entry.title: Denoising Implicit Variational Inference

author.name: Zitong Wang, Zekun Wu, Longlin Yu, Cheng Zhang

entry.summary: DIVI improves semi-implicit variational inference by learning the intractable marginal score directly via denoising score matching, used as a plug-in estimator in reparameterized ELBO gradients. This replaces the indirect, costly score estimation of UIVI-style methods with a more stable approach.

entry.title: LastWords: Boring Problems Revisited

author.name: Huayang Li, Richard Sproat

entry.summary: This retrospective revisits a 2022 Last Words column arguing that seemingly trivial NLP problems like number name reading resist purely neural solutions, written just before ChatGPT's release. The authors document that frontier models have now essentially solved number name reading, while analyzing what remains hard and what this trajectory implies about neural progress on classical NLP problems.

entry.title: DF-PALM: Dynamic Fusion Prompt Learning for Audio--Language Models

author.name: Yulin Sun, Shenghua Li, Yong Dou, Xinwang Liu, Cheng Yang, Kele Xu

entry.summary: DF-PALM improves few-shot audio classification with audio-language models by conditioning class representations on the input audio after text encoding and adding asymmetric cross-attention for audio refinement, while keeping both pretrained encoders frozen. This addresses input-independence of class representations in prior prompt-adaptation approaches.

entry.title: Non-Acceleration of the Heavy-Ball Method in 1D

author.name: Konstantinos Fotopoulos, Michael Helcig, Karl Deck, Jannis Alsbach

entry.summary: The paper resolves the long-standing open question of whether Polyak's heavy-ball method accelerates on univariate smooth strongly convex functions, using a Fourier-based analysis to show it does not in general. This completes the picture started by prior two-dimensional counterexamples.

entry.title: Spectral Adaptive Graph Transformer for Efficient and Scalable Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Amirhossein Ghaffari, Susanna Pirttikangas, Ekaterina Gilman

entry.summary: The paper introduces a graph transformer for traffic forecasting whose spatial operator is learned and directed rather than derived from a Laplacian eigendecomposition, removing cubic-time costs while avoiding dense attention memory bottlenecks. This makes large directed sensor networks tractable for spatio-temporal prediction.

entry.title: Sampling of Signals on Multigraphs: From Removable and Uniqueness sets to Spectral Proxies

author.name: Alejandro Parada-Mayorga

entry.summary: This paper develops a sampling theory for bandlimited signals on multigraphs, where multiple non-commuting shift operators on the same nodes yield matrix-valued frequencies. It introduces layer-independent notions of frequency and bandwidth, extends removable and uniqueness sets to multigraphs, and proves that sampling set optimality is determined by the common Fourier basis and its invariant subspaces.

entry.title: FLMNet: Self-Ensemble Distillation from Masks to Seeds for Single-Tower CTR Prediction

author.name: Yifan Wang, Yifei Du

entry.summary: Analyzes why self-ensemble distillation helps CTR prediction models like FinalNet and QNN, showing the dropout-pattern objective converges exactly to logit-averaged label loss plus a disagreement penalty as the number of masks grows. Derives a deterministic formulation removing the need for random sampling.

entry.title: Residual-Based Adaptive Refinement in Hybrid Variational-Collocation PINNs for Singular Elliptic PDEs with Mixed Dirichlet-Neumann Boundary Conditions

author.name: Somnath Giri, Muslim Malik, Rishikesh Yadav

entry.summary: This paper develops residual-based adaptive refinement for hybrid variational-collocation physics-informed neural networks targeting singular elliptic PDEs on cracked or nonconvex domains with mixed boundary conditions. A multiscale Fourier-feature network is trained with a composite loss combining a variational residual needing only first derivatives and a strong-form collocation term. The approach targets gradient singularities at re-entrant corners and crack tips.

entry.title: Modeling Human Behavior in the Prisoner's Dilemma with Large Language Models

author.name: Raina Gao, Tristan Raffo

entry.summary: Tests whether five open-source 7B-8B LLMs with memory components can reproduce human cooperation patterns in repeated Prisoner's Dilemma games, comparing against empirical human data. Addresses gaps in prior work by using accessible open models and memory-enabled agents.

entry.title: Multi-author style detection with stylistic embeddings

author.name: Man-Ling Sung, Chak Fai Li, Damianos Karakos, Fred Bernardin, Brian Ulicny

entry.summary: Fine-tunes Mistral-7B as an embedding model for multi-author style change detection via cross-domain transfer, comparing against DeBERTa from prior PAN-25 SOTA systems. Shows the two models excel in different scenarios and that combining both embeddings improves detection.

entry.title: SLA-LENS: From Classroom Transcripts to CSLA-Informed and Evidence-Linked L2 Interaction Analytics

author.name: Nemika Tyagi, Olga Kellert, Phanos Kareen, Nelvin Licona-Guevara

entry.summary: Introduces SLA-LENS, an LLM-assisted framework connecting classroom transcripts to structured pedagogical annotations grounded in interactionist Second Language Acquisition theory, capturing learner errors, pedagogical functions, and repair/uptake. Applied to 40 authentic L2 Spanish classroom transcripts.

entry.title: Modeling bilingual naming performance through laterally-connected SOMs

author.name: Divya Prabhakaran, Uli Grasemann, Erie Shivers, Marissa Russell-Meill, Swathi Kiran, Risto Miikkulainen

entry.summary: Extends the BiLex computational model of the bilingual lexicon with excitatory and inhibitory lateral connections between self-organizing maps, enabling prediction of response times and error patterns. Applied to modeling individual bilinguals, including clinical populations with aphasia.

entry.title: Beyond Recall Saturation: Scaling Hard-Negative Reranker Training for Industrial Legal Retrieval

author.name: Yunhan Li, Mingjie Xie, Zeyang Shi, Gengshen Wu, Min Yang

entry.summary: This industrial study of Chinese legal retrieval shows that enlarging embedding candidate pools yields diminishing returns once top-300 recall is high, so attention should shift to reranker quality. It compares embedding-mined, self-mined, and dynamic hard-negative strategies under aligned protocols, finding an embedding-to-self-mined staged configuration most effective. The work offers practical guidance for production retrieval pipelines where evidence must rise above an output cutoff.

entry.title: Morpheus: a fully local, defense-in-depth de-identification engine for Greek clinical text - a benchmark evaluation

author.name: Filippos-Paschalis Rorris (Onassis Hospital, Athens, Greece, Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children, London, United Kingdom), Nikoleta Stanitsa (Evangelismos General Hospital, Athens, Greece), Tatiana Rorri (Onassis Hospital, Athens, Greece), Foteini Rorri (Universita della Svizzera italiana, Lugano, Switzerland), Constantine N. Antonopoulos (Attikon University Hospital, University of Athens Medical School, Athens, Greece)

entry.summary: The paper evaluates Morpheus, a fully local de-identification pipeline for Greek clinical documents, on 500 synthetic discharge summaries generated by a frontier model and independently clinician-annotated. It reports recall over must-redact identifiers and over-redaction rates, filling a gap as no Greek clinical de-identification benchmark previously existed.

entry.title: Towards Figurative Language Understanding in Moroccan Darija: An Evaluation of Large Language Models

author.name: Jihad R'baiti, Youssef Hmamouche, Emmanuele Chersoni, Chu-Ren Huang, Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni

entry.summary: Introduces the Moroccan Darija Figurative Language Corpus (MDFC), a benchmark for machine translation and multiple-choice selection covering idioms, metaphors, and proverbs in Moroccan Darija. The paper evaluates 19 open and closed models under zero- and six-shot settings and probes internal representations of figurative meaning.

entry.title: Conditional information Retrieval for Longitudinal Survey Harmonisation

author.name: Wing Yan Li, Zeqiang Wang, Michelle Lin, Jon Johnson, Suparna De

entry.summary: This work frames identifying conceptually equivalent survey questions across longitudinal studies as a two-step conditional retrieval task: a fine-tuned generative model extracts the underlying sociological concept, which then conditions question representations for retrieval. This handles cases where lexical similarity misleads, capturing conceptual equivalence despite surface differences.

entry.title: Expert L2 English Speech Evaluation on a Gaming PC: Accuracy, Fluency, and Prosody with XLS-R, XEUS, and PhoneticXeus

author.name: Richard Rose (Hankuk University of Foreign Studies)

entry.summary: oollim is a locally executable system for evaluating L2 English pronunciation accuracy, fluency, and prosody on consumer hardware, combining pretrained XLS-R, XEUS, and PhoneticXeus representations with ridge regressions trained on learner speech corpora. On 305 expert-rated held-out recordings, several configurations outperform archived Azure API scores on correlation and weighted kappa.

entry.title: TeleASR-Amharic: A Benchmark for Robust Amharic ASR in Realistic Telecommunication Conditions

author.name: Dagnachew Mekonnen Marilign, Enrique Molero, Abrham Haile, Louis Powell, Israel Abebe Azime

entry.summary: This paper introduces TeleASR-Amharic, a benchmark for evaluating Amharic speech recognition under realistic telecommunication channel conditions, environmental noise, and telecom-domain variations. The authors show that telecom degradation can drastically reduce WER, rendering even strong ASR models impractical in severe conditions, highlighting a gap between clean-studio training data and real-world deployment for low-resource languages.

entry.title: EpiLens: Lightweight RAG for Epidemiological Knowledge Acquisition

author.name: Vincenzo Perri, Ciro Cattuto, Daniela Paolotti

entry.summary: EpiLens is an open-source retrieval-augmented generation package that applies a fixed retrieval template and output schema to a corpus of 2,297 epidemiology papers, linking outputs to source passages to reduce hallucination. Its classifier matches or exceeds supervised and zero-shot baselines on four tasks without task-specific training data, supporting outbreak-preparedness literature mapping.

entry.title: Desirability Confirmation: Relational Sycophancy in AI Intimate Roleplay

author.name: Huiqian Lai, Runze Ding

entry.summary: Using a controlled audit of 2,016 outputs from two open-weight LLMs, the authors identify recurrent relational moves in AI intimate roleplay, such as legitimating desire and preserving non-rejection while communicating limits. They connect sycophancy research with sexual script theory to define desirability confirmation, a relational form of sycophancy distinct from propositional agreement. This reframing has implications for AI companion safety and design.

entry.title: Label Authority in Speech Emotion Recognition: Intended and Perceived Ground Truth in Emozionalmente

author.name: Marco Giordano, Stefano Giacomelli, Claudia Rinaldi, Fabio Graziosi

entry.summary: Using an acted Italian speech corpus with both elicited production labels and five listener judgments per clip, the paper compares three label authorities (expressed condition, listener plurality, full vote distribution) with matched probes on frozen XLS-R, HuBERT, and WavLM representations. Results show recovering the expressed condition is easier than predicting tie-broken listener labels because they are different questions, not different difficulties. It argues SER evaluation should be explicit about which ground truth is intended.

entry.title: Game of Phones: Harnessing Game Theory and LLMs in 'Bot Wars' to Counteract Phone Scams

author.name: Nardine Basta, Robin Carpentier, Benjamin Zi Hao Zhao, Dali Kaafar

entry.summary: The authors present a game-theoretic framework where LLM agents learn counter-strategies against phone scammers through in-context experience, modeling scammer-baiter interactions as a two-player game with Nash equilibrium as an evaluation benchmark. Experiments run across 300 simulated interactions without fine-tuning. The work proposes proactive scam-baiting as a defense that imposes real costs on perpetrators.

entry.title: Controllable Multi-Object Insertion for Detection Data Augmentation

author.name: Jiyang Huang, Tianwei Zhang, Xiaoqin Zhang, Ling Shao, Shijian Lu

entry.summary: SceneP2F is a two-stage framework for controllable multi-object insertion into images for detection data augmentation, coordinating scene-aware planning with layout-aligned generation to satisfy category-count fidelity and annotation alignment. It introduces ScenePlan for joint planning plus explicit instance-level layout control. The focus is on practical dataset augmentation rather than visual realism alone.

entry.title: FocusOVD: Geometric and Contextual Feature Refinement for Open-Vocabulary Small-Object Detection

author.name: Hanlin Kou, Beiqi Bai, Li Chen, Youjia Jing, Shupan Li, Mingyuan Jiu

entry.summary: FocusOVD improves open-vocabulary detection of small objects by refining features without modifying a frozen vision-language backbone. It combines reweighted cross-scale fusion, adaptive geometric/contextual aggregation, and region-level discriminability enhancements.

entry.title: Decoupled Representation Learning for Face Presentation Attack Detection under Smart Glass Capture

author.name: Raghavendra Ramachandra, Narayan Vetrekar, Neha Naik, Rajendra Gad

entry.summary: The paper introduces SmaGla-FPAD, a large face presentation attack dataset (297,000 images) captured with Ray-Ban Meta Wayfarer smart glasses across indoor, outdoor, and in-car settings with silicone mask attacks. It also proposes DeCoupPAD-FAS++, a decoupled representation learning framework separating spoof evidence from capture-related nuisance variation. This addresses an underexplored egocentric acquisition setting for biometric security.

entry.title: Spherical Geometry-Aware Panoptic Scene Graph Generation for Equirectangular Panoramas

author.name: Zhe Wu, Xiaoyan Fei, Xinyi Jiang, Yanxu Wei, Junming Rao, Yihong Yan, Xuewei Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage spherical geometry-aware framework for panoptic scene graph generation on equirectangular panoramas, fusing perspective-view predictions using observation reliability, spherical overlap, and angular proximity, with spherical-area-aware relation reasoning. It also contributes a dataset of 340 high-resolution panoramas with over 10,000 nodes and 6,600 relations, improving PQ by 36% over matched baselines. A specialized but thorough contribution to panoramic scene understanding.

entry.title: Reliability-Guided Vision-Language Decoding with Text-Aware Skip Refinement for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Sivan Talaei, Fatemeh Daneshfar, Mustaqeem Khan, Abdulhady Abas Abdullah, Mourad Oussalah

entry.summary: RELiF is a vision-language segmentation framework that fuses medical text guidance selectively, using a reliability-guided fusion gate and a text-guided skip refinement adapter to avoid unreliable cross-modal updates. It shows competitive results across radiographic, CT, and endoscopic segmentation tasks.

entry.title: GazeLens for Efficient Egocentric Video Question Answering with Simple Gaze-Driven Adaptive Token Reduction

author.name: Trong-Thang Pham, Anh Nguyen, Hien Van Nguyen, Ngan Le

entry.summary: GazeLens improves efficiency of question answering on egocentric video from smart glasses by combining frame selection (via HOG transitions and sharpness) with gaze- and question-guided token reduction, pooling tokens into gaze-focused and complementary summaries. This preserves question-relevant evidence within tight on-device compute budgets.

entry.title: Towards Autonomous Bricklaying Using Boston Dynamics Spot

author.name: Karl-Johan Sorensen, Nico vom Hofe, Frank H. P. Fitzek

entry.summary: This paper presents a proof-of-concept system for autonomous brick stacking using a Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped with a manipulator arm, navigating between supply and assembly areas via AprilTag fiducials and CAD-exported brick placements. Evaluation across ten repeated assemblies of a curved four-layer wall of 14 wooden bricks reports placement accuracy results. It matters as an early demonstration of legged robots for unstructured on-site construction tasks.

entry.title: Robot-Task Suitability in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Task Allocation

author.name: Daniel Weiner, Raj Korpan

entry.summary: This study compares ten deterministic methods and two LLM-based variants for estimating robot-task suitability in heterogeneous multi-robot task allocation, spanning rule-based, similarity-based, requirement-oriented, fuzzy, and semantic approaches. The methods frequently disagree on identical scenarios, and generic similarity measures can violate desirable formal properties. The work provides a systematic taxonomy and sensitivity analysis across team composition, scale, and capability uncertainty.

entry.title: Reinforced Iterative Learning Control for elastic joint arms: Guaranteed cross-trajectory generalization under model uncertainties

author.name: Yuri De Santis, Michele Pierallini, Franco Angelini, Manolo Garabini

entry.summary: The paper proposes Reinforced Iterative Learning Control (RILC), combining the precision and passivity preservation of iterative learning control with the cross-trajectory generalization of reinforcement learning for compliant robot arms. The method achieves fast adaptation and guaranteed tracking convergence across diverse trajectories despite nonlinear dynamics and modeling uncertainty.

entry.title: MAPLE: Mondrian-Anchored Prior for Learning-free Indoor Exploration

author.name: Kelvin Aladum, Nisar Ahmed

entry.summary: MAPLE is a training-free approach to predicting occupancy of unseen indoor space during exploration, adapting the Mondrian process into an online generative prior conditioned on observed geometric cues. It generates multiple plausible map hypotheses and evaluates frontier visibility gain within each, avoiding the offline training and repeated inference required by learned predictors.

entry.title: Quadratic Sample Complexity for Strictly Replicable Realizable Learning with Unknown Marginals

author.name: Guangjian Zhang

entry.summary: This paper determines the finite-class sample-complexity exponent for strict replicability under realizable distributions with unknown marginals, proving a worst-case Theta((log M)^2) bound and an Omega(d^2/(epsilon rho^2)) lower bound, with matching Theta characterizations for the full Boolean parity class. The results quantify how costly exact replicability is when two samples and a shared seed must yield identical learners.

entry.title: Robust Latent Variable Graphical Models: Exact Recovery and Fundamental Limits

author.name: Chuansen Peng, Xiaojing Shen

entry.summary: The paper studies robust estimation of Gaussian precision matrices decomposing as sparse minus low-rank, arising from latent-variable marginalization plus conditioning on linear measurements. It proposes a convex estimator using measure-transformed covariance and a congruence-transform nuclear norm, with a primal-dual witness theorem giving exact signed-graph recovery and matching fundamental limits under restricted invertibility and irrepresentability conditions.

entry.title: MiCLA: Mixture-to-Constituent Latent Alignment for Polyphonic Audio Representation Learning

author.name: Kohei Yamamoto, Kosuke Okusa

entry.summary: MiCLA is a two-stage self-supervised pre-training framework for audio that uses synthetic log-mel mixing to align mixture representations with their constituent clips, employing masked self-distillation and bidirectional residual alignment on patch tokens. It explicitly models mixture-constituent relationships that standard self-supervised audio methods ignore.

entry.title: BARRR: Bidimensional Augmented Reduced Rank Regression for Multi-View Multi-Cohort Data

author.name: Jiuzhou Wang, Eric F. Lock

entry.summary: BARRR is a supervised method for bidimensional integration of multi-view, multi-cohort biomedical data that simultaneously models covariate-related and unrelated effects while decomposing them across views and cohorts. It fills a gap left by existing integrative methods that handle only one dimension and are mostly unsupervised.

entry.title: Firewalls for the Mind Before We Need Them

author.name: Will Duncan

entry.summary: The author argues that persuasive AI is an underrated risk and proposes preemptively deploying cognition firewalls that use cheap LLM classifiers to filter or flag manipulative content for users, addressing both current recommender-system harms and future strong persuasive AI. The post reviews evidence that AI persuasion is modestly superhuman in lab settings but not yet demonstrably in the wild, and frames firewalls as both defense and a detection sensor array.

entry.title: HypTI: Hyperbolic Geometry-Aware Multimodal Feature Fusion Framework for Dementia Detection Based on Tabular-Image Data

author.name: Jianfei Xu, Huizhi Liang, Judith Harrison, John-Paul Taylor, Jaume Bacardit, Varun Ojha

entry.summary: HypTI fuses clinical tabular assessments with MRI scans in hyperbolic space for dementia detection, exploiting hyperbolic geometry's fit for hierarchical clinical structures and multi-scale anatomical patterns. It extends hyperbolic multimodal fusion to a clinically meaningful diagnosis task.

entry.title: Agentic Ensemble with Vision-Language Models for Visual Anomaly Detection

author.name: Shangquan Sun, Wenjun Luo, Xu He, Yoonsoo Lee, Shijian Lu

entry.summary: AnomalyAgent is a post-training agentic framework for visual anomaly detection that aligns heterogeneous scores and maps from multiple pretrained detectors and treats fusion as a finite action-selection problem over score- and region-level disagreements. This adaptively handles cases where fixed fusion rules fail due to detector disagreement.

entry.title: Enhancing analytical photon transport in turbid media through physics-guided neural network corrections

author.name: Guojun Tang, Paul D. Teal, Alexander Doronin

entry.summary: This work proposes a physics-guided residual learning framework that combines fast analytical models of light transport in turbid media with neural network corrections trained against Monte Carlo simulation, the gold standard but computationally expensive. The approach targets real-time and inverse-problem applications where repeated forward evaluations are needed. The diffusion approximation is the representative case study.

entry.title: HierDTA: Hierarchical Structure-Aware Representation Learning for Drug--Target Affinity Prediction

author.name: Huangchao Xu, Baohua Zhang, Qian Liu, Zhong Jin, Yi Du

entry.summary: HierDTA is a hierarchical framework for drug-target affinity prediction that represents drugs as atom-motif heterogeneous graphs with motif-to-atom semantic propagation, and models protein binding sites with kinase-domain structural conversion. It aims to improve compound-protein pair prioritization before experimental validation.

entry.title: Progressive Subset Selection and Cascaded Consistency for Unsupervised Vision-Language Model Adaptation

author.name: Hao Yan, Guanghui Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a simple unsupervised adaptation framework for pretrained vision-language models combining progressive margin-based subset selection with cascaded consistency learning. It tackles unreliable pseudo-labels and the lack of labeled validation sets via class-balanced gradual expansion of the pseudo-labeled set. This improves zero-shot models under domain shift without any labeled target data.

entry.title: Learned Readout Tokens for Extracting Large Language Model Confidence

author.name: Nima Seifi, Martin Ester

entry.summary: ScratchProbe improves LLM confidence estimation by training probes on hidden states of a newly learned readout token rather than existing vocabulary tokens. The learned token gives cleaner access to correctness-relevant internal information. Better confidence estimates support responsible deployment of LLMs in consequential applications.

entry.title: Hearsay or Fact? How Framing and Elicitation Shape LLM Probability Updates

author.name: An-Sheng Jhang

entry.summary: This study measures how much LLM probability estimates move in response to single new pieces of information, comparing stated versus reported (hearsay) updates and different elicitation formats using SNLI-derived premise-hypothesis items. By eliciting priors and posteriors in separate calls with signed directional movement, it quantifies Bayesian-style update behavior. The work informs both judgment-assistant use and LLMs as participants in psychology experiments.

entry.title: PULSE: Personalized Opportunistic Learning for Wearable Devices

author.name: Mattia Giovanni Campana, Dariush Salami, H\"useyin Yi\u{g}itler, Stephan Sigg

entry.summary: PULSE is an event-driven framework for personalized learning on wearables that treats each device encounter as an online collaboration decision, selecting among no interaction or promising neighbor interactions based on utility, compatibility, and communication cost. This avoids the stable-connectivity assumptions of federated learning while respecting limited local data.

entry.title: DS-Net: A Dynamic Split Network for Edge-Cloud Collaborative Inference

author.name: Xinyun Zhang, Li Wang, Lei Jin, Lianming Xu, Zhu Han

entry.summary: DS-Net enables edge-cloud collaborative inference with flexible switching among multiple split points within a single model, avoiding the storage and switching overhead of loading separate models per split point. It improves collaborative speed and accuracy across varying communication and device conditions.

entry.title: Dynamic Neural Optimal Transport for Subset Alignment

author.name: Austin J. Brockmeier, Bilal Riaz

entry.summary: The paper formulates optimal transport between distributions when only a subset of the target population is relevant, constraining the density ratio to [0, c] to select a target subpopulation while limiting over-emphasis. A dynamic neural OT framework uses two networks: one for a time-dependent potential whose gradient is the velocity field and whose terminal value enforces the constraint, and one for the interpolation. This extends neural OT to a practically meaningful constrained setting.

entry.title: Learning Administrative Boundary-Aware Location Encoders via Reverse Geocoding

author.name: Lakshay Sharma, Alex Marin

entry.summary: The authors introduce the first method for learning administrative boundary-aware location encoders, using reverse-geocoded text as self-supervised supervision for lat-lon representations. The approach is architecture-agnostic and consistently improves downstream geospatial prediction across existing encoder designs. They also introduce evaluation benchmarks to measure boundary awareness.

entry.title: TopoCompile: Molecular Generation with Exact Global Count Constraints

author.name: Xiang Wu, Rong-Hua Li, Quanqing Xu, Kangfei Zhao, Guoren Wang

entry.summary: TopoCompile combines an autoregressive component-tree generator with a dynamic-programming compiler to guarantee exact satisfaction of global count constraints (size, elemental composition, ring content) in molecular generation. A transformer scores actions while the compiler masks invalid ones, ensuring hard constraint satisfaction rather than soft steering.

entry.title: From Overparameterised Expressions to Parsimonious Models: Fisher-Geometric Pruning for Symbolic Regression

author.name: Veronica Guidetti, Luca La Rocca, Fabr\'icio Olivetti de Fran\c{c}a, Gabriel Kronberger

entry.summary: Fisher-Geometric pruning (FGP) is a post-hoc model-reduction framework for genetic programming symbolic regression that combines local information geometry at the maximum-likelihood solution with compatibility tests for interpretable parametric boundaries. It complements existing syntactic complexity-control strategies by pruning dormant branches and noise-fitting configurations from fitted models.

entry.title: Multi-site Learning for Forecasting Day-Ahead Wind-Power Production for Onshore Wind Farms in Great Britain with Deep Neural Networks

author.name: James Kean, Aidan O'Sullivan

entry.summary: The authors train multi-site deep recurrent networks on pooled production and reanalysis data from 88 onshore wind farms in Great Britain, matching NESO's operational day-ahead forecast schedule and combining reanalysis training covariates with NWP forecasts at inference. This improves day-ahead wind forecasting relevant to grid balancing. It is a solid applied energy-ML contribution with operational realism.

entry.title: NADS: Navigator-Guided Data Selection for Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting in Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jianhao Zhang, Ou Wu, Yi Du

entry.summary: NADS mitigates catastrophic forgetting during single-stage LLM fine-tuning when pretraining data is unavailable, by first running the fine-tuning recipe without preservation regularization to obtain a navigator signal, then using it to select useful synthetic data from noisy candidate pools. This replaces indirect proxy signals with a signal more aligned with actual training benefit. It targets a common practical constraint in fine-tuning pipelines.

entry.title: PnP-CF: A Consensus Flow-Matching Solver for General Inverse Problems

author.name: Dibyanshu Kumar, Magda Gregorova

entry.summary: PnP-CF extends a flow-based plug-and-play framework to nonlinear inverse problems, including those with learned neural-network forward operators. It combines a flow-matching denoiser with ADMM-like dual updates and a time-adaptive pullback onto the intermediate flow probability path, seeking consensus between the solver and generative sampler. This broadens generative-prior inverse problem solving beyond linear settings.

entry.title: Super-resolution as Spatial Downscaling: Coherence, Structure and Task Utility in Earth Observation

author.name: Bright Wiredu Nuakoh, Ebenezer Afrifa-Yamoah

entry.summary: The paper reframes satellite super-resolution as spatial downscaling and evaluates four lightweight networks (including a 0.36M-parameter model) against interpolation using structural criteria beyond pixel metrics, such as directional variograms, codispersion, and observation coherence. Networks beat bicubic by about 1.4 dB at x2 but recover only roughly 30% of spectral power above the observed resolution.

entry.title: Corrected Block Sparse Spectral Optimization: Exact Models, Finite Identification, and Local Dynamics

author.name: Omid Shams Solari

entry.summary: This paper rebuilds the block generalized-power method for sparse spectral optimization from first principles, showing that the standard formulation conflates two nonequivalent objectives and proving exact identities for both. It supplies explicit conventions for degenerate cases and provides finite identification and local dynamics analysis for the corrected model.

entry.title: Physics-Driven Framework for QoS-Constrained Satellite System with Non-Linear PA Distortion

author.name: Hamza Ahmed Qureshi, Abuzar Babikir Mohammad Adam, Vu Nguyen Ha, Konstantinos Ntontin, Symeon Chatzinotas
