entry.summary: Develops a self-supervised graph neural network that jointly designs distortion-aware precoders and admission control for a downlink MISO satellite system under nonlinear correlated power amplifier distortion, using a differentiable Ito-Hermite model without optimizer-generated labels. Minimizes nonlinear PA power consumption subject to user QoS constraints.

entry.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Market Making on Prediction-Market Order Books

author.name: Skander Lejmi

entry.summary: A single-author study training cooperative multi-agent RL market makers for prediction markets like Polymarket, whose thin order books create challenges of adverse selection, delayed action consequences, and unlabeled order-level data. The paper reconstructs LOBSTER-format order data from Polymarket and trains agents in JaxMARL-HFT across 417 real markets. It enriches baseline market-making agents to cope with these dynamics.

entry.title: AfriBED: a Speech Recognition Bias Evaluation Dataset for Low Resource African Languages

author.name: Claytone Sikasote, Hussein Suleman, Jan Buys

entry.summary: AfriBED is a speech recognition bias evaluation dataset for Bemba and Nyanja, comprising nine hours of comparable speech across demographic subgroups to measure gender and speaker-type bias in ASR systems. It enables rigorous assessment of speaker-attribute bias in low-resource settings where such evaluation resources are scarce.

entry.title: GTSM: Gaussian Splatting with Thermal State-Space Dynamics for Spatio-Temporal Thermal Field Reconstruction and Prediction

author.name: Yunpeng Zhao, Haoxiang Zhang, Chao Liu

entry.summary: GTSM reconstructs and predicts 4D spatio-temporal temperature fields from 2D multi-view observations without predefined 3D models or thermodynamic equations. It combines Gaussian splatting with a state-space dynamics model, using shared scene-level latent processes and per-Gaussian thermal states propagated via differentiable RK2 integration. Applications include industrial condition monitoring and process analysis.

entry.title: Text-Anchored Modality Experts with Uncertainty-Guided Routing for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Xiaohua Huang, Bingrui Lei, Xiuyan hao, Ling Zhou, Yuan Zong, Wenming Zheng, Guoying Zhao

entry.summary: TAME reformulates multimodal sentiment analysis as uncertainty-guided refinement, treating text as a fixed always-active shared expert and routing noisy audio and visual evidence selectively. This asymmetric mixture-of-modality-experts design respects language's dominant semantic role.

entry.title: Media Intelligence Platform: Multimodal Detection of Synthetic and Manipulated Content

author.name: David Fischinger, Marcel Hasenbalg, Silvia Poletti, Davide Antonutti, Mina Sch\"utz, Lam Pham, Justin Ilyes, P\'eter Rjabcsenk\'o, Simon Freitter, Martin Boyer

entry.summary: The Media Intelligence Platform (MIP) is a unified web-based system integrating modules for fake video, face morphing, AI-generated image, audio deepfake, localized image manipulation, and text analysis detection. Its modular architecture handles heterogeneous real-world media sources where single-manipulation detectors fall short. A systems contribution for media forensics.

entry.title: Learn to Modify: Self-evolving Multi-agent Refinement Framework for Conversational Text-to-Motion Generation

author.name: Jianan Li, Jiawei Zhao, Yangtao Zhou, Zhifu Zhao, Shaoxin Wu, Yutao Wang, Dezhen Wang, Hua Chu, Fu Li

entry.summary: This work introduces a conversational text-to-motion paradigm where users iteratively refine specific motion regions via feedback rather than regenerating whole sequences. It uses an LLM-driven multi-agent framework coordinating instruction understanding, localized editing, generation, and quality assessment, with a self-evolving refinement loop.

entry.title: Updatelessness explained

author.name: Chi Nguyen

entry.summary: A tutorial-style introduction to updateless decision theory for readers familiar with EDT and CDT, using examples like Parfit's Hitchhiker to motivate agents following policies they would have committed to before observing their situation. It covers pseudo-updateless agents, full updatelessness, an argument against combining EDT with updating, and distinctions between action, policy, and logical updatelessness.

entry.title: LSA-PAST: Layer-Specific Adaptation and Prototype Transport for Compositional Incremental Learning

author.name: Kyle Stein, Andrew Arash Mahyari, Guillermo Francia III, Eman El-Sheikh, Jiangpeng He

entry.summary: LSA-PAST addresses compositional incremental learning where visual concepts combine state and object primitives, introducing layer-specific adaptation and prototype transport to stabilize shared primitive representations and prevent drift as new state-object compositions arrive. This improves on standard class-incremental methods that treat each composition independently.

entry.title: Model Exposure on One Device Endangers Others: Rethinking Edge Neural Network Security across Devices

author.name: Yuyang Zhang, Kangjie Chen, Yihui Jin, Run Wang

entry.summary: This paper formalizes the cross-node attack threat for centrally distributed on-device neural networks, showing adversarial examples crafted on one unpacked, compromised device transfer to all nodes sharing the model. It proposes VeilNN, a defense that injects controlled model diversity via obfuscation while preserving task functionality to reduce adversarial transferability.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models for Electrical Load Forecasting

author.name: Aliullah, Julian Oelhaf, Edouard Fouch\'e, Jessica Deuschel, Christian Bergler, Andreas Maier, Siming Bayer

entry.summary: A systematic comparison of pretrained inference, full fine-tuning, and LoRA adaptation for time series foundation models on electrical load forecasting across four aggregation levels and both in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings. MOIRAI 1.0 Large is the primary backbone, with Chronos-2 used to check cross-family transferability of findings.

entry.title: Compose the Horizon: Parameter-Shared Blockwise Forecasting under a Sequential-Compute Trade-off

author.name: Zeyan Li, Weiheng Li, Shengda Zhuo, Libing Chen, Min Chen, Yin Tang

entry.summary: Recursive Functional Decomposition (RFD) rethinks long-horizon forecasting by having a compact parameter-shared operator emit contiguous future blocks sequentially, trading stored parameters for sequential computation. Controlled multi-seed experiments isolate that forward feedback's useful signal is the evolving forecast state itself, since removing feedback hurts while stopping gradients through it changes little.

entry.title: Computation, Not Memory: Chain-of-Thought and State Tracking in LLM Agents

author.name: Pedram Mouseli, Massieh Moayedi

entry.summary: Using a small file-system lock-tracking task with Qwen3-8B and Qwen3.5-9B (existing released models), this study separates two roles of chain-of-thought reasoning in agents: generating reasoning at the moment of action versus retaining earlier reasoning in the prompt. Most reduction in lock-violating errors comes from reasoning generated at action time, while retaining earlier reasoning adds little. The result suggests CoT primarily serves as computation rather than a memory mechanism.

entry.title: From Retrieval to Recognition:Knowledge-Enhanced Post-training of Time Series Foundation Models for Classification

author.name: Zhen Liu, Yucheng Wang, Yingpeng Du, Tianjun Wei, Qianli Ma, Min Wu, Jie Zhang, Zhu Sun

entry.summary: The paper proposes R2R (Retrieval-to-Recognition), a plug-and-play post-training paradigm for time series foundation models in classification. Instead of implicit fine-tuning that entangles task knowledge in parameter space, R2R uses a decoupled query encoder to retrieve discriminative patterns and make them explicit inputs to the frozen model. This improves knowledge activation for downstream classification without retraining a foundation model.

entry.title: Two hidden layer suffice: the caterpillar net

author.name: Jakob Paul Zimmermann

entry.summary: In the study of ReLU network expressivity, the paper gives the Caterpillar Net, a nonrecursive two-hidden-layer construction for the maximum of N inputs, with widths O(N^2) and 2^{O(N log N)}, building on a 2026 proof that two hidden layers suffice for general continuous piecewise-linear functions. It provides a direct geometric interpretation of the construction. This settles aspects of a central question about representing maxima, following the disproof of the logarithmic-depth conjecture.

entry.title: VEOcc++: Learning Persistent Voxel Feature Maps for Embodied Online Semantic Occupancy Mapping and Offline Refinement

author.name: Ruoyu Wang, Jiahan Li, Yong Liu, Kexin Zhang

entry.summary: VEOcc++ unifies online incremental semantic occupancy mapping and offline global refinement through a persistent sparse voxel feature map, with reliability-guided updates during exploration and cached-feature refinement afterward.

entry.title: Codec-Compatible Learned Compression for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Feiyang Yu, Qi Yang, Wenjie Huang, Yunfeng Guan, Yiling Xu, Zhu Li

entry.summary: CCT-GS improves 3DGS compression by learning a generalized transform for spherical harmonic attribute maps that converts them into codec-friendly representations before coding with standard video codecs, exploiting cross-scene regularities and nonlinear coefficient dependencies. This targets the dominant share of the 3DGS bitstream carried by non-DC SH maps.

entry.title: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System

author.name: He Ma, Lan You, Qiyang Wu, Chen Liu

entry.summary: LightCRS unifies multimodal conversational recommendation across many product domains by precomputing product representations offline with frozen encoders and using a compact 5.3M-parameter query-conditioned module online, avoiding per-domain VLM deployment cost and the accuracy loss of naive domain merging.

entry.title: Securing Agentic Commerce Through Behavior-Aware Fraud Detection and Cybersecurity for Trusted AI-Agent Payment Authorization

author.name: Kayode L. Ogunsusi

entry.summary: Introduces ACAGS, a cybersecurity framework combining supervised ML (XGBoost), behavioral analytics, agent-specific authorization controls, and explainable AI to counter agent impersonation, unauthorized payments, and misuse of delegated authority in agentic commerce. Evaluated on synthetic transaction data with five adversarial scenarios, behavioral features improved mean F1 from 52.12% across ten runs.

entry.title: From Encoding to Generation: Towards Empathetic Large Language Models

author.name: Samhita Bollepally, Takashi Yamauchi, Marissa West

entry.summary: Uses layer-wise linear probing and token-attention analysis on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct to distinguish cognitive empathy (decoding another's emotional state, peaking around layer 11 with 63.6% held-out accuracy) from affective empathy (generating appropriate responses). It examines how emotion information is attended to and carried through response generation.

entry.title: Quantum-JEPA: Quantum Born Priors for Latent-Action JEPA World Models

author.name: Zhiyuan Liu, Sicheng Liu, Haiyu Wu

entry.summary: Quantum-JEPA introduces a latent-action JEPA world model using a conditional quantum Born prior, where circuit measurements generate binary latent actions mapped by a shared predictor to alternative future representation distributions. It trains the prior via a sampled energy objective and shows distinct continuation learning on multimodal tasks and D3IL, including multi-agent coordinated futures.

entry.title: Polyscene: Scenario Planning as Diversity Planning

author.name: Mustafa F. Abdelwahed, Joan Espasa, Felipe Meneguzzi

entry.summary: Polyscene automates strategic scenario planning by recasting it as a diversity planning problem, generating sets of plausible futures that are plausible, consistent, relevant, and mutually differentiated. This replaces manual expert workshops that are slow, biased, and hard to repeat as conditions change.

entry.title: Large Language Models for Agent-Based Modelling: Current and possible uses across the modelling cycle

author.name: Lo\"is Vanh\'ee, Melania Borit, Peer-Olaf Siebers, Roger Cremades, Christopher Frantz, \"Onder G\"urcan, Franti\v{s}ek Kalvas, Denisa Reshef Kera, Vivek Nallur, Kavin Narasimhan, Martin Neumann

entry.summary: A position/review paper from the agent-based modelling (ABM) community examining current and prospective uses of LLMs across the entire modelling cycle, from problem formulation to documentation. It reviews existing LLM applications in ABM and reflects on opportunities and challenges. The author list includes established ABM methodologists.

entry.title: Mind Your Boundaries: Boundary-Aware Model Obfuscation against Cross-node Attack

author.name: Yuyang Zhang, Yihui Jin, Kangjie Chen, Leyang Wu, Run Wang

entry.summary: The paper addresses cross-node attacks on edge-deployed models, where an attacker with white-box access on one compromised device crafts adversarial examples that transfer to peer devices with the same model. It proposes a boundary-aware model obfuscation defense that diversifies model decision boundaries across distributed deployments.

entry.title: Trail-Weighted Influence Scores for Approximate Outcome Prediction in Bayesian Networks

author.name: Sahil Kumar Rajput, Randhir Kumar

entry.summary: The authors study trail-weighted pruning of evidence in Bayesian networks, enumerating active trails from evidence nodes to the outcome and dropping low-scoring evidence. For collider-free networks over binary variables they prove the trail score equals exact endpoint correlation and bound the pruned posterior within a computable sum of per-trail terms, verifying exhaustively on small trees. This offers principled, efficient approximate inference for restricted network classes.

entry.title: Cross-Visibility-Gap Identity Persistence for 4D Scene Graphs

author.name: Jiahui Hu, Li Gao, Yu Liu, Pengzhan Zhou

entry.summary: CVG-SGM addresses persistent object identity in 4D scene graphs when objects disappear inside opaque carriers and reappear as fresh detections, using relational history rather than appearance. It introduces a transfer-maintain-read memory with geometry-weighted cross-node interaction and a per-node GRU. This is relevant to robotics and scene understanding in occlusion-heavy environments.

entry.title: From Code Generator to Engineering Companion: A Plant-aware Agent for PLC Programming

author.name: Joschka Kersting, Gesa Benndorf

entry.summary: The paper presents a plant-aware conversational copilot for PLC programming that extends retrieval-augmented code generation with plant-specific context ingestion, a chat-first interaction model for explanation and debugging, and a graduated tool-access ladder from chat to deployment. It targets the manual, IDE-centric workflow of industrial automation engineers.

entry.title: Model- and Layer-Level Closed-Loop Forecasting with SSM-Based Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Erik Stolt, Sanja Karilanova, Ayca Ozcelikkale

entry.summary: This paper addresses the open question of how to perform time-series forecasting with spiking neural networks, whose standard autoregressive processing requires values unavailable at forecast time. The authors propose closed-loop forecasting approaches at model and layer levels for SSM-based SNNs.

entry.title: SECURE-AI: Multi-Signal Uncertainty Quantification for Trustworthy Acoustic Cough Detection

author.name: Sejal Solkhan, Feiya Xiang, Mayur Sanap, Geet Khatri, Edgar Lobaton

entry.summary: This paper presents SECURE-AI, a framework that wraps a frozen MobileNetV3 cough classifier with multiple uncertainty quantification techniques — Monte Carlo Dropout, Temperature Scaling, and Mahalanobis distance in embedding space — to flag predictions that should not be trusted in deployment. Evaluated on a held-out split of 12,161 Coswara recordings, it addresses the problem of acoustic health-monitoring models failing silently under speech, noise, and out-of-distribution audio. The work matters because confidently wrong medical predictions are more harmful than abstaining, and this provides a practical trust layer for deployed health AI.

entry.title: SPADE-KD: Peer-to-Peer Collaborative Learning under Heterogeneous Settings

author.name: Harikrishna Kuttivelil, Katia Obraczka

entry.summary: SPADE-KD is a decentralized peer-to-peer learning method that avoids central aggregators and supports heterogeneous client architectures without shared public data, using knowledge distillation and personalized local solutions rather than a single global model. It targets robustness to non-IID client distributions.

entry.title: Graph-Regularized Synthetic Control for Stable Counterfactual Estimation under Donor Redundancy

author.name: Yanlin Zhang, Sungyong Chung, Alireza Talebpour

entry.summary: The paper proposes Graph-SC, a convex synthetic control estimator adding a graph Laplacian penalty on donor similarity to stabilize weights when the donor pool is large, highly correlated, and short in pre-treatment history. The authors provide theoretical results on bias-variance tradeoffs while preserving the interpretability of synthetic controls. It targets causal estimation in settings with redundant donors.

entry.title: VBO-MI: A Differentiable Black-Box Optimization Framework via Variational Mutual Information Estimation

author.name: Farhad Mirkarimi

entry.summary: VBO-MI is a fully gradient-based Bayesian optimization framework that replaces Gaussian processes and expensive posterior sampling with variational mutual information estimation, avoiding cubic scaling in observations and inner-loop acquisition optimization. It targets expensive noisy black-box optimization in high dimensions.

entry.title: Native Probability Outputs for Clinical Triage: An Evaluation of Calibration and Decision Accuracy

author.name: Liang You, Zhiyin Zhou, Dawei Tang, Chuchu Wu, Jingzhuo Hu

entry.summary: This evaluation examines Jev, a decision model returning native probabilities over predefined triage actions, against four general-purpose LLMs and baselines on CARE-Bench and HealthBench. Notably, Jev ranks fourth of five on macro-F1 but achieves the lowest multiclass Brier score with an 18.7% improvement over uniform prediction, highlighting a calibration-versus-accuracy distinction clinically.

entry.title: TrustAgent-RFF: Agentic Diagnostic Planning for Reliable RF Fingerprinting under Domain Shift

author.name: Chuan Liu, Tianya Zhao, Xuyu Wang

entry.summary: TrustAgent-RFF is a prediction-level reliability framework for radio frequency fingerprinting that acquires multiple evidence types (counterfactual stability, prototype consistency, domain similarity, signal quality) for each device prediction under a frozen I/Q classifier without target labels. A source-calibrated trust estimator combines these diagnostics to flag unreliable predictions under domain shift.

entry.title: Sampling and Curvature in First-Exit Comparisons for Momentum SGD

author.name: Haiyi Li

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that first-exit behavior of momentum SGD depends on sampling information that pointwise gradient laws omit, proving that pools with identical pointwise laws can have different exit probabilities under persistent versus iid minibatch sampling. It establishes an explicit O(h) mean-exit comparison in one dimension and validates predictions in trained ridge-logistic runs. It deepens the stochastic-process understanding of SGD dynamics.

entry.title: Data-driven forecasting of tropical cloud forest phenology: A dynamical systems and machine learning hybrid approach

author.name: Pedro Garcia, Saul Flores

entry.summary: The authors combine dynamical systems theory with Gaussian Process Regression to forecast flowering and fruiting cycles in a Venezuelan tropical cloud forest, using a 35-year dataset and Takens-theorem-based delay embeddings with climate forcings. The approach provides uncertainty estimates without preconceived functional forms. This matters for ecology under climate change, though it is a domain-specific application.

entry.title: KPI-Aware Multimodal Anomaly Detection for 5G and Open RAN Telemetry

author.name: Chiman Salavati, Liang Wu, Kelly Wan, Mayank Darbari, Liangjie Hong

entry.summary: KAC is a deployment-oriented anomaly detection framework for 5G/Open RAN telemetry that aligns compact operator-style text summaries with full-KPI temporal evidence, combining broad numerical coverage with sparse KPI-specific reasoning. It targets practical deployment bottlenecks: hundreds of heterogeneous KPIs, severe class imbalance, and strict alert budgets. Evaluated on public telecom telemetry and enterprise-scale data.

entry.title: PRISM: Prior Relational Information for Self-supervised Modeling to Enhance Solubility OOD Generalization

author.name: Xinyi Chen, Jiahuan Pang, Titus Chima, Paul Weng, Wendong Wang

entry.summary: PRISM is a label-free pretraining framework for molecular property prediction that learns chemically meaningful relational information between solutes and solvents, applied to solubility out-of-distribution generalization. It aims to alleviate data scarcity where supervised methods fail on unseen solutes, solvents, and mixtures. Relevant to drug discovery and chemical engineering.

entry.title: Can Metadata Fix the Gauge? Calibration Turns Sparse Multi-Source Learning from Sparse PCA into Sparse Mean Recovery

author.name: Yirong Xiang, Yibo Zhou

entry.summary: The authors formalize how source-specific sign gauges change a sparse multi-source learning problem: without calibration, pooled data reduces to sparse PCA, but with relative-gauge metadata the problem becomes the easier sparse mean recovery. They introduce AlignedMass to quantify how much first-order signal metadata-induced alignment restores. The result clarifies when metadata has provable statistical value.

entry.title: Residual-Guided Adaptive Tucker Rank Allocation for Parameter-Efficient MCI Conversion Prediction

author.name: Guanghua He, Hancan Zhu, Gaohang Yu, An Zhang

entry.summary: This work proposes a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for 3D convolutional networks that adaptively allocates Tucker rank pairs across layers under a fixed adapter budget. Perturbation analysis bounds output discrepancy via layerwise reconstruction residuals, motivating a residual-guided allocation strategy. It is applied to predicting conversion from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's disease.

entry.title: Training with ML-labeled Data via Stochastic First- and Zeroth-Order Optimization

author.name: Maria-Eleni Sfyraki, Jun-Kun Wang

entry.summary: The authors study training when a dataset mixes ground-truth labels with potentially noisy labels from an ML predictor, proposing both first-order and zeroth-order stochastic optimization methods. This addresses the practical scalability concern that human labeling cannot keep pace with large datasets, making ML-assisted annotation increasingly common. The work provides theoretical and algorithmic tools for robust optimization under such mixed-label regimes.

entry.title: ASR Personalization in Pathological Voice: Accuracy, Efficiency, and Duration Effects

author.name: Giuseppe Giaimis, Sergei Katkov, Muhammad Azfar Yaqub, Antonio Liotta

entry.summary: This empirical study analyzes LoRA adapter placement in Whisper for personalizing speech recognition to speakers with pathological voice, a setting with limited per-speaker data. It finds that model scaling alone does not remove the speaker mismatch and that full-attention LoRA offers the best accuracy and time-accuracy trade-off, with effects varying by utterance length. Results are relevant to clinical and accessibility applications.

entry.title: Scalable and Adaptive Distribution Regression via Random Features

author.name: Yinsong Wang, Xiao Liu, Yu Ding

entry.summary: The paper develops Random Feature Distribution Regression (RaDR) with finite-sample theory under two-stage sampling, using perturbation analysis to separate the effects of distribution-level sampling, finite within-bag sampling, and random feature approximation. It establishes sufficient feature-budget conditions for scalability and provides adaptive kernel selection within the distribution regression framework.

entry.title: An Information-Geometric Framework for OCS-Reconfigurable Interconnect Topology in Large-Scale AI Clusters

author.name: Shintaro Yoshizawa

entry.summary: This work provides a unified information-geometric framework for designing programmable optical circuit switch wiring in AI clusters, modeling wirings as points in a probability simplex and optimizing free energy combining smoothed critical-path cost with KL divergence from a symmetric Fat-Tree prior. The authors prove well-posedness and adaptation bounds for the resulting optimization.

entry.title: ChronoChart: Setup-Agnostic Channel Charting for Label-Free Indoor Localization

author.name: Majid Sharghi Foroushani, Jonas Pirkl, Jonathan Ott, Maximilian Stahlke, George Yammine, Tobias Feigl, Christopher Mutschler

entry.summary: ChronoChart improves channel charting for radio-based indoor localization by removing dependence on setup-specific dissimilarity metrics and precomputed quadratic distance matrices, enabling scalable label-free position estimation in dynamic multipath environments.

entry.title: Narrow Decision Models: A System-1 Architecture for Calibrated, Typed Decisions

author.name: Carlos Andr\'e Antunes, Aldry Albuquerque, Gabriel de Melo Schmith, Nat\~a Batista, Pedro Oziel Escobar da Silva, Stefano Benko Rossi, Lingrid Dietrich Lorenz da Silva, Fl\'avia Cristina da Costa, Thiago Bertotto, Luis Fernando Fausto

entry.summary: The paper explores the opposite end of the design space from general-purpose System-1 models like TypeSafe's Jev: Narrow Decision Models (NDMs) share a typed decision interface (Choice, Score, Noul) with calibrated probabilities but are trained for one organization's decisions, small enough for on-premise deployment with an open, testable architecture.

entry.title: The Control Layer Behind Rule-Following Agents Trading Across Market Conditions

author.name: Saad Naja, Nasser Odtallah, Jake Van-Praag, Sarah May

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether four AI trading agents adhered to their declared strategies and risk rules across 2,627 closed positions between February and August 2026, mostly simulated against live prices with 18% real orders on Hyperliquid. It provides traders with an evaluation toolkit to distinguish rule-following from luck before granting agents autonomy or capital. The fleet finished net positive after fees with high rule adherence.

entry.title: How Well Can LLMs Verbalize Mathematical Formulas? A Multi-Domain Evaluation

author.name: Peter Volbach, Tim Schlippe

entry.summary: The authors evaluate five state-of-the-art LLMs on generating spoken verbalizations of LaTeX mathematical formulas across six scientific domains, releasing Read-Aloud Math, a balanced multi-domain corpus with manually validated transcriptions. GPT-5.2, an existing frontier model, achieves the highest multi-reference BLEU for simple transcriptions at 75.9% without context, dropping to 64.9% with context. The task matters for text-to-speech accessibility, especially for visually impaired learners.

entry.title: Behave Like Experts: Fusing Data with Semantic Knowledge for Effective and Efficient Semantic Map Construction

author.name: Zhu Liu, Zhen Hu, Yuxuan Liu, Ying Liu

entry.summary: The paper improves semantic map model construction by fusing distributional semantic knowledge from language-model internal representations into a top-down, data-driven graph-building algorithm, mimicking expert use of prior knowledge. This re-sorts candidate graphs in a large search space, improving both accuracy and efficiency.

entry.title: Modal Sense Disambiguation in Language Models: The Role of Context, Training Domain, and Input Frequency

author.name: Ezgi Ba\c{s}ar, Yevgen Matusevych, Annemarie van Dooren, Arianna Bisazza

entry.summary: Evaluates seven language models on distinguishing root versus epistemic senses of modals like may and must, using vector similarity and surprisal measures across four datasets. The study examines whether LMs use context to disambiguate modal senses and whether performance tracks training data distributions.

entry.title: Training Negatives Still Matter After Calibrating Answerability Readouts

author.name: Jinchen Zhang, Zheyuan Liu, Yihan Zhu, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: A controlled study showing that keeping negative passages during training (native training) yields better-calibrated answerability predictions than removing them (empty training), even when calibration is applied afterward. Experiments on SQuAD 2.0 and RepLiQA with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B-it show lower Brier loss and better fusion behavior for native-trained readouts.

entry.title: I$^2$-Med: Interpretable Medical Inference through Visual-Guided Dynamic Logits Calibration

author.name: Md Sajid, Shreeyut Maheshwari, Akshat Mishra, Ritik Mishra, Mohammad Tanveer

entry.summary: I2-Med is a framework for medical vision-language models that calibrates logits dynamically using visual guidance to improve interpretability, visual grounding, and clinically coherent explanations. It aims to reduce visual hallucination, where generated text is not grounded in the given image, a key barrier to clinical deployment.

entry.title: Information Theory of Random Composition Trees

author.name: Doron Sivan, Weishun Zhong, Tankut Can, Mikhail Katkov, Misha Tsodyks

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes random composition trees, a stochastic model in which texts are recursively split into coherent chunks, showing that tree entropy grows linearly with root size and deriving an analytical entropy rate as a function of branching factor. The model connects to observed entropy-rate regularities across text types. It provides a formal foundation for hierarchical structure in language.

entry.title: Decision4Rec: A Jev-Inspired Framework of Decision Models on Knowledge and Active Graphs for Multi-Agent Recommender Systems

author.name: Marco Polignano, Het Darshan Mehta, Pasquale Lops, Ernesto William De Luca, Giovanni Semeraro

entry.summary: Decision4Rec is an open, modular framework that applies decision models (LLMs returning option probabilities rather than text) to recommendation, using knowledge graphs to serialize scenarios as typed statements and a multi-agent pool with a residual ranker. A decision model trained once on real choices from three scenarios fuses with the ranker score, and the interface is model-agnostic. It bridges the emerging decision-model paradigm with recommender systems.

entry.title: CodecMotion-OAD: Efficient Online Action Detection with Compressed-Domain Motion

author.name: Zepeng Sun, Naichuan Zheng, Hailun Xia, Junjie Wu

entry.summary: CodecMotion-OAD replaces costly optical flow with motion vectors available directly from video decoders for online action detection, retaining existing temporal detector architectures. A two-stage training first aligns MV features with a pretrained flow-feature interface. The paper quantifies the flow-versus-MV gap, showing it shrinks from 11.2 to 3.7 mAP points after RGB fusion on THUMOS'14.

entry.title: SuperClip Pyramid for Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Sanghyeok Lee, Juyeon Ko, Joonmyung Choi, Jongha Kim, Dohwan Ko, Ji Soo Lee, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: SCVTG tackles video temporal grounding (moment retrieval and highlight detection) with a multi-scale temporal hierarchy that groups adjacent clips into semantically coherent segments, forming a SuperClip pyramid. This addresses limitations of single-scale feature maps and uniform downsampling in DETR-style or temporal-pyramid baselines, better capturing semantic boundaries and variable-length events.

entry.title: OmniVLoc: Topo-metric Visual Localization for Omnidirectional Cameras

author.name: Zhuo Yu, Shuyang Zhang, Huihua Zhu, Wenjia Ouyang, Zuo Zuo, Jianhao Jiao, Yilong Zhu, Xiaopin Zhong, Zongze Wu

entry.summary: OmniVLoc is a surround-view visual localization system combining global place recognition and monocular depth estimation in a topo-metric framework. It solves a scale-aware pose graph with spherical bundle adjustment to remain robust to scene and illumination changes.

entry.title: Manifold Prior Guided Deep Unfolding for Hyperspectral Image Reconstruction

author.name: Shuqi Liu, Yingkai Zhang, Lin Gu, Tao Zhang, Ying Fu

entry.summary: The paper improves deep unfolding for hyperspectral image reconstruction with a two-stage manifold learning strategy that yields an adaptive data-consistency projection and a denoiser capturing global spatial-spectral dependencies. It targets the mismatch between fixed gradient steps and spectral content adaptivity in existing unfolding methods. This is a computational imaging contribution with moderate novelty.

entry.title: In PRAISE of Attributes: Grounding Retrieval Geometry with Query-Conditioned Subspaces for Person Re-Identification

author.name: Rajarshi Bhattacharya, Aryan Shukla, Shakeeb Murtaza, Christian Desrosiers, Jose Dolz, Maguelonne Heritier, Eric Granger

entry.summary: PRAISE improves vision-language person re-identification by grounding attribute-prompt similarities in query-conditioned subspaces, addressing bias and poor calibration of templated attribute prompts for both image-to-image and text-to-image retrieval. It provides fine-grained matching cues while avoiding unreliable direct attribute scoring. A focused ReID method paper.

entry.title: GAMF-Net: Grouped Availability-Aware Multimodal Fusion for Smartphone Skin Lesion Classification

author.name: Yue Zhuo, Jingjia Yan, Fangyu Liu, Lingjun Liu, Zongjun Chen, Zhisheng Luo, Zhonghua Xie

entry.summary: GAMF-Net fuses smartphone clinical images with structured clinical variables for skin lesion classification in resource-constrained settings. It groups ten clinical variables into semantic categories, encodes field-level availability masks to handle missing and imputed data, and guards against clinical information interfering with visual evidence.

entry.title: Learning from Automatic 3D Gaussian Splatting Edits for Online Bayesian Scene Change Detection

author.name: Changrui Zhu, Simon Julier

entry.summary: The paper learns scene-specific evidence models for online change detection by generating labeled training views from automatic edits of a reference 3D Gaussian Splatting model, removing the need for manual annotations. At test time, generalized Bayesian evidence fusion updates change beliefs as new images arrive, with learned priors and response statistics.

entry.title: XoNav: An Exoskeleton as a Personalized Haptic Interface for Assisted Navigation

author.name: Debadrata Sarkar, Soumen Sen, Aman Arora

entry.summary: XoNav is a four-actuator hip exoskeleton that renders navigation cues, advance, braking, and steering, directly at the hip joints instead of via audio or vibrotactile signals requiring translation. A bilateral LSTM gait-state classifier using thigh IMUs coordinates cues with the wearer gait, generalizing to unseen users with 95-98 percent recall. This is a well-executed assistive robotics and wearable interface contribution with accessibility implications for blind and low-vision users.

entry.title: Gaussian Approximation of Besov Functions for Logistic Classification on Manifolds

author.name: Guanhang Lei, Lei Shi, Xiaoming Yuan

entry.summary: The paper derives fast oracle inequalities for Gaussian kernel regularized logistic classification on compact smooth manifolds, without assuming a bounded Bayes function, via a Bernstein-type inequality with predictor-norm-dependent constants. It also constructs Gaussian approximants exploiting intrinsic dimension and target regularity without saturation using a uniform Sobolev-type result.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Block Selection for Sparse Variational Gaussian Processes

author.name: Matteo Hoxha

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether selecting block structures that tighten the variational objective improves test RMSE and NLL for sparse variational Gaussian processes with block-diagonal scaling matrices, at a fixed inducing-point budget. It empirically probes recent theoretical improvements to the SVGP framework.

entry.title: Do Neural Models Prefer Their Submodels?

author.name: Alvaro Ribot, Yulia Alexandr, Anna Seigal

entry.summary: This work develops a geometric framework to determine whether loss minimizers of neural networks lie within natural submodels, such as subnetworks with inactive neurons or lower-rank self-attention models. It proves that for shallow MLPs, subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are never preferred, and gives conditions for deep MLPs and lightning self-attention.

entry.title: 1000 Years of AI Safety

author.name: Simon Steshin

entry.summary: The author presents a quantitative model of AI pauses estimating how much additional AI safety research would be produced if frontier labs redirected GPUs and researchers to safety work, finding a three-year pause could yield roughly 1000 times the safety research done in 2025 and a nine-year pause 100,000 times. The model also analyzes verification bottlenecks, estimating that checking nine years of autonomous AI research output could require hundreds of thousands to millions of verifiers depending on protocol safety.

entry.title: Language Guidance for Supervised Vision Training: An Empirical Study of Generalization

author.name: Shruthi Gowda, Nikita Jain, Elahe Arani, Bahram Zonooz

entry.summary: An empirical study of whether pretrained language models can serve as lightweight auxiliary supervision for vision training without paired image-text data, prompt engineering, or contrastive objectives, by enriching one-hot labels with semantic structure from language. It evaluates effects on distribution shift, spurious correlations, texture bias, adversarial perturbation, and forgetting.

entry.title: Which Answers Agree? Evaluating Self-Consistency from Incomplete Logs

author.name: Zhengtao Gui, Zexi Chen, Weining Shen

entry.summary: This paper derives sharp bounds on self-consistency voting accuracy using only correctness labels plus incomplete agreement information, employing stochastic majorization and abstention counts, and introduces Plurality-U, a dynamic program that exactly averages voting accuracy when answer-category counts are available. It also bounds accuracy changes across voting budgets sharing a response pool. This enables rigorous evaluation of self-consistency when full voting logs are unavailable.

entry.title: CheXFuse: Guided Differential Joint Attention Fusion for Robust Multimodal Chest X-Ray Classification in Data-Scarce Medical Settings

author.name: Muntaqim Ahmed Raju, Priyanka Siddappa, Md Shifat Haider Al Amin, Ruizhe Ma, Md Ripon Ahammed

entry.summary: CheXFuse addresses fusing modalities of unequal predictive strength in multimodal learning using Guided Differential Joint Attention, which emphasizes informative tokens and suppresses weak attention responses for chest X-ray image-text classification. It targets data-scarce medical settings where naive cross-modal fusion can degrade below the strongest unimodal baseline.

entry.title: Regime-Aware Interpretable Ranking for Sector Rotation

author.name: Kelvin J. L. Koa, Ziling Liu, Xinyang Li, Shuowei Feng, Ruoyu Liang, Mathieu Giroux, Eugene Y. Wen, Xuan Yao, Ke-Wei Huang, Hugo Lamarre

entry.summary: RegimeRank is an interpretable sector-ranking model for benchmark-relative portfolio management that ranks sectors by expected forward risk-adjusted active performance. It uses expert-defined temporal signal characteristics, conditions on learned macroeconomic regimes, and captures inter-sector dependencies. The formulation targets economically interpretable outputs suited to real portfolio decisions.

entry.title: Inferring continuous cognitive traits from limited neuroimaging data using pairwise convolutional neural networks

author.name: Marjan Rashidi, Robert Bain, Craig Stark, Jeffrey Krichmar, Mary Hegarty, Elizabeth Chrastil

entry.summary: Introduces a pairwise convolutional ranking framework that predicts cognitive trait differences from comparative rather than absolute judgments of whole-brain MRI, achieving strong prediction of spatial-ability performance even with only 108 subjects. It outperforms traditional predefined-metric linear brain-behavior analyses in small-sample regimes.

entry.title: EASformer: Environment-Action-State Alignment for Industrial Generative Ranking

author.name: Bohao Li, Dinglun Cao, Pengcheng Huang, Yingda Tang, Zhiting Zhao, Yi Cao, Jilei Fu, Miao Yan, Tianying Liu, Heng Chang, Bowen Du

entry.summary: Introduces EASformer, a generative-ranking architecture that aligns asymmetric sequence and non-sequence feature representations (environment-action-state semantics) in tokenized Transformer backbones for industrial recommendation. It addresses query-key interaction degradation caused by mixing context-laden historical representations with candidate-side features lacking action semantics.

entry.title: Interruption-Aware Recurrent Reinforcement Learning for UAS Navigation Under Temporary Overrides

author.name: Christopher Conrad, Deepak Panda, Weisi Guo, Antonios Tsourdos

entry.summary: This paper studies how recurrent RL navigation policies for uncrewed aircraft systems behave when temporarily overridden by remote pilots, detect-and-avoid systems, or runtime assurance mechanisms under partial observability. It fills a gap in understanding policy recovery and safety-efficiency trade-offs when learned control is interrupted mid-flight.

entry.title: BR-MoE: Budgeted Semantic Release for Privacy-Preserving Traffic Analytics

author.name: Abdolazim Rezaei

entry.summary: BR-MoE extends a prior RL and mixture-of-experts framework for privacy-preserving traffic-camera analytics by introducing budgeted semantic release: scene experts map video chunks to a bounded semantic schema while an RL controller decides which summaries to release and how to spend a fixed privacy budget across repeated releases.

entry.title: Less is More: Concise Retrieval and Critic-based Re-ranking for Composed Image Retrieval

author.name: Yuqian Zheng, Hyoju Ahn, Hyeongjin Ahn, Eunil Park

entry.summary: This training-free two-stage framework for zero-shot composed image retrieval generates concise target-oriented captions that keep only the most discriminative modification semantics, then applies critic-based re-ranking. It reduces semantic noise from verbose LLM-generated captions used in prior approaches. The result is better retrieval without additional training.

entry.title: TRCM: Topology-Aware Route-Consistency Modeling for Robust Neural Vehicle Routing

author.name: Peiheng Jian, Zhenwei Wang, Tiehua Zhang, Lei Zhang, Zhishu Shen, Ruibin Bai, Zhijun Ding

entry.summary: TRCM explicitly models route-level customer co-assignment in neural solvers for the capacitated vehicle routing problem, predicting pairwise same-route probabilities from existing node representations and injecting them as a consistency signal into construction decisions. This makes route organization explicit rather than implicit in autoregressive solvers. It improves robustness of neural combinatorial optimization for CVRP.

entry.title: GLOW: General Linear Models Optimized with Ward's Method

author.name: Matt Higger

entry.summary: GLOW builds a hierarchy of nested brain regions by greedily minimizing GLM error, provably a special case of Ward's clustering, for neuroimaging analysis. This bridges region-based and voxel-based analysis, avoiding effects being diluted or split by fixed atlases while retaining statistical control via maximum-statistic correction. It addresses a well-known limitation of standard neuroimaging pipelines.

entry.title: Torch-DPhys: A Torch-Native, MOOSE-Compatible Framework for Differentiable Physics Simulation and Hybrid Machine Learning Integration

author.name: Akzhol Almukhametov, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Torch-DPhys is a PyTorch-native differentiable physics framework implementing thermal-hydraulic modeling concepts from MOOSE with a preliminary continuum mechanics extension. It supports CPU/GPU execution, kernel compilation, sparse direct solves, and sensitivities via autodiff or discrete adjoints, verified against analytical solutions and reference codes. The framework enables hybrid physics-ML workflows in nuclear/engineering simulation.

entry.title: From Score to Diagnosis: Search-Independent Post-Diagnosis for Symbolic Regression

author.name: Qian Li, Yuxiao Hu, Juncheng Liu, Yanhao Jia, Yuntian Chen

entry.summary: PostDiag provides a search-independent feedback mechanism for symbolic regression, using Patch-wise Feature Profiling to diagnose why a candidate expression skeleton fails and how to revise it, decoupled from any particular solver's search process. The shared diagnostic can improve diverse SR solvers that otherwise rely only on low-information scalar fitness.

entry.title: Paired-Outcome Learning for Selective Spacecraft Attitude Capture under Torque Limits

author.name: Donghe Chen, Jia Deng, Zehao Jia, Lin Cheng, Shengping Gong

entry.summary: This paper frames torque-limited spacecraft attitude capture as a baseline-relative learning problem, combining interpretable continuation policies, separate prediction of task failure and tracking gains, and context-dependent rejection that falls back to the unchanged baseline controller. Paired simulations with shared plant parameters provide labels, validated in Basilisk experiments.

entry.title: Process-Aware Event Log Augmentation for Process Prediction under Labeled Data Scarcity

author.name: Sjoerd van Straten, Alessandro Padella, Marwan Hassani

entry.summary: SiamSA-PPM is a self-supervised framework for predictive process monitoring combining Siamese learning with statistically grounded data augmentation that respects control-flow semantics. It generates realistic trace variants to learn generalizable prefix representations without labels, evaluated on real-world event logs with exhaustive hyperparameter tuning.

entry.title: Multifidelity Monte Carlo Estimator for High-Dimensional Quantities of Interest

author.name: Zhibo Dai, Hamdi A. Tchelepi, Daniel M. Tartakovsky

entry.summary: The paper extends multifidelity Monte Carlo estimation to vector-valued quantities of interest by replacing scalar control-variate coefficients with matrices, deriving closed-form optimal full-matrix coefficients and an effective-correlation summary of variance reduction. Nested block-diagonal, diagonal, and scalar coefficient classes trade variance reduction against cost.

entry.title: Simulating Infant Senses with Age-Tuned Networks

author.name: Somesh Mohapatra

entry.summary: The paper consolidates cross-sense measurements of infant sensory development over the first two years and encodes each sense's immaturity as fixed age-indexed input filters, with small prediction networks trained behind them. The filters reproduce maturation ordering by construction while networks reveal effects like early-stage under-extraction of visual information. It offers an inspectable simulation connecting developmental psychology and neural network modeling.

entry.title: Structured Relevance Determination and Channel Additive Gaussian Processes for Image Data

author.name: Harald Ro{\ss}els, Ludovico Scarton

entry.summary: The paper proposes RBF kernels for Gaussian processes on images with structured hyperparameter sharing, tying lengthscales across adjacent pixel groups and within color channels to reduce overfitting and improve uncertainty calibration in low-data regimes. It also introduces channel-additive Gaussian processes. This addresses a known scalability limitation of anisotropic GP kernels.

entry.title: CVTA: Cross-Variable Temporal Attention for Multivariate Irregular Time Series Prediction

author.name: Ankitkumar Joshi, Milos Hauskrecht

entry.summary: CVTA is a continuous-time forecasting framework for irregularly sampled multivariate time series that uses Variable-Conditioned Embeddings to project heterogeneous variables into variable-specific latent spaces and temporal attention to capture cross-variable dependencies. It targets healthcare, climate, and monitoring domains where asynchronous observations complicate prediction. The method emphasizes a compact, interpretable state.

entry.title: Stochastic Tracking of Drifting Affine Fixed Points

author.name: Sajad Khodadadian

entry.summary: This work analyzes linear stochastic approximation with time-varying affine operators and correlated noise, establishing upper and matching lower bounds for constant-stepsize tracking of drifting fixed points. It identifies conditions under which a suitably chosen constant stepsize is optimal. The results extend finite-time SA theory beyond the standard fixed-operator assumption.

entry.title: An Analysis of Semantic and Spatio-Temporal Co-evolution for Edge Classification on Dynamic Text-Attributed Graphs

author.name: Tyler Bonnet, Marek Rei

entry.summary: The authors investigate letting text representations co-evolve with dynamic graph topology rather than freezing pretrained LM embeddings, using a unified text-graph alignment framework with a lightweight Transformer adapter updated by spatio-temporal gradients. Evaluated on dynamic edge classification for text-attributed web graphs such as review networks and forums. The work quantifies the benefit of jointly adapting semantics and structure.

entry.title: Topological Sheaves of Irreducibility: A Theoretical Framework for Multi-Agent Task Obstructions

author.name: Steven Motta, Davide Mambelli, Alessandro Rozza

entry.summary: This paper introduces Topological Sheaves of Irreducibility, a sheaf-theoretic framework that separates task-level compatibility obstructions from system capability in multi-agent systems. Tasks are represented via an interaction complex and capacity sheaf, with cohomology classes providing structural signatures and registered interventions testing capability; cochain realization is solvable exactly when the represented cohomology class vanishes. It offers a formal language for why identical agents and communication budgets can still differ in achievable joint interaction.

entry.title: Measuring the Influence of Modality-Specific Node Representations on Graphs

author.name: Xu Wang, Xunkai Li, Yinlin Zhu, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: The paper defines and studies influence measurement for modality-specific node representations (text and image) on multimodal attributed graphs, scoring candidates by replacement-based retraining probes. This reveals which modality inputs a trained graph predictor relies on and how predictor design modulates that reliance, relevant to recommendation and multimedia analysis.

entry.title: Certified neural approximations for parabolic obstacle problems

author.name: Davood Damircheli

entry.summary: The paper derives guaranteed error bounds for neural network approximations of parabolic obstacle problems, formulated in first-order state-flux-multiplier form, bounding flux and energy errors by constitutive residual, initial mismatch, complementarity defect, and PDE residual. It extends an existing a posteriori majorant technique for the heat operator to general coefficients and free multipliers.

entry.title: Can AI agents make law? Evaluating AI legal relevance and creativity

author.name: Benjamin Ricaud, Artem Galushko

entry.summary: The authors run simulated constitutional assemblies in which a single LLM plays multiple debating personas to draft a hypothetical constitution for a community of AI agents, then analyze the legal relevance and creativity of the outputs. Assemblies converge on a stable floor of provisions with varied proposals around it, including AI-specific provisions lacking human-law equivalents. The work probes the boundaries of AI legal creativity and multi-persona deliberation.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Interpolation for Inverse Problems

author.name: Pourya Shamsolmoali, Masoumeh Zareapoor

entry.summary: The authors propose GAIN, a variational autoencoder-based framework that replaces the linear or bilinear interpolation used in Spatial Transformer Networks with geometry-aware interpolation for image restoration inverse problems. The method aims to better capture geometric structure of image data and improve gradient propagation stability during optimization.

entry.title: LowNet: Looped Wavelet Neural Networks with 24 Learnable Parameters for Solving Poisson Equations

author.name: Yuanhao Gong

entry.summary: The paper proposes a wavelet-inspired neural Poisson solver with only 24 trainable scalars arranged in four 5x5 kernels, positioned between traditional iterative solvers (high certainty but CFL-limited iterations) and data-driven deep methods (efficient but data-hungry). The extreme compactness enables deployment in constrained settings.

entry.title: Dialogue Generation for Conversational Recommendation Using User Search Interactions and Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Minsung Hwang, Donggyu Yoon, Gowoon Hwang, Kwanghee Jang, Joyce Jiyoung Whang

entry.summary: SearCl automatically generates conversational recommendation dialogues from real user search and click behaviors, using a probabilistic state machine for dialogue flow, LLM agents as seeker and recommender, and knowledge graphs built from item metadata. This avoids costly manual annotation of conversational recommendation datasets.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Gated SHAP-Dirichlet Refinement for MRI-Based Depression Classification

author.name: Phuc Truong Loc Nguyen, Nguyen Truong Toan To, Truong Thanh Hung Nguyen, Hoang-Loc Cao, Hung Cao

entry.summary: The authors propose a post-hoc reliability layer for MRI-based major depressive disorder classification that retrieves similar labeled SHAP explanations, builds Dirichlet class evidence, and selectively refines uncertain predictions while deferring unreliable cases for expert review. Evaluated on 504 SRPBS subjects across five classifiers with repeated nested cross-validation, refinement improved accuracy consistently for several models.

entry.title: LaMER: Language-Conditioned Multi-Expert Routing for Weakly Supervised Referring Expression Comprehension

author.name: Yu Yu Chang, Tzu-Hsuan Weng, Youssef Mohamed Amin, Mohaned Ahmed Elsayed, Hung-Hsuan Chen, Min-Te Sun, Sherine Shawky

entry.summary: LaMER is a weakly supervised framework for referring expression comprehension that dynamically routes among four frozen pretrained visual encoders, each contributing complementary properties such as semantic alignment, texture, and boundary awareness. A language-conditioned aggregation addresses the visual-linguistic semantic gap when only image-level supervision is available.

entry.title: SafeWall: A Risk-Aware Job Walltime Recommendation for HPC Scheduling

author.name: Kanglin Xu, Michael Papka, Zhiling Lan

entry.summary: SafeWall is a recommendation method for HPC job walltimes that explicitly accounts for the asymmetric risk of underestimation, which causes premature job termination. It adjusts learned walltime predictions with a nonnegative risk adjustment rather than optimizing raw accuracy. This addresses systematic user overestimation behavior in production HPC schedulers.

entry.title: Best of Both Worlds: Fine-Tuned Small Models Complement LLMs for Cost and Performance Benefits

author.name: Shivam Mathur, Sri Harish Popuri, Priya Krishnan Sundararajan, Kevin Horecka, Michael Mugo

entry.summary: Compares a fine-tuned RoBERTa classifier against GPT-3.5 for 16-class survey text classification, measuring performance, cost, and latency. Finds large efficiency gaps (12 minutes vs 6 hours for 10,000 records) and explores prompting strategies like batch prompting for the LLM.

entry.title: BanglaBBQ: A Bias Benchmark for Question Answering in the Bangladeshi Context

author.name: Sumit Anthony Gomes, Yasin Rahman, Taeeba Tasnia, Faiza Nooren Suhita

entry.summary: BanglaBBQ adapts the BBQ bias benchmark to the Bangladeshi context in both Bangla and English, classifying original templates as directly translated, context-modified, or removed, and adding five newly authored categories reflecting Bangladeshi stereotypes such as marital status, regional origin, and educational background. The result retains 140 templates across six original categories plus new ones. It enables bias evaluation that reflects local social realities rather than Western stereotype taxonomies.

entry.title: Reranking Answers of Large Language Models with Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Mikhail Salnikov, Hai Le, Olga Tsymboi, Ivan Lazichny, Dmitrii Iarosh, Egor Cheremiskin, Andrey Savchenko, Dmitry Simakov, Alexander Panchenko

entry.summary: The paper proposes extracting query-related subgraphs from Wikidata via shortest paths between LLM-inferred candidate entities, then using subgraph-derived features with reranking models to select the most probable answers from LLM candidate lists. This grounds LLM question answering in structured knowledge without processing the full graph.

entry.title: Flattening Fantasies: Analyzing Stereotypes in Pornographic Discourse

author.name: Sarmad Chandio, Osama Khalid, Sharaf Zia, Ethan Kutlu

entry.summary: Presents a large-scale computational sociolinguistic analysis of 5.4 million video titles from a major pornography platform, quantifying how nationalities, ethnic groups, and gender identities are depicted. The study identifies persistent ethnic stereotypes, colonial power dynamics, religious fetishization, and American pornography acting as a de facto industry norm.

entry.title: LVMem: Image-Augmented Memory for Long-Horizon Question Answering

author.name: Victoria Khoruzhaya, Maksim Kalmykov, Tuong Do Minh, Tatiana Zemskova, Yixin Zhu, Dmitry Yudin

entry.summary: LVMem extends view-based memory for embodied agents by linking stored textual descriptions back to original image paths, enabling long-horizon spatio-temporal question answering over persistent scene memory. It improves annotation informativeness via non-uniform sampling and supports verification against visual content. The work targets robotic settings requiring reasoning over extended observation histories.

entry.title: CILA: Confusion-based Instance-wise Logit Adjustment for Long-Tailed Recognition

author.name: Jiyoung Lim, Jee-Hyong Lee

entry.summary: CILA adapts logit adjustment for class-imbalanced learning at the instance level, using confusion between target and confusing non-target classes to restore informative gradients that class-frequency-based adjustments suppress. A complementary method is also proposed.

entry.title: S$^3$E-Det: A Strict Spatial-Spectral Equivariant Detector for Multispectral Object Detection

author.name: Peng Zhang, Tingfa Xu, Jinrui Sui, Yuyang Tian, Jianan Li

entry.summary: S3E-Det couples ordered spectral modeling with transformation-consistent prediction for multispectral object detection, imposing local order constraints on spectral features and regulating geometric responses under rotation. It addresses unified spectral fusion across pyramid levels and geometric equivariance. A technical but specialized detection contribution.

entry.title: AGGR-Mamba: Mamba-based Network with Attention-Guided Gated Residual Refinement for Undersampled MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Yue Zhuo, Wenbin Deng, Lingjun Liu, Xuhang Chen, Zhonghua Xie

entry.summary: AGGR-Mamba applies a Mamba-based backbone to undersampled brain MRI reconstruction, adding a lightweight attention-guided gated residual refinement stage that corrects aliasing artifacts and recovers high-frequency details. It aims to reduce scan time while improving reconstruction quality.

entry.title: WildMAE: Structure-Aware Masked Autoencoding for Wildlife Image Reconstruction

author.name: Yicheng Zhang, Yujie Jin, Ke Zhang, Jiaxin Wu

entry.summary: WildMAE adapts masked autoencoders to camera-trap wildlife imagery via a decoder-side extension combining a zero-gated convolutional residual path for neighborhood priors and gated cross-attention from masked to visible positions, plus a staged training recipe introducing normalized pixels and Sobel-edge targets. It targets label-free modeling under heavy appearance, illumination, and clutter variation.

entry.title: Towards Interaction State Recognition in Sensorized Gecko-Inspired Adhesive Interfaces for Orbital Servicing

author.name: Eduart Abdullahu, Francesco Grella, Carol Martinez

entry.summary: This paper presents a real-time interaction-awareness framework for gecko-inspired dry adhesive interfaces used in on-orbit satellite servicing, classifying five contact states across the adhesion lifecycle using embedded capacitive sensing. This closes the loop on adhesive capture systems that currently operate open-loop against non-cooperative targets. It is a focused hardware-integration contribution to a specialized space robotics application.

entry.title: Distributed Platoon Control for Safe and Smooth Crossing at an Unsignalized Intersection-Part I: Stability Analysis

author.name: Bin-Bin Hu, Shuwei Pei, Saeed Ahmed, Bayu Jayawardhana

entry.summary: The paper proposes a distributed platoon controller guaranteeing safe, smooth multi-vehicle crossing at unsignalized intersections, analyzed on a closed-path setting that captures coupling between intersection control and platoon convergence. It establishes local exponential convergence of the switched closed-loop system induced by repeated vehicle switching.

entry.title: Learned Control Variates for Rare Grid-Outage Estimation at Electric Vehicle Charging Stations

author.name: Sulyman Iyanda, Mansur Arief

entry.summary: The paper builds a control variate from a learned outage classifier trained on cheap features such as temperature and load forecasts, to reduce the number of expensive grid-simulator Monte Carlo runs needed to estimate rare EV-charging-induced feeder overload probabilities. This helps planners design for high-reliability cascading-outage scenarios.

entry.title: When Does Feedback Help? Auditing Learned Voltage-Clamp Experimental Design

author.name: Rayan Nyaupane, Abhiram Bhupatiraju

entry.summary: Audits learned controllers for synthetic voltage-clamp experimental design tasks, finding that recurrent policies repeat one fixed protocol across all rollouts, ignore current-masking interventions, and merely tie a correctly specified Bayesian controller. The study shows that apparent use of feedback can reflect a fitted threshold rather than genuine adaptive experimental design.

entry.title: Beyond Trajectory Statistics: Community-Consistent Human Mobility Generation via Evolving User-Location Graphs

author.name: Bo Liu, Tong Li, Jiapeng Zhang, Zhu Xiao, Zhuo Tang, Kenli Li

entry.summary: MOTION formulates human mobility generation as dynamic user-location graph generation to preserve evolving community structures, going beyond individual trajectory statistics. It uses a multi-agent framework to generate community-consistent synthetic mobility data for web-based location services and urban applications.

entry.title: Assessing Representation Semantics Under Language Pretraining in Fine-Grained Classification

author.name: Md Raisul Kibria, S\'ebastien Lafond

entry.summary: The paper proposes an explainability-driven framework comparing vision encoders trained with classification-only versus caption-generation supervision on CUB-200, using a controlled two-stage protocol where both are optimized for the same task. Saliency maps via attention rollout and gradient-weighted rollout are evaluated with five metrics to reveal structural differences invisible to downstream accuracy.

entry.title: Beyond a Single Sentiment Score: Topical and Affective Dimensions of Emoji Meaning on Twitter

author.name: Rohan James, Ioannis Christofilogiannis, Yuuv Jauhari, Shreya Shah, Gauri Pethkar

entry.summary: Using 16,575 English tweets and a stability-delta metric based on embedding clustering, the paper shows that emojis used in tightly clustered topical contexts exhibit more polarized crowd-sourced sentiment, contradicting the view of emoji meaning as a single affect score. Findings are validated against two independent sentiment/emotion lexicons with moderate correlations. It is a careful empirical study of emoji semantics with implications for affective NLP.

entry.title: Pack and Extract: An Effective Graph-Based Approach for Feature Selection

author.name: Faisal N. Abu-Khzam, Joseph R. Barr, Cynthia Chaaya, Nadim Obeid, Peter Shaw

entry.summary: The paper improves combinatorial feature selection based on the Independent Dominating Set model by favoring diverse features and generalizing to a node-packing formulation, targeting high-dimensional molecular biology datasets with thousands of correlated features. This reduces reliance on computationally expensive greedy approaches.

entry.title: Margin Certificates for Voting Classifiers under Mixing Dependence

author.name: Adria Binte Habib, Ibne Farabi Shihab

entry.summary: The paper derives explicit uniform voting-margin generalization certificates for ensemble classifiers trained on stationary beta-mixing (dependent) data, combining independent-block Rademacher theory with clipped margin loss. It includes a black-box transfer theorem showing i.i.d. guarantees remain valid on regularly spaced subsequences. The work makes dependence assumptions and failure budgets explicit rather than hiding them in effective-sample-size heuristics.

entry.title: EasyResearch: Honest Regression, Forecasting and Signal Classification for Researchers Who Do Not Program

author.name: Ahmad B. A. Hassanat, Ghada A. Altarawneh

entry.summary: EasyResearch provides open-source, no-code tools for regression, time-series forecasting, and signal classification with methodologically sound defaults such as training-only learning, fixed seeds, and held-out final evaluation. It extends prior EasyClassifier work to more task types plus a Windows desktop app. It matters because defaulting to honest evaluation reduces common statistical errors in applied non-ML research.

entry.title: Consistent LLM Call Handling Across Java Frameworks: A Reference Implementation and Benchmark

author.name: Oleksandr Klymenko

entry.summary: The paper defines a six-clause reliability contract for how Java LLM integration frameworks should handle failing providers (retries, backoff, truncated responses, failure metrics) and benchmarks Spring AI 2.0.1 and LangChain4j 1.21.0 against it using a scripted OpenAI-compatible provider across fifteen failure scenarios. Spring AI passes substantially more cases than LangChain4j. It provides a practical reliability benchmark for the growing LLM application infrastructure ecosystem.

entry.title: Conditional Average Treatment Effect Distillation for Hypothetical State-Intervention Targeting Under Budget Constraints

author.name: Vasundhara Acharya, B\"ulent Yener

entry.summary: The paper studies budget-constrained public-health targeting via causal distillation, where Causal Forest and Bayesian Causal Forest teachers estimate conditional average treatment effects that are distilled into interpretable policies. It handles observational data without a logged historical policy, applied to obesity, glucose, and smoking states with capacity capped at 70%. Focused methodological contribution at the causal-ML and policy interface.

entry.title: MT-CC: Multi-Group Temperature Scaling for Asymmetric Calibration Behavior in Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Sungjun Yun, Yonghee Choi, Dong-Jun Han

entry.summary: This paper identifies asymmetric calibration behavior in class-incremental learning, where confidence changes do not track accuracy changes across class groups, and proposes MT-CC, a post-hoc multi-group temperature scaling framework. It extends rarely-explored static calibration techniques to continual learning settings with evolving distributions. Calibration matters for trustworthy deployment of continually adapting models.

entry.title: Scenario Generalization and Sector Transfer in Real Surface Irrigation Surrogate Modelling with Tabular Models

author.name: Alessandro Cagiano, M. Aybars Seyhan, Fabiola Gangi, Matteo Zignani, Daniele Masseroni

entry.summary: The paper evaluates tabular surrogates (gradient-boosted trees, neural tabular models, AutoML, tabular foundation models) for replacing expensive shallow-water-equation simulations in surface irrigation planning, predicting maximum water height from drone-derived morphology and terrain descriptors. It distinguishes same-sector generalization to unseen scenarios from sector-out transfer, assessing real deployment feasibility. This enables cheap screening of many operating conditions in agricultural water management.

entry.title: GeoSplit: Selective Edge--Server Map Acquisition for Cross-User Travel-Mode Recognition

author.name: Zepu Wang (Xuegang), Luyao Niu (Xuegang), Ruolin Li (Xuegang), Jeff (Xuegang), Ban

entry.summary: This paper introduces GeoSplit, an edge-server framework for travel-mode recognition that decouples map-evidence utility, training-time distillation, and runtime selective acquisition of geospatial context. Experiments on GeoLife with 10% labels show aligned full-map context boosts macro-F1 for unseen users from 0.7154 to 0.7864, while an entropy-gated query interface achieves comparable performance (0.7729) while querying only 39.5% of trajectories, reducing communication overhead. The work is significant for treating communication decisions as a first-class part of the prediction pipeline in networked mobile sensing.

entry.title: EAGLE: Entropy-Aware Geometric Learning Enhancer for Partially Polygon-Supervised Object Localization

author.name: Naveen Stewart

entry.summary: EAGLE targets object localization under partial polygon supervision, addressing the counterintuitive problem that segmentation losses can degrade box localization for low shape-complexity classes. An entropy-aware mechanism modulates the use of geometric supervision to improve high-IoU localization without full mask annotation costs.

entry.title: lepidoptera: A Domain-Agnostic Engine for Causal Simulation with Mixed Variable Types, Vine Copula Dependence, and Individual-Level Counterfactual Propagation

author.name: Danilo Augusto Sarti

entry.summary: lepidoptera is an open-source R and Python package for simulating data from structural causal models with mixed variable types, featuring a typed mechanism library covering all combinations of continuous, categorical, and ordinal variables, plus vine copula dependence modeling and individual-level counterfactual propagation. It aims to make causal simulation accessible without users implementing type-specific sampling themselves.

entry.title: HullProbe: Measuring Interventional Part Reliance in Maritime Vessel Classifiers

author.name: Faisal Mohammad, Mohamed Younis

entry.summary: HullProbe measures whether vessel classifiers rely on distinctive superstructure versus generic hull features by performing controlled part swaps and reading decision sensitivity, going beyond worst-group accuracy as a proxy. The approach targets compositional objects where bias detection matters for surveillance and monitoring applications.

entry.title: Motor compound fault diagnosis using an attention-based cross-talk architecture

author.name: Wonjun Yi, Wonho Jung, Junho Kim, Rismaya Kumar Mishra, Yong-Hwa Park

entry.summary: Applies a multi-task learning architecture with attention-based cross-talk instead of a shared trunk to classify multiple simultaneous motor fault components and their severities from vibration signals. Positioned within the broader trend of physical AI and condition monitoring for industrial machinery.

entry.title: Local data augmentation for imbalanced binary classification

author.name: Harold Gu{\'e}neau (SAMM), Alain Celisse (LPP, MODAL), Pascal Delange

entry.summary: This paper analyzes rebalancing strategies for imbalanced binary classification, proving that merely changing class proportions cannot improve performance while a local data augmentation scheme can. The two-step procedure subsamples anchor points and augments locally around them. Results include theoretical characterization and empirical validation for maximizing recall while limiting false detections.

entry.title: Ben-Misandry: A Bengali Dataset and Late-Fusion Transformer Framework for Detecting Anti-Male Gender Hate

author.name: Md Mehedi Hasan Nipu, Chinmoy Mitra, Tarannum Ahmed Nowshin, Israt Moyeen Noumi

entry.summary: The authors introduce Ben-Misandry, the first Bengali dataset for detecting anti-male gender-based hate speech, with 5,000 comments across six taxonomy classes including a novel category for mocking male emotional vulnerability. The corpus is taxonomy-controlled synthetic data generated with GPT-4.1 and spot-checked by human reviewers on a small sample. It addresses a genuine gap in moderation research for Bengali, which has focused almost exclusively on misogyny.

entry.title: Concept Representations in Vector Space: Toward an Interdisciplinary Study of Meaning Variation

author.name: Simon Josef Durstewitz

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues for an interdisciplinary study of concept representations as subjective, latent mental structures that vary across individuals, raising whether people mean the same thing when invoking the same concept. It sketches how such private meaning structures could be modeled empirically in vector spaces.

entry.title: GardenBench: A lightweight, daily evaluation of LLM capabilities

author.name: Benedict Cummins-Mburu, Mariana Garcia Mejia, Oscar Heath, Sabrina Kreyzerman, Ellie Murray, Arusan Surendiran, Rohan Alexander

entry.summary: GardenBench is a benchmark with 11 test suites that runs lightweight LLM queries daily, tracking accuracy, cost, and latency changes over time, including post-deployment model changes and new releases. Results are published on a live dashboard, complementing static benchmarks with longitudinal monitoring.

entry.title: A Cross-Domain Evaluation of Prompting Techniques for Large Language Models

author.name: Kevin Krazius, Tim Schlippe, Paul Libbrecht

entry.summary: This paper presents a controlled comparison of Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, RAG, and automatic prompt optimization (PE2-inspired) using the same LLM across six benchmark datasets spanning arithmetic, logical, and other reasoning domains. By holding the model and settings fixed, it enables direct comparison that prior studies lacked. The results map which prompting techniques pay off in which domains.

entry.title: System X: An LLM Decision Model That Replies from Its Own KV Cache

author.name: Syed Usama Khalid Bukhari, Syed Safwan Khalid, Muhammad Aamir

entry.summary: System X extends an LLM decision model (probability readout over options) with a text-reply mode that continues decoding from the decision call's KV cache, avoiding repeated prompt prefill. Fine-tuning Qwen3-0.6B with LoRA preserves decision accuracy while improving calibration and achieving 98.3% routing accuracy for reply triggering. Cache reuse cuts latency 15-37% on an Apple M4 Pro.

entry.title: What Not to Erase: Saliency-Constrained Augmentation for Low-Resource Handwritten Character Recognition

author.name: Paraskevi Platanou, John Pavlopoulos

entry.summary: This work studies saliency-guided data augmentation for low-resource handwritten character recognition in degraded historical collections, evaluating not just accuracy but whether improved performance comes with stable saliency patterns. The approach constrains augmentation to avoid erasing discriminative regions. It brings an explanation-aware lens to a task where models handle variable, degraded letterforms.

entry.title: Revealing Inter-Channel Modality Discriminability: Channel Selective Interaction Fusion Network for Optical-SAR Object Detection

author.name: Haojie Li, Yuanfei Huang, Lingfei Song, Jia Li, Lizhi Wang

entry.summary: CSIF-Net performs selective channel-level cross-modal fusion for optical-SAR remote sensing object detection, using frequency decomposition and channel discriminability analysis to highlight task-relevant channels and suppress redundant or conflicting features.

entry.title: SGLDet: Spectral-aware Global-Local Dynamic Modeling for Multispectral Aerial Object Detection

author.name: Peng Zhang, Shuaihao Han, Tingfa Xu, Jianan Li

entry.summary: SGLDet targets multispectral aerial object detection by addressing severe foreground-background imbalance and large local variations in scale and orientation through spectral-aware global-local dynamic modeling. It appears alongside a companion paper by the same group (S3E-Det), advancing spectral-spatial fusion for aerial scenes. Contribution is domain-focused engineering.

entry.title: Can a Display Be Used for Rapid LiDAR-Camera Extrinsic Calibration?

author.name: Zuhao Zou, Xiangcheng Hu, Jianhao Jiao, Jin Wu

entry.summary: ScreenCalib performs LiDAR-camera extrinsic calibration using an ordinary programmable display as a calibration target, with AprilTags observed by the camera and the screen surface measured by LiDAR. It handles cross-modal association ambiguities via tag-guided extraction, geometric hypothesis refinement, and scene edges, supporting single-pose and joint multi-pose modes.

entry.title: Determination of the Human-Robot Interaction Workspace for Robot Assisted Head Stabilization Control

author.name: Xinmin Liu, Alexander L. Van Slyke, Destinee Holloman, Ahmad Sakaamini, Rodney D. Wiersma

entry.summary: This study establishes safe and effective motion limits for a 6-DoF robotic head holder integrated with optical tracking, intended to replace invasive stereotactic frames and masks in neuroimaging and radiation therapy. It derives biomechanical skull-cervical spine interaction models to define the human-robot interaction workspace for dynamic head motion compensation. This is a specialized medical robotics contribution addressing patient comfort and workflow in clinical procedures.

entry.title: Annealed correlation and quenched noise sensitivity in biased deep neural networks

author.name: Johan Jonasson

entry.summary: This extends earlier work on noise sensitivity of deep fully connected networks with sign activations by adding independent Gaussian biases, showing quenched noise sensitivity is retained across a broad range of depths. The result clarifies how architectural perturbations affect stability of random deep networks.

entry.title: Pattern Intelligence: Unsupervised, LLM-Interpreted Discovery of Systematic Underpayment and Denial Patterns in Healthcare Revenue Cycle Management

author.name: Harshil Lodhiya, Alex McManus
