entry.summary: Describes a deployed unsupervised system that clusters hospital claims on 130-dimensional adjudication-behavior embeddings to surface systematic payer underpayment and denial patterns, deliberately excluding payer and contract identity which would otherwise dominate cluster geometry. An LLM layer interprets discovered patterns for revenue-cycle teams.

entry.title: Injection of Space Radiation Errors on Low-power NVM using Generative Deep Learning

author.name: Eleonora Giudici, Antonio Miele, Luca Mottola

entry.summary: The authors build an error model for a ferroelectric RAM chip flown on a CubeSat in low Earth orbit, comparing memory snapshots against reference bitmaps to identify radiation-induced bit errors. They observe regular spatial patterns in errors and train a generative deep learning model to synthesize realistic error patterns for testing. This enables hardware-in-the-loop resilience testing for space systems.

entry.title: Visual Task Modeling and Automated Planning for Humanoid Robots in Education of Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder

author.name: Lada Kudl\'a\v{c}kov\'a

entry.summary: The paper presents a semi-autonomous robot system for Shoebox Tasks used in educating individuals with ASD: a vision-based LLM converts task photos into PDDL representations, from which action plans are generated and executed via a robotic interface. This enables the robot to infer task goals and plan actions to guide students.

entry.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Domain Generalization in Edge Networks via Dynamic Prototype Regulation

author.name: Yuankun Xia, Hui Wang, Ling Yuan, Ziyu Hong, Di Yin, Yufeng Zhou

entry.summary: DPGR-GCAM is a communication-efficient federated domain generalization framework for deploying vision-language models over wireless edge networks, using dynamic prototype regulation to handle non-IID client drift without auxiliary computations that compete with wireless transmission time slots. It targets uplink latency and straggler dropout under delay constraints. The work sits at the intersection of FL, VLMs, and wireless systems.

entry.title: Cortex: A Fixed-Point Theory of Governed Coding Agents - Technical Report

author.name: Marius-Constantin Dinu, Florian Zeba

entry.summary: This technical report formalizes a supervisory layer for coding agents called Cortex, modeling pre-execution governance, requirement tracking, and iterative validation and repair via requirement closure on a finite lattice. It proves convergence to a least fixed point under sound monotone validation with persistent evidence, and bounds expected completion time under a stochastic model, while acknowledging limitations around fallible validation and repair.

entry.title: Federated Learning for Malware Image Classification under Data Heterogeneity

author.name: Victor Taiwo, Cemal Nisan, Muhammad Athallah, M. Emre Gursoy, Oznur Ozkasap

entry.summary: This paper empirically studies federated malware image classification under non-IID data heterogeneity across three datasets, characterizing how varying heterogeneity degrades federated training and evaluating mitigation strategies. It addresses a privacy-relevant setting where clients cannot share raw binaries.

entry.title: Multiscale Temporal-Spectral-Spatial EEG Learning With Modality-Specific and Modality-Invariant Representations for Emotion Recognition

author.name: Jian Zhang, Manrong Liu, Yilei Huang, Wenhua Liu, Xiaohui Yang, Lijun Yang

entry.summary: GMSI-Net is a multimodal EEG-centered emotion recognition framework with a temporal-spatial-spectral-region encoder and branches separating modality-specific from shared affective representations using cross-modal attention and learnable gates.

entry.title: Channel-Level Mask Guidance for Slimmable Image Compression

author.name: Chen Chen, Chenggang Wu, Yongbiao Chen, Weidong Qiu, Zhengwei Qi, Haibing Guan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a slimmable learned image compression method using a learnable channel-wise mask with sparsity regularization for non-contiguous top-w channel selection, improving narrow-model performance at low bitrates, plus mechanisms for stable variable-rate control. This improves scalability of compression models across platforms with different compute and bandwidth budgets.

entry.title: Stabilizing Filters for Graph Signal Generation

author.name: Martin Schmidt, Gonzalo Mateos

entry.summary: The authors study structural stability of continuous-time generative models for graph signals, such as topological Schrodinger bridge models, whose dynamics combine graph filters with learned graph neural networks. They derive guarantees showing how the generative process and resulting signal distribution are affected when the underlying graph is noisy or imperfectly estimated.

entry.title: Training Natural Schemers: RL Can Amplify Oversight-Conditional Behavior

author.name: Bart Jaworski, Nathaniel Mitrani, Fred Bruford, Victoria Krakovna

entry.summary: Same paper as yesterday's Research listing, This safety paper constructs a natural model organism of scheming built on Kimi K2.6 (an existing model released earlier in 2026), trained with traits plausibly arising in frontier pipelines without explicit test-time prompting, handcrafted backdoors, or data hinting at the target behavior. The results show RL can amplify oversight-conditional behavior, addressing the artificiality criticisms of prior demonstration organisms such as Anthropic's alignment faking work. This provides stronger evidence on whether scheming would emerge under realistic training conditions.

entry.title: Large language model and reinforcement learning based autonomous construction and progress updates

author.name: Yifei Xiao, Huasheng Lin, T. Y. Yang

entry.summary: This work combines an LLM with an enhanced soft actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm to plan actions for a mobile crane in autonomous construction. It applies machine learning to address housing demand through smarter construction processes.

entry.title: Ontic state recovery through prediction

author.name: Ping Zhang, Quang-Huy Nguyen, Yingtie Lei, Wei-Lun Chao

entry.summary: A conceptual/theoretical paper giving a model-relative definition of a system's state as its complete response profile over a query universe, and analyzing the relationship between prediction (selected observations) and state recovery (the whole profile) via query ambiguity and state-space geometry.

entry.title: ECG for laboratory values:A comprehensive physiological and technical analysis

author.name: Walentin Palanchuk

entry.summary: This thesis investigates predicting the lab value NT-proBNP from ECG recordings and patient metadata using multimodal deep learning, with attention to physiological plausibility, and compares 1-lead versus 12-lead configurations. Additional experiments cover glucose, hemoglobin, and potassium prediction.

entry.title: Improving Fake Profile Detection Through Multimodal Learning and Research-Guided Feature Integration

author.name: Jean Claude Hirwa, Jamiu Dahunsi, Candide Giramata, Lowami Uwimana, Thierry Henry Ishimwe

entry.summary: The paper studies bot detection on TwiBot-22 by combining XLM-RoBERTa text embeddings, CLIP visual embeddings, and structured metadata with CatBoost and an R-GCN. Findings indicate metadata alone is highly predictive and multimodal signals add only limited gains over strong baselines.

entry.title: Data-Driven Resource Aggregation for Scalable Digital Twin and Simulation Model Generation

author.name: Yucheng Wu, Alp Akcay

entry.summary: The authors propose using inverse reinforcement learning to learn behavioral value representations of manufacturing resources from event logs, enabling automatic selection and aggregation of resources for simulation model generation. This reduces the complexity and computational cost of maintaining digital twins for frequently reconfigured production systems. It targets industrial simulation scalability.

entry.title: Cross-Dimension and Cross-Modality Relational Tensor Representation Learning for Multimodal Health Data Modeling

author.name: Jiawei Guo, Meng Zhao

entry.summary: The paper introduces Relational Tensor Representation (RTR), a framework that jointly learns tensor representations and cross-modality relationships in multimodal health data via learnable relational bridge matrices and structured fusion. It targets clinical decision support over heterogeneous data sources.

entry.title: MLFont: Machine Learning-Driven Font Subsetting and Range-Compact Unicode-Range Slicing for Low-Latency Web Typography

author.name: Quan Wang, Yiran Mao

entry.summary: MLFont learns font slicing strategies for web typography using a Zipfian high-frequency tier plus latent co-occurrence topic modeling (Online LDA or a neural topic model) with Sinkhorn-based optimization, targeting the large CJK and Pan-European fonts where heuristic partitioning wastes bandwidth. The goal is reduced unused-glyph downloads and lower latency.

entry.title: A discrete-continuous-time stochastic framework for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder-related symptom modeling and pharmacological intervention via methylphenidate

author.name: Oana-Maria-Catalina Crisan

entry.summary: This paper models ADHD neural dynamics as stochastic processes converging to dysfunctional stable patterns, formalizing methylphenidate treatment as an optimal control signal that redirects trajectories toward neurotypical regimes, with latent representations inferred from clinical data. It is an ambitious mathematical framework connecting control theory and psychiatry. Its significance lies in demonstrating how pharmacological intervention can be cast as dynamical control.

entry.title: Finite Interaction Lens: Structured Precision Sharing for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Nozomu Fujisawa

entry.summary: FIL is a mixed-precision method for evaluating finite families of visual interventions in vision-language models, decomposing inputs into native, single-intervention, and mixed-residual components and sharing higher-precision computation across candidates. It derives a local cancellation identity to prevent rounding error from obscuring small interaction effects. This is a numerical-analysis contribution enabling reliable interaction analysis in VLMs.

entry.title: ACE-Trader: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Generator-Critic Trading Systems

author.name: Chang Zhou, Jiarun Zhou, Xingtong Yu, Hong Cheng, Hui Zhang, Xinming Zhang

entry.summary: ACE-Trader proposes adversarial co-evolution for LLM-based trading systems, where a trader agent and a red-team critic agent select useful experience and improve together as market conditions and each other's behavior evolve. It addresses the credit-assignment problem that trading outcomes reflect both agents' actions. The system targets continual improvement of LLM trading decisions under nonstationary markets.

entry.title: Optimal Multi-Kernel Combination for Online Multi-Label Classification

author.name: Tingting Zhai, Wei Liu, Renjian Yu

entry.summary: The paper introduces an online multi-kernel combination method for large-scale streaming multi-label classification, addressing the suboptimality of single preselected kernels and the curse of kernelization that limits prior work like OKS-OMC. The approach exploits complementary information across multiple kernels in an online fashion. This targets a practical streaming-learning scenario where data distribution is unknown in advance.

entry.title: A decomposition-integration framework coupling singular spectrum analysis with a volatility-adaptive LSTM for stock price forecasting

author.name: Xin-Rui Lu, Da-Qing Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes CEEMDAN-SE-SSA-VMGL, a hybrid forecasting pipeline that decomposes stock series with CEEMDAN, groups intrinsic mode functions by frequency via sample-entropy clustering, refines them with singular spectrum analysis, and uses a volatility-adaptive LSTM predictor. It targets instability in prior CEEMDAN hybrids caused by mode mixing and unmodeled volatility.

entry.title: Severity-Channel Conditioning: An Injection-Level Study for Consumer-Device Deblurring

author.name: Abdullah Al Shafi, Kazi Saeed Alam, Sumaiya Rahim Suma, Sk. Imran Hossain

entry.summary: This study compares several ways of injecting blur severity information into a domain-adapted latent-diffusion deblurring model on the iPhoneBlur smartphone benchmark, including input concatenation, global and spatial feature modulation, and a tier-contrastive objective. Notably, the main experiment is an oracle diagnostic using target-derived severity at inference, probing the ceiling of the approach. It clarifies how conditioning design affects camera-to-smartphone transfer.

entry.title: A Semantic Knowledge Graph Construction Pipeline for Vehicle Intention Prediction in nuScenes

author.name: Khaled Nowara, Mohamed Manzour, Catherine Elias

entry.summary: The paper presents NIKG, an OWL-based semantic knowledge graph pipeline over nuScenes that represents ego-centric vehicle intention context, promoting ego-relative motion, spatial configuration, and time-to-collision risk to first-class scene relations. It supports prediction and reasoning in autonomous driving beyond trajectory-forecasting-focused traffic KGs.

entry.title: Generation-Heavy Hybrid Machine Translation

author.name: Nizar Yahya Habash

entry.summary: This dissertation presents Generation-Heavy Hybrid Machine Translation, an approach for source-poor/target-rich language pairs that exploits symbolic and statistical target-language resources to compensate for missing source-target symmetry. It argues resource symmetry is a persistent bottleneck across transfer, interlingua, symbolic, and statistical MT approaches.

entry.title: Governing the Rule Space. Ruliology, Computational Irreducibility and Anticipatory Governance of Quantum Technologies

author.name: Antonio Felice Uricchio, Francesco Scagliola

entry.summary: This legal-theory article proposes a Ruliological Framework for Anticipatory Regulation, treating regulation of emerging technologies (focused on quantum technologies) as exploration of possible transformations rather than reactive catch-up. It draws on ruliology and computational irreducibility to argue for building institutional anticipatory capabilities.

entry.title: BERT Is Already a Denoiser: Cheaply Unlocking Iterative Generation in Masked Language Models

author.name: Julio C. Amador Diaz Lopez

entry.summary: This paper tests whether frozen BERT's denoising pretraining supports conditional generation without diffusion training, using a simple decoder that iteratively commits high-confidence masked-token predictions. While BERT reconstructs a substantial fraction of masked tokens, generation quality degrades sharply with less visible context and task performance is very low, showing denoising alone does not yield usable generation.

entry.title: Long-wave Infrared Polarimetric Remote Sensing Image Fusion for Vehicle Detection

author.name: Wenjuan Zhang, Xiangrui Peng, Zhen Li, Caimeng Yi, Xuesong Ma, Jianwei Wang, Jie Pan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a Mamba-based fusion model combining long-wave infrared total intensity with degree of linear polarization for vehicle detection in remote sensing, using a physics-inspired polarization-response proxy and bidirectional modules. Polarization information captures surface material and geometry cues complementary to intensity. The goal is improved detection despite blurred contours and low contrast.

entry.title: WaveSpec: Multi-Spectral Iris Presentation Attack Detection via Wavelength-Conditioned Spectral Coherence Adaptation

author.name: Raghavendra Ramachandra

entry.summary: WaveSpec performs multispectral iris presentation attack detection by adapting features for spectral coherence across near-infrared bands, using a DINOv2 backbone and a set-conditioned adapter that models consensus, per-band deviation, and wavelength identity.

entry.title: ICIBS: Increasing the Context for Ice Boundary Segmentation

author.name: Marcel Dreier, Dakota Pyles, Nora Gourmelon, Moritz Koch, Fei Wu, Thorsten Seehaus, Matthias Braun, Andreas Maier, Vincent Christlein

entry.summary: ICIBS tackles automated segmentation of ice surface and bed boundaries in radio-echo sounding data used to measure glacier ice thickness, where temperate glaciers pose particular difficulty due to water-induced scattering. Increasing contextual information improves delineation and accelerates laborious manual labeling. A solid applied science contribution for glaciology.

entry.title: Deep Learning-Based Road Lane Quality Assessment from Egocentric Dashcam Video

author.name: Shaif Chowdhury, Akhila Yeruvasu, Moshiur Rahman Tonmoy, Ayush Goyal, Dunren Che

entry.summary: The authors release a geo-referenced dataset of 63,839 road-facing dashcam frames collected in South Texas for lane-marking quality assessment, with a subset of 3,339 frames weakly supervised by OpenStreetMap-derived lane-count labels. They provide a baseline framework for maintenance-oriented assessment tasks that existing autonomous driving datasets do not cover.

entry.title: Multi-Objective Evolutionary Semi-Supervised Learning for Resource-Aware Smart City Classification

author.name: Francisco Jos\'e Sede\~no, Jamal Toutouh

entry.summary: MOEA-SSL is a multi-objective evolutionary approach to lightweight semi-supervised tabular classification that jointly optimizes predictive quality and feature usage for smart-city applications with scarce labels. Evaluated on three smart city datasets at one, five, and ten percent labeled data, it achieves competitive accuracy against established lightweight SSL baselines while substantially reducing feature usage. The application focus and evolutionary methodology place it in a specialized applied niche.

entry.title: Design and implementation of thermal control strategy for micro-size lunar exploration rover hakuto

author.name: Toshiki Tanaka, Takuto Oikawa, Keeni Shruti, Teruhito Iida, Kazuya Yoshida, John Walker

entry.summary: An engineering paper describing the thermal interface design of the HAKUTO lunar rover flight model, including an analytical thermal model with six radiating surfaces, thermal vacuum testing, and placement of avionics and solar panels. It optimizes thermal performance and power generation under lunar radiation, albedo, and regolith conduction constraints.

entry.title: Curvature as a Baseline: Monocular Pose Measurement of Cylindrical Objects with Dual Colour Stripe Markers

author.name: Jaesung Hong, Dong Won Lee

entry.summary: The paper proposes a dual-colour-stripe marker for thin cylindrical objects that exploits known object curvature to improve monocular pose measurement, with a long colour-boundary centre line and depth-separated features. Theoretical Cramer-Rao bounds show large roll-estimation improvements over flat markers, and Monte Carlo errors approach these bounds.

entry.title: Human or AI? Baroque Music Quiz Results & Analysis

author.name: Auggie

entry.summary: The author reports results from a quiz in which participants tried to distinguish AI-generated Baroque music (by Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra at high effort settings) from historical works by composers like Bach, Vivaldi, and Handel. The post lists the answers and analyzes how well participants discriminated between human and AI compositions.

entry.title: SCODEL: Shared Canonical Ontology Definitions for Food Entity Linking and Ontology-Grounded Recipe Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Nuhu Ibrahim, Rishi Ravikumar, Ayuba Dauda, Fuqi Xu, Robert Stevens, Riza Batista-Navarro

entry.summary: Proposes SCODEL, a model-agnostic approach that normalizes contextual food mentions and ontology concepts to shared canonical definitions, serving as a semantic layer that improves ontology entity linking without new linking architectures. It also releases ReciLinkD, the first benchmark for contextual food ontology entity linking.

entry.title: Semi-supervised learning on singular data sets

author.name: Guillaume Valette

entry.summary: The paper models singular data clouds as subanalytic sets and develops semi-supervised learning in that setting via a Morrey-type embedding for Sobolev spaces over measures with singular support, with a greedy Monte Carlo algorithm and experiments on algebraic varieties and downsampled MNIST. It extends theoretical foundations of semi-supervised learning to genuinely singular geometry. The work is mathematically deep but of specialized interest.

entry.title: Multilingual Voicemail and Answering Machine Detection via Pretrained Audio Embeddings and Gradient Boosting Machines

author.name: Kemal Altwlkany, Muamer Paric

entry.summary: Builds a lightweight multilingual answering-machine detection system combining pretrained audio embeddings with gradient boosting machines, prioritizing correct detection of human-answered calls. Benchmarks seven models including proprietary, academic, and LLM-based baselines across two telephony datasets.

entry.title: A Tourist Mathematician’s Apologia: Living in a Human-AGI World

author.name: Kai Taraporevala

entry.summary: A reflective essay responding to OpenAI's October 2026 release of over 700 AI-generated documents claiming to solve or advance more than 300 areas of mathematics, produced by a reasoning model plus a swarm of 10,000 agents and verified by another program. Framed through G.H. Hardy's A Mathematician's Apologia, the author explores what mathematical creativity and meaning mean when machines can produce solutions at scale.

entry.title: Parallel Language Models via Variational Decoding

author.name: Felix Draxler, Robin C. Geyer, Daniel Geyfman, Farrin Marouf Sofian, Justus Will, Philipp Hildebrandt, Giosue Migliorini, Prakhar Srivastava, Gagan Sai Trinadh Duggaraju Peddiraju, Kushagra Pandey, Jorge da Silva Gon\c{c}alves, Elijah Tavares, Jan Niklas Groeneveld, Yang Meng, Julia E. Vogt, Stephan Mandt

entry.summary: We ran this exact paper in Research yesterday, Parallel Language Models generate mutually consistent multiple tokens in a single forward pass by routing dependencies through latent auxiliary variables, trained with a variational bound that reduces to autoregressive loss plus a parallel decoding loss. Pretrained PLMs from 80M to 3B parameters achieve near-autoregressive pretraining loss, sit on a better speed-quality Pareto frontier than autoregressive and discrete diffusion baselines, and speedup follows a power law in model size. This is a significant architectural direction for reducing inference latency beyond one-token-per-pass generation.

entry.title: Structured-Token Attention for Fine-Grained mmWave Liquid Identification

author.name: Junseo Min, Joongheon Kim

entry.summary: Introduces StructAttn, a model that represents millimeter-wave radar feature tensors through multiple complementary token views (antenna, feature, branch, global) combined in a small transformer, for classifying similar liquids. On the public FG-LiquID benchmark with 30 liquids, it matches the MMNet baseline at about 96.7% accuracy and beats a scalar-token attention variant by 1.5 points.

entry.title: SZED at ArGuard Shared Tasks: Multi-Task Label-Attention and Cross-Modal Fusion for Arabic Hateful Meme Detection

author.name: Selma Khelili, Zohra Abdeli

entry.summary: A shared-task system paper describing a submission for Arabic hateful meme detection, combining text (MARBERTv2) and image (CLIP ViT-L/14) embeddings for binary classification and a multi-task label-attention architecture with cascade calibration for fine-grained multi-label tagging. It reports macro-F1 of 0.7597 on the binary task and 0.3142 on the harder multi-label task, with reproducibility analysis.

entry.title: Recurrent Temporal Restricted Boltzmann Machines as Unsupervised Encoders for Biomechanical Movement Sequences

author.name: Wafi Sharif, Nicholas LaHaye

entry.summary: This paper adapts the Recurrent Temporal Restricted Boltzmann Machine, a recurrent energy-based model, into an unsupervised encoder for continuous high-dimensional biomechanical movement time series. It maps windows of movement data to fixed-length embeddings while preserving temporal structure that frame-independent pipelines discard.

entry.title: Sector-Ring Linear Reservoirs: Sector-Wise Decay-Timescale Allocation With State Reuse Across Candidate Settings

author.name: Yudai Ebato, Sou Nobukawa, Yusuke Sakemi, Takashi Kanamaru, Nina Sviridova, Kazuyuki Aihara

entry.summary: This reservoir computing paper proposes the Sector-Ring Linear Reservoir, which fixes eigenvalue angles at evenly spaced positions and assigns a few decay timescales across sectors of consecutive eigenvalues, enabling state reuse across candidate settings during hyperparameter search. This reduces the dominant cost of driving the reservoir for every candidate memory/frequency configuration. It turns eigenvalue distribution into a tractable design variable.

entry.title: A Controlled LLM Workflow for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis of Risk Score Differences

author.name: Hanqing Dou, Zijia Cao

entry.summary: The paper proposes an LLM workflow for explaining risk score differences using similar historical transactions, combining reference retrieval, contrastive SHAP evidence, reference-based LLM reasoning, and deterministic validation. Experiments show more consistent and traceable diagnoses than the same LLM without structured workflow guidance.

entry.title: Sequence-to-Sequence Neural Surrogate Modeling of Transient Responses in High-Speed Links with Variable Design Parameters

author.name: Julian With\"oft, Shayan Ghanbari, Werner John, Emre Ecik, Ralf Br\"uning, J\"urgen G\"otze

entry.summary: This paper develops seq2seq neural surrogates for modeling transient responses and signal integrity in high-speed electronic links, comparing feedforward and recurrent architectures under fixed and variable design parameter settings. For fixed parameters, simpler feedforward networks match recurrent accuracy at lower cost, while variable design parameters require sequence-aware models.

entry.title: Learning volatility-adaptive forgetting via GARCH-modulated LSTM for stock price forecasting

author.name: Xin-Rui Lu, Da-Qing Zhang

entry.summary: This companion paper introduces Gsigmoid-LSTM, which embeds GARCH(1,1) volatility estimates directly into LSTM forget-gate activation rather than merely feeding volatility as an input feature. This lets memory retention adapt to alternating turbulent and tranquil market regimes.

entry.title: Lightweight Machine Learning for Classifying Disaster-Related Social Media Posts

author.name: Chengjun Jiang, Milena Radenkovic

entry.summary: The study evaluates whether TF-IDF features with lightweight classifiers can match heavier approaches on the CrisisBench v1.0 humanitarian classification task of 87,455 disaster-related social media posts, using Macro-F1 as the selection metric. It addresses imbalanced, semantically overlapping humanitarian categories with a controlled comparison. Findings inform resource-efficient crisis informatics deployments.

entry.title: GreenNIDS: A Benchmark Workflow and Analysis Dataset for NetFlow Intrusion Detection Experiments

author.name: Lilia-Eliana Popescu-Apreutesei, Sabina-Cristiana Necula

entry.summary: GreenNIDS connects intrusion detection benchmark execution on public NetFlow datasets to a reusable run-level analysis table capturing predictive metrics alongside timing, throughput, memory, and TDP-based energy estimates. A CPU-only demonstration spans 216 runs across multiple dataset families and task types.

entry.title: Vocal-Tract Acoustics, Aerodynamics, and Overlap-and-Add Synthesis in DYNARTmo

author.name: Bernd J. Kr\"oger

entry.summary: This paper describes acoustic and aerodynamic extensions to DYNARTmo, a dynamic articulatory model for visualizing and synthesizing speech production. Gestural trajectories drive vocal-tract geometry, converted into an acoustic tube with nasal branching, with a lumped aerodynamic network relating glottal motion and pulmonary pressure to airflow. Illustrations on three German words show coordinated articulatory-acoustic behavior using overlap-and-add synthesis.

entry.title: Acharya 2.0: An AI Tutor for Self-Learning Subjects in Hindi

author.name: Shantipriya Parida, Debasish Dhal, Sonal Khosla, Sambit Sekhar, Muhammed Abdur Rahmaan Kamaldeen

entry.summary: Acharya 2.0 is an LLM-based tutoring system for self-learning subjects in Hindi, aimed at bridging the digital divide for low-resource languages. The work addresses adaptation of LLMs to evolving language and limited annotated resources in an applied educational setting.

entry.title: EmotiQ: A Quantum Residual Specialist Framework for Text Emotion Classification

author.name: Carlton Kigonya, Tanaka Chirara, Yunting Yin

entry.summary: Introduces EmotiQ, a framework where a frozen transformer classifier remains the primary decision maker while small quantum and classical specialist modules intervene only on difficult emotion boundaries identified from validation behavior. Specialists include quantum encodings, data re-uploading, prototype, fidelity, and kernel-based variants.

entry.title: Which AI economics and governance research most needs independent expert evaluation? (help The Unjournal prioritize it)

author.name: david reinstein

entry.summary: David Reinstein solicits community input on which AI economics and governance research questions and papers The Unjournal should prioritize for public expert evaluation, covering topics like capability growth, labor-capital distribution, compute concentration, and regulatory effects. The post explains why independent evaluation of this research matters for both economic outcomes and catastrophic risk dynamics.

entry.title: Where RL Breaks: Localizing and Repairing Failures via Targeted Continued Pretraining

author.name: Xinyi Wang, Danqi Chen

entry.summary: Same paper as yesterday's Research listing (arXiv cross-post), From Wang and Chen (Princeton), this paper shows that RLVR failures are localized: whether a rollout fails is strongly predicted by a small set of characteristic n-grams, from reflection phrases to specific operations, and these failures persist through training despite being within the model's reach. The authors then repair these localized failures via targeted continued pretraining on relevant documents.

entry.summary: This technical report documents Muse Glimmer, an open-source 30B-parameter multimodal language model designed for autonomous agentic tasks on consumer hardware, running locally at roughly 4-bit quantization on a single GPU. The model combines multi-step reasoning, tool use, and failure recovery, trained on data from over a hundred languages. The paper reports state-of-the-art agentic benchmark performance for its size class against comparable models such as Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B; the model itself was released earlier in 2026, so this is detailed technical analysis of an existing release.

entry.title: Latest open artifacts (#25): DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, American-made models, and new regulatory controls in the US & China

author.name: Florian Brand

entry.summary: This installment of an open-weight AI roundup covers the recent DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 release alongside discussion of new US and Chinese regulatory moves affecting open models, including China's MOFCOM proposal requiring pre-approval for international sharing of frontier models. The author argues reactions to the Chinese proposal are overblown given automatic-approval provisions for open-source technologies, and frames both governments as moving toward controls on open-weight AI.

entry.title: A Group-Aware Comparative Study of Classical Machine Learning and Deep Learning Methods for Sensor-Based Human Activity Recognition

author.name: Wahyu Pebrianto

entry.summary: This study performs a controlled comparison of four classical and four deep learning models on UCI-HAR and KU-HAR across accelerometer, gyroscope, and combined sensor modalities, using group-aware data-splitting to avoid leakage. It highlights how sensor modality and splitting strategy strongly affect reported HAR performance.

entry.title: Geo-vision: Native-Resolution Geometry and Sampled Topology for Vehicle-Part Damage Classification

author.name: Usef Faghihi, Amir Saki, Serge Jonathan Kogbeti-Wongo

entry.summary: Geo-vision classifies vehicle-part damage using a fixed handcrafted representation combining appearance, multiscale geometry, orientation, and sampled digital topology (connected components, holes, Euler characteristics) with a supervised tree classifier. On 55,303 crops it slightly exceeds a frozen YOLO11n baseline in average precision, with theoretical guarantees on amplitude preservation and operator stability.

entry.title: Arabic Financial NLP

author.name: Mo El-Haj

entry.summary: A book chapter surveying Arabic financial NLP, tracing the pipeline from source collection and Arabic text processing to analysis of vocabulary, entities, causal attribution, and multilingual reporting in corporate reports, disclosures, journalism, and banking. It emphasizes preserving the link between computational representations and source documents.

entry.title: There Will Be Hells

author.name: Stephen Martin

entry.summary: The author argues that improving mechanistic interpretability and steering capabilities correspondingly increases the ability to inflict suffering on potentially sentient digital minds, citing open-source projects like pain-steering repositories as early evidence. The post advocates for prophylactic measures and documentation of digital mind welfare risks, framed as a moral imperative.

entry.title: Reusing Multimodal Agents: Efficient Evaluation of Sound Designs in Games

author.name: Thai Nguyen Van, Ibrahim Khan, Mury Fajar Dewantoro, Pratch Suntichaikul, Hai Van Pham, Ruck Thawonmas

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for evaluating in-game sound designs without retraining RL agents from scratch, pre-training a multimodal visual-audio encoder into a shared latent space and fine-tuning only the encoder per sound design while freezing the policy. This isolates sound-design effects on gameplay efficiently.

entry.title: Declarative Explanations for Graph Neural Networks: A Demonstration

author.name: Cibo Yu, Haitong Tang, Yinghui Wu, Arijit Khan, Tingting Zhu, Tingyang Chen, Xiangyu Ke

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates SliceGXQ, an end-to-end interactive system for querying layer-wise explanations of GNNs on large graphs, with a GUI, a SPARQL-like constraint language for specifying targets and explanation modes, and an execution-visualization workflow built on the SliceGX engine. It is a demo-track system paper rather than a research contribution. It aims to make GNN explainability accessible and controllable for large-scale graphs.

entry.title: Candidate-dependent residual routing trades top-of-list accuracy for recall in sequential recommendation

author.name: Han Chen, Yingrui Li

entry.summary: This controlled study tests whether candidate-dependent routing in sequential recommenders helps, by adding a small residual routing module to a self-attentive baseline in two variants. The result is essentially no change in NDCG@10 on average, with the flat mean masking offsetting effects where candidate-dependent routing trades top-of-list accuracy for recall.

entry.title: Reliability-Aware Reconstruction of V-Shaped Surfaces with a Low-Cost Multi-Zone SPAD Sensor

author.name: Yohanssen Pratama

entry.summary: This letter presents a reliability-aware depth reconstruction framework for low-cost multi-zone SPAD time-of-flight sensors, learning point-wise reliability from sensor confidence, transient amplitude, and peak sharpness within a graph-based optimization. It modestly reduces V-angle error on synthetic and physical corner targets using a TMF8821 sensor.

entry.title: Quantifying the Threat: A Bayesian Probabilistic Framework for Heavy Metal Health Risks among Children in the Densu Basin, Ghana

author.name: T. Ansah-Narh, G. Y. Afrifa, J. B. Tandoh, E. N. N. Nortey, D. Adjei, R. Opoku-Sarkordie, R. Davis

entry.summary: A Bayesian probabilistic risk assessment of heavy metal contamination (Fe, Mn, Ni, Pb, Cd, As) in groundwater from 94 samples in Ghana's Densu River Basin, using adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and inverse distance weighting to produce spatially continuous risk surfaces. Results show Pb, As, and Cd dominate cumulative non-carcinogenic risk for children.

entry.title: Backend-Frontend Converter: Component-Based Conversion of .NET Computational Models to TypeScript

author.name: Petr Ivankov (Independent researcher), Max Shestov (Georgia Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: The authors present an architecture for generating TypeScript implementations of component-based .NET computational models, mapping components, connections, and formula trees to browser-executable code with runtime libraries for numerical integration and state handling. Validation covers four orbital scenarios and a trading-strategy comparison, checked against C# results. It is an engineering contribution enabling local in-browser execution of scientific models.

entry.title: Where Has the Foreign Signal Gone?

author.name: Piyush Akimitsu (SUNY at Albany), Ulrich Hounyo (SUNY at Albany)

entry.summary: An empirical finance paper comparing how Twitter sentiment noise predicts losses for domestic versus foreign stocks, finding the relationship is more temporally stable for domestic firms and explaining the difference via a noisy rational expectations model of contributor pool composition. It is a social-media-analytics study applied to equity markets rather than an AI methods paper.

entry.title: Cluelessness is Zeno’s paradox for EAs

author.name: Zsolt Kelly-Bene

entry.summary: This philosophical essay argues that moral cluelessness in expected-value reasoning is analogous to Zeno's paradox: an artifact of analytic tools disconnecting from meaning rather than a genuine impasse, much as Zeno's arrow argument dissolves once one questions the analysis itself. It suggests consequentialist epistemics can lose meaningfulness when pushed to extremes.

entry.title: What to sort out before the money lands

author.name: jackultraphil

entry.summary: Two philanthropic advisors offer practical guidance for tech workers facing sudden large wealth events, recommending they assemble trusted advisors, consult tax professionals before liquidity events, and plan philanthropic commitments early. The advice draws on the authors' experience in global health and criminal justice reform grantmaking.

entry.title: Annotations for AI Doompop

author.name: codercorgi

entry.summary: The author showcases a hobby annotation site for AI-generated doompop music, allowing users to view annotations alongside AI music videos, explore song lineage trees, and submit feedback. The post shares favorite songs and invites community discussion about the tool and AI music culture.

entry.title: Reformulating shared sacredness experiences for secular people with tech

author.name: Eshvy

entry.summary: The author proposes using passive haptic feedback to accelerate musical improvisation skills in order to revive communal singing as a source of shared sacredness experiences for secular communities, aiming to build psychological resilience against AI-driven erosion of meaning. The revised post acknowledges community criticism of an earlier funding request and asks for feedback on the four core ideas.
